### 14w. WHOSE ROWS MAY A LOGIN READ — the third scope question (owner directive 2026-10-05)

Owner, verbatim: *"currently employees can see the schdule of the whoel company, i saw when i used
rana to clok in as him, it should only show the reps wown schdule and the managers his own schdule
and if any employee works under him"* — and, the same hour: *"same for sales report, they shoudl be
gated out of all stores other and thier own, also the flags should only be seen by them for thier
own not all stores"*.

**TWO GRAINS, and the owner named both correctly.** The sales report is per STORE, so it is fixed at
the SPAN (Q1, below). A flag and a shift are per PERSON, so they are fixed at the PERSON (Q3). Both
halves are the same class — *a rep's reach was never their own* — which is why they ship together.

**THE CLASS, not the instance.** Every schedule read answered *"which STORES may I see"* and never
*"which PEOPLE"*. `storeops.scope_keyset` is a store keyset and `scope_emp_ids` only re-expresses
that same keyset as employee_ids, so a login that resolved a store resolved every person who ever
worked at it. Two independent widenings then made that the whole company, both measured read-only on
2026-10-05 against production:
- the house `sales_rep` role carries `permissions.scope = 'store'`, **not `'self'`** — a rep was
  never self-narrowed at all; and
- `caller_scope` unions MARKET grants into a scope-`'store'` span, and **28 of 37** house rep logins
  carry a market, **5 of them three markets** (`"NYC, NJ, LI"` — the entire company).
`self_store_codes` already refused to read market grants for exactly this reason and `roster_keyset`
already applied that refusal to the NAME PICKER (§13). The schedule READ never got it.

**THE THIRD QUESTION.** `app/core/scope.py` opened with a two-way split; this is Q3, and it lives in
that same file rather than as a fourth private copy of "how wide is this person":

| | question | answer | shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 REPORTING | whose NUMBERS may I see? | `reporting_span_codes` / `storeops.scope_keyset` | store keyset |
| Q2 ROSTER | whom may I PUT on a shift? | `roster_reach` / `roster_keyset` | deliberately WIDE |
| Q3 PEOPLE | whose PERSON-KEYED rows may I READ? | `people_visibility` / `visible_people_keyset` | deliberately NARROW |

Q2 and Q3 point opposite ways on purpose: a manager must be able to schedule a borrowed rep they
cannot otherwise see, and a rep must be able to read their own week without reading the register
they are picked from. One set can never answer both — that is the §13 defect in a new place.

**Q3 GOVERNS EVERY ROW THAT NAMES A PERSON**, not just shifts: the schedule and its templates, time
off, swaps, the punch list, and the per-rep rows of a report. ONE declaration, so the owner's second
message needed no second switch.

**THE Q1 HALF — A MARKET PIN NO LONGER WIDENS A STORE-SCOPED SPAN.** `caller_scope` unioned
`_login_extra_codes` (market + store pins) into every non-`self` scope, so a rep pinned to one store
and three markets reported on all of them — which is what made the SALES REPORT, the flags queue and
every other store-keyed report company-wide. A market is *what area this person covers*, a manager's
fact; `scope = 'store'` says this login covers a STORE. So for `scope = 'store'` the span now
resolves through `_cscope.self_store_codes` (the login's `store_code` + `store_codes`) unioned with
any org unit the login actually manages. `scope = 'market'/'region'` is untouched — its market still
binds. `scope = 'self'` is untouched — it stays the empty, deny-all keyset the ~54 `in_keyset` call
sites already rely on.
- **STRICTLY NARROWING, measured read-only 2026-10-05** by running the real `self_store_codes` /
  `login_grant_codes` over production: of **90** logins holding a store/self-scoped role, **32
  narrow** — worst cases `alondra.navarro@luxelinkwireless.com` (store_manager) and two Luxelink reps
  at **27 → 1** store, `ramosbonilla19@gmail.com` **22 → 1**, nine more Cellfonz reps **16 → 1-2**.
  The other 58 are unchanged. Nobody gains a store: `employees.home_store` is deliberately NOT read
  here (it would GRANT a store to the **8** logins that resolve none today — those are reported as a
  setup gap, "pin the store on the login", not papered over in a reporting span).
- **One judgement call worth the owner's eye:** `alondra.navarro` is a `store_manager` pinned to one
  store with a market grant. She narrows to that store. If she genuinely covers the Chicago market
  she wants `market_manager`, or more `store_codes` on her login — a setting, either way.

- **THE ONE HOME (the ruling):** `app/core/scope.py` —
  `people_visibility(role_perms) -> 'self' | 'span' | 'all'` and
  `visible_people_keyset(...) -> (employee_ids | None, why)`. Module graph fact
  `people_visibility`.
- **THE ONE WIRING POINT:** `storeops/router.py::schedule_emp_ids(authorization, org_id, since, until)`
  — `None` unrestricted (rbac off / no token / unprovisioned, same posture as `caller_scope`),
  `set()` deny-all. `keep_visible_people(rows, eids, *fields)` is the only comparison helper, and
  `_widen_emp_id_forms` resolves BOTH id forms (a Schedule-page shift stores the numeric
  `employees.id`, the roster and punches store `E45` — the `payroll_identity` mismatch), so a rep is
  never filtered out of their own schedule.
- **DECLARED, NOT INFERRED (RULE TWO):** `roles.permissions.people_visibility`, editable on
  Admin → Roles & Access ("Schedule visibility — whose shifts they can see"); frontend mirror
  `rbac.ts::peopleVisibility`, drift-locked. With nothing declared the fallback derives from
  `scope` and **FAILS NARROW**: `'all'/'company' → all`, `'market'/'region(al)' → span`, everything
  else including `'store'` **→ self**, because in the house org a rep AND their store manager are
  BOTH `scope = 'store'` and the schema cannot tell them apart. Migration
  `1058_people_visibility_declaration.sql` declares every live role so nothing rides the fallback
  — **required before managers are correct**; reps are correct either way.
- **"WORKS UNDER ME" RESOLVES FROM STORE ASSIGNMENT, not the org tree.** `reporting_employee_ids`
  (home store UNION actually-worked-a-shift/punch-there, bounded by the caller's own date window) is
  the primary source; the org tree is unioned in where it exists but cannot lead, because it
  resolves a manager for only **6 of 29** house stores and **0 of 20** Luxelink stores (§47.17's
  measurement, 2026-10-04). `_caller_org_unit_codes` feeds the ruling the org tree ALONE —
  deliberately NOT `_caller_span_codes`, which unions the login's market pin and is the widening
  above.
- **MARKET GRANTS BIND ONLY FOR A SCOPE THAT CAN USE A MARKET** — the same line `self_store_codes`
  and `roster_keyset` draw. A DM (`scope='market'`) gets their market; a store-scoped manager gets
  their own store(s) plus any org unit they actually manage, and their market pin is ignored.
- **THE ONE GATE for a person-keyed read:** `storeops/router.py::gate_person_rows`. **When
  people-visibility restricts, the PERSON set IS the gate — the store keyset is not additionally
  applied.** That is deliberate: a rep's own shift at a store they were borrowed to is still their
  own shift, and once the Q1 half stops a market pin widening their span, a stacked store gate would
  hide it from them. The person set was derived from that same span plus the caller, so it can never
  reach anyone the span did not already allow. Unrestricted callers keep exactly the gate they had
  (store keyset for a table with a store column, `scope_emp_ids` for one without).
- **ONE answer to "is this login an individual contributor":** `storeops.role_is_self_scoped`. It
  was `scope == 'self'` alone — False for every rep in this tenant — **which is the whole reason the
  flags ask had done nothing**: every per-rep narrowing in the platform hangs off this one answer. It
  now also returns True for a role declaring `people_visibility = 'self'`, so the schedule, the punch
  list and the per-rep report rows all follow one declaration.
- **`GET /commcalc/flags/{period}`** gates on the person through the EXISTING one-homes —
  `_caller_rep_keys` ("which rep rows are mine") and `payout_audience.mine_only` ("is this row
  mine"), which the commission, coaching and action-plan surfaces already share. A flag names
  `epay_salesperson`, already in `payout_audience.REP_NAME_FIELDS`, so no new predicate was written;
  the lock fails the build if one appears. A manager's queue is unchanged (still their span, by
  store), and `/flags-unrouted` still catches a flag no span can match.
- **The reads wired (NARROWING ONLY):** `GET /storeops/shifts`, `/schedule/hours-trend` (payload
  gains `scope.people_restricted`), `/shift-templates`, `/time-off`, `/shift-swaps`,
  `/timeclock/list`, `GET /commcalc/flags/{period}`. **The sibling sweep also closed
  `GET /storeops/staffing-heatmap`, which had NO scope gate of any kind** — any signed-in caller
  could heat-map any store; it is a store-level aggregate with no names, so its gate is the store
  keyset, not the per-person one. `GET /timeclock/status` was already token-identity self-only.
- **Proof:** `backend/harness_people_visibility.py` — **47 checks over the REAL endpoints**
  (`get_shifts`, `schedule_hours_trend`, `get_shift_templates`, `get_time_off`, `get_shift_swaps`,
  `timeclock_list`, `staffing_heatmap`, `commcalc.get_flags`). §A and §K1/§K9 reproduce BOTH reported
  leaks on the **pre-fix** gate (computed from `_login_extra_codes` directly, never from the current
  `scope_keyset`, so the regression cannot quietly stop being reproduced); §I proves every caller
  reads a subset of what the pre-fix gate gave them. **Lock:**
  `backend/harness_people_visibility_lock.py` — **27 checks**; fails the build when the ruling is
  copied, the wiring re-derived, a wired read stops asking, a NEW person-keyed GET lands unwired
  without an EXCUSED reason, `gate_person_rows` stops letting the person set win over the store
  keyset, `caller_scope` goes back to reading a market pin for a store scope (or starts reading
  `home_store` into a reporting span), `role_is_self_scoped` stops dereferencing the declaration, the
  flags queue grows its own rep predicate, or the frontend mirror drifts. CI job *People visibility*
  in `org-scope-guard.yml`.
- **Owner-facing SQL (surfaced, NOT applied):**
  `/mnt/project-files/schedule-visibility/RUN_people_visibility_1058_2026-10-05.sql` — numbered
  steps with a BEFORE query, the declarations, a VERIFY and an UNDO block. Numbered **1058**: it was
  drafted as 1057 and collided with #388's `1057_notify_send_log_report_label`, which merged and was
  applied while this sat awaiting approval — the normal cost of surfacing a migration rather than
  applying it (see §19.18's sibling note on 1015).


### 14x. A SPAN IS EVIDENCE, NOT A PIN — and a per-rep report is their own numbers (owner directive 2026-10-05)

Owner, on seeing §14w land: *"the store pin is not desired, the employee shoudl have teh visibility
in the store they have been schduled and actually worked and only their numbers, the concept of home
store does not apply for vistibility into the performance of the store"*.

- **THE CLASS.** `app_users.store_code` / `store_codes` and `employees.home_store` are SETUP — what
  somebody typed on a form once. They were serving as the answer to a question about the present:
  where is this person, therefore whose numbers are theirs to read. Measured read-only 2026-10-05
  across both tenants: of the 71 logins declaring `people_visibility = 'self'`, **64 have a shift or
  a punch at a store no pin names**, and **7 are pinned to a store they have never once worked**. A
  span is now resolved from EVIDENCE, of exactly two kinds: the roster said be there (a shift), or
  the clock says they were there (a punch).
- **TWO DIMENSIONS, ONE DECLARATION, SHIPPED TOGETHER.** The same `people_visibility` fact answers
  both halves of the owner's sentence, and either half alone is a regression:
  | | question | home |
  |---|---|---|
  | store | which stores' rows reach me at all? | `core.scope.visible_store_codes` |
  | person | whose rows among them are mine to read? | `core.scope.visible_people_keyset` (§14w) |
  Evidence makes an individual contributor's store list **WIDER** — 84 pinned stores become 354
  worked — because reps are moved around constantly. That is safe only because the person filter
  reads the same declaration: more stores, and at every one of them only their own rows.
- **ONE EVIDENCE REGISTRY.** `core.scope.WORKED_AT_SOURCES` is the one statement of what records a
  person being somewhere (table, store column, date column, soft-delete filter). Both directions
  dereference it — `worked_store_codes` (employee → stores) and `reporting_employee_ids` (stores →
  employees) — so a third kind of evidence, a column rename or a second soft-delete flag lands in
  both or in neither. Before this directive only the second existed and it carried that knowledge
  inline.
- **`caller_scope` decides nothing.** It dereferences `visible_store_codes` and holds no pin, market,
  `home_store` or evidence scan of its own. `since`/`until` are optional pass-throughs (~90 call
  sites predate them); a surface that knows its period should pass it, so "which stores can I see
  for September" reads as "where I was in September".
- **A MANAGER KEEPS THEIR ASSIGNED STORE** (`people_visibility = 'span'`): there the pin means "the
  store this person RUNS", a different fact, and the only record of it while the org tree is unwired
  (§14w). Measured: 4 of 17 span-tier logins — two store managers, two DMs — have never been
  scheduled at a store they manage, so evidence alone would take it from them. Assigned-OR-worked for
  a manager; worked, full stop, for an individual contributor. Keyed off the declared tier, never a
  role name (RULE TWO).
- **`employees.home_store` is still read by `reporting_employee_ids`, deliberately.** There it
  answers "who is ASSIGNED to my store", a fair reading of *"if any employee works under him"*. The
  owner's sentence rules it out as an answer to "whose PERFORMANCE may I see", which is the store
  dimension.
- **THE SALES REPORT'S ROWS ARE PER REP** — one per (store, salesperson, day), carrying that named
  person's revenue, GP and accessory revenue. So a store gate alone was never the owner's sentence:
  the moment a login resolved a shared store it read every colleague's money by name. `sales_report`
  now also gates the person through the existing one-homes (`_caller_rep_keys` +
  `payout_audience.mine_only`; `salesperson` was already in `REP_NAME_FIELDS`, so no new predicate),
  and **totals are summed after both filters** — summing before would print the company's revenue
  under a rep's name. Its gate also **fails closed**: it used to swallow every exception and fall
  through to unrestricted.
- **TWO SIBLINGS HAD NO ACCESS GATE OF ANY KIND** — found by asking what ELSE answers this question,
  the same way §14w found the ungated staffing heat map:
  - `GET /sales-report/detail` took **no `authorization` parameter at all**, and takes a store and a
    rep NAME off the query string: any signed-in caller could read any store's any rep's
    transactions, including customer name, phone (`mdn`) and device serial. That made the report's
    own gate decorative — the cell was hidden and the data behind it was one URL away. Now gated on
    store, on the requested rep (`requested_rep_is_mine`), and on the ROWS (`mine_only`), because a
    blank `salesperson=` asks for nothing and would otherwise return the whole cell.
  - `GET /sales-report/narrative` likewise took no caller, so a rep's banner totalled the company's
    revenue, activations and gross profit in sentences above a gated grid. "Display-only" is not a
    reason to skip a gate. `_sales_narrative` now takes the keyset and applies it to the same cells.
- **Proof:** `backend/harness_people_visibility.py` — **65 checks, DB-free, over the real endpoints**
  (`sales_report`, `sales_report_detail`, `sales_report_narrative`, `_sales_narrative`, plus §14w's
  schedule set). §J is the basis test: a fixture whose roster store is B-7 and whose only shift is at
  B-8 must resolve B-8, which is the only way to tell the two bases apart; §J6 pins that a pin plus a
  `home_store` plus no evidence resolves NOTHING (the 7 live logins) and that empty stays a deny-all;
  §J7 that the scan is window-bounded; §J8 that a cancelled shift is not evidence. §K8–K8e run the
  real sales report: the rep reaches both stores they worked, reads only their own rows at each, and
  their totals are their own. §L1–L7 reproduce the two ungated endpoints.
- **Lock:** `backend/harness_people_visibility_lock.py` — **47 checks, stdlib only.** Fails the build
  if `caller_scope` grows a basis of its own, if either ruling is copied, if the two directions stop
  sharing `WORKED_AT_SOURCES` or spell a table name themselves, if an empty evidence answer becomes
  the unrestricted `None`, if the people ruling re-derives the store dimension or reads `home_store`
  again, if a per-rep store-keyed report carries one dimension without the other, if the sales
  report's gate goes back to failing open, or if its totals move before the filters. Two planted
  controls verified: reverting the basis fails 4 checks; dropping the person half fails 10b. Same CI
  job, *People visibility*.
- **No migration.** The declaration this reads is the one migration 1058 (§14w) already wrote.

### 15.1 THE SEND RECORD — "has this finding reached this recipient, on this channel?"

**Owner decision 2026-10-04** (decision card, *"Fix it properly"*), after the store-visit alerts went
live: every alert recorded "sent" as soon as **any** channel delivered. A digest whose email went out
and whose WhatsApp failed was marked done and the WhatsApp was **never retried** — the tenant had
asked for both channels and got one, silently, forever. The reported instance was the store-visit
digest; the CLASS was every alert in the estate.

**ONE HOME:** `backend/app/modules/storeops/alert_log.py`. It is the only file that reads or writes
`storeops.alert_log`. Four separate implementations preceded it, each with its own idea of what
"already sent" means, and that is why the defect survived three rewrites:

| the old copy | what was wrong with it |
|---|---|
| `storeops/router._lateness_already_sent` / `_lateness_record_sent` | no channel on the row — the defect itself. **Deleted**, not wrapped |
| `storeops/router._expiry_already_sent` + its own insert | one row naming every contact as soon as ONE address worked, so a bounced contact was counted as told |
| `closing/_send_alert`'s own select/insert pair | same, plus one person's success suppressed the alert for **everybody else** on that finding |
| the four fan-out loops (follow-up, ePay, zero-sales, bill-pay declarations) | four copies of the same ladder; three sent on both channels, two on email only |

**What a row means now:** this scope's finding `ref_key` was CARRIED to `recipients` over `channel`.
Written only after that channel actually delivered — *an alert that reached nobody is not "already
alerted"* (the 2026-09-20 rule, kept and now exact). `channel` is **required**: `record_sent` raises
rather than write a row that does not say how it was carried. A row with no channel is either a
recorded SILENCE (nobody configured to tell) or a legacy row migration `1051` could not classify;
either way it satisfies no channel, which is the honest reading.

**Recipient matching** tolerates the pre-1051 rows written as a joined list, so switching to
per-recipient records re-alerts nobody already told.

Migration `1051_alert_log_channel.sql` — additive, idempotent, `-- REVERT:` noted. Adds
`storeops.alert_log.channel`, a CHECK limiting it to what the code can speak, the lookup index, and
a backfill setting `channel='email'` on every row with an email-shaped recipient (measured
read-only 2026-10-04: 709 rows, 706 email-shaped, 3 recorded silences).

### 15.2 DIGEST DELIVERY — carry it on each channel, record what each channel did

**ONE HOME:** `backend/app/modules/notify/digest_delivery.py`. `pending_by_channel` (PURE) decides
what each channel still owes a recipient; `deliver_recipient` is the ladder; `deliver_digests` is the
fan-out over `manager_digest.plan_digests` output. Every alert sweep in the estate dereferences it:
the lateness sweep, doc expiry, the manager follow-up digest, the ePay discrepancy digest, the
zero-sales digest, the bill-pay declaration digest, the two store-visit digests, and
`closing/_send_alert`.

Not parameterised: that a channel is spoken to only when it is **configured AND reachable**; that
the record is written per channel and only after that channel delivered; and that an **unconfigured**
channel is not a channel that was tried, so it records nothing and is offered again next run. A
caller supplies its subject/body builder and nothing else about delivery.

**"Already sent" means every reachable channel is square — never "no channel is configured."**
Collapsing those two let an estate with no credentials report its whole backlog as delivered; found
by driving the real sweeps on 2026-10-04 and pinned as §D8.

Proof: `backend/harness_alert_channel_record.py` — **66 checks, stdlib only, DB-free**, in the
carrier-vocab-guard job. §A row semantics · §B what each channel owes · §C the real
`deliver_recipient` over a stub client, including the retry carrying WhatsApp only · §D the fan-out
and the dry run · §E a record with no channel cannot be written · §F a recorded silence suppresses
nothing · §G migration `1051` tied to the code · §H eight locks, each with an armed control.


### 15.3 THE SEND RECORD'S REPORT — "which report did this send carry?" (owner 2026-10-05)

**Owner 2026-10-05:** *"in the notify app, the employees are sending themselves reports or
notification, in the notify history it should show which report was exported"*.

**The class, not the instance.** The instance was the export-bar send. The class is that nothing owned
the question, so each of the three send_log writers answered it differently: `/notify/send` +
`/notify/send-to-designated` stored the MACHINE key and the history rendered it raw although the
registry has held a human label for every report all along; **`/notify/send-file`** — the universal
path every page's "📤 Send" button uses, i.e. the one employees actually use to send themselves a
report — stored the literal `"(client-export)"` for EVERY report and DISCARDED the `title` the browser
had already sent; the no-login download row stored `"(download)"` on the same terms.

**ONE HOME:** `backend/app/modules/notify/send_identity.py` (PURE — no IO, no app import).
`report_label` resolves the name (a REGISTERED key is named by `report_registry.report_labels()`, so a
browser cannot introduce a second spelling of one report; otherwise the caller's title; never a
machine key dressed up as a name). `log_identity` returns the `report_key` + `report_label` columns of
one row, spread by **every** writer. `display_label` / `stamp_display` are the read side.

- Writers: `_dispatch` (`/notify/send`, `/send-to-designated`, every scheduled run), `send_file`
  (`/notify/send-file`), `_store_artifact`, and the download row in `GET /notify/dl/{token}`.
- Reader: `GET /notify/send-log` stamps every returned row, so a row written **before** mig `1057`
  still displays a name — the §13b.1 pattern (a display name is resolved by the read, never assumed to
  be stored). The Notify history page renders `report_label || report_key`.
- Migration `1057` (additive, idempotent) adds `report_label TEXT` to `notify.send_log` and
  `notify.send_artifact`. Degrades both ways: un-run → `_insert_log` strips the column and retries
  (`_OPTIONAL_LOG_COLUMNS`, one column at a time, so a history row is never lost) and the read still
  resolves the name; run → the name is stored **as sent**, so a report later renamed or unregistered
  reads back as the name it actually went out under.

Proof: `backend/harness_notify_send_identity.py` — **32 checks, stdlib only, DB-free**, CI job *Notify
history names the report sent* in `carrier-vocab-guard.yml`. §A the resolution · §B the reported
regression · §C the read side with no column · §D the writers · §E the degrade + the migration ·
**§F THE UN-WIRING LOCKS** — an AST scan of every send_log row literal in `notify/router.py` fails the
build if a send path goes back to naming the report itself (armed control: the pre-fix row is
flagged), `send_identity` is the only module that may define `report_label`, and the page must keep
rendering the resolved name.


### 14y. PAID HOURS HAVE ONE HOME, AND IT ANSWERS WITH THE BASIS (owner directive 2026-10-10, mig `1073`)

Owner: *"for the payroll menu need to turn off the payroll automatically being calculated as per
schedule, it is only based on actual hours clocked in unless a button is checked for each employee
separately against that employee name."*

**THE CLASS, not the instance.** Paid hours were decided by `actual_hours or scheduled_hours` in
**six** modules at once, over a column effectively nothing writes. MEASURED on production 2026-10-10:

| fact | measured |
| --- | --- |
| `storeops.shifts` rows in total | 7,740 |
| …carrying `actual_hours > 0` | **7** — and in all seven `actual == scheduled == 9` |
| anything that WRITES `shifts.actual_hours` | only `PATCH /storeops/shifts` (a DM editing one shift) |
| `storeops.timelog` punches | 3,663 rows, **3,555 with `hours > 0`** |
| …of those, auto-clocked-out by the kiosk sweep | **290**, and they are being PAID today |
| `storeops.manual_hours` corrections | **569 rows, which `GET /storeops/payroll` has never read** |

So the punch data **exists**; the measurement never reached the column payroll reads. Every one of
the six `or`s was locally reasonable, and collectively they meant payroll ran off the schedule and
told no reader which of the two they were looking at. The second half of the same class: a DM's
corrections in `manual_hours` never reached pay either.

**THE ONE HOME** — `backend/app/modules/storeops/payroll_hours_basis.py`. It answers *"which hours is
this employee paid for on this day, and on what BASIS"*, and it returns the hours **with** the basis,
never the number alone, so no caller can display a figure without saying where it came from.

| basis | pays? | a measurement? | what it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clocked` | yes | yes | a usable closed punch measured the day |
| `clocked_corrected` | yes | yes | a human corrected it (`manual_hours`, or a DM's `actual_hours` edit) |
| `clocked_reconciled` | yes | yes | two clock records disagreed and the org's declared rule chose (§14z) |
| `clocked_override` | yes | yes | a manager set the day by hand, with a reason, audited |
| `measured_zero` | yes (0.0) | yes | the day WAS measured and the answer is zero |
| `schedule_opt_in` | yes | **no** | nothing measured the day and this employee's tick box is on |
| `not_measured_unpaid` | no | no | nothing measured it and the box is off |
| `punch_unusable` | no | no | the punch is open, or the kiosk closed it — not evidence of anything |

`PAYING_BASES` is an **ALLOWLIST** on the `carrier_dollar_class.component_is_evidence` pattern (§66):
`NON_PAYING_BASES` is DERIVED from it, and `basis_pays_hours` of an unruled basis is **False**. A
basis added in 2027 cannot silently start paying the schedule again.

**THE PER-EMPLOYEE TICK BOX** is `storeops.employees.pay_from_schedule BOOLEAN`, deliberately
NULLABLE: NULL means *use the org default*, so a database that has not run 1073 behaves exactly as it
does today. The org default is `payroll_hours_basis_config.pay_from_schedule_default`, seeded TRUE.
A flip writes `storeops.payroll_change_log` with `entry_point = 'pay_from_schedule_change'`.

**NOTHING MOVES ON APPLY, AND THE MIGRATION PROVES IT WITH A ROW COUNT.** `resolve_shift_row`
reproduces `actual_hours or scheduled_hours` byte-for-byte under the shipped default, and
`resolve_config` makes two deliberate mode-dependent forcings so that applying 1070 moves no money:
`count_manual_hours` is forced FALSE in schedule-fallback mode (because `/storeops/payroll` has never
read those 569 rows, and folding them in WOULD move pay), and `count_auto_clockout_punches` is forced
TRUE unless an org has set it (because those 290 punches are paid today). Migration 1073 STEP 7 is a
read-only SELECT union that must all read `OK` — a receipt, not a promise.

**THE INTERLOCK.** `coverage` + `interlock` REFUSE to compute clocked-only hours when the measured
share of scheduled employee-days falls below `min_punch_coverage_pct` (default 85), and REPORT a data
defect instead of paying a shortfall. It trips on PARTIAL coverage, not only on zero — a period that
is 60% measured would otherwise look like a finished payroll that underpays four employees in ten.

**WHAT CLOCKED-ONLY WOULD COST, measured per tenant per month** — stated so switching it on is a
decision and not a surprise. See the PR for the table; the harness pins the shape.

Callers, all DEREFERENCING (no local `or` survives): `storeops/router.py` (`/payroll`,
`/payroll-by-store` — the money path), `storeops/salary_owed.py`, `storeops/salary_expense.py`
(whose three hours states `MEASURED_NONZERO` / `MEASURED_ZERO` / `NOT_MEASURED`, §14s, now DELEGATE
to `measurement_state`), `storeops/pto_accrual.py`, `account/coa.py` (the P&L wage line, via
`derive_wage_cells_with_basis`), `commcalc/labour_coverage.py`, `hr/router.py`.

Proof: `backend/harness_payroll_hours_basis.py` — sections A–I, **R the regression** (the `or` paying
the schedule while a punch measured the day), **O the owner ruling** (§14z), **P + Q** (§14y.1 below),
Z an armed negative control. Lock: `backend/harness_payroll_hours_basis_lock.py`, EIGHT axes, CI job
in `carrier-vocab-guard.yml`.

- **DRILL-DOWN (§CORE-17.3x, batch 24):** the basis is now a REPORT'S PROVENANCE as well as its
  reason. `storeops/payroll_hours_drilldown.py` keys a basis→relation map on THIS module's own basis
  constants (`BASIS_RELATIONS`, with `PAYING_BASES` / `MEASURED_BASES` dereferenced by identity), so
  `/storeops/payroll` and `/storeops/reports` can tell a reader, per person, whether the hours above
  came out of the time clock, out of the schedule, or out of nothing at all — and the build fails if
  a basis added here has no provenance there. `NOT_MEASURED_UNPAID` and `PUNCH_UNUSABLE` are the
  reason words a drill row carries, with reader-facing sentences in
  `core/report_drilldown.UNMEASURED_REASONS`; this module's own longer explanations stay here. This
  module is also a `module_graph` fact of its own now (`payroll_hours_basis`), with its eleven
  callers named by hand.


#### 14y.1 THE ONE HOME ANSWERED, BUT FOUR CALLERS ASKED IT WITH NOTHING (owner ruling 2026-10-12, mig `1076`)

Owner, verbatim: *"Payroll from clack in should be from Oct 4 th onwards which would be the new
cycle"*.

**THE DEFECT, MEASURED on live house data 2026-10-12 — not a hypothesis.**
`resolve_shift_row(shift, cfg, employee_row)` with **no `cell`** can answer only from the shift row,
i.e. from `shifts.actual_hours` — the dead column §14y exists because of (7 of 7,740 rows). FOUR pay
paths called it exactly that way, and **none** consulted `interlock`, so nothing stopped the result:

| caller | what it prices | call site before the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `account/coa.py` | the P&L wage line (`derive_wage_cells_with_basis` → `wages_by_store`) | `:655` `resolve_shift_row(s, cfg, emp)` |
| `commcalc/labour_coverage.py` | the labour-coverage report's paid-hours basis | `:225` same |
| `storeops/pto_accrual.py` | hours worked, which is what PTO accrues on | `:115` same |
| `hr/router.py` | HR total compensation | `:263` same |

The house org is LIVE on `hours_basis_mode = 'clocked_only'` with `pay_from_schedule_default = false`,
so every such row resolved `not_measured_unpaid` = **ZERO**. A Run Calculation would have booked:

| month | shifts | today | clocked-only, evidence-free |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2026-06 | 555 | $75,837.00 | **$0.00** |
| 2026-07 | 640 | $88,128.00 | **$0.00** |
| 2026-08 | 613 | $85,389.00 | **$0.00** |
| 2026-09 | 603 | $81,132.02 | **$0.00** |
| 2026-10 | 341 | $44,247.00 | **$0.00** |
| **total** | 2,752 | **$374,733.02** | **$0.00** |

The punches were present throughout (`storeops.timelog`: Aug 3,781.6 h, Sep 4,724.0 h). **The class**
is not "the P&L reads a dead column"; it is **a pay-path caller could reach the one home WITHOUT the
evidence the one home needs, and publish the answer anyway** — because there was no shared way to GET
that evidence and no gate that noticed its absence.

**THE ONE PUNCH READ** — `backend/app/modules/storeops/payroll_evidence.py`. The only place on the
pay path that fetches `storeops.timelog` + `storeops.manual_hours` for a period. It used to live
inside `clock_variance_api._load`, which is **why** the other four had no way to get the rows;
`_load` now dereferences it, so there is ONE path and not two. Org-scoped, half-open `[lo, hi)`,
never raises — a failed read is REPORTED in `blockers` and REFUSES the period, because "we could not
look" and "nobody clocked" must never print the same.

| function | answers |
| --- | --- |
| `read_pay_evidence(client, org, lo, hi)` | the period's punches + manual-hours rows, `(rows, blockers)`. `PUNCH_SELECT` is the column list, spelled once |
| `period_evidence(…, shifts)` | the `build_evidence` index **plus** `cfg`, `coverage`, `interlock`, `blockers`, `refused`, `reason` — a caller cannot get the evidence without the verdict |
| `paid_hours_rows(res, shifts)` | ONE ROW PER SHIFT ROW, each carrying its share of its DAY's paid hours |
| `refusal(res)` | the one sentence to report when the period may not be paid from |
| `day_after(d)` | an INCLUSIVE period end → the half-open boundary, so no surface reads a month one day differently |
| `EvidenceRefused` | raised by a producer whose whole output is money (`coa.wages_by_store`), so a refusal is louder than an empty dict |

★ **WHY A BARE `cell` IS NOT THE FIX** ★ — the trap, caught by §P4 while this was being written.
`resolve_shift_row(…, cell)` returns **0.0** for a day a punch measured, on purpose: the punch's
hours are counted off the PUNCH row at the store the person actually stood in. The Payroll screen can
do that because it iterates `shifts` AND `timelog`. **These four iterate shifts only**, so handing
them a cell merely swaps `not_measured_unpaid` 0.0 for `clocked` 0.0 and the wage line still books
$0.00. So `paid_hours_rows` resolves the **DAY once** and ALLOCATES it back across that day's shift
rows, weighted by each row's own pre-evidence contribution — exact for a single-row day, the same
proportions a multi-store day always had, and the day's total is the one home's answer. A borrowed
day is placed at the **punch's** store (`clock_variance_api._store_of`'s rule, now stated once). A
punch on a day no shift covers is **NAMED** in `unscheduled_punch_days`, never folded in: widening
four reports' day universe is a separate question with its own answer.

**THE EFFECTIVE-FROM FLOOR** — `storeops.payroll_hours_basis_config.clocked_basis_effective_from`
(date, NULLABLE, mig `1076`; the house org seeded `2026-10-04`). On and after it the org's
`hours_basis_mode` applies as declared; **strictly before it** the day resolves exactly as
`schedule_fallback` would, so recomputing a closed month restates nothing. **NULL = NO FLOOR**, which
is every other org, so the column changes nobody on apply.

| function (the one home) | answers |
| --- | --- |
| `effective_from(cfg)` | the ISO floor, or None |
| `day_is_before_floor(day, cfg)` | strictly before? False with no floor, and False for an UNDATED day |
| `config_for_day(cfg, day)` | **THE one place the boundary is decided.** Every resolver routes through it |

**THE FLOOR RESTORES THE WHOLE SWITCH, not a third of it** — and this is the trap the first cut fell
into. Forcing only `hours_basis_mode` back to `schedule_fallback` leaves `pay_from_schedule_default
= false` (the live house value), and schedule-fallback + no opt-in + nothing measured is **still
$0.00** — so Jun–Sep stayed at zero through the one door the floor had left open. `_SWITCH_FIELDS`
names all three (`hours_basis_mode`, `pay_from_schedule_default`, `count_manual_hours`) and the
pre-floor config drops them to the HOUSE DEFAULT; the per-employee tick box is the fourth expression
of the same switch and is **not consulted** on a pre-floor day. Every OTHER field (the tolerances,
the thresholds, the auto-clockout policy, the feed) is the org's own on both sides.

**THE DATE TRAVELS IN THE EVIDENCE, so a caller cannot forget it.** `build_evidence` writes the key's
own date into each cell as `"day"`, so `resolve_day(cell, cfg)` keeps its exact existing signature and
still knows the day. An explicit `day=` wins, for the one shape that hand-builds a cell
(`resolve_shift_row`, which reads it off the row's own `shift_date`). `resolve_day`,
`resolve_shift_row`, `punch_counts_for_pay` and `measurement_state` all take it; `coverage` and
`interlock` **count only days ON OR AFTER the floor** and report the rest as
`pre_effective_from_days` — without that, June 2026 (no punches by construction) would hold the
measured share below the threshold forever and refuse a period the floor had already excused.

**HOW A REFUSAL IS REPORTED, per surface** (CLAUDE.md: a defect in live data is REPORTED, never
hidden behind a figure):

| surface | on a refusal |
| --- | --- |
| P&L wage line | `wages_by_store` raises `EvidenceRefused`; **no cell is booked**, and the `wages` line's `note` carries the interlock's own sentence |
| labour coverage | `hours_interlock` on the result, and the banner's note leads with *"PAID HOURS ARE NOT SAFE TO COMPUTE FOR THIS PERIOD"* |
| PTO accrual · payroll expenses · payroll tax | `hours_interlock` / `hours_refusal` / `hours_blockers` on `_pto_gather` / `_payex_gather`'s meta |
| HR total comp | `out["hours_basis"]`, `hours_basis_warning`, and an `X-Hours-Basis-Refused` header |

**LOCKED** — `harness_payroll_hours_basis_lock.py` §H fails the build if a pay path stops passing
evidence (H1/H2, matched on the imported ALIAS so a same-named local cannot pass for it), stops
consulting the interlock (H3; two pure modules have it consulted at their NAMED call site), grows a
second punch read (H4 — and every remaining `timelog` reader is excused **in writing**, including
`marketing/router.py`'s event payroll, which is the one real sibling and a named FOLLOW-UP), loses
the business date a resolver needs (H5), or spells the floor's date as a literal instead of reading
the config row (H6, RULE TWO). Proof: §P (the defect at period grain, and the bare-cell trap) and §Q
(the floor) in `harness_payroll_hours_basis.py`, 143 checks with a 5-way armed negative control.

**THE coa.py MOVEMENT GUARDS**, which pin every function in the P&L module byte-identical to the
branch point, are satisfied through ONE shared sanction —
`harnesslib.COA_PAID_HOURS_EVIDENCE_SANCTION` (`wages_by_store`, `derive_wage_cells`,
`derive_wage_cells_with_basis`) — read by `harness_device_payable.py`,
`harness_device_purchases.py` and `harness_finance_sync_in_async.py` rather than spelled three
times. **Every store and company RESOLVER and ATTRIBUTION function in `coa.py` is still pinned
byte-identical**: nothing here changes WHICH store or WHICH company money books to, only HOW MANY
HOURS a day is worth, which is `payroll_hours_basis`'s decision and never `coa`'s.


### 14z. THE B2B CLOCK REPORT — a claim, then a PAY SOURCE; the ask, the gate, the run (owner directive 2026-10-10, mig `1073`)

Owner: *"also need to import the clock in clock out report from b2b and match with what we have in
metrics pro and asses the difference and ask the DM on every monday and require the correction to be
done before the payroll is run … block them from logging in unless they fix it by tuesday so the
payroll can be run on Wednesday. this will be picked from the emails for each store like other
reports."*

Owner ruling, same day, which changes the feed's STATUS: *"if they are clocking out at earlier time
from the elevate then it means they are spending time in store to make extra hours and they ahve no
more work to do, use that as the time used to create payroll and mention on the report why you are
doing so."* **The clock report is therefore a PAY SOURCE, not only a check.**

**INGEST — the existing email sweep, not a second one.** `upload_type` `clock_punch` →
`commcalc/column_mapping` layout → `_ingest_mapped_df` → `storeops.raw_clock_punch`. The feed-shape
post-step is `storeops/clock_feed.normalize`, beside the footer-row / row-period / blank-key
post-steps already there. `commcalc/column_mapping.TABLE_SCHEMA` is the ONE home for the fact that
this landing lives in `storeops`, not `commcalc` — `_table_has_column` / `_known_columns`
dereference it rather than probing the wrong schema and reporting every column absent.

**THE ELEVEN MEASURED SHAPE TRAPS** (the real export, `A1:M47`, 45 punch rows for 2026-10-09; each
one silently corrupts the import or the comparison if ignored, and `clock_feed.py`'s docstring carries
them in full): the trailer row is a **CHECKSUM** (`Duration = '249:10'` = the 249.17h row sum, so a
file that does not tie is REJECTED, naming both numbers); `Store` is an ADDRESS resolved through
`account/store_identity.build_store_resolver` (28/28 on the real file) and never matched here;
`Salesperson` is `"Last, First"` and sometimes `"Last, First, M"` and carries accents; the stamps are
LOCAL WALL CLOCK with no zone, converted through the store's own `ZoneInfo` and REPORTED when none
resolves; `Duration Decimal` is TRUNCATED so hours come from the timestamps; `Type` is an ALLOWLIST;
the back-office login is not a store shift (14 rows / 12.48h across twelve stores, as a CONFIG array
— RULE TWO); the key is (employee, date, **punch**) because one person has two stores on the sample
day; a zero-duration row is a `measured_zero`; B2B's `Division`/`Region`/`District` are feed METADATA
that may never resolve a recipient; and the business date comes from `Clock In`, **never** from the
filename — stamping rows from an upload label is the defect that once read carrier commission 28×
high, so `claim_agrees` reports a mismatch and the rows keep their own dates.

**THE FEED NEVER WRITES `storeops.timelog` OR `shifts.actual_hours`.** It lands in its own table as
evidence we keep, and every row lands — payable or not — with `excluded` naming why, because a
landing that dropped the back-office rows could not explain where 12.48 hours went.

**THE OWNER'S RULING, AS A DECLARED CHOICE** (`payroll_hours_basis.reconcile_clock_records`, config
`clock_source_rule`; no `min()` in a handler and no feed name in code):

| rule | 2026-10-09, 16 measured pairs | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| today (our kiosk alone) | **146.42 h · $2,156.45** | `ours_only` reproduces this exactly |
| `earlier_clock_out` — the ruling read literally | **143.63 h · $2,113.60** | pays **MORE than today on 3 of 16 rows** |
| `narrowest_window` — **HOUSE DEFAULT** | **142.98 h · $2,102.63** | never pays more than today on any row |

The literal reading takes the earlier-clocking-out record's WHOLE duration, which also takes its
earlier clock-**in** — so on Khan Amir, Mohammed Abdullah and Seelam Sunethri it pays more, the
opposite of the ruling's intent. The house default pays the window the two records **agree** on
(later clock-in → earlier clock-out). The literal reading is one config value away, and both carry
their own explaining sentence. **The resolved hours travel WITH the reason string** — the owner asked
for *"mention on the report why you are doing so"*, so the reason is part of the return value, not a
label a screen adds later. Under `clock_agreement_tolerance_hours` (default 0.034h, two minutes) the
two records are treated as AGREEING and ours stands, so a rounding difference never shaves a minute
off somebody's pay. **A DM may override any row**, with a reason, and the override OUT-RANKS the rule
(`clock_variance_correction.override_hours`, basis `clocked_override`, logged to
`payroll_change_log` under `entry_point = 'clock_variance_override'`; the schema refuses an override
with no reason and no name).

**THE VARIANCE BOARD** — `storeops/clock_variance.py`. Nine kinds, each with its own sentence:
`missing_punch`, `extra_punch`, `hours_differ`, `employee_unmatched`, `store_unmatched`,
`login_unlinked`, `no_clock_feed`, `store_mismatch`, `auto_clockout`. **An UNRULED kind BLOCKS** —
the safe direction for *"is it safe to run payroll"* is the opposite of §14y's, and the two facts live
in two modules so neither can be read off the other. A day whose file never arrived is its own
blocking kind, never an implicit zero: with no rows from a store every other test is trivially
silent. A `store_mismatch` is raised although the hours tie, because the labour cost would land on
the wrong store's P&L; an `auto_clockout` is raised **even when the numbers agree**, because today's
default PAYS those punches — the fact is read from `payroll_hours_basis.auto_closed_punches`,
separately from whether policy pays it.

**WHO IS ASKED** — `storeops/org_chain.chain_for` (§48.7) and nothing else; B2B's own district column
may never resolve a person. `recipient_ladder` goes DM → the nearest manager above the district →
`unowned`, REPORTED. The ladder exists because the coverage demands it: **6 of 29 Cellfonz stores and
0 of 20 Luxelink stores resolve a DM** (2026-10-10), so a DM-keyed ask alone would reach eight stores
of fifty-one and look as though it had asked everybody. Delivery is `storeops/alert_log.py` (the only
reader/writer of `storeops.alert_log`; `channel` required) + `notify/digest_delivery.py` (the only
channel ladder) — no bespoke sender.

**THE ASK, END TO END.** `clock_variance.ask_plan` (who) → `ask_digests` (the fan-out shape the
ladder eats, ONE item per **store** so a store that turns blocking mid-week is asked about rather
than deduped away by a recipient-only key) → `build_ask_digest` (subject/html/text, the WhatsApp
text carrying the same facts in the same order) → `digest_delivery.deliver_digests` under scope
`clock_variance_weekly_ask`. **`ASK_WHY` puts the owner's ruling in the email body**, because
*"mention on the report why you are doing so"* is not satisfied by a correction request that does not
say why the earlier Elevate clock-out is being paid. **No pay figure is ever in the ask** — it goes to
district managers and money is market-manager-and-above (§14 pay visibility, mig 434), and an email
is past every RBAC check once it is sent. `POST /storeops/payroll/clock-variance-ask` previews by
default (`dry_run=True`); `POST …/clock-variance-ask/run-due` is the `NOTIFY_RUN_SECRET`-guarded
pg_cron entrypoint, **one hourly job for every tenant** — each org's `ask_weekday` is compared against
ITS OWN business weekday via `_biz_tz_for`, so no weekday is spelled in the cron line and a
behind-UTC store is not asked on Sunday evening. The job is registered by
`/mnt/project-files/payroll-clocked-hours/TURN_ON_monday_clock_ask_2026-10-10.sql`, and registering
it sends nothing while `variance_ask_enabled` is false.

**THE SCREENS.** `frontend/src/app/(platform)/storeops/payroll/clock-variances/page.tsx` is the
correction board and the gate's escape — standard filters + `ReportExportBar` (no exporter of its
own), both numbers and OUR BASIS with its sentence on every row, a store with nothing wrong shown
saying so, and a Record button the reason gates. The tick box is a column beside the NAME on
HR → Employees & Pay, saving ITSELF through `lib/employeeRowSlices.buildPayFromScheduleWrite` (a
one-click write, deliberately NOT a row-save slice — a yes/no that decides whether somebody is paid
must not depend on remembering to press Save, §19.35). `/storeops/payroll` gains an `Hours basis
(why)` column, read from `hours_basis` / `hours_basis_reason` which `GET /storeops/payroll` now
carries per row from `_shift_actual_contribution_with_basis` + `basis_reason` — additive and purely
explanatory, with `hours_basis_mixed` saying "mixed" out loud rather than naming a winner for a
fortnight that mixed punched and scheduled days. Lock: axis B3–B6 of
`harness_payroll_hours_basis_lock.py`.

**THE CONFINEMENT HAS ONE HOME** — `frontend/src/lib/setup-gate.ts::confineRedirect`. The setup
wizard (§39) was the first gate of this shape and this is the second, so the rule was FACTORED OUT
rather than copied: `setupRedirect` is now an adapter onto it, `clockGateConfinement` shapes the
clock gate's reply, and the account pages are always open in both. Proof:
`frontend/prove_confinement.mjs` (35 checks, armed) — it also reads the shipped layout, because a
rule no gate calls is not a rule, and asserts the gate can never sign anybody out.

**THE GATE IS A CONFINEMENT, NOT A REFUSED SIGN-IN.** This is the one place the package does not do
what the owner literally said, and the reason is ★ NO LOCKOUT ★ (§22): a person who cannot sign in
cannot fix what blocks them, so a refused sign-in would make the Wednesday payroll impossible rather
than protected. `gate_decision` alerts on ANY weekday as soon as something is uncorrected, and from
the gate weekday confines the session to the correction board — signing in always succeeds.
Mon / Tue / Wed are the house defaults of `ask_weekday` / `gate_weekday` / `run_weekday`; a tenant
that runs payroll on Friday changes three numbers.

**THE RUN GATE REFUSES AND NAMES WHAT BLOCKS IT** — a refusal that does not say which rows is a wall,
not a gate. TWO preflight refusals: uncorrected variances (only when the org switched the gate on),
and **employees this run would price at NOTHING**. That second one fires either way, because
**13 of 46 active hourly house employees have no `pay_rate` at all** (E252, E257–E267, E282, measured
2026-10-10) and ten of them are the reps a 3 October runbook was meant to set to $17.00/h — still
NULL, so it was never applied. Pricing them at zero produces a payroll that looks complete and pays
nobody; that is reported, never fixed in code.

**EVERYTHING SHIPS OFF.** `clock_feed_enabled`, `variance_ask_enabled`, `login_gate_enabled`,
`payroll_run_gate_enabled` and `clock_feed_is_pay_source` are all FALSE, no mailbox rule is seeded
and no `pg_cron` job is registered. The ask endpoint additionally previews by default, so a cron line
pasted early describes what it would send and sends nothing.

Proof: `backend/harness_clock_feed.py` (the 45 real rows as a fixture; every number re-derived, not
asserted), `backend/harness_clock_variance.py` (all nine kinds, the ladder, the rendered ask and its
money-free body, ★ NO LOCKOUT ★, the two run-gate refusals) and
`backend/harness_clock_variance_api.py` (the shipped endpoints over an in-memory client: off reads as
OFF and not as clean, the board's period IS payroll's period, a gate that cannot look does not gate,
an override with no reason is refused, and the ask holds no mail call or send record of its own). Lineage: `clock_punch_report` in `data_lineage_registry.py` +
`925_data_lineage_seed.sql`, four edges (ingest · derive · gate · **pay**), data-date column
`business_date` — never `arrived_at`, since the file arrives at 08:00 for the PREVIOUS day.
Cross-ref §14s (the three hours states), §14y, §13d/§64 (the store resolver), §48.7 (the org walk),
§22 (no lockout), §66 (the allowlist pattern), §16–§18.

Its per-scope snapshots now carry real per-line drill `detail` (§4e).
- `GET /commcalc/peer-comparison?period=&metric=&bands=` — stores grouped into BILL-PAYMENT traffic bands, then ranked inside their band on boxes / AAL / family plan % / accessories per box, with the band median, the band best and the gap to each; and `GET /commcalc/targets/{period}/action-plan`, which now carries the SAME verdict per store as a `peer_gap` item (`peer_meta` reports a comparison that could not run, and the lagging stores it could not carry). Both callers read ONE assembly, `router._peer_comparison_payload`, so the screen and the plan cannot coach different stores (§59, §59.7).
- `GET /commcalc/spiff-impact?period=&spiff=&bands=&markets=` — ONE carrier pay type per store: its dollars and paid units, its share of the P&L line those dollars ACTUALLY book to (§58’s classification, so the figures tie to the P&L’s carrier lines by construction), the store’s net profit WITH it against WITHOUT it from the stored per-store snapshot (§4’s `analysis.pl_totals` via `statement_filter.store_snapshots`), and the paid units per 100 boxes ranked inside the store’s own §59 traffic band through `peer_comparison.with_extra_metric` — so “behind” keeps ONE definition. The pay-type dropdown is derived from the month’s own statement, never a list in code, and a report that chose its own subject SAYS so (`selection_basis`). READ-ONLY (§60).
- `GET /commcalc/accessory-target-plan/{period}?mode=&value=&basis=&stores=&markets=` — ONE company accessory goal, split per store on that store's own accessories-per-box over the last two months against the boxes it is projected to sell: the two history months in their own columns, MTD, the projected month-end (§5's `_targets_trending_by_code`), the target in force (mig `006`), the proportionate target and the extension it represents. READ-ONLY. `POST /commcalc/accessory-target-plan/{period}/assign` writes `accessories_monthly` on the selected stores through `_require_target_edit` — the same permission + store-span gate as `PUT /targets/{period}` — recomputing the plan server-side and moving no other column (§61).
- `GET /commcalc/product-mix?period=&markets=&bands=` — per STORE and per REP: boxes, accessory $ per box, port-ins per box, and the device mix banded by what the CUSTOMER paid (free / budget / mid / premium, money cuts stated on every payload and overridable per call), plus the most-sold models with their average customer price and how many went out free. A rep is flagged only when BOTH signals are below the median of the reps in view, and the measured Pearson correlation between the mix and each outcome ships with the payload so the owner's claim can be falsified rather than assumed. The lagging-store ACTION PLAN is §59's own band, median, gap, verdict and sentence through `_peer_comparison_payload` + `with_extra_metric` on the SAME rows (no second feed read, no second definition of behind), with this report's flagged reps attached to each store item. The carrier's own port-in rate per store rides BESIDE ours through `kpi_failing.port_in_rate` — the column migration 002 has carried since 2026 and nothing ever displayed. READ-ONLY (§62).
- `GET /commcalc/device-line-reimbursement?period=&store=` — one row per DEVICE the distributor ledger claims a reimbursement for in the month: what it claimed, what the handset cost (`asset_ledger.owed_to_vip`), what the store charged for it (`selling_price`, `null` when the ledger records no price — never `$0.00`), who the carrier paid the line against, and what the carrier's own PER-LINE feed paid for that device at THIS store and at any OTHER store, those stores named. Four verdicts: paid · **paid_to_other_store** · not_paid · not_measured. Classifies nothing (§58 `carrier_dollar_class` + the org's own `carrier_component_lines` routing, injected), resolves no store itself (§64 `coa.store_resolver`), re-derives no coverage (§19.54) and states no lag rule (§27 `period_window`, read symmetrically). READ-ONLY, no writer, no migration (§65).
- `GET /commcalc/mdf-entitlement-coverage?store=` — one row per store-month inside a store's DECLARED entitlement window (`commission_org_config.mdf_entitlement_config`, mig `1068`): `received` · **`missing`** (the month's payment run demonstrably arrived for other stores and this store is not in it) · **`unconfirmed_missing`** (no payment of this kind reached us for ANY store that month — OUR feed, counted apart and never netted into the gaps) · `not_due` (the month has not finished) · `not_measured` (`entitlement_window_not_declared` / `no_entitlement_configured` / `store_identity_ambiguous`). Takes NO period: the question is the whole window. Declares nothing itself — the payment types are the org's own `payment_categories` through §57, the store key is §64's `coa.store_resolver` (+ `ambiguous_store_keys`), the calendar is `feed_period.month_state`, the verdict vocabulary is `pay_data_quality`'s. READ-ONLY, no writer, no flag (§68). **DRILL-DOWN §CORE-17.3v:** all five tiles open, counts AND money — each count ties over the store-months its own verdict put there, money that ARRIVED names the carrier's two payment relations and nothing else (a receipt is a measurement; a declaration had no part in it), and what an ABSENT month was worth names PER ROW whether the rate was DECLARED in `commission_org_config` or OBSERVED from that store's own payments — two grains on one row in one unit separated by PROVENANCE ALONE (§CORE-17.3n). A store with no declared first month is never counted as missing; its observed absence is its own figure. A gap nothing can price is counted as a gap, shown without a figure, and the priced total comes back explicitly NOT TIED rather than letting a short sum look complete. Server-folded. Declaration `commcalc/entitlement_coverage_drilldown.py` (`entitlement_drilldowns`), proof `harness_batch22_drilldown.py` §E.
- `GET /commcalc/device-line-reimbursement?period=&store=` — one row per DEVICE the distributor ledger claims a reimbursement for in the month: what it claimed, what the handset cost (`asset_ledger.owed_to_vip`), what the store charged for it (`selling_price`, `null` when the ledger records no price — never `$0.00`), who the carrier paid the line against, and what the carrier's own PER-LINE feed paid for that device at THIS store and at any OTHER store, those stores named. Four verdicts: paid · **paid_to_other_store** · not_paid · not_measured. Classifies nothing (§58 `carrier_dollar_class` + the org's own `carrier_component_lines` routing, injected), resolves no store itself (§64 `coa.store_resolver`), re-derives no coverage (§19.54) and states no lag rule (§27 `period_window`, read symmetrically). READ-ONLY, no writer, no migration (§65). Its per-device verdict is also what the COST side dereferences to place a handset's cost on the activating store (§70) — one reconciliation, two readers, never two derivations.
- `GET /closing/cash-variance?date_from=&date_to=&markets=&stores=&reps=&verdict=` — shortage and overage AFTER management recon: what management received (`envelope_count` first, else `cash_pickup.actual_picked_amount`), the cash envelope the rep declared (`daily_closing.t_cash`) and the POS cash the close gate recorded (`closing_attempt.b2b_cash`), per store-day-rep — each figure carried WITH its basis, and a pair whose bases differ reported as NOT MEASURABLE rather than subtracted. Plus `by_store` / `by_employee` rollups off ONE summariser, the four trend kinds, and `blockers` naming what cannot be measured and why. Band + trend threshold are per-org config (mig `1070`); the verdict is `deposit_recon.status_for`; the POS figure is read, never re-derived from the feed. READ-ONLY, no writer (§72).
- `POST /closing/pickup/open-count` · `POST /closing/billpay-pickup/open-count` — open a SEALED envelope and record the count, **or CORRECT a count already entered** (owner 2026-10-10). Optional `note` for why. Every changed field appends to `commcalc.cash_count_revision` through the one writer, and the reply carries `corrections` / `history_recorded` / `history_detail` so a trail that could not be written is stated rather than implied (§73.5). `POST /closing/pickup` and `POST /closing/envelope-count` return the same two keys.
- `GET /account/config` · `PUT /account/config` — … plus `device_cost_store_basis` (mig 1069): WHICH store carries a handset's cost, `stocking` (today's behaviour, and the default for NULL) or `activating`. MONEY-TOUCHING and per-store: the company total does not move, each store's gross profit restates, so a recompute follows a declaration. Validated against `device_cogs.DEVICE_COST_STORE_BASES`; the read side returns the resolved basis and `moves_cost_to_activating_store` (§70).
- `GET /commcalc/commission-leg-store-trend?period=&months=&market=&store=` — **the month-of-life (M1..M12) commission rungs PER STORE with the months side by side** (owner ask 2026-10-15): one row per store, one column per month, each cell carrying 1st-month / M2–M12 / Unsplit and that store's own rung ladder, plus `worst_rung` naming the rung that fell hardest between the first and last COMPLETE month — so a store shrinking NOW (M1 falling) is distinguishable from one echoing a cohort lost months ago (M1 flat, M4–M6 falling). It CALLS `router._commission_leg_trend_compute` with its store axis on and PIVOTS the result through the pure `commcalc/commission_leg_store_trend.py` — the same read, the same carrier classification (§58/§66), the same store identity (§64), the same rung convention (§4a.2) — so Σ(per-store) == the company figure to the cent (§A of the lock). An unfinished month is flagged `partial` and excluded from every delta; money matching no store is its own named row; `ties` states per month whether the displayed total equals the company series. READ-ONLY, no writer, no table, **no migration** (§COMMCALC-12).
- `GET /commcalc/month-focus/{period}?plays=` — this month's DECLARED focus (`commcalc.month_focus`, mig `1065`): the headline, the pay type named as driving its spiffs, the temporary spiffs on the table with their status, the weekly check-ins done, and — computed, never stored — what the month still owes plus the plays its own measured numbers support. `plays=0` skips the sales read, for the two login surfaces. `PUT /commcalc/month-focus/{period}` declares or amends it (market manager or above, `month_focus.may_declare` → `core.scope.is_market_or_wider`; a partial save cannot blank the month, and check-ins are never writable from the body). `POST /commcalc/month-focus/{period}/checkin` confirms the CURRENT check-in day, computed server-side and idempotent, so a confirmation cannot be back-dated. Pays nothing; writes only `commcalc.month_focus` (§63).
- `GET /closing/metric-catalog` — **what this business declares at the end of a day, and what a unit is worth**: every category with its `value_kind`, `declared_by`, `unit_price`, `in_revenue` and `storage`, plus `revenue_keys` / `employee_keys` and the vocabularies themselves. THE one answer; the closing form and the incentive-rule editor read it instead of listing categories. `GET /closing/declared/{date}?store_code=` folds both physical stores into one store-day (plus `by_employee`, `store_revenue`, `employee_revenue`); `PUT /closing/metric-lines` saves the money-bearing and per-employee lines (full replace per store-day, and a line naming an undeclared category is REFUSED, not stored) — `closing/metric_catalog.py`, mig `1072` (§76).
- `GET /commcalc/incentive-rules` — the tenant's daily-incentive rules **with the catalog they may point at**, the three rule shapes, the split bases, the qualifier scopes and the comparisons. `PUT /commcalc/incentive-rules` upserts one (money-posture gated by `_require_commission_admin`; **refuses** a rule whose qualifier or payout names an undeclared category); `DELETE /commcalc/incentive-rules/{id}` switches it OFF rather than destroying its audit trail. `GET /commcalc/daily-incentive/{date}?store_code=` COMPUTES one store-day — per-employee lines, `by_employee` totals, `top_earner`, `unallocated`, and a `rules[]` why-trail carrying each qualifier verdict. **Computes only; nothing is persisted and nobody is paid by calling it** — `commcalc/daily_incentive.py`, mig `1072` (§76.4).
- `GET /commcalc/targets/{period}/axis` — **what is targetable for this tenant**: the four built-in sales categories, then every category the admin declared on Count Fields (§76), each with the label they typed, its unit, where its target physically lives (`column` / `derived` / `line`) and whether its achievement comes from the sales feed or from a declaration. THE one list; nine screens and modules used to keep their own. `PUT /commcalc/targets/{period}/lines` saves the declared half into `commcalc.target_line` — gated on the SAME permission and store span as `PUT /targets/{period}`, and it REFUSES a built-in category key because two homes for one number is the divergence the design removes — `commcalc/targets_engine.py`, mig `1074` (§COMMCALC-02).
- `GET /commcalc/targets/{period}/calendar?grain=week&week_starts=0` — the existing schedule-weighted calendar, plus a `windows` block giving the owner's per-day / per-week / per-month target. A window is a SUM OVER THE CALENDAR already in the response (`targets_engine.grain_windows`), at full precision, never a second calculation — so the weeks always add up to the month. Additive: omitting `grain` returns exactly what it always did (§COMMCALC-02.4).
- `GET /commcalc/targets/{period}/backward?goal=&metric_key=&scope=&rep=` — **"what do I need to reach X?"**: `need`, `per_day`, `per_week`, per category or for one. The GOAL is a parameter, not the stored target, so an arbitrary level can be asked. Computed from the same `compute_scope` the calendar uses, so the two cannot disagree; with no open days left `per_day` is `null` rather than the need restated as a daily figure (§COMMCALC-02.5).
- *(no endpoint added)* — §CORE-03 changes nothing a caller can see: the credential columns were ALREADY stripped from every API read (`router._SOURCE_SECRETS`, each `_*_public_cfg`, `google_reviews.public_config`, `billing._pc_out`) and that stays the first line of defence. What changed is what a DATABASE dump holds. `portal_secret.protection_state()` is the one thing a screen may newly ask: `'protected'` once a key is configured, `'unprotected'` without one — so a page taking a portal password can SAY which, rather than let an operator assume (§CORE-03.5).
- `POST /hr/onboarding/encrypt-existing` (§CORE-04) — unchanged to its caller, but it no longer holds the loop: it calls `encryption_backfill.backfill_intake_sensitive`, which `run_all()` also runs, so the `ENCRYPTION_BACKFILL_ON_BOOT=1` route now covers this family too. Before that it was the ONLY path, which is how two bank routing numbers stayed readable: nothing was wrong with the code, nobody had pressed the button.
- *(no endpoint added)* — §CORE-09 adds no route: `POST /core/users/set-password` (`core/router.py::admin_set_password`) already set a SPECIFIC admin-chosen password, validated server-side by `validate_password`, toggling `app_users.must_reset_password` and audited as `password_admin_set`, gated on `_can_edit_setting(caller, "security")`. What changed is the number of SURFACES that offer it — one (`/admin/security`) became three (`+ /admin/roles` 👥 Assign people, `+ /hr/employee-password`), all rendering the one card `frontend/src/components/AssignPasswordCard.tsx`; `GET /core/security-settings` is the `can_edit` read each of them shows the form on (§CORE-09.3).
- *(no endpoint added)* — §CORE-10 adds no route and no table: both gates are CI, not product. They run as the workflow jobs **The branch was cut from its base (no re-proposed commits, no lost CI job)** (`.github/workflows/branch-base-guard.yml` → `scripts/check_branch_base.py`) and **A guard that goes blind fails CI (derived subject sets)** (`.github/workflows/security.yml` → `backend/harness_subject_set_lock.py`). The first is the only workflow here triggered by `pull_request_target`, deliberately, and it never checks out or runs PR code (§CORE-10.3).
- *(no endpoint added)* — §CORE-11 adds no route and no table either. It is a component fix plus a CI gate: `frontend/src/components/ReportShell.tsx` grows ONE `bodyCell(c, r)` home for what a body cell shows (both row paths on it), `crm/reports/page.tsx` dereferences the same rule for its own bespoke table, and the gate runs as the workflow step **Run the column-render lock** (`carrier-vocab-guard.yml` → `backend/harness_column_render_lock.py`). Three already-shipped columns began rendering with no change of their own (§CORE-11.1).
- *(no endpoint added)* — §CORE-12 adds no route, no table and no migration: the seven existing authority writers (`POST /core/users/assign`, `/users/bulk-assign`, `/users/deactivate`, `POST|PUT /core/roles`, `POST /core/revoke-super-admin`, and `purge_app_user` behind `POST /core/employees/purge` and the StoreOps employee delete/merge) each ask ONE new pure home, `core/self_lockout.py`, whether the write would remove the caller's own `security` authority in the tenant it affects, and refuse it with a 400 if so. `_can_edit_setting` MOVED into that home and `core/router.py` dereferences it. A write that names somebody else's row, or a caller who keeps the authority, is byte-identical to before (§CORE-12).
- *(no endpoint added)* — §CORE-13 adds no route, no table and no migration. It is a CI gate plus a house convention: `backend/harness_data_api_grant_guard.py`, run as the `security.yml` job **A new table is granted by the migration that creates it (Data API)**, fails the build when a migration newer than its cutoff creates a relation the Data API serves without granting it to `service_role` in the same file. Nothing about the running system changes (§CORE-13).
- `GET|PUT /storevisit/alerts/config` · `GET /storevisit/visits/{id}/todos` · `POST /storevisit/alerts/run-due` (secret) · `POST /storevisit/alerts/run-now` (dry run by default) — store-visit follow-through alerts, the accessory notification and the draft PO (§47.16).

| `POST /pos/inventory/standard` — put standard (qty-tracked) stock on hand at ONE store: `{product_id, store_code, qty, mode?: add|set, qty_on_order?, qty_reserved?, bin_location?}`. `mode` DECLARES which fact is being recorded — `add` (default) is a receipt and adds to on hand, `set` is a count and replaces it; the writer never guesses from whether a row happened to exist. The first single-row write path this table has ever had (before it, qty arrived only via the CSV count importer or an inter-store transfer). Refuses a serial-tracked product — those land through `POST /pos/inventory/serial`, behind the duplicate-IMEI guard (§11b). Gated `pos_inventory_adjust`, org-scoped, store-span checked; answers `before` AND `after` so a double entry is visible | `pos.router.receive_inventory_standard` → `pos/stock_landing.plan` | §POS-01 |
| `GET /pos/held-sale?store_code=&register_number=` · `PUT /pos/held-sale` · `DELETE /pos/held-sale` — the cart left on this register, suspend it, drop it. Restored VERBATIM (the agreed price, the override it overrode, the discount and the serial), with `held_at` so the screen can say how old the prices are; `held_by` is the CALLER's employee id, never a body field. An EMPTY cart with no customer CLEARS the hold instead of storing a row, so an idle register leaves nothing behind. All three org-scoped and store-span checked; all three answer `available: false` rather than erroring before mig `1088` | `pos.router.get_held_sale` / `put_held_sale` / `delete_held_sale` → `pos/held_sale.py` | §POS-01 |
| `GET /pos/sales/{sale_id}/receipt` — THE receipt of one sale, rendered server-side. Query `layout` / `paper_width_mm` / `destination` are FOR THIS PRINT ONLY (§POS-03, §POS-04): nothing is stored, and both are resolved through `pos/sale_receipt.print_choice`, so a request cannot reach a layout or a width a stored setting could not. Answers `html` (print it as given), `layout`, `layout_note` (set when the stored choice is not what will actually print, e.g. the POS layout asked for with no POS declared — the fallback is said out loud, never silent), `email` (`to`, `to_source`, `valid`, `from_name`, `subject`) `layout_source` / `paper_source` (request | store | org — which of the three won), `paper_width_mm`, `layout_options`, `paper_options` (both DERIVED from the renderer's own `LAYOUTS` / `PAPER_PX`, never a second list) and `printer_label` (what the store declared it prints on); `destination` / `destination_source` / `destination_options` / `helper_url` and `escpos_base64` — the printer's own bytes, present ONLY when this copy is going to the printer (§POS-04); `remit` / `remit_source` / `remit_available` and the MASKED `remit_routing_masked` / `remit_account_masked`, so the screen can say which account the customer will be told to pay into before anybody prints it (§POS-06 — query `remit=1` is the tick, off on every receipt otherwise, and it cannot turn on unless both numbers are declared); and `company_name`. The rendered `html` carries the customer's own address under their name when the template shows the customer and their record holds one (§POS-07 — `customer_bill_to`, the same block an imported receipt of that POS bills to). Refuses a sale with no stored `pos.sales.receipt` snapshot rather than re-pricing it from the sale row. Org-scoped | `pos.router.get_sale_receipt` → `pos/sale_receipt.print_choice` → `pos/sale_receipt.html` (× `pos_config_effective`, `core/tenant_identity`) | §POS-02, §POS-03 |
| `POST /pos/sales/{sale_id}/email-receipt` — email that receipt, in the body AND as a PDF attachment (§POS-08: `attached`, `attachment_name`, `attachment_error` say whether the file rode along; a file that could not be built does not hold up the mail, which goes with the body alone and says so). Body `{to?, layout?, paper_width_mm?}`: blank `to` = the address the GET already showed (the customer's own); the print choice rides with it so the emailed copy is the copy that was handed over (§POS-03). 400 with no address and 400 on a broken one (refused before the provider sees it), 503 when no email provider is configured, 502 on a provider refusal — each a plain sentence, never a 500. Sends with `from_name` = the tenant's company name, so the customer sees the business, not the platform. Answers what it sent and to whom. Org-scoped | `pos.router.email_sale_receipt` → `pos/sale_receipt.email_view` → `notify/channels/email_resend.send_email(from_name=…)` | §POS-02 |

## 18. Cross-reference: by METRIC / KPI

| metric | basis | where it is decided |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Paid hours, and the BASIS they rest on** | a usable closed punch, else a human correction, else the two clock records under the org's declared rule, else the schedule when that employee's tick box is on — and NEVER `actual_hours or scheduled_hours` | `storeops/payroll_hours_basis.resolve_day` / `resolve_shift_row` — THE one home, returning hours WITH the basis so no caller can show one without the other (§14y). Lock: `harness_payroll_hours_basis_lock.py` |
| **Punch coverage %**, and THE INTERLOCK | measured employee-days ÷ scheduled employee-days for the period, **counting only days on or after this org's `clocked_basis_effective_from`** | `payroll_hours_basis.coverage` / `interlock` — below `min_punch_coverage_pct` (default 85) a clocked-only period is REFUSED and reported as a data defect, never paid as a shortfall. Pre-floor days are excluded and counted in `pre_effective_from_days`, else June 2026 (no punches by construction) would refuse a period forever (§14y, §14y.1) |
| **When does the clocked-only basis START for this org?** | one config date, `payroll_hours_basis_config.clocked_basis_effective_from` (NULL = no floor) | `payroll_hours_basis.effective_from` / `day_is_before_floor` / `config_for_day` — THE one place the boundary is decided; every resolver routes through it and no date is spelled in code (§14y.1, mig `1076`) |
| **The period's punches and corrections, for a pay path** | `storeops.timelog` + `storeops.manual_hours` over `[lo, hi)`, org-scoped | `storeops/payroll_evidence.read_pay_evidence` — the ONE read; `period_evidence` returns it WITH `coverage` + `interlock`, so no caller can get the evidence without the verdict on it (§14y.1) |
| **Clock variance** (ours vs the B2B report), per store-employee-day | both numbers, our basis, the classified kind, and whether it blocks | `storeops/clock_variance.compare` — nine kinds, an unruled kind BLOCKS, a day with no file is its own kind (§14z) |
| **Reconciled paid hours**, and the sentence saying why | the window the two clock records agree on (house default), or the ruling read literally, or ours alone — declared per org | `payroll_hours_basis.reconcile_clock_records`. Measured 2026-10-09 across 16 pairs: today 146.42h/$2,156.45 · literal 143.63h/$2,113.60 · house default 142.98h/$2,102.63 (§14z) |
| **Employees a payroll run would price at $0.00** | an active hourly employee with no `pay_rate` | `clock_variance.employees_without_rate` → `payroll_run_gate`, which REFUSES and names them. Measured 2026-10-10: 13 of 46 house hourly employees (§14z) |
