### 29.11 A REFUSED CLOSING LEFT NO TRACE — the submit audit trail only started once every check had passed (owner bug report 2026-10-02)

Owner, verbatim: *"also abid did the daily closing for the 117 bunrsoide ave as a dm whoc is now working as a
sales rep int eh store - we cannot see the daily closing which was submitted, , also he did it again today it
is stikll not shwoing , 2 things first investigate and fix amd second dont let duplicate entries"*.

**LIVE EVIDENCE FIRST (read-only, before a line was written).** 117 E Burnside Ave is `B-117`
(`commcalc.store_mapping`, market NYC, sfid `001U100000Ga3kfIAB`; the store master knows it too, with a NULL
address, which is the house norm there).

| where a closing can land | what was there for B-117 |
|---|---|
| `commcalc.daily_closing` | rows on 09-28 (Kashif), 09-29 and 09-30 (Rohit) — **none on 10-01 or 10-02** |
| `commcalc.closing_attempt` (the submit audit trail) | **nothing from that submitter at ANY store since 09-28** |
| `commcalc.daily_closing_verification` | no `B-117` row — it did not land on the DM-verify screen either |

The submitter is `abid.akhter@cellfonzrus.us` = app_user `full_name` **"Rana"**, employee **E012** (`storeops.employees.name`
"Rana", home store B-509, role Market Manager), login role `district_manager`. Every closing he has ever filed is
under "Rana", so a search for "Abid" finds none of them — worth knowing, and NOT the bug.

**Three candidate causes were ruled out by measurement, not by reading code.** (1) *Scope* — `caller_scope` is a
strict no-op platform-wide: `_rbac_enabled` reads `app_config.rbac_enabled` and that table does not exist, so
every keyset is `None` and nothing is being filtered from anyone. (2) *Market resolution* — B-117 carries market
NYC in BOTH vocabularies, so no market pick drops it. (3) *A twin store identity* (the §511 luxelink shape) —
B-117 has exactly one mapping row and no alias. The closing was **not hidden. It was REFUSED and nothing was kept.**

**ROOT CAUSE — THE CLASS.** `closing/router.create_row` runs every validation BEFORE the first write, and
`closing_attempt` — the table that exists so management can see what a rep tried — was written only once they all
passed (`_log_attempt`, after the close gate). So ALL EIGHT refusal paths stored nothing at all:

| refusal | status | stored before this fix |
|---|---|---|
| the close date could not be read | 400 | nothing |
| the submitter may not use that name / has no name on file | 403 | nothing |
| the envelope photo would not save | 502 | nothing |
| **cash declared with no envelope photo** (`require_photo_if_cash` is **true org-wide here**, since 2026-08-11) | 400 | nothing |
| already submitted for the day / more than one row exists / the index race | 409 | nothing |
| an expense line, or an expense with no description | 400 | nothing |
| no store or no employee name on the submit | — | the row was WRITTEN, with no dedup key and no index protection |

A rep says "I submitted it", management sees nothing, and there is no evidence either way — for any store, any
rep, any tenant. "Burnside's closing is missing" is the instance; **"a refused closing leaves no trace" is the
class**, and it is what made this unanswerable rather than merely wrong.

**DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate).** Searched this index and the code for an existing mechanism before building:
`commcalc.closing_attempt` (mig 103) IS the submit audit trail and `GET /closing/attempts` IS its reader, so both
are **REUSED** — the refusal is three additive columns on that table and three additive keys on that response, not
a sibling table, endpoint or screen. On duplicates the owner asked to prevent: **migration 502 already prevents
them**, in the app and as a partial unique index, and the live data agrees — **1,799 closings since 2026-08-01,
zero duplicate groups, zero NULL dedup keys, zero blank store codes or names**. So no second guard was built. Two
real gaps in the existing one were closed instead (below). `closing/closer_pick` (§29.7) keeps the one rule for
WHOSE name a closing carries; it now returns a declared refusal code instead of raising its own 403.

**THE FIX — one home per fact, every caller dereferencing it.**
- `closing/submit_refusal.py` (pure) — **THE refusal registry**: code → (HTTP status, the sentence the submitter
  reads). `Refusal`, `audit_row`, and `is_real_try` — the ONE rule for "does this row count as a try".
- `closing/router._refuse` — **the single raise site**. Records the refusal in `commcalc.closing_attempt` with the
  reason, then raises the registry's error. `create_row` raises no `HTTPException` of its own any more.
- `closing/dedup_key.py` (pure) — **THE dedup key**. It had been spelled twice and had already drifted: Python
  folded a STRIPPED employee name, mig 502's SQL folded the raw one, so a name stored with a stray space produced
  two keys for one person and the index could not see the duplicate it exists to stop. `SQL_EXPR` is the same
  formula in SQL and the migration must contain it verbatim.
- **A refusal is never a try.** `_real_attempt_count` dereferences `is_real_try`, so two failed photo uploads no
  longer carry a rep to the auto-accepting third try without recounting. That one is money-affecting.
- **Identity is required.** A submit with no store or no employee name is refused (`identity_missing`) instead of
  being written with a NULL dedup key, outside the index.
- **The released window is closed.** Mig 502's index was `where dedup_key is not null and released_at is null`; a
  release→resubmit UPDATEs the same row, so that second half protected nothing and only left a window for two
  concurrent inserts. Mig 1037 drops it, after asserting no key is held twice.
- **Management Review shows it** (`closing/management/page.tsx`): "⚠ N submits turned away — cash declared with no
  envelope photo", each try row says `turned away`, and a store-day that was only ever refused reads **"never
  counted"** instead of "0 attempts" and always qualifies for `only_review=true`.

**#349's REFUSAL JOINED THE REGISTRY, it did not sit beside it (merge 2026-10-02).** `§19.39` gave a store a
daily-closing SOURCE and refused a rep's submit on a feed-derived store with its own
`raise HTTPException(409, closing_source.refusal_message(...))` — a ninth refusal path storing nothing, the exact
class this section fixes. It now goes through `_refuse` as `closing_source_not_rep` and is audited like the other
eight. Its SENTENCE stays owned by `closing_source.refusal_message` (it names the store and where to change it):
`submit_refusal.DELEGATED_MESSAGE` declares the code delegated, the registry **dereferences** that module for the
status and the store-less fallback, and `_refuse(..., message=)` carries the store-specific rendering through —
so the words exist in ONE place. A non-delegated code cannot have its words overridden. Checked by **§H9** (7
checks), which fails the build if the registry ever retypes those words or the router stops passing them.

**MIGRATION 1037 — SURFACED FOR OWNER APPROVAL, NOT APPLIED.** Additive columns + the index widening + a
dedup-key recompute that refuses rather than merging anything ambiguous. No amount column is read or written.

**Lock: `backend/harness_closing_submit_refusal.py` — 115 checks, DB-free.** §A–C pure (registry complete, no
storage name in submitter copy, the whitespace divergence gone), §D the REGRESSION (each refusal path through the
real `create_row`: no closing stored AND exactly one audited reason — before the fix every one of those found
zero rows), §E the money point, §F the Management Review view, §G degrade pre-migration, **§H the WIRING LOCKS
that fail the build**: no submit validation may raise `HTTPException` directly, every code raised must be
declared and every declared code must be raised, the router may spell no dedup key, the try counter must
dereference `_real_attempt_count`, the migration's SQL must be `dedup_key.SQL_EXPR` verbatim, and the screen must
have words for every code, and **§H9** that a delegated sentence keeps one home. Verified to BITE:
re-inlining one `raise HTTPException` turns ten checks red; §H9b caught a literal copy of #349's sentence in a
code comment during the merge itself.
`harness_closing_closer_pick.py` B5 was updated to pin the new shape (still a 403 carrying the reason).

**OPEN — reported, not fixed.** Which of the nine refusals Abid actually hit cannot be known: the refusals that
predate this fix left nothing behind, which is the defect. `require_photo_if_cash` being on org-wide makes the
photo gate the likeliest. From the next refusal on, the answer is on the Management Review screen.


### 29.12 A STORE-DAY SOMEBODY STARTED AND DID NOT FINISH READ AS A STORE-DAY NOBODY WORKED (owner bug report 2026-10-04)

Owner, verbatim: *"If the stops the reform entering the 1st closing and tells them to correct it, the rep tries
again but stops at 2 or even after the 1st attempt, the system should say to correct the entries like it does but
also save the last entered data in thr system so the system is not blank at any time like what happened with
Abid"*

**LIVE EVIDENCE FIRST (read-only, before a line was written).** B-117 / `2026-10-01`, employee **"Rana"**:

| what was there | value |
|---|---|
| `commcalc.closing_attempt` rows | **two, two seconds apart, both `blocked`** (attempt_no 1 and 2) |
| entered cash vs POS | **$2,826.00** vs $2,631.83 → **$194.17 OVER** (`cash_dir` 'over') |
| entered credit vs POS | **$270.00** vs $146.59 → **$123.41 OVER** (`credit_dir` 'over') |
| also entered | `t_zelle` $225.00 |
| `commcalc.daily_closing` for that store-day | **none** |

The 3-try close gate blocks tries 1–2 and auto-accepts the 3rd (§29.11 counts the tries). He stopped at two. Oct 2
and Oct 3 ARE stored and DO render — verified by driving the real `closing_rollup` (B-117, 2 days, $3,863 cash) and
`closing_summary`. Only Oct 1 is absent, and it is absent because it was never written.

**THE MONEY WAS NEVER LOST.** `commcalc.closing_attempt` has carried every entered tender, the POS figure it was
compared against and the variance direction since mig `103`. What was wrong was that every reader took **"no
closing row" to mean "nobody submitted"**, when it can equally mean **"somebody submitted and the gate sent them
back"** — opposite operational facts (one needs a nag, the other holds real declared cash and needs a correction),
indistinguishable platform-wide. On the DM-verify screen the store did not appear **at all**: the card loop is keyed
on who clocked in or sold (`if not worked: continue`), and a district manager covering the floor is not on that
roster. That is the whole of "we cannot see it".

**DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate).** Searched the index and the code for an existing mechanism before building.
`commcalc.closing_attempt` + `GET /closing/attempts` (§29.11) already store and report what a rep tried → **REUSED**;
the entry is not stored a second time. `harness_intake_fakes.FakeDB` is the house's shared in-memory client →
**REUSED** rather than a fourth fake client. The localStorage draft already in `ClosingSubmitForm` → **EXTENDED**,
not replaced: it survives the camera reloading the PWA and nothing else, so the server resume sits beside it and
only offers itself when there is no local draft.

**NO PROVISIONAL CLOSING ROW — and that is the design, not a shortcut.** Writing the blocked entry into
`commcalc.daily_closing` would have been the obvious reading of the owner's words and is the wrong fix twice over:
a second home for "what did the rep declare", beside the attempt trail that already holds it (the sibling
derivation the index rules forbid), and known-wrong money in front of all **51** readers of that table. Asked on
2026-10-04 whether an un-corrected entry should count in cash totals, the owner chose **"not until corrected"**.
Because an unfinished day writes no closing row, that is now **structural** rather than a rule somebody must
remember — every figure in `by_store` / `by_rep` / `totals` is byte-identical to before this package.

**ONE FACT, ONE HOME.** `closing/unfinished_day.py` (pure; no I/O, no client, no framework) is the only place that
decides what an unfinished store-day is: `state_for` → one of `not_started` / `awaiting_correction` / `turned_away`
/ `finished`, `describe` (state + label + the entered money + the gate's own recorded variance), `resume_entry`,
`is_finished` (the predicate a money reader honours), `summarize`. `TENDER_COLUMNS` and `ENTRY_COLUMNS` are the one
declaration of which columns are money and which are the rest of the form. The try/refusal rule is
`submit_refusal.is_real_try`, dereferenced — never a second copy.

**WIRED (the callers that had each assumed it independently):**

- `_closing_summary_for_date` — the no-closing card now says WHY, and a store with tries but nobody on the roster
  **gets a card at all** (the Burnside shape).
- `closing_rollup` — `unfinished` + `unfinished_counts`, reported BESIDE the money and never inside it.
- `_run_closing_missing_alerts` — stops telling a rep who did submit that nobody did; the day is still open, so the
  alert still fires, it just says the true thing. No amount reaches that copy (it goes to the store too).
- `GET /closing/resume` + the submit form — the rep comes back to a filled-in form. **It answers with the rep's own
  numbers only**: no POS figure, no variance, no direction. The gate tells a rep the direction and never the
  amount, and that rule holds here; `harness_closing_unfinished_day.py` §H2 fails the build if it stops holding.
- `_log_attempt` — keeps the accessory sale, the three counts, the remarks, the envelope photo (mig `1052`) and the
  configured-tender jsonb, so try three is not retyping. Retyping everything is a reason to stop at two.

**ONE STORE-DAY, ONE KEY — found by VERIFYING mig 1052 against live data, 2026-10-04.** Joining
`commcalc.closing_attempt` to `commcalc.daily_closing` on the raw `store_code` is wrong, and was wrong in
production: seven house store-days had an ACCEPTED closing under `B-1800` and the attempt rows for the same
submit, to the second, under `1800GreatNeckRd`. The owner-run `store_identity_merge` runbook (§13) re-keyed the
closing rows onto the canonical code and left the audit trail on the spelling the picker had sent. So the first
cut of this package reported **15** unfinished store-days where **8** are real: four in August and three in
September were FINISHED days, each shown to a manager as a correction to chase on money already accepted and
banked. **The class** is that a store's identity is spelled differently in different tables — the roster carries
canonical codes, the closings and the tries carry whatever the submit sent — and §13 already names that class.
**The fix dereferences the platform's ONE answer**: `closing/unfinished_day.store_key(resolve, store_code)` over
`account.coa.store_resolver` (exact address → alias → raw-is-a-code → unambiguous leading street number), built
once per request by `closing/router._store_key_resolver` and used by all four readers. It also closes the
case-folding trap that made `b-1115` a phantom store. A store the resolver cannot place keeps its own raw code,
so an unknown store groups with itself and never with another; no resolver at all degrades to the raw code
rather than failing the report. **Measured after the fix, live:** August 0, September 0, October 1 (B-117 /
2026-10-01), and the seven genuine July days unchanged — and `GET /closing/resume` now answers `finished` from
EITHER spelling of a closed day instead of offering the rep a day that is already closed.

**MIGRATION 1052 — APPLIED 2026-10-04 (owner ran it).** Verified live: all six resume columns present on
`commcalc.closing_attempt` and the `closing_attempt_store_day` index in place. Attempt rows written BEFORE it
carry NULL in the six columns, so a resume of an older try hands back the tenders only — the degrade path (§G),
not a fabricated zero. Original terms, unchanged: Six additive resume columns on
`commcalc.closing_attempt` + one `(org_id, close_date, store_code)` index, `-- REVERT:` notes, a `DO` block that
aborts unless all six landed. **It touches `commcalc.daily_closing` not at all and reads or writes no money
column.** Unapplied, `_log_attempt` degrades to the mig-103 column set and still records every try (§G).

**Lock: `backend/harness_closing_unfinished_day.py` — 104 checks, DB-free**, CI job `closing-unfinished-day-lock`.
§A–C pure, §D the regression (the live Burnside numbers through the real code: `awaiting_correction`, $2,826
entered, $194.17 over — before this package those inputs produced no state at all), §E the money point, §F the real
resume endpoint, §G degrade pre-mig-1052, **§H the wiring locks that fail the build**: a blocked submit may never
write a provisional closing row; the rep-facing endpoint may never reveal the POS figure or the variance; no caller
may spell a state string or re-derive the rule; the screen must word every state and invent none; the migration must
add every column the logger writes and touch no money column. **Verified to BITE:** inserting a provisional
`daily_closing` row in the blocked branch turns §H1a red. §29.11's own `H4b` allow-list names these four readers
explicitly and proves each one only asks this registry, so the two locks hold each other from both sides.
**§I the store-day key**: the two live spellings collapse to one key and two different stores never do; the
regression drives the REAL `/closing/resume` over the REAL `account.coa.store_resolver` (fixtures carrying the
measured B-1800 / `1800 Great Neck Rd` shape) and proves a day closed under the canonical code reads as finished
from the twin spelling; and a build-failing lock that the maps grouping attempt rows by store-day are BUILT from
that key and nothing else. **Verified to BITE:** regrouping `_att_by_store` on the raw `store_code` turns §I5b
red. `_by_sd` was renamed `_att_by_sd` because a dozen unrelated envelope and deposit maps in the same file share
that suffix and a name-based lock could not have told them apart.

**OPEN — reported, not fixed.** B-117 / 2026-10-01 is **still not closed**, and this package does not close it: the
row needs Abid's third submit, and the **$194.17 cash overage is a real discrepancy** somebody should look at rather
than have the platform absorb. Three harnesses are red on `main` and unchanged by this PR —
`harness_closing_submissions` (legacy-row tender fallback), `harness_closing_hardening` (B1e/B1f oracle) and
`harness_closing_reports_span_scope` (7B) — confirmed by stashing these changes and re-running.


### 29.13 TWO REPS CLOSED ONE STORE-DAY AND NOTHING NOTICED (owner bug report 2026-10-13)

Owner, verbatim: *"2 reps did the closing for Oct 10 for nostrand ave , for luxelink , by rana Bilal and Moza Ali ,
one the system should not have taken duplicate entries - it should have flagged the second person that they cannot
enter , research ,move the entries for ran a Bilal to 531 utica"*

**LIVE EVIDENCE FIRST (read-only, Supabase REST, before a line was written).**

| what was there | value |
|---|---|
| `commcalc.daily_closing`, Luxelink, store `Nostrand`, `2026-10-10` | **THREE accepted closings**: Rana Bilal **$230.00** (23:03:21), moza ali **$140.00** (23:04:02), Dixit Chauhan **$0.00** (submitted 2026-10-13 16:35) |
| the store-day's declared cash | **$370.00** against a POS day of **$140.00** |
| `commcalc.daily_sales_feed`, `2026-10-10` | `3560 Nostrand Avenue` cash $140.00, salesperson **"Ali, Moaz"**; `531 Utica Ave` cash $447.29 + External $12.00, salesperson **"Bilal, rana"** |
| store `Utica`, `2026-10-10` | **no closing at all** |
| every other Nostrand store-day 2026-09-05 → 2026-10-12 | **exactly one closing** |
| house-wide store-days holding more than one closing | **54**, of which **16 hold two DIFFERENT reps**, at 3–4 a month, across **both** tenants |

So the POS feed independently says who was where: moza ali's row is right, Rana Bilal's belongs to Utica, and the
platform noticed neither the duplicate nor the misfiling.

**THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE.** The platform had exactly ONE answer to *"is this store-day already closed?"* and it
was **"only if this same REP closed it"** — carried in the dedup key (`closing/dedup_key`, `(org, store, employee,
day)`), in the partial unique index built from it (`daily_closing_one_active_per_rep_day`, mig 502 / 1037), and in
`create_row`'s pre-insert guard. A second **person** was therefore a duplicate to none of them, for any store, rep or
tenant, and the day's cash doubled into `closing_summary`, the cash recon, the envelope report and the deposit chain
in silence. It is also why a closing filed at the **wrong store** goes unnoticed: `_gate_row` compares a rep against
the POS day for the store they picked, and Rana Bilal had no POS rows at Nostrand, so the gate had nothing to compare
and passed him as `recon_pending`.

**THE HOME: `backend/app/modules/closing/closing_grain.py`** (PURE, DB-free) — `GRAINS` /
`normalize` / `resolve` / `grain_map` / `blocks_other_reps` / `key_omits_employee` / `refusal_detail` /
`refusal_suffix`. Per-org config row with a per-store override and a house default of **`store_day`** — one closing
for the whole store-day. RULE TWO: no tenant or store name in code; a tenant that genuinely banks an envelope per rep
declares `rep_day` and behaves exactly as the platform did before.

**THE EXISTING MECHANISM IS EXTENDED, NOT DUPLICATED (duplicate-check gate).** `dedup_key.for_row` now takes the
grain and, at `store_day`, leaves the employee out of the key — so the unique index mig 502 already built on that
column refuses the second rep's row **with no new index and no new column**. The two spellings cannot collide (three
`|` segments vs four). Migration 1080 creates the config table and **recomputes no stored key**: rewriting history to
the store-day spelling would collide on the 16 two-rep store-days above, and mig 1037's §3 guard would correctly
abort. History keeps the key it was written with.

**THE CALLERS, ALL OF THEM.** `closing/router.create_row` (the submit) refuses with the new
`store_day_already_closed` code through the one `_refuse` site, naming who holds the day; `closing/router.
_ingest_dataframe` (the closing-sheet upload — the **second** writer of `daily_closing`, which set no dedup key at
all and could do by file exactly what the form did by hand) asks the same registry from one config read and
**skips + reports** (`skipped_already_closed`) rather than inserting a second declaration or merging two people's
money into a figure nobody declared. The derive sweep (`_derive_closing_day`) is **excused and the excuse is
locked**: it is already store-day grained and never overwrites a human's row (`kept_manual`).

**THE CORRECTION PATH.** A manager's release now lets the RIGHT person redo a store-day the WRONG person closed: the
resubmit UPDATEs that one row, carries the new name onto it, re-locks it and audits the correction — never a second
insert. The same rep resubmitting without a release is refused exactly as before.

**ENDPOINTS:** `GET /closing/grain-config` (the org default, every override, the effective answer for one store) and
`PUT /closing/grain-config` (org default, one store, or several in one call through
`_closing_grain_write_one`, the ONE writer) — gated to the same `closing` settings area as the closing-source and
tender config.

**LOCK:** `backend/harness_closing_store_day_grain.py`, **82 checks**, wired into
`carrier-vocab-guard.yml` as its own job (`closing-store-day-grain-lock`) and named in the paths filter. It drives the
REAL submit endpoint and the REAL sheet ingest against the shared `harness_intake_fakes.FakeDB`, reproduces the
Nostrand 2026-10-10 shape as its regression, and fails the build if `create_row` or the sheet upload stops
dereferencing the registry, if the key is composed without the grain, if a second copy of the vocabulary appears
(`flag_registry`'s own older `grain` vocabulary is excluded BY NAME and held apart by §H3c), if migration 1080 starts
rewriting stored keys, or if the Management Review screen has no words for the new refusal. Five negative controls.
`harness_closing_submit_refusal.py` §C was updated to name the grain explicitly (120 passed / 0 failed) — its old
assertion *"two reps at one store on one day are two keys, by design"* **was** the defect.

**OPEN — reported, not fixed.**
- Moving Rana Bilal's row to `Utica` puts his declared **$230.00** against Utica's POS cash of **$447.29** — a
  **$217.29 shortage** that nobody has looked at, because while the row sat at Nostrand the close gate had no POS
  figure for him there. The repair runbook states this and adjusts nothing.
- **A rep with no POS activity at the store they are closing is still not flagged.** `_b2b_day`'s `by_rep` already
  holds the answer and the gate already reads it; turning it into a hard refusal would turn away a legitimate rep on a
  no-sale shift or a late feed, so the honest shape is a non-blocking management flag. Not built here.
- The Store Setup screen has no control for the grain yet — the endpoints above are the whole surface, so switching a
  tenant to `rep_day` is an API call today.


### 29.14 A MANAGER MOVES A CLOSING TO THE RIGHT STORE (owner 2026-10-13)

Owner, verbatim: *"also the manager should be able to go in and move the wrong closing tor trh cioreect store"* — asked
immediately after he ran a hand-written SQL runbook to move one misfiled closing (`Nostrand` → `531 Utica`,
2026-10-10, Rana Bilal, the §29.13 incident) and watched its safety block abort with
`ABORT: Utica already has 1 closing(s) for 2026-10-10. Moving this one there would make a duplicate.` — because the day
had meanwhile been re-entered by hand at the destination. **Both halves of that are the requirement:** the move belongs
on the screen, and it must REFUSE rather than create the duplicate it exists to undo.

**DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate).** Searched §29.1–29.13 (every closing surface), §16–18 for an existing
"change a closing's store" path, §64 (`account/store_identity` — the ONE home for *which store is this address*) and
§29.11 (`dedup_key`). **Nothing moves a closing between stores today**: `PUT /closing/row/{id}` exists but is the
amounts editor and sets no store column, `POST /row/{id}/release` unlocks a row for a corrected resubmit at the SAME
store, and the store-identity merge (§64) retires a store CODE for everybody rather than re-filing one row. So this is
a new mechanism, and it REUSES rather than re-derives: the permission gate is `_can_mgmt_review(_caller_perms(...))`
(the release gate, DMs excluded), the destination identity comes from the same `commcalc.store_mapping` roster
`create_row` resolves a submit through, "is the destination already closed" is `closing/closing_grain` (§29.13), and
the new key is `closing/dedup_key.for_row` (§29.11). No second index, no second resolver, no second dedup spelling.

**THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE.** "Rana Bilal's 2026-10-10 closing is at the wrong store" is the instance. The general
fact that was missing: **a closing's store was immutable to the platform, while a rep picking the wrong store is an
ordinary mistake** — so every repair was hand-written SQL, per incident, by whoever was asked. And a closing's store
is not carried by the closing alone: **fifteen tables in the schema carry both `close_date` and `store_code`**, so SQL
that moves one and forgets the rest leaves a *half-moved store-day*, which is worse than an unmoved one.

**THE HOME: `backend/app/modules/closing/closing_refile.py`** (PURE, DB-free). `TABLES` is the registry of every table
carrying both columns, each with a ruling and its reason:

| Disposition | Tables | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **FOLLOWS** (re-keyed with the closing) | `cash_pickup`, `billpay_pickup`, `closing_expense`, `closing_metric_line`, `envelope_count`, `envelope_withdrawal`, `cash_count_revision` | they are part of THIS rep's store-day — the cash the DM collected, the bill-pay cash, what was paid out of the envelope, the declared counts, the count, the corrections. Leaving them behind IS the half-move |
| **STAYS** | `closing_attempt`, `raw_epay_daily_tx` | the attempt log records what was ATTEMPTED and he really did attempt it at the old store (the §64 posture); the ePay feed is the carrier's, keyed to where the transactions happened, and we never rewrite it |
| **BLOCKS** (refuse, 409, nothing written) | `bank_deposit`, `closing_deposit_adjustment`, `closing_mgmt_review` | money is already settled against the store-day; re-filing underneath a banked figure would restate it with nothing saying so. The refusal names the table, the count and what to clear |
| **REVIEW** (reported, never moved, never deleted) | `daily_closing_verification`, `daily_closing_verification_audit` | a DM verified the store-day against the closings it then held; after the move it covers a different set, so a human has to re-check it. 715 live rows makes blocking unusable and silence dishonest |

`plan()` is the whole decision and is pure: the subject row, the destination, the grain, the destination's existing
closings and the satellite counts go in; `{ok, refusals, moves, review, stays, closing_patch}` comes out. **`ok: false`
means nothing may be written** — which is the behaviour the runbook's abort had, kept.

**REFUSES** (409, nothing changed): the destination store-day is already closed (`closing_grain.blocks_other_reps` —
so a manager cannot create the very duplicate §29.13 stops; a RELEASED row does not block, because releasing is how a
manager says *this one is being corrected*); money settled downstream; a one-per-store-day satellite already standing
at the destination for this person (`cash_pickup` / `billpay_pickup` / `closing_metric_line` are `UNIQUE (org,
close_date, store_code, employee_name)`, so this is a sentence instead of a 500); any registered table that could not
be READ — *"the query failed"* is never read as *"no rows"*, which is how a move lands under a settled deposit.

**ENDPOINT:** `POST /closing/row/{row_id}/refile` — body `{store_code | sfid, note?, refiled_by?, dry_run?}`, gated to
`_can_mgmt_review` (the release gate; a DM cannot re-file). `dry_run: true` returns the identical plan and writes
nothing, which is what the screen shows before the manager confirms. The satellites are written **before** the closing,
so a failure leaves the store-day whole and retryable. The closing then takes the destination's `store_code` /
`store_address` / `sfid`, a `dedup_key` recomposed at the destination's grain, and the audit columns.

**THE SCREEN:** Management Review (`/closing/management`) — a `Move to store…` picker (the same roster the filter
bar uses, so a store code is picked and never typed) beside the existing `Release for correction` button, then
`Check move`, which shows what will move with it (or the refusal), and only then `Confirm move`. Two steps on purpose:
a store-day can carry seven satellite tables and that is not something a manager can eyeball.

**MIGRATION `1081`** (additive, idempotent, no money): `refiled_from_store_code`, `refiled_at`, `refiled_by`,
`refile_note` on `commcalc.daily_closing` + a partial index. It is a TRAIL, not a gate — without it the move still
works and the response says the trail is missing (`audit_columns_missing`), because a repair that cannot be
distinguished from the mistake never happening is the thing worth fixing.

**LOCK:** `backend/harness_closing_refile.py`, **101 checks**, its own CI job (`closing-refile-lock`). It
**re-derives the table list FROM THE MIGRATIONS** and fails the build if any table carrying `close_date` +
`store_code` is unclassified — so a new such table cannot quietly join the schema and be forgotten by the move. It
also drives the REAL endpoint against the shared `harness_intake_fakes.FakeDB`, reproduces the abort Sanjot hit, and
fails if the router stops dereferencing the registry, the grain or the dedup key, if the satellites stop moving first,
if a second copy of the disposition vocabulary appears, or if migration 1081 stops being additive. Six negative
controls.

**OPEN — reported, not fixed.** The destination-shortage finding of §29.13 still stands ($230 declared against
$447.29 POS cash at Utica on 2026-10-10): a re-file moves a store, never a figure, and it deliberately does not
"reconcile" the day it lands on.


## 30. TENANT ONBOARDING — the COMMISSION-STATEMENT INTAKE, stage 3 of the new flow (owner 2026-09-20)

Owner: *"I will not do anything manually — the system should ask me while onboarding under 3.4 what is
considered commission positive or negative. The user does not know how this system works, they only
can upload their existing data: Sales reports, Commission reports, POS reports, Inventory reports — ask
the user if we have uploaded any other report like bill payments or credit card payments or x reports.
We should be able to take those reports and assign the existing fields to the uploaded data and SAVE
that, use the intelligence to assign the categories to the fields and ask the user to confirm. Whatever
is being uploaded should be able to save is most important — previously mostly all imports did not
save the first time."*

**Design of record: `docs/ONBOARDING_FLOW_DESIGN.md` — read before setting up a new tenant** (in the repo since
Stage C; §7 "Report availability is DERIVED from the tenant's declaration — never listed" is the owner's directive
of 2026-09-20 and is BUILT in §30.9 — the report-kind registry, mig 1010). Design of record: the workflow architect's `onboarding_flow_design.md` (2026-09-20) — §0 principles, §3
the commission stage (3.1–3.9), §4 state model, §5 must-not-happen. **This is the FIRST slice: stage 3
only.** Stage B (sales / inventory / POS / "other reports" on the same spine) is the next PR; the
payloads already carry `source_kind`, `target_table`, `identity_fields` and a `verify` block so it
generalises without a second shape.

**No carrier, tenant or product is named** in `onboarding_intake.py`, the router's intake functions or

### 30.2 The flow, and what each step reads and writes

| Step | Screen | Reads | Writes |
|------|--------|-------|--------|
| 3.1 | carrier (row; add one inline) + statement type + dropzone | `GET /carriers` | `PUT /state` (carrier, type, filename) |
| 3.2 | sheet / header row / footer shown, overridable | `analyze.detect` (every sheet listed with role + rows; footer value + whether it equals the lines' sum) | `PUT /state` |
| 3.3 | platform field · your column (pre-selected) · provenance badge · 3 samples; every MONEY column with Σ (the unpicked ones recorded as ignored — design §5.9) | `analyze.columns`, `money_columns` | `PUT /state` (column_map) |
| 3.4 | **"In this file, is money you EARNED positive or negative?"** — [Earned is positive] [Earned is negative]; three largest positive + three largest negative rows (label › sub-label · store · amount). NO default; cannot proceed unanswered; the stored answer is shown when one exists | `analyze.sign` | `PUT /state` (sign_answer); on commit → `column_mapping.sign_convention` |
| 3.5 | labels: count · Σ raw · Σ canonical (None until 3.4) · sign mix · sub-labels · reversal pre-flag (text says chargeback/deact/reversal/clawback, or all-negative after normalisation) | `analyze.labels` | — |
| 3.6 | five bucket columns + an Unassigned tray; dropdown per card (no drag library); provenance badge on a pre-placed card; reversal toggle; exit gate = tray empty (no "other") | `analyze.labels[].bucket/provenance` | `PUT /state` (assignments); on commit → `commission_category_map` rows under `<carrier_code>__<statement slug>` |
| 3.7 | store / account / rep strings surfaced with count + Σ. **Resolution is NOT in this slice** (see 30.5) | `analyze.identity` | — |
| 3.8 | gross / chargebacks / net per bucket · Σ canonical · the file's own total (footer row N, or typed) · difference · rows in file / usable / footer / to land · ignored money columns · the §3.4 sanity banners · attestation textarea when the difference is non-zero or there is nothing to compare | `analyze.verify` (in-memory preview, labelled as such) | `PUT /state` |
| 3.9 | "Confirm <carrier> — <period> — net $X" → commit → the RE-READ card (rows landed of built, per-bucket, tie-out) → "Another carrier?" | `POST /commit` | everything, in order: (a) map (b) sign (c) rules (d) rows (e) re-read (f) stage row VERIFIED / NEEDS_INPUT with `verified_numbers` |

### 30.3 THE SIGN QUESTION maps onto the mapping's convention — and needed one more name

The 3.4 answers are stored as `column_mapping.sign_convention` on the amount row for (org,
`commission_ledger`, carrier): **positive → `payout_positive`**, **negative → `payout_negative_netted`**.
Both NET a reversal into the bucket it reverses (design §3.6; a reversal-flagged label does not change
booking — direction comes from the sign — it drives the sanity banner and is kept on the stage row).
`payout_negative` could not serve the negative answer: on the master-agent feeds it describes, the
opposite sign is a DIFFERENT stream (dealer purchases) and books as a `charge`, so a negative-earned
statement with positive deactivation clawbacks would either inflate or never tie out. Mig `1008` widens
the CHECK constraint; `commission_ledger.CONVENTIONS` gains the third entry; nothing existing changes
(NULL still reads as `payout_negative`; `harness_commission_ledger_sign.py` re-pins the vocabulary at
three). Until 1008 is applied, a commit answering "earned is negative" is REFUSED naming the migration —
it is never written as something else.

**⚠ Reported for the owner, not decided here:** the 3.4 question conflates "the opposite sign is a
chargeback that nets" with "the opposite sign is a different money stream". For the master-agent
feeds that keep using `payout_negative` through the existing wizard this is correct today; a tenant
whose new carrier's file carries BOTH clawbacks and purchases on the opposite sign would see the
purchases netted. The three-largest-rows panels and the per-bucket chargebacks column make that visible;
a third answer on 3.4 would be the fix, and is an owner call.

### 30.4 THE SAVE GUARANTEE — what "saved" means here

`POST /onboarding/intake/commit` refuses (400, nothing written) when 3.4 is unanswered, any label is
unassigned, the file states no total and none was typed, or the difference is non-zero — unless the body
carries an attestation with a reason (recorded with name and time; $0.00 = $0.00 needs one too, design
§5.3). It then saves the map, READS IT BACK (every header must match; the amount row must carry the
convention), saves the rules, READS THEM BACK (`rules_source` must be `tenant`), builds the rows from the
read-back rules, lands them, and RE-READS the landed rows in pages (the client caps a read at 1,000 —
a 1,203-line statement would otherwise "verify" short). `ok` is true only when rows re-read = rows built
= rows inserted, the re-read tie-out matches (or is attested) and the re-read total equals the preview.
Anything else is `ok:false` with `problems[]`, the stage row `needs_input` with `blocking_reason`, and the
page paints it red — a landing that silently drops rows can never read "Saved and verified".

### 30.5 Proof, registration, and what is OPEN

**Proof: `backend/harness_onboarding_intake.py` — 119 checks, DB-free.** Written as the scenario (a
carrier the platform has never seen; the real 522-line statement as DATA: title block, 521 lines,
deactivation chargebacks, the file's own 86,970.34 total row): §A–F the pure rules; §G the REAL endpoint
functions over an in-memory fake of the client — analyze → answer → assign → commit → **re-read 521
rows, tie-out 86,970.34 = 86,970.34, difference 0.00**; the same file written the other way up gives the
same buckets under "earned is negative"; a second carrier is prefilled from nothing of the first. §H
negative controls: unanswered sign / unassigned label / disagreeing total each refused with nothing
written; a landing that drops rows → `ok:false` + `needs_input`; a pre-1008 database refuses "earned is
negative" naming the migration; no mig 1007 → still lands, `state.saved:false`; no footer → refused until
typed/attested. §I wiring (the writers and the re-read are really called; `/commission-ledger/import`
lands through the same helper), RULE TWO, migrations, this registration, and the page's verbatim 3.4.

**Files:** `backend/app/modules/commcalc/onboarding_intake.py` (PURE), `router.py` (`onboarding_intake_*`,
`_intake_*`, `_read_upload_grids`, `_ledger_map_records`, `_ledger_land_rows`), `commission_ledger.py`
(third convention), `database/migrations/1007_onboarding_intake_state.sql` + `1008_sign_convention_netted.sql`
(**written, NOT applied**), `frontend/src/app/(platform)/onboarding/intake/page.tsx`, `lib/rbac.ts` (NAV),
`components/ScreenLink.tsx` (`onboarding_intake`), `lib/flow-return.ts` (`/intake`).

**Money surfaced, not moved.** Nothing is recomputed for anyone; no row anywhere changes until a tenant
walks the flow for their own carrier. The two migrations create empty state tables and widen one CHECK.

**OPEN after Stage A — items (1), (2) and (3) are CLOSED by Stage B (§30.6):** (1) 3.7 store resolution
now runs through the shared resolver and gates the commit; (2) every kind of the enum lands or is recorded
honestly; (3) the file is kept between visits. Still open: (4) A tenant that also saved a GLOBAL
(carrier-NULL) `commission_ledger` mapping through the older wizard has those rows merged under carrier
rows at import time for fields the intake left unmapped; the re-read tie-out would expose any effect, and
no such rows exist on the platform today (§25.11 measured the table empty). (5) The 3.4 conflation in 30.3.

**Stage 2, step by step (design §2).** 2.0 "What do you have?" — Sales export (per POS: source + kind

**THE SAVE GUARANTEE, generalised (`_intake_commit_stage2`).** Refuse (400, nothing written) while:
a required column is unmapped; a store string is unresolved; any row carries no parseable date (sales) or
no store; nothing would land; the file states no total and none was typed, or the difference is non-zero,
without an attestation carrying a reason ($0.00 = $0.00 too); inventory has no as-of date. Then: save the
map (carrier-NULL rows for the layout) and READ IT BACK; write the identity decisions and READ THEM BACK
through a fresh resolver; land through the kind's existing path; RE-READ exactly the slice the file owns
(`_intake_reread_sales`: org × store-set × date range, paged; `_intake_reread_inventory`: org × store-set ×
as_of, paged); `ok` only when rows re-read = rows built = rows inserted AND Σ re-read = Σ shown (and the
tie matches or is attested). 3.7 is now a gate too: `_intake_commit_commission` refuses an unresolved
store string (assign / create / company-level / not ours with a reason) and writes the decisions through
the same `_intake_apply_identity` before landing.

**Proof: `backend/harness_onboarding_intake_b.py` — DB-free, over an in-memory fake of the client + its
storage.** A POS export as a workbook (title block, header, 48 invoice lines over 24 invoices for THREE store
strings — one spelled like the roster address, one already a code, one unknown — a footer, a continuation
sheet); an inventory listing with 3 ordered units without an IMEI; a "bill payments" report nobody has a
table for. The resolver knows two strings and not the third; the commit is refused until it is assigned /
created / not-ours-with-reason; then the map, the alias and the rep alias save and read back, the rows land

**What a residual upload now does (the Verizon tenant, or any).** 3.1 offers "Residual report from the carrier" from the
registry; the intake derives `commission_ledger__residual`, proposes the residual layout's columns (amount ← Residual,
label ← Plan, line ← Account / MDN, period ← Service Month) with NO prefill from the commission statement's map, asks
3.4 afresh for THIS type, buckets the labels through the mig-1009 hint words (`residual`, the auto-pay spellings — already
present, nothing added), lands under `verizon__residual_statement`, ties out to its own total, and Stage 4 shows one row
per (carrier, statement type). The commission statement's map and sign answer are byte-identical afterwards. The
Commission Ledger page's template picker lists both `source_report` values from the data.

### 30.11 STAGE D — REPORT LINKS: every report a tenant loaded, linked to every other by the columns they share, with the match counts EACH WAY (owner 2026-09-20)

Owner, verbatim: *"we need to link the different reports automatically with each other with common columns."*

**THE CLASS (CLAUDE.md "A fix is a DESIGN fix").** *A pairing rule spelled per consumer.* Before this, ONE consumer paired
lines to devices (the inventory auto-check of §30.8, `inventory_sold_recon.activation_index`); the report links would be a
second consumer of the same rule (serial, else the phone number through a sale line, else unpairable with a reason), and the
platform already carried siblings of its normalisers (`whatif._norm_mdn` ≡ `mobile_key`; `device_history.norm_order` ≡
`device_cost_recon.norm_order`). Fixed as a mechanism: the rule is factored ONCE (`line_pairings`), `activation_index`
FOLDS it (output byte-identical — the 43 checks unchanged), the links CALL it, the normalisers are INJECTED from their
homes, and a lock fails the build on a second copy.

(`inventory_sold_recon`: `activation_index`, `sales_mobile_index`, `mobile_key`, `sales_evidence`), §13a (`_store_maps` /
`_store_code_resolver`, `_intake_store_resolver` / `_intake_rep_resolver`), §2 (`column_mapping.TARGET_FIELDS` — the one
vocabulary of canonical field names), §30.6–30.8 (the intake's re-reads per kind, `KIND_FIELDS` / `kind_fields`, the

(`_ledger_mapping_key` — the residual layout is where the phone number is the line identity), §15 (`ma_recon` — a
device→rep attribution for ONE feed shape, not a generic pairing), §17 (`GET /onboarding/intake/state`). NOT rebuilt: no
new table, no new query path, no second normaliser, no second pairing, no second column vocabulary, no second label.**

**What "never guess" means here.** A line with no usable key is counted as "carries no <column>", never matched. A key that
fits SEVERAL lines on the other side is counted as matched AND flagged ambiguous with the count (a store key is ambiguous by
nature and the page says so); it is never resolved to one line. A phone-number-only line is paired to a device ONLY through a
sale line that carries that number, and only when the number names exactly one unit — several → `UNPAIR_AMBIGUOUS` with the
candidates listed (the negative control: a sibling that resolves the ambiguous number to its first candidate reports 3 matched
where the honest core reports 2 — the pin goes RED). Every direction reconciles: matched + unmatched + no key = lines.

**Money surfaced, not moved.** Read-only: the only write is the cache row on the intake's own state table. Nothing is
recomputed for anyone; no row of any report changes (pinned §C: sales 10 / ledger 11 / inventory 5 / tender 5 before = after).

### 30.12 STEP 2.5a — WHAT COUNTS AS AN ACTIVATION: the words are mapped at intake, one predicate counts them everywhere (owner 2026-09-21)

Owner, verbatim: *"sales report shows 88 txns but not a break up in to activations and upgrade etc, also nothing on
exec mtd"*.

**Measured (org f4f1c16e…, August 2026):** 1,056 line-level rows, 88 distinct invoices, `contract_type` BLANK on every
row (the export has no such column). The activation TYPE is in the category PATH leaf — `… >> New Activation (…)` (40
lines), `… >> Upgrades (…)` (25), `… >> Cellular Equipment >> Customer Provided Device` (24; product "Customer Owned
Device …"), `… >> Prepaid/Hardware Only (Equip)` (4) — and the handsets under `… >> SmartPhones >> …` (61) / `… >> Basic
Phones >> …` (6). `_exec_mtd` read 0 for every activation column and 0 phones (`metric_coverage` flagged `phones`);
the Sales Report showed 88 transactions with no split. No tenant rows in `exec_metric_config`, no
`activation_details_rules` of its own.

**THE CLASS.** A sale line's activation type was classified from ONE fixed column (`contract_type`) by token lists
hard-coded in three places (`calculator.classify_contract_type`, `router._exec_act_class`, the mig-213
`_resolve_ct_bucket`), and the Exec-MTD line buckets from a house vocabulary. A POS that carries the same fact in
another field — or in other words — yielded silent zeros on every report and in every commission calculation.

**THE FIX (config, one home, mapped at onboarding, locked).**
1. **One predicate.** `commcalc/line_class.py` — `activation_class(row, rules)` /
   `classify_line(row, rules)` (§3). Rules per org in the EXISTING `accessory_config.activation_details_rules`
   JSON (mig 313, extended with `fields` / `tokens` / `exact` — no migration): which COLUMNS carry the type and which
   WORDS name each class, matched by contains over every configured column; the mig-213 `contract_type_map` is the
   `exact` layer of the same fact. House defaults = the retired chain, byte-identical (`harness_line_class.py` §B).
   Every sibling dereferences it (the list in §15's row); `activation_bucketing` (the carrier-portal Activation-Details
   basis), `asset/router._promo_type` (the hotsheet promo taxonomy) and `sale_installment_engine` (the residual
   category chain) are excused BY NAME in the lock, each with the reason it is a different question.
2. **The Exec-MTD line buckets** stay `exec_metric_config` (mig 204/962/963); `exec_metric_defs.line_match` gains
   `category_contains` / `department_contains` (additive) so a category PATH can be matched; `metric_coverage` stays
   the detector; the retired `activation` bucket row is no longer offered by the Metric-definitions panel.
3. **The intake maps it, with intelligence, and the person confirms — step 2.5a** (`onboarding_intake.STEPS_STAGE2`,
   between 2.5 and 2.6; `frontend …/onboarding/intake/line-class-step.tsx`, rendered by `stage2.tsx`): the
   suggestion engine (`line_class.suggest_rules` / `suggest_metric_rules`) scans the DISTINCT values of
   `contract_type` / `category` / `department` / `product_desc` / `trans_type` in the frame (analyze) or the LANDED
   slice (`GET /onboarding/intake/line-class`), matches generic hint words per class (`HOUSE_HINTS` /
   `HOUSE_METRIC_HINTS`, overridable per org under `hints` / `metric_hints` in the same JSON), drops a word that
   names ≥80% of all lines (a department word inside every category path — "activation" here — is TOO BROAD and is
   reported, never proposed), shows each proposal's column, sample values and the count it would classify — computed
   by THE predicate, so what is confirmed is what every report counts. Over the measured vocabulary it proposes
   category "new activation" → activation, "upgrade" → upgrade, category "customer provided" + product "customer
   owned" → BYOD, "hardware only" → hardware_only, and `category_contains` "smartphone" / "basic phone" → phones.
   Save = `PUT /onboarding/intake/line-class` → `put_accessory_config(activation_details_rules)` +
   `put_exec_metric_config` (the two writers; nothing else) → the landed slice RE-COUNTED onto the stage row.
4. **The gate.** A line-level sales commit whose landed slice classifies ZERO activation-type lines LANDS (the rows
   are in the table) but is NOT verified: `onboarding_intake.activation_gate` → stage row `needs_input`, blocking
   reason naming step 2.5a, Stage-4 `fix_step` = 2.5a and `activation_note`; verified once a rule classifies ≥1 line
   or the person attests "this file truly has no activations" (`attestation.no_activations` on the commit form, or
   `no_activations` on the 2.5a save — recorded with the name in `verified_numbers.activation_gate.attested`). The
   Exec MTD payload's `landing.classified` (the same `count_classes` over the page's own rows) drives the banner
   *"… no line could be told apart as an activation or upgrade — map it under Onboarding — Commission Intake (step
   2.5a)"* (ScreenLink; no second link map).
5. **Lock** (`backend/harness_line_class_lock.py`, in `carrier-vocab-guard.yml` beside the other locks): no second
   token list / retired classifier / contract-type token check outside `line_class.py` (excused files named, each
   re-verified); every caller dereferences (`classify_line` / `_lc.activation_class`), no app module calls the bare
   alias; `activation_details_rules` touched only by the loader, the writer and the two resolvers; the 2.5a step
   touches no table of its own; the surfaces render the step, the banner and no retired editor row; negative
   controls prove each rule can go red.

**Counting rule, stated:** activations are DISTINCT invoices per class (`_sales_cell_agg`, `calc_rep_commissions`);
an invoice with two new-activation lines counts once; an invoice carrying two classes counts in both
(`activation_bucketing.mixed_bucket_transactions` measures that). Over the measured-shape fixture — 40 / 25 / 24 / 4
lines on 88 invoices — the split is **39 activations, 25 upgrades, 23 BYOD** (Total Activation 87; the hardware-only
invoice is not one), Total Phones 67; on the live tenant the same rule yields its own distinct-invoice counts.

**Money.** The pay path (`calc_rep_commissions` via `cfg['line_class_rules']`, `payout_accrual`, the plan engine)
now reads the SAME rules the reports read. Under house defaults every existing tenant is byte-identical (the pin
replays the retired classifiers over 1,554 spellings × empty / foreign / pinned maps + 4,000 fuzzed labels). A tenant
with a `contract_type_map` and a legacy-engine carrier mode would now also PAY on its mapped labels (the plan
engine already did); no such tenant is known — stated, not hidden. A tenant-authored exec `activation` byod /
upgrade token wider than the built-in word used to only suppress the Port sub-split and now classifies the line —
measured at 0 spellings on the battery. Migrations: **none**.

**Duplicate check (what was searched, what is REUSED):** `activation_details_rules` (mig 313 — extended, the same
column), `contract_type_map` (absorbed as `exact`), the mig-224 `activation_rules` (transaction-level, kept as the
supplement it is), `exec_metric_config` + `exec_metric_defs.line_match` (extended with two contains keys),
`metric_coverage` (unchanged detector), `put_accessory_config` / `put_exec_metric_config` (the two writers),
the intake auto-save + `_intake_save_state`, `_intake_reread_sales` (the slice re-read), `ScreenLink`
(`onboarding_intake`), `landing_identity` (`landing` payload extended with `classified`). The fake supabase client
is factored out of `harness_onboarding_intake_c.py` into `backend/harness_intake_fakes.py` (with the measured
fixture) so the new proofs carry no fourth copy. Proofs: `harness_line_class.py` (35), `harness_line_class_lock.py`
(15), `harness_onboarding_intake_d.py` (34); `harness_onboarding_intake.py` pins the 2.5a Save row.

**Files:** `backend/app/modules/commcalc/line_class.py` (new); `calculator.py`, `router.py` (`_accessory_config_uncached`,
`_line_rules_of`, `_line_skip`, `_blank_ct_bucket_map`, `_classification_gaps`, `_sales_cell_agg`, the calc endpoint,
`_exec_mtd` landing, `/sales-report/detail`, `_intake_line_class_block`, `_intake_landed_slice`, `_intake_prepare_stage2`,
`_intake_commit_stage2`, `onboarding_intake_line_class` / `_put_line_class`, `put_accessory_config`), `onboarding_intake.py`
(`STEP_LINE_CLASS`, `activation_gate`, `activation_note`, `verify_table`), `exec_metric_defs.py`, `commission_engine.py`,
`plan_options.py`, `whatif.py`, `sales_comparison.py`, `payout_accrual.py`, `closing/router.py`, `marketing/event_sales.py`
+ `marketing/router.py`; frontend `onboarding/intake/line-class-step.tsx` (new), `stage2.tsx`, `page.tsx`,
`intake-shared.tsx`, `commcalc/exec/mtd/page.tsx`; `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml`;
`docs/ONBOARDING_FLOW_DESIGN.md` §10.

**ADDENDUM 2026-09-21 — THE SECOND CLASS: "the effective rule is not what the person confirmed".** The owner opened
2.5a on the landed August export and saved; the database then held `activation_details_rules = {fields: ['category'],
tokens: {activation: ['new activation', 'activation', 'add a line', 'new act', 'prepaid'], upgrade: ['upgrade'], byod: ['customer
provided', 'byod', 'customer owned'], port: ['port'], hardware_only: ['hardware only']}}` and **0** tenant rows in
`exec_metric_config` (the phones tick did not persist). `_exec_mtd(…, "August 2026")` → activation **88** / upgrade 9 / byod 15 /
total_phones **0**; `landing.classified` activation **856 of 898** scanned lines → every invoice an activation, because the bare word
"activation" sits inside every category path (`Activations (Price Sheet) >> …`). With `tokens.activation = ['new activation']` only,
the same rows count 25 / 17 / 15 / 2 by distinct invoice. Four faces, one mechanism, each fixed for every caller:

| # | Face | The fix (one home) |
|---|------|--------------------|
| 1 | **The too-broad guard ran over the PROPOSALS, never over what is SAVED.** | `line_class.token_shares` / `broad_tokens` / `refused_tokens` measure the EFFECTIVE rules over the rows in hand; `PUT /onboarding/intake/line-class` resolves the merged JSON through **`router._line_rules_resolve`** (the loader's own resolver, factored out — no second resolution) and REFUSES (400, nothing written, each word named with its share and class) unless `broad_ok` attests the word by name — recorded in the same JSON under `broad_attested['<class>:<word>'] = {by, at, ratio}` (pruned when the word leaves the rule). Basis: the LANDED slice, or the kept file's frame re-read through THE prepare path (`_intake_draft_frame` → `_intake_prepare`) when nothing is landed; "not measured" is stated when neither exists and the commit re-validates. Everything is validated first; the metric rows are written before the activation rules so a failed write leaves nothing half-saved. **Re-validation of what is already saved:** `count_classes` carries `broad` / `refused` (tenant-declared tokens only — house defaults are never measured, the pin); `onboarding_intake.activation_gate` is BLOCKED by a refused word (no "no activations" attestation closes it), `activation_note` reads *"rule refused — "activation" names 95% of 898 lines — fix the words at step 2.5a"* (never "activations: 88 new activation"); the GET block carries `refused` / `rules_ok` / `refusal_note` and the step opens in the refusal state; Exec MTD's `landing.classified.rules_refused` + note drive a red banner beside the silent-zero one. The guard's ratio is `BROAD_RATIO` (≥ 0.8), the same the hints use. |
| 2 | **House contract-type tokens leaked across a field switch.** `resolve_rules` filled every undeclared class from `HOUSE_TOKENS` (" aal", "idv", "port" …); under `fields: ['category']` they applied to the wrong column. | **THE NO-LEAK RULE** in `resolve_rules`: `house_fill = fields == HOUSE_FIELDS`; the house tokens, the legacy exec `activation` layer and the mig-213 auto tokens fill an undeclared class ONLY under the house field; under tenant-declared fields an undeclared class has `[]` (the step shows it empty and says why). A tenant with declared tokens but house fields keeps today's behaviour; every org with no declaration is byte-identical (`harness_line_class` §B pin + G8). `merge_into_raw` now stores ONLY the classes given (per-class merge; no copy of the house list in a tenant row — the resolver fills) and prunes attestations. |
| 3 | **The editable words were seeded from the wrong source; hint words too generic on their own.** | The step's editable words come from **`suggest_rules(...).proposal` only** (`frontend …/intake/line-class-logic.ts` `seedFromBlock` — a pure module the step imports; the block the router returns carries `rules: {fields, tokens, exact, source, declared, house_fill}`, never a hint list). The proposal per class = the person's declared words MINUS any refused, PLUS the file's hint hits; with nothing declared, the hits — else the house words under the house field only, `[]` under tenant fields. **Decision on `HOUSE_HINTS`:** the bare words `activation` and `port` are REMOVED as hints (a department word inside every path / a substring of "support"); the guard would catch them only once proposed and only at ≥ 80% — a word wrongly naming 30% of the lines would sail through — so a word generic on its own is never a proposal. `port` hints are now `port-in`, `port in`, `port in activation`, `number port`, `ported`. |
| 4 | **The metric tick did not round-trip.** ROOT CAUSE = **server**: mig 962 DROPPED mig 204's `UNIQUE (org_id, bucket)` and created the unique index `(org_id, bucket, carrier) NULLS NOT DISTINCT`; `put_exec_metric_config` still upserted `on_conflict='org_id,bucket'` → Postgres 42P10 ("no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification") → `{ok: false, hint: "run migration 204"}` → the 2.5a PUT raised 400 AFTER `put_accessory_config` had already written (the owner's row persisted, the phones row did not). Every `PUT /exec-metric-config` (the Metric-definitions panel too) has failed on a post-962 database. | `put_exec_metric_config` upserts `{…, carrier: None}` with `on_conflict='org_id,bucket,carrier'` and falls back to the legacy target on a pre-962 database (the reader's own column ladder); the error is reported verbatim, never as "run migration 204". `harness_intake_fakes.FakeDB` gains `unique_indexes` (a conflict target must name one → 42P10, as Postgres) so the fake REPRODUCES the defect (`harness_onboarding_intake_d` H5) and proves the fix (H6–H8: the row written, updated in place, pre-962 shape still served, `_exec_mtd` `total_phones` 67 > 0). The frontend proof (`prove_line_class_step.mjs`, the real transpiled TS over the engine's own block) pins that ticking "use" puts `metric_rules.phones` = the proposal in the body. |

**Money.** The classifier feeds pay: under house defaults every existing tenant is byte-identical (the §B pin unchanged: 1,554 spellings + 4,000 fuzzed labels; G8 / H15 add "nothing refused, house_fill True"). A tenant with tenant-declared fields and an undeclared class no longer classifies that class by a contract-type word (the no-leak rule) — the only behavioural delta, and it is the defect. Migrations: **none**.

**Lock** (`harness_line_class_lock.py`, now 29): (f) the save resolves through `_line_rules_resolve`, measures (`_lc.refused_tokens(`) and refuses BEFORE either writer (a hoisted write → RED; a second `_lc.resolve_rules(` in router.py → RED); the block hands no hint list (`"rules": rules` → RED); the step seeds through `seedFromBlock` reading `suggest.proposal` only (a seed from `block.rules` → RED; a step reading `hints` → RED); behavioural: a saved broad word → refused, the attested word → not refused, tenant fields + undeclared class → no house / legacy / auto token, the pin; the bare hints absent; the frontend proof exists.

Owner, verbatim: *"sales by invoice report also has the tender types on the report, need to capture that as well"* — *"tender
types is in columns"* — and later the same day: *"nothing on cash collected either"*.

**THE FILE, measured** (kept in the private bucket `onboarding-intake`, path `f4f1c16e-…/pos_rq_pos_product_sales/sales-by-invoice-report.xlsx`,
1.7 MB, 10,823 rows, 41 columns): ONE ROW PER INVOICE — Created On, Invoiced By, Invoiced At, Tendered By (+ username), Sold By (+
username), Invoice #, Customer, Application, Invoice Comments, Invoice Subtotal, Adjustments, Net Sales, Sales, Total Cost, Gross
Profit, Extra Charges, Total Donations, Invoice Total, Total Coupons, Gift Card Sales, Non-Revenue Sales, Channel, Region, District,

**THE MIS-CARDING, stated plainly.** On 2026-09-20 this file was committed as the BY-PRODUCT aggregate (`pos_product_sales`); it is
not a per-product report, it is a per-invoice report. Its instance `pos:rq:pos_product_sales` still reads "verified"; the rows it

10,823 invoice-level rows** (source `pos_product_sales`). Nothing of its tenders is captured anywhere. The recovery is the intake's
own clicks (the PR body): retire the stale line (with the COUNTED removal of the 10,823 rows, or the owner-approved SQL surfaced
there), add the invoice card, re-read the kept file under it — never a DB edit.

**THE DECISION ON MIG 1011's TABLE — option (b), new tables; `raw_sales_product` KEPT for a genuine per-product export.** The
by-product card describes a real report at the line grain; an invoice header plus a VARIABLE set of tender columns is two grains
and needs a child table; repurposing would re-point the product card at nothing. Nothing is dropped (the emptiness precondition a
repurposing migration would need is written into 1012's header so it is on the file, not in a head).

#### 30.13a ONE ANSWER TO "DID THE CUSTOMER PAY THIS TENDER?" (owner 2026-09-24: *"i cant get the uploaded data to convert in to receipts … if i cant get it tennat can never get it"*)

**The instance (measured live, org `f4f1c16e…`).** The invoice card (`invoice:rq:sales_by_invoice`) sat at 2.4/2.5b and never committed, so
`raw_sales_invoice` held 0 rows and `POST /pos/sales-from-reports/rebuild` built 0 receipts. The only refusal: *"the tender columns add up to
7,887,489.25 and the invoice totals to 1,032,971.45 — a difference of 6,854,517.80 on 7,948 invoice(s)"* — exactly the `Ven Reb Act` column.
Measured on all 10,823 invoices: Σ customer tenders = the invoice total on EVERY invoice (0 off); with the rebate counted, 7,951 off. The
invoice total is what the customer paid; the vendor rebate sits beside it.

**The class.** "Is this tender the customer's payment?" had THREE answers: the 2.5b tie (`invoice_tenders.invoice_verify`) said *every*
declared tender; the receipt builder (`sales_from_reports`) said *a class with a place on the closing axis*; Cash Collected's invoice leg
(`_invoice_tenders_by_store`) said *every tender, the rebate as 'other'* (it would have added 6.85M of vendor money to "collected" under the
`invoice` basis). The X-report leg (`_xreport_rows_by_store`) likewise counted a printed "Vendor Rebate" line as 'other'.

**The fix — one home, dereferenced.** `closing.router.is_customer_payment(cls)` (over `fold_to_axis`: an axis class is the customer's; a
vendor rebate / coupon / unclassed tender is not) and its label twin `is_vendor_paid_label(raw)` (a label the vocabulary POSITIVELY places
as not the customer's; an unplaced label keeps its stamp). Readers: `invoice_verify(…, *, pays)` — a REQUIRED keyword, no default; the tie
is Σ customer tenders vs Σ invoice total, the rest reported beside as `tenders.not_customer` {sum, by_label, invoices} and in the words;
`tender_tie.our_total` = `customer_sum`; the router injects it through `_intake_tender_pays()` at both calls (analyze + commit);

**WHAT A REBUILT RECEIPT CAN AND CANNOT SAY (measured on the real invoice, diffed line by line against the register's own print — the
numbers are in the delivered analysis, not here).** Identical: the invoice #, the store block, the tendered-on date, sales person /
tendered by / tendered at, the customer name, every handset line, every financed line (qty −1, the bracketed total), Subtotal, Cash,
Financed, Total, Change, the Contract Details pairs. Different, and why: (1) the register prints ~half of the invoice's lines — the
line-level export carries the invoice's whole ledger (the vendor-paid rebate / kicker / financing-fee / loan-number lines) and nothing
says which lines print or that a vendor-paid line prints at $0.00 — so the rebuilt receipt prints every landed line at its own price
and the totals from the invoice header, and the record SAYS in words that the lines add up to more than the customer paid by exactly
the vendor-rebate tender; (2) a line on the receipt that the export does not carry (an order-number tracking SKU) cannot be rebuilt;
(3) the tendered-on TIME (the landing keeps the date); (4) the register's short display name for the rep vs the export's full name;
(5) the bill-to address (the reports carry the name only; the matched POS customer's address prints when known); (6) the tax label is
the format's spec label, not the jurisdiction's name; (7) invoice comments (not landed); (8) the legal footer and the page footers
(the org's receipt-template footer prints instead); (9) the item order (the landed rows carry no file order — SKU / tracking # order).
OPEN, an owner decision: a per-org rule naming the lines a vendor pays (words / SKU patterns, like the activation rules) would print
them at $0.00 as the register does; which lines the register OMITS is not in any report.

**Proof.** `backend/harness_pos_sales_from_reports.py` (63, DB-free, the intake fake client driving the REAL readers, resolver,
importer and endpoints; the fixture is SYNTHETIC and shaped like the measured receipt — four handsets, financed lines with qty −1,
perks, order-number tracking, one cash tender, a vendor-rebate tender, a tax residual, contract details): §A the format's declarations
and the generic readers; §B the builder (header, order, financed, totals, the axis-injected payments, the pairs, the words, coverage
both ways, idempotence, provenance, a classifier that puts the vendor rebate on the axis makes it a payment — the fact lives in the
vocabulary); §C **the round trip** — document → `render_words` → `parse` → the same document on three invoices, the rendered text
carrying every item / total / payment row verbatim, the HTML the same walk, the default layout; §D end to end — 3 sales / 3 imports /
3 customers, the full-name match (Bob Doe first in the roster does not take Jane's receipt), the sale's money / date / store / rep /
customer / provenance, the re-run replaces (a corrected line re-lands into the same sale), a scanned receipt of the same invoice is a
separate record, the scanned path's sale now carries subtotal / tax / date, an edit brings the sale in step, the list, the endpoints,
no POS declared → a sentence, a declared POS with no format → a sentence, the intake hooks both branches, `stores=None`; §E the lock
dereferenced + the page + registration. Lock 14 (seven negative controls). **Pins CHANGED (stated):** `harness_sales_by_invoice` G9 —
the invoice card's `shows_in` now names the POS screen beside the intake. **Unchanged and green:** receipt_formats 46, pos_receipt_parse
16, pos_onboarding 193, sales_by_invoice 95, landing_identity 54 + lock 32, report_links 77 + lock 15, report_kinds 121 + lock 20,
intake 164 / B 87 / C 92 / D 49, line_class lock 29, mapping-key 17, tender-vocab lock, org-scope 25, lineage 63, the carrier-vocab
guard; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

receipts already write, dated on the invoice date; no P&L, GP, payout or tax path reads them. Nothing runs until a commit of either

#### 30.14a THE LINES THE VENDOR PAYS print at $0.00, as the register prints them (owner 2026-09-24)

Owner: *"the same receipt shown above shows the commission earned for each line but not the cost of phone charged to the customer"*;
asked how those lines should print: *"$0.00 like register"*.

**Measured (live tenant, the 10,823-invoice file).** The line-level export carries, beside the goods, the lines a VENDOR pays the store for
(rate-plan rebates, kickers, feature perks, installment rebate amounts, promotions) WITH their amount; the register prints them at $0.00
(the owner's own receipt). The handsets DO carry their price (50 of 57 August handset lines; the other 7 were discounted to $0 at the
register — list price = pricing discount). On every invoice the vendor-paid lines add up to the invoice's non-customer tenders (§30.13a).

**One home, config never code.** `pos/vendor_paid_lines.py` (PURE, stdlib; spells no category word): `segments` (the `>>` path),
`resolve_config` (the org row `pos.pos_settings['vendor_paid_lines']` → `{tokens[]}`; house = none), `matcher` (the predicate the
builder is handed), `costed_segments` (every segment on a line with a cost of goods — never vendor-paid), `non_customer_by_invoice`
(over the injected `closing.router.is_customer_payment`), `propose` (greedy: the segment that makes the most invoices tie, then brings
the rest nearer — never a costed one; then drops any it no longer needs), `proof`, `check_save`. Learned on the live tenant: 7 segments,
**3,816 of 3,882 invoices tie (98.3%; 79 with no rule), 0 handset lines caught**.

**Readers.** `sales_from_reports.build_document(…, vendor_paid)` — a REQUIRED keyword: a matched line prints price and total $0.00; its
amount is kept in the report (`vendor_paid_count`, `vendor_paid_sum`, `sum_printed`) and said beside the invoice's vendor-paid tenders;
`rebuild` hands it `_vpl.matcher(load_vendor_paid_rule(...))` and says, when no rule is saved, where to confirm one. The POS Receipts page
card `pos/receipts/vendor-paid-card.tsx` (GET/PUT `/pos/sales-from-reports/vendor-paid-lines`) shows the proposal, its proof and the saved
rule; Save → rebuild. The landed rows are never changed: commission reports keep reading the amounts.

line classifier), §30.13a (`is_customer_payment`), §30.14 (`FINANCED_ITEMS`, the format's own rule). **Reused:** `pos_settings` + the
one writer `upsert_pos_setting`, the intake re-reads, `is_customer_payment`. **Not** `line_class`: it answers "what TYPE of activation"
from contract words; this answers "who paid this line", proven against the tenders. **Not** the format's `FINANCED_ITEMS`: that is the
