## 68. AN ENTITLEMENT IS A COUNT OF MONTHS PER STORE — name the store-month that never arrived (owner instruction 2026-10-10)

Owner, verbatim: *"mdf / ramp up subsidy is being finsihed it is inly for 12 months, if we did not
get for 12 months for each store it should be flagged and the missing month and store to be poimted
out , make it into management overview"*.

A **completeness** check, not a money change. It books nothing, pays nobody, writes no flag and
recomputes no payout.

### 68.1 What the feed actually says — measured, not guessed

Read-only against production, house org, **2026-10-10**, through the shipped code and the real §64
store resolver. `commcalc.payment_categories` already declares `Ramp Up Subsidy` and
`4.0 $1K Ramp Up Bonus` into the org's own category **`MDF`** (0 rows live for the second).

| | rows | total | months |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commcalc.raw_payment_detail` (per line) | 44 | **$287,500.00** | March–October 2026 |
| `commcalc.raw_comp_report` (the statement) | 40 | $260,500.00 | March–September 2026 |

The two agree **store-for-store and dollar-for-dollar in every month both carry** (address SETS
compared, not just counts: Mar–Jul 6 stores / $39,300 each; Aug and Sep 5 / $32,000). The whole
difference is **October's 4 rows / $27,000.00** not yet in the statement — the known month-end lag,
**not a gap**. A lump sum, one row per store per month, on a single day early in the month (03-06,
04-07, 05-06, 06-08, 07-07, 08-06, 09-09, 10-07), with `imei` **and** `mdn` blank on all 44 rows —
correctly identifier-less, so this money has no device to name.

Per store, at the canonical keys the ONE identity home returns (§64 — note
`116-36 Springfield Blvd …` resolves to **`11636 Springfield Blvd`**, which is why a config keyed on
the raw address would miss):

| store | per month | received | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `509 Nostrand Ave` | $7,500 | March–October | still being paid |
| `151 E 170th St` | $7,500 | March–October | still being paid |
| `1750 5th Ave` | $7,000 | March–October | still being paid |
| `11636 Springfield Blvd` | $5,000 | March–October | still being paid |
| `103 Fulton Ave` | $5,000 | March–**September** | **nothing in October** |
| `3565 Broadway` | $7,300 | March–**July** | **nothing in August, September or October** |

Those two stores and their four store-months are what the owner asked to have pointed out. None of
the six is one of the three deliberately AMBIGUOUS identities (§64), so no verdict is withheld on
that ground here.

### 68.2 The class, named — and the fabricated accusation this report refuses to make

> **An entitlement is a COUNT OF MONTHS PER STORE, and nothing in any feed says when a store's count
> began or how long it runs.** That is the owner's knowledge. A report that infers the window from
> the data it happens to hold would accuse the carrier of withholding months it was never owed.

So the window is a per-org, per-store **config declaration** (RULE TWO: `term_months` a declared
number, `store_windows` a declared first month per canonical store key — no store name and no month
count in any branch), and:

- **A store with no declared start month is `not_measured` WITH A NAMED REASON — never "12 months
  missing."** For `3565 Broadway`, "it stopped in August" and "its twelve months ended in July" are
  indistinguishable without the start month, and only one of them is the carrier's doing.
- **A month that has not finished yet is `not_due`**, not missing. `feed_period.month_state` is the
  only clock in the module and `today` is injected, so a proof stands on a fixed date.

What the report DOES do with an undeclared store is name what was **observed**: a month whose payment
run arrived, after that store's own first payment, with no payment for it. That is evidence, reported
as `not_measured` with the reason on the row, with its own counter
(`undeclared_absence_store_months`) and an amount explicitly labelled
`undeclared_absence_amount_at_observed_rate` so the field cannot be read as money owed.

### 68.3 THE SPLIT — "this store missed its month" is not "we never got that month"

The §19.53 `unconfirmed_*` precedent, built here deliberately because it is the thing most likely to
be skipped:

| status | what it means |
|---|---|
| `missing` | the month's payment run **demonstrably arrived** — other stores were paid in it — and this store is not in it. **A fact about the carrier.** |
| `unconfirmed_missing` | the month is closed, in window, and **no payment of this kind reached us for ANY store**. **A fact about our ingest**, with its own counter and its own amount, **never netted into `missing`**. |

Collapsed into one number, the report would accuse the carrier of withholding a subsidy every time a
portal pull failed. The harness measures exactly that difference as a negative control (§D5).

**Why "the run arrived" is the confirmation test and not day coverage.** `statement_month_coverage`
(§19.54) reports **every** closed month FAILED on its own final day ($111,949.22, the end-exclusive
window). A missing 31st cannot hide a lump sum that posts on the 6th, so gating on full day coverage
would withhold every finding this report exists to make. The honest confirmation at a monthly-lump-sum
grain is the feed's own evidence that the month's run happened at all.

**Why both feeds are read and UNIONED.** They are two reads of ONE payment and they agree wherever
both carry it, so money that arrived in either is money that arrived: the union can only ever
withhold a finding, never invent one — the same direction-asymmetric floor §65 uses. Reading the
statement alone would have reported four October store-months as absent purely because of the lag.

### 68.4 Where it lives, and what it dereferences rather than re-deriving

| | |
|---|---|
| ONE home | `backend/app/modules/commcalc/entitlement_coverage.py` — PURE, DB-free, no writer. **`entitlement_store_months(received, cfg, months_with_feed, today, ambiguous_stores, stores)` is THE "expected but absent" home at store × month grain over an entitlement window** — dereference it rather than growing a second. Plus `entitlement_window`, `entitlement_type_matcher`, `normalize_config`, `config_from_rows`, `month_key`, the five `ROW_*` statuses, the four `ROW_REASON_*` and their human labels |
| the calendar | `feed_period.month_state` / `.period_month_year` / `UNKNOWN`/`OPEN`/`CLOSED` — the ONE authority. The module contains no `date.today()` and no month arithmetic on the clock (AST-locked, §C8) |
| the verdict vocabulary | `pay_data_quality.VERDICT_PASSED` / `_FAILED` / `_NOT_MEASURED`, **imported**, so the three strings are literally the same objects `statement_month_coverage` emits and cannot drift (§G1/§G2). `ok` is `None` for anything unjudgeable |
| which payments are the entitlement | the org's OWN `commcalc.payment_categories` through §57 `payment_category.load_map` / `.category_of` — the config names the CATEGORY LABEL to follow and the module lists **no payment type at all**, so adding one is a row in §57's home |
| the store key | §64 `account/coa.store_resolver`; and for "may these two addresses be ONE physical store" the **pairwise** predicate §70 put in its place (`coa.shared_store_identity_pairs` + `store_identity.may_be_one_store`), injected as a callable. Asked **per store-month**: only a month in which a possible twin WAS paid is `store_identity_ambiguous`, and that twin is NAMED on the row — never the store wholesale, which is the read §70 superseded after it withheld 23 true findings. The module derives no key and states no identity rule (AST-locked, §G6/§B14b) |
| NOT re-parameterised | `pay_data_quality.statement_month_coverage` answers **day** grain within **one** month (§19.54). This is store × month across a multi-month window. Making one function answer both would make one home two mechanisms; this reads it for its shape and its vocabulary and writes its own |

**Pricing.** A gap is priced from the store's declared `monthly_amounts` row, else from its own
payments **when they agree**; a store whose payments disagree prices nothing and the gap is reported
**UNPRICED**, never valued at $0.00 — `statement_month_coverage.unpriced_missing_days`' own rule.

### 68.5 Surfaces (§17) and how the owner reaches it

- `GET /commcalc/mdf-entitlement-coverage?store=` → `router._mdf_entitlement_run`. Takes **no
  period**: the question is the whole window, not one month. `require_org`-scoped; both feeds read
  through the paged one home (`core/feed_read.read_all`). **READ-ONLY** — no writer, no flag, no
  table, and the only migration is the config column and the dashboard tile.
- Page `frontend/src/app/(platform)/commcalc/mdf-entitlement-coverage/page.tsx` — renders and never
  computes a verdict, a window or a term. The two absence facts are separate tiles and separate
  columns; an unpriceable amount shows an em dash.
  **DRILL-DOWN §CORE-17.3v:** every tile links its count and its money figure to the shared
  `<DrillDownPanel`; the panels are the server's own fold and are NOT narrowed, because this page
  has no browser filter above its figures (§CORE-17.3o, decided by reading the page).
- **Management Overview** (`/hub/management-overview`) tile **"Subsidy Months Missing"** — mig `1068`
  Block 2, the `ui_label_override` `scope='tiles'` jsonb **append** with an `@>` containment guard
  and mig 1016's post-flight "exactly 1 tile" assertion. A string-matching migration into a tile
  layout is broken by construction (§19.31 (8)), and this one does not try.
- Also listed under **Incentives** beside the carrier reconciliations (`rbac.ts`), in
  `REPORT_DIRECTORY` (`'comm'`), `reports.ts`, `route-index.ts` and `ScreenLink.tsx`.

### 68.6 The lock

Module-graph fact **`entitlement_month_coverage`**, with the two edges it dereferences recorded
beside it (`month_archive_due` for the calendar, `pay_feed_balance` for the shipped verdict strings),
so a caller that stops dereferencing either fails `harness_module_graph_guard.py`.

`backend/harness_mdf_entitlement_coverage.py` — **96 checks, DB-free, stdlib only**, verified RED
against the pre-change tree (without the module every §A–§G check fails BY NAME through the
`_Missing` shims rather than dying with a traceback). §A the ask · §B the undeclared window, with the
CONTROL that declaring one store's window flips its three absences to `missing` while the others stay
put · §C the calendar, including the month in flight before and after its run · §D the split and the
negative control that measures what collapsing it would cost · §E pricing, with the unpriceable
fixture · §F RULE TWO (no store, carrier, category or month count in a branch) · §G one home,
dereferenced, with the three verdict strings pinned equal to the shipped ones · §H the live numbers.

### 68.7 What is NOT settled, and it is the crux

**Nobody has declared a single store's first entitled month**, so today the report names the four
store-months and reports every one of them `not_measured`. `term_months` 12 and the `MDF` category
are seeded by mig `1068`; `store_windows` is seeded **empty on purpose**. Until the owner supplies
the start month per store (and says whether any store not in the six was ever entitled at all), this
report cannot say whether `3565 Broadway` was cut off or simply finished — and saying it anyway is
the one thing it must not do.

**Placement is not this report's question, and §69 landing proves it.** §69 moves MDF-declared money
off the device-reimbursement P&L line onto `mdf_income` (merged the same day). This report asks only
whether each store-month ARRIVED; it reads the payment by the org's declared CATEGORY through §57,
not by the P&L line it books to, so re-routing that line changes nothing here — and the two sections
agree on the one fact they share, that `MDF` is the org's own declared category for this money.
## 76. A CATEGORY YOU DECLARE IS A CATEGORY YOU CAN BE PAID ON — one declared-metric registry, dereferenced (owner directive 2026-10-10, mig `1072`)

> **Section number — renumbered FOUR times in under two hours, which is the finding.**
> Written as §72 / mig `1070`. #435 (cash variance) had opened twenty minutes earlier claiming both,
> so this moved to §73 / mig `1071`. **While that renumber was being made, #437 merged to `main`
> carrying §73 AND mig `1071`** — the same pair, again. §74 was taken next, by #439 merging
> mid-review; §75 was already held on #438's branch, invisible in `main`. It now sits at
> **§76 / mig `1072`**. The migration number survived every move because nobody else claimed `1072`.
>
> Four moves for one change, and #438 independently recorded three of its own for another, inside the
> same hour. **This is no longer a race to narrate; it is a missing allocator.** The number is chosen
> by READING the file, so every open branch reads the same free number and whoever merges last always
> loses — which means the cost falls on the change that took longest to get green, every time. The
> fix is to claim the number when the branch opens (a reservation file on `main` appended in the
> first commit), or to stop numbering sections at all and address them by slug. Neither is this
> change's subject, so both are stated here rather than built.
>
> The earlier races this generalises (§61/§62, §67, §68/§71, #435, #437, #438, #439):
>
> - **A migration collision is materially worse than a section collision.** A duplicate `## 72.` is a
>   merge conflict a human reads. Two files named `1070_*.sql` are two different schema changes with
>   one name, and `harness_unique_numbers_lock.py` — the only thing that catches it — cannot fire
>   until both are on `main`, by which point one has been handed to the owner to run.
> - **Checking "the last number in the repo" is not a reservation.** Every agent here did that and
>   every one of them got the same answer. The number has to be claimed somewhere all of them can see
>   BEFORE the work, not inferred from a tree that four branches are moving at once.
>
> **This is a standing defect in how the repo is worked, not an incident.** It wants a reservation
> file on `main` that a change appends to in its first commit; until something like that exists,
> every index-and-migration change pays this cost, and the next one will pay it again.

Owner, verbatim: *"the categories on teh submit daily closing should be available for the admin to add
based on the business requirement and also when you add a category it should be available in teh
cincentive payout plan to be assesed to be paid out , this is in ref to ny logistics / ups store
tenant, they need to declare how many drop offs, how may 2nd day or 3rd day , also the commisison /
incentive for the employees is based on how much total sales ahve been done during the day and which
employee geenrates the most revenue during the day … but i dont wnat them to be hard coded it should
be a design effect"*.

### 76.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

The instance is "NY Logistics has no drop-off category". The class is that **what a business counts
and sells had three disconnected homes**, each carrying its own copy of the vocabulary:

1. `closing/count_config.py` (mig `501`) — admin-defined, but **counts only, store-day only, with no
   notion of what a unit is worth**. A category's PRICE, a category's MONEY and WHO declared it had
   nowhere to live.
2. The targets editor — four wireless categories hard-coded **in the page (`CATS`) and in the schema**
   (`commcalc.targets.activations_monthly` / `upgrades_monthly` / `accessories_monthly` / `byod_pct`).
3. The incentive side — **nothing at all**. A rule had no category to point at.

The third hole is the one that cannot be patched per-tenant: `commcalc.daily_closing` carries exactly
ONE `employee_name`, whoever submitted the sheet, so "which employee generated the most revenue today"
was not merely unanswered — answering it from the stored row would have **fabricated an attribution**,
crediting the submitter with everyone's work.

### 76.2 THE ONE HOME

**`backend/app/modules/closing/metric_catalog.py`** — "what does this business declare at the end of a
day, and what is a unit worth". PURE (no DB, no network, no imports). Built from the count-field
registry (mig `501`, extended) plus the tender registry (mig `111`, read-only — a tender is HOW money
arrived, never additional revenue, so `in_revenue` is false for every one).

Each entry: `key`, `label`, `value_kind` (`count`|`amount`|`both`), `declared_by` (`store`|`employee`),
`unit_price`, `in_revenue`, `recon_class`, `source`, **`storage`**.

- **`gross_revenue` / `employee_revenue` are THE definition of "a day's sales"**, at store and person
  scope, summing the same `revenue_keys`. A target and a payout rule that both ask here can never
  disagree about what the day was.
- **`by_employee` refuses to invent.** A store-level metric is never attributed to a person, and the
  `closing_row` argument is accepted and deliberately unused — crediting the submitter is the bug.

### 76.3 TWO PHYSICAL STORES, ONE READER (the `envelope_report.is_modern_row` precedent, §29.7)

`storage_for(metric)` is THE rule, and every catalog entry carries its answer so no caller works it out:

| | writes | why |
|---|---|---|
| count-only, store-level | `daily_closing.counts` jsonb + the three physical columns (mig `501`) | **byte-for-byte unchanged** — Cellfonz R Us, Luxelink and Vzone do not move |
| carries an amount, or declared per employee | `commcalc.closing_metric_line` (mig `1072`) | a figure with money or a person on it has no home in a jsonb of ints |

**Nobody reads either store directly.** `declared(catalog, closing_row, metric_lines)` folds both and
returns an entry for EVERY catalog metric — a metric nobody declared comes back with zeros and
`declared: False`, so "declared nothing" is distinguishable from "has no such category", which a
sparse dict cannot express.

### 76.4 THE INCENTIVE ENGINE KNOWS SHAPES, NOT RULES

**`backend/app/modules/commcalc/daily_incentive.py`** — PURE. Three shapes, and nothing else:

| shape | pays |
|---|---|
| `per_unit` | rate $ × the employee's OWN units of the payout metrics |
| `percent_of_amount` | rate × the employee's OWN declared $ |
| `threshold_pool` | rate × the STORE's figure makes a pool, split `hours` / `individual_sales` / `equal` |

**"Who ran the sale" is the house default for a pool** (owner, 2026-10-10: *"employees will clock in
but we will change the logic by who ran the sale, tis should be customized in incentive payout - make
it easy to confgure"*). `individual_sales` weights by each person's own figure in the **pool's OWN
categories**, not by their whole day — a pool built on printing is divided by printing, so somebody
who sold none of what made the pool gets none of it. A pool built on the whole day falls back to the
whole day, which is the same number, so there is no second setting to get wrong. A new pool is
created on this basis; `hours` and `equal` are a dropdown away, each with a sentence saying what it
does, and the editor reads the whole rule back as English while it is being built (`plainWords`).
`harness_metric_catalog_lock.py` §D3/§D4 fail the build if that screen ever FILTERS the server's list
of bases rather than merely ordering it — a basis added on the server must never vanish silently.

A **qualifier** gates at `store` / `employee` / `none` scope over any metrics on the catalog, several
**combined** — which is how "store overnight **+** express together must reach 5" is said with neither
product named in code. **Scope precedence is NOT redefined**: which rules apply to whom is
`management_incentive.resolve_plan`, the same ladder the employee commission plan uses.

**Money posture**, inherited from `management_incentive.py` and not weakened: computing is not paying;
a gate that cannot be VERIFIED fails **closed**; an unresolved input is zero production, never a
guess; a rule naming an undeclared category is **refused at save**; and **a pool whose split cannot be
measured comes back unallocated with a reason** rather than quietly becoming an even share — paying
people a share of a basis nobody recorded would be inventing a payment.

Hours come from `storeops.shifts` through `_incentive_hours_for_day` (actual where recorded, else
scheduled). Measured 2026-10-10: NY Logistics store `7710` has scheduled hours and **zero** actual
hours, so a by-hours pool there would run on scheduled hours until people actually clock in — which
is part of why the owner moved the default off hours and onto who ran the sale.

### 76.5 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

`backend/harness_metric_catalog_lock.py` (38 checks, stdlib, in `carrier-vocab-guard.yml`): §A the
vocabulary has one copy (`STANDARD_KEYS` mirrors `count_config.STANDARD_DEFS`; no module re-declares
the shapes or splits; **nobody but the home decides where a declaration is stored**); §B the new
tables are named only by their owning router, through a constant; §C the catalog is CONSTRUCTED in
exactly one place and the engine touches no database; §D no screen hard-codes a shape or split list;
§E the `daily_closing.counts` readers are pinned as `(file, receiver)` pairs and **may only shrink**;
§F six negative controls. It caught **three real un-wirings while being written**, one in this change's
own code.

**Proof:** `backend/harness_daily_incentive.py` (83 checks, DB-free, same workflow). Its oracle is the
owner's screenshot of the six live rules, each reconstructed as a **config row**; §H asserts no tenant
category and no tenant rate appears in either module's executable text (docstrings stripped — doctrine
may quote the owner's examples; code may not).

### 76.6 DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate)

| Checked | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `closing/count_config.py` (mig `501`) | **EXTENDED** — gained `value_kind`, `declared_by`, `unit_price`, `in_revenue` |
| `closing/tender_config.py` (mig `111`) | **REUSED** read-only into the catalog |
| `commcalc/management_incentive.py` (mig `852`) | **REUSED** — `resolve_plan`. Its framework is per-MANAGER and store-AGGREGATED, a different shape, so it was not bent to fit |
| `commcalc/commission_engine.py`, `boost_terms.py` | untouched — carrier commission, owned elsewhere |
| `commcalc/target_registry.py` (mig `070`) | not it — maps UPLOAD columns |
| `commcalc/targets` (`CATS`, `targets.*_monthly`) | **the next sibling, stated not hidden** — see §76.7 |

### 76.7 WHAT IS NOT DONE, STATED

- **Targets over the declared categories** (day / week / month gross revenue, and the backward "what is
  needed to reach X"). The engine already computes the backward figure — `GET /targets/{period}/calendar`
  serves `need`, `today_target`, `pace`, `open_days_left`, per store and per rep. Its **category axis**
  is hard-coded twice (the page's `CATS`, and four physical columns on `commcalc.targets`), so a store
  that sells no activations cannot set a target. That is its own change, and until it ships the
  targets editor remains the one surface still carrying a copy of the vocabulary.
- **Migration `1072` is SURFACED, NOT APPLIED.** Additive, idempotent, `-- REVERT:` noted, **no seed** —
  every new column defaults to the mig-`501` behaviour.

## 71. SIMILAR WORDS — a module nobody can name is a module nobody can find (owner directive 2026-10-10)

> **Section number:** this was written as §68 and renumbered to **§71** on merge. Four changes were
> in flight at once on 2026-10-10: #434 took §69, #433 had already moved off §67 onto §69 and so must
> move again, and #432 claims §68 with **migration `1068`** coupled to it. This change carries no
> migration and no §16–18 rows, so it was the cheapest of the four to move; §68 stays with the one
> whose migration number matches it and §70 is left clear for #433. That is the **third** number race
> in two days (§61/§62 on 2026-10-09, §67 the same evening) — the repo wants a reservation
> convention, not four agents each discovering the collision in a merge conflict.

**The report.** The owner had just been offered a dashboard tile for a new report, and declined the
remedy rather than the problem: *"having too many tilles will also cluter the space, leave it like
this but all modules should be searcable, index and found by susing similar wordslike a search
engine"*. Placing 24 more tiles answers the instance (this report is hard to find). Making every
module findable by the words a manager would actually type answers the class.

### 71.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

> **The catalogue carries the words on the MENU, and a person types the words in their HEAD. A
> search that only matches menu wording cannot find a module whose menu wording nobody guessed.**

§54 built the console: one ranker, one catalogue assembled from the registries that already exist,
one derived page index, one viewer gate (§54.12). It made every page *reachable*. It did not make
every page *nameable* — and that is a different fault, because 251 of the 354 catalogue entries are
**label only**: no alias, no description, nothing but the words somebody chose for the nav.

**Measured before anything was changed**, against the real registries (nav 376, reports 34, screens
47, routes 328 → 354 folded entries), with a 30-query corpus of what a manager plausibly types:

```
catalog: 354 entries | with aliases: 80 | with desc: 33 | label only: 251
11 of 30 queries return NOTHING
missing: headcount, wages, holiday, sick leave, rota, margin, turnover, clawback, trade in, …
```

"wages" finds nothing because the module is called **Payroll**. "rota" finds nothing because it is
called **Schedule**. "margin" finds nothing because it is **Gross Profit**. The module is right
there; the word is not.

### 71.2 Why a VOCABULARY, and not an alias on each page

The obvious fix is to add aliases to the 251 label-only entries. That is the patchwork the house
rules forbid, for three separate reasons:

- It is **O(pages)**, and it must be redone for every page added — exactly the thing that goes stale.
- It is a **second copy of the nav wording**, in a second place, which §19.18 has already caught
  three times.
- It would be **wrong twice over**: "wages" does not belong to Payroll alone, and whoever adds the
  next payroll page will not think to repeat it.

A vocabulary is **O(vocabulary)**: *"wages, payroll, salary, pay, compensation, earnings"* is one
fact, stated once, and it reaches the page added next year with no edit. One fact, one home,
dereferenced — never copied.

### 71.3 The one home

**`frontend/src/lib/search-vocabulary.ts`** — the ONE home for *"which words mean the same thing in
this platform"*. 60 groups, 535 terms, each group carrying a `note` saying what the group is for.

```ts
export const VOCABULARY: readonly VocabGroup[]           // { terms, note }
export const UNMAPPED: Readonly<Record<string, string>>  // word -> why it finds nothing
export function synonymsOf(t: string): string[]          // [] for digit runs and unknown words
export function phraseHits(q: string): string[]          // word-boundary multi-word matches
export function unmappedReason(q: string): string | undefined
```

Groups are **symmetric** (every term in a group expands to every other, phrases included) and
contain no carrier, tenant or product name — **RULE TWO**, enforced by §G's `FORBIDDEN` scan.

**`frontend/src/lib/search-rank.ts`** dereferences it. The import is deliberate and not an injected
argument, because *"wrote the registry without wiring the callers"* is the failure §19.18 names
three times over.

### 71.4 A synonym helps you FIND something; it does not let the console claim it UNDERSTOOD you

§54.10 settled a rule that a vocabulary could quietly undo: *a search that always returns its best
guess cannot tell a bad match from no match*, so an unexplained question goes to the assistant rather
than to the closest-looking page. If a synonym counted as coverage, *"which sales rep worked in 509
today"* would become "fully covered" and navigate again — the §54.10 defect, reintroduced by the fix
for a different one. It did, in testing, before this was added:

- `Hit` now carries **`literal`** (the words actually typed that matched) alongside `matched`.
- `fullyCovered` reads **`literal`**, never `matched`. §B5 of the proof replays the defect by
  rewriting `literal` → `matched` in the real source and asserts it goes red.
- `tokenScore` tries the **literal word first** and returns on a hit, and the sort breaks a tie on
  `literal.length`, so a vocabulary can never REORDER two pages that both match what was typed.
- Coverage counts **typed words only** — a synonym can surface a page, never certify a sentence.

**`UNMAPPED` is the honest register**: 8 words that still find nothing, each with the reason
(`trade in` → no trade-in module exists). §G asserts every reason is a real sentence and that a word
listed there genuinely finds nothing — one entry was removed during the build because it turned out
to find something, which is exactly what the check is for.

### 71.5 Locked so it cannot un-wire

- **§H** (the vocabulary proof): the ranker's import exists, BOTH halves are used, there is no second
  `VOCABULARY`, the vocabulary itself imports nothing, only one module declares it, and
  `fullyCovered` reads `literal`.
- **§A2 / §B11b** (`prove_search_console_lock.mjs`): the ranker's imports are an **ALLOWLIST** of
  exactly one — a second import is red, and *dropping* the vocabulary import is also red. The old
  rule there was "imports nothing", which was a proxy for the two things actually at stake (the
  ranker holds no registry; the proof can drive it under bare Node). It now names them.
- **§E, the RATCHET**: a frozen `FINDS_NOTHING_BASELINE` of everyday words that still find nothing.
  It is **1 word** and **may only shrink** — raising it means changing the number on purpose.
- **The multi-month OFFER lock allowlists SURFACES, and a word list is not one.**
  `harness_multimonth_offer_lock.py` names every frontend file that may mention multi-month without
  asking the pay-offer predicate, and one group's note said "Multi-Month Installments". The note is
  reworded rather than added to that allowlist: a vocabulary offers nothing, since what a search can
  reach is still decided by the §54.12 viewer gate, and the group's TERMS (`instalment`,
  `installments`) do not match the lock's pattern and still find the page. §G5d pins it.
- **The DERIVED carrier guard owns RULE TWO here, and a hand-written echo proved weaker.** §G5 was a
  local list of the obvious carrier and product names and it passed, while
  `harness_carrier_vocab_guard.py` — which DERIVES the vocabulary from the seed migrations and scans
  every `frontend/src/**/*.ts` — found two carrier-side page names (`PayGo`, `Asset Ledger`) in group
  **notes**, because the local check read only the TERMS. The notes are reworded, §G5b now scans the
  whole file including prose, and §G5c pins the file inside the derived guard's reach so the real
  check cannot stop covering it. The lesson generalises: a second copy of a derived fact is not a
  check, it is a thing that agrees until it matters.

### 71.6 One shared loader, because three proofs needed the same dance

`search-rank.ts` now imports through Next's `@/lib/...` alias, which bare Node cannot resolve, and
**three** proofs drive the ranker. Rather than copy the transpile-and-rewrite into three files,
`frontend/prove_load_ts.mjs` is the one home: `loadLibs(root, names, mutate)` recursively emits every
alias-imported lib into one temp dir rewriting the alias to a relative path, and its `mutate` hook
lets an ARMED control edit the real source **in flight** rather than keeping a deliberately wrong
copy on disk.

**It must not depend on `typescript`, and that cost a red CI run to learn.** The `search-console` job
runs with **no `npm ci`** — that is what keeps the whole guard in the seconds-not-minutes class — so
the loader's first version called `require('typescript')` to transpile, which passed locally (where
`node_modules` happens to exist) and died on the runner with `Cannot find module 'typescript'`.
Node strips erasable TypeScript itself, which is how these proofs drove these modules before the
alias existed, so the loader now emits `.mts` files and changes **only the import specifier**. The
fix was verified by re-running all five proofs from a copy of `src/` and the provers with no
`node_modules` present at all — 389 checks, the runner's condition reproduced rather than assumed.

### 71.7 Duplicate check (build gate)

Searched the index for an existing mechanism answering "which words mean this" before building.
Found and **extended, not duplicated**: §54.1's ranker (`search-rank.ts` — the one home for *"what
did the person mean"*, now dereferencing the vocabulary rather than growing a second scorer), §54.2's
catalogue fold, §54.7's derived page index, §54.12's viewer gate, and §54.10's never-guess rule
(tightened, not bypassed). Nothing new answers a question an existing path already answered; the
`menuless` baseline, the stopword list and the page registry all still have exactly one home.

### 71.8 Result, measured

```
BEFORE  11 of 30 everyday queries return NOTHING   (251 of 354 entries label-only)
AFTER    1 of 30 — "trade in", declared in UNMAPPED and pinned by the §E ratchet
```

On the proof's own 43-word corpus, §E5 (armed) reports **15 of 43 find nothing without the
vocabulary** and 1 of 43 with it. No ordering of two literal matches changed, no page became
reachable that a viewer could not already open (the gate is untouched), and no sentence became
"covered" that was not covered before.

### 71.9 Status

Code complete and proved: **394 checks** across five Node, dependency-free proofs
(`prove_search_rank.mjs` 114, `prove_search_catalog.mjs` 94, `prove_route_index.mjs` 59,
`prove_search_console_lock.mjs` 61, `prove_search_vocabulary.mjs` 66), run by the `search-console`
job in `.github/workflows/data-qa-guard.yml`, plus `harness_carrier_vocab_guard.py` (104 checks,
green under CI's Python 3.11) which owns the RULE TWO verdict on this file. **No migration, no
endpoint, no money moved** — this is
frontend ranking only. Nothing is switched on or off: the two existing search boxes (⌘K and ⌘/) both
dereference the ranker, so both gain the vocabulary on deploy.

**Registered in no §16–18 table, deliberately:** those are cross-references by TABLE, ENDPOINT and
METRIC, and this adds none of the three — like §54 itself, it is frontend ranking over registries
that already exist. The registration that matters here is the CI step and the §E ratchet.

**Files:** `frontend/src/lib/search-vocabulary.ts` (new, the one home),
`frontend/src/lib/search-rank.ts` (dereferences it; `Hit.literal`; phrases rejected as stems),
`frontend/prove_search_vocabulary.mjs` (new), `frontend/prove_load_ts.mjs` (new, shared loader),
`frontend/prove_search_rank.mjs` / `prove_search_catalog.mjs` / `prove_search_console_lock.mjs`
(wired to the loader; the lock's import rule narrowed to an allowlist).

## 69. A DECLARATION THE VOCABULARY CANNOT EXPRESS IS A HOLE IN THE VOCABULARY — the org's own word must be HONOURABLE, or a keyword guess stands in its place (owner ruling 2026-10-10)

Owner, on a decision card and again in his own words the same day: **"mdf is not equipment
ereimbursement- prepare and fix"**, and *"Its own MDF line"*. He approved the OUTCOME; the config
write that moves the money is SURFACED, not applied (§69.6).

§58 ruled that the org's own declaration beats the platform's keyword ladder. §66 ruled that a
component reached on a fallback basis is not evidence about the dollar. Both are right, and both left
the same hole open: **a declaration can only be HONOURED if the component vocabulary can express
it.** It could not, so §58 fell through to the ladder, said so honestly in `basis`, and a platform
guess kept booking the money.

### 69.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

> **A DECLARATION THE PLATFORM'S VOCABULARY CANNOT EXPRESS IS A HOLE IN THE VOCABULARY, NOT A FACT
> ABOUT THE DOLLAR — and while the hole is open, a keyword guess stands where the org's own word
> already exists.**

Measured live read-only, house org `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`, with the REAL functions
and the LIVE config (not read off the code):

    classify('Ramp Up Subsidy')            ->  component='REIMBURSEMENT',
                                               basis='declared_category_unmapped',
                                               declared=False, declared_category='MDF',
                                               subtype='subsidy'
    component_of_declared_category('MDF')  ->  None
    component_line('REIMBURSEMENT', {'REIMBURSEMENT': 'vip_reimb'}, 'carrier_comm') -> 'vip_reimb'

The org DOES declare that payment type into category `MDF` (`commcalc.payment_categories`, §57 — it
and `4.0 $1K Ramp Up Bonus`, 0 live rows, are its only two MDF declarations). The pay engine's own
`pay_data_quality.PLACEABLE_CATEGORIES` has listed `Commission`, `Re-imbursement`, `MDF` and
`Chargeback` as the categories the platform can place **all along** — and the four-component
vocabulary could express only two of them. So the money booked where a keyword rule for a subsidy
word put it: **$260,500.00, 40 rows of `commcalc.raw_comp_report`, March–September 2026**
($39,300.00/mo over 6 stores Mar–Jul, $32,000.00 over 5 in August and September, October 0.00 in that
feed) on the device-financing reimbursement line — while the `mdf_income` COA line
(`coa.py`: `("mdf_income", "MDF (market spiffs)", "revenue", "auto_opt", "store")`) got none of it.

The same payments sit in `raw_payment_detail` at 44 rows / $287,500.00 (Mar–Oct). October's $27,000
has not reached the comp feed — the known month-end lag, NOT a defect and not "fixed" here. The P&L
reads `raw_comp_report`; `coa.py` never selects `raw_payment_detail`.

### 69.2 THE MECHANISM CHOSEN, AND THE ONE REJECTED

Two shapes could place the dollar on the MDF line. They are not equivalent, and the criterion is
**which of them makes the org's DECLARATION the thing that places the dollar**:

| shape | what places the dollar | `basis` | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CHOSEN — the vocabulary expresses the category.** `carrier_map.COMPONENTS` gains the kinds of money the platform's own routing maps can already name a destination for, so `carrier_class_category_components` can map the declared category to a component and `carrier_component_lines` routes that component to a line | the org's declaration, through the path that already exists | **`declared`** | ONE path: category → component → line |
| REJECTED — a category→P&L-line map beside `component_line` | a second routing map | stays `declared_category_unmapped` — a FALLBACK | `component_line` already answers "which line does this money book to". A sibling keyed by category is two paths to one answer — the duplicate defect the index rules forbid — and they would drift the first time either was edited. It also leaves `basis` on a fallback, which §66's four callers correctly refuse to trust |

So `COMPONENTS` is `("RESIDUAL", "COMMISSION", "SPIFF", "REIMBURSEMENT", "MDF", "CHARGEBACK")`, still
spelled in exactly one place (`commcalc/carrier_map.py`) and dereferenced by §58's home. These are
KINDS OF MONEY — platform vocabulary, like the Gross-Profit column keys `mdf` and `chb` that have
been in the engine since §58.7. WHICH tenant category means which kind stays a config row
(`carrier_class_category_components`), and where each kind books stays a config row
(`carrier_component_lines`). RULE TWO is intact: no category, carrier or tenant name decides anything
in a branch.

**THE STRUCTURAL RULE THAT CLOSES THE CLASS**, locked so it cannot re-open: every Gross-Profit money
column except the unclassified one must be REACHABLE from some component, and every component must
HAVE a column. An unreachable column is a kind of money no org can declare into — which is exactly
what forced a guess — and a component with no column would turn real money into "unclassified" by
omission. Both halves fail the build (§69.5 §B5/§B6).

### 69.3 WHAT ELSE IS THE SAME FACT, AND THEREFORE MOVED INTO THE HOME

| fact | where it was | now |
|---|---|---|
| what a component is CALLED for a human | a private four-entry dict in the P&L carrier block (`_CC_LABEL`), defaulting to **"Undeclared"** | `carrier_dollar_class.COMPONENT_LABELS` / `component_label()`. The private dict would have rendered the owner's DECLARED MDF money under the word for money nobody declared. The existing wording is carried over unchanged, so the drill-down reads exactly as before |
| which component IS the device-financing side, and which LINE it books to | spelled `"REIMBURSEMENT"` at three call sites (two in `coa.py`, one derivation in `router.py`) | `DEVICE_FINANCING_COMPONENT` / `device_reimb_line()` / `device_reimb_components()` |
| the component vocabulary itself | a SECOND tuple in `commcalc/comp_trend.py` (`_COMPS`), which would have folded a new kind of money into its `UNMAPPED` bucket while the P&L booked it correctly | `carrier_map.COMPONENTS + ("UNMAPPED",)` — dereferenced; `UNMAPPED` is that report's own "no rule matched" bucket, not a component |
| the vocabulary the Carrier Mapping SCREEN offers | a hardcoded array of four in `frontend/src/app/(platform)/commcalc/carrier-mapping/page.tsx` | **HALF-DONE, deliberately, and said so.** `GET /commcalc/carrier-category-options` now SERVES `components` (additive), so the page has a source to read; the page still reads its own array, and wiring it is a visible UI change that waits for the owner's eyeball under the house merge policy. Until then the lock pins that array as a strict SUBSET of the vocabulary, so it can never offer a kind of money the platform does not know. **Consequence, stated: the dropdown on that screen cannot yet pick the two new kinds of money.** It edits the KEYWORD LADDER — the fallback — so nothing in the owner's ruling depends on it; the declaration path is `payment_categories` plus the config write in §69.6 |

**THE §65 SIBLING — a protection re-founded on the right fact, measured.** `router.is_device_dollar`
decides what the per-DEVICE reimbursement report counts, and §66 had it decline a dollar whose
component was reached on a fallback basis. Honouring the declaration makes this money's basis
`declared`, so that guard correctly stops protecting it — and the layer's OTHER rule, "the device
components are every component this org routed OFF the generic commission line", is an INFERENCE that
held only while exactly one component was routed anywhere. Measured both ways over the live config:

| `carrier_component_lines` | the pre-fix derivation | `device_reimb_components` |
|---|---|---|
| `{"REIMBURSEMENT": "vip_reimb"}` (live today) | `{REIMBURSEMENT}` | `{REIMBURSEMENT}` — identical, so nothing moves today |
| `{"REIMBURSEMENT": "vip_reimb", "MDF": "mdf_income"}` (after the owner's write) | `{REIMBURSEMENT, MDF}` — **$91,000.00 a month of per-store lump sums back inside a per-device report** | `{REIMBURSEMENT}` |

**So `GET /commcalc/device-line-reimbursement` does exactly what it did before, by design** — 140
devices / $43,568.83 and the September figures of §65 are unchanged — and it does so because the
question is now asked as it is meant ("which components book to the line the device-financing
reimbursement books to") instead of inferred from what else happened to be routed. A ramp subsidy is
a per-store lump sum with no device identifier; there is no phone for it to name.

### 69.4 THE MONEY — per month, house org, same live rows, both sides in one pass

Measured read-only over `commcalc.raw_comp_report` (78,053 rows for the org) with the REAL
`classify` / `component_line` / `gp_column*` functions, the LIVE declarations (154 rows) and the LIVE
keyword ladder (19 rules). The P&L side is what the owner's ruling moves; the Gross-Profit side is
unchanged because §66 already placed this money by the declared category.

| period | P&L `vip_reimb` before | after | P&L `mdf_income` before | after | moved | `carrier_comm` (unmoved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| March 2026 | 618,846.88 | 579,546.88 | 0.00 | 39,300.00 | 39,300.00 | 152,725.69 |
| April 2026 | 446,491.33 | 407,191.33 | 0.00 | 39,300.00 | 39,300.00 | 131,948.58 |
| May 2026 | 396,008.25 | 356,708.25 | 0.00 | 39,300.00 | 39,300.00 | 134,901.45 |
| June 2026 | 467,685.90 | 428,385.90 | 0.00 | 39,300.00 | 39,300.00 | 118,886.90 |
| July 2026 | 475,630.90 | 436,330.90 | 0.00 | 39,300.00 | 39,300.00 | 155,574.12 |
| August 2026 | 418,922.21 | 386,922.21 | 0.00 | 32,000.00 | 32,000.00 | 120,799.55 |
| September 2026 | 373,211.61 | 341,211.61 | 0.00 | 32,000.00 | 32,000.00 | 110,780.14 |
| October 2026 | 77,685.42 | 77,685.42 | 0.00 | 0.00 | **0.00** | 30,112.05 |
| **TOTAL** | **3,274,482.50** | **3,013,982.50** | **0.00** | **260,500.00** | **260,500.00** | **955,728.48** |

Each month's "after" re-sums to its "before" to the cent — the arithmetic statement that this is a
reclassification between two revenue lines and nothing else. **TOTAL REVENUE AND NET PROFIT DO NOT
MOVE in any month**: both lines are revenue, so the company and store totals are identical and only
the composition changes. October moves $0.00, which is the rows' own answer and not a blanket.

**The Gross-Profit report does not move either, in any month**: `comp_reimb` / `comp_mdf` /
`comp_comm` / `comp_chb` / `comp_unmapped` are byte-identical before and after on the comp side, and
the payment-detail side likewise (it reached the `mdf` column through the declared category already —
§66). Verified column-by-column over the same live rows. The MDF money's GP column is `mdf` both
before and after; what changes is that it now gets there through its component, which is why the two
can no longer disagree.

**The other two tenants are untouched, provably**: `commcalc.payment_categories` holds 154 rows and
every one of them belongs to the house org — the other two orgs declare NOTHING, so `classify` never
reaches the declared path for them and every answer is byte-identical whatever the vocabulary can
express. Neither has a `carrier_class_category_components` or `carrier_component_lines` row
(both NULL live).

### 69.5 THE LOCK

**`backend/harness_declared_category_honourable.py` — 76 checks**, DB-free, network-free, stdlib
only. **§A** THE REGRESSION: the live case as a fixture, the pre-fix answer (the keyword's component
standing on a declaration) armed as a DEAD control, and the dollar moving off the reimbursement line
onto the line the org named · **§B** the vocabulary IS the mechanism — one spelling, every PLACEABLE
category expressible and honoured, every component with a GP column, every GP money column reachable
from a component, `load_config` keeping a row that maps each kind (pre-fix it DROPPED the two it did
not know), and **the rejected shape absent from the tree** (no category→line map beside
`component_line`) · **§C** the whole CROSS-PRODUCT: for every placeable category and every contrary
keyword verdict the declaration wins and `basis` is `declared`, the line follows the declaration, and
the coverage report names the reclassification · **§D** declared money is never LABELLED undeclared
· **§E** the §65 sibling: the pre-fix derivation kept live and asserted to get it WRONG · **§F** the
measured restatement re-sums, and an org that declares nothing is byte-identical · **§G** THE
UN-WIRING LOCK: the callers must keep asking the home, the pre-fix comprehension may not come back,
the vocabulary / the labels / the device-side derivation may each exist in exactly ONE module, and
the carrier recon's own last-mile map is pinned to DEFER for a component it has no column for, and
the Carrier Mapping screen's own array of components is pinned as a strict SUBSET of the vocabulary ·
**§H** purity, RULE TWO, the module graph and this section.

Verified **RED** against the pre-fix tree, by checkout and run: **A3 A4 A6 A7 A8** (the declaration
not honoured, and the dollar still on the reimbursement line), **B3 B4 B6 B7 B8** (the kind of money
inexpressible, the GP column unreachable, and `load_config` DROPPING the org's own row), **C1 C2 C3
C6 C7** (the keyword guess winning the cross-product, and the coverage report calling the money
undeclared), and then the run DIES at **D1** — `component_label` does not exist pre-fix, which is the
private dict in the P&L that would have labelled declared money "Undeclared". The fixtures are built
through `load_config` over a stub row, deliberately: a hand-built config dict would sail past the
very gate that rejected the org's declaration, and the A-section would have passed on the pre-fix
tree. Wired into `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml` — paths
filter AND a step; counted before and after by parsing the workflow, not by eye: **jobs 23 → 23,
steps 204 → 205, paths-filter entries 420 → 423** (the lock, `comp_trend.py` and `coa.py`). Nothing
was removed — a silently deleted job removes its own gate.
`harness_component_basis_evidence.py` (61), `harness_carrier_dollar_class.py` (88),
`harness_gp_carrier_class_dereference.py` (65), `harness_device_line_reimbursement.py` (87) and
`harness_device_reimb_recon.py` (117) all stay green unchanged — the §66 fixture still reproduces the
pre-fix shape because the shipped DEFAULT map is deliberately unchanged (§69.6).

### 69.6 THE ACTIVATION IS A CONFIG WRITE, AND IT IS SURFACED — not a code default

The code ships INERT and byte-identical for all three tenants: the shipped default
`category_components` does NOT seed the two new kinds of money. That is deliberate and is the same
reason `carrier_component_lines` ships empty (§58). **Mapping a category is a money move**: it
decides which P&L line every payment type declared to that category books on, and the destination is
the owner's to name in the same breath. A default row would have restated a booked statement on
merge — and worse, with the destination defaulting to the caller's generic commission line, because
the house org's own `carrier_component_lines` row (live `{"REIMBURSEMENT": "vip_reimb"}`) replaces the
default map wholesale and has no row for a kind of money that did not exist when it was written.

So ONE self-committing SQL file does both halves in one statement, for the owner to paste into the
Supabase SQL Editor: **`/mnt/project-files/2026-10-10_mdf_books_on_its_own_pl_line.sql`**. No
migration is needed — `carrier_class_category_components` and `carrier_component_lines` are mig
`1062` columns and both exist live. The file writes `carrier_class_category_components` as the house
default map PLUS the two new rows (jsonb-merged over `COALESCE`, never assigned bare: assigning only
`{"mdf": "MDF"}` would drop the commission and reimbursement mappings and restate $3.1M), and
`carrier_component_lines` as the live routing PLUS `{"MDF": "mdf_income"}`. Idempotent, no
`BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` (the SQL Editor ends each Run's transaction, so a split transaction is silently
discarded), with a commented post-run verification query.

**AFTER the SQL is run, the P&L needs a Recompute for MARCH–SEPTEMBER 2026** (seven months; October
has no such row in the comp feed, so it is unaffected). The stored statements carry the old
composition until then, and nothing here recomputes one.

**DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate).** Searched: §58 / §58.1 / §58.2 / §58.4 / §58.5 / §58.7 (the

## 70. WHICH STORE CARRIES A HANDSET'S COST — the ledger stocks it, the carrier pays whoever sold it (owner directive 2026-10-10)

Owner, on the decision card: *"Move the cost"* — move device cost to the store the carrier paid, for
the proven transfers. The ask that led to it (§65): *"move the cost to a different store if this
happens but capture that in a report for phones activated under different report"*.

### 70.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

> **"Which store does this handset's cost belong to?" had two authorities and nothing reconciled them
> per device.** `commcalc.asset_ledger` books the unit's cost to the **stocking** store, on the row's
> own `store`. `commcalc.raw_payment_detail` pays the **activating** store. A phone stocked at one
> door and sold at another charged one store a cost whose reimbursement a different store received.

That is the same class §65 named for the reimbursement side, now answered on the cost side. It is not
652's problem and it is not one tenant's: the fix is the MECHANISM by which any cost row acquires a
store, for every caller of it.

**Measured live** (house org, read-only, 2026-10-10) — Jun–Oct 2026, through the shipped code:

| month | devices on the ledger | proven activated elsewhere | cost that moves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06 | 1,233 | 86 | $40,039.14 |
| 2026-07 | 1,474 | 118 | $47,148.82 |
| 2026-08 | 1,222 | 117 | $46,968.83 |
| 2026-09 | 1,029 | 135 | $56,958.65 |
| 2026-10 (partial) | 195 | 12 | $4,039.88 |
| | | **468** | **$195,155.32** |

Across 100 store pairs, and it **nets to $0.00 company-wide**: every dollar leaves one store and
lands on another. Consolidated COGS and consolidated gross profit do not move. What restates is each
STORE's gross profit — which is the point. The largest net movers in that window: `1750 5th Ave`
−$14,829.66, `1800 Great Neck Rd` +$13,689.72, `4712 White Plains Rd` −$13,089.74, `3605 Germantown
Ave` −$13,059.73, `3 Palisade Ave` +$11,399.57, `11636 Springfield Blvd` −$11,199.72.

### 70.2 THE GUARD THAT ASKED THE WRONG QUESTION — a design fix found by the owner's question

§65.4 shipped a third guard that withheld "the carrier paid a different store" whenever **either**
address was one §13d reports as claimed by two `store_mapping` records. The owner asked what the 23
withheld devices were (2026-10-10), and the answer was that the guard could not be right:

- An ambiguous identity is **one canonical address claimed by two codes**, and
  `build_store_resolver` step 3 places **both codes on that same canonical key**. So a payment under
  either code is already counted at that store and can never reach the "different store" branch —
  **the guard could not fire for its own stated reason.**
- What it actually caught was pairs of two plainly different addresses (`1750 5th Ave` is not `1800
  Great Neck Rd`), so **all 23 withholdings were false**: $6,164.95 of payments and $9,769.77 of cost
  withheld from a verdict the evidence supported.
- The fact that genuinely makes two addresses one store is the **relocation shape** — one `store_code`
  or one `salesforce_id` (the carrier's own door) on record at two addresses. Measured the same day:
  **zero of either** across the house org's 34 records.

**The fix is the question, re-keyed, in the identity home.** `store_identity.shared_identity_pairs`
derives the pairs that may be one store; `store_identity.may_be_one_store(a, b, pairs)` is the
predicate; `coa.shared_store_identity_pairs` is the I/O twin that reads the rows. The pure layer takes
the **predicate**, for the same reason it takes `classify` and `resolve_store` — the rule stays in its
own home and `device_reimb_recon` keeps no copy, not even a set-membership test. A **pair relation**,
never a per-address flag, because nothing about one address can answer a question about two. ALL, not
ANY: one payment at an address that cannot be this store proves the transfer. The superseded
`coa.ambiguous_store_keys` is **deleted**, and §K11 fails the build if any caller reaches for it
again. `ambiguous_identities` itself stays — §13d's report of the collisions is a legitimate and
different use.

### 70.3 THE ONE HOME — and it dereferences §65 rather than forming a second opinion

| | |
|---|---|
| **The verdict** ("where was this device activated") | `commcalc/device_reimb_recon.activation_store_moves(rows)` — derived from §65's own `device_lines` rows, from `LINE_PAID_OTHER_STORE` and nothing else |
| **The declaration** | `account_config.device_cost_store_basis` (mig 1069), resolved by `account/device_cogs.resolve_device_cost_store_basis` |
| **The I/O read** | `device_cogs.load_device_cost_store_basis` · `device_cogs.load_activation_index` (which calls `commcalc.router._device_line_reimb_run`, §65's one assembly, and reads neither feed itself) |
| **The placement** | `device_cogs.cost_store(ledger_store, device_id, activation)` — **the only place a device's cost is given a store** |
| **The caller** | `device_cogs._vip_sold_cost`, every unit through `cost_store`; `coa.build_inputs` hands the period down |

`cost_store` returns the placement **and why**, from three reasons —
`distributor_ledger_store` · `carrier_paid_store` · `unmeasured_stays_put` — so a reader never has to
infer whether a store's cost moved, stayed, or could not be judged. The restatement is reported on the
line's `meta`: `moved_to_activating_store` (devices, amount, store pairs) and `unmeasured_stayed_put`
(devices, amount). A moved store figure is never silent.

### 70.4 OFF UNTIL DECLARED, AND IT FAILS IN THE SAFE DIRECTION

`device_cost_store_basis` NULL ⇒ `stocking` ⇒ **byte-identical** to every figure this module produced
before §70. Only the declared word `activating` moves a cost (case and surrounding space folded, the
same way the sibling mig-1041 basis folds its own). A cost moves ONLY on a proven activation
elsewhere; a device with no identifier, a short month, a possibly-same-store pair, an unreadable
reconciliation, or an org with no device-financing routing declared **moves nothing**, stays on the
ledger's store, and says so. A cost is never left unplaced and never moved on a verdict nobody proved.

**The sibling, excused explicitly.** The MA/VidaPay cost path (`device_cogs._ma_sold_cost`) places
cost by an account→store index and its rows carry **no device identifier**, so §65's per-device
verdict cannot reach it. Excused — and PINNED: §H6 asserts that path is identifier-free, so the day it
gains one the check goes red and the sibling must be fixed too.

### 70.4a THE OWNER STATEMENT, VERSIONED

The column is migration `1067`; declaring `activating` is a separate owner-approved statement, and it
lives at **`database/runbooks/device_cost_store_activating.sql`** — the column and the declaration in
one paste, printing the declarations before and after, as ONE Supabase SQL Editor Run that commits
itself (a BEGIN in one Run and a COMMIT in another is silently discarded). It is versioned in the
repo rather than left in a chat share, because an owner statement that exists only in a share cannot
be audited later. **A recompute follows** for each month to be restated (Jun–Oct 2026); a month that
is not recomputed keeps its stored per-store figures. Undo is `SET device_cost_store_basis = NULL`
plus the same recomputes.

### 70.5 THE LOCK

`harness_device_inventory_cogs.py` **§H** (the harness that already owns the device-cost basis; 70 →
89 checks, 0 failed). H1 the home exists and is pure · H2/H2b/H2c off until declared, exhaustive over
every input, with the folding rule pinned against its sibling · H3–H3c the placement ladder ·
**H3d/H3e the controls** (the same proven verdict moves nothing undeclared; no junk index can move a
cost) · H4 the cost side assembles nothing and reads §65's own verdict reader · H4b only proven
transfers become moves · H4c the two dollar columns never netted · H5 the cost loop keeps no placement
rule · **H5b `coa` hands the period down** (the §19.18 un-wiring failure mode) · H5c the restatement
is reported on the line's meta · **H5e and stated ON the statement line itself**, because `meta`
alone never reaches a reader — the §K3(b) lesson applied to a restatement, with the honest zero still
winning where both could apply · H5d one reader, no second · H6 the sibling's excuse, pinned ·
H7 RULE TWO.

`harness_device_line_reimbursement.py` **§K is RESTATED, not relaxed** (84 → 89 checks): the predicate
is injected (K1), a possibly-same-store pair withholds (K2), **the defect that named this** — an
address with two records paid at an unrelated one is a PROVEN transfer (K3) — ALL not ANY (K6), the
one home and the router's binding of it (K9/K10), **the superseded name is gone from every caller**
(K11), and two controls (K12/K13). `A9b` is RESTATED the same way: it used to forbid the name
`store_identity` anywhere in the router's run function as shorthand for "derives no identity"; it now
says what it always meant — the router may NAME the home's answers (`may_be_one_store`) and must never
build a key itself (no `store_identity_index`, `build_store_resolver`, `squash_key`, `lead_num_key`,
`store_key(`, `split(`).

### 70.6 DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate)

Searched §64 (store identity, `store_identity_index`, `ambiguous_identities`), §65 (the per-device
reconciliation and its guards), §42.5 / §42.1 / §42.3 (the device-cost basis and its three
consequences), §23n (the dead inventory predicate), §19.53 (the store-month recon), §13d (the identity
audit), §4 / §4e (the P&L engine and the drill grain), §16–18. **REUSED, not rebuilt:** §65's
`device_lines` verdict and `_device_line_reimb_run` assembly (the cost side reads neither feed), §64's
resolver and identity index, §42.5's `account_config` declaration pattern and its `load_*` defensive
read, `device_cogs._vip_sold_cost`'s existing dedup and fee exclusion, and both existing locks
(extended, never duplicated). **BUILT NEW:** one pure verdict reader (`activation_store_moves`), one
pure pair relation and predicate in the identity home, one declaration + resolver + placement in the
cost home, one nullable column (mig 1069), and the config read/write on the existing
`/account/config` endpoint. **Nothing else:** no new table, no new endpoint, no new report, no
frontend change, and no second store resolver.

Module-graph fact: `device_cost_store` — new, because "which store carries a handset's cost" is a
question no existing fact answered; its callers are DERIVED from the import graph (§50) and its locks
are the two above. Written by hand, multi-line (never `--bless` — §50).

**Section number:** this section was written as `67`, then `69`, and is `70`. Each renumber was a
concurrent PR merging first and taking the number (`67` + migration `1067` to the bank-deposit work,
`69` to the honourable-declaration ruling above, `68` already claimed in flight). The migration
number `1069` is NOT renumbered — it is unique on disk and uniqueness is the only property the
numbering lock asserts (`harness_unique_numbers_lock.py`); a migration number does not have to match
its index section, and renaming an applied-or-pending file is the riskier change. See the
index-section-number race in §62.

## 75. THE FRONTEND TYPE CHECK IS A CHECK — a type error must fail something, not only a deploy nobody is required to read (owner directive 2026-10-10)

Owner, verbatim: *"fix the frontend type error"*.

### 75.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

The instance: a `SCREENS` entry whose key sat outside the closed `ScreenKey` union in
`frontend/src/components/ScreenLink.tsx`. It was found **by hand** with `npx tsc --noEmit` during the
§68 work, and it is already fixed and merged — so this section is not about it.

The class is the reason it stayed hidden: **nothing in `.github/workflows/` ran the TypeScript
compiler at all.** Measured on `origin/main` (`1c73ba09`) before any of this was designed:

- `frontend/package.json` declared exactly `dev`, `build`, `start`, `lint` — **no type-check script**.
- Across all ten workflows, the only occurrence of `tsc` was a **comment** describing a proof that
  transpiles ONE display module. No job, step or script ran `tsc`, `typecheck` or `type-check`.
- So all **49** checks on every head of PR #432 were green while the Vercel deploy was **red on every
  one of them** — and Vercel is not a required check, so its red told nobody.

This is §19.18's class once more: a mechanism that fully exists (TypeScript, `strict: true` already
set in `frontend/tsconfig.json`) with **no caller wired to it**. Fixing the union and stopping there
would have left the next type error exactly as invisible as this one was.

### 75.2 WHAT MAIN ACTUALLY MEASURED — and therefore NO debt file

Measured on a clean `origin/main` with the repo's own compiler (`typescript@5.9.3`), after a real
`npm ci`:

| What | Measured |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` over the whole frontend | **0 errors** |
| Files in the program / under `frontend/src` | 1309 / **547** (every `.ts`/`.tsx` on disk) |
| Same, WITH Next's generated route types (`next typegen`) | **0 errors** |
| `@ts-nocheck` / `@ts-ignore` / `@ts-expect-error` under `frontend/` | **0 / 0 / 0** |
| `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors` in `next.config.ts` | absent |

Main is **clean**, so this ships as a plain gate that must stay clean. It deliberately does **NOT**
get a pinned debt list in the shape of `frontend/table_sort_pending.txt` or
`backend/harness_unrun_pending.txt`: there is no debt to register, and a ratchet file holding zero
entries is a decoration that teaches the next reader the gate is negotiable. If the frontend had been
red, that ratchet shape — and not a relaxed `tsconfig` — would have been the answer.

### 75.3 THE ONE HOME, AND THE GATE

**One home for the command.** `frontend/package.json` now declares

    "typecheck": "next typegen && tsc --noEmit"

CI **dereferences** that script (`npm run typecheck`) rather than spelling the compiler invocation a
second time, so what CI checks is exactly what a developer runs — the §19.18 "one fact, one home,
dereferenced, never copied" rule applied to a command. `next typegen` is inside the script because it
generates `next-env.d.ts` (gitignored) and `.next/types/**`, both of which `tsconfig.json` already
`include`s; without it CI would check strictly LESS than the Vercel build does.

**The gate.** Job `frontend-typecheck` in `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml` — checkout,
`setup-node@v4` (node 22), `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`, `npm run typecheck`.

*Why that workflow, and not a new one (the duplicate-check gate).* `carrier-vocab-guard.yml` already
fires on `frontend/src/**` for **both** `pull_request` and `push`, already declares the top-level
`defaults: run: shell: bash` that `harness_ci_pipefail_lock.py` requires, and already carries the
`setup-node` + `npm ci --ignore-scripts` recipe in its `pl-drill-path-proof` job. A new workflow would
duplicate all three. *Why its own job, and not a step inside `pl-drill-path-proof`:* a whole-frontend
type failure must not report as "P&L drill-path proof" failing, and the two gates should not share a
runtime.

*Why the path filter was widened.* `frontend/src/**` alone does **not** match `frontend/tsconfig.json`,
`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `next.config.ts` or `site-routing.ts` — every one of which can
introduce or hide a type error. The filter now names **`frontend/**`** on both `pull_request` and
`push`, plus the lock's own harness (the §13e lesson: a harness at the backend root is outside the
`backend/app` glob it guards). **A gate that skips silently on the very file that broke the build is
worse than no gate, because it reports green.**

### 75.4 THE LOCK — so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_frontend_typecheck_lock.py` — **33 checks**, stdlib only, DB-free. It runs **in the
`frontend-typecheck` job itself**, as the first run step, before `npm ci` (it needs no `node_modules`),
so its verdict is reported even when `tsc` is what goes red. It is deliberately NOT in the
dependency-free `carrier-vocab-guard` job: a lock belongs with the gate it guards, and in that 94-step
job it would sit behind 90 unrelated steps, any one of whose failure would stop it running at all
(§19.25). It fails the build on each way the gate could quietly stop being one:

| | Fails the build when |
|---|---|
| (a) | `frontend/package.json` has no `typecheck` script, or one that does not run `tsc --noEmit` |
| (b) | no workflow runs `npm run typecheck`, or runs it in a job that never installs `node_modules` (§19.25: a gate that dies on its first line is not a gate) |
| (c) | a workflow **runs** `tsc --noEmit` itself instead of dereferencing the script — a second home that will drift |
| (d) | the gate's workflow `pull_request` or `push` filter stops covering `frontend/**` — i.e. the gate could skip silently |
| (e) | `tsconfig.json` drops `strict: true` / `noEmit: true`, drops a source glob from `include`, or `exclude`s anything under `src` |
| (f) | `next.config.ts` sets `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true` — the one switch that silences the only signal that reported this defect |
| (g) | a blanket `@ts-nocheck` or `@ts-ignore` appears anywhere under `frontend/` (both at 0 today). `@ts-expect-error` is deliberately **permitted**: it fails the build once the error it names is gone, so it cannot rot, and banning the honest form pushes people to the dishonest one |
| (h) | any rule above has stopped being able to go RED — every one is driven against a synthetic input |

Verified RED against the pre-fix tree: run against `origin/main`'s own `package.json` and workflows it
reports 4 failures and exits 1, naming (a) and (b).

Two of its own negative controls caught real bugs in it while it was being written — a job-boundary
slice that read every correctly-wired job as having no install, and a second-home scan that flagged
the lock's own job comment and step `name:` for *saying* `tsc --noEmit` while running nothing. A prose
mention is not a second home; a `run:` value is, and only `run:` values are scanned now.

### 75.5 What this does NOT do, stated so it is not mistaken for done

- **FOUND AND NOT FIXED: this repo's harnesses are Python-version-sensitive, and
  `harness_carrier_vocab_guard.py` goes RED on Python 3.12+ while CI pins 3.11.** On Python 3.13 it
  reports `modules/commcalc/router.py:22512` as naming a migration in a shape the setup-notice
  boundary would miss, and its own negative control N10 fails too. That line is an implicitly
  concatenated `str` + f-string (`"… (is migration " f"248_….sql applied?): {e}"`), and **PEP 701**
  changed f-string tokenisation in 3.12, so the AST walk reads it differently. Verified both ways:
  on a pristine `origin/main` worktree the harness exits 1 under `python3.13` and **0 under
  `python3.11`**, and the CI run for `1c73ba09` is green. So it is a FALSE red that only a developer
  on a modern Python sees — CI is honest. Nothing here is broken in production, and this change does
  not fix it: the harness is in another subsystem and the fix (pin the harnesses' parse to the
  version CI runs, or make the walk PEP-701-proof) is owed its own change. Recorded because the next
  agent will hit it, spend time on it, and may "fix" live code to satisfy a phantom.
- **It does not make the Vercel deploy a required check.** That is a repository setting, not code, and
  it is the other half of this class: a build host whose red is advisory. Worth the owner's one toggle.
- **It does not run ESLint as a gate.** `npm run lint` exists and nothing runs it either. Same class,
  separate change — the eslint surface was not measured here and a gate nobody measured first is how
  a debt file gets invented.
- **It does not type-check `frontend/prove_*.mjs`.** Those are plain `.mjs`, outside `tsconfig.json`'s
  `include`, and each is already executed by its own CI job.
- **`website/`** was checked for a sibling frontend: it is plain HTML/CSS with no `tsconfig.json`, so
  there is no second type-check path to wire.

### 75.6 Cross-references

Registers **no table, no endpoint, no metric and no report** — so §16 (by TABLE), §17 (by ENDPOINT)
and §18 (by METRIC/KPI) carry nothing for it, and a row invented in any of them would be noise in the
cross-reference people rely on. What it registers is a CI gate and a lock:

- `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml` → job `frontend-typecheck`, which runs BOTH the lock and `npm run typecheck`; `frontend/**` on both the `pull_request` and `push` path filters.
- `frontend/package.json` → the `typecheck` script (the one home).
- `backend/harness_frontend_typecheck_lock.py` → the lock (33 checks).
- Ratchet precedents read and deliberately NOT copied: §19.25 / `harness_unrun_pending.txt` + `PINNED_MAX`, and `frontend/table_sort_pending.txt` (§75.2 says why).
- Same class: §19.18 (a mechanism written, callers left unwired), §19.25 (a gate that cannot run is not a gate), §13e (a harness outside the glob it guards).

Variance) took `72` while this was open, `#437` took `73`, and `#439` took `74` minutes after this
section was renumbered TO `74`. Each time the later arrival moved, never theirs. Same race as
