reads the same free number. Worth a real fix (claim-on-open, or stop numbering sections at all). Nothing outside this section
depended on the number except four §-references in `carrier-vocab-guard.yml`, which moved with it.
Renumbering file-wide also rewrote #435's OWN `index §72` reference in its cash-variance step name;
that was caught by diffing the workflow against `origin/main` and restored.

## 72. A VARIANCE BETWEEN TWO CASH FIGURES IS MEANINGLESS UNLESS BOTH COUNT THE SAME CASH (owner ask 2026-10-10)

Owner, verbatim: *"need to create a report after management recon to assess the shortage and overage
based on what the management received compared with the b2b data and the cash envelope, the data will
never match so we ignore upto $5 of variance, the system should then be smart to find the trends of a
particular store / employee and highlight the same- ti shoudl be all dynamic with all filters"*.

### 72.1 The owner is right that the data never matches, and the reason is not shortage

Measured on live house-org data 2026-09-01 → 2026-10-10, **before** any of this was written:

| Comparison | Inside $5 | Over | Short |
|---|---|---|---|
| management count vs the figure stored on the pickup row | 113 | 21 | **141** |
| management count vs the NET store cash (drawer − declared bill-pay) | **194** | 70 | 11 |
| rep's declared drawer vs `closing_attempt.b2b_cash` | 36 | 114 | 16 |
| rep's declared drawer NET vs `b2b_cash` | 1 | 3 | **162** |

Six of the "shortages" were checked by hand and were the bill-payment cash **to the cent**:
574−324=250, 866−585=281, 240−200=40, 335−260=75, 1699−929=770, 1378−1083=295. The money had left
the store in the OTHER envelope (`billpay_pickup`). A report built on naive subtraction would have
accused nine named employees of about **$20,000** they never took.

### 72.2 The class, not the instance

The instance is "the management count reads short by the bill-pay cash". The class is that
**subtraction does not care what its operands mean**, so any reader holding two bare floats can
manufacture a shortage out of a definition. The platform already RECORDED the basis of each figure
and had nowhere to use it: `cash_pickup.amount_basis` (mig `1039`), `envelope_count.basis`
(mig `1036`), `deposit_recon.cash_for_basis` (mig `509`).

So in `closing/cash_variance.py` **a cash figure is never a float**. It is `leg(amount, basis,
source)`, and `compare()` returns `measured: False` with a reason — `leg_absent` / `basis_unknown` /
`basis_mismatch` — instead of a number. There is no overload taking two bare floats, so a caller
cannot opt out. `harness_cash_variance.py` §B/§C fail the build if it ever subtracts across bases,
replaying all six live store-days above as a regression.

**Absence is never zero.** `billpay_pickup` holds 50 rows of which exactly ONE is counted, so the
whole-drawer management figure is NOT MEASURABLE on 264 of 275 counted store-days. The report says so
(`blockers`) rather than reconstructing the uncounted envelope as $0.00 and billing the rep for it.

### 72.3 The three legs, each from the ONE table that records it

| Leg | Source | Basis, and how it is known |
|---|---|---|
| management received | `envelope_count.counted_amount` (mig `936`) first, else `cash_pickup.actual_picked_amount` (mig `949`) | `envelope_count.basis` (mig `1036`), else `PICKUP_BASIS_TO_CASH[cash_pickup.amount_basis]` (mig `1039`: `off`/`none` ⇒ whole drawer, `pos`/`declared` ⇒ store cash). NULL ⇒ **unknown**, never inferred — 181 of 275 live rows, 126 of which would "tie" on the net basis |
| the cash envelope | `daily_closing.t_cash` (fallback `store_cash`) | `total_cash` **by definition** — owner 2026-09-02, *"Total cash in store including Bill Payments"*. It does NOT net: 81 live store-days declare more bill-pay cash than total cash, so netting would produce negative cash |
| B2B cash | `closing_attempt.b2b_cash` (mig `103`) | `total_cash`, PROVEN not assumed: the gate compares it against `entered_cash`, which equals `t_cash` on all 166 live store-days |

Where BOTH envelopes were counted the two are added and the leg is promoted to the whole drawer,
which is the only thing that makes the end-to-end POS check possible at all.

**NO SECOND DERIVATION.** `router._b2b_day` is deliberately NOT replayed: the POS cash for a
(store, day, rep) is already stored at exactly this grain, and it is the figure the rep was judged
against. The verdict is `deposit_recon.status_for` — the platform's existing truth table — so
negative is short here like everywhere else.

### 72.4 The $5 band is config, never code (RULE TWO)

`HOUSE_BAND = 5.00` is the ONE literal in the subsystem; the per-org override is
`commcalc.cash_pickup_config.cash_variance_band` / `.cash_variance_min_days` (mig `1070`, on the
EXISTING per-org config table for this chain — a new table for two numbers would be the sibling the
index rules forbid). NULL / blank / negative / unparseable resolve to the house default, **never to
zero**: zero would make every rounding difference a shortage against a named employee.
`harness_cash_variance.py` §F fails the build if a second non-zero dollar literal appears in the
module or if the endpoint spells a band of its own.

**NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD.** Six existing readers each carry their own band as a default argument
— `deposit_recon.status_for` ($1), `envelope_report.count_fields` ($0), `deposit_accountability.
pos_next_to` ($1) / `.dm_shortage_rows` ($0), `billpay_pickup.billpay_pos_mismatch` ($1),
`external_credit_recon.recon_row` ($0). Widening them to $5 would SILENTLY STOP SURFACING variances
those screens report today, which is a money-visibility change nobody asked for. They are excused
here deliberately, not overlooked: the one home now exists and migrating each screen is its own
reviewable change.

### 72.5 The trends

`cash_variance.trends()` runs over the rollups `by_store` / `by_employee` already produced, so a
highlight can never disagree with the table under it. Four kinds, declared as data:
`repeat_short` · `repeat_over` · `one_direction` (a run that is only ever one way — random counting
error lands on both sides) · `nothing_measurable` (every day unmeasurable, so the subject is invisible
to the control rather than clean). The threshold is `min_days` (house 3), which deliberately matches
`flag_registry.DEFAULT_PARAMS['CASH_REPEAT_VARIANCE']['min_days']` — the same question already had an
answer on the findings side and two answers would be the divergence.

This is a REPORT, not a watchdog. `cash_watchdog` (§53) owns cash FINDINGS off the submit trail; this
module compares the RECEIPT side, writes nothing, and assigns no chargeback — `envelope_report.
chargeback_parent_row` stays the one home for turning a counted shortage into money off a rep's pay,
from a screen where a human ticks the box.

### 72.6 Surfaces

- `GET /closing/cash-variance?date_from=&date_to=&markets=&market=&stores=&reps=&verdict=` — RULE FIVE
  standard filters (bucket-aware markets, manager-span keyset at admission) + `verdict`
  (`short|over|ok|not_measured|discrepancy`). Serves `rows`, `totals`, `by_store`, `by_employee`,
  `trends`, `blockers`, and the `pairs` / `bases` vocabularies so the screen spells no pair key, no
  basis word and no label. READ-ONLY.
- `/closing/cash-variance` — Cash Variance. Nav: Daily Closing group, `tileOnly` (so it is a dashboard
  tile, not a sidebar row — the owner's 2026-09-01 "cleaner look" ruling); ⌘K via `route-index.ts`.
  Placed ABOVE Bank Deposit because `prove_deposit_recon_nav.mjs` locks ePay Recon and Cash Deposit
  Recon as adjacent.
- Migration `1070` (additive, nullable, no backfill; 💰 moves no money).

### 72.7 Seams, reported not hidden

- **The bill-pay envelope is essentially never counted** (1 of 50 rows), so the end-to-end check is
  unmeasurable almost everywhere. No report code can fix that; somebody has to count the envelope.
- **181 of 275 counted pickups predate mig `1039`** and carry no basis, so they are unmeasurable here
  by design. They become measurable as new pickups are recorded, with no backfill and no guess.
- **81 store-days declare more bill-payment cash than total cash** — a subset exceeding its whole, the
  same defect `billpay_netting` documents as the reason the declared figure cannot be netted by. Left
  visible as a blocker rather than absorbed into arithmetic.
- **`envelope_count` holds 1 row**, so the preferred leg of the ladder is almost unused and the
  pickup side carries this report today — which is exactly why its basis had to be honoured rather
  than assumed.
- Identity is `employee_name`, the only identity `daily_closing` carries, so same-named people merge
  and a rename splits a history. The `stores` column makes a merge visible.
- **Section number**: §68 was claimed in flight by an open PR and §69–71 are taken, so this is §72;
  migration `1070` is NOT renumbered to match (uniqueness is the only property
## 73. A CASH FIGURE A HUMAN TYPED IS A STATEMENT BY THAT HUMAN — replacing it without keeping the old one destroys evidence (owner ask 2026-10-10)

Owner, verbatim: *"also need to edit the cash entered by the management during cash recon"*.

### 73.1 Two defects wearing one hat

1. **No way in.** The deposit-accountability board offered `📂 open & count` on a **SEALED** envelope
   only (§67.2). Once a count existed the cell rendered *"N counted · by X"* as text, so a typo — a
   transposed figure, a count entered against the wrong envelope — could not be corrected from the
   screen it was entered on.
2. **And no record if you got in anyway.** All three writers of a management cash count UPDATE or
   UPSERT in place, so a second save REPLACED the first with nothing kept: not the previous figure,
   not who had entered it, not that it had ever been different.

### 73.2 The class, not the instance

Defect 2 is **migration `935` happening again** — that migration exists because *"the verification
row is an UPSERT, so a second DM save overwrote the previous `dm_*` correction with no history"*. The
same sentence was true of a cash count, and a cash count is worse: when it reads short,
`envelope_report.chargeback_parent_row` can turn it into money off a named rep's pay.

So the fix is not an edit button on one screen. It is ONE append-only trail that EVERY writer of a
management cash count appends to:

| Writer | Screen | Table |
|---|---|---|
| `router._confirm_pickup_impl` | Cash Pickup / Bill Payment Pickup | `cash_pickup` / `billpay_pickup` |
| `router._open_count_impl` | the late open on the recon board (§67.2) | `cash_pickup` / `billpay_pickup` |
| `router.save_envelope_count` | Management Envelope Receipt (§12) | `envelope_count` |

`closing/count_revision.revision_rows` is the ONE place that decides what a correction IS; the router
has ONE writer, `_write_count_revisions`, that inserts what it returns.
**`harness_cash_count_revision.py` §D fails the build** if a writer of a count column stops calling
it, if anything else inserts into the table, or if anything updates or deletes a revision row — so
the trail cannot un-wire, which is the failure mode §19.18 records three times.

`_confirm_pickup_impl` previously had no prior value to compare (it upserts blind), so it now does
ONE batched read of the existing rows for the dates in the batch. Without that, the trail would have
covered one of two pickup writers — the half-fixed defect CLAUDE.md calls *"the same defect wearing a
hat"*.

### 73.3 What is recorded, and what is not

- **Only a real change.** Re-saving the same number writes nothing (compared on **rounded cents**, so
  `250` and `250.00` are one figure; text trimmed). A **first entry is not a correction** — nothing
  was overwritten. A value being **REMOVED is** a correction: a figure taken away is exactly what a
  reviewer needs to see. `$0.00 → $0.00` is a no-op, `absent → $0.00` a first entry, `$0.00 → absent`
  a correction.
- **The write, not a diff.** `revision_rows` takes the writer's own patch, so a field the writer never
  touched can never be logged as changed.
- **Money and text in separate columns**, so a figure is never read back out of a string and a
  reviewer can total the corrections.
- **Re-attribution counts.** Changing `actual_counted_by` / `counted_by` is a change like moving the
  figure — a count silently re-attributed to a different person is still a different statement.
- **Never a change without a changer, never a lost change either.** `changed_by` is NULLABLE and a
  NULL reads as *not recorded*; dropping the revision because the actor is unknown would lose the
  evidence to protect the attribution, which is backwards.
- **The reason is OPTIONAL.** A correction refused for want of a reason is a correction that does not
  happen; the un-reasoned edit is on the record either way.

### 73.4 Why a new table and not a column (the duplicate-check gate)

A column cannot hold a HISTORY: one `previous_amount` keeps only the last-but-one value, the same
defect one step back. The existing audit tables are each bound to their own subject
(`daily_closing_verification_audit` mig `935` is keyed on a verification row and names the six `dm_*`
money columns; the `core.access_log` family records READS, not value changes), so none can carry a
cash count from three different tables. `commcalc.cash_count_revision` (mig `1071`) is deliberately
**subject-parameterised** — `subject_table` is a VALUE, not a branch (RULE TWO) — so the fourth count
writer needs no fourth audit table. Its CHECK constraint is pinned to `count_revision.SUBJECTS` by the
harness, so the database cannot hold a subject the module has no behaviour for.

### 73.5 Surfaces

- **Module:** `backend/app/modules/closing/count_revision.py` — PURE (no I/O, no framework
  import, no clock of its own; the caller passes `changed_at`). Proof:
  `backend/harness_cash_count_revision.py`.

- `POST /closing/pickup/open-count` · `/closing/billpay-pickup/open-count` — now accept an optional
  `note` and return `corrections` / `history_recorded` / `history_detail`. `POST /closing/pickup`
  and `POST /closing/envelope-count` return `corrections` / `history_recorded` too.
- `GET /closing/deposit-accountability` — each envelope carries `pickup_row_id`, `corrections` and
  `correction_history` (sentences built by `count_revision.describe`, so the screen words nothing
  itself), plus a board-level `corrections` fold over the **visible** rows only (keyset consistency,
  like `summary`) and `history_available`.
- `/closing/deposit-recon` — a **counted** envelope now carries `✏️ edit`, the modal pre-fills the
  stored figure, offers a reason, lists what has already been corrected, and the reply says when a
  correction saved but its history could not be recorded (never silently).
- Migration `1071` (new table, append-only; 💰 moves no money — it books nothing, pays nothing,
  settles nothing, and no payout path reads it).

### 73.6 Seams, reported not hidden

- **Adaptive, not blocking** (the mig-201 precedent): on an un-migrated database the correction still
  records the COUNT and the response says the history was not recorded. A trail that refused the edit
  would be a worse outcome than a missing trail.
- `amount_moved` is the sum of **ABSOLUTE** deltas, not the net: `+$200` then `−$200` is two people's
  figures being changed, not nothing happening.
- Correcting a count can change a variance that a human later turns into a chargeback — through the
  EXISTING, human-ticked `envelope_report` flow (§12), never from here. This module creates no
  liability and settles none.
- A revision whose `changed_at` is missing still appears in its own history rather than being dropped.
- **Section number**: §68 and §72 were claimed in flight by open PRs, §69–71 are taken, so this is
  §73; migration `1071` is not renumbered to match (uniqueness is the only property
  `harness_unique_numbers_lock.py` asserts). See the index-section-number race in §62.

## 74. A COUNT OF THE WHOLE ENVELOPE IS NOT COMPARABLE WITH A NETTED EXPECTATION (owner question 2026-10-10)

Owner, verbatim: *"on teh management recon for 3 pl on 10/2 it shows declard on envelope is 552 but
written on enevelp 671 actual cash is 671 , where is the 552 coming from"*.

**Module:** `backend/app/modules/closing/billpay_netting.py` (the gate) ·
`backend/app/modules/closing/pickup_actual.py` (the one application of it)
**Lock:** `backend/harness_envelope_count_basis.py` — 53 checks, run by `carrier-vocab-guard.yml`

### 74.1 What the owner saw, traced to the cent

Nothing was wrong with the money. B-3PL / 2026-10-02, measured in production and verified line by
line against the sales feed:

| Figure | Amount | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `daily_closing.t_cash` | $2,646.00 | the whole drawer, as the rep declared it |
| declared `epay_on_cash` | $1,975.00 | the rep's own bill-payment cash |
| POS bill-payment cash | **$2,093.50** | $2,013.50 of bills + $80.00 of service fees, **cash tender only** (26 + 20 feed lines) |
| `cash_pickup.amount`, basis `pos` | **$552.50** | $2,646.00 − $2,093.50 — the system's expectation |
| `actual_picked_amount` | **$671.00** | $2,646.00 − $1,975.00 — what the rep bagged and the DM counted |

The screen called $552.50 *"declared on the envelope"*. **Nobody declared it.** The $118.50 "over"
is exactly $2,093.50 − $1,975.00: the rep under-declared his bill-payment cash by $38.50 and did not
count $80.00 of service-fee cash as bill-payment money at all.

### 74.2 The class — and the distinction §72's vocabulary cannot express

§72 says a variance between two cash figures is meaningless unless both count the same cash. This is
the same class one level down. Here **both figures count the same cash** (store cash) and they still
disagree, because they were **netted from different sources**: the expectation by the POS figure, the
bag by the rep's own declaration. §72's bases name WHICH CASH; a pickup basis names **whose figure
came out**. So the judgement lives beside the pickup basis words, not folded into §72's cash bases —
which would make `pos` and `declared` look identical.

### 74.3 The gate — one home, read by the read path AND the write path

`billpay_netting.count_comparable(basis)` is the only place that decides, on the **resolved** basis:

| basis | what was netted | comparable? |
|---|---|---|
| `off` | nothing | ✅ both figures are the whole drawer |
| `none` | nothing (no POS figure that day) | ✅ |
| `declared` | the rep's own figure | ✅ the bag was netted the same way |
| `pos` | the POS figure | ❌ the bag was netted by the rep's figure instead |
| not recorded / unrecognised | resolves to `off` | ✅ see 74.4 |

`pickup_actual.gate_on_basis` applies it once and is dereferenced by **both** `row_variance` (the
board and the two pickup lists) and `count_patch` (the open-and-count save) — a figure scored on
save and refused on the board is the drift the lock forbids. A refused comparison gets
`status='not_comparable'` and `variance=None`: **not** `match` and **not** `0.00`, either of which
would read as "it tied out". Both figures are kept so a screen can still show what was expected.

### 74.4 An unrecorded basis is NOT "unknown" — and that was not a free choice

`router.pickup_basis_label` had already ruled it: unrecorded resolves to `off`, worded "total cash
(not recorded — collected before the basis was stored)". That is right on the facts — netting did not
exist before mig 1038/1039, so an amount written before the column IS the whole drawer. The first cut
of this fix invented a second answer ("unknown, refuse it") and would have **withdrawn 226 sound
shortage findings worth $59,321.53**. The resolution is therefore MOVED into `billpay_netting`
(`resolved_basis` / `basis_recorded`) and `pickup_basis_label` dereferences it. One fact, one home.

### 74.5 The sibling — checked before shipping, and it needed no migration

`amount_basis` exists on `commcalc.cash_pickup` **only** (mig 1039). Left alone, the gate would have
read the bill-payment envelope's missing column as unknown and refused **every** bill-pay count — the
fix breaking the sibling it was meant to protect. The fact is settled by construction: netting moves
bill-pay cash *into* that envelope, never out, so its amount is never reduced.
`billpay_netting.pickup_amount_basis_for(table, stored_basis)` is the one home for it, so neither the
confirm path nor the late open decides for itself, and **no migration is needed** for a knowable
fact. A blank table name fails closed to the row's own basis.

### 74.6 Measured effect (house org, 998 cash pickups, 660 with a DM count)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| short | 285 | **226** |
| over | 59 | **13** |
| match | 316 | 286 |
| not comparable | — | **135** |

**135 verdicts withdrawn** ($2,316.80 of "variance" no longer asserted), every one of them on the
`pos` basis; **239 sound verdicts preserved**. Nothing books, pays or settles from this figure — the
pickup variance is display plus a flag, and chargebacks key off `envelope_count.counted_amount`
(§29) — so no money moves and no migration ships.

### 74.7 What the screens say now

- The open/correct dialog reads **"Expected in this envelope: $552.50 — sales cash (the
  POS-calculated bill-pay cash netted out)"**, the basis words served by `pickup_basis_label`, so the
  page spells no basis of its own.
- A refused comparison states its one-sentence reason where it is rendered.
- The board shows a **neutral** "N not comparable" count — not red, which would accuse somebody of
  the POS-versus-declared gap as though it were missing cash, and not hidden, which would lose it.
- The by-DM shortage rollup — the surface that **names a DM** — keeps them in their own bucket,
  never as uncounted (untrue: somebody did count) and never as a match (untrue, and it hides the
  finding).

## §CORE-01. A SECTION ID CARRIES ITS MODULE, AND A CLAIM ON ONE IS A CLAIM NOBODY ELSE CAN TAKE (owner directive 2026-10-11)

Owner: *"So we should assign the numbers with a prefix of the module we are working with and update
the same in the index and back connection it"*.

### CORE-01.1 The defect, stated once

A section number in this file had **no allocator**. The number was chosen by *reading the file*, so
every branch open at the same time read the same free number as free — and a collision was the
normal outcome of parallel work, not a slip. On 2026-10-10 one pull request's number was taken out
from under it three times in about an hour (§72, §73, §74 each claimed by a different, earlier
merge), costing four renumber-and-re-dispatch cycles; and the file-wide renumber that followed
rewrote a *different* pull request's `§72` reference, caught only by diffing against `origin/main`.
`harness_unique_numbers_lock.py` already failed the build on a duplicate number — but only once both
claims were in one tree, which is after one of them has merged. Detection was never the gap;
**allocation** was.

### CORE-01.2 The scheme — `§<MODULE>-NN`

A new section's id is the **module directory name, upper-cased, a hyphen, and a two-digit number
that counts within that module**: `§COMMCALC-01`, `§CLOSING-01`, `§CORE-01`. Subsections keep the
dotted form under it: `§CORE-01.2`.

- **The prefix is not a vocabulary somebody has to maintain.** It is literally the folder under
  `backend/app/modules/`, so there is nothing to keep in step and nothing to drift. `ls
  backend/app/modules` is the whole list.
- **The number is per module.** Two branches can only reach for the same id when they are writing
  about the same module — which is also exactly when they should be talking to each other.
- **Nobody reads this file to find the next number.** `python3 backend/harness_index_section_register.py
  --next commcalc` prints the next free id for that module and the register line to paste.
- **A reader sees the module in the id.** "§CLOSING-03" says what it is about before it is opened.

### CORE-01.3 How a collision now FAILS instead of happening quietly

Three gates, in the order they bite:

1. **The claim is one line in one table** — the register in CORE-01.5, kept in the index's own
   section order, so a newly allocated id is appended at the end of it. Two branches claiming
   `COMMCALC-01` therefore write *different content at the same position*, and the second one to
   reach GitHub has a **merge conflict in that table**, shown on the pull request before it merges
   rather than discovered after. The cost of losing the race is re-running `--next` and re-pasting
   one line — not a renumber, because nothing outside the branch references a section that does not
   exist yet.
2. **A duplicate id fails the build** — `harness_unique_numbers_lock.py`, which stays the ONE home
   for "a number that names one thing is claimed once", now matches the prefixed shape too. If
   somebody resolves the conflict by keeping both sides, CI is red.
3. **An unregistered section fails the build** — `harness_index_section_register.py` requires every
   top-level `##` heading to have a register row and every register row to resolve to a real
   heading. A section that skips the register cannot land, so the allocator cannot be bypassed.

What this is **not**: collisions are not impossible by construction. Making them impossible needs an
id that is not a sequence at all (a slug, `§COMMCALC-ma-tx-installments`), and the directive asked
for numbers. What is guaranteed is that a collision is a **conflict or a red build**, never a silent
overwrite, and that it is confined to one module.

### CORE-01.4 The back connection, and what fails when one side drifts

`harness_index_section_register.py` (CI: `module-graph-guard`) checks both directions:

| Direction | What must be true | What fails it |
|---|---|---|
| section → module | every `##` section has a register row naming its module(s) | a new section with no row |
| module → section | every folder under `backend/app/modules/` is either named by a register row or listed in CORE-01.6 with a reason | a new module that documents itself nowhere |
| register → index | every register id resolves to a real heading | a renamed or deleted heading |
| declared → cited | the declared module(s) intersect the modules whose code paths the section actually cites, wherever it cites any | a row that names the wrong module |
| code → section | every `module_graph.FACTS[*]["index"]` reference resolves to a **registered** section (or a subsection of one) | a fact pointing at an unregistered section |
| the scheme is closed | every *numeric* register id is one of the 112 that predate this directive; the list may only shrink | allocating a new bare number instead of a prefixed id |
| a heading has an id at all | every `##` heading carries one of the two id shapes | a top-level section headed with prose and no number |

The last row is what keeps this ONE scheme rather than two live ones: bare numeric ids are **frozen,
not permitted**. `§77` cannot be allocated.

`backend/app/modules/core/module_graph.py` stays the one home for *which files answer which
question*; it already carried an `index` reference per fact and the guard already checked it
resolved to a heading. This change does not copy that — it **tightens** it to "resolves to a
registered section" and adds the module↔section direction it never had.

### CORE-01.5 THE REGISTER — section → module

122 rows: the 109 numbered top-level `##` sections (§23s is grandfathered as two headings and
registers once), plus §15.1–§15.3, which are where the `notify` module is actually documented, plus
the eleven `§<MODULE>-NN` sections allocated since CORE-01 (§CORE-01, §CORE-02, §CORE-03, §CORE-04,
§COMMCALC-01, §COMMCALC-02, §COMMCALC-03, §COMMCALC-04, §COMMCALC-05, §COMMCALC-06, §COMMCALC-07,
§CLOSING-01, §STOREOPS-01).

Declared, and verified against the code paths each section cites wherever it cites any: 81 of the
110 sections cite a backend module path and are checked against it, 12 of those cite four or more
modules and are cross-cutting (reported, not ruled on), and the remaining 29 are declared from their
subject and are the rows most worth a second pair of eyes. The three cross-reference sections, the
gap list, the TOC and the harness audit are `core` because they are index infrastructure, not a
module's documentation.

## §CLOSING-01. AN ENVELOPE COUNT IS SCORED AGAINST THE ENVELOPE'S EXPECTED FIGURE (owner report 2026-10-12)

Owner, verbatim: *"Build the label fix"* — after asking on 2026-10-10 where the $552 on the
Management Recon screen came from (§74).

**Module:** `backend/app/modules/closing/pickup_actual.py` (`day_variance`, the one home for a
store-day's verdict) · `backend/app/modules/closing/router.py` (`GET /cash-recon-management`, which
now computes no variance of its own)
**Lock:** `backend/harness_management_recon_expected.py` — 41 checks, run by `carrier-vocab-guard.yml`
**Migration:** none. Every fact this needs is already stored.

### CLOSING-01.1 Why §74 did not reach this screen

§74 gated `pickup_actual.row_variance`, which the pickup list and the deposit-accountability board
read. The Management Recon screen — the screen the owner was actually looking at — reads neither. It
summed `cash_pickup.actual_picked_amount` per store-day and subtracted `daily_closing.t_cash`, **the
whole declared drawer**, in its row builder.

Under bill-payment netting the bag never holds the drawer: it holds the drawer less the bill-pay
cash. So that subtraction returns **minus the rep's declared bill-pay cash**, on every netted
store-day, on the one surface that names the DM who did the counting.

**The class, one step up from §74's: a sum has no basis.** The gate cannot run on two totals, so any
caller wanting a store-day figure must aggregate the ROWS' gated verdicts. That is why a fix to
`row_variance` alone could not reach here, and why the aggregation itself had to become a one home
rather than arithmetic in a router.

### CLOSING-01.2 Measured on live data (house org, 470 counted store-days, 2026-10-12)

| | short | over | match | refused |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| what the screen showed | 344 (−$118,249.40) | 2 | 124 | — |
| against the envelope's expected figure | 244 (−$60,685.07) | 33 | 193 | — |

**278 of the 470 store-days showed a "shortage" exactly equal to the declared bill-pay cash —
$90,280.01** of variance that was an artifact of netting and nothing else. B-3PL / 2026-10-02 read
$1,975.00 short where the envelope's own figures give $118.50 over, and §74's gate refuses even that.

### CLOSING-01.3 What it reads now

| figure | expected against | decided by |
|---|---|---|
| the DM's count at pickup | `cash_pickup.amount` with its mig-1039 basis | `pickup_actual.day_variance` → `row_variance` → `billpay_netting.count_comparable` (§74) |
| management's later count | `envelope_count.expected_amount` **as stored at count time** | the counter, on the mig-1036 basis they chose |

Management's variance is no longer re-derived at all: `envelope_count` already stores
`expected_amount`, `variance` and `status`, so the screen reads the score the count actually carries.
A count written before that score existed reads **None**, never 0.00 — "it tied out" is not something
to assert about a count nobody scored (`mgmt_unscored_days`).

### CLOSING-01.4 A mixed store-day fails closed

If any one of a store-day's counted envelopes is refused by the basis gate, the **day** is refused:
`variance=None`, `status='not_comparable'`, and the reason is that envelope's own. Summing the
comparable ones and dropping the rest would publish a number that is neither the day's shortage nor
any envelope's — the exact shape of defect this mechanism exists to stop. Both totals are still
returned so the screen can show what was in play, and `dm_not_comparable_days` counts the refusals
rather than letting them vanish from both buckets.

### CLOSING-01.5 The label the owner read

The column read **"DM verified cash"**, tooltipped *"the declared envelope figure"* — which is why
$552.50 looked like a number somebody had typed. Nobody types it. It now reads **"Expected in
envelope"**, and says it is the declared drawer less bill-payment cash where the tenant nets it out.
A refused row carries a neutral *not comparable* marker and the reason, and the export writes the
status word rather than a blank that reads as nil.

### CLOSING-01.6 Seams

- **No money moves.** The pickup variance is display plus a flag; chargebacks key off
  `envelope_count.counted_amount` (§29), untouched.
- **No new route**, so the `harness_db_resilience` route pin is unchanged.
- **The sibling was checked first.** `amount_basis` exists on `cash_pickup` only, so the bill-pay
  rows go through `billpay_netting.pickup_amount_basis_for` — §74's one home for that fact — rather
  than an assumption written here.

### CORE-01.7 Why the 112 existing ids were NOT renumbered

Measured before deciding: **4,061 `§NN` references outside this file, in 895 files** — 2,676 in
`backend/`, 614 in `frontend/`, 318 in `database/`, 295 in `.github/`, plus 2,577 cross-references
inside this file. A file-wide renumber rewrites all of them, conflicts with every open pull request,
and the one renumber already attempted rewrote another author's reference by accident. So the
existing ids **keep their numbers and are registered as they are**, and the numeric space is closed
to new claims.

This leaves one allocator, one register and one set of rules — but **two id shapes**, said plainly:
legacy numeric (frozen, 112 of them) and module-prefixed (every new one). That is a closed scheme
plus a frozen tail, not two live schemes, and the build check in CORE-01.4 is what keeps it so.

### CORE-01.8 Duplicate check (build gate) — what was checked, what was reused

- `harness_unique_numbers_lock.py` already owned "an id is claimed once" and already parsed this
  file's headings, `§N.M **…**` paragraphs and TOC rows. **Reused**: its three id patterns were
  taught the prefixed shape — and, in the same change, a multi-letter suffix, because `\d+[a-z]?`
  could not see **§23aa** at all, and the pattern allowed no `§`, so neither §23aa nor **§43** (whose
  heading is written `## §43 …`) was visible to the uniqueness check — two sections whose numbers
  could have been claimed a second time with nothing failing. This guard's stricter parser found
  both. Its checks moved inside `main()` so a second caller can
  import it, and the register guard dereferences `_HEADING` and `_PARA` from it rather than keeping
  a second copy of either. No new uniqueness check was written.
- `backend/app/modules/core/module_graph.py` already owned "which files answer this question" with
  an `index` reference per fact, derived callers and a resolution check. **Reused** and tightened;
  the section↔module mapping is a different fact at a different grain (113 rows against 52
  facts) and would have corrupted `FACTS`, so it lives in this register and the two are interlinked
  by the check above rather than copied.
- `.github/workflows/module-graph-guard.yml` already ran on this file and on `backend/harness_*.py`.
  **Reused**: one step added to the existing job; no new workflow, no job removed or disabled.
## §CORE-02. THE CODE STYLE CHECKER IS A CHECK — and a ratchet only turns one way (owner directive 2026-10-11)

Owner, verbatim: *"Run the code style checker and fix the problems"*.

### CORE-02.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

§75 closed this hole for the type checker and **named this one on its way past**: *"It does not run
ESLint as a gate. `npm run lint` exists and nothing runs it either. Same class, separate change — the
eslint surface was not measured here and a gate nobody measured first is how a debt file gets
invented."* This is that change, and it measured first.

The instance is 5953 lint findings. The class is **a checker the repo declares and never executes**:
`frontend/package.json` has carried `"lint": "eslint"` all along, and `grep -r "npm run lint"
.github/workflows/` returned **nothing**. §19.18 again (a mechanism written, no caller wired to it)
and §19.25 again (a gate that does not run is not a gate) — the same defect the type check had, one
layer over, in the script sitting directly above it in the same `scripts` block.

### CORE-02.2 WHAT MAIN ACTUALLY MEASURED — and therefore a debt file that holds REAL entries

Measured on `origin/main` (`567e7050`) with a clean `npm ci`, before anything was changed:

| | |
|---|---|
| **5953** | problems — **5675** errors, **278** warnings |
| **422** | files with at least one finding |
| **4903** | `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` (82% of everything) |
| **666** | React Compiler / hook rules: `set-state-in-effect` 334, `exhaustive-deps` 158, `static-components` 141, `immutability` 20, `preserve-manual-memoization` 7, `purity` 5, `refs` 1 |
| **249** | `react/no-unescaped-entities` |
| **96** | unused vars (73), unused expressions (23) |
| **20** | ESLint's own "unused eslint-disable directive" — suppressions suppressing nothing |
| **1** | a **parse error**: one tracked proof script ESLint could not read at all |

So this ships the opposite way round from §75. §75 found the frontend type-checking **clean** and
therefore refused to create a ratchet file, because *"a ratchet file holding zero entries is a
decoration that teaches people the gate is negotiable"*. Here the register holds **real entries**,
and the reason is in the numbers above: 5569 of the 5953 are `no-explicit-any` or React-Compiler
rules whose fixes change **runtime behaviour**, overwhelmingly in `commcalc/`, `storeops/payroll/`,
`closing/` and `accounts/` pages — money paths. Money-touching changes are surfaced for owner
approval in this house; a lint job does not get to make 5569 of them unasked.

The shape is the one the house already uses for exactly this: `frontend/table_sort_pending.txt` and
`backend/harness_unrun_pending.txt` + `PINNED_MAX`. Both were read before this was instantiated.

### CORE-02.3 THE ONE HOME, AND THE GATE

`frontend/package.json` keeps **one** spelling of the linter and adds one for the gate:

    "lint":      "eslint"
    "lint:gate": "node tools/eslint-ratchet.mjs"

`frontend/tools/eslint-ratchet.mjs` **shells out to `npm run lint`** rather than importing ESLint or
spelling `eslint` itself, so CI, a developer and the gate run byte-identically the same command —
§19.18's "one fact, one home, dereferenced, never copied" applied to a command, as §75.3 did for
`tsc`. CI never spells the linter either; it runs `npm run lint:gate`.

**The ratchet, stated once.** A finding not in `frontend/eslint_pending.txt` fails the build. A pinned
count that goes **up** fails. A count that goes **down**, or an entry whose findings are all gone,
also fails — until the register is corrected — so the register can never read as worse than reality
and quietly re-admit debt somebody already paid off. There is deliberately **no `--write` flag**: a
trapdoor that re-pins the register from whatever the tree currently says is how a ratchet becomes a
rubber stamp.

### CORE-02.4 WHAT WAS FIXED, AND WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT

**Fixed — the defects, not the formatting:**

- **The parse error.** `frontend/scratchpad/prove_rule5_commission_wave1.mjs` was not being linted at
  all. An arrow function returning a parenthesised object literal, with no statement terminator,
  immediately followed by a bare `{ … }` scoping block: Node's parser accepts it, the **TypeScript**
  parser reads `({ period: '', … })` as that arrow's *parameter list* with the block as its body, so
  `period: ''` becomes a destructuring rename wanting an identifier. The file reported one parse error
  instead of being linted, and its 37 assertions ran green the whole time. Also replaced two **raw
  NUL bytes** used as composite-key separators (`p + '\0' + st`) with the `\u0000` escape — identical
  runtime value, and raw NULs in tracked source are their own defect. 11 sibling proof scripts use
  the same bare-block idiom and parse fine; the gate is what will catch the next one.
- **20 suppressions that suppressed nothing**, which ESLint itself was reporting as unused directives.
- **8 BLANKET `// eslint-disable-line` directives** (no rule named — they switch off *every* rule on
  the line, including ones nobody has written yet) now **name the rule** they rely on. This **raised**
  the measured count, because naming the rule exposed `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` errors those
  blanket directives had been hiding in `admin/access-log` and `commcalc/coaching`. Those are now in
  the register, visible, instead of invisible. That is the intended direction.
- **2 `prefer-const`**, and **20 unused import specifiers** — unambiguous dead code, each verified by
  `npm run typecheck` staying at 0 errors over 547 files.

**Deliberately NOT fixed, and never suppressed — each left in the register where it can be seen:**

- **4903 `no-explicit-any`.** Typing these properly is the right fix and it is a large, careful change
  across commission, payroll and P&L pages. Annotating them `unknown` to reach green would move the
  errors into `tsc` and change behaviour at every call site.
- **666 React Compiler / hook findings.** `exhaustive-deps` and `set-state-in-effect` fixes change
  *when effects re-run*. On `commcalc/ma-commission`, `commcalc/commission-ledger`,
  `storeops/payroll`, `accounts/pl` and `closing/*` that decides which period's money a screen shows.
  Not guessed at; see 77.5.
- ~~**249 `react/no-unescaped-entities`** and **23 `no-unused-expressions`**~~ — left for budget, not
  for principle, and the only two groups of which that was true. **Both are now ZERO** — paid off in
  full by the follow-up in **CORE-02.8**, which also corrects the word "cosmetic" used here: the 23
  unused expressions were not cosmetic and not dead, they were load-bearing.
- **7 `no-require-imports`** in `scratchpad/prove_plan_match_render.cjs` — a `.cjs` file **must** use
  `require`. This is a case of the rule being wrong for the file, stated here rather than silenced
  with a disable comment.
- **4 `no-img-element`, 4 `no-html-link-for-pages`, 1 `incompatible-library`, 1 `refs`** — each a
  behaviour change (`<a>` → `<Link>` changes a full reload into a client navigation, which §"nav no
  reload" already has opinions about).

**MEASURED AFTER, on the same clean install:** **5917** findings — **5679** errors, **238**
warnings — over **419** files, pinned as **932** `(rule, file)` entries in
`frontend/eslint_pending.txt`. Against main's 5953 / 5675 / 278 / 422 that is **36 fewer findings and
3 fewer files**, with warnings down 40 and **errors UP 4** — the four are the
`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` errors that naming the 8 blanket directives stopped hiding, minus
the parse error and the em-dash rule name. An honest gate that reports 4 more errors than the tree
admitted to yesterday is the point; they were always there. `eslint-disable` directives went
**110 → 92**, and PINNED_SUPPRESSIONS is pinned at exactly 92 so the count cannot grow at all.

**MEASURED NOW, after CORE-02.8:** **5645** findings — **5430** errors, **215** warnings — over
**413** files, pinned as **842** `(rule, file)` entries. `PINNED_TOTAL` is **5645**; suppressions are
still **92** (CORE-02.8 added none).

### CORE-02.5 UNUSED VARIABLES THAT ARE CANDIDATE DEFECTS — reported, not deleted

`no-unused-vars` is the rule the owner's brief singled out as possibly "shadowing a real bug", and it
does. **Deleting an abandoned variable hides the fact that nobody wired it up**, so these were left
alone and are listed for a human:

- **`commcalc/commission-structure/page.tsx:166` — a permission gate that cannot fire.**
  `const [accCanEdit, setAccCanEdit] = useState(true)`; the setter is **never called**. So
  `accCanEdit` is permanently `true`: the read-only notice at line 547 ("Read-only — you don't have
  the Classification permission") can **never render**, the four `disabled={!accCanEdit}` editors are
  never disabled, and the Save button always shows. The Classification permission check on a
  commission-config surface is dead code. **Money-adjacent — not touched.**
- `accounts/device-purchases/page.tsx:118` — `qtyTotal` computed and never rendered beside the
  `deviceTotal` / `unitTotal` that are.
- `commcalc/settings/page.tsx:307` — `groupedRates`, under the comment *"Group comp rates by
  comp_type for display"*. The display was never wired.
- `closing/tender-recon-3way/page.tsx:89`, `commcalc/custom-report/page.tsx:50` (`grants` — a fetched
  permission list never read), `commcalc/productivity/page.tsx:236`,
  `storeops/payroll-change-log/page.tsx:50` and `storeops/salary-advances/page.tsx:43` (`ppSettings`
  — pay-period settings declared and abandoned in both), `storeops/payroll/PtoAccrualPanel.tsx:23`
  (`runResult` — a PTO accrual run's result never shown).
- `admin/support/docs/page.tsx:56` — `async function del(d: Doc)`, a delete handler never wired to
  anything.
- `components/ReportShell.tsx:56` — the exported component destructures a **`compact` prop and
  ignores it**, so every caller passing `compact` gets no effect. Not money; still a real defect.

### CORE-02.6 THE LOCK — so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_frontend_lint_lock.py` (stdlib only, DB-free, does **not** run ESLint) fails the
build when: the `lint` or `lint:gate` script loses its one home (a); no workflow runs the gate, or
runs it in a job that never `npm ci`s (b); a workflow spells `eslint` itself (c); the `pull_request`
or `push` path filter stops covering `frontend/**` (d); `eslint.config.mjs` stops spreading
`core-web-vitals` or `typescript` (e); `globalIgnores` grows beyond build output (f); the count of
`eslint-disable` directives exceeds **PINNED_SUPPRESSIONS**, or any directive is **blanket** (g); the
register fails to parse or pins more than **PINNED_TOTAL** (h). Every rule has a negative control
driving it RED over a synthetic input (i), so a rule that has stopped matching cannot sit here reading
green. It runs **before** `npm ci` in its own job, so its verdict is reported even when the lint step
is what goes red — the §19.25 lesson about a lock sitting behind the thing it guards.

Rule (g) is the one that answers the owner's brief directly: **the suppression ceiling is what makes
"fix the problems" mean fix, rather than comment out.**

### CORE-02.8 THE TWO GROUPS THAT WERE A BUDGET CALL — paid off to zero (2026-10-11, follow-up)

CORE-02.4 registered 5917 findings and was explicit that only two of those groups were held back for
**budget rather than principle**. This is those two, measured to zero. Nothing else in the register
was touched: no `no-explicit-any`, no hook rule, no suppression added, no rule downgraded, no
`globalIgnores` widened.

| rule | before | after | files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `react/no-unescaped-entities` | 249 | **0** | 74 |
| `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-expressions` | 23 | **0** | 16 |
| **total findings** | 5917 | **5645** | 419 → 413 |

**`no-unescaped-entities` — escaping only, and that is PROVEN, not asserted.** All 249 were `'` (179)
or `"` (70) in JSX text; no `>` or `}` occurred. Each was replaced with `&apos;` / `&quot;` **at the
exact line and column ESLint reported**, never by a regex over JSX text — the brief's own warning
about a tidy-up regex that mangled two files by −91 and −147 lines is why. Two audits back this:
in **each** of the 74 files the insertion count **equals** the deletion count, so no file gained or
lost a single line (187 changed lines in total, carrying all 249 replacements — some lines hold more
than one); and on every one of those 187 lines, **reverting the inserted entities reproduces the
original line byte for byte**, with the length change exactly 5 characters per replacement. Not one character of
visible copy changed.

> **The trap worth recording: ESLint columns are UTF-16 code units, not code points.** Five findings
> sat on lines containing an astral emoji (`💵`, `📋`, `📝`), each of which is ONE Python character but
> TWO UTF-16 units — so indexing the reported column in Python landed one character late, on the `s`
> of `employee's` rather than the apostrophe. The rewriter **asserted that the character at the
> reported position was the one the message named** and refused to write any file when it was not,
> which is how this surfaced instead of shipping five corrupted strings. Index in UTF-16 units.

**`no-unused-expressions` — all 23 read individually, and the brief's two categories did not fit.**
The brief anticipated *dead code* (delete it) or an *unfinished statement* (report it, never guess).
Read one by one, **23 of 23 were neither**: every one is a ternary- or `&&`-as-statement whose **both
branches have real side effects**, so it is working, load-bearing code that the rule objects to on
the grounds of IDIOM, not effect:

- 20 are `n.has(k) ? n.delete(k) : n.add(k)` — the select-all/toggle behind every multi-select in the
  app (`src/lib/multiselect.tsx`, `ReportShell`, `commcalc/item-mapping`, `plan-installments`, …).
  **Deleting these would have broken every one of those toggles.**
- 2 are `ok ? pass++ : fail++` — how two proof harnesses count their own results.
- 1 is `onApplied && onApplied()` — a guarded optional callback, typed `onApplied?: () => void`.

So **0 deleted and 0 reported as unfinished**; each was restructured into the equivalent statement
form `if (cond) a; else b`, which is provably behaviour-identical (the ternary's value was discarded
at both sites, and a function is never falsy, so `if (onApplied)` ≡ `onApplied &&`). 23 insertions,
23 deletions — exactly one line per finding. `frontend/scratchpad/prove_entity_picker.mjs` (53/53)
and `prove_org_append.mjs` (22/22) still pass, which is the direct check that the two counter
rewrites preserved their meaning.

**No money path's behaviour moved.** Several of these files are money-adjacent — `commcalc/
plan-installments`, `commission-plans`, `targets/*`, `CoverageWizard`, `accounts/*` — so the standing
rule applies. Nothing here changes a figure or when an effect re-runs: the entity work is text
escaping inside JSX text nodes, and the expression work is an if/else transliteration of an
already-evaluated ternary. No `useEffect`, no dependency array and no arithmetic was touched.

**Register corrected downward, as the ratchet demands.** The gate fails when a count FALLS without
the register being fixed, so all **90** now-empty entries (74 + 16, exactly the two rules and nothing
else — verified by grouping the gate's own `- delete:` output by rule) were removed: **932 → 842**
entries, sum **5917 → 5645**, which equals the measured total. `PINNED_TOTAL` lowered 5917 → 5645 per
CORE-02.6(h), which says to lower it as the register shrinks. The register's own header carries the
same numbers so it does not state a stale count.

Proof on the final tree: `npm run typecheck` **0 errors** over 547 files; `npm run lint` **5645**;
`npm run lint:gate` **OK** (measured 5645 == pinned 5645); `harness_frontend_lint_lock.py`
**42 passed, 0 failed**.

**WHAT THIS EXPOSED — an apostrophe was hiding real leaks from the carrier-vocab guard.**
`harness_carrier_vocab_guard.py` decides "is this line display copy?" in `jsx_prose_line`, and its
prose-vs-code test `_prose_bad = [<>=;'"`]` **rejects any line containing a raw apostrophe**. So a
tenant-facing sentence that happened to contain `isn't`, `can't` or `that's` was discarded as CODE
and never scanned at all. Escaping those apostrophes — which `react/no-unescaped-entities` requires —
removed the thing that was hiding them, and **5 genuine pre-existing leaks in tenant-facing copy
became visible for the first time**:

| lock | file:line | what a tenant can read |
|---|---|---|
| setup-internals | `commcalc/plan-installments/page.tsx:638` | "Migration 245 isn't applied yet, so these boxes can't be saved." |
| setup-internals | `commcalc/plan-installments/page.tsx:815` | "Migration {payCfg.migration} isn't applied yet, so this can't be saved." |
| setup-internals | `storeops/payroll-change-log/page.tsx:195` | "…table isn't set up yet on this tenant (migration 414)" |
| setup-internals | `storeops/salary-advances/page.tsx:378` | "…ledger isn't set up yet on this tenant (migration 419)" |
| infra-names | `commcalc/connectors/page.tsx:116` | "point **pg_cron** at POST /api/v1/… and it fans out to every connector that's due." |

These are **NOT regressions** — every one is on `main` today, rendered to tenants; `main` is green only
because the apostrophe made the sentence unreadable to the guard. Since the whole rule is now at zero
and the ratchet refuses a new raw apostrophe in JSX text, **this coverage hole is structurally closed
and stays closed** — which is the lasting value here, over and above the 272 findings.

Their disposal was the owner's call, not a lint job's — each option changes what a tenant-facing
screen says, or accepts a leak as carried debt (`SETUP_PROSE_DEBT`, 11 existing entries), or opens
the deliberately-EMPTY `INFRA_FE_ALLOW`. **The owner ruled on 2026-10-12: "Reword the four."** The
copy was reworded through the one home; see **CORE-02.9** below, which also corrects the
recommendation put to him about the fifth.

**One design fix WAS made, because it is a defect in the guard and not a copy decision:**
`jsx_prose_line` **deleted** HTML entities instead of decoding them, so `isn&apos;t` was read as
`isnt`. That is not what the screen says, and it means a sentence pinned by its own text stops
matching its pin the moment an apostrophe in it is escaped. Entities are now **decoded** to the
characters they render as. The deletion was not arbitrary, so the fix separates the two uses rather
than reversing it: the prose-vs-code gate still reads the entity-**stripped** line (so **no line
changes visibility** and coverage is unchanged), while what the scans **match on** is the
**decoded** line. Armed controls **E13–E16** pin all of it, including E15 — decoding before the gate
would classify escaped prose as code and make it invisible, which would be strictly worse than the
bug.

**Duplicate check (the build gate).** Nothing new was built: no new report, endpoint, query, table,
function or feed, so there is nothing to register in §16–18 or the lineage registry. This EXTENDS
CORE-02 — the same gate, the same runner, the same register, the same lock — which is why it is a
subsection here and not a new `§<MODULE>-NN`. Searched the index for an existing mechanism before
touching anything: CORE-02 itself is that mechanism and the two groups above are its own named
leftovers. No second lint path, no second register and no second home for the linter invocation was
created; `frontend/package.json`'s `lint` script remains the one home, dereferenced by the gate.

### CORE-02.9 THE FIVE EXPOSED LEAKS — reworded through the one home (owner 2026-10-12)

Owner, on the five sentences CORE-02.8 exposed: *"Reword the four."* (the four setup-internals hits;
the fifth, `pg_cron`, had been recommended for keeping — see the correction below).

**The class, not the instance.** The general fact that was wrong is not "four screens name a
migration": it is **a caller that does not dereference the one home**. `lib/setupNotice.tsx` has been
the ONE home for "this feature's setup is not finished" since §19.36, and each of these pages wrote
the sentence inline instead. So the repair is wiring, not wording — exactly the §19.18 failure mode
("a mechanism written, callers left unwired"), and the reason no new copy helper was created.

| file:line | before (what a tenant read) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `commcalc/plan-installments/page.tsx:638` | "Migration 245 isn't applied yet, so these boxes can't be saved." | `<SetupNotice lead="These boxes cannot be saved yet." detail="245" />` |
| `commcalc/plan-installments/page.tsx:815` | "Migration {payCfg.migration} isn't applied yet, so this can't be saved." | `<SetupNotice lead="This cannot be saved yet." detail={payCfg.migration} />` |
| `storeops/payroll-change-log/page.tsx:195` | "…table isn't set up yet on this tenant (migration 414)" | `<SetupNotice lead="The Payroll Change Log is not switched on yet, so no entries can be recorded or shown." detail="414" />` |
| `storeops/salary-advances/page.tsx:378` | "…ledger isn't set up yet on this tenant (migration 419)" | `<SetupNotice lead="The Salary Advance ledger is not switched on yet, so no advances can be recorded or shown." detail="419" />` |
| `storeops/timeclock/page.tsx:302` | "…table isn't set up yet on this tenant (migration 414) — manual-adjustment markers below are unavailable" | `<SetupNotice lead="The Payroll Change Log is not switched on yet, so the manual-adjustment markers below are unavailable." detail="414" />` |

**A FIFTH site, found by looking for the siblings before shipping.** `timeclock/page.tsx:302` renders
the SAME migration-414 sentence as `payroll-change-log:195` and the guard **never flagged it** —
`display_copy` does not extract that line's shape, so it was invisible to both the scan and the pin.
Fixing the four and leaving it is "the same defect wearing a hat", so it was converted too. Note what
this says about the pin: `SETUP_PROSE_DEBT["…/timeclock/page.tsx"] = 2` is **unchanged**, because its
two counted hits are at lines 433 and 537; the pin never covered 302. **A pinned count is a ratchet on
what the scanner can SEE, not an inventory of a file's leaks.**

**THE RECOMMENDATION PUT TO THE OWNER ABOUT `pg_cron` WAS WRONG, and is corrected here.** It was put
to him as "leave it — the Connectors page is only read by whoever wires up the schedule". That premise
does not survive checking `rbac.ts`: `{ href: '/commcalc/connectors', module: 'commissions', scopes:
['all'], tileOnly: true }` — **not** `platformOnly`, so any user with the commissions module can open
it. The sentence was tenant-facing after all, which is why the guard was right to be red about it, and
leaving it would also have left the build red. It was reworded on the same principle as the other
five.

**`<PlatformDetail detail />` — a new export of the EXISTING home, not a new home.** `<SetupNotice>`
was the wrong instrument here: Connectors **is** switched on, so rendering "This feature isn't
switched on for your company yet" would have been a false statement to every tenant. The need is
narrower — *an operational route that only the platform team can act on, on a page tenants also open*
— and `setupNotice.tsx` is where "who may read an internal name" is already answered. So the file
gained a second export that dereferences the same `useSetupDetailVisible()` (→ `rbac.isPlatformAdmin`,
→ `core.router._require_super_admin`): it renders the detail for the super admin and **`null`** for
everyone else, with no customer sentence. One gate, one file, two shapes — rather than a second
predicate somewhere else, which is the §19.18 defect this repo has shipped three times.

- tenant copy now: *"One schedule drives them all: every connector below runs by itself when it next falls due."*
- super admin additionally sees: `[setup: pg_cron -> POST /api/v1/commcalc/connectors/run-due, header X-Notify-Secret]`

**No accommodation was taken.** `SETUP_PROSE_DEBT` gained **no** entry (it still carries its 11 and
its `timeclock` pin of 2, unchanged) and `INFRA_FE_ALLOW` is still **EMPTY**. Both locks are green on
their own terms rather than on an excusal, which is the whole point of the two ledgers being

**Proof on the final tree.** `harness_carrier_vocab_guard.py` (run as `python3.11` — see

reported holding, where the same harness on the parent commit printed `FAIL 4 migration …` and

(measured 5645 == pinned 5645, so the rewording introduced no new lint finding and retired none —

`harness_index_section_register.py` and `harness_ci_pipefail_lock.py` both exit 0.

**Duplicate check (the build gate).** Nothing new was built: no report, endpoint, query, table or
feed, so §16–18 carry nothing new. Searched the index for an existing mechanism before touching

extended it by one export rather than adding a sibling. The five page edits DELETE inline copy and
