## §CORE-03. A STORED CREDENTIAL IS ENCRYPTED AT REST — one registry, every reader and writer dereferencing it (owner directive 2026-10-12)

Owner, before the UPS Store portal login existed to protect: a portal password should not sit in the
database in plain text.

The honest version of what he was told first, and the correction: this platform has had working
field encryption since the employee-bank-details work (`app/core/crypto.py` — Fernet, AES-128-CBC
with HMAC-SHA256, the stored form `enc:v1:<token>`). It was never pointed at a portal credential.
So the answer was not "build encryption"; it was "wire the encryption that exists".

### §CORE-03.1 The defect, stated once

The defect was never *"epay's password is plaintext"*. It was that **a stored credential had no
home**. Ten columns across ten tables each carried their own secret, each module read and wrote its
own, and whether a value was protected depended on which module happened to own the table. Measured
2026-10-12, every one of these was stored exactly as typed:

| table | column(s) | migration |
|-------|-----------|-----------|
| `commcalc.vip_sweep_config` | `portal_pass` | `011` |
| `commcalc.dlar_sweep_config` | `portal_pass` | `012` |
| `commcalc.epay_sweep_config` | `portal_pass` | `020` |
| `commcalc.b2b_sweep_config` | `portal_pass` | `026` |
| `commcalc.ftp_sweep_config` | `password` | `046` |
| `commcalc.email_sweep_config` | `password` | `049` |
| `commcalc.data_source` | `password`, `totp_secret`, `session_state`, `pending_state` | `083`, `084`, `955` |
| `storeops.google_review_config` | `api_key` | `411` |
| `storeops.platform_billing_connector` | `credential` | `090` |

And the sting: the **vision** module got it right, on its own, years of commits earlier — migs 900+
store `client_secret_enc` / `refresh_token_enc` / `secret_enc` / `extension_token_enc` as `enc:v1:`
ciphertext. Because that decision lived *inside that module*, nothing carried it to the other ten.
**One module's good decision that its siblings cannot inherit is the same defect as a bad one.**

### §CORE-03.2 One fact, one home, dereferenced

`backend/app/modules/core/portal_secret.py` is the ONE home for *"which stored columns hold a
credential"*. `TABLES` carries, per table, four facts that a caller would otherwise each guess at:

| | |
|---|---|
| `schema` | where the table lives (`''` when the caller's client is already scoped to it) |
| `key` | the primary key, as columns — **only `data_source` has a surrogate `id`**; the nine config tables are keyed on the tenant, and `email_sweep_config` on `(org_id, account)` since mig `075`. A backfill that assumed `id` would have silently done nothing on nine of the ten |
| `secrets` | the TEXT columns that are encrypted at rest |
| `json` | the JSONB columns that hold a secret. A separate field because they need a different PRIMITIVE, not a different policy: `enc:v1:<token>` is not valid JSON, so a JSONB column takes `crypto.encrypt_json`'s `{"enc": …}` envelope. Getting that wrong would not have been a silent weakening — it would have been a Postgres error the first time a portal login tried to save its session |

`SECRET_COLUMNS` and `JSON_COLUMNS` are **derived views** of `TABLES`, computed in source, never
typed out again. The API is `seal_row(table, row)` on the way to the database and
`open_row(table, row)` on the way back; both return a NEW dict, so a caller that logs or returns the
dict it passed in is never handed ciphertext.

### §CORE-03.3 No migration, and no backfill window

`crypto.decrypt` keys off the `enc:v1:` prefix and returns anything without it **unchanged**. So a
row written yesterday (plaintext) and a row written tomorrow (ciphertext) both read correctly, from
the same column, at the same time. There is no migration in this change and no cutover to schedule.

`core/encryption_backfill.backfill_portal_secrets` seals what is ALREADY stored — idempotent, paged,
safe to re-run on every boot while `ENCRYPTION_BACKFILL_ON_BOOT=1` and across replicas. It is how
the old rows stop being readable from a database dump, **not** how this becomes correct. It spells no
table name of its own: it iterates `portal_secret.SECRET_COLUMNS` and reads `table_schema` /
`table_key`, so a credential column registered tomorrow is backfilled with no edit to it. §F of the
lock fails the build if a table name appears in its body.

### §CORE-03.4 Where it is wired

| writer | what it protects |
|---|---|
| `commcalc/router._status_update(client, table, upd, filt)` | THE chokepoint. It already took the table NAME, so sealing once there covers every sweep status write **and every portal SESSION patch** — `_source_stamp` writes `session_state` / `pending_state` through it from all four login paths |
| each `*_sweep_config` upsert (vip, dlar, b2b, epay ×2, ftp, email ×4) | the portal passwords, as typed on the sweep settings pages |
| `commcalc/router.save_data_source` (update + insert) | the portal password and the authenticator secret |
| `storeops/router.put_google_reviews_config` | the Google Places API key |
| `billing/router` insert + update | the platform's own vendor API tokens |
| `supply/api_credential.access_token` | a freshly minted OAuth token, before it is cached on the login row |

| reader | |
|---|---|
| `_vip_cfg` · `_dlar_cfg` · `_b2b_cfg` · `_epay_cfg` · `_ftp_cfg` · `_email_cfg` | the six per-sweep config readers — each sweep's only route to its own credential |
| `commcalc/router._ds_rows(q)` | THE `data_source` read. The eight call sites each build their own query (one row by id, the due list, the tenant's list); what they must not each decide is WHICH columns to open, so they hand the query here |
| `storeops/google_reviews.get_config` | the one reader of `api_key` — which is why opening it there makes the sweep, the masked public config and the store resolver all see the real key without any of them knowing it was sealed |
| `account/router.sweep_credit_memos` | the one credential read that never lived in `commcalc/router.py` |
| `billing/router._pc_rows(q)` | the vendor credential |

The email due-list is opened too, because those rows go **straight to the sweep worker**, password
and all, rather than being re-read through `_email_cfg`.

### §CORE-03.5 What this is NOT

- **Not a secrets manager.** The key lives in the backend's environment, so this protects against
  someone reading the DATABASE — a leaked backup, raw service-role access, a support engineer — not
  against someone who already has the backend's environment. That is the same bar `app/core/crypto.py`
  was built to and states for employee bank details.
- **Not a replacement for stripping the columns from API reads.** They already are, by
  `router._SOURCE_SECRETS`, each `_*_public_cfg`, `google_reviews.public_config` and `billing._pc_out`,
  and that stays the first line. Encrypted-at-rest and never-returned are two controls, and this is
  one of them.
- **Not for platform login passwords.** Those are one-way HASHED by `core/auth_security`, and hashing
  beats encryption for anything that never has to be replayed. §B8 of the lock fails if a
  platform-login table is ever added to this registry.
- **Not a silent no-op.** With no `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` configured, `crypto.encrypt` passes values
  through and the platform keeps working exactly as it does today — deliberately, so a missing key
  cannot stop a portal login. `protection_state()` exists so a surface can SAY `'unprotected'`
  instead of implying a safety that is absent. **Silence about an absent control is how a control
  gets forgotten.**

### §CORE-03.6 Lock — `backend/harness_portal_secret_lock.py` (158 checks, DB-free, stdlib only)

Wired into `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml`, which names the harness and every module
wired to the registry in its own paths filter — a lock behind an allowlist that does not name its
subjects skips silently (the §13e lesson).

| § | what it refuses to let happen |
|---|---|
| A | the primitive misbehaves — a round trip loses the value, a partial update wipes a stored secret, a caller's dict is mutated, legacy plaintext stops passing through, or a live browser session is logged out by this deploy |
| B | the registry grows a second source of truth, loses a schema/key fact, or acquires a platform-login table |
| C | the registry names a table or column the SCHEMA does not have, gets a key wrong, or puts a JSONB column in the text tuple. **It caught two real errors while being written**: the first draft said `google_reviews_config` (the table is `google_review_config`, singular), and `session_state` / `pending_state` are JSONB, which the `enc:v1:` string cannot be stored in |
| D | a credential column exists in the schema and is neither registered, nor already `_enc`, nor **excused in writing**. This is the check that FINDS THE SIBLINGS: it is what turned up `platform_billing_connector.credential`, a tenth table nobody had mentioned, which is now registered and wired |
| E | a reader or writer stops dereferencing the registry |
| F | the backfill grows its own list of tables, addresses rows by `id`, or stops being run by `run_all` |
| G | seven negative controls — every scanner above is proven to SEE a planted violation, and §D's scanner is proven not to flag an ordinary column |

§D's excuse list is the part worth reading, because the recurring reason is **lookup by value**: an
encrypted column is opaque, so a token the server has to find a row BY
(`employee_onboarding_profile.access_token`, `chat_push_tokens.token`) cannot be encrypted without
breaking the lookup. The right tool for those is `crypto.blind_index`, which is named in the excuse
as open work rather than left implied.

### §CORE-03.7 What was checked for duplication before building

| asked | found | done |
|---|---|---|
| does field encryption already exist? | YES — `app/core/crypto.py`, in use for employee bank details, customer PINs and the vision module's `_enc` columns | REUSED unchanged. No new primitive, no new key, no second envelope format |
| is there already a backfill mechanism? | YES — `app/core/encryption_backfill.py`, with `run_all()` and the `ENCRYPTION_BACKFILL_ON_BOOT=1` route for an operator with no shell | EXTENDED with one more sweep in the same shape, not a sibling script |
| is there already a registry of "which column is sensitive"? | NO. The closest was `router._SOURCE_SECRETS`, which answers a DIFFERENT question — *which columns to strip from an API read* — for ONE table | NEW home. `_SOURCE_SECRETS` is left alone: stripping and encrypting are two controls, and collapsing them would weaken the first |
| is there already a per-table write chokepoint? | YES — `commcalc/router._status_update`, which already took the table name | REUSED. One edit there seals every sweep status write and every portal session patch |
| is there already a per-table read chokepoint? | PARTLY — the six `_*_cfg` readers and `google_reviews.get_config` were already single readers; `data_source` had eight scattered `select("*")` sites | the six reused as-is; `_ds_rows` added as the one `data_source` read rather than opening the row at eight call sites |

## §CORE-04. AND THE ROWS ALREADY STORED — every encrypted column has a sweep, and `run_all` is derived from the registry (measured 2026-10-12)

§CORE-03 made every stored credential ciphertext **on write**. This section is the other half, and it
exists because of something found while verifying that one: encrypting on write protects nothing that
was written before.

**Module:** `backend/app/core/encryption_backfill.py` (the one home: `SWEEPS`, `BORN_SEALED`,
`NO_STORED_WRITE`, four sweeps, a derived `run_all`) ·
`backend/app/modules/pos/receipt_import.py` (`seal_stored_row` + the column declarations) ·
`backend/app/modules/hr/router.py` (the button now calls the sweep)
**Lock:** `backend/harness_encryption_backfill_coverage.py` — 175 checks, DB-free, its own job in
`carrier-vocab-guard.yml`
**Migration:** none. No money moves.
**Module-graph fact:** `encryption_backfill_coverage` (§50)

### §CORE-04.1 The defect, as measured

The owner said field encryption was already set up. It was — and the production check that confirmed
it is what found this. Of 88 sensitive employee-intake values in
`storeops.employee_onboarding_profile.intake_data`, **84 were encrypted and 4 were plain text**: the
`dd_routing` and `dd_bank_name` of two employees, readable by anyone holding a database dump.

Nothing in the code was wrong. Sealing those values existed only as
`POST /hr/onboarding/encrypt-existing` — a manual, per-tenant button — and it was **not** in
`encryption_backfill.run_all()`, the one function whose docstring said it ran *"every backfill
sweep"*. So `ENCRYPTION_BACKFILL_ON_BOOT=1` could be set, the server could boot indefinitely, and
those four values would never be touched. Everything written after the key was configured **is**
correctly encrypted, which is exactly why this looks fine from the application and only shows up if
you count.

### §CORE-04.2 Name the class, not the instance

The instance is HR intake. The class is that **"encrypted on write" and "sealed at rest" were two
separate facts with nothing tying them together**, so every newly encrypted column started life half
protected and no surface could tell. Remembered twice out of four:

| encrypted on write | sweep before this | after |
|---|---|---|
| `pos.customers.password` (the carrier PIN) | YES `backfill_customer_pins` | unchanged |
| the ten credential columns of §CORE-03 | YES `backfill_portal_secrets` | unchanged |
| `storeops.employee_onboarding_profile.intake_data` | **NO** — a manual button only | `backfill_intake_sensitive`, and the button calls it |
| `pos.receipt_imports`.`imei` / `notes` / `parsed` / `raw_ocr` | **NO — none at all** | `backfill_receipt_imports` |

The fourth row is the sibling nobody had reported: found by looking for the class rather than fixing
the instance.

### §CORE-04.3 One fact, one home, dereferenced

`SWEEPS` is the one home for *"which encrypted-at-rest column family has a sweep"*, and `run_all()`
**iterates it** — it holds no list of calls that can fall behind the registry. A family that raises
is reported under its own key and the rest still run: one tenant missing a migration must not leave
another family's PII plaintext.

No sweep spells a column name of its own. Each reads the declaration its WRITER already
dereferences — `portal_secret.SECRET_COLUMNS` (§CORE-03), `receipt_import.ENCRYPTED_IMPORT_COLUMNS` /
`..._JSON_COLUMNS` / `IMPORT_BLIND_INDEX_COLUMNS`, and HR's own `_public_intake_fields(org_id)`. So a
column added to a writer, or a field a tenant newly declares sensitive, is covered with no second
edit. **Which keys are sensitive is a per-tenant declaration** (`storeops.onboarding_intake_field`),
read per org, so a field one tenant treats as sensitive is not sealed in a tenant that does not.

`receipt_import.seal_stored_row` is separate from `_encrypt_import_row` for one reason that matters:
a **blind index must be derived from the plaintext**. The new-row writer always has it; a stored row
may already be sealed, and indexing that ciphertext writes a token matching nothing. The sealer
recomputes the index only where the stored IMEI is still readable, and returns `{}` when a row needs
nothing so the sweep issues no write at all.

### §CORE-04.4 Born encrypted is a claim, and it is proved

`app/modules/vision/router.py` encrypts stored values and owes **no** sweep: migrations 900 / 911
create those columns as `*_enc` and every writer has always passed through `encrypt()`. Measured
2026-10-12 — 3 of 3 `core.vision_credential` rows and 1 of 1 `core.vision_edge_agent` row carry the
`enc:v1:` prefix, with no plaintext row in either.

That claim lives in `BORN_SEALED` with its reason **in writing**, and the lock does not take it on
trust: §C walks the module's AST and fails the build on any write to one of those columns that is not
an `encrypt()` call (clearing one to `None` is a revoke, not a plaintext write). The day someone
writes one in the clear, the exemption stops being true and the build says so.

### §CORE-04.5 Lock — `backend/harness_encryption_backfill_coverage.py` (175 checks)

| | |
|---|---|
| §A | `SWEEPS` is well-formed; every sweep it names exists, is callable, takes the sibling shape and no-ops without a key |
| §B | `run_all` **derives** from `SWEEPS` and hard-calls no sweep |
| §C | **coverage** — every module under `backend/app` that encrypts a value it STORES is named by a family, claims `BORN_SEALED` (proved, above) or is excused in `NO_STORED_WRITE` with a written reason |
| §D | no sweep keeps its own copy of a column list |
| §E | reachable without a shell (the boot flag), and the HR button holds no second loop |
| §F | the stored-row sealer is idempotent, never indexes ciphertext, returns `{}` when nothing is due |
| §G | nine negative controls, each proven to see a planted violation |
| §H | **functional** — a REAL Fernet key over a fake database: the measured regression (a plaintext routing number sealed by `run_all`), idempotence on a second boot, and a raising family not taking the others down |
| §I | **the sealer wiring** (added 2026-10-13, §CORE-04.7) — every family declares a public `sealer`, every sweep CALLS it, this module makes no `encrypt` call of its own, no sweep type-guards values by shape, and the second measured regression is reproduced functionally: a plaintext JSONB credential column sealed into the `{'enc': …}` envelope and read back byte for byte |

### §CORE-04.6 What was checked for duplication before building

| asked | found | done |
|---|---|---|
| is there already a backfill module? | YES — `app/core/encryption_backfill.py` with `run_all()` and the boot flag | EXTENDED. The two new sweeps are functions in it, in the same shape; no sibling script, no second entry point |
| is there already a sweep for HR intake? | YES, but only as an ENDPOINT (`POST /hr/onboarding/encrypt-existing`) holding its own loop | MOVED into the module and the endpoint now CALLS it — one implementation, so the button and the boot sweep cannot diverge |
| is there already a registry of encrypted columns? | YES for credentials — `core/portal_secret.SECRET_COLUMNS` (§CORE-03) — and per-module declarations elsewhere | REUSED, all of them. `SWEEPS` answers a different question (*which family has a sweep*) and dereferences those declarations rather than restating them |
| is there already a lock on encryption at rest? | YES — `harness_portal_secret_lock.py`, which asks whether a credential COLUMN is registered | its subject is the write path for one family; this lock's subject is whether a family has a sweep at all. Both kept, neither widened |

§C is parsed, not grepped, for a reason worth keeping: `portal_secret.py` discusses `crypto.encrypt`
four times in prose, and a grep-based scanner counted those as call sites. The same correction
applies in §D, where a sweep's docstring legitimately names the columns it seals.

Proved RED before shipping: removing the `intake_sensitive` family (the state that left two routing
numbers plaintext) → 4 failures; putting `run_all` back to its literal list of two calls → 5
failures.


### §CORE-04.7 The half-dereference — WHICH columns was read, HOW to seal them was not (measured 2026-10-13)

Verifying §CORE-03 and §CORE-04 against production is what found this, the same way §CORE-04 itself
was found: the sweep had run, reported success, and left a whole class of credential readable.

**Measured.** After `ENCRYPTION_BACKFILL_ON_BOOT=1` and a redeploy, 180 of 180 sensitive intake
values were sealed and 6 of 7 portal passwords were sealed — and **0 of 3 stored browser sessions
were**. `commcalc.data_source.session_state` is a registered credential column (§CORE-03 registers
it precisely because *a stolen session is a stolen login*), and it held live portal cookies in plain
text.

**Why, and it is not a typo.** `backfill_portal_secrets` built its patch itself:

```python
patch = {c: crypto.encrypt(row[c]) for c in cols
         if isinstance(row.get(c), str) and row[c] and not crypto.is_encrypted(row[c])}
```

A JSONB column comes back from the client as a **dict**, so `isinstance(..., str)` was False and the
column was skipped — on that boot and on every future boot, silently, while the sweep counted the
row as needing nothing. `portal_secret.seal_row`, which the WRITE path calls, knows the distinction:
`enc:v1:<token>` is not valid JSON, so a JSONB column takes `crypto.encrypt_json`'s `{"enc": …}`
envelope instead. The registry's own comment had even anticipated getting this wrong — and predicted
it would be *loud*, "a 400 from Postgres the first time a portal login tried to save its session".
It was not loud. The sweep never wrote at all.

**Name the class.** §CORE-04.3 above says *"No sweep spells a column name of its own"*, and that was
true. It is also only half of what a sweep needs to know. Every sweep read its writer's declaration
of **WHICH** columns hold a secret, and every sweep then decided **HOW** to seal them itself with an
inlined `crypto.encrypt`. Three of the four agreed with their writer **by luck** — one text column
takes one primitive, so there was nothing to disagree about. The fourth had two primitives and
disagreed. **Reading a registry for WHICH while deciding HOW yourself is a half-dereference, and a
half-dereference is a whole second home.** Which of the four it bites is decided by how many
primitives the family happens to need, not by how carefully the sweep was written.

**Find the siblings.** All four were the same shape, so all four were fixed in this change — not
only the one that had bitten:

| family | sealer it now APPLIES | was |
|---|---|---|
| `portal_secrets` | `portal_secret.seal_row` | its own patch, text-only — **the defect** |
| `customer_pins` | `pos.router.seal_customer_pin` (made public for this) | its own `crypto.encrypt`, agreeing by luck |
| `intake_sensitive` | `hr.router.seal_intake_value` (new — the save path inlined it too) | its own `crypto.encrypt`, agreeing by luck |
| `receipt_imports` | `receipt_import.seal_stored_row` | already correct; it is the shape the others now take |

`receipt_imports` was already right, which is the useful part: the fix is not a new pattern, it is
the pattern one sweep already had, applied to the other three.

**One fact, one home, dereferenced.** `SWEEPS` gains a `sealer` field — the writer-side function
that answers *"what does sealing a row of this family mean"*, as `module.function`. The sweep
APPLIES it and holds no primitive. Every sealer is **public**, because having a second caller is the
point; a leading underscore on a name two subsystems share is a lie about its blast radius.

**Locked so it cannot un-wire.** §I is a ratchet, not a repair: it asserts `encryption_backfill.py`
makes **no `encrypt` call at all**, so the next sweep cannot be written the old way and still pass.
Proved red both ways — reverting the sweep to the old comprehension fails 7 checks, three of them
the functional regression (the session blob stays readable, `sealed_columns` loses `session_state`).
`app/core/encryption_backfill.py` was consequently **removed** from `NO_STORED_WRITE`, whose excuse
for it had been *"the sweeps themselves encrypt, which is the point"* — that sentence was the defect
stated as a design principle, and §C's own staleness check removed it.

**Still true after this, and reported rather than fixed:** one `data_source` row (the V Accessorize
admin credential) carried a plaintext password, every other row being sealed — consistent with its
having been written after that boot's sweep, not with a sweep defect. Re-saving the row seals it,
and the next boot now catches it.

## §COMMCALC-03. EVALUATE A STORE WE DO NOT OWN YET — its own carrier feeds, our average expenses, its actual rent (owner directive 2026-10-12)

Owner, verbatim: *"need to make a module for evaluating the store sales for the store we need to take
over, but without creating the actual stores but upload the ma comm, max tx and handset prdering
data, import the expenses from our average expenses, keep the rent as what the actual rent is for the
new store and calculate the p&l also need to fillter out the family plans with more than 2 lines from
these reports for each month to assess if fraud is going on and cjhecking which phones are sold on
those, create a sub report in that menu to take out those phones from profitability or leave them.
thisis platform wide but situation at hand is for total, nothing hardocded and everything should be
clear with analysis"*

**Module:** `backend/app/modules/commcalc/prospect_eval.py` (the one home; pure, DB-free) ·
`backend/app/modules/commcalc/router.py` (six endpoints) ·
`frontend/src/app/(platform)/commcalc/store-takeover/page.tsx`
**Lock:** `backend/harness_prospect_eval.py` (380 checks) + `backend/harness_prospect_pl_trend.py`
(25 checks, the ENDPOINT over a fake client) — both run by `carrier-vocab-guard.yml`
**Migration:** `1077_store_prospect_eval.sql` (two new tables, five NULL config columns; moves no money)
**Module-graph fact:** `store_takeover_evaluation` (§50)

### COMMCALC-03.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index for an existing mechanism before building: `takeover`, `prospect`, `pro forma`,
`what-if`, `scenario`, `acquisition`, `family plan`, `lines per account`, `multi-line`. **Nothing
answers this question.** The three near misses, and why each is not it:

| candidate | why it is not this |
|---|---|
| the **What-If simulator** (§30.7) projects OUR OWN stores' payout under a changed pay plan — it has no concept of a store whose figures are not already in the books |
| the **P&L** (§4) computes a statement for a store that EXISTS. A prospect has no `store_mapping` row, deliberately, so no scope of it can be assembled |
| `raw_dlar_store.family_plan_pct` (§10) is the CARRIER's own store KPI — a percentage, with no account, no line and no device behind it, so it cannot answer "which phones are on that account" |

**What was reused instead of built** — every one of these is dereferenced, not copied:

| the question | the one home the evaluation reads |
|---|---|
| which P&L line does MA commission money book to, with what sign | `account/ma_store_pnl.ma_commission_bookings` |
| which P&L line does MA daily-TX money book to (residual / MDF / month spiff) | `account/ma_store_pnl.ma_tx_bookings` |
| where does a rebate dollar present (contra-COGS vs income) | `account/ma_store_pnl.rebate_route` |
| what did a handset cost, and what did the month's activated devices cost | `account/device_cogs.ma_unit_price_from_rows` / `ma_sold_cost_from_rows` (both FACTORED OUT of the existing I/O functions here, which now call them — no behaviour changed) |
| which P&L line does an expense row book to | `account/coa.route_expense_line` |
| what is the chart of accounts, and its labels | `account/coa.PL_SPEC` / `PL_SECTION` / `PL_LABEL` |
| how is a statement assembled from an inputs dict | `account/engine._assemble` |
| what are a statement's four totals | `account/analysis.pl_totals` |
| what were a month's effective store expenses | `commcalc/expenses_effective.effective_series` |
| how is an uploaded sheet read, mapped and shape-corrected | `commcalc/column_mapping` (`load_rules` → `default_mapping` → `map_records` → `split_footer_rows` → `derive_row_periods`), via `router._read_upload_df` |
| which table does a prospect feed mirror | `commcalc/column_mapping.TABLE_MAP` |
| how is a period spelled | `account/_period.period_keys` |

§D of the lock is an **AST scan that fails the build** if `prospect_eval.py` ever names a P&L line
outside its declared coverage vocabulary, reads a carrier money column directly, defines a booking
function of its own, or imports a database client. That is the anti-un-wiring: a registry written and
left un-dereferenced has happened three times here (§19.18).

### COMMCALC-03.2 Why a prospect is NOT a store row

The cheap implementation is to create the store, upload its feeds into the live `raw_*` tables and
read the P&L. The owner forbade it, and the structural reason is worth stating once: a
`commcalc.store_mapping` row is reachable by **every** live surface — the consolidated P&L, the GP
report, the expense matrix, the commission engine, payroll, the dashboards and the targets. A store
we are only *considering* would move the company's real books and real payouts, and would keep moving
them after we walked away from the deal. There is also no staging database to rehearse it in.

So a prospect is a row in `commcalc.store_prospect`, carrying **no `store_code`** — that absence is
the safety property, not an omission — and its uploaded rows land in `commcalc.prospect_feed_row`,
which no live reader reads. The evaluation is computed on demand and persisted nowhere a statement
can find it. §G of the lock walks the router's prospect functions in the AST and **fails the build**
if any of them names a `raw_*` table, a store-mapping / alias / roster table or
`account_statements`, or if a write lands anywhere but the two prospect tables.

### COMMCALC-03.3 ONE landing table, not three

The obvious shape — `prospect_ma_commission`, `prospect_ma_daily_tx`, `prospect_ma_fulfillment` — is
three sibling derivations of three live tables, which is the duplicate defect these rules already
forbid: three schemas to keep in step with three live ones forever. `prospect_feed_row` holds **one
row per uploaded line as JSONB in the live table's own column shape**, so the booking one-homes above
read a prospect row and a live row identically and there is no translation layer to drift. A new
prospect feed is an entry in `prospect_eval.FEED_REGISTRY` — whose keys ARE the platform's own report
keys — never a migration.

The upload replaces **(prospect, feed, period)** only: the slice the file proves it owns, the same
posture `ingest_slice` gives the live feeds (§2). An identical re-upload replaces its own slice and
nothing else, so it can never double-count, and another month is never touched.

### COMMCALC-03.4 The family-plan question, answered from the data

**WHICH COLUMN IS THE ACCOUNT is a declared ordered ladder read per ROW**, not a column name in code
(`prospect_account_key_columns`, house default `['ban','bin']`). The default is MEASURED, not guessed
— live house platform, LuxeLink August 2026, `raw_ma_commission`, 1,248 rows:

| column | populated | distinct | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ban` | 27 rows | 27 | the account number by name, but filled on 2% of this platform's file |
| `bin` | 1,248 rows | 1,031 | **the account**: max 5 lines on one value |
| `activation_order` | 1,248 rows | 1,248 | the LINE, not the account |

and **every one of the 163 multi-line `bin` values resolved to ONE store, on ONE day, with
consecutive activation orders, all `activation_type='Add'`**. That is the signature of a multi-line
account and nothing else. Live distribution: 860 accounts with one line, 129 with two, 24 with three,
7 with four, 6 with five — so at the house threshold (more than 2, **exclusive**, as the owner said)
**37 accounts carrying 130 lines** are flagged for August.

**It is a who-to-look-at list, not a verdict.** A family of four buying four phones on one account on
one day is a good sale and reads identically in this feed to the thing the owner is worried about. So
a flagged account carries the evidence a human needs to tell them apart — the lines, the devices and
their IMEIs, the day span, the processor account, how many are add-a-lines — and **no verdict field
exists on it**; §B of the lock asserts that.

### COMMCALC-03.5 The sub-report: take the phones out, or leave them

Both scenarios are **always computed** and returned together. A toggle that recomputed one of them
would mean the two numbers never appear side by side, which is the only way to read what the flagged
accounts are worth; `exclusion_mode` only names which one the screen opens on.

Excluding a flagged line removes **its handset from COGS too** — `device_cogs.ma_sold_cost_from_rows`
gained a `skip_imeis` argument (inert for every existing caller: `None` reproduces the pre-factoring
behaviour exactly) because dropping a line is not enough when the same physical handset also sits on
a line that was kept. The live feed repeats an IMEI on 17 of 1,248 August rows, so this is not
hypothetical: without it, excluded revenue would be measured against a cost that stayed. What was
skipped is counted on `meta.skipped_imeis`, never silent. On live August data the flagged accounts
carry **3.86% of the carrier-side bottom line**.

### COMMCALC-03.6 "Our average expenses" — and the two ways averaging goes wrong

The average is taken over the last `prospect_expense_basis_months` (default 3) **complete** months,
through `expenses_effective.effective_series` — the same figures the Expenses sheet and the live P&L
book, never the raw table. The first draft divided each line's window total by every (store, month)
cell in the window, and running it over the live house matrix showed that **understates a cost on a
takeover decision, twice**:

| fault | live evidence | effect |
|---|---|---|
| a month whose sheet OMITS a line | May 2026 records no salary line at all (Dm Salary, Employee Salaries, Owner / Mgmt Salaries, Employee Commission: 0 of 25 stores) | Employee Salaries read **$2,371.17**/month against a real **$4,329.96** — a $1,958 hole in the largest controllable cost |
| a month whose store ROSTER is wider than the line | July 2026 has expense rows for 34 store codes while every line is recorded on 25 | **every one of the 17 lines** divided by 34, understating all of them by 26% |

So the fold is per (line, **month**) first and only then across months: Σ ÷ the stores carrying the
line THAT month, then the mean over the months the line **appears in**, never over the window. Both
faults disappear by construction, and §C of the lock carries **armed negative controls** that
reproduce the pre-fix arithmetic and assert it is wrong, so a regression to it cannot pass. On the
live matrix the house opex total moved from $10,965.73 to **$14,225.48**.

`months_present` / `months_missing` and `store_coverage` are reported **per line**, so a line the
window only half-covers is visible rather than quietly smoothed — the house rule that an absence is
never a finding, applied to an average.

Two figures are always returned on every line and the declared basis
(`prospect_expense_average_basis`) only picks which one books: what a store that **has** the line
pays (house default — the store being taken over will pay rent, electric and salaries), or what a
**typical** store pays once the stores with no such line are counted (live house: Garbage / Waste
$100.00 on 12 of 25 stores ⇒ $43.76 typical).

**Rent is the one substitution.** The prospect's own `actual_rent_monthly` replaces the averaged rent
in place, keeping the average it displaced on `replaced_average` so the two can be compared on screen.
No rent entered ⇒ the average stands and is LABELLED `origin='average'`, never presented as the real
figure. Several declared rent lines split the entered figure in proportion to our own averages and
still sum to it exactly.

### COMMCALC-03.7 What this evaluation CANNOT answer, said out loud

The three uploads are the DISTRIBUTOR's view of a store: what the carrier paid, what airtime margin
it earned, what handsets it bought. They are **not** a point-of-sale feed, so retail device and
accessory revenue, bill-pay fee income and the store's own cash are not in them. A P&L booking those
as `0.00` would read as a measurement of zero and would understate the prospect by whatever its
counter actually takes.

So `coverage()` walks the whole chart and gives every line one of three verdicts — `measured`,
`not_measured` (with the reason) or `uploaded_feed_missing` (naming the feed that would answer it) —
and the bottom line is LABELLED a **carrier-side contribution**, not net income. On live August data:
12 lines measured, 23 not measured. §E of the lock asserts no line nothing can answer is ever
reported as a measured zero.

### COMMCALC-03.8 Where it is, and what it reads

| surface | path |
|---|---|
| the prospect list and its config | `GET /commcalc/prospects` |
| open / change / drop an evaluation | `POST /commcalc/prospects`, `PUT`/`DELETE /commcalc/prospects/{id}` |
| upload one feed (live reader + live mapping, prospect destination) | `POST /commcalc/prospects/{id}/upload` |
| THE MONTH-OVER-MONTH P&L and the month-or-range window (§COMMCALC-03.28) | `GET /commcalc/prospects/{id}/pl-trend?period=&period_to=&mode=` |
| THE evaluation — P&L both ways (the commission line in its two month-of-life parts, §COMMCALC-15), the flag list, the coverage, `commission_leg_store_months` (M2–M12 per store, every uploaded month, both bases) and `scenarios[mode].leg_split` (what the split moved, with its own identity proof) | `GET /commcalc/prospects/{id}/evaluation?period=` |

**ONE ASSEMBLY, TWO SURFACES**: the P&L screen and the family-plan sub-report read the same payload
(the §59.7 pattern), so the two can never disagree about which accounts were flagged or what
excluding them is worth. The screen is a Management Overview **dashboard tile**, not a sidebar row
(owner's "cleaner look" ruling) — placed on the hub so it can be found.

Config, all five NULL-seeded on `commcalc.commission_org_config` (RULE TWO — no carrier, tenant or
product name anywhere in the module): `prospect_account_key_columns`,
`prospect_family_line_threshold`, `prospect_expense_basis_months`, `prospect_rent_expense_names`,
`prospect_expense_average_basis`. Every one falls back to its measured house default, so the module
behaves identically before and after mig 1077 is applied.

---

### COMMCALC-03.9 An upload that failed left no record anywhere (owner report 2026-10-13)

Owner, verbatim: *"jose was not able to uloasd the filres"*, and an hour later *"i just upladed
handset infor monthwise and also all teptherg but it does nto show me any link for a report"*. Both
reduced to one fact, and it was not the fact either of them described.

**Measured in production before anything was built.** Two tables, each written BEFORE parsing, agree
that nothing a person uploaded reached the API that day: `commcalc.upload_trace` (written in a
`finally`, so a wrong file, a parse error, a crash and a refused duplicate all land a row) and
`core.import_batches` (the bytes are claimed before they are read). Jose was signed in at 18:05 UTC
and his `market_manager` role carries `permissions.scope = 'all'` plus the `commissions` module, so
RBAC was not hiding the tile. That pair is the triage table, and it is now written down so nobody
re-derives it:

| `upload_trace` | `core.import_batches` | what it means |
|---|---|---|
| present, `status='error'` | present | the importer refused it — read `error` verbatim |
| **absent** | **absent** | the request never reached the API (browser, auth, CORS, gateway 502/413) |
| absent | present, stuck `parsing` | died between the claim and the trace (rare) |

**THE CLASS, not the instance.** "Did this ingest happen, and what did it do" has ONE home —
`commcalc/router._write_upload_trace`, the owner's debug-first surface — and the prospect upload was a
writing ingest that did not dereference it. Fixing only that endpoint is the patchwork CLAUDE.md
forbids, so the general fact is enforced: `harness_upload_trace_coverage.py` (34 checks, run by the
store-takeover job) scans the router, DERIVES which upload endpoints write rows from the call graph
rather than from a name list, and fails the build when a writing upload endpoint is silent and
unregistered. **Six siblings are still silent** and are declared with a reason each
(`upload_mapped`, `commission_ledger_import`, `onboarding_intake_analyze`,
`onboarding_intake_commit`, `import_product_mrc`, `ma_overview_upload_report`); the register may only
shrink, and `PINNED_MAX` must EQUAL the measured count, so a slack pin cannot stop the ratchet. Two
of them trace through a helper the scan cannot follow — the scan resolves writers inside
`commcalc/router.py` only, and that limit is stated in the lock rather than implied, which is why a
register line for an endpoint the scan calls read-only also fails the build.

The prospect upload is now a thin traced wrapper over `_upload_prospect_feed_impl`, the posture
`upload_file` already had, tracing under `source='prospect-upload'` with the prospect named in the
note (no migration: `upload_trace` carries no prospect column, and a diagnostic does not justify
mutating the schema).

### COMMCALC-03.10 A row count is not a measure of what a file answered

The same report, second half. `rows_written: 66,388` was reported for "empire" and read as success.
What had actually landed was 66,388 rows of ONE feed — the commission and daily-TX feeds had never
been uploaded at all — and the marketplace export lists **twenty order types** while carrying a
ship-to, a cost and a date on the handset orders ALONE: of 68,000 rows scanned, **897 carry a store
and 798 are branded-handset orders**, and 3,103 carry no date. Seven Empire stores are in there
(TSPIDs 169291/169292/169335/169336/169441/169442/169445), which is what makes a per-store report
possible at all — and `raw_ma_commission.merchant_account_id`, `raw_ma_daily_tx.account_id` and
`raw_ma_fulfillment.tspid` are the SAME identifier space (verified on live house data: 170074,
170083, 170084 appear in both feeds), so one key joins all three.

`prospect_eval.substance(rows)` measures it, and deliberately knows nothing about any feed: it asks
only whether a mapped row carries a value outside the period columns, and those columns are read from
`data_lineage_registry.MONTH_COLUMNS` — the one home — never from a list kept beside it. So it cannot
drift from a feed's real shape and it is right about a feed that does not exist yet.
`substance_note` returns **None** when nothing is wrong (an absence is never a finding), names the
column mapping as the thing to check when EVERY row is hollow, and the screen stops calling such an
upload a success.

### COMMCALC-03.11 Which month the report opens on, from every feed

The actual cause of the blank screen, and a third instance of the same shape. The default period was
`max(period)` over the **commission feed alone**; with no commission rows it fell through to *today's
month*, which no uploaded row covers, so seven months of uploaded handset orders were filtered out of
the read and the report was empty on data sitting in the table.

`prospect_eval.default_period(periods_by_feed)` is the one home. Commission still LEADS where it has
rows — it is where the P&L's revenue comes from, so opening on a month with money in it is the useful
default — otherwise the latest month ANY feed names wins, and a month only the other feeds name beats
a month nothing names. It ALWAYS returns a stated `basis` (and names the commission gap when that is
why), every month with rows in `months_available`, and `""` rather than a guess when no row names a
month. The endpoint publishes the basis on the payload and the screen prints it, so the month the
report opened on is never implied. §J of the lock fails the build if the retired single-feed read
reappears.


### COMMCALC-03.12 Which column names the store — one home, and FOUR copies rewired to it

A distributor feed carries no store code. It carries the dealer's **processor account**, and the three
master-agent feeds each spell it differently: `raw_ma_commission.merchant_account_id`,
`raw_ma_daily_tx.account_id`, `raw_ma_fulfillment.tspid`. They are ONE identifier space, verified on
live house data (170074 / 170083 / 170084 appear in both the commission and the fulfilment feed),
which is what lets one key join all three.

Those spellings were hand-written inline — three times in `account/ma_store_pnl.py`, once per booking
function, and a fourth time in `prospect_eval.flag_multi_line_accounts`, which §L of the lock caught
the moment it was written. §19.18's shape exactly: one fact, four copies, nothing holding them
together. The fact is now declared once in
`data_lineage_registry.STORE_ACCOUNT_COLUMN_BY_TABLE` / `store_account_column(table)` — the registry
that already owns per-table column facts — and **every reader dereferences it, including the three
that were already there**. `None` is a declaration: the table names no dealer account, so its money
is booked company-wide rather than guessed onto a store. §L3 fails the build if any of the three
spellings reappears outside the registry; `harness_ma_store_pnl.py` holds at its pre-change result
(37 passed / 2 failed, both pre-existing on `main` and unrelated), so the live booking path is
byte-identical.

### COMMCALC-03.13 A column per store, from the uploads (owner ask 2026-10-13)

Owner, verbatim: *"it shoud automatically pick up the store names from teh uploaded sheets … similarly
the c P&l will also be displayed in columns based ont eh stores infor uploaed"*.

**Nothing new resolves a store.** `account/ma_store_pnl.account_store_index` is already the pure
answer to "which store is this processor account": it reads the dealer's own fulfilment rows (account
plus ship-to on every order line) and **drops** an account seen at two different addresses rather than
mis-attributing it — the phantom-store lesson the house has already paid for. It is injected pure
(never `load_store_index`, which would read OUR fulfilment table) so a prospect's stores come from the
prospect's own rows. Live "empire": **7 stores**, TSPIDs 169291 / 169292 / 169335 / 169336 / 169441 /
169442 / 169445.

`store_index` adds only what a prospect needs: the display **name** (`business_name`, beside the
address), and the accounts that appear **only** in the commission or transaction feed — those have no
address because no handset was ever shipped to them, and dropping them would silently move their money
out of the per-store view, so they are kept and labelled by account number with `has_address` saying
which is which. A prospect's addresses are deliberately NOT collapsed onto our canonical store
spellings: they are not our stores, and resolving them through `coa.store_resolver` is how a prospect
starts appearing in the company's own rollups.

**ONE booking path builds the whole and every column.** `evaluate`'s inner `_book` is called once for
the prospect and once per store, and each column is assembled by the same `_assemble` the
whole-prospect statement uses — a second loop over a store's rows is exactly how the columns would stop
summing to the total, which is the only thing that makes a per-store view trustworthy. §N1 asserts
revenue, COGS and net income tie, and §N4 that activations do.

**A store's column carries no share of our average expenses, and says so** (`expenses_included:
false`). That average is already ONE store's worth of rent, salaries and utilities (§COMMCALC-03.6):
splitting it across seven sites would divide a per-store cost by seven and make every column look
profitable, and repeating it on each would multiply the chain's cost sevenfold against the statement
above. So a column is the store's carrier-side contribution, and the expense comparison stays where it
is honest — on the whole-prospect statement and in the break-even block, which is per store by design.
A row naming no store lands under `UNATTRIBUTED_STORE`, a label and never a store, which is what keeps
the columns summing to the whole.

### COMMCALC-03.14 What the counter has to sell for this store to work

Owner, verbatim: *"Since no pos data is being loaded, the system should calculate … how much
accessories have to sold … that will be gross expnses less teh gross revenue = total loss = break even
needed by selling accessories , then deivde teh number with the total actiavations done for tehat store
in a particlua month to get teh APB needed to be profiavle"*.

This **turns the evaluation's own limit into the answer**. §COMMCALC-03.7 already says out loud that
the three uploads are the distributor's view and carry no retail accessory revenue, so those lines read
`not_measured` rather than zero. His question is the right one to ask of exactly that gap: not what the
counter took — nothing here can know — but **what it would have to take**. So
`accessory_break_even` is a REQUIREMENT, never a measurement, and every field name says so.

The arithmetic is not re-derived: revenue, COGS and expenses come from `analysis.pl_totals` injected —
the one home for a statement's totals, the same figures the dashboard reads — so this block can never
disagree with the statement printed above it. The shortfall is taken off the statement's own
`net_income` rather than re-summed from the sections, which is what keeps it tied. Handset cost is
inside it (the default the owner was told about): a store that must buy phones to earn the commission
carries that cost either way.

Two refusals, both load-bearing. **A store already in profit gets `needed: None`, not `0.00`** — a
zero target reads as "sell nothing", the opposite of true — with `already_profitable` saying so. And
**no activations means `per_activation: None`, never a division and never a zero**, with
`per_activation_basis` stating that the commission feed records no box to divide by.
`activation_count` counts one per line on `activation_order`, the identifier `line_id` already uses
(measured 1,248 distinct over 1,248 rows); a row with no identifier still counts as a line, because it
is a line the feed named badly, not a line that did not happen.

### COMMCALC-03.15 The accounts at the bottom, and the number underneath them

Owner, verbatim: *"hightlight the 3 lines plus deemed fraud at the bottim of the report imn nunmber of
those accounts and below that subtract the inform received from those accoutns to assess a real
number of there is any fraud going on"*.

Two figures in the order he asked for them: how many accounts, then the same report with their money
taken out. The second is why the evaluation already computes BOTH exclusion modes side by side
(§COMMCALC-03.5), so `fraud_exposure` **names that pair as the fraud read** rather than computing a
third answer — the money comes off the two assembled statements through `scenario_delta`, injected.
`net_without_them` and `moved` are `None` when no delta is supplied; not measured is never shown as
zero.

Banded by line count from the data, never a fixed list, because "3 lines" and "nine lines on one
account" are not one finding and a single count hides the difference. The whole file is reported
beside it so a count has a denominator.

**`deemed_fraud` is deliberately not a field.** That is not a style preference: it is the lesson
§COMMCALC-05 paid for on live data, where a legitimate household bundle and a four-handset $0.00 promo
run are indistinguishable until a human opens the receipts. What is returned is a count, the money, and
the report without the money; the word belongs to the person reading it. §P6 fails the build if a field
here claims fraud.

### COMMCALC-03.16 What handsets this store ordered

Owner, verbatim: *"it does nto show me any link for a report to asses teh handsets ordered"*. There was
no such report: the fulfilment feed was read only as a PRICE LIST (`ma_unit_price_from_rows`), which is
what it is for costing an activated line, and nothing showed the orders themselves.

**Measured first, and it changes what the report may claim.** Over 68,000 live rows the export lists
**twenty order types** and carries a ship-to, a cost and a date on the handset orders ALONE: 798 rows
are branded-handset orders, 897 carry any store, 3,103 carry no date. So `handset_orders` reports what
carries a price, **counts what does not beside it, and names the order types it set aside** with the
reason — an absence stated, never smoothed into a total as zero. `number_ordered` is units and `price`
is the unit price, multiplied the way the live device-costing home multiplies them, so the extended
cost here and the COGS on the statement cannot disagree. A priced row with no unit count is one unit,
not none. Broken out by model, by store (reading as its address, through `store_index`) and by month,
across every month uploaded, because a handset ordered in one month is often activated in the next.

### COMMCALC-03.17 A month that has not ended is not the month to open on (owner report 2026-10-13)

Owner, verbatim: *"i uploaded all files, it is not givening the p&l for each in columns"*. Everything
was uploaded and the data was right: 5,495 commission rows over eight months, naming **7** dealer
accounts. The report opened on **October 2026**, which held **3 of those 5,495 rows** — 0.05% —
because it was the 13th of October and the statement had barely started. The P&L, the per-store
columns and the break-even all rendered off a part-month and read as broken.

§COMMCALC-03.11 had replaced "today's month" with "the latest month the feed covers", which fixed a
blank report and introduced this one. **Recency is not coverage.** The rule now opens on the latest
month that has ENDED, and says so:

- A part-month is a fact about the CALENDAR, so no row-count threshold is guessed anywhere —
  a month is skipped only because it has not finished. `harness_prospect_eval.py` §J24 fails the
  build on a month skipped for being small.
- The unfinished month is NAMED (`in_progress`) and stays in the picker. Skipped is not hidden.
- When the ONLY month with rows is the current one, the report still opens on it and the basis says
  *"these figures are a part-month"* — a report that opens on nothing is the defect this replaced.
- A FUTURE month (a mis-stamped row) is not opened on either: the test is "has ended", not "is not
  this month".
- `default_period` stays PURE and reads no clock; the endpoint supplies `today`. §J22 asserts the
  endpoint passes it and §J23 that the home has no `datetime` of its own. With no date supplied the
  answer is byte-identical to the old rule (§J21), which is what keeps §J1–J11 unchanged.

### COMMCALC-03.18 The P&L with a column per store (owner ask 2026-10-13)

Owner, verbatim: *"it shoudl ahve 8 columns for each seaporate store"*. §COMMCALC-03.13 gave a table
with **a row per store** — the same figures, the wrong axis for reading a P&L. He wants the lines
down the side and the stores across the top, which is how the finance P&L reads.

**No server change, and no new arithmetic.** The per-store statements are already assembled by the
same builder as the whole-prospect one (§COMMCALC-03.13), so the matrix is a transposition of data
already returned:

- The ROWS are the whole-prospect statement's own lines, in its own order — the screen invents no
  line and names no account.
- Each CELL is read from that store's own statement by line `key`. Nothing is summed on the screen,
  so **the columns adding across to "All stores" is a check, not an arrangement**: if a store's
  dollars were missed, the row visibly fails to add rather than being quietly balanced.
- Then the subtotals (carrier revenue, device cost, gross profit, expenses, carrier-side
  contribution), the activated-line count, and the two break-even figures per column.
- The expense lines sit under **All stores** only, for the §COMMCALC-03.13 reason: our average is
  already ONE store's worth of rent, salaries and utilities, so charging it to each column would
  make every store look profitable. Each column's accessory target IS figured against the full
  single-store expense (§COMMCALC-03.14).
- Through `ReportShell` with a dynamic `ExportColumn[]`, so it sorts, filters and exports like every
  other table (owner directive 2026-08-10, locked by `harness_table_sort_lock`).

The row-per-store table stays: it sorts by contribution and answers "which site is carrying this
deal", which a matrix does not.

### COMMCALC-03.19 The expense in every column, and the profit-or-loss line (owner directive 2026-10-13)

Owner, verbatim: *"add teh expenses in teh expenses line and give ,e teh final p&l nunmber to see if
teh store is profitable aor loss, give me the net income line calcculated"*.

§COMMCALC-03.13 had left every store column carrying **no** expenses, with the reasoning stated
there. The owner has now ruled on it, and the ruling is sound, because our average expense figure is
**already one store's worth** of rent, salaries and utilities (§COMMCALC-03.6) — so there were only
ever two honest things to do with it:

| | What it does | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **Split** it across the prospect's sites | divides a per-store cost by seven; every column looks profitable | refused — it answers no question anyone asked |
| **Charge each column the whole of it** | the column answers *"could THIS site stand on its own?"* | **ships** — and it is the basis the per-store break-even has used since §COMMCALC-03.14 |

**The consequence is stated, not hidden.** Revenue, device cost and activated lines still add across
to the all-stores column, because those are the store's own money. **The expense and net-income rows
deliberately do not** — seven columns carry seven copies of a one-store cost on purpose. The screen
prints that in the panel above the table, and `prospect_eval.STORE_EXPENSE_BASIS` is the ONE sentence
saying it, carried on every column as `expenses_basis` so a reader of a column is never left to
assume.

**One phrase for the bottom line, everywhere on the screen.** With expenses charged, the figure is
the P&L bottom line, so "carrier-side contribution" became misleading; but calling it net income
would overstate it, because a takeover pack carries **no accessory and no bill-payment feed**
(§COMMCALC-03.7). Both labels are now **"profit or loss on measured revenue"**, on the summary tile,
in the matrix and in the row-per-store table, with the tile's subtitle saying a real month is better
than this figure by whatever the counter sells — which is exactly what §COMMCALC-03.14's accessory
target quantifies. The screen no longer says "NOT net income" in one place and "net income" in
another.

**Locked** by `harness_prospect_eval.py` §N7–N15 (224 passed / 0 failed), which holds BOTH halves:
N8 every column is charged the whole expense and not a share; N9 the expense row therefore does not
add across; N10/N11 revenue, device cost and activations still tie; **N12 the net-income gap is
exactly the extra copies of the one-store expense, so nothing is lost or invented**; N13 a column's
bottom line is its own revenue less its own costs less the full expense; N14 the basis is one
sentence in one place and warns that those rows do not add.


### COMMCALC-03.20 Every month at the bottom, and the filters at the top (owner ask 2026-10-13)

Owner, verbatim: *"Also I need the accounts which are 2 more summarized at the bottom for each month
with the drill down will all standard filters on top of the page so they run all across"*.

**Two asks, and the first one is a comparison no single month can make.** One account carrying four
lines in one month is a family; the same shape in five consecutive months is a pattern. The month
report (§COMMCALC-03.15) could only ever answer for the month on screen.

`prospect_eval.multi_line_by_month(rows, columns, threshold)` answers it, and it is **not a second
count**: it calls `account_groups`, `flag_multi_line_accounts` and `multi_line_summary` — the month
report's own three functions — and slices their output per period. A per-month counter of its own
would be the duplicate derivation the index rules forbid and would drift from the figure on screen the
first time either changed. **§R1 fails the build if the month on screen and this table's row for that
month ever disagree**, by rebuilding the month report the way the screen builds it and asserting the
two dicts are equal. R3/R4 hold the partition (the months add up to the whole, nothing double-counted
and no flagged account lost or shown twice), R5 reports a month with rows and nothing flagged **as
zero rather than omitting it**, R12/R13 fail the build if the function stops dereferencing those three
or starts re-tallying, and R10 keeps §P6's rule: no field here reaches a verdict.

It costs **no extra query**. `router._prospect_feed_rows` already read every row the prospect has in
order to filter one month out of them, so it now returns `(feeds, every_month)` from that same read —
a second query for rows already in hand is both a cost and a chance for two reads to disagree about
what was uploaded. The month is stamped on the **feed row**, not reliably inside the row, so it is
carried onto the row there; `_row_period` is the ONE home for reading it and the grouping, the
substance check and the handset report were all rewired to it (three hand-written copies, found by
§R15 the moment the lock was written).

**The filters.** The platform already has the one home for this — `<StandardFilterBar>` over a
`StandardFilterValue` (RULE FIVE, §3d) — so the page adopts it and has no bar of its own:

- **Month** drives the server query, exactly as before.
- **Stores** narrow every section that names a store: the P&L matrix columns, the row-per-store
  table, the handset orders by store and the flagged-account list. `storeFilter` is the single place
  deciding which stores are admitted, because a matrix showing three stores beside a store table
  showing five is worse than no filter at all. It carries the store's key, its address and its
  processor account off ONE store record, so a section keyed by address and a section keyed by
  account number narrow to the same stores.
- **Market** and **person** are omitted and the deviation is stated: a store we do not own sits in no
  market of ours and has nobody on our roster, so those two could only filter everything away.
- The module's own five filters (min lines, account, model/IMEI, one-day, add-a-lines) and the
  keep-versus-exclude switch are **appended** on the right. The core set is never substituted.

**Where the filters do NOT reach is printed on the screen, not left to be discovered.** The
whole-prospect P&L, its tiles and the keep-versus-exclude figures are the whole month either way —
they are what the prospect is worth in total. The month table is every uploaded month on purpose, so
the Month filter does not narrow it; and the Stores filter does not either, because an account's lines
can sit on more than one processor account and a per-store count of them could be tied back to neither.

**A shared-component defect the adoption surfaced.** `StandardFilterBar`'s month dropdown selected
`value.period` only when it was seven characters long (ISO `YYYY-MM`) while **also** appending an
option for a period its list does not carry — two contradictory rules. Any surface whose months are
spelled the way a carrier statement spells them (`August 2026`, which this platform stores as a
period) therefore rendered its month dropdown **blank over a report that was showing that very
month**. Fixed as a class, in the lib rather than the page: `standard-filters.monthSelectValue` and
`monthNeedsOwnOption` are the one home, the bar dereferences them, and
`scratchpad/prove_standard_filters.mjs` (40 passed / 0 failed) holds both halves plus a source check
that the bar has not un-wired and that no copy of the discarded `length === 7` rule survives. **It is
a byte-for-byte no-op for every adopter whose months are ISO** and a fix for every adopter whose
months are not.

**Where it is:** `/commcalc/store-takeover`, bottom of the page, every table through `ReportShell`
(the one sorted/exportable table, `harness_table_sort_lock`) with the drill-down opened by a row
click.


### COMMCALC-03.21 The breakup of what was sold (owner ask 2026-10-13)

Owner, verbatim: *"Also summarize at the end of the report, the breakup of Phones tablets, Fios VHI,
and if any other item was sold"*.

**RULE TWO decides the vocabulary, not the wording of the ask.** "Fios" and "VHI" are one carrier's
brand names for home internet, and a carrier name in code is what RULE TWO forbids — the
`carrier-vocab-guard` job fails the build over it. So the CLASS is `home_internet`, labelled "Home
internet", and the WORDS that match it are config: the house tokens are generic (`home internet`,
`router`, `internet`, `gateway`) and a tenant whose feed spells it its own way declares its own
tokens. `harness_prospect_eval.py` §S10 fails the build if a brand reaches the mechanism's source,
and §S11 proves a tenant declaring `vhi` gets it matched.

**One home, not a sibling.** The rules live in `commcalc/product_mix.py`, which has owned "read a
product description" since §62 (`model_of`). It gains `resolve_product_classes`, `product_class_of`
and `product_breakup`; `prospect_eval.products_sold` only names WHICH COLUMNS of the prospect's sheet
answer, through `PRODUCT_DESC_COLUMN` / `NO_DEVICE_COLUMN`. §S17 fails the build if a second copy of
the rules appears in the report, and §S14 — which **caught a second read of the product column in
`device_keys_of` the moment it was written** — fails it if a caller stops dereferencing them.

**Measured on the live feed first (5,495 commission rows, Total by Verizon, 2026-10-13), and it
changed the design twice.**

| | Lines | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Phone | 4,650 | residual — a real product name matching no class token |
| Tablet | 354 | a word in the product name |
| Home internet | 78 | a word in the product name |
| Hotspot | 1 | a word in the product name |
| Watch, accessory | 0 | declared classes nobody sold — **reported as zero, never omitted** |
| No device sold | 383 | the feed's own `byop` declaration |
| No product named | 29 | nothing to read |

- **There is no declared product-class column.** `sub_type` is blank on 4,027 of 5,495 rows and `TWP`
  on the rest; `activation_type2` says only `branded` or `byop`. So the class is read from the product
  description, and every line therefore carries its **basis** — a class read off a keyword is not the
  evidence a declared one is, which is the §66 lesson, and the screen prints the four counts.
- **`Product Not Available` looks like missing data and is not.** 383 of those 412 rows DECLARE
  `byop` — the customer brought their own phone and no device was sold. A declared fact outranks a
  description (§S3), so those land in `no_device`; the 29 that declare nothing are named on their own
  line and **never folded into phones** (§S7).

**The residual is a device, and that is a choice with a cost, stated.** A real product name matching
no class token counts as a phone, because a handset feed's unmatched names are overwhelmingly
handsets. The cost is that a genuinely new category reads as a phone until its token is declared, so
`basis_counts.residual_device` reports how many were placed that way and the phone row carries its own
model list — which is where a human scanning the breakup sees something that is plainly not a phone.
`unplaced` deliberately lists ONLY the rows that named nothing: an "unplaced" list carrying 4,650
ordinary handsets is a list nobody reads (§S8).

**What it is not narrowed by, and why.** The store filter (§COMMCALC-03.20) does not touch this
table: a commission row names a processor account, not the store address the classes would have to be
keyed by, and a per-store count nobody could tie back is worse than none.

**Locked** by §S1–S17 (256 passed / 0 failed): S1 the classes add up to the file with nothing lost or
double-counted; S4 a declared class nobody sold is a zero, not an omission; S9 the models come from the
one model home so a promo-decorated line and a bare one are one product; S12 a token matches on a WORD
boundary (`tab` inside another word is not a tablet); S13 an empty class list is honoured; S16 an empty
feed produces an empty breakup rather than a zero claim.

**Where it is:** `/commcalc/store-takeover`, the last section of the report, through `ReportShell`
with its "share of lines" column declaring `agg: 'none'` (§COMMCALC-03.20 — a share does not add).


### COMMCALC-03.22 Booked under the ORG'S OWN declared rules, not the house defaults (owner report 2026-10-14)

Owner, verbatim: *"gross profit shoudl includea ll incoming income like reisduakl merchant discoutn
ayto pay , all spiff etc, recheck and fix"* and *"the Store by store — 8 stores named by the uploaded
sheets should have gross profit instead of carrier evenue to claculate accessories to be sold"*.

He was right, and the cause was not a missing booking rule. §COMMCALC-03 books through the company's
own `ma_store_pnl` functions — and `router._prospect_homes` handed them **`default_config()` /
`default_ma_pnl_config()`**, the HOUSE answers, while the live P&L for the same organisation reads
that organisation's own row. Those functions are config-driven by design, so four declarations were
silently overridden:

| switch | the org declares | the house default | what the default cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pl_ma_month_spiff_source` | `daily_tx` | `commission_sheet` | every month-spiff cash row in the daily-transaction feed booked **nothing** — and in the other direction the sheet's `spiff_m1`, the ONLY place the first month is reported, books nothing (§COMMCALC-17) |
| `pl_ma_month_spiff_source_by_rung` (mig `1087`) | `{"m1":"commission_sheet"}` | `{}` | with `{}` every rung reads the scalar, so the first month read the cash that had arrived instead of the sheet's `spiff_m1` — §COMMCALC-17.7 |
| `pl_mdf_product_tokens` | one token | `[]` | market-development money booked **nothing** |
| `pl_ma_store_attribution` | `true` | `false` | all airtime margin, residual, MDF and spiff money booked company-wide, so **no store column could carry one dollar of it** |
| `pl_ma_residual_order_types` | one family | the mig-309 default | (identical in effect here, and that is why it must still be read rather than assumed) |

**THE CLASS:** *an evaluation that books through the company's own code must book under the company's
own declared config. Injecting a default is a second, invisible declaration* — invisible because the
figures it produces look exactly like figures.

### COMMCALC-03.22a MEASURED on the live prospect, both ways

65,491 daily-transaction rows + 5,495 commission rows + the 66,388-row handset price list, 2026-10-14,
read-only. The daily-transaction feed alone books **$435,121.34** of income over eight months under the
org's declared rules against **$112,740.46** under the house defaults — $322,380.88 of month spiffs and
MDF that the report was not showing.

Whole-prospect revenue and gross profit, house default → the org's own rules:

| month | revenue | gross profit |
|---|---|---|
| June 2026 | 89,632.45 → **98,357.97** | 64,776.79 → **73,502.31** |
| July 2026 | 81,965.97 → **97,580.15** | 55,924.11 → **71,538.29** |
| August 2026 | 46,730.96 → **103,543.54** | 56,917.31 → **113,729.89** |
| September 2026 | 32,844.47 → **78,094.72** | 22,131.13 → **67,381.38** |

**NOT A UNIFORM INCREASE, and the reason is stated rather than smoothed:** the spiff source also decides
WHICH MONTH a spiff lands in — the commission sheet stamps it on the activation month, the cash rows on
the month it was paid. April 2026 therefore **falls** about $35k while August rises about $57k. Both are
coherent; only one is this tenant's declaration.

Every one of the seven store columns gains airtime money it could not previously hold — e.g. 64 Graham
Ave in August: revenue $8,311.48 → $18,034.26, gross profit $30,327.06 → $40,049.84.

**A month whose gross profit EXCEEDS its revenue is not an error** and the screen now says so: with
`rebate_presentation = contra_cogs` (the house ruling, unchanged) a device purchase rebate books negative
inside cost of goods, so in a month whose rebates exceed its handset purchases cost of goods is negative.
August is such a month (gross profit $113,729.89 on revenue $103,543.54).

### COMMCALC-03.22b WHOSE RULES BOOKED THIS, ON THE SCREEN

`prospect_eval.rule_basis` is the one home for the question, and it reports **three bases, not two**,
because a loader reports which COLUMNS the table has and never whether this org's row carried a value:

- `declared` — the resolved value DIFFERS from the house answer, so somebody set it;
- `house_default` — it equals the house answer, which this org may have chosen or may never have set,
  and those two are genuinely indistinguishable from here (said in those words, not glossed);
- `column_absent` — the table has no such column yet, so the house answer is the only possible one until
  the named migration runs.

Each switch carries what it MOVES in the tenant's own words, because a switch name tells a reader
nothing. `residual_subs.MA_PNL_CONFIG_COLUMNS` was named in this PR so the mig-309 half of the column
list has a home too, and `rule_basis` reports `unknown_columns` — a column it names that the loaders do
not — so a renamed column can never read as "set" forever.

### COMMCALC-03.22c GROSS PROFIT ON THE STORE TABLE

The store-by-store table gains a **Gross profit** column, read from that store's own statement
(`totals.gross_profit`) — the same figure the P&L matrix row shows, never a subtraction done in the
browser. The accessory requirement has always come off `net_income`, which IS gross profit less our
average expenses (§COMMCALC-03.8), so nothing about the target's arithmetic changes; the column is what
makes the basis visible, which is what the owner asked for.

**PROOF** `harness_prospect_eval.py` — **268 passed / 0 failed** (§T1–T12). §T1 fails against the
pre-fix wiring by construction (it requires the loaded config on the booking keys and forbids a default
there), §T8/§T9 are armed on a live-shaped spiff row — the same row books one leg or two depending on the
spiff source, and lands on account `169335` or company-wide depending on store attribution — §T5 proves
nothing is claimed as declared when it equals the house answer, §T7 that an absent column names its
migration instead of reading as a choice, §T11 that the screen reads gross profit off the statement.

Same class: §66 (a value read without its basis), §19.18 (a registry written and its callers left
unwired), §58 (one home for what a carrier dollar IS).


### COMMCALC-03.23 ACTIVATIONS PER MONTH — counted by the PLATFORM'S classifier, not a second tally (owner ask 2026-10-14)

Owner, verbatim: *"the activations per month details is also missing which breaks up teh new acts
upgrade tablet fios etc"* and *"the filter for each month is missing from each report"*.

**The duplicate check came first and changed the design.** §6f/§19.31 already own "what kind of
activation is this line" — `commcalc/line_class.py`, whose classes are exactly the owner's words
(`activation` / `port` / `byod` / `upgrade`), with an add-a-line as a MODIFIER on one rather than a
fifth class, and `new_activation_units` as the ONE derivation of the count the Sales report,
Executive MTD, the Boost pay engine and the DLAR reconciliation all print. A private New/Add tally in
the prospect report would have been a second answer to that question. **Reused:**
`line_class.activation_units` / `new_activation_units` / `add_a_line_units` / `is_add_a_line` /
`ACTIVATION_TYPE_CLASSES` / `CLASS_LABELS`, `product_mix.product_breakup` (via §COMMCALC-03.21's
`products_sold`), `prospect_eval._row_period`. **Created:** `rows_by_period`, `activations_by_month`,
`products_by_month`, `house_activation_declaration` / `activation_rules`, migration 1082. No new
endpoint and no new table.

**What that cost, measured before deciding.** The house classifier reads `contract_type`, which a
takeover pack does not have, so on the live upload it placed **0 of 5,495 rows** — every class would
have read zero, which is the fake answer this report must never give. The feed carries the fact in
two narrow columns whose values are exact rather than prose: `activation_type` (New 3,907 · Add 1,588)
and `activation_type2` (branded 5,083 · byop 383 · blank 29). So the vocabulary is **declared** for
those two columns (fields + tokens as config, RULE TWO) and the declaration was measured against every
row before it shipped:

| | lines |
|---|---|
| activation | 5,112 |
| bring-your-own | 383 |
| **total** | **5,495** — the file exactly |
| of which add-a-lines | 1,588 |
| unplaced | **0** |
| excluded | 0 |

`'add'` is declared as the add-a-line **MODIFIER** and not as a class on purpose: 166 `Add` lines are
also `byop`, and as a class it would have mis-called every one of them.

**Upgrade and port read zero, and say so.** This feed records neither, so `classes_absent` names them
and the card states in words that the file carries nothing to count — never a count of zero sales.
Same refusal as §COMMCALC-03.21's product classes.

**Per month, live 2026-10-14** (months sum to the total on lines, new activations and add-a-lines —
asserted by §U3):

| month | lines | new activations | add-a-lines | bring-your-own | phone / tablet / home internet |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| March 2026 | 39 | 39 | 2 | 2 | 34 / 3 / 0 |
| April 2026 | 866 | 866 | 44 | 37 | 754 / 57 / 10 |
| May 2026 | 1,066 | 1,066 | 61 | 41 | 946 / 57 / 16 |

**The copy that was deleted.** `flag_multi_line_accounts` carried
