### COMMCALC-03.23a THE MONTH FILTER COMES FROM THE SHARED SHELL

Owner: *"the filter for each month is missing from each report"*. The page already had ONE month
control at the top driving the server query (§COMMCALC-03.20); what was missing was a month control on
each sub-report, so one month could be read without moving the whole page.

**`ReportShell` already turns any month-roled column into a By-month dropdown.** So the fix is a
`role: 'month'` column on each per-month table rather than a selector typed onto the page: the control
is the same on every report on the platform, and no page owns a copy of it. The activations table and
the products table (now every month, flattened to one row per month and class) carry it.

### COMMCALC-03.23b THE NOTICE BAR AND THE COLUMN LEGEND — `ReportShell`, for every report

Owner: *"also give me notification bar ont eh top of each report"*, and of the flagged-account table
*"expain on teh report what each filter signifies"* / *"explain each coloumn"*.

Both live in `components/ReportShell.tsx`, not on the page that asked:

- **`notice` / `noticeTone`** — ONE bar above every `ReportShell`, rendered before the toolbar so it
  is read before the numbers. Three tones sharing `NarrativeBanner`'s palette, so a warning on a
  report and a warning on a banner do not read as two severities. A report that passes neither renders
  byte-identically to before.
- **`ExportColumn.tip`** is now the ONE home for "what this column means". `ReportShell` prints it as
  the header tooltip AND in an openable **"What each column means"** legend, because a tooltip is
  invisible on a touch screen and to anyone not hunting for it. The explanation rides the COLUMN, so a
  renamed or deleted column takes its explanation with it instead of leaving a paragraph describing
  something that is no longer there — the drift a paragraph typed beside a table always produces.

Every report on the takeover page carries a notice; the flagged-account table answers the owner's own
question on itself (*"do tehy mean there is only ne accoutn for 27 lines"* → one row is ONE carrier
billing account, and `Lines` is how many lines sit on it).

**Proof.** `backend/harness_prospect_eval.py` §U — **286 checks, 0 failed**. §U1 forbids a tally of
prospect_eval's own; **§U2 is ARMED** (the house classifier really does place none of these rows);
§U3 ties the months to the total; §U5 proves `'add'` as a class would mis-call the byop lines; §U6 the
absent classes; §U7 an unknown value reported by name; §U9 `rows_by_period` dereferences the one home
for a row's month; §U11 the deleted comparison; §U12 a declared map replaces the house one whole;

### COMMCALC-03.24 COMPARE IT WITH A STORE WE ALREADY OWN (owner ask 2026-10-14)

Owner, verbatim: *"Add one more column to it with to pick our existing store to compare the sales of
the existing PNL with the new ones we might take over"*.

The store-by-store table gains a **"Compare with our store"** picker per row, and five columns
reading that store's own monthly P&L beside the target's. The pick is per ROW because that is the
question a takeover asks — *this* site looks like *that* site of ours — and nothing is pre-selected: a
comparison nobody asked for would read as a judgement the report never made.

#### The duplicate check (the build gate)

| what it needed | who already answers it | what was done |
|---|---|---|
| "what did this store of OURS earn this month" | `account/statement_filter.store_snapshots` (§19.50's deduped read) + `analysis.pl_totals` (§4) — and §60's spiff-impact prep held that LOOP INLINE | the loop moved to **`statement_filter.store_pl_totals`**, beside the read it is made of, with the store key INJECTED; the spiff endpoint now dereferences it. Two copies deleted to one. |
| "what part of a statement's revenue is these lines" | `analysis._line_amount`, private | made public as `analysis.pl_revenue_lines_total` — never a second walk of a statement payload |
| "which month's figures are these, and when were they computed" | the same read's `computed_at` | returned with the figures, and `computed_at_label` is the one wording both callers show |
| a per-store P&L recompute | `statement_engine.statement(scope="store:…")` | **deliberately NOT used** — it rebuilds every input per call, so one call per picked store would recompute our whole business to fill a column. The STORED snapshot is the figure the Finance hub already published. |

#### WHAT MAKES THE TWO SIDES COMPARABLE — and it is not a classification

A takeover pack carries the target's CARRIER feeds and nothing else: no accessory sale, no bill
payment, no counter revenue of any kind. §COMMCALC-03.7 has always said that out loud, and this is the
first surface where saying it is not enough — our own store's P&L carries all of it, so putting its
whole revenue beside the target's would read as *the target earning a fraction of what our store
earns* when the real difference is which lines each side's data can speak to.

So the comparable figure is **what our store earned on the SAME P&L revenue lines the target's
statement booked**, and the line list comes from the target's own assembled statement
(`prospect_eval.comparable_revenue_lines` — the lines carrying a non-zero amount, in chart order):

- the two statements are assembled by ONE builder off ONE chart (`coa.PL_SPEC`), so a line key means
  the same thing on both sides by construction;
- a pack that one day carries an accessory feed widens the comparison in the same upload — no code
  change, no config row;
- a declared "these lines are carrier money" list would be a second answer to a question the chart
  and §58 already answer, and the obvious candidate for it (`ma_store_pnl.GP_INCOME_COLUMNS`) files an
  UNRECOGNISED revenue line into the carrier `unmapped` column — so asking it "is this carrier money?"
  answers **yes for every counter line in the chart**. A last-resort placement read as evidence is
  §66's defect exactly, and `harness_prospect_eval.py` §V2 is ARMED on it.

The whole revenue sits in its own column beside the comparable one, with the reason on the notice bar:
*read a gap there as the counter business this pack cannot show, never as the target earning less*.

#### MEASURED on live data, September 2026

The prospect `empire` (org `854f6d7b`), 7 store columns, against the 20 of our stores that have a
stored September P&L (computed 2026-10-14 14:18 UTC):

| | |
|---|---|
| lines the pack booked | 7 — carrier commissions & incentives, MI residual, merchant discount, device margin, fee income, consumer financing, MDF |
| target revenue, all stores | $78,094.72 |
| our stores, comparable revenue | $4,190.40 – $11,138.86 |
| our stores, WHOLE revenue | $5,784.47 – $15,020.98 |
| our stores, net income | mostly NEGATIVE (−$7,696.25 … +$1,091.09) |

The last row is the comparison's whole point and it is honest arithmetic, not a defect: our store's
bottom line carries its OWN real expenses, while a target store column carries one of our stores'
AVERAGE monthly expense (§COMMCALC-03.19). The two bottom lines are therefore the closest thing this
data can give to *"could that site stand on its own"*.

#### The traps the columns are shaped around

- **Every comparison column declares `agg: 'none'`.** They are figures about OUR stores and the same
  store can be picked on two rows — a summed total row would show a figure our business never earned
  (`report-totals` sums a money column unless the column says otherwise, §COMMCALC-03.20).
- **A store with no stored P&L for the month is ABSENT from the pick list**, never a $0.00 row, and the
  notice says the month was never computed. Absence is never a finding — and this is the one surface
  where a zero would read as a judgement about our own business.
- **`revenue_on_lines` is `None`, not 0.00, when no lines were asked for**: "not asked" is not "$0".
- **A scope key that resolves to nothing is skipped**, never filed under `""`, which would collide
  every unresolved store into one row.
- **The picker is display-only.** The column's `get` returns our store's NAME, so an export carries the
  comparison that was on screen; the `<select>` is the `render`.

#### Where it is

| | |
|---|---|
| one home, our side | `account/statement_filter.store_pl_totals` (+ `analysis.pl_revenue_lines_total`) |
| one home, the comparison | `commcalc/prospect_eval.comparable_revenue_lines` / `peer_store_options` (PURE) |
| endpoint | `GET /commcalc/prospects/{id}/evaluation` → `our_stores` |
| screen | `commcalc/store-takeover` → `comparisonCols()` on the store-by-store table |
| callers of the shared read | this, and §60's spiff impact (its inline copy deleted) |

**Proof.** `backend/harness_prospect_eval.py` — **301 passed / 0 failed**, §V1–V15. §V2 is armed on the
classification that was rejected; §V3 proves the comparable figure is not the whole revenue; §V4/§V5
that an uncomputed month and an empty pack REPORT rather than compare; §V8 that the second copy of the
per-store P&L loop is gone (and `harness_spiff_impact.py` §I7 now locks the home rather than the old
spelling); §V14 the `agg: 'none'` trap; §V15 that nothing is compared until a human picks it.

Same class: §19.18 (a registry written and its callers left unwired), §66 (a value read without its
basis), §COMMCALC-03.7 (what this evaluation cannot answer, said out loud).


### COMMCALC-03.25 THE FIRST SCREEN TELLS YOU WHAT TO DO (owner report 2026-10-14)

Owner, verbatim: *"the main screen does nto tell you what to do it just sits tehre and it pops up teh
dat aautoamatically also it does not let you pick fromt eh drop down what we have evelauterd so far"*.

**ONE CAUSE, BOTH COMPLAINTS.** `loadList` selected `prospects[0]` on load. That did two things at
once: it fetched a whole evaluation nobody asked for ("it pops up the data automatically"), and
because `pid` was never empty the `{!pid && …}` panel — the only thing on the page that says what to
do — **could never render**. The dropdown did list every evaluation, but you were never looking at the
dropdown, and a name in a `<select>` does not tell you whether that evaluation has anything in it.

#### The class: instructions that live in help text are not instructions

Both of this page's intro paragraphs carry `className="pg-note"`, and `globals.css` holds

```css
.pg-note { display: none !important; }
html[data-help="on"] .pg-note { display: revert !important; }
```

so they are **hidden unless an approved role has help switched on**. That gate is deliberate and
stays (the app reads as a finished product by default, §3h). What does not stay is a page whose
*only* account of what to do sits behind it: with help off, this page was a title, a dropdown and
nothing else. **Guidance a reader needs in order to USE a page is the page, not its help.**
`harness_prospect_eval.py` §W2 is ARMED on it — the start panel may not carry `pg-note`, and the page
may not grow a third one.

#### What the first screen is now

| | |
|---|---|
| **Start here — three steps** | pick one below or name a new one · upload its carrier reports (**named from the feed registry**, never a count typed into the copy) · type its actual rent, then read the P&L and compare it with one of your own stores |
| **What you have evaluated so far** | one row per evaluation through `ReportShell`: months uploaded, latest month, rows uploaded, which reports landed, **what is still to upload**, status, and an **Open** button |
| **No evaluations at all** | says so, and says how to start the first one — never an empty table |

- **ONE WAY IN.** The row button and the dropdown both call `openProspect`, so the two cannot drift
  (§W5 counts the state-setting once).
- **"Still to upload" is DERIVED** from the registry (`keys.filter(k => !present.has(k))`), never a
  literal list of feed names: a feed the registry does not name is a gap in the registry, not in
  somebody's upload (§W6).
- **The row counts are what LANDED** — the list endpoint's own per-period feed counts — not what an
  uploaded file claimed about itself (§W7, the §COMMCALC-03.10 rule applied to the list).
- **An evaluation with nothing in it reads as empty**, with "nothing yet" in Reports in and a notice
  saying an evaluation with no commission report has no P&L yet (§W8). Never $0.00.
- Every column carries its own `tip` through the §COMMCALC-03.23b one home, because the point of the
  table is to be read BEFORE anything is opened.

**A derived list must be memoised or the table re-mounts.** `list?.prospects || []` is a new array
identity on every render, so the column and row memos rebuilt every time and the table re-mounted
under the pointer. Both derivations are `useMemo` now; eslint had flagged exactly this.

**Proof.** `backend/harness_prospect_eval.py` — **309 passed / 0 failed**, §W1–W8. Frontend
`tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on the page, with the two warnings the memo fix removed.

Same class: §COMMCALC-03.7 (what the evaluation cannot answer, said out loud), §COMMCALC-03.10 (a row
count is not a measure of what a file answered), §19.36 (the one home for a setup notice).


### COMMCALC-03.26 WHAT THE SELLER DECLARES: ACCESSORY SALES AND THIS SITE'S RENT (owner ask 2026-10-14)

**Migration:** `1083_prospect_store_declared_input.sql` (one new table, `commcalc.prospect_store_input`;
moves no money). **Endpoint:** `PUT /commcalc/prospects/{id}/store-inputs`.

Owner, verbatim: *"add a line for accessories sales asa declared by seller to include in gorss profit
and then calculate the net income, the cell sould be able to fill in manually and include the rent cell
also for each store, if the rent is declared then the suystem will automaticalluy subtract our avg rent
from the expenses if the rent is nto declared then it will keep our average as a part of the expense or
the bettwe rway is to create a cell with ouer rent and if it is diff then it can vbe user overwritten"*
— two designs named for the rent, and he chose the second, so **the rent cell opens on OUR OWN average
and typing over it replaces that average for that store alone**.

| question | one home |
|---|---|
| what has the seller declared for this store | `commcalc/prospect_eval.store_declared_inputs` |
| what does a declared accessory sale book | `commcalc/prospect_eval.declared_accessory_bookings` |
| what do the two cells print beside themselves | `commcalc/prospect_eval.declared_meta` |
| what does an entered rent replace | `commcalc/prospect_eval.apply_rent_override` (§COMMCALC-03.6, unchanged) |
| what does accessory revenue cost | `account/coa._account_config['accessory_cogs_pct']` (mig 611) |

**THE DUPLICATE CHECK CHANGED THE DESIGN TWICE, and that is the whole value of this section.**

1. **The rent substitution already existed** and was NOT rewritten. `apply_rent_override` has replaced
   an averaged rent with an entered one since §COMMCALC-03.6, splits it across several declared rent
   lines and reports the average it displaced. The per-store cell is that same function, applied
   **ONCE PER COLUMN** off the averaged matrix. `evaluate` now owns that application (`_exp_for`) and
   the router no longer overrides the rent before calling it.
   **NEVER CHAIN IT.** A second override over an already-overridden matrix records the FIRST override
   as `replaced_average`, and the screen then tells the reader our own stores pay the prospect's rent.
   §X5 is the CONTROL that proves the chained form misreports (9,000 instead of 4,200) and §X6 holds
   that exactly two `apply_rent_override(` spellings exist in the module: the definition and one call.
2. **The accessory cost rate was not invented.** `coa.PL_SPEC` has carried `accessory_rev` and
   `accessory_cost` all along, and `account_config.accessory_cogs_pct` (mig 611) is the rate **the
   owner himself set to 20% on 2026-06-20**. A declared sale books its cost at the ORG'S rate, read
   through that one home and injected into the pure function. Booking the declaration as revenue with
   no cost would have shown a gross profit the store has never earned; a second rate here would have
   been the divergence the index rules forbid. §X2 fails the build if a literal rate appears.

**THE VOCABULARY ALREADY NAMED THE HOLE.** Both lines were already listed in
`prospect_eval.NEEDS_POS_FEED` — the map of P&L lines that need a point-of-sale feed a store we do not
operate will never give us. The seller's declaration is the only measurement of that hole that exists,
so it is **stored as a declaration and rendered as one** (§X4).

**NULL IS NOT ZERO, and the two are kept apart end to end.** A cleared cell means the seller has
declared nothing: the column charges our average rent and books no accessory line. A declared `0.00`
is a CLAIM — this site pays no rent, or this counter sells nothing — and is charged as one. The screen
sends `null` for a blank and never `0` (§X19), `store_declared_inputs` keeps `None` as `None` (§X1),
and `rent_declared` needs BOTH an entered figure and an applied override, so a column that declared
nothing cannot inherit the whole-prospect override's `applied` and claim a declaration (§X7).

**WHAT ADDS ACROSS THE COLUMNS, unchanged from §COMMCALC-03.19.** A declared accessory sale is the
store's own money, so it sums to the whole-prospect column and **revenue still ties** (§X25). Rent is
an expense, and every column already carries one whole store's expense on purpose, so a per-store rent
moves that column alone (§X23). A declaration keyed to a store the uploads do not name is **reported by
name** rather than added to a total nobody can drill into (§X26), and a store with no declaration is
named too, so an empty cell reads as an invitation (§X27).

**MEASURED END TO END** (`harness_prospect_eval.py` §X21–X28, DB-free): a declared $5,000 at 20% moves
revenue +$5,000, cost of goods +$1,000, gross profit +$4,000 and the bottom line +$4,000, and drops the
accessory break-even target by exactly that $4,000 — through the statement's own arithmetic, never an
adjustment. With no declarations the evaluation is byte-identical to what it was before this ask (§X28).

### COMMCALC-03.27 FIRST MONTH AND M2–M12, NAMED (owner report 2026-10-14)

Owner, verbatim: *"also i cant see the m2-m12 commision line"*. No migration, no new column.

| question | one home |
|---|---|
| what did the commission sheet say was EARNED, by month-of-life | `account/ma_store_pnl.ma_earned_month_ladder` |
| what did the cash rows say was RECEIVED, by month-of-life | `account/ma_store_pnl.ma_received_month_ladder` |
| which rung is the first month and which is trailing | `commcalc/commission_legs.bucket_for_leg` |
| what are the two buckets CALLED | `commcalc/commission_ledger.LEG_LABELS` |
| in what order do the rungs read | `commcalc/commission_legs.ladder_sort_key` |
| the prospect's view of all five | `commcalc/prospect_eval.commission_leg_ladder` |

**The money was never missing.** It sat inside one `carrier_comm` line with the legs only in that
line's drill-down detail, so nothing on the report named them. **Measured on the live prospect's
September 2026: $39,704.49 of month-spiff cash, of which $38,451.50 — 97% — is M2–M6.**

**WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE ON THE PLATFORM.** M2–M12 is commission owed on lines
that were **already sold before the takeover**. It keeps arriving for a while after the keys change
hands and then stops, so it is not recurring revenue, and a price built on the commission total
overpays for it. The card and the per-store column both say so in those words.

**NOTHING IS DERIVED HERE.** `commission_leg_ladder` is handed the two ladder payloads and the three
vocabulary answers; it parses no label, slices no `M`-prefix off a detail string and calls neither
month parser (§X15 fails the build on `re.search`, `startswith("M")`, `[1:].isdigit()`,
`month_leg_of` or `parse_payment_month` appearing in it). A rung the feed does not carry is not
invented — there is no `range(1, 13)` and no max-month config (§X12).

**BOTH BASES ARE ALWAYS REPORTED, and an absent one says so.** The sheet answers what was earned in
the activation month; the cash rows answer what landed. For a takeover those are different questions
(what the book is worth against what is arriving now), so neither is folded into the other, and a
basis with no rows reads as **not measured** rather than as a measured zero (§X14). A commission sheet
that states no month-of-life keeps the rung **Unlabelled** and is never read as a first month (§X13) —
reading a trailing book as fresh is precisely the error that would overprice a deal.

### COMMCALC-03.28 THE MONTH-OVER-MONTH P&L, AND THE EXPENSE THAT WAS NOT THERE (owner, 2026-10-16)

Two asks on the same screen, one of them a defect. **Carrier-neutral and platform-wide**: the owner
said so explicitly at 14:49 — *"this stays a platofrm wide chaneg / report not a patch for any one
carrier, this evaluation is specilfially for total"* — so nothing below names a carrier, and the
commission the evaluation books is the prospect's OWN uploaded sheets and nothing else.

**Endpoint:** `GET /commcalc/prospects/{id}/pl-trend?period=&period_to=&mode=`
**Lock:** `backend/harness_prospect_pl_trend.py` (the endpoint, over a fake client) +
`harness_prospect_eval.py` §Y/§Z (the pure rules). **No migration, no new table, no new column.**

#### The duplicate check (the build gate), and what it changed

| candidate | verdict |
|---|---|
| the per-store P&L matrix (§COMMCALC-03.18) | **REUSED whole.** The trend is `prospect_eval.evaluate` + `router._prospect_assemble` called once per month — the same booking path and the same assembler. §Z of the lock requires a column and that month's own report to agree on **every line, both totals and the activation count**, which is what makes this a shape and not a sibling derivation |
| `GET /commcalc/commission-leg-store-trend` (§COMMCALC-12) | not this — it answers a COMMISSION question for stores we OWN, off live tables, and knows nothing of a prospect's uploads or of a P&L |
| the per-month tables this report already carries (§COMMCALC-03.20/.23) | counts of accounts, activations and products. None of them is a statement |
| the shared filter bar's period value (RULE FIVE, §3d) | **REUSED.** "A month OR a date range" is already one value (`period` + `periodTo`), so the window takes the same two strings rather than inventing a vocabulary |

**Three one-homes came out of it, and each has a build-failing lock:**

| the fact | the one home | who dereferences it |
|---|---|---|
| which of a prospect's rows belong to a month | `prospect_eval.feeds_for_months`, over the registry's own `period_scope` | the month report AND the trend (§Y6) |
| has this month ended | `prospect_eval.month_has_ended` | `default_period` (which month to open on, §COMMCALC-03.17) AND `expense_window` (which month may be averaged) — §Y7 fails the build on a second copy |
| which of OUR months the expense benchmark is taken over | `prospect_eval.expense_window` | `router._prospect_expense_window`, its only caller (§Z8) |
| assembling a prospect statement | `router._prospect_assemble` | both endpoints; §Z23 holds that exactly one `_eng._assemble(` exists in the router's prospect section |

The month slice **replaced two hand-written copies**: `if feed != "ma_marketplace_orders" and
stamped not in wanted` spelled a feed key in code (RULE TWO) and compared period TEXT against a
variant list. Both spellings of a month now collapse through `period_sort_key`, the module's single
period parser, so a file stamped `2026-04` and one stamped `April 2026` select the same rows — and
`_period_keys_for_prospect` is gone rather than left as a second answer (the `period_stored_spelling`
module-graph fact lost its `_ap` binding in the same change).

#### ASK 2, THE DEFECT: "expenses only appear in the Sept statement… there are no expenses showing up for any store"

**He was right, and no data was missing.** Measured live on 2026-10-16, read-only over the REST API:

| | what the live rows say |
|---|---|
| this organisation's own `commcalc.store_expenses` | **two months only** — July 2026 (304 rows, $225,080.58) and August 2026 (288 rows, $276,162.69). Nothing earlier was ever entered |
| the prospect's own uploads | **eight months**, March to October 2026 (`empire`: 5,495 commission rows, 65,491 handset-order rows, 137,374 rows in all) |
| the window the evaluation used | `complete_months(...)` — the months **strictly before** the evaluated one |

So the window resolved to `[August, July]` for September and October, `[July]` for August, and
**`[]` for July, June, May, April and March** — which is exactly the one month he could find an
expense in and the five he could not. The HOUSE org has March–September, which is why this never
showed up on the house platform: it is a per-ORGANISATION fact, and the fix had to be one too.

**THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE.** The general fact that was wrong is not "April has no expenses". It
is that **our own average store cost was treated as a time series read backwards from the evaluated
month, when §COMMCALC-03.6 defines it as a BENCHMARK** — "the full average monthly expense of one of
our own stores". A benchmark has no month of its own: the question is *what does a store of ours cost
to run*, and the best available measurement is the months we actually recorded, whichever side of the
evaluated month they fall on. A backward-only window answers for recent months and silently answers
**nothing** for every month before a tenant's first expense sheet — for every tenant, every prospect
and every month, not just this one.

`expense_window(periods, period, want, today)` is the fix, and it has four halves:

1. **Prior months still lead, unchanged.** Where enough complete months sit before the evaluated one
   the window is **byte-identical** to what it was — §Z2 asserts that against `complete_months`
   itself for three window sizes, so this adds a fallback and changes no existing answer.
2. **A shortfall is filled from the NEAREST months after it**, nearest first, and only months that
   have ENDED (`month_has_ended`, dereferenced — a part-month's sheet drags every line down by
   however much of the month is left, which is why prior months had to be complete too).
3. **The direction is reported, never implied.** `direction` (`before`/`after`/`both`/`none`) and a
   one-sentence `basis` ride on the payload and the screen prints them: *"we had entered no expenses
   before April 2026, so the NEAREST months we did record are the benchmark; they fall AFTER the
   month on screen"*.
4. **An unmeasured expense side SAYS SO instead of booking zero.** `measured: false` with a reason,
   because a zero expense line makes every takeover look profitable — the dangerous half of this
   defect, and the half that had no symptom.

**ARMED NEGATIVE CONTROLS, at both levels.** §Z1a asserts the pre-fix window is the empty one from
April. `harness_prospect_pl_trend.py` §A7–A9 reinstates the old rule inside the ENDPOINT and asserts
it reproduces the defect: every month `measured: false`, every store a flat `0.00` expense, and every
column's bottom line **overstated by a whole store's running cost**. A regression to the old rule
cannot pass.

**Nothing was "fixed" by hiding a data gap.** Where a tenant has entered no expenses at all the
report still says NOT MEASURED, in red, and names what to enter.

**THE SIBLING, FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT "FIXED".** The other reader of this organisation's expense
sheet is the live P&L / GP report, through `expenses_effective.effective_expense_rows` (§19.50) —
and it has the same SHAPE of hole: its carry-forward rule carries the latest **strictly prior**
month forward, so for this organisation April 2026 books **$0.00 of store opex** on the live P&L too.
It is **excused, not fixed, and the reason is the whole distinction this section turns on:**

| | what the figure means | what an absent month should read as |
|---|---|---|
| the takeover evaluation | our average store cost used as a **benchmark** — §COMMCALC-03.6, a yardstick with no month of its own | the nearest months we recorded, labelled |
| the live P&L / GP report | **what this company actually spent in that month** | nothing entered — and saying so |

Carrying August's actuals **backwards** into April on a real statement would invent a booking in the
company's own books, which is exactly the patchwork the house rules forbid. So the live P&L keeps its
forward-only carry, and the April gap there is a **DATA defect to report** (nobody has entered
January–February 2026 or any month before March for the house org, and nothing before July 2026 for
this one), never a code change. `expenses_effective` is untouched by this PR and still supplies every
month's rows to both readers, which is what keeps the benchmark and the statement over the same
figures.

#### ASK 1: the month-over-month P&L, with the statement for a month or a range on the right

Owner, verbatim: *"i also need to see the month over omont h p&l for each store in the same report
with a filter which gives the p&l on the righ tside for a particuklar monmth selected or a data range
selected"*.

- **The grid** is one row per (store, P&L line) and **one column per month**, grouped by store with
  **All stores** first as the row the others are checked against. The line vocabulary and the labels
  are the server's own statement's (`coa.PL_LABEL` through `lineLabelOf`) — the screen names no line.
  Through `ReportShell`, so it sorts, filters and exports like every other table.
- **The panel on the right** is the selected month, or the selected date range, **booked ONCE over
  all of its rows** — never the monthly columns added together. §Z29 and §C3 prove the window's
  revenue and device cost equal the columns added up to the cent, which is the check that it is the
  same rows through the same path.
- **A range charges as many months of running cost as it carries of revenue.** Our average is a
  MONTHLY figure, so `expense_bookings(matrix, route, months=N)` charges it once per month in the
  window — after the rent override, so a seller's declared monthly rent is charged for the same N
  months. `months=1` is the default and every existing caller is byte-identical (§Z9). The sentence
  saying so is `prospect_eval.range_basis`, carried on the payload and printed under the figures.
- **A range covers the WHOLE months its two ends fall in**, even when the dates sit mid-month: a P&L
  cannot be cut at the 14th, and dropping a half-covered month would understate the window (§Z17).
  An empty filter does not narrow — it is every month, not none (§Z18).
- **The grid's columns are never narrowed by that filter.** A trend you can filter down to one column
  is not a trend (§Z31), and the screen says so rather than leaving it to be noticed.
- **The Stores filter narrows which stores appear**, through the page's existing `storeFilter` one
  home, and the All-stores row is kept whatever it says.

**ITS OWN REQUEST, off the first screen's critical path.** It costs one `evaluate` per month, so
hanging it on `/evaluation` would make the month report wait for work nobody has asked for yet — the
same reasoning that took the row tally off the list's critical path. Within the endpoint, the
prospect's rows and our expense sheet are each read **once** (§Z26) and ONE handset price list serves
every month (§Z27, injected through `evaluate(price_list=…)`, which §Z28 proves changes no figure).

**Where it is:** `/commcalc/store-takeover`, a new card between the per-store P&L matrix and the
store-by-store table — the grid on the left, the month-or-range statement on the right, with the two
date boxes beside the panel they govern (empty = follow the page's **Month** filter).

---

## §COMMCALC-04. WHETHER A ROW IS FILED UNDER A MONTH IS A FACT ABOUT THE TABLE (owner report 2026-10-12)

Owner, relaying a tenant's user: *"user cannot upload the handset ordering report, fix it from back
end"*. The upload card showed **"This feature isn't switched on for your company yet. Contact
support to enable it."** It was switched on. Nothing was ever licensed off.

### §COMMCALC-04.1 The defect, stated once

Every upload of **MA - Marketplace Handset Fulfillment Orders** has been refused since
**2026-10-06**. `commcalc.upload_trace` carries each attempt, same error every time:

```
500: Insert failed: {'message': "Could not find the 'period' column of 'raw_ma_fulfillment'
in the schema cache", 'code': 'PGRST204'} — the existing 0 row(s) were left untouched.
```

Six refused attempts on one tenant (2026-10-06 ×4, 2026-10-08, 2026-10-12), 0 rows saved each time.
The last upload that landed was **2026-10-02** — the day before §19.46 shipped.

Two things made it read as a licensing problem rather than a broken write. The API boundary (§19.36)
rewrites a schema-cache error into the one customer sentence, correctly — a customer must not be
shown a column name. And the tile's own "newer attempt saved no rows" line was true. So the screen
said *not switched on* and *saved nothing*, and neither sentence pointed at the actual cause.

### §COMMCALC-04.2 The cause: §19.46 generalised one table too far

§19.46 (`feed_period.day_stamp`) re-stamps `period` / `period_month` / `period_year` on every
DAY-KEYED feed's rows from the row's own date — the fix that stopped a rolling re-pull filing one
month's commission under the next. `raw_ma_fulfillment` **is** day keyed (`date_ordered`), and is
the one landing table on that path that stores **no month columns at all**: its upload mapper has
always skipped them, and the portal-pull spec says `has_period: false`. The stamp wrote a column the
table does not have, and PostgREST refused the whole insert.

### §COMMCALC-04.3 The class, not the instance

The general fact that was wrong is not "one feed lost its uploads". It is **"a feed row's month can
always be written to period columns"**. Whether a landing table STORES a row's month is a schema
fact that had **no home**, so each write path answered it for itself:

| Path | How it used to answer | Now |
|---|---|---|
| manual upload / email sweep (`router._upload_file_impl`) | `has_period = file_type not in ['catalog', 'master_cats']` — a hand-written file-type list | `has_period = _lineage.stores_row_month(table)` |
| portal sweep (`epay_sweep`) | a `period` stamped into every mapped row's base, unconditionally | `_month_base(spec, …)` — only the columns that table stores |
| portal pull (`report_pull.apply_column_map`) | a `has_period` flag carried per report spec | `_lin.stores_row_month(target_table)` |

That is §19.18's shape again: the stamp reached the feeds somebody remembered to exclude. The fact
now lives next to the day-grain fact it travels with —
`data_lineage_registry.month_columns(table)` / `stores_row_month(table)`, with
`NO_MONTH_COLUMN_REASONS` carrying a sentence per exception — and all three paths dereference it.

**"Replaced whole" is a different fact from "stores no month", and reading one as the other would be
worse than the bug.** The upload handler's snapshot branch used to fire on `not has_period`; a
day-keyed feed that stores no month columns now also answers False there, and that branch DELETES
the org's entire table. It reads `_lineage.is_snapshot(table)` instead.

### §COMMCALC-04.4 The siblings, found by the lock rather than by hand

`harness_feed_day_grain.py` §M re-measures **every** declaration against the `CREATE TABLE` /
`ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` statements in `database/migrations/`, so a drifting declaration fails the
build. Writing it immediately named four more tables carrying the same wrong default, each confirmed
against the live schema: `raw_epay_daily_tx`, `merchant_settlement_day`, `merchant_settlement_batch`,
`asset_ledger`. None is reached by the manual-upload handler today — which is exactly the silence
`raw_ma_fulfillment` kept until the stamp was generalised to it.

### §COMMCALC-04.5 What was checked for duplication before building

- `data_lineage_registry.DATA_DATE_COLUMN_BY_TABLE` / `day_keyed_date_columns()` (§19.46) already
  answer "which column is this row's day". The month-column fact is **added beside it**, in the same
  registry, not in a new module.
- `router._table_has_column` asks the live schema per call; it was deliberately not used here — a
  per-request schema probe on an ingest path answers the same question slower and without a build
  gate, and the registry is checkable offline against the migrations.
- `feed_period` stays pure: it is GIVEN the columns, it does not look them up.

### §COMMCALC-04.6 Files, locks and what is NOT in this change

| Thing | Where |
|---|---|
| the fact | `commcalc/data_lineage_registry.py` — `MONTH_COLUMNS`, `NO_MONTH_COLUMN_REASONS`, `month_columns()`, `stores_row_month()`, `SNAPSHOT_TABLES`, `is_snapshot()` |
| the stamp | `commcalc/feed_period.py::day_stamp(rows, column, month_columns=MONTH_COLUMNS)` — default unchanged, so an un-updated caller behaves exactly as before |
| the three callers | `commcalc/router.py::_upload_file_impl`, `commcalc/epay_sweep.py`, `commcalc/report_pull.py` |
| the lock | `harness_feed_day_grain.py` §M (M1 re-measures the registry against the migrations; M6/M7 fail the build if any caller keeps its own answer again) |
| module graph | fact `feed_lineage` (§50) gains `report_pull.py` as a caller |

**No migration.** `raw_ma_fulfillment` is correct as it stands: the order date IS its month fact, and
adding period columns would create the second copy this house rule forbids. **No data repair:** every
refused upload left the table untouched, so nothing is wrong in storage — the tenant re-uploads the
file once this ships.

- Same class: §19.46 (the row-date stamp this corrects), §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers
  left unwired), §19.36 (the boundary that made a broken write read as an unlicensed feature).


## §COMMCALC-05. SEVERAL HANDSETS TO ONE BUYER IN ONE DAY — the live feed, counted across the receipts the sale was split over (owner ask 2026-10-12)

Owner: *"add the famimly check to the regular activations also under the flags tile"*, then, deciding
the feed himself: *"this wooulkd check the flags for ongoing actyivation not the test data uploaded
for evauluation"* and *"good point , it should be daily sales feed"*.

**One home:** `backend/app/modules/commcalc/multi_handset_day.py` (pure, DB-free).
**Lock:** `backend/harness_multi_handset_day.py`. **Flag type:** `MULTI_HANDSET_ONE_BUYER`, area
`fraud`, severity HIGH, grain `store_day`, registered in `flag_registry.TYPES`.

### COMMCALC-05.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

| Already answers something near it | Why it is not this | What this reuses |
|---|---|---|
| `DUPLICATE_IMEI` (§53, fraud) | ONE device on SEVERAL lines — the inverse shape | nothing to share |
| `RSK_ACTIVATIONS` (§53, fraud) | counts RSK-REGISTER activations per rep: about the till and the salesperson, not the buyer | untouched |
| §COMMCALC-03 prospect eval | the SAME question on an UPLOADED statement for a store we do not own | deliberately NOT shared — see .2 |
| `router._sales_cell_agg` box count (§3, mig 218) | counts boxes per cell, not per buyer | **the `box_departments` membership test, injected** |
| `flag_registry` (§53) | — | severity, area, label, threshold, on/off switch |

New here and nowhere else: grouping handset lines by **(store, day, buyer) ACROSS receipts**, and the
receipt breakdown inside a case.

### COMMCALC-05.2 Why this and §COMMCALC-03 are two detectors and must stay two

They ask one question of two feeds that cannot answer for each other. §COMMCALC-03 reads
`prospect_feed_row` — an uploaded carrier statement for a store nobody owns yet — keys on the
carrier's own account column, and answers weeks late from money already paid. This reads the live
`commcalc.daily_sales_feed` and answers the morning after, while the handsets are still recoverable.
The owner drew this line himself. **Merging them would let a prospect's uploaded rows raise live
operational flags**, which is the one thing §COMMCALC-03's AST lock exists to prevent.

### COMMCALC-05.3 A handset is a BOX-DEPARTMENT line — never a serial number

Measured against production 2026-10-12, the whole feed (151,102 rows):

| Candidate test | Rows | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `serial_1` present | 24,452 | **WRONG.** Plan lines carry a serial: 1,062 `Total MAX 5G Plan $55`, 435 `Total Wireless Home Internet`, the tablet plans. One phone plus two plans counted as three devices. |
| `customer_no` present | 21,188 (26%) | **WRONG as a buyer key.** Absent on 59% of serial-bearing rows, and the rows that carry it are mostly `Other Carr. payments` and `System`. A check keyed on it reports a clean bill of health it has not earned. |
| department ∈ the org's `box_departments` | 9,759 | **RIGHT.** The same membership test the box count uses, so this detector and that store's own box count cannot disagree. |

The set is **injected by the caller**, never read or defaulted inside the module — `harness_multi_handset_day.py` §G
fails the build if that changes. An undeclared set yields no findings **and says so**, rather than
falling back to the house Boost-XP labels and reading as "all clear".

### COMMCALC-05.4 Why it groups ACROSS receipts (the measurement that forced the design)

A per-receipt check was the obvious design and the wrong one. On the same live feed:

- **392** receipts carry more than 2 handsets.
- But **501** buyer-days do, and **191 of those are split across several receipts** — invisible to a
  per-receipt test.
- Worst case: **16 handsets over EIGHT separate receipts**, 3248 W Lawrence Ave, 2026-09-18, every
  line **$0.00**. Also 18 handsets / 3 receipts (2640 Narragansett, 2026-07-02) and 17 handsets /
  4 receipts at $0.00 (4640-A W Diversey Ave, 2026-07-18).
- **129 of the 501 cases are entirely $0.00** — promotional activations in volume to one name.

A threshold a till can evade by ringing a second sale is not a threshold.

### COMMCALC-05.5 The buyer key, and what it deliberately cannot do

`(org, store, day, normalised name)`. The name is folded for case and spacing only. Initials,
nicknames and misspellings are **not** folded — that would invent an identity, and a flag that
accuses the wrong person is worse than one that misses. The live placeholder values the feed actually
carries (`No Customer` on 203 device rows, `walk  in`, `BOOST MOBILE`, `Back Order`) are **not
grouped**: they are counted and reported as unattributable, because fusing hundreds of unrelated
walk-ins into one case is a worse answer than no answer.

Same day and same store is what makes an exact-name match defensible. The cost is stated on screen,
not buried: it cannot see one buyer across different days, different stores, or under a differently
spelled name.

### COMMCALC-05.6 It reports evidence and returns no verdict

Nothing here concludes that fraud happened and no function returns a judgement — `harness_multi_handset_day.py`
§E walks the module's own strings and fails the build if any user-facing sentence calls something
fraud, abuse or a scheme. A family of five buying five phones is a good sale and reads identically in
this feed. So a case carries what a human needs to tell them apart — the handsets and models, the
receipt split and per-receipt counts, the dollars, whether every line was $0.00, the reps, the day —
and the coaching note asks for a check (*"Confirm these were one genuine sale and not split to stay
under a per-sale limit"*), never an accusation.

### COMMCALC-05.7 Where it is

| Thing | Where |
|---|---|
| the rules | `commcalc/multi_handset_day.py` — `handset_rows` / `group_by_buyer_day` / `cases` / `findings` |
| the proof | `harness_multi_handset_day.py` (CI: "Several handsets to one buyer lock") |
| the type, severity, threshold | `commcalc/flag_registry.py` — `TYPES` + `DEFAULT_PARAMS['MULTI_HANDSET_ONE_BUYER']['max_handsets'] = 2` |
| the tenant's override | a `commcalc.watchdog_rule` row (no migration — the table already exists) |
| the board | Flags & Compliance, area `fraud` |
| the caller (the only one) | `commcalc/watchdog_router.py::_run_for_org` — the one sweep, one cron line |
| the live sales read | `commcalc/watchdog_router.py::_read_sales` → `router._open_month_source` (§19.16) |

### COMMCALC-05.8 Which sales table it reads, and the sibling that fix closed

The owner named the feed himself on 2026-10-12: *"good point , it should be daily sales feed"* — the
check must see activations as they happen, not a month-end archive. But `daily_sales_feed` is **not
named** anywhere in the sweep. `router._open_month_source(client, org_id, period)` is the ONE home for
"which sales table answers for this period" (§19.16): the OPEN month reads the daily feed, where the
hourly Sales Transaction Details email lands, a CLOSED month reads the authoritative `raw_sales`, and
each falls back to the other. A literal table name in the sweep would be a second opinion about which
feed is live, and §H15 of the lock fails the build if one appears.

`_read_sales` is that dereference, and it is shared by **every** sales-reading surface in the file —
which is how building this found and fixed a sibling, as the design rule requires:

- **The void sweep** (`_run_for_org`) and **the void register** (`GET /watchdog/voids`) both named
  `raw_sales` literally. On the month in progress — the only month anybody can still act on — that
  archive does not exist yet, so both read **zero lines and reported no voids rather than no data**.
- Every CLOSED month is byte-identical, because the one home returns `raw_sales` first for them. The
  change is that the open month is looked at at all.
- The sales rows are now read **once** per sweep and handed to both detectors, so the two can never
  disagree about what the month contained.

Buyer-name coverage differs between the two tables and is reported, never assumed (measured live
2026-10-12): `daily_sales_feed` carries a `customer` on **151,102 of 151,102** rows, `raw_sales` on
**141,758 of 219,375** (65%). Lines with no buyer, or a placeholder like `No Customer`, are counted as
`unattributable_lines` in the summary rather than dropped silently — a bare empty case list would read
as "all clear" when it can also mean "nobody recorded who bought these".

### COMMCALC-05.9 The `source` string, and the retirement defect it avoids

`flag_persist.sync` RETIRES every open flag in the period that carries one of the caller's `sources`
and that the run did not produce. `router._CALC_FLAG_SOURCES` already claims `'sales'` for the
commission recalculation's own flag pass. The detector's first draft wrote its findings under
`'sales'`, which would have had **the next recalculation of that month silently resolve every one of
them away** — the detector would have looked correct and then emptied itself. It owns
`SOURCE = "multi_handset_watchdog"`, and §H1–H3 of the lock fail the build if that collides with a
source the commission pass retires.

The POS store spelling goes in `store_address`; `flag_store_resolver.stamp_flags` (mig 285) is the one
home that turns it into a `store_code` a district manager's board can filter on. A code guessed in the
detector would be a second store resolver (§64).

### COMMCALC-05.10 The drill-down, and what was sold alongside

Owner, 2026-10-12: *"for all these flagged activations with more than one phone sold we need to have
the drilldown to check who made the sale for how much, if no accessories are sold with the sale and no
activation fee it is definletly leaning towards fraud"*.

| Thing | Where |
|---|---|
| the drill-down | `GET /commcalc/watchdog/multi-handset` — per case: every handset line's rep, amount, device, serial, receipt |
| accessory dollars on the same receipts | `router._is_accessory`, INJECTED |
| set-up / activation fee lines | `router._is_setup_fee` (mig 217 keyword list), INJECTED |

**Why an endpoint and not a column.** `flag_persist._ROW_FIELDS` is the set of columns the findings
table holds and a per-line breakdown is not one of them — the evidence dict is dropped on write by
design. The board keeps the one-line finding a manager scans; the drill-down answers "show me the
lines" from the feed at read time, through the same `_read_sales` one home, so the two cannot disagree
about what the month contained. It applies the district-manager span filter BEFORE counting.

**Both companion predicates are injected, over the SAME `accessory_config` row `box_departments` comes
from.** One declaration therefore answers "is this a handset", "is this an accessory" and "is this a
fee", so the three readings cannot disagree about one line. There are about eight divergent accessory
classifiers in this codebase (see `accessory_definition.py`); picking a different one here would have
made the drill-down disagree with the Sales Report's own accessory dollars. A fee is not counted as an
accessory — the Sales Report's rule, kept so both numbers mean here what they mean everywhere else.

**Not measured is not zero.** With no predicate supplied the signals are `None` and the sentence
asserts nothing about them. Only a real look that found nothing yields `0.0`, which is when the
coaching note changes to *"Nothing was sold alongside these handsets … pull the receipts and the
buyer's ID before the return window closes."* §I4–I6 of the lock fail the build if an unmeasured run
can ever render as "none sold" — otherwise an unconfigured tenant reads as a chain full of fraud.

**THE OWNER'S RULE WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS BUILT, AND HIS CONJUNCTION DOES NOT FIRE.** On live
October 2026, across both tenants with sales (17 flagged cases):

| | house org | the other tenant |
|---|---|---|
| flagged cases | 4 | 13 |
| **no accessory on the sale** | 0 | **2** |
| no set-up/activation fee | 0 | 0 |
| **neither accessory nor fee** | **0** | **0** |

A set-up or activation fee is present on every flagged case — the house org bills one per handset —
so "no activation fee" discriminates nothing on this data, and the AND of the owner's two conditions
would have shown him an empty screen. **Accessory dollars alone are the signal**: they narrow 17 cases
to 2. Both numbers are reported and neither is turned into a verdict; `signal` on each case lists which
of the two is absent, as a filter.

The standout the signal surfaces: **4 promo iPhones at $0.00 each, one receipt, one rep, no
accessories**, on a port-in multi-line promotion. The other of the two reads like a genuine household
bundle (a tablet, a home-internet router and a phone), which is exactly why the detector reports and
does not conclude.

## §COMMCALC-06. AN ACCESSORY ATTACH DECIDES WHICH DECLARED RATE A LINE EARNS (owner directive 2026-10-12)

**Owner, verbatim.** *"Payment for edge on total which is defined as $25 must be accompanied with
atleast $25 worth of accessories , add this logic in the system not as hard coded but as a logic
platform wide which might be used by other carriers also , label the commission as $25 acc is must to
be qualified for $25 commission otherwise the commision falls back to $10 or whatever is paid to
Chicago market"*

**THE CLASS, not the instance.** The missing thing was not Total's edge payout. It was that **every gate
in the plan engine could only turn a payment OFF** — `plan_pay_gate` suppresses (scope, exclusion, unit
dedup, §6f) and `financing_tiers` re-rates from a MONTH's attainment (mig 273). Nothing could say "this
line earns a LESSER declared rate because of a fact about the SALE it belongs to". That is the
mechanism, and it is carrier-agnostic.

**HALF THE ASK ALREADY EXISTED, and was reused rather than rebuilt.** *"or whatever is paid to Chicago
market"* needs nothing new: migration **262** already lets a rule state the market, store or employee it
applies to — it was built from the owner's own 2026-08-01 report (*"All activations are being paid $10
flat, this is only for NY employees, but this empluee is in Chicago"*). A tenant either enters that
market's figure as the fallback, or leaves the fallback NULL and lets that market's own scoped rule pay.

| | |
|---|---|
| one home | `backend/app/modules/commcalc/attach_qualifier.py` — PURE, imports nothing from `app` |
| config | `commcalc.commission_rule` (mig **1079**): `qualifier_min`, `qualifier_measure`, `qualifier_scope`, `qualifier_match_field`, `qualifier_match_op`, `qualifier_match_value`, `qualifier_fallback_amount`, `qualifier_label`. All nullable; a NULL `qualifier_min` is NO condition, so applying 1079 changes nothing |
| wired at | `commission_engine.preview` — context built ONCE from `valid` (the period's whole validated feed), applied at the single line where `_line_payout` turns a rate into dollars, via `attach_qualifier.rule_view` |
| save path | `router.save_commission_plan` round-trips all eight columns. That path is DELETE-THEN-INSERT with an explicit column list, so a column not written back is **WIPED on the next plan save** — §19.18 at its most expensive, since what it erases is money policy. Locked by `harness_attach_qualifier.py` §J |
| lock | `harness_attach_qualifier.py` — 83 checks, DB-free; **6 of them were RED against the un-wired engine** |

**WHAT IS NOT DUPLICATED, and this is the whole design.** *"Is this line an accessory"* is **not answered
here.** There are already ~8 accessory classifiers in this codebase (§19.42 and the `accessory_definition`
docstring enumerate them), and the one the money path honours is `plan_pay_gate.accessory_predicate` →
`accessory_definition.classify`, the map the owner curates by hand on `/commcalc/accessory-definition`.
It is **INJECTED**. *"Does this line match a rule"* is injected too — `commission_engine._rule_matches`,
exactly as `financing_tiers.build_context` takes the same callable, so the condition is counted by
precisely the code that decides what pays. The lock proves this structurally: the module **reads no
classifying column at all** (only `trans_id`, `ext_price`, `gp`), so a keyword list cannot appear in it.

**MEASURED OVER THE WHOLE SALE, not the rep's share of it.** What the customer bought is not an accident
of who rang which line, so two reps on one sale read the same verdict.

**AN UNMEASURABLE SALE PAYS THE FULL RATE, AND IS REPORTED.** A row with no `trans_id` has no knowable
siblings, and an unreadable accessory definition makes the condition unanswerable — neither is "zero
accessories". Treating unknown as zero would quietly dock a rep on a data defect. Such lines earn the
full rate, carry `basis = "unmeasured"`, and are counted in the engine's guard. Same posture as
`payroll_hours_basis` for an undated cell (§14y.1) and the §66 allowlist rule.

**A FLAT FALLBACK CANNOT BE APPLIED TO A PERCENTAGE RULE**, because `_line_payout` prices those off
`pct`: overwriting `amount` would change nothing while the screen claimed a lesser rate was paid. The
pairing is **refused and reported** (`basis = "unsupported"`), and that rule keeps paying what it pays.

**THE LABEL IS DERIVED, NEVER WRITTEN.** The owner asked to see *"$25 acc is must to be qualified for $25
commission"*. Those dollars are one tenant's figures, so `describe()` builds the sentence from the config
— today it renders *"$25 of accessories is required to qualify for the $25 commission; otherwise $10."*
and a tenant with other numbers reads their own. RULE TWO holds: no carrier, tenant, product, market or
dollar figure appears in the code, and the lock scans for them.

**MEASURED ON LIVE DATA before anything moves** (read-only, 2026-10-12, the Total tenant's two $25
`edge` rules, DISTINCT sales, at a $25 minimum with a $10 fallback). The live `accessory` flag is stamped
by a classifier this container cannot run, so that tenant's own `department in (Accessories,
C2Wireless)` declaration stands in and these are therefore a FLOOR:

| month | sales | qualified | short | pays today | with the rule | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jul 2026 | 2 | 0 | 2 | $50.00 | $20.00 | −$30.00 |
| Aug 2026 | 7 | 6 | 1 | $175.00 | $160.00 | −$15.00 |
| Sep 2026 | 8 | 4 | 4 | $200.00 | $140.00 | −$60.00 |
| Oct 2026 to date | 2 | 2 | 0 | $50.00 | $50.00 | $0.00 |

**One of those sales carried $24.99 of accessories** — a penny short cost the rep $15 under the rule as
literally stated. Surfaced for the owner rather than rounded away in code: a tolerance is a config
decision, not something the engine should invent.

Nothing is switched on. Migration 1079 was **applied to production 2026-10-13** (owner ran it; all eight
columns present, three CHECK constraints created, **zero** rules declaring a qualifier), no rule declares
a qualifier, and no stored payout is touched.

### COMMCALC-06.1 Cross-references

- **§16 (by TABLE):** `commcalc.commission_rule` — eight new columns (mig 1079), read by
  `attach_qualifier.resolve` and round-tripped by `router.save_commission_plan`.
- **§17 (by FUNCTION):** `attach_qualifier.resolve` / `build_context` / `verdict` / `rule_view` /
  `describe`; `commission_engine.preview` (the one caller); `plan_options.vocabulary` (the editor's
  vocabulary, §COMMCALC-06.2); `router.list_commission_plans` (serves the derived sentence).
- **§18 (by QUESTION):** "Did this sale earn the line its full rate, or the lesser one — and who decides
  what counts toward the condition?" → `attach_qualifier`, dereferencing
  `plan_pay_gate.accessory_predicate` for the accessory answer and `commission_engine._rule_matches` for
  the sibling match. Never a classifier of its own.
- **Siblings checked and NOT duplicated:** `plan_pay_gate` (suppression — a different outcome, and the
  home for it), `financing_tiers` (re-rating from a month's attainment, not from one sale),
  `daily_incentive` (§76.4 — declared qualifiers, but it computes only and pays nobody),
  `management_incentive` (§9 — manager-level qualifier gates), `accessory_definition` (mig 257 — the
  definition this dereferences).
- **§6f / §19.42:** the accessory-classifier divergence this deliberately does not add to.

### COMMCALC-06.2 The screen that declares it (owner 2026-10-14: "Nothing is hardcoded")

**The mechanism shipped without a way to reach it.** #457 delivered the module, the engine wiring, the
save path and the columns — and **no input on the Commission Plans editor**. That is §19.18 in the shape
that matters most: the only way to declare a qualifier was a hand-written `UPDATE`, and
`router.save_commission_plan` is DELETE-THEN-INSERT over an explicit column list, so the **next plan save
would have wiped the owner's money policy silently**. A capability an operator cannot reach is not
shipped, and here reaching it by hand was actively unsafe.

**One home, dereferenced three hops.** `plan_options.vocabulary()` serves `qualifier_measures`,
`qualifier_scopes` and `qualifier_defaults` by reading `attach_qualifier.MEASURES`, `MEASURE_LABELS`,
`SCOPES` and the new `DEFAULT_MATCH_FIELD` / `DEFAULT_MATCH_OP` / `DEFAULT_MATCH_VALUE` constants —
which `resolve()` itself now reads, replacing the three inline literals it used to fall back to. The
editor (`_lib/QualifierEditor.tsx`, imported by `commission-plans/page.tsx`) renders only what that
endpoint served: it names **no measure, no default and no dollar figure**, so the owner's "nothing is
hardcoded" holds through the browser and not just the engine.

**The sentence has one renderer.** `attach_qualifier.describe` is called on `GET /commission-plans` and
served per rule as `qualifier_requirement`; the editor DISPLAYS that string. A TypeScript rebuild of the
same figures would be the second home that drifts, because nothing recomputes the stored one — and the
owner reads that sentence as the rule.

**Two refusals the screen states rather than swallows.** A `%`-of-basis rule cannot take a flat
fallback (`_line_payout` prices it off `pct`, so the figure would be stored and never read): the input is
disabled and the reason given. And when the vocabulary endpoint is unreachable the fields are **hidden**,
not rendered against `FALLBACK_VOCAB` — a money condition is not editable against a guessed list of
measures.

**Locked** by `harness_attach_qualifier.py` §K (K0–K14, 105 checks total, verified **12 named failures
and no traceback** against pre-fix `main`): the editor sends every one of the eight columns, a blank
minimum goes as NULL and never 0, clearing clears all eight, the sentence is not rebuilt in the browser,
no measure literal appears there, and a rule that already declares a qualifier is shown open rather than
collapsed. K10's first draft flagged the owner's own directive quoted in a header comment — it now strips
comments and matches `describe()`'s own phrases, with K10a failing the build if that phrase list drifts
from the function.

## §COMMCALC-07. ONE PULL LOOP, MANY FEEDS — AND A REPORT LINE IS NOT A CATEGORY UNTIL THE TENANT SAYS SO (owner directive 2026-10-12)

> **Section number:** written as §COMMCALC-05 and renumbered to **§COMMCALC-07** on merge. #453 took
> §COMMCALC-05 and #457 took §COMMCALC-06 while this was in flight, and both carry a migration
> (`1079`, `1080`) coupled to their number; this change's migration (`1078`) is not coupled to a
> section id, so it was the cheapest of the three to move. That is the **fifth** number race in four
> days (§61/§62, §67, §68/§71, and now this) — the allocator added by §CORE-01 hands out the next
> free id but cannot RESERVE it on `main`, which is the gap each race keeps finding.

Owner, verbatim: the back-office portal's reports *"should be checked against what the employees
declare daily … but i dont wnat them to be hard coded it should be a design effect"*. This is step 2
of the three he approved (step 1 was §CORE-03, the portal credentials); step 3, the comparison
itself, is its own change and is deliberately NOT claimed here.

### §COMMCALC-07.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

The instance is "the tenant's POS report has no puller". Two classes sat behind it.

**(a) The pull loop and the feed were one lump.** Pulling a report is six steps and only the last two
are about the feed: resolve the window of days, reach the report, press its export control, read the
download, parse it, store it. The first four were written INSIDE
`commcalc/merchant_portal_sweep.py`, bound to card settlement by three hard-coded calls — the
descriptor lookup, the normalizer and the lander. So a second feed on the same machinery could only
be built by **copying that file**, and with it the calibration ladder, the export words, the
honest-failure wording and the cold-session restore. Four facts, duplicated, drifting from the day
they were written. The live session's dispatch made it concrete: `router._live_pull` asked
`merchant_portals.is_portal(proc)`, so a new feed could not have ridden the authenticated browser
without editing that line.

**(b) The portal's words and the tenant's words had no join.** The portal publishes its own labels;
what the business declares at closing is a config registry since §76 (`closing/metric_catalog.py`).
Both wrong answers to "which declared category is this report line?" are worse than none:

- **Spell the categories in code** — breaks for the next tenant, freezes a vendor's wording into the
  repo, and is exactly what the owner's last sentence and RULE TWO forbid.
- **Resolve to the closest-looking category** — produces a comparison that *reads as evidence and is
  not*. A line matched by resemblance, then compared against a rep's declaration, manufactures a
  disagreement (or hides a real one) with nothing to show a reader which it was.

### §COMMCALC-07.2 THE TWO ONE-HOMES

**`backend/app/modules/commcalc/portal_report_pull.py`** — "reach a report on a portal we are logged
into, export it, land it", written exactly once. A feed is an **ADAPTER**: a module exposing four
functions (`connector_keys`, `portal_descriptor`, `report_specs`, `ingest_report`), optionally a
fifth (`setup_hint`). `ADAPTER_MODULES` is the registry, and a connector key is never spelled there —
each adapter is ASKED which keys it serves, so the card keys stay in `merchant_portals.PORTAL_KEYS`
and the POS-report key in its own module. The loop imports no feed, names no table, and mentions no
card brand, settlement role or declared category.

**`backend/app/modules/commcalc/pos_report_feed.py`** (PURE) — "what does a report line MEAN in this
tenant's declared vocabulary, and may that meaning be read as the tenant's word". The match ladder,
best first, with the basis recorded on every row:

| basis | how it matched | the tenant's own word? |
|---|---|---|
| `line_map` | the tenant mapped this portal line to this category (config on the source row) | **yes** |
| `label` | the portal's wording IS the category's own label — *the design effect: name the category what the portal calls it and nothing needs mapping* | **yes** |
| `label_part` | the wording contains exactly one category's label | no |
| `ambiguous` | two categories could claim it, so **neither does** | no |
| `unmatched` | nothing claimed it — reported with the money it carried | no |

`DECLARED_BASES` is an **ALLOWLIST**, so a basis invented later reads as NOT the tenant's word until
somebody rules on it. That is §66's rule (`component_is_evidence`) in the second place that needed
it, and the reason `metric_basis` is a stored column: a surface reading `metric_key` without it would
treat a text coincidence as a declaration. A metric key is never invented here — the catalog is the
tenant's, and this module only points at a key it already has.

### §COMMCALC-07.3 A CONNECTOR KIND, NOT A VENDOR

`pos_report_sweep.CONNECTOR = "pos_report"` is the `data_source.processor` of *a back-office portal
that publishes a daily sales report* — the `supply/portal.SUPPLY_PROCESSOR` posture. **No vendor's
name, URL, menu wording, report name or category appears anywhere in this repository.** The portal's
address is `data_source.portal_url`; its report list is `data_source.portal_reports` (jsonb, a list
of declarations or of bare keys); its selectors are `data_source.portal_calibration`, captured once
by an operator on the live-login screencast; its line-label → category mapping is
`portal_calibration.line_map`, narrowed per report if wanted. The consequence is deliberate and
stated in the code: **this connector does nothing at all until an operator declares a portal and at
least one report** — and it says so in the operator's own words rather than pulling zero rows and
looking healthy.

### §COMMCALC-07.4 WHAT WAS REUSED, NOT REBUILT (duplicate check — build gate)

| Checked | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `commcalc/live_login.py` | **REUSED verbatim** — one live browser from login through the second factor, streamed to the operator. No second login engine |
| `commcalc/vidapay_sweep` primitives | **REUSED** — `_launch` / `_new_context` / `_proxy_arg` / `_classify` / `_wait_settle` / `capture_session_state` / `VidaPayAuthError` |
| `commcalc.data_source` | **REUSED, no new column** — `portal_url`, `portal_reports`, `portal_calibration`, `portal_window_days`, `session_state`, `auth_status` all already exist (mig 955) |
| `POST /commcalc/data-sources/sweep/run-due` + mig 956 cron | **REUSED** — one `_SOURCE_SCRAPERS` registration IS "daily scheduling" |
| `commcalc.connector_route_policy` (mig 998) | **REUSED, no row needed** — no rows reads as OPEN |
| `commcalc/portal_session_health`, `portal_backoff`, `import_audit.p_portal_sessions` | **REUSED unchanged** — the dead-session chip, the cooldown and the admin popup all key off `data_source`, so they cover this connector the day it is configured |
| `commcalc.report_pull_map` (mig 207) | **REUSED** — one house row, so a consumer finds the table and column spelling without hardcoding either (the mig-955 contract, second use) |
| `account/store_identity` via `coa.store_resolver` | **REUSED** — THE store resolver. The feed takes `resolve_store` as an argument and derives no mapping of its own |
| `closing/router._metric_catalog` | **DEREFERENCED** — the single construction site of the catalog (`harness_metric_catalog_lock` forbids a second). The adapter never builds one |
| `merchant_portals.money` / `iso_date` | **DEREFERENCED** — the platform's PURE portal value readers. *Stated, not hidden:* ten private `_money` parsers already exist across the backend. That sprawl is a real duplicate defect and it is NOT this change's; what this change owes is not adding an eleventh, which it does not |
| `commcalc.raw_sales` / `raw_sales_product` (migs 002 / 1011) | **NOT reused, and mig 1011 is the reason** — it exists because two report kinds sharing one table let one kind's slice-replace delete 48,875 rows of the other. Those tables are slice-replaced per store × date × kind, carry no `source_id` / `report_key`, and have no declared-category axis |
| `commcalc.closing_metric_line` (mig 1072) | **deliberately separate** — that is what the REPS declared. Writing a portal's figure into it would destroy the comparison this feed exists for |
| `commcalc.merchant_settlement_day` (mig 955) | same MECHANISM (now shared), different grain and subject — money by card brand, not units and dollars by category and worker |
| `storeops` employee identity (§STOREOPS-01) | **not touched on purpose** — `employee_name` lands as the portal spelled it, unresolved. A feed that guessed which spelling is which person would be that defect in a new place |

**NEW:** two modules, one adapter, one table (`commcalc.portal_metric_day`, mig **1078**), one
`report_pull_map` house row, two lineage edges.

### §COMMCALC-07.5 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

`backend/harness_portal_report_pull.py` (101 checks, stdlib, in `carrier-vocab-guard`):

- **§C is the ratchet.** A module that downloads a report (`expect_download`) or defines a pull loop
  (a `*_pull_on_page` function) is either the ONE home or is **PINNED** in `UNFOLDED_PULL_LOOPS` with
  a written reason — and the count **may only shrink**. Three are pinned today, each pre-existing and
  each driving a live feed: `vidapay_sweep.py` (also the home of the browser primitives every sweep
  borrows; folding it means re-proving the carrier feeds that pay commission),
  `epay_sweep.py` (reaches its reports by submitting a form, which this loop does not yet model) and
  `supply/portal.py` (not a report download at all — a catalog crawl, named so a reader looking for
  copies finds it and is told why it is not one). **The siblings were found and are listed rather
  than quietly tolerated**; folding them is its own change with its own proof, and doing it beside a
  new feed would put six working connectors at risk to tidy a file.
- §D the card feed **imports** the moved names from the one home and re-defines none of them, so
  every existing caller and `harness_merchant_portals.py` (73 checks, unchanged and green) read
  exactly the code they always did. §E the router dispatches on the pull registry and dereferences
  the connector constant rather than re-spelling it. §F drives the whole loop on a fake page: the
  zero-row pull that is never delivered, the two different operator failures, an adapter that raises,
  Cancel between reports. **Proved red both ways** before shipping — adding an `expect_download` to
  an unpinned module, and giving the card feed its own copy of `pull_reports_on_page`.

`backend/harness_pos_report_feed.py` (111 checks): the match ladder and what it refuses, the fold
that takes the **weakest** basis (one coincidence in a sum makes the sum not a declaration), the
store-code case trap closed at the natural key, the unplaced store that is stored and reported but
excluded from store totals, §I asserts the code's `ON_CONFLICT` equals mig 1078's unique index column
for column, and §K is a whole-word RULE TWO scan over the executable text of both modules. **It found
a real bug:** a mapping onto a category the tenant had deleted was honoured when the map arrived
already normalized.

### §COMMCALC-07.6 WHAT IS NOT DONE, STATED

- **The comparison is not built.** The rows land, they are readable, and nothing checks them against
  what the reps declared. That is the owner's actual ask and it is the next change; the lineage edge
  for it is seeded `auto_updated = false` with `(not built yet)` as its code reference, because a
  lineage edge claiming a check nobody wrote is worse than no edge.
- **Nothing pulls yet.** Migration 1078 is **SURFACED, NOT APPLIED**, and even applied, the feed is
  inert until an operator declares the portal, logs in once on the live screencast so the second
  factor is satisfied, and saves the report's navigation and export control. The portal credentials
  and the authenticator secret are already encrypted at rest (§CORE-03).
- **Three older sweeps still drive their own pull loop** (§COMMCALC-07.5), pinned and visible.
- Same class: §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers left unwired), §66 (a value read without
  its basis), §76 (the declared-category registry this feed points at), §36 (the connector KIND
  precedent), mig 1011 (two report kinds, one table).
