## §COMMCALC-08. A FILE THAT PRODUCED NO ROWS IS TOLD WHY — the pairing, not the spreadsheet (owner report 2026-10-13)

Two uploads were refused with *"That file produced no rows once its header and any total row were
read."* Both files were fine. They were `MA - Empire October Commission Details (24).xls` and its
September twin, and both were handed to the **MA Daily Transactions** reader — which shares **not one
column name** with the Commission Details layout (proved, not assumed: §COMMCALC-08.4 g1 asserts the
intersection of the two declared layouts is empty). Every row mapped to nothing, `map_records`
dropped them all, and the refusal stated a fact about the FILE when what was actually wrong was the
PAIRING. The owner spent his evening looking for a defect in a spreadsheet that did not have one.

### COMMCALC-08.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

| Mechanism that already exists | Question it answers | Why it is not this |
|---|---|---|
| `report_kinds.detect_report_kind` | "which report KIND is this file", from registry rows + confirmed fingerprints | A different question and a different key. It ranks *registry kinds* using `norm_header`, which collapses punctuation to match **loosely** — right for detection, wrong here, because a looser key reports a column as found that the mapper then does not read. **EXTENDED, not duplicated:** it stays the detector; this is the mapper answering for itself. |
| `uploadGuard.readUploadOutcome` (frontend) | "does a zero-row upload render honestly" | THE SAME CLASS, one feed further in — so it was **extended** with one branch rather than given a second interpreter. The wording is not copied into the UI; the backend sentence is displayed verbatim. |
| the X-Report's `skipped` / `note` ladder | why a tender file produced nothing | The precedent this follows ("name the columns found"), scoped to one feed. Generalised here instead of copied again. |
| `harness_mapping_key_lock` | which report_key a commission statement type maps under | About the mapping KEY, not about header matching or empty results. |
| `prospect_eval.substance` / `substance_note` (§COMMCALC-03.10) | "rows landed, but do they carry anything" | The step AFTER this one. That reads rows that exist; this explains why none do. |

### COMMCALC-08.2 One fact, one home, dereferenced

`commcalc/column_mapping.py`, in dependency order:

- **`match_key(header)`** — THE key the mapper pairs a rule's `source_header` with a file's column
  by, and the one home of that fact. Anything answering *for* the mapper must ask the same question
  the same way or its answer is a guess. Factored out of `apply_mapping`, which now dereferences it
  on both sides of the match.
- **`header_fit(headers, rules)`** → `{found, missing, expected, extra, fraction}`, in the ORIGINAL
  spellings so a message can quote the file and the mapping back verbatim.
- **`no_rows_diagnosis(...)`** → the reason token and the sentence. **Returns `None` when nothing is
  wrong**, so no caller can print a cause over a successful upload.
- **`resolve_rules(rows, carrier_id)`** — the per-field resolution, factored out of `load_rules` so
  the bulk read cannot resolve a rule differently from the single read the upload itself used.
- **`rules_by_report_key` / `candidate_rules`** — "which feeds could this file be", in ONE query.
  A key the tenant configured is scored against the tenant's OWN column names; a key it has not
  configured falls back to the built-in layout, because an unmapped feed is still a feed the file
  may belong to — which is exactly the case on a brand-new prospect.

**A fourth copy found and rewired on the way:** `suggest()` spelled the mapper's header key inline
four times. It is the function that tells the column-mapping wizard which header to propose, so a
drift between it and `apply_mapping` would propose a column the mapper does not read. All four now
dereference `match_key`.

**RULE TWO:** no feed, carrier or tenant is named in the mechanism. The candidate feeds and their
display labels are the CALLER's — which is why the sentence says "MA Commission Details" and not
`ma_commission` (COMMCALC-08.4 g8).

### COMMCALC-08.3 The siblings, fixed in the same change rather than excused

`map_records` has three landing callers, and all three answered this question differently:

| Caller | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `_upload_prospect_feed_impl` | refused with the blanket sentence | refuses with the cause, and names the feed the file belongs to |
| `_ingest_mapped_df` (the `/upload-mapped` core — also the onboarding intake commit and a custom report's dataset binding) | returned `saved: 0` with **no reason at all** | returns `no_rows_reason` + `no_rows_note` |
| `commission_import_commit` (the wizard's own copy of the pipeline) | same silence | dereferences the same one home |

The two live cores **report** rather than raise, because an automated sweep is allowed to hand them
an empty day; the prospect upload still **refuses**, because a person pressed a button and is owed an
answer. `_ledger_map_records` is a separate mapper and a separate change — stated, not covered.

### COMMCALC-08.4 Locked so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_mapping_diagnosis.py` — **51 passed / 0 failed**, DB-free, run in CI inside the
`store-takeover-eval-proof` job (which already installs the backend's dependencies), and named in
the workflow's path filter alongside `column_mapping.py`.

- **(a)** a `map_records` caller that does not dereference the diagnosis → RED. Derived from the AST,
  never a name list, so a NEW landing path that drops every row silently is the defect and fails.
- **(b)** a second match key: any header-matching function that spells the normalisation itself → RED.
- **(c)** the diagnosis is silent for a file that produced rows.
- **(d)** one resolution — both reads go through `resolve_rules`.
- **(e)** RULE TWO over the mechanism's own source.
- **(f)** the cause reported is the FIRST thing that was wrong, in pipeline order: `file_empty` →
  `no_data_rows` → `no_columns_match` → `rows_blank_in_columns` → `all_rows_are_totals`. So a
  mis-paired file is never reported as an empty one, and a totals-only file is only read that way
  once the columns DID match.
- **(g)** the owner's own case, rebuilt from the two DECLARED layouts (no header list is written in
  the harness): his headers must diagnose as `no_columns_match`, must name MA Commission Details,
  must quote his file's own columns back, and the SAME file under the right feed must map all 31 rows
  and get no diagnosis at all.
- **(h)** negative controls: each check above is shown going red.

### COMMCALC-08.5 Cross-references

| Code | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `commcalc/column_mapping.match_key` | which key a header is matched by — the mapper's own |
| `commcalc/column_mapping.header_fit` | which of a mapping's columns this file carries |
| `commcalc/column_mapping.no_rows_diagnosis` | why a file produced no rows, and whose columns these are |
| `commcalc/column_mapping.resolve_rules` | the effective rule per target field |
| `commcalc/column_mapping.rules_by_report_key` | every key's effective rules, in one query |
| `commcalc/column_mapping.candidate_rules` | which feeds a mis-paired file could belong to |
| `uploadGuard.readUploadOutcome` | whether a zero-row upload renders honestly (extended, not duplicated) |
| `harness_mapping_diagnosis.py` | the lock: every landing path names the cause, from one home |

No migration. No table. No report. Nothing money-touching: the diagnosis is produced only when
zero rows were written, and it changes no write, no delete and no figure.

Same class: §COMMCALC-03.9 (an upload that failed left no record anywhere — the defect that made
this one visible), §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers left unwired), §66 (a value read
without its basis), §64 (one home for "which store is this address").

## §COMMCALC-09. A STORED PAY SLICE NOBODY COMPUTED IS NOT $0.00 EARNED (owner report 2026-10-15)

Owner, verbatim: *"rep incentive report for luxelink shopws ACC GP as zero but calculates the
commission when you click on teh linke 0 if the source for the data is teh same then why is the index
not updateiong all areas when one is claculated , check for all such things in the commission module
and the sales module so everywhere the same data is visible"*.

**Both reads were right about their own source.** The Rep Incentive table reads the STORED
`commcalc.rep_commissions` row (`router.get_commissions`); the 🔬 drill-down RE-COMPUTES from the plan
engine. The accessory slice of a plan-mode row has only been written since the 2026-09-17 itemisation
(§6b), and Luxelink's earlier months were last calculated on **2026-09-10** — so August's row carries
`plan_comm = 957.36` beside `subtotal = 0` and `acc_comm = 0`: a correct total next to a breakdown
that was never computed. Nothing on the screen said which, so $0.00 read as "this rep earned nothing
on accessories".

**Measured read-only, 2026-10-15.** Of 192 stored Luxelink rows, **102 contradict themselves** this
way — August 45/46, July 42/44, June 10/10, May 3/8, March 2/8 — holding **$23,440.15** of correct
total pay beside a $0.00 breakdown. September (45) and October (31) are clean: they were calculated
after the itemisation shipped. The house (Boost) org: **0 of 379**, because `calculator.py` has always
written every slice. Vzone has no rows.

### COMMCALC-09.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index and the module graph for an existing home for "may this stored figure be read as a
figure". §66 (`carrier_dollar_class.component_is_evidence`) is the same RULING on a classified dollar
and its allowlist posture is **reused verbatim here**, not re-invented; §19.28 (`kpi_failing`) is the
same lesson for a KPI with no value — and lives three lines from one of the surfaces fixed below,
which had learned it for KPIs and not for `subtotal`. The `not_measured` family (§29.12 unfinished
closing day, the store-takeover lines) is the same posture on a computed read. None of them answers
this question for a stored pay row, so `commcalc/payout_slice_evidence.py` is the new one home and
every surface dereferences it.

### COMMCALC-09.2 How a never-written slice is known — no migration, no new column

In plan mode the writer (`router._apply_new_engines`) sets `subtotal` and `plan_comm` to the SAME
figure in the same statement, and `tier_source` to `'plan'`. **A plan-mode row where `plan_comm` is
positive and `subtotal` is zero therefore contradicts itself** — it says the plan paid money and that
the subtotal of that pay was nothing. Only a row written before the itemisation can say both. That is
the whole predicate and it reads two columns that already exist.

Verified against every row shape that is actually in the table, not just the broken one:

| shape | live rows (Luxelink) | verdict | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plan mode, `plan_comm > 0`, `subtotal = 0` | 102 | `not_recorded` | contradicts itself |
| plan mode, itemised | 70 | `recorded` | the slices were written |
| plan mode, installment-only (`plan_comm = 0`) | 20 | `recorded` | a zero subtotal is TRUE — no plan paid them |
| Boost (`tier_source != 'plan'`) | 379 (house org) | `recorded` | the calculator always wrote them |

The installment-only row is why the predicate needs both halves: a test on `subtotal = 0` alone would
withhold 20 rows whose zero is a measurement. Harness §A/Z1 pins exactly that.

### COMMCALC-09.3 What is NOT done, and why

**No backfill, and no recalculation.** Recomputing those five months writes stored pay, which is money
and the owner's own button (CLAUDE.md: money-touching changes are surfaced, not applied). It would also
leave the next surface unable to tell. The registry comes first; the report now NAMES the months to
recalculate, so a backfill afterwards is visible rather than silent.

**The sales module was checked and is not affected** (the owner asked for it explicitly). Its accessory
figure comes from `router._compute_feed_actuals_py` → `_sales_cell_agg`, **recomputed on every read**
from the sales feed — there is no stored snapshot to go stale. The one stored sales-side snapshot, the
Account dashboard's, already differs from the live GP report BY DESIGN and already carries its own
staleness cross-check (§23d `tie_delta`). Nothing to fix; stated here so the next reader does not
re-derive it.

### COMMCALC-09.4 The six readers and the one writer

| surface | what it did | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `router._get_commissions_rows` | served the stored row raw | stamps `payout_slice_basis` + `payout_slice_reason` on the ONE read every Rep Incentive surface goes through |
| `payout_audience.EMPLOYEE_REP_ROW_FIELDS` | an allow-list, so a new field would be stripped | carries the basis to every audience — a rep is entitled to know their breakdown was never computed |
| `rep_incentive_range.assemble` | summed `subtotal` / `acc_comm` across months, adding an unknown as zero | sums named slices through `sum_slice`, reports `*_rows_not_recorded`, and names `periods_not_recorded` — the module is **injected**, see below |
| `whatif._boost_actuals` | BACK-DERIVED baseline sales (`acc_comm / acc_rate`), so a blank slice started a projection from the wrong baseline | excludes those rows from the slice aggregates, keeps their `total_payout`, reports `slices_not_recorded` |
| `router` coaching card (§19.28's own file) | `at_risk = subtotal × (1 − tier)` on a never-computed subtotal | reads `slice_value`; withholds `at_risk` rather than printing $0.00 at risk |
| `router` action plan | same, and emitted `subtotal` as $0.00 | same, and emits `None` with the basis |
| `router._apply_new_engines` 2nd branch (WRITER) | wrote `subtotal` and NOT the slices, so it could store a positive subtotal beside a $0.00 breakdown — **undetectable after the fact** | itemises the row it creates (0 such rows exist live, 0 can be created now) |

The screen (`reports/page.tsx`, three tables) renders an unrecorded slice as **—** with the server's
reason on hover, never a figure of its own; the TOTAL column is never dashed, because `total_payout`
has always been written. `repIncentiveRange.ts` skips unrecorded rows in its client-side slice sums
(it imports nothing by design, so it reads the server's stamped verdict rather than re-deriving the
test).

**The range assembler is the one caller that is handed the module rather than importing it.**
`harness_rep_incentive_range.py` D5 locks `rep_incentive_range.py` to ZERO imports — an assembler that
can reach into `app` can grow a read of its own, which is the whole point of that lock — so `assemble`
takes the verdict as its **required** third argument, `assemble(months, per_month, evidence)`, and the
router hands it `payout_slice_evidence`. That is still a dereference and not a copy, and because the
argument has **no default**, a caller that stops passing it raises instead of silently reverting to
adding zeros (§19.18, the failure mode where a registry is written and the callers left un-wired).
The consequence for §50: there is no AST import edge for this caller, so `core/module_graph.py` cannot
declare it; the comment in the fact says so, and `harness_payout_slice_evidence` G4a/G4b/G4c hold the
wiring instead — the argument is required, the assembler imports nothing, the router passes the real
module.

### COMMCALC-09.5 Locks

`harness_payout_slice_evidence.py` — **65 checks, 0 failures; verified 18 named failures and no
traceback against pre-fix `main`** in a clean worktree. §G9 fails the build if any caller spells the
contradiction test itself; §H fails it if either plan-mode writer stops itemising; §I pins the screen
to the server's verdict; §C pins the allowlist (an unruled basis is not evidence). `F1`'s first draft
flagged this module's own header, which names the tenant measured — it now scans CODE with docstrings
and comments stripped, and `F1b` pins the one product-named string to the existing `acima_comm`
column. `frontend/tools/rep-incentive-range-proof.mjs` grew 7 checks (17 total) for the client sums.

### COMMCALC-09.6 Cross-references

- **§16 (by TABLE):** `commcalc.rep_commissions` — the named slices (`subtotal`, `acc_comm`,
  `setup_fee_comm`, `premium_comm`, `byod_comm`, `upgrade_comm`, `trade_in_comm`, `acima_comm`,
  `custom_comm`) are read through `payout_slice_evidence`, never straight off the row.
- **§17 (by FUNCTION):** `payout_slice_evidence.basis` / `slice_value` / `sum_slice` / `annotate` /

- **§18 (by QUESTION):** "Is this stored pay breakdown a figure at all, or a blank that prints as
  $0.00?" → `payout_slice_evidence`, module-graph fact `payout_slice_evidence`.
- **Same class:** §66 (a value read without its basis — the posture reused), §19.18 (a mechanism

## §COMMCALC-21. A NON-PAYMENT SOMEBODY CHOSE IS NOT A FINDING (owner report 2026-10-19)

OWNER, verbatim: *"if home internet is not required to pay the multi month as defined inte h incentive
struture it shoud not appear as not paid and create confusion for teh user"*, following *"rep incentive
report ... check for all such things ... so everywhere the same data is visible"* and his root-cause ask
that device categories come from the carrier's own data rather than a checklist.

### COMMCALC-21.1 What was actually wrong — and what was NOT

Measured read-only on the owner's own tenant before any change, because the notice's wording invited the
wrong diagnosis:

| | count | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| multi-month activations in the period | 409 | — |
| classified correctly and then EXCLUDED BY A STORED SETTING | 405 | not a defect |
| genuinely unclassifiable (`unknown`) | 4 | the real gap |
| products in `raw_catalog` for this tenant | **0** | the automatic rung is empty |
| rows in `installment_category_rule` | 0 | built-in rules only |
| rows in `carrier_category_map` | 0 | the commission/rebate registry is empty |

**Classification was not the problem.** The ladder (§6n) identified 115 home-internet boxes and 290
tablets correctly; the stored `installment_category_qualification` then said `home_internet: false`,
`tablet: false`, `sim: false`, `accessory: false`, `unknown: false`, `phone: true`. The engine obeyed,
and the notice reported the owner's own decision back to him every month as a shortfall.

**Reported, not built.** The automatic path the owner asked for already exists and is EMPTY: the ladder
prefers the product catalog's Department / Category over any hand-typed rule, and this tenant has
uploaded no catalog. That is a data gap, reported. And the carrier statement's categories answer *"is
this dollar commission or rebate"* — not *"is this a phone or a tablet"*. Wiring one to the other would
invent a link the data does not support, so it was not wired; it was put to the owner instead.

### COMMCALC-21.2 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index for an existing home for "why did this not pay". Three near-neighbours, each the SAME
posture on a different subject, so the posture was reused and no sibling built:

- **§66 `carrier_dollar_class.component_is_evidence(basis)`** — the allowlist shape is copied exactly.
- **§COMMCALC-09 `payout_slice_evidence`** — a blank is not a measurement; here, a decision is not a
  finding. Different subject (a stored pay column vs a qualification layer), no shared helper.
- **§19.28 `kpi_failing`** — no-data is not a 0% failure.

The question "which layer excluded this category" belongs to the module that already owns "which
category is this" and "does it qualify", so `commcalc/installment_category.py` was **extended** rather
than joined by a sibling. Both callers dereference it; neither writes a reason or names a basis
(harness §F9).

### COMMCALC-21.3 The four bases, and the allowlist direction

`BASIS_TENANT_SETTING` · `BASIS_SCHEDULE_OVERRIDE` · `BASIS_PLATFORM_DEFAULT` · `BASIS_UNSTATED`.

`_DECIDED_BASES` is an **allowlist** of the first three, so `is_decided` is false for any basis a later
migration invents and does not rule on, and `is_actionable` is its exact complement. The unknown case
shouts; it never hides. `exclusion_reason(category, basis)` is the only place the sentence lives, and an
unrecognised basis yields *"the reason it is excluded could not be established"* rather than a guess.

`BASIS_UNSTATED` is the latent bug made visible: a `qualifying_categories` stored as a LIST of included
categories says nothing whatsoever about a category it omits, and the engine used to report those
omissions as *"that category is unchecked"* — a sentence nobody had earned. The verdict is unchanged
(the list still means what it meant); only the basis, and therefore whether it is a finding, is now
honest. The owner's tenant stores the dict shape, so it is not affected today; the code path is live.

### COMMCALC-21.4 What moved, and what did not

| surface | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `installment_category.qualification_with_basis` | — | the same verdict and source as `qualification_for`, plus a basis per category (harness §C proves equality over all ten config shapes) |
| `sale_installment_engine` | one `category_excluded` warning per category, one asserted reason | `category_excluded_decided` vs `category_excluded`, reason from the one home |
| `sale_installment_engine` (`unknown`) | counted in the excluded bucket AND warned about separately | `excluded_unknown`, reported once by its own warning |
| `router` calc notices | every exclusion in "What this calculation did not pay" | only the actionable ones; decisions get one `severity: "decided"` line with chains and dollars |
| `commcalc/page.tsx` | one amber list | the amber list plus a quiet "Excluded by your settings" block; the screen reads `severity` and decides nothing |

**No figure moves and no payout changes.** A notice with no `severity` reads as open, so an older server
renders exactly as before.

### COMMCALC-21.5 Reported, never repaired

- **4 devices were paid TWO installments for the same month** — real money paid twice, pointing at a
  duplicate active schedule. Surfaced, not silenced; its own job.
- **200 transactions matched no rule and paid nothing** — a separate cause, its own job.
- All three schedule lines read `mrc_source: product_catalog` against an empty catalog, which is why
  several per-rep figures in the notice were $0.00.

### COMMCALC-21.6 Locks

`harness_installment_exclusion_basis.py` — **68 checks, 0 failures; verified 27 named failures and no
traceback against pre-fix `main`** in a clean worktree. §A the basis ladder, §B the allowlist direction
(an unruled basis is a finding), §C no figure moves, §D one sentence per basis, §E/§F the wiring and the

paths filter and its own step. `core/module_graph.py` fact `installment_exclusion_basis`, callers

## §COMMCALC-22. A CLAIM WITH NO AMOUNT CANNOT BE FILED (owner report 2026-10-20)

Owner, verbatim: *"trace teh 4 devices which were aid twice , 200 sales which matched no commision ,
it could be a part of the discrepancies to be filed with the carrier and as a matter of fact they
shoudl be a part of the discrepancies if we did not get paid"*.

### COMMCALC-22.1 What was actually wrong

What he asked for already existed and could not be used. The B2B-sold / carrier-paid recon (§15)
resolves every sold activation against the statement and writes the unpaid ones to
`commcalc.discrepancy_results`. Measured read-only 2026-10-20: **every row it has ever written
carries `expected_amount` $0.00, `commissionable_mrc` $0.00 and `gap` $0.00** — the literal `0.0` at
the write site (`ma_recon.py`) — so `discrepancy_appeals.summarize_appeals`' open-$ card sums to
$0.00 for the whole tenant. A claim the platform says is worth nothing is a claim nobody can file.

Luxelink, June–October 2026, every activation matched to `raw_ma_commission` on digit-normalized
`serial_1` ∪ `sim` (the recon's own sold basis):

| | activations | comparable value | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| carrier paid | 3,642 | — | — |
| sold after the last day that period's statement reaches | 285 | ~$55,824 | not yet due — **not a claim** |
| all on **28 July**, a day the statement holds ZERO rows for | 33 | ~$5,914 | our feed gap — **not a claim** |
| explained by the tenant's own `ma_payment_rule` rows | 206 | ~$11,025 | a decision (§COMMCALC-21) |
| **nothing explains them** | **298** | **~$55,946** | **the claims** (July 230 / ~$40,505) |

Before this change all four shapes were written as `open` or `info` with a $0.00 value — so filing
from the report would have invoiced the carrier for money not yet owed and for a statement day
nobody uploaded, and every real claim would have been worth nothing.

**The class, not the instance.** The instance is "the carrier-statement recon writes zero". The class
is **two writers answering one question, one wired and the other left hardcoded** — the sibling
defect the index rules already forbid. One table has two authors: the rate-card engine
(`discrepancy_engine`) SIZES each claim; the recon wrote `0.0`. And a hardcoded `0.0` is the same
shape §19.28 (`kpi_failing`), §66 (`component_is_evidence`), §COMMCALC-09 (`payout_slice_evidence`)
and §COMMCALC-21 each already outlawed on a different subject: a figure nobody measured, printed as a
measurement.

### COMMCALC-22.2 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index for an existing home for "what should this activation have paid". Four
near-neighbours, each the same posture or the same table on a different question — posture reused, no
sibling built:

- **§15 `ma_recon`** owns *whether* the carrier paid, through the mig-308 gate. It keeps that job
  entirely; this section adds only *is it a claim, and what is it worth*.
- **`discrepancy_engine`** owns the Boost rate card. It is not a general estimator (it needs an MI
  line or a parseable MRC), so it could not price this feed — but it is the SIBLING, and it is fixed
  in the same change rather than excused: its unsizeable `SOLD_NOT_IN_MI` claim now writes NULL.
- **§66 `component_is_evidence`** — the allowlist shape, copied exactly, twice.
- **§COMMCALC-21 `installment_category`** — a decision is not a finding; here a decision and a feed
  gap are both not *claims*.

### COMMCALC-22.3 The one home

`backend/app/modules/commcalc/carrier_claim_value.py`. Pure: no I/O, no `from app`, no table, and no
carrier, tenant, market or product name (RULE TWO) — the contract family is whatever string the
caller's own rows carry, and the money columns come from the gate's existing
`ma_month_field_prefix` / `ma_month1_extra_fields` / `ma_payout_sign` config ladder, so a comparable
can never be built from a different definition of money than the test that decided the activation was
unpaid.

**Four states, one claim.** `STATE_OPEN_CLAIM` · `STATE_NOT_YET_STATEMENTED` ·
`STATE_STATEMENT_DAY_MISSING` · `STATE_EXPLAINED_BY_RULE`. `is_claimable` is an **allowlist** of the
first alone, so a state a later migration invents — or one missing entirely — is never filed.
`classify_non_payment` applies them in order of evidence strength: past the statement's reach wins
over everything, a day the statement demonstrably skipped explains its own silence before any rule
does, and a rule speaks only about an activation the statement really did cover and really did skip.

**Absence of coverage is not a gap.** `statement_day_missing` may be asserted only when the day-level
coverage is actually known (`statement_days` non-empty). A statement whose rows carry no usable dates
says nothing about any particular day, and claiming a gap from that would be the very defect this
section exists to remove. Caught by §D of the lock, which was written after the first draft got this
wrong.

**One figure, one basis.** `claim_value` returns `(amount, basis, sample_n)`. The amount is the
median the carrier ITSELF paid for the same contract family in the same period;
`MIN_COMPARABLE_SAMPLE` is 3, the smallest sample whose median is not simply an endpoint, and below
it the figure is **withheld as None with the `not_measured` basis — never rounded down to 0.00**.
`value_is_measured` is the second allowlist. `CLAIM_VALUE_CAVEAT` is the only place the limit is
worded ("a comparable, not an invoice"), so no surface can overstate it. `claim_gap` returns None
when the expected side was not measured, because a subtraction cannot exist where one side does not.

### COMMCALC-22.4 What moved

| surface | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ma_recon` row | `expected_amount` 0.0, `gap` 0.0, `commissionable_mrc` 0.0 | the one home's figure, or **NULL** with the basis in `evidence.claim` |
| `ma_recon` status | `open` for every unexplained non-payment | `open` only for a real claim; `pending` for not-yet-due, `info` for a missing statement day |
| `ma_recon` notes | the rule's text, or the no-rule literal | the one home's sentence; the `'no business rule configured'` literal is kept EXACTLY where that is why the row is open, so `summarize_appeals.no_rule_count` reads as it always did |
| `ma_recon` summary | counts only | plus `claims` from `ccv.summarize` — claimable count, claimable amount over MEASURED values only, and how many claims are unpriced |
| `discrepancy_engine` `SOLD_NOT_IN_MI` | `expected_amount` 0.00, filed | NULL, still `open` — a real finding whose value is unmeasured |
| `/discrepancy/run` response | — | `statement_last_day`, `statement_days_loaded`, `comparables_built` |

No migration: `expected_amount`, `commissionable_mrc` and `gap` are nullable `NUMERIC` (mig 312 DDL),
and the precise state rides in the existing `evidence` jsonb rather than taking a new column. **No
priced figure moves** — the rate-card engine rounds a sized claim exactly as before (§F of the lock),
and nothing here decides whether the carrier paid.

### COMMCALC-22.5 Reported, never repaired

Per the house rule, found in live data and handed to the owner rather than coded around:

- **The recon last ran 2026-09-02.** Nothing for September or October. 806 Luxelink rows exist, 717
  of them under the period spelling `2026-07` and 89 under `August 2026` — two spellings in one
  table (the §COMMCALC-07 class).
- **28 July has no statement rows at all.** Needs re-pulling from the portal.
- **The tenant's two Upgrade rules contradict the statement.** Both say Total pays no activation
  bounty on Upgrades, and they hold 206 activations off the claim list — yet **the carrier paid 121
  Upgrades at a median $75.00**. Worth ~$15,000 if the rule is wrong. A config row, and the owner's
  call; nothing was changed.
- **Re-rings pay per ring** (traced the same day): all 19 duplicated device-months use ONE schedule,
  so the engine's "two schedules" wording is wrong for every live case. $17.25 overpaid, but 100
  Luxelink and 63 Cellfonz activations are OVER-COUNTED, and 83 of 117 re-rings carry no signal in
  the feed at all. Its own job, awaiting the owner's answer on whether to retire the unambiguous ones.

### COMMCALC-22.6 Locks

- `backend/harness_carrier_claim_value.py` — **99 passed / 0 failed**. Verified against pre-fix
  `main` in a clean worktree WITH the new module and graph fact staged, so only the wiring could
  fail: **19 named failures, no traceback** — it catches "registry written, callers unwired" (§19.18)
  rather than merely "module absent".
- `reconcile_ma_activations(..., cfg, claim_ctx)` — `claim_ctx` is **required with no default**, so
  forgetting it is a TypeError at the call site, not a zero in a letter to a carrier.
- §J asserts the hardcoded zeros are gone from BOTH writers and that no second copy of the state or
  basis vocabulary exists outside the one home.
- CI: the lock job's paths filter (4 paths) and its own step — jobs 33, steps 296 → 297, verified
  with `yaml.safe_load`.
- `core/module_graph.py` fact `carrier_claim_value`, both callers AST-derived.

### COMMCALC-22.7 Cross-references

- §15 — the recon that decides whether the carrier paid; unchanged, and the only owner of that test.
- §66 / §COMMCALC-09 / §COMMCALC-21 / §19.28 — the allowlist posture this reuses, now four subjects deep.

## §COMMCALC-10. A LIVE LOGIN THAT STOPS MAKING PROGRESS MUST SAY SO (owner report 2026-10-15)

Owner, verbatim, minutes after declaring his first `pos_report` login (§12a.2a): *"it has been over 5
minutes it is startying teh love login and does not move freom tehre"*. He was right, and waiting
would never have helped — there was going to be no message, ever.

**Measured read-only on the live row before changing anything.** `commcalc.data_source` /
`processor='pos_report'`, label "Team Portal", `portal_url` the UPS Store FRS reporting page,
password stored sealed (`enc:v1:`, 107 chars): `auth_status='authenticating'`,
`auth_message='Live login in progress…'`, `pending_started_at=03:13:42Z`, `pending_state` empty,
`login_shot` NULL. Two explanations ruled OUT and worth not re-deriving: it was not the SERVICE_ROLE
split (browsers are allowed unless `SERVICE_ROLE=api` is explicitly set, and that path returns a
clean 503 at the endpoint, not a wait), and it was not a deploy restarting underneath him (a lost
in-memory session makes `/live-login/state` answer `phase:"idle"` with "No live session running",
not a freeze). His own words named the phase: `starting`, which `live_login` sets once at
construction and which **no code ever timed out**.

**THE CLASS.** *"How long may this phase go without progress" WAS answered — by one inline
conditional inside `_preauth_loop`. But that loop is only reached once the login is already WORKING,
so every phase before it — launching the browser, the first navigation, the sign-in submit — had no
limit of any kind.* The rule existed and did not cover the phases where a stall is most likely. A
session that stalls there sits in "Starting the live login session…" indefinitely: no error written,
the row left reading `authenticating` forever, and the operator staring at a frozen word. Same shape
as §19.41 (`empty_ok` recording a broken filter as a successful zero-row run) and the owner's own
2026-09-20 directive — **a status that cannot say a session died is not a record of what it did.**

### COMMCALC-10.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

- **`live_login._IDLE_CLOSE_SECONDS` / `_HUMAN_ACTION_IDLE_SECONDS`** — the OPERATOR-inactivity rule.
  **EXTENDED, not forked**: its inline conditional became `inactivity_limit(phase)`, same answers.
  Widening it to cover `starting` was rejected — it would silently shorten the human's 20-minute
  window for fetching a 2FA code, which is the one place a long wait is CORRECT.
- **`_TERMINAL_TTL` / `_prune_locked`** — drops FINISHED sessions. A different question (how long to
  keep a corpse), and it never fires on a session that never finishes. Untouched.
- **`portal_session_health` / `portal_backoff`** — the DURABLE session's condition and the portal's
  cooldown. Neither watches a live interactive session. Untouched.
- **`job-run.ts` `POLL_GIVE_UP_MS` (§6q)** — the FRONTEND's "we stopped watching". Deliberately not
  reused: a page giving up on polling must not be what ends a server-side session, and the row has to
  be told either way. The two are complementary, not duplicates.
- No new table, no new column, no migration.

### COMMCALC-10.2 One fact, one home, dereferenced

Two different questions, each with exactly one home and one reader:

| question | home | reader | answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| no progress, **before** the command loop | `PRELOOP_PROGRESS_LIMIT_S` + `PRELOOP_PROGRESS_DEFAULT_S` | `preloop_limit(phase)` | `starting` 180s; everything else 600s |
| waiting on the **operator**, inside it | `_IDLE_CLOSE_SECONDS` / `_HUMAN_ACTION_IDLE_SECONDS` | `inactivity_limit(phase)` | `human_action` 8 min; else 20 min |

An **undeclared phase takes the default**, which is the whole point: "unlisted" must never mean "may
hang forever", and that is exactly what the pre-change shape meant. The budgets are generous against
the real worst cases they must not kill — `_launch` tries real Chrome then bundled Chromium (~30s
Playwright launch timeout each), and `_goto_login` can spend two ladders of 3 × 60s `_goto_with_retry`
plus settles, which is where the ~7-minute figure comes from. Every phase change **restarts that
phase's clock**; re-setting the SAME phase does not, so a chatty message cannot refresh the budget
forever. The phase clock is distinct from `_last_activity` (which a frame or a keystroke also
touches).

### COMMCALC-10.3 The watchdog is a SECOND thread, and it ends the session rather than the call

The worker thread cannot time itself out: a blocked `p.chromium.launch()` or `page.goto()` never
returns to look at a clock, which is precisely why `starting` could sit forever. Playwright offers no
way to interrupt that call, so `LiveLoginSession._watch` does not try to kill it — it sets
`phase="error"`, calls `_persist_diag()` (so the row flips from `authenticating` to `error` with the
reason, instead of lying), and returns; the stuck call dies with its daemon thread. It **stands down**
the moment `_loop_entered` is set by `_preauth_loop` / `_post_auth_loop`, so no operator window is
ever shortened — the one regression this fix must not cause. The message names what the session was
DOING in the operator's words (`_PRELOOP_DOING`: "opening a browser on the server", "loading the
portal's sign-in page", "waiting for the portal to accept the sign-in"), never a phase slug.

### COMMCALC-10.4 The sibling found while tracing — the bot-wall fallback named the WRONG VENDOR

`vidapay_sweep._goto_login` is the pre-auth navigator **every** portal connector uses, and its
bot-wall retry destination was the module constant `LOGIN_URL` — the master-agent portal's own
id-server. So a `pos_report` or `supply_vendor` login that hit a bot wall retried at a **different
vendor's login server**, spending up to three 60-second attempts on an address with nothing to do
with the portal the operator configured. One vendor's URL reached through a shared path by every
other vendor's connector is the RULE TWO defect wearing a hat.

`_goto_login` now takes `login_url`, defaulting to this module's own constant only because this
module's two entry points ARE that portal; both of them now name it explicitly. `live_login`
dereferences `_preauth_login_url`, which answers from the connector: the master-agent family
(`_VIDAPAY_PROCESSORS`) → its id-server, the POS-reports portal family (`_B2B_PROCESSORS`) → its own
base, and **None for a connector KIND whose address is per-tenant config** — `connector_registry`
carries no host for those rows by design (§12a.2a), so there is no house default to fall back to and
`login_url=None` SKIPS the fallback rather than guessing. The caller then reports "could not find the
login form" against the page the operator actually configured, which is the honest answer.

### COMMCALC-10.5 The lock

`backend/harness_live_login_progress.py` — **64 checks**, DB-free, no browser, no network (a
`_FakeVp` whose hosts are deliberately NOT the real ones, so a check cannot pass by testing the
constants instead of the branch). §A one home each + an undeclared phase takes the default; §B the
operator's windows byte-for-byte unchanged; §C the budgets clear the real worst cases; §D the phase
clock and its restart rule; §E the watchdog is a second daemon thread spelling no budget of its own;
§F a stalled session becomes terminal AND the row is told, in plain words; §G it stands down on
`_loop_entered`; §H controls; §I the fallback belongs to the portal it is for.

**Proved red on the state `main` was in**, three ways: `PRELOOP_PROGRESS_LIMIT_S` emptied with no
default → 4 fail (`preloop_limit` answers `None`, i.e. no limit); the inline conditional restored in
`_preauth_loop` → 2 fail (two homes again); the watchdog thread removed from `start()` → 2 fail. And
for §COMMCALC-10.4, the call site reverted to passing nothing → **8 fail**, including *"ARMED: the
pre-change shape (inheriting the master-agent id-server) is RED"*.

### COMMCALC-10.6 Cross-references

- **§16 (by TABLE):** `commcalc.data_source` — `auth_status` / `auth_message` can no longer stay at
  `authenticating` / "Live login in progress…" after a live session dies; `_persist_diag` is the one
  writer of that stop.
- **§17 (by FUNCTION):** `live_login.preloop_limit` / `inactivity_limit` / `_watch` /
  `_preauth_login_url`, `LiveLoginSession._phase_since` / `_loop_entered`;
  `vidapay_sweep._goto_login(login_url=)`.
- **§18 (by QUESTION):** "How long may a live portal login sit in this phase before it is dead?" →
  `live_login.preloop_limit` (no progress) / `inactivity_limit` (waiting on the operator) — two
  questions, one home each, never merged. "Where does a bot-walled portal login retry?" →
  `live_login._preauth_login_url`, never a module constant.
- **Same class:** §19.41 (`empty_ok` recorded a broken filter as success — a status that is not a
  record), §12a.2a (the connector this surfaced on), §6q (the UI treating "accepted" as "finished"),
  §66 (a value read without its basis), §19.18 (a mechanism written, callers unwired).
