## §CORE-12. A WRITE MAY NOT SHUT THE DOOR ON ITS OWN AUTHOR — one self-lockout home (owner report 2026-10-16)

Owner: *"i made my self market manager under vzone and cannot get admin privilidges anymore under
ss, fix urgently"*.

### CORE-12.1 THE INSTANCE, AND THE CLASS BEHIND IT

The `ss@1313global.us` login holds FOUR memberships, one per tenant (`storeops.app_users` is keyed
per `(auth_id, org_id)` since mig 706), three of them `admin`. Its **Vzone** membership was moved to
`market_manager` through `POST /core/users/assign`. Vzone's Market Manager role carries
`modules.admin: false` and `scope: 'market'`, and that login holds no `super_admin` flag on any row,
so after the write **no screen inside Vzone could undo it and no other tenant could reach in**. A
hand-written `UPDATE` in the database was the only way back.

The class is not "market manager" and not "Vzone". Every role / membership / role-permission write
in `core/router.py` gates on `_can_edit_setting(caller, 'security')` and then writes **whatever it
was asked to write — including the row or the role that answer was computed from**. The house
already refused three INSTANCES of exactly that question, each inline and each unaware of the
others:

| already there | what it protects |
|---|---|
| `PUT /core/auth-config` — "no active user has the Admin role" | the TENANT, at enforcement time |
| `POST /core/revoke-super-admin` — "cannot remove the last platform super-admin" | the PLATFORM |
| `DELETE /core/roles/{id}` — "The admin role can't be deleted." | the TENANT's role catalog |

None of them asked it about the CALLER, which is the instance that actually happened.

### CORE-12.2 THE FIX — one home, asked by every writer

`backend/app/modules/core/self_lockout.py` (pure, stdlib only) answers **"would this write take away
the authority that just made it?"**: it computes `can_edit_setting` for the affected tenant BEFORE
and AFTER the proposed write and refuses only when the answer flips `True -> False`.

**The authority answer moved INTO that home.** `_can_edit_setting` was `core/router.py`'s private
function; the router now dereferences `self_lockout.can_edit_setting` and defines nothing. A copy
would be the divergence the owner's design-fix directive forbids — a guard asking a different
question than the gate protects a different door.

What it therefore does NOT refuse, by construction:

- demoting **somebody else**, whatever it does to them;
- a caller who **never had** the authority (the gate already refused them);
- demoting yourself while the authority survives another way — a `super_admin` flag on any
  membership, or an explicit `settings.security` grant on the new role;
- narrowing the role literally **named `admin`**, because the name is itself a rung of
  `can_edit_setting` — the guard agrees with the gate rather than out-guessing it.

### CORE-12.3 EVERY DOOR, NOT THE ONE THAT WAS REPORTED

The same question is asked by all seven writers of authority in the module, and the subject set is
DERIVED from the router source by the lock, so a new writer joins it by existing:

| writer | the door it could shut |
|---|---|
| `POST /core/users/assign` | the reported instance — your own membership's role or `is_active` |
| `POST /core/users/bulk-assign` | the same, from a spreadsheet (non-raising: the row fails, the sheet applies) |
| `POST /core/roles` | an UPSERT on `(org_id, name)`, so it rewrites an existing role's permissions |
| `PUT /core/roles/{id}` | your own role's permissions |
| `POST /core/users/deactivate` | a login switched off cannot sign in to switch itself back on |
| `POST /core/revoke-super-admin` | your own platform flag, where the role behind it does not carry the authority |
| `purge_app_user` (`POST /core/employees/purge`, StoreOps employee delete / merge) | the row deleted outright — the bluntest form of the same door. The two roster callers now hand over the caller's token so the one home can refuse |

EXCUSED, by name and with the reason (pinned by §D of the lock, so an excuse cannot become an
oversight): `_provision_tenant`, `create_super_admin`, `reinstate_login`, `bulk_provision` (each can
only ADD authority) and `disable_and_switch` (the user's own deliberate hand-over, which mints the
replacement login FIRST). `reset_tenant_admin_password`, `set_2fa_settings` and `verify_phone` are
not in the subject set at all — they write a password, a 2FA channel and a phone, never a role.

### CORE-12.4 THE LOCK

`backend/harness_self_lockout.py` — 45 checks, DB-free: §A reproduces the instance on the real
membership shape and Vzone's real role permissions (before `True`, after `False`), §B the decision
table including everything deliberately NOT refused, §C every authority writer dereferences the
guard **and** `can_edit_setting` has no second copy anywhere under `backend/app`, §D the excused
writers named, §E five armed negative controls. Runs in CI as the job **A write may not lock out its
own author** (`.github/workflows/org-scope-guard.yml`).

Neighbours: §CORE-07 (the login/person link, the other `app_users` write-path fix), §38.6 (the two
platform-authority rungs), §14w (people visibility — the other question answered off a role row).


## §CORE-14. ONE PALETTE, DEREFERENCED — the side menu's alternating colour (owner ask 2026-10-19)

Owner, verbatim: *"make the colors of the side menu alternate and different colors swicth between
logo colors so it stands out and it can show the different items on teh menu"*.

### §CORE-14.1 DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate)

Searched this index for an existing mechanism that colours, themes or labels the sidebar rows before
building anything. What exists and was NOT duplicated:

| Found | What it owns | Why it is not this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(platform)/layout.tsx` + `.mp-*` in `globals.css` (§W2.1) | the sidebar's structure and its hover/active STATES | extended in place — no second nav component, no second stylesheet |
| `/admin/menu` nav layout, `/admin/labels` (`navCfg.labels`) | what the rows are CALLED and in which group/order | a different fact; untouched |
| §23q white-on-near-white | a table-cell contrast defect | same *class* of risk (colour costing legibility), which is why the contrast bar here is computed, not eyeballed |
| `TrendChart.TREND_COLORS` | the chart series palette | a chart is not the chrome; the nav palette is declared where the nav is styled |

### §CORE-14.2 THE MECHANISM

One fact — *which colour is slot N* — with one home, dereferenced by every caller:

| Link | Where |
| --- | --- |
| the palette (ONE home) | `frontend/src/app/globals.css` → `.mp-sidebar { --nav-accent-1 … --nav-accent-6 }`, every value a light variant of a colour the brand already uses (`--accent` / `--accent2` logo blues, `--green`, `--amber`, `--red`, the chart violet) |
| the rotation | `(platform)/layout.tsx` → `accentStyle(i)` sets `--mp-accent: var(--nav-accent-N)`; it names **no colour**, so a colour cannot be changed in two places |
| how many slots | `NAV_ACCENT_SLOTS` in `layout.tsx`, asserted **equal** to the count declared in the CSS |
| what carries the colour | a painted CHIP behind the row's icon (full accent strength), a 3px left edge bar, and a label mixed 85% toward the accent from white |
| the ACTIVE row | the only row with a filled background (26%), a 3px full-strength bar and pure-white bold text |
| the index a row gets | its position in its OWN group's render order (loose items, then each sub), so neighbours never share a colour and a row keeps its colour whatever else is open |

**Why the chip, and not the glyph.** The first attempt tinted the icon with `color` and the owner
reported *"i cold see any difference"*. The nav's icons are EMOJI (`NAV` carries 🏪, 🛒, 📦 …) and an
emoji is painted from its own font's colour table, so `color` does nothing to it; with a 40% label
tint as the only other signal, the change was invisible on the navy rail. The colour has to be a
painted BOX, so the icon chip is what carries it — and the lesson generalises: **a colour applied to
an emoji is not applied at all.**

Readability is a computed property, not a judgement: every slot's label clears **WCAG AA 4.5:1** on
both ends of the navy gradient in all three states (measured 5.0:1 – 7.4:1 resting), and every chip
stands at least 3:1 off the rail. The coloured rules sit
inside `@supports (color: color-mix(…))`, with the old white-on-navy declarations still above them, so
a browser without `color-mix()` keeps today's nav rather than rendering something broken.

### §CORE-14.3 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

| Lock | What fails the build |
| --- | --- |
| `frontend/prove_nav_accents.mjs` (**67 checks**, CI job *Sidebar colour proof*) | reads the REAL `globals.css` and `layout.tsx`: the palette is declared once with contiguous slots; `NAV_ACCENT_SLOTS` equals that count; the rows dereference `var(--nav-accent-N)` and spell no colour; neighbours never share a slot, and consecutive slots are at least **90° apart in HUE** so the alternation is visible and not merely numbered; the icon chip is a painted BOX with a size of its own and **not** a `color` on the glyph (the invisible-change regression); **per-slot contrast computed** for resting / hover / active, the chip's standoff from the rail, and the active row's filled background and thicker bar; the `@supports` fallback is intact; §H for the headings — every group and every report category declares an icon, `groupIcon` answers from the declaration, the fallback covers a tenant-created group, `applyNavLayout` carries the icon through (driven against the REAL `rbac.ts`), and the heading is bolder, larger, left-aligned and contrast-checked per slot; nine negative controls (a gap in the palette, a count disagreement, a literal colour, a label with no white left, a tinted chip, two adjacent rows sharing a slot, a one-colour palette, two slots a shade apart in one hue) |

### §CORE-14.5 THE GROUP HEADINGS (owner ask 2026-10-21)

Owner, with the rows already live: *"side menu looks good when clicked on the first label but the look
of the first label like CRM .POS , finance etc needs to be in bolder and with different colors and
favicon"*. The headings had stayed 9.5px, weight 700, flat `rgba(255,255,255,0.4)` — the one part of
the rail the colour had not reached.

| Link | Where |
| --- | --- |
| which icon a group has (ONE home) | `rbac.groupIcon(group)`, DERIVED from the declarations — `NavGroup.icon` on every built-in group and `icon` on every `REPORT_CATEGORIES` row — with `GROUP_ICON_FALLBACK` for a group a tenant created at `/admin/menu`, which declares nothing |
| how it survives the tenant layout | `applyNavLayout` rebuilds every group by NAME, so it returns `icon: groupIcon(group)` rather than carrying the input object's field; an item moved into another group, a tenant group and a Reports category all resolve the same way |
| the heading's colour | the SAME `--mp-accent` rotation as the rows, keyed by the group's index, at the same 85% mix — a heading differs from its rows by **weight and size**, not by a palette of its own |
| the look | 11px / weight 800 (was 9.5px / 700), the icon in a 21px slot so a heading and its rows share one left edge, and `text-align: left` because a `<button>` would otherwise centre the label now that it is the flexible child |

Every heading colour is computed against the rail exactly as the rows are (5.0:1 – 7.4:1). The
sidebar spells **no icon of its own**: it renders what the nav hands it, which is why a group that
nobody declared gets a folder rather than a gap where its neighbours have an icon.

### §CORE-14.6 TWO COLOURS, NOT SIX (owner ask 2026-10-26)

Owner, with the six-colour rotation live: *"too many colors just stick to 2 colors blue and orange
alternating"*.

Nothing about the mechanism changed, which is the point of §CORE-14.2: the palette is the ONE home
and the cycle length is **derived from its size**, so the whole ask is two lines — the list goes from
six entries to two (`--nav-accent-1: #60a5fa` logo blue, `--nav-accent-2: #fb923c` orange) and
`NAV_ACCENT_SLOTS` follows it from 6 to 2. No row, no heading and no stylesheet rule names a colour,
so none of them needed touching, and with two slots the rotation IS a strict alternation.

**The class the new lock answers.** "Two colours" decays in one specific way: a later change adds a
second *blue*. It alternates by slot number and not to the eye, and the old checks would all have
passed it — "no two adjacent rows share a slot" is about slot numbers, not about colour. So the
alternation bar is now a HUE distance: consecutive slots must sit **at least 90° apart on the colour
wheel**, computed from the real declared values (the shipped pair is **174° apart**, nearly
opposite), with a negative control that the two logo blues `#60a5fa` / `#38bdf8` are rejected.
Both colours re-clear the contrast bars unchanged (resting label 5.26:1 and 5.73:1 on the navy).

The retired green, amber, pink and violet slots were nav-only values; no other surface dereferenced
them (checked across `src/`), so nothing else restates or loses a colour.

### §CORE-14.4 WHAT IS NOT DONE HERE

The **operator console** (`(operator)/operator/layout.tsx`) has its own internal rail on its own `OPS`
palette and is deliberately untouched — it is not the tenant app's side menu the owner is looking at,
and giving it this palette would make an internal console look like the product. It is excused, not
forgotten.

Files: `frontend/src/app/globals.css`, `frontend/src/app/(platform)/layout.tsx`,
`frontend/prove_nav_accents.mjs` (**new**), `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml`.

## §CORE-15. THE DARK THEME — one home for what a colour BECOMES (owner ask 2026-10-21)

Owner, shown a rendered mock-up of the workspace on black: *"convert to black looks very impressive"*.

### §CORE-15.1 DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate)

Searched the index and the frontend for an existing theme mechanism before building. There is one, and
it is **extended rather than duplicated**: `components/RunbookDoc.tsx` already switches on
`:root[data-theme="dark"]`, so that attribute is the app's switch here too — no second mechanism, no
second attribute, no `prefers-color-scheme` fork competing with it. The chrome tokens at the top of
`globals.css` (§CORE-01) are likewise **redefined**, not joined by a parallel dark set; the nav accent
palette (§CORE-14) is untouched.

### §CORE-15.2 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

The instance is "the page background is white". The class is that **a colour the app paints is not
always reachable from a stylesheet**: 377 page files carry ~5,200 colour LITERALS inside inline
`style={{…}}` props, and an inline style beats every rule short of `!important`. A dark theme that only
restates the chrome tokens therefore leaves pale alert tints, status inks and hairlines glowing on
black — each one a separate little patch waiting to be made, which is the patchwork the house forbids.

So **the literal itself becomes a dereference**. `frontend/theme_palette.mjs` is the ONE home for *what
does this colour become on the dark theme*:

- Each `(role, colour)` pair is a token, `--c-bg-<hex>` / `--c-fg-<hex>`, declared in `:root` **as its
  own literal** — which is why the light theme is byte-identical **by construction**, not by eye — and
  redefined under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` as the derivation.
- **The role is part of the fact, not a property of the value.** `#fff` is a white panel 20 times and
  the white LETTERING on a coloured button 92 times; the dark theme must darken the first and leave the
  second alone. The role is read from the CSS property at the call site against two DECLARED lists.
  Guessing it from lightness was measured first and rejected: on the 4,275 sites that do name their
  property it gets the fills right only 70% of the time.
- **The token list is derived from the callers**, not hand-kept: the generator takes the union of the
  literals still spelled and the tokens the pages read, so it is idempotent and a colour nobody uses
  any more leaves the stylesheet on the next run.
- The derivation keeps the **hue** and mirrors the **lightness band**, because what a pale tint and a
  dark ink are FOR swaps when the page goes black. A fill above L 0.60 was built to carry dark text and
  comes down to carry light text; a colour already dark is left alone, so `#000` stays `#000` rather
  than inverting to near-white.
- `frontend/src/lib/theme.ts` is the ONE home for the switch: the attribute, the storage key, the two
  themes, the default (**dark**, as asked) and the pre-paint script. Nothing else in the app spells
  `data-theme` or the storage key, so the script, the toggle and the lock cannot disagree. The theme is
  applied **before the first paint** — left to an effect it would paint white and then repaint.
- `ThemeToggle` in the rail is the way back to the light app, remembered per person.

### §CORE-15.3 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

`frontend/prove_theme_tokens.mjs`, CI job **Dark theme lock**, 33 checks: the stylesheet is exactly
what the generator produces (a hand edit fails the build); no literal remains on a property whose role
is declared; every token a page reads is defined for **both** themes and every defined token is read;
every lettering colour clears WCAG AA against the page AND against a card; every fill the derivation
moved can carry white lettering and every fill it left alone was already dark; only `lib/theme.ts`
spells the switch; plus negative controls, including the one the type checker caught — `c.lamp !==
'green'` is a STATUS, so a colour KEYWORD is converted only directly after a property colon.

### §CORE-15.4 WHAT IS NOT DONE HERE

**833 colour literals in 173 files sit on a property that names no role** — local map keys such as
`status:`, `accent:`, `tone:`, `COLORS:`, where the colour's job is decided where the map is consumed.
They are NOT converted, because a role this code guessed would be a role nobody could check. They are
**pinned** in `frontend/theme_ambiguous_pin.txt` and the pin may only shrink. **169 of them are pale
enough to read as a light patch on black**, in 72 files; 18 of those are RunbookDoc's own `--rb-*`
declarations, which already carry a dark variant of their own. That is the measured remainder, stated
rather than hidden, and the next pass at it is a shrink of the pin.

The **operator console** keeps its own palette, as in §CORE-14.4. The **rail** keeps its navy on both
themes: it was the one surface already dark, and restating it would both cost the edge that separates
the menu from the page and restate the accent contrast §CORE-14 measured against that gradient.

Files: `frontend/theme_palette.mjs` (**new**), `frontend/prove_theme_tokens.mjs` (**new**),
`frontend/theme_ambiguous_pin.txt` (**new**), `frontend/src/lib/theme.ts` (**new**),
`frontend/src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx` (**new**), `frontend/src/app/globals.css`,
`frontend/src/app/layout.tsx`, `frontend/src/app/(platform)/layout.tsx`, 371 page/component files
(mechanical dereference), `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml`.

## §COMMCALC-11. AN INVISIBLE HUMAN CHECK IS STILL A CHECK (owner report 2026-10-15)

Owner, in his own words, after declaring the UPS reporting-portal login: *"it has been over 5 minutes
it is startying teh love login and does not move freom tehre"*. §COMMCALC-10 made that silence
audible. This section is what the audible failure then revealed: the sign-in was **not** failing on
the credentials, and the platform could not tell.

**THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE.** A human check was recognised by whether it was **PAINTED**, not by
whether it **GATES THE SUBMIT**. `vidapay_sweep._looks_like_captcha` held the right selector list —
`.g-recaptcha` was in it — and then asked `el.is_visible()`. Google's documented invisible-reCAPTCHA
setup renders the widget `data-size="invisible"` (deliberately 0×0) and posts the form only from its
`data-callback`, so the widget is present, armed, and gating — and invisible. It read as *no check*.
The live session therefore took its fast path and **auto-submitted past exactly the check its own
comment says it must never auto-submit past**; the portal refused the post, the page stayed on the
form, and the caller reported *"Login was rejected — Account ID / User ID / Password not accepted"*.
A correct password was reported as a wrong one. Same shape as §19.41: **a detector that cannot see a
state is not a record of that state.**

Measured on the real page, 2026-10-15: `renderCaptcha = 'True'`, one `div.g-recaptcha` with
`data-sitekey`, `data-size="invisible"` and `data-callback="captchaSuccessCallback"`. Ruled out and
recorded so nobody re-derives them — the portal answers a datacenter IP in ~1s and redirects cleanly
to its sign-in page (**no IP block, no bot wall, so no proxy is needed**), the form is Username +
Password only (an **empty** account id is correct for it), and the deep report URL 302s to sign-in
rather than erroring.

### COMMCALC-11.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

- **`_looks_like_captcha` / `_CAPTCHA_SELECTORS` / `_CAPTCHA_TEXT`** — the existing detector.
  **EXTENDED, not forked**: `human_check(page)` is now the one reader, and `_looks_like_captcha` is a
  boolean wrapper over it, so every existing caller sees the invisible case through the same code.
- **`live_login._captcha_present`** — the live session's own wrapper. Also kept as a wrapper over the
  new `_human_check_kind`, because the scratchpad proof scripts call it by name.
- **`_wall_note` / the bot-wall detectors** — a different question ("is this an anti-automation
  BLOCK page"), not "does a check gate this form". Untouched.
- **The §COMMCALC-10 watchdog** — makes a stall visible; it does not say why. Complementary.
- No new table, no new column, **no migration**, no new endpoint, no new report — so nothing to add
  to §16, §17 or §18.

### COMMCALC-11.2 One fact, one home, dereferenced

| question | home | reader |
|---|---|---|
| does a human check gate this page, and of which kind? | `vidapay_sweep._CAPTCHA_SELECTORS` + `_CAPTCHA_TEXT` + `_INVISIBLE_MARK` / `_ARMED_MARK` | `vidapay_sweep.human_check(page)` → `"visible"` / `"invisible"` / `""` |
| what do we TELL the operator, per kind? | `live_login._HUMAN_CHECK_MESSAGE` | `live_login._human_check_kind(vp, page)` |
| why was a submit refused while still on the form? | `vidapay_sweep._HUMAN_CHECK_BLOCKED` | `vidapay_sweep.human_check_blocked_message(page)` |

**Three states, not a bool, because the two kinds need different words.** A visible challenge is on
the screen in front of the operator. An invisible one appears only once **Sign in is pressed** — so
"complete the box on the screen" would send them hunting for something that is not there yet. Both
stop an automatic submit.

**Visible, or ARMED — not merely rendered.** A bare reCAPTCHA v3 `api.js` include needs no human and
renders no widget element, so the element selectors already exclude it. A widget element that is
neither visible nor carrying a `data-callback` is deliberately left as **not** a check: pushing every
portal login into `human_action` would stop the carrier feeds that pay commission from signing in
unattended.

### COMMCALC-11.3 The siblings, fixed in the same change rather than excused

"Still on the login form" has **two** causes that send the operator to opposite places: a bad
credential, or a human check that silently refused the post. Both post-submit sites blamed the
credential, and both are the same question, so both now dereference
`human_check_blocked_message(page)` **before** wording the failure:

- `vidapay_sweep.begin_login` — the master-agent portal family.
- `vidapay_sweep.begin_login_b2bsoft` — the POS-reports portal family. **This is the path the owner
  hit**, and fixing only it would have been the patchwork the house forbids.

Each falls back to its own existing wording when no check gates the page, so a page this cannot
inspect is never given an invented cause.

### COMMCALC-11.4 Locked so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_human_check_kind.py` — **45 checks**, DB-free, no browser, no network, loaded by
`importlib` so it runs in CI's bare Python. §A the three states and their one home · §B the two marks
are declared, never spelled at a call site · §C the operator's words live in `_HUMAN_CHECK_MESSAGE`
and nowhere else · §D a widget that is neither visible nor armed stays *not a check* · §E **both**
post-submit siblings ask the human-check question before blaming the credentials, through the same
home · §F `_drive` reads the message from the one home, with none inlined · §G controls, including the
owner's real widget attributes carried verbatim as a fixture.

Wired into `carrier-vocab-guard.yml` as *"human-check lock"*, with `harness_human_check_kind.py` and
`live_login.py` in the paths filter beside `vidapay_sweep.py`.

**Proved red on the pre-change shape:** the visibility-only rule **misses** the owner's real widget
(§G, armed as a control so it can never silently start passing); restoring main's shape at the two
sibling sites and inlining the message again fails **5** checks, naming `begin_login`,
`begin_login_b2bsoft` and the inlined wording.

### COMMCALC-11.5 Cross-references

Same class: §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers left unwired), §19.41 (a status that cannot
record a failure is not a record), §COMMCALC-10 (the stall this made visible), §12a.2a (a connector
kind carries no host, so its address is per-tenant config), §CORE-03 (where the portal credential is
sealed), §COMMCALC-07 (the pull loop this login feeds).

## §COMMCALC-12. WHICH STORE'S TRAILING COMMISSION LEGS ARE RUNNING DOWN, AND IN WHICH RUNG (owner ask 2026-10-15)

Owner, verbatim, in the Store Takeover thread, on a prospect table that put the month-of-life rungs
side by side for two months: *"this is a good insight , this means we need to see these numbers as a
report sisde by sie as shown above for each store to analyze , create one"*.

**What the insight was.** On that prospect, **96% of a 41% fall in carrier commission was M2–M5
trailing legs** paying on an activation cohort that had collapsed (Activation Order lines 1,386 Jul →
787 Aug → 557 Sep). The fall was not this month's selling; it was the echo of a cohort lost months
earlier. **Per store, the same shape separates two different businesses**: a store whose M1 is falling
is shrinking NOW; a store whose M1 holds while M4–M6 fall lost its cohort four to six months ago. The
rung is the only place that difference is visible, and until this the ladder could be read across
months (company-wide) or per store (one month at a time) — never both.

### COMMCALC-12.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Checked, and the answer is that NOTHING new computes money here.

| already exists | what it answers | what this did |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gp_report.calc_gp_report` → `comm_ladder` + `comm_month_<n>` on every store row; the GP page's 📅 Months toggle and "Commission by month-of-life" card (§4a.2) | per-store rungs, ONE month at a time | **not touched, not re-derived** — a different read of a different grain |
| `GET /commcalc/commission-leg-trend` (`router._commission_leg_trend_compute`) | the ladder ACROSS months, company-wide, with `market` / `store` FILTERS but no store AXIS | **EXTENDED**: its compute now accumulates a `by_store` grain in the SAME pass over the SAME rows |
| `commcalc/commission_legs` — `ladder_key` / `ladder_sort_key` / `months_present` / `ladder_column` / `ladder_label` | which rungs exist, what they are called, in what order | **dereferenced**; no second convention, no month count |
| `router._leg_store_index` → `account/store_identity` (§64) | which store a carrier line belongs to | **dereferenced**; no street-number token |
| `carrier_dollar_class` (§58) + `component_is_evidence` (§66) | which dollar is commission | **dereferenced**; the trend already resolves them once per request |
| `account/ma_store_pnl.canonical_store_index` (mig `314`) | processor account → store | **dereferenced** for the MA grain |

The new file is **`backend/app/modules/commcalc/commission_leg_store_trend.py`**, and it is a PURE
PIVOT: it reshapes the trend's output store-major and derives the plain-English "running down"
read-out. It computes no money. This is §4c's precedent (*a multi-month P&L loops THE single-month
read; it computes no line*) applied to the leg trend: **one money path, two shapes.** §A of the lock
fails the build the moment Σ(per-store) stops equalling the company figure to the cent.

### COMMCALC-12.2 The blocker the index named was in the wrong place — and NO migration was needed

Index line ~1227 said: *"the reason this rollup cannot filter by store is that
`commission_leg_ma_rollup` aggregates per period WITHOUT the account column."* **That diagnosis was
right and the remedy was being looked for in the wrong object.** Established here, plainly:

- **`commcalc.commission_leg_label_rollup` (mig `274`, superseded by mig `1066`) CAN carry the store
  key, and already does** — mig 1066 made it return the BTRIMMED RAW ADDRESS the feed carried, which
  the backend resolves through §64. Verified live 2026-10-15 against production: the RPC returns
  `store_num` as a full address (`"1 S 60th St Philadelphia, PA 19139"`), 3,717 rows over two months,
  **28 distinct stores**. So the ePay Payment Detail and Comprehensive Comp sides — the entire
  commission series for the acting org — are store-grained with **no schema change at all**.
- **`commcalc.commission_leg_ma_rollup` (mig `274`) CANNOT** — it is `GROUP BY 1` on `period` and the
  account column is not in its `RETURNS TABLE`. But **it is a PRE-AGGREGATION of rows that DO carry
  the account** (`raw_ma_commission.merchant_account_id`, the column
  `data_lineage_registry.store_account_column` already names). The store grain therefore needed the
  **ROWS**, not a changed RPC: the window's rows are read once (paged, §19.48), grouped per
  (period, resolved store), and bucketed with the SAME `legcls.ma` over the SAME `_MA_LEG_COMPONENTS`
  list the per-period path uses. Because `split_ma_components` is **LINEAR in the component sums**,
  Σ(per-store buckets) == the per-period rollup's buckets to the cent — the grain is strictly finer
  and the money cannot move. §B of the lock proves exactly that equality.
**VERIFIED LIVE, 2026-10-15, on the tenant that actually has MA rows** (3,981 rows carrying
`merchant_account_id`; the acting org has none, so this path is only exercised there). Σ(per-store)
against `commission_leg_ma_rollup`'s own per-period figure, four months, computed by calling both:

| period | period rollup | Σ per-store | gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| June 2026 | $60,034.62 | $60,034.62 | **$0.00** |
| July 2026 | $124,043.34 | $124,043.34 | **$0.00** |
| August 2026 | $241,853.82 | $241,853.82 | **$0.00** |
| September 2026 | $229,148.87 | $229,148.87 | **$0.00** |

**20 stores, every processor account resolved** (no `(No store matched)` row), `all_ties` true on
every month. This is precisely the money the index said this rollup could not split by store.

- **Therefore: NO migration ships with this, and none is waiting.** The schema is untouched.

**This fixed the CLASS, not the instance.** The note above was not only a gap in the new report: the
existing `market` / `store` FILTER on `/commission-leg-trend` SILENTLY EXCLUDED all MA money and
merely apologised in `notes`. Both callers of the same missing fact are fixed by the same change, and
the apology now fires only when the rows genuinely cannot be read.

### COMMCALC-12.3 Honesty rules that ARE the report

1. **A partial month is marked and never an endpoint.** The window ends on the page's own period,
   normally the CURRENT calendar month. Read on 2026-10-15, the house org's October was running at
   roughly a quarter of September — as an endpoint it would have reported **all 28 stores collapsing
   at once**. `partial_months` names it from the caller's clock, the money is still SHOWN, and every
   derived delta uses the first and last COMPLETE month instead.
2. **Money matching no store is its own named row** (`(No store matched)`), sorted last, never spread
   over the stores and never dropped. Its presence is a mapping finding.
3. **A negative rung keeps its sign.** Carrier withholding lands in whichever rung its label states;
   nothing is flipped to make a store look better.
4. **Arithmetic that would lie is refused.** A $0 baseline yields `pct` `None` — never 0, never
   infinity. A store the window sees in one complete month gets `delta` `None`, not 0.
5. **A gap is reported.** `ties_to` states, per month, whether the displayed all-stores total equals
   the trend's company total, with both figures and the gap.
6. **The rungs come from the DATA.** An M13 is a column the day it arrives; a rung a store has no
   money in reads $0.00, not a hole; a rung nobody has is not invented.

### COMMCALC-12.4 Live finding, 2026-10-15 (read-only, acting org, the endpoint's own output)

Measured by calling `commission_leg_store_trend` itself, `period=October 2026&months=6`. **28 stores,
`all_ties` true on every month** (the store axis places every dollar the company series carries; no
`(No store matched)` row exists for this org), October correctly flagged partial and excluded from
every Δ.

**Company, May → September 2026 (complete months): −$25,534.27, −19.4%. Only −3.7% of that is M1.**
M2–M12 is **−17.9%** and the Unlabelled rung is **−50.6%** ($15,126.55 → $7,477.85). So the owner's
prospect insight holds for our own stores: the fall is the trailing legs and the unlabelled bucket, not
this month's selling.

**And per store it separates into two different problems**, which is the whole point of the rung axis:

## §COMMCALC-13. A FINISHED LIVE LOGIN LEAVES AN HONEST STATUS (found 2026-10-15)

Found while reading the owner's live row back to him, not reported by him — which is the point: his
screen said a login was in progress and he had no way to know it was not.

**THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE.** *A status is a record of what IS.* `router.live_login_start` stamps
`auth_status='authenticating'` / "Live login in progress…" before the worker starts, which is true
while the worker runs. §COMMCALC-10 taught a session that **dies** to write `'error'`. But a session
that merely **ends** — the inactivity timeout, or the operator pressing Close — wrote only
`auth_message` and left the status in flight. `_persist_diag` is the ONE place that writes a terminal
status and it wrote one for only ONE of its two terminal phases. The chip on
`commcalc/email-imports` (`authBadge`) maps `authenticating` to "⏳ Logging in…", so the row read
*"Live session closed after inactivity."* and *"Logging in…"* at the same time, for an hour.

Measured read-only on the live `pos_report` row, 2026-10-15 04:31Z: `auth_status='authenticating'`,
`auth_message='Live session closed after inactivity.'`, `pending_started_at=03:27:13Z`,
`session_state` empty. The session had been gone for 64 minutes.

### COMMCALC-13.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

- **§COMMCALC-10's `PRELOOP_PROGRESS_LIMIT_S` / watchdog** — answers "has this phase stopped making
  progress", and writes `'error'`. **EXTENDED, not forked**: that path still owns the row on `error`;
  this change gives the *other* terminal phase an answer too, through the same `_persist_diag`.
- **`_IDLE_CLOSE_SECONDS` / `PRELOOP_PROGRESS_DEFAULT_S`** — "how long may this take". **READ, never
  copied**: `in_flight_stale_after_s()` is one expression over both, so changing either moves the
  staleness budget with it. The lock fails on any three-digit duration spelled inside it.
- **`portal_session_health.evaluate`** — the DURABLE session's health. A different question (is the
  saved session still good), and it already reads `auth_status`, which is why the presenter runs
  **before** it: the chip and the health line must not disagree.
- **`_source_stamp` / `PENDING_TTL_MINUTES`** — the two-call flow's own staleness rule, on
  `pending_state`. Untouched; it gates a different field and a different endpoint.
- No new table, no new column, **no migration**, no new endpoint, no new report.

### COMMCALC-13.2 One fact, one home, dereferenced

| question | home | reader |
|---|---|---|
| what status does a terminal session leave? | `live_login._STATUS_IN_FLIGHT` | `live_login.terminal_status(phase, status_before)` |
| how long may an in-flight claim stand? | `_IDLE_CLOSE_SECONDS` + `PRELOOP_PROGRESS_DEFAULT_S` + `_IN_FLIGHT_STALE_MARGIN_S` | `live_login.in_flight_stale_after_s()` |
| what status should a SURFACE show? | the two above | `live_login.present_auth_status(row)` |

`terminal_status` answers `'error'` for the session's own verdict and otherwise **restores the row's
pre-login status** — captured in `__init__` from the row, which `live_login_start` reads *before* it
stamps over it (the lock pins that order). The one value never restored is `_STATUS_IN_FLIGHT`: a row
already carrying it would be handed the same lie back. It becomes `NULL`, which the chip renders
"○ Not connected" — the honest reading of a login with credentials and no session.

### COMMCALC-13.3 The sibling, fixed here rather than excused

`terminal_status` can only speak for a session that reaches its own end. **A worker killed mid-login
never runs `_persist_diag` at all** — and every merge to `main` redeploys both hosts, so that is
routine here, not exotic. Nothing *on* the row distinguishes that from a login genuinely still
going, so the only honest discriminator is **age**: `in_flight_is_stale` reads an in-flight claim
older than the budget as a leftover, and `present_auth_status` presents it as cleared. Deliberately
conservative — a missing, naive or unparseable timestamp reads as **not** stale, because reading a
LIVE session as finished is the one regression this must not cause.

### COMMCALC-13.4 Locked so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_terminal_status.py` — **49 checks**, DB-free, no network, no browser, loaded by
`importlib`. §A the one home answers for BOTH terminal phases · §B the in-flight status is never
handed back, from any direction or spelling · §C a session that changed nothing leaves the row as it
found it · §D the write happens and nothing is left pending · §E the endpoint still reads the row
before stamping it (armed, because the capture depends on that order) · §F the read side, with the
budget derived not copied · §G the surface dereferences it exactly once, before `session_health`, and
the router holds no copy of the rule · §H controls.

Wired into `carrier-vocab-guard.yml` as *"terminal-status lock"*.

**Proved red on main's shape, two ways:** restoring the `if phase == "error"` write fails **5**
checks; removing the presenter from the row decorator fails **3**.

### COMMCALC-13.5 Cross-references

Same class: §COMMCALC-10 (the phase that could stall forever), §19.41 (`empty_ok` recording a broken
filter as a successful zero-row run), §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers left unwired).
Neighbours: §COMMCALC-11 (why that session could not sign in), §12a (the connector surfaces that read
this row), §CORE-03 (where the credential on it is sealed).

## §COMMCALC-14. A CHEAP ANSWER IS NEVER HELD HOSTAGE BY AN EXPENSIVE DECORATION (found 2026-10-16)

**Owner report 2026-10-16, verbatim:** *"Store Takeover Evaluation takes along time to load , and
existing evaluation is not in the pull up list"*. **One cause, both complaints**, which is why they
are one section.

`GET /commcalc/prospects` (§COMMCALC-03) answers *which stores am I evaluating* — two rows, one
indexed query, milliseconds. It then DECORATED each row with *and how many rows has each feed got in
each month*, and computed that decoration by **shipping every feed row to Python and counting them**.

**Measured live 2026-10-16** (read-only, Supabase REST, acting org):

| | |
|---|---|
| `commcalc.prospect_feed_row`, this org | **202,865** rows (137,374 + 65,491 across two prospects) |
| at the platform's 1,000-row page | **203 round trips** |
| timed from a container, 10 pages | 0.289 s/page → **~59 s** for the count alone |
| behind it | `gunicorn --timeout 120`, **two** workers |
| growth | every upload makes it worse |

So the list the owner came for was **empty for a minute**, which is exactly how a slow count reads as
a missing evaluation — and the same read occupied half the platform's request capacity while it ran,
on a path to being killed outright by the worker timeout as the feed grows. **Both prospects were
present in the table the whole time** (verified: same org, both `evaluating`); nothing was lost.

### COMMCALC-14.1 The class, not the instance

> **A cheap primary answer must never be withheld until an expensive decoration beside it is ready —
> and a count of rows belongs in the database, not in a loop that ships the rows.**

### COMMCALC-14.2 Duplicate check (the build gate)

| already exists | what it answers | what this did |
|---|---|---|
| `core/feed_read.read_all` (§19.48, §CORE-05) | *every row of a feed*, paged on a stable key | **left alone** — it is correct; it was being asked the wrong question |
| `prospect_eval.default_period` (§COMMCALC-03) | which month an evaluation opens on | **dereferenced**, unchanged |
| `router._prospect_feed_rows` | the prospect's rows, for the money | **left alone** — it genuinely needs the rows |
| `_write_upload_trace` (§19.x) | *did this ingest happen* | **deliberately NOT used as the tally** — a log of what an upload did is not a record of what is in the table now, the same reason a sweep's status is not a record of what it swept |

No sibling mechanism answered *how many rows per feed per month*, so this registers one home for it
rather than a second derivation.

### COMMCALC-14.3 One fact, one home, dereferenced

`commcalc/prospect_feed_tally.py` is the one home for the shape

    {prospect_id: {period: {feed_key: n}}}

with **two readings of it and one accumulator** (`_add`), so they cannot drift:

- `from_grouped` — counts the **database** grouped (`commcalc.prospect_feed_tally(p_org_id)`,
  migration **1085**): one round trip, a few dozen counted slices instead of 202,865 rows.
- `from_rows` — the same shape from the rows themselves, for a database where that function is not
  applied yet. Correct, merely slow, and `source` **says which reading was used** so a slow answer is
  never mistaken for a fast one.

`router._prospect_tally_read` is the only place that choice is made. `periods_of` and `by_feed` are
the same tally read the other two ways the screens want.

### COMMCALC-14.4 The sibling, fixed here rather than excused

`get_prospect_evaluation` did the same thing one endpoint over: with no month named it read **every
row the prospect has** — 137,374 and ~137 round trips for the biggest — and looked at two columns of
each, purely to decide which month to open on. It now dereferences `_pft.by_feed` over the same
tally. Two surfaces, one fact, one reader.

### COMMCALC-14.5 Unknown is not zero

The decoration now arrives **after** the list, so for a moment every count on screen is unread. The
old shape would have rendered that as `0 months · 0 rows · nothing yet` — a confident lie about
137,374 uploaded rows, and the same wrongness as the original defect wearing a hat. So:

- `missing_tally` is the one place *unread* is distinguished from *counted and empty*;
- the payload carries `missing`, the row carries `tally_unknown`, and **every counted column on the
  table goes through one guard** that prints `counting…`;
- the store name and the **Open** button are deliberately NOT behind that guard — the list is the
  answer, and it must be usable the instant it lands.

### COMMCALC-14.6 Locked so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_prospect_feed_tally.py` — DB-free, **61 checks**: §A the two readings produce one
identical shape through one accumulator · §B `list_prospects` reads no feed rows, sets no
`feed_rows`/`periods`, and exactly one place decides how a tally is read · §C unknown is not zero on
both sides of the wire, with one guard · §D the sibling is wired and the money read is untouched ·
§E the pre-fix shape reproduced and asserted **wrong** · §F RULE TWO, no DB or clock in the module,
and the migration idempotent, org-scoped, `STABLE`, money-free, with a `-- REVERT:` note.

Wired into `carrier-vocab-guard.yml` as *"prospect feed-tally lock"*.

**Migration 1085 is not required for correctness** — the fallback answers without it — so the page
is fixed on merge and the tally becomes one query when the owner applies it.

### COMMCALC-14.7 Cross-references

Same class: §19.48 / §CORE-05 (a read with a literal ceiling, and a paged read with no total order —
both *quietly wrong*, where this one was *quietly slow*), §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers
left unwired), §CORE-11 (a column accepted and never drawn). Neighbours: §COMMCALC-03 (the
evaluation this list opens), §4a.2 and §COMMCALC-12 (the other tallies read per store per month).

## §COMMCALC-15. THE FIRST MONTH AND M2–M12 ARE TWO P&L LINES (owner ask 2026-10-16)

for any one carrier, this evaluation is specilfially for total"*.

**THE CLASS, named rather than the instance.** *A P&L line that mixes money earned on THIS month's
activations with money owed on cohorts already sold is one line answering two questions.* A store
whose first-month commission is falling is shrinking **now**; a store whose first month holds while
its M4–M6 fall lost its activation cohort **months ago**. Those are different problems with different
fixes, and while the two families share a line the statement cannot tell them apart. §COMMCALC-12
measured the size of it: 96% of a 41% fall on a takeover prospect, and of the house estate's own
**−$25,534.27 / −19.4%** May→Sep 2026 only −3.7% was M1 — **−17.9% was M2–M12**.

§COMMCALC-03.27 had already NAMED the two halves on a card. This puts them on the statement.

| the question | the ONE home |
|---|---|
| which P&L line does a month spiff book to | `account/ma_store_pnl.MA_COMMISSION_HEADS` → `carrier_comm_source_line()` (DERIVED, never spelled) |
| which line does the trailing half book to | `account/ma_store_pnl.CARRIER_COMM_TRAILING_LINE` + `CARRIER_COMM_TRAILING_SUFFIX` / `CARRIER_COMM_TRAILING_BASIS` |
| is this rung the first month or trailing | `commcalc/commission_legs.bucket_for_leg` (the platform's three buckets) |
| which month-of-life is THIS booking | the booking function's own `ma_field_leg` / `month_leg_of` call, handed out as a lockstep tag |
| what is the trailing bucket CALLED | `commcalc/commission_ledger.LEG_LABELS['trailing']` — "M2–M12" |
| the split itself | `account/ma_store_pnl.split_leg_bookings(bookings, legs, cfg)` |
| whether an org gets two lines | `pl_carrier_comm_leg_split` (mig **1086**), house answer ON |

### COMMCALC-15.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index for an existing mechanism before building: `m2-m12`, `month-of-life`, `trailing`,
`leg`, `rung`, `split the commission line`, `per-store commission trend`.

| already answers something near it | why it is not this | what this REUSED |
|---|---|---|
| §COMMCALC-03.27 `commission_leg_ladder` | names the two halves on a CARD; the statement still carried one line | **dereferenced** — the trailing line's amount is asserted equal to this ladder's trailing bucket (§V3), so the card and the line are two readings of ONE derivation |

### COMMCALC-15.2 The month-of-life is a fact about the BOOKING

The reason this is a design fix and not a report trick: `carrier_comm` is reached by the MA sheet's
`spiff_m1..m6` columns (month = `ma_field_leg`) **and** by the daily-transaction cash rows (month =
`month_leg_of`, carried in the drill-down detail as `M<n>`) **and** by other engines' ledger and POS
dollars that have no month-of-life at all. A splitter that asked "which month is this dollar" after
the fact would be a **second derivation** of a question the booking function had already answered —
and for the sheet basis it could not even ask, because the booking's detail label is `SPIFF / bounty`
with the month dropped.

So the two booking functions now **emit the rung they used**:
`ma_commission_bookings(rows, cfg, legs=None, leg_cfg=None)` and
`ma_tx_bookings(rows, pnl_cfg, cfg, legs=None, leg_cfg=None)` append a `(bucket, leg_month)` tag per
emitted booking, in lockstep, from the call they already make. **Omit `legs` and the emitted sequence
is byte-identical** — that is why it is an out-parameter and not a tuple-shape change (§V7 pins both
halves). A booking with no month-of-life concept is tagged `(None, None)` and **never moves** (§V6,
§V8): the owner's *"whatever they ave righ tonw"* is literally everything that is not a trailing rung.

### COMMCALC-15.3 THE MONEY DOES NOT MOVE, and that is asserted by name

Both halves are **revenue lines of the same section**, so splitting one into two cannot move a
subtotal. `harness_prospect_eval.py` §V2 is named **`no_total_moved`** and asserts that revenue, cost
of goods, gross profit, expenses, the bottom line **and every section subtotal** are identical to the
cent with the split on and off, and that the only difference anywhere is which line the trailing
dollars sit on. §V11 carries the per-feed identity `moved + kept == source_total`, reported *with the
money* on `scenarios[mode].leg_split`, so the split ships its own proof to the screen.

The new chart line is `auto_opt`: `engine._assemble` materialises it only when it carries a value, so
every statement that does not ask for the split is **line for line** what it was (§V1). It is
INSERTED into `coa.PL_SPEC` beside the line it divides, with its label built from **that line's own
label** and the trailing bucket's own name — so the two halves can never read as unrelated accounts,
and a future ruling that renames or re-sections the commission line carries its twin with it.

### COMMCALC-15.4 Carrier-neutral by construction (RULE TWO)

The owner asked for this on the Total side and forbade a per-carrier patch in the same breath.
Nothing in the mechanism names a carrier, a tenant or a product: the source line is derived from the
component→head map, the destination is one declared key, the bucket comes from the platform's own
`bucket_for_leg`, and the label comes from the platform's own `LEG_LABELS`. **There is no month count
and no month ceiling** — "M2–M12" is the NAME of the trailing bucket, not a bound, so an M13 books on
the trailing line the day it arrives. §V13 fails the build on a carrier word, on `range(`, on a month
ceiling or on a spelled line key inside the split; §V14 is the anti-un-wiring check: the build fails
if the evaluation stops calling the injected splitter, if the router stops injecting it, or if the
chart stops deriving the twin from the source row.

### COMMCALC-15.5 The sibling that is EXCUSED, in writing

Every other path that books commission to this line was checked:

| path | verdict |
|---|---|
| the Store Takeover Evaluation P&L (§COMMCALC-03) | **wired** — it asks for the split, for both the whole prospect and every store column |
| the Gross Profit report (§4a.2) | already shows the rungs; the new line files into its existing commission column so no GP figure moves |
| the LIVE P&L (`coa.build_inputs`) | **NOT wired, deliberately.** The mechanism is platform-wide and the switch is per org, but turning it on for live statements needs the destination line registered in `carrier_dollar_class.component_lines` and the Boost P&L classification one-homes, which another thread owns (session `cse_019HK7xiWRyHYfufPFsfKJaB`) and which this change does not touch. The dereference it needs is one call to `split_leg_bookings` beside the two booking calls in `build_inputs`, with the `legs` list those calls now accept. Until then a live statement is byte-identical and the trailing line does not render |

### COMMCALC-15.6 The separate block: M2–M12 per store, every month

`prospect_eval.commission_leg_store_months(every_month, stores, homes, today, months)` — PURE, and it
is §COMMCALC-12's pivot fed by this prospect's own uploads. Each cell comes from
`commission_leg_ladder`, so a cell here cannot disagree with the P&L line above it.

- **One row per store, one column per month.** "All months" is the default, because the comparison IS
  the answer; the month selector narrows the COLUMNS and nothing else, and its options are the
  payload's own `months_available`, so a month nobody uploaded can never be offered.
- **The store filter is the page's shared one** (§COMMCALC-03.20), keyed off the same store record as
  the P&L matrix, so a pick narrows this block to the same stores.
- **Both bases, always** — what the sheet says was EARNED and what the cash rows say was RECEIVED —
  and an unmeasured basis reads *not measured* rather than as zeros. The block opens on cash, because
  a takeover reader asks what is arriving.
- **A month that has not finished is marked a part month** (`partial_months`, the pivot's own rule,
  shared with the live leg trend) and is left out of every change figure: half a month of cash reads
  exactly like a store falling off a cliff.
- **Money naming no store is its own named row**, never spread and never dropped, and `ties` reports
  per month whether the rows still add to the company figure — a mismatch is printed as a finding.
- Through `ReportShell`, so it sorts, filters and exports like every other table; the change-% column
  declares `agg: 'none'` and a $0 baseline gives a BLANK percentage, never 0% ("up from nothing" has
  no percentage).

**Where it is:** `/commcalc/store-takeover` — the P&L and the per-store matrix now carry two
commission lines, the First-month/M2–M12 card says so in words, and the new "M2–M12 per store, month
by month" card sits under it. **No extra query:** the endpoint already read every month in one pass.

### COMMCALC-15.7 Files, locks, and what is waiting on the owner

| thing | where |
|---|---|
| the split, the destination line, the switch | `backend/app/modules/account/ma_store_pnl.py` (`carrier_comm_source_line`, `leg_split_routes`, `split_leg_bookings`, `CARRIER_COMM_TRAILING_*`, `pl_carrier_comm_leg_split` in `PL_CONFIG_COLUMNS`) |
| the chart line | `backend/app/modules/account/coa.py` — `_insert_leg_split_line(PL_SPEC)`, `auto_opt` revenue |
| the rung tags | `ma_commission_bookings` / `ma_tx_bookings`, lockstep `legs` out-parameter |
| the wiring + the per-store block | `backend/app/modules/commcalc/prospect_eval.py` (`_book`, `commission_leg_store_months`), `commcalc/router.py` (`_prospect_homes`, `get_prospect_evaluation`) |
| the screen | `frontend/src/app/(platform)/commcalc/store-takeover/page.tsx` |
| the lock | `backend/harness_prospect_eval.py` §V (14 checks) + §W (14 checks) — **365 passed / 0 failed**; run by `carrier-vocab-guard.yml` |
| the migration | `database/migrations/1086_pl_carrier_comm_leg_split.sql` — **optional**, and NOT applied from a container. The feature works without it (a missing column reads the house answer and is REPORTED as missing by `rule_basis`); applying it only lets a tenant turn the second line OFF. It moves no money and rewrites no row |

**No Recompute is required.** Nothing stored changes: the takeover evaluation is computed on demand
and persisted nowhere, and no live statement asks for the split.

Same class: §COMMCALC-12 (which rung is running down, per store), §COMMCALC-03.27 (the two halves
named on a card), §4a.2 (the rung convention's one home), §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers
left unwired — what §V14 exists to prevent).

## §COMMCALC-16. A FIGURE THE PORTAL DID NOT SEND IS NOT A ZERO (owner report 2026-10-16)

**Owner report 2026-10-16, verbatim:** *"Check why atu information for atu and other metrics is not
pulling up same as in elevate go for boost , need to fix it asap"*.

**Measured live 2026-10-16** (house org `00000000-…0001`, `commcalc.raw_dlar_store`, read-only via the
Supabase REST API — the container cannot reach the carrier portal, whose password is `enc:v1:`
ciphertext and whose key is the backend's):

| period | pulled | `gross_adds` | `total_upgrades` | `total_acts` | the rate columns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| September 2026 | 2026-10-02 | 1,061 | 494 | 1,555 | populated |
| **October 2026** | **2026-10-16** | **0** | **0** | **0** | **populated** |

Every rate arrived; every unit count landed as **zero**, in the same 28 rows, on the same pull. A
store cannot attach 66.67% of nothing. Those zeros are the portal no longer sending those fields,
**written down as a measurement** — and the run that wrote them was recorded `last_status = ok`.

### COMMCALC-16.1 The class, not the instance

> **An unsent figure is not a zero — for a COUNT exactly as much as for a RATE. And which source
> field feeds which column is a DECLARATION, or a rename upstream arrives as data instead of as an
> alarm.**

`dlar_sweep._rate` already existed for the first half of that rule (§19.28, owner defect 2026-09-26:
*no denominator is not a score of zero*). `_num` sat two functions away in the same file returning
`0.0` for a cell that was never there, so the next shape change landed as 28 confident zeros. The
second half is the deeper one: the only record of *this column comes from that portal field* was the
`rec.get("…")` literal inside the normalizer, so when a portal **renames** a field the platform
cannot say so — it reads the old name, gets nothing, and stores a zero.

### COMMCALC-16.2 The one home

`app/modules/commcalc/portal_cell.py` — *did the source SEND this figure, and which source field
feeds which column*. PURE, stdlib only, no portal knowledge, no vendor word (RULE TWO).

| function | the fact |
|---|---|
| `measured(v)` | THE parse. Absent / blank / `n/a` → `None`; a cell that SAYS `'0'` → `0.0`; `'1,061'`, `'66.67%'` and `'0% / 71.43%'` all understood |
| `rate(v)` · `count(v)` | the two named readings, deliberately identical in behaviour — the distinction is what the caller MEANS, not how the text is read |
| `total(*parts)` | a derived total of parts the source did not send is **absent**, not zero (`total_acts`) |
| `as_int(v)` | an INT column gets an int or `None`, never a float Postgres rejects (22P02) |
| `field_arrival(records, declared)` | `missing` / `blank` / `consumed` / `unconsumed` / `shape_changed`, one entry per FIELD (alternative spellings are ONE field, so a reader that accepts two is not missing the one it did not get) |

`unconsumed` — the fields the source IS sending that nothing reads — is reported **only when
something is missing or blank**. A feed ignores fields by design, so listing them on a healthy run
would teach an operator to ignore the line; listing them beside a field that stopped arriving **is
the renamed field's new name**, printed by the feed itself on the first run after a rename.

### COMMCALC-16.3 The callers, wired (not a registry written and left unwired — §19.18)

- `dlar_sweep._num` / `_rate` **dereference** `portal_cell.count` / `.rate`. One rule, one home.
- `dlar_sweep.STORE_FIELDS` / `REP_FIELDS` / `FIELD_MAPS` / `declared_source_fields()` — the source
  field → column mapping, declared once per report with its `kind` (`TEXT` / `COUNT` / `RATE`).
  `normalize_store` / `normalize_rep` dereference it; **no `rec.get("…")` literal remains** in the
  sweep, and the lock fails the build if one reappears.
- `run_dlar_sweep` returns `fields` (the source-side arrival, per report) beside the existing
  `content` (the column-side arrival). `status_sentence` prints `⚠ PORTAL FIELD CHANGED: …` and
  `FIELDS THE PORTAL SENDS THAT NOTHING READS …`, capped at eight names plus a count, and a portal
  field change **cannot sit under a green OK**.
- `data_lineage_registry.REQUIRED_CONTENT_COLUMNS['raw_dlar_store']` gains `gross_adds`,
  `total_upgrades`, `total_acts` — undeclared is why October's store grain drew no comment at all.
- `core/module_graph.py` fact `portal_cell`.

### COMMCALC-16.4 What this does NOT do, stated plainly

It does **not** recover October's counts. The portal's new field spelling is not knowable from here
(the carrier portal is unreachable from the container and its stored password is encrypted), and
**guessing a key name on a feed that tiers pay is the §19.26 defect** — *missing beats wrong on a
money gate*. What it does is make the next run NAME the new spelling, after which the mapping is one
declared alternative spelling added beside the old one. Until then the counts read **absent**, which
is true, instead of **zero**, which was not.

### COMMCALC-16.5 Siblings checked (the §19.18 requirement)

| sibling | verdict |
|---|---|
| `dlar_sweep._rate` | already correct (2026-09-26); now shares the home |
| `dlar_vs_platform` | already correct on the READ side — `reported` / `measured_zero` / `not_reported`, *"the figure is None, NEVER 0"*. It was being handed a zero the landing point had invented, so this fix is what makes that vocabulary able to tell the truth |
| `b2b_sweep._num` | **excused**: its portal client is stubs — no live pull lands through it |
| `vendor_rebate_feed._num` | **excused**: it parses a workbook where a blank money cell legitimately means nothing owed, and its contract is explicitly "never raise on a totals row" |
| `epay_sweep` (`safe_float`, `_comp_get`) | **not fixed here, named**: it lands MONEY from a file download whose headers are the field names, already reads two spellings per field (`_comp_get`), and a missing header there fails differently. Its own PR |

### COMMCALC-16.6 Locks

- `backend/harness_portal_cell.py` — 47 checks, DB-free. §B is the **October 2026 regression**, from
  the real record shape; §F proves the declared maps produce **exactly** the columns and values the
  hand-written normalizers produced for a record carrying every field; §E proves a healthy run stays
  quiet. Red on the pre-change sweep.
- `harness_kpi_registry_lock.py` — the rate-vs-count pin was re-pointed at the DECLARATION (scanning
  for the retired `rec.get` literal would now pass **vacuously**, which is how a lock stops locking),
  and gains the `rec.get("…")`-count-is-zero check and the green-OK check for a portal field change.
- `harness_kpi_vintage.py` §B5 **pinned the opposite** — *"an absent count is still 0, because for a
  count it is"*. The premise died on the measurement above; it now pins the rule, keeps a pre-fix
  control, and adds the derived-total case.

Same class: §19.28 (the three freshness axes — this is the fourth question, asked of the SOURCE's
fields rather than our columns), §19.26 (missing beats wrong on a money gate), §66
(`component_is_evidence` — a surface reading a value without reading how it was arrived at), §19.18
(a mechanism written and its callers left unwired).

## §COMMCALC-17. THE FIRST MONTH AND THE TRAILING MONTHS ARE REPORTED ON DIFFERENT FEEDS (owner report 2026-10-16)

**Owner, verbatim:** *"something is wrong on teh m1 commmission it cannot be that low, jsut a rule
of thumb , if the store does 100 activation and an mrc of 50, teh first month payout is 25, so the
month shoudl have 2500 plus any spiff etc, recheck"*.

He is right, the arithmetic is his, and the answer is NOT the month-label vocabulary of
§COMMCALC-15 / `harness_month_leg_resolution.py` §A–§F — that mechanism is sound and is proved
sound on the REAL September labels below. The first month's money is reported on the feed the org's
`pl_ma_month_spiff_source` switch **suppresses**.

### COMMCALC-17.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

| asked of the index | found | what was reused |

| where "which month-of-life is this row" lives | `commcalc/commission_ledger.month_leg_of` (§COMMCALC-15.2, the 2026-09-21 one-home) + `commission_legs.ma_field_leg` for a sheet column | asked, not re-derived; both proved correct on the real labels |
| where the two bases live | `ma_store_pnl.ma_earned_month_ladder` / `ma_received_month_ladder` (§4a) | the measurement below IS those two functions, not a third reader |
| where the M1 proof lives | `backend/harness_month_leg_resolution.py` | **EXTENDED** with §G rather than a new harness — the owner has now reported the same number twice and the evidence belongs in one place |
| whether a second capture path is needed | no | no new table, endpoint, report or query; nothing to register in §§16–18 |

And again for the FIX (§17.7), before building it:

| asked of the index | found | what was reused |
|---|---|---|
| where "which feed states this org's month-spiff money" is decided | `commission_org_config.pl_ma_month_spiff_source` (mig 314), read by `ma_store_pnl.load_config` — one answer for all rungs | **EXTENDED in place**: the same switch, the same reader, the same config row; a per-rung map (mig 1087) with the scalar as its fallback. No sibling switch, no second config table |
| whether a rung vocabulary already exists | `commission_legs.ladder_key` / `bucket_for_leg` / `LADDER_UNKNOWN` (§4a.2) | the map's KEYS are that vocabulary; nothing here spells a rung or a month count |
| where the proof belongs | `backend/harness_month_leg_resolution.py` §A–§G | **EXTENDED with §H** — the fix is proved in the same home that reproduced the defect, not in a sibling harness |
| where the one-home gate belongs | `backend/harness_ma_income_one_home_guard.py` (CHECK 2 / 2b / 2c already gate the MA money, the LEG and the RUNG homes) | **EXTENDED with CHECK 2d** rather than a new lock |
| whether the P&L needed a new line | no — §COMMCALC-15's first-month / M2–M12 split already exists (mig 1086) | the movement lands on the EXISTING first-month line; `split_leg_bookings` is untouched |
| whether the takeover evaluation needed its own copy | no | `prospect_eval.rule_basis` gains the switch as a declared-vs-house row; it books through `ma_store_pnl` as before |

### COMMCALC-17.2 Measured, read-only

Prospect uploads of org `854f6d7b-…` (`commcalc.prospect_feed_row`, seven months) — and the same
shape on that org's LIVE `raw_ma_commission` / `raw_ma_daily_tx` for Jul–Sep 2026:

| period | activations | Σ `mrc_net_discount` | EARNED M1 | RECEIVED M1 | EARNED M2–6 | RECEIVED M2–6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mar 2026 | 39 | 1,841 | 1,018.53 | 1,061.01 | 2,643.75 | 861.25 |
| Apr 2026 | 866 | 26,957 | 13,385.25 | 10,521.92 | 50,941.25 | 18,837.50 |
| May 2026 | 1,066 | 29,521 | 16,269.18 | 13,057.88 | 51,965.00 | 27,020.00 |
| Jun 2026 | 1,209 | 30,446 | 16,657.58 | 13,306.10 | 38,365.75 | 37,442.75 |
| Jul 2026 | 1,217 | 32,149 | 17,164.44 | 9,544.87 | 26,665.75 | 49,874.50 |
| Aug 2026 | 613 | 21,524 | 12,323.03 | 2,762.36 | 4,935.50 | 64,308.75 |
| **Sep 2026** | **482** | **16,364** | **7,899.24** | **1,237.99** | **555.00** | **38,451.50** |

The owner's rule of thumb holds exactly — on the SHEET. September: 482 activations, MRC $16,364.12,
first-month commission **$7,899.24 = 48.3% of MRC**. The figure the Store Takeover Evaluation showed
him was **$1,237.99 — 15.7% of it**, because that is the other feed.

**Each rung is reported by exactly ONE of the two feeds.**
- The **sheet** states the first month at activation and almost nothing else: September, **410 of
  482** rows carry a non-zero `spiff_m1`, **26** carry any of `spiff_m2..m6`.
- The **cash** feed states the trailing months promptly and the first month **retroactively** — the
  family carrying untokened first-month cash is named `Retroactive Postpaid Spiff`, and its row
  count collapses **582 → 467 → 139 → 60** over Jun→Sep while activations only halve. Cumulatively
  the cash M1 is **$51,492.13** against **$84,717.25** earned — 60.8%, **never above**: the same
  money with a lag, not a second payment.

### COMMCALC-17.3 What is NOT wrong (checked, not assumed)

- **The month test does not read the wrong field.** On the real September labels, through the real
  `ma_tx_bookings`: the untokened `… New Activation Commission` cash row reads as M1, `TBV MONTH 3
  …` reads as M3, nothing lands in `Spiff (other)`. `ma_field_leg('spiff_m1')` → `(m1, 1)`.
- **`Activation Order` is not misfiled commission.** Its `retail_cost` is **positive** (the dealer is
  CHARGED — Sep: +$18,330.22 over 557 rows) and its `product_name` is a plan name. Neither field
  makes it commission. Every other negative-money family in the feed is already accounted for:
  `Postpaid Promo Order` = `Subsidy` (device rebate class), `Postpaid Branded Void` / `MarketPlace
  RMA` = device returns, `Postpaid Residual Order` → `mi_income`, `Premium Store Spiff` →
  `mdf_income` by configured token, `Postpaid Consumer Promotion` = consumer promo.
- **`mrc_net_discount` books nowhere, correctly.** It is the MRC the commission is computed FROM, not
  money owed, so it is absent from `residual_subs._MA_COMPONENTS` and from `MA_COMMISSION_HEADS`.

### COMMCALC-17.4 The class-level defect

`commission_org_config.pl_ma_month_spiff_source` (mig 314) picks **one feed for ALL rungs**. It was
built to stop one payment booking twice, on the assumption that both feeds carry the same money at
the same time. They do not: the feeds are **complementary by rung and lagged by rung**. So:

| the switch | the first-month rung books | the trailing rungs book | September reality |
|---|---|---|---|
| `daily_tx` (this org) | the cash that has arrived — **$1,237.99** | the cash — $38,451.50 | the sheet's $7,899.24 books **nowhere** |
| `commission_sheet` (house default) | the sheet — $7,899.24 | the sheet's near-empty columns — **$555.00** | the cash's $38,451.50 books **nowhere** |

**Neither setting can state the month.** The right answer, $7,899.24 + $38,451.50, is unreachable by
either — pinned by name in `harness_month_leg_resolution.py` §G10–G13.

### COMMCALC-17.5 The shape of the fix (decided 2026-10-16 — see §17.7 for what shipped)

The design fix is **per-RUNG sourcing**: `pl_ma_month_spiff_source` becomes resolvable per
month-of-life rung (a rung→source map, per org, with the house answer reproducing today's single
value byte-identically — config, never code, no carrier or month count anywhere). The choice must be
made **per rung, wholesale**: MEASURED, of the 2,661 first-month cash rows, **zero** carry an
`order_number` that appears as an `activation_order` on any of the 5,495 sheet rows, so the carrier
files a spiff payment under its own transaction number and the two feeds **cannot be matched row to
row**. A fix cannot book the sheet's first month and suppress "the same" cash row later.

**It was not shipped with the finding, and the reason was stated plainly:** whether the commission
line states the first month on an **accrual** basis while its trailing months stay **cash** is an
accounting policy for the owner, not a choice an agent makes — and it moves real money on the P&L.
The mechanism, the measurement and the regression were ready; the policy decision and its migration
were surfaced for approval. **The owner answered the decision card on 2026-10-16 22:33 UTC: option
A, "Earned first month"** — the first month reported on the commission SHEET (earned at activation),
months 2–12 still from the daily cash feed (received). §17.7 is what that decision shipped as.

### COMMCALC-17.7 THE FIX, SHIPPED: the feed is chosen PER RUNG (owner decision 2026-10-16)

**Owner's decision, verbatim from the card:** option **A, "Earned first month"**, on *"Report the
first month when earned, while trailing months stay on cash?"*. It is an accounting policy and it is
not re-litigated here.

**THE CLASS, named rather than the instance.** The instance is "this org's first month reads
$1,237.99 instead of $7,899.24". The class is: **"which feed states this org's money" was asked once
for ALL rungs, of two feeds that are complementary by rung and lagged by rung.** The fix is to the
QUESTION: it is only answerable per rung, so that is the only form it is asked in now.

| the fact | its ONE home | every caller |
|---|---|---|
| which feed states THIS rung | `account/ma_store_pnl.month_spiff_source_for_rung` (+ `books_month_spiff_from`, `month_spiff_feeds_used`, `month_spiff_rung_sources`) | `ma_commission_bookings` (sheet side), `ma_tx_bookings` (cash side), `ma_tx_coverage`, `gp_carrier_income` |
| what the basis is CALLED | `ma_store_pnl.booked_basis` (`BASIS_PER_RUNG` + a label built from `BASIS_LABELS`) | `router._ma_summary_legs` (`booked_basis`), the GP payload / page |
| the ladder the BOOKS carry | `ma_store_pnl.booked_month_ladder` — rung by rung from the feed that states it | `gp_carrier_income` (so "the ladder explains the Commission column" survives a mixed basis) |
| a rung whose feed sent NOTHING this period | `ma_store_pnl.rung_source_gaps` | the GP/P&L payload (`rung_source_gaps`) |
| the switch itself | `commission_org_config.pl_ma_month_spiff_source_by_rung` (mig **1087**), jsonb `{rung key: feed}` | `ma_store_pnl.load_config` (the only reader), `prospect_eval.rule_basis` (so the evaluation SHOWS the declaration) |

**Config, never code.** A rung key is the vocabulary `commission_legs` already owns — a ladder key
(`'1'`…`'13'`…), a bucket name (`'m1'` / `'trailing'` / `'unsplit'`) or `'default'`; resolution is
exact rung → bucket → `default` → the mig-314 scalar. No carrier, tenant, product or month COUNT
appears anywhere in the resolver, `'trailing'` covers an M13 the day it arrives, and an unknown key
or a mistyped feed is DROPPED so that rung keeps the scalar — a typo can never restate a P&L line.
**The house answer is `{}`**: every rung reads the scalar, which reproduces mig 314 byte-identically,
so an org that declares nothing sees no change at all (pinned `harness_month_leg_resolution.py`
§H6–H9, both settings, both booking functions).

**NO DOUBLE COUNT, and it is the code's shape rather than a comment.** Exactly one feed answers yes
for a rung; the other feed's rows for that rung book NOTHING. So when the first month is sourced
from the sheet, the retroactive first-month CASH rows do not book — they are the same money with a
lag (§17.2: cumulatively 60.8% of earned, never above it), and they cannot be netted row by row
because ZERO of 2,661 of them join a sheet activation (§17.5). The suppressed rows are NAMED rather
than silently dropped: `ma_tx_coverage` reports them under `sourced_elsewhere` with the rung and the
feed that states them, so "everything has a reason" (owner 2026-09-08) still holds — they are never
counted as a family with no business rule.

**WHAT MOVES, measured read-only through these very booking functions (2026-10-16).** Org
`854f6d7b-…` is the only org on the cash scalar, so it is the only live book that moves:

| period | `carrier_comm` today | under the decision | Δ | first-month rung |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jun 2026 | 26,999.54 | 29,229.41 | **+2,229.87** | 2,605.54 → 4,835.41 |
| Jul 2026 | 28,830.94 | 41,158.45 | **+12,327.51** | 1,275.19 → 13,602.70 |
| Aug 2026 | 98,656.37 | 115,878.31 | **+17,221.94** | 6,049.96 → **23,271.90** |
| Sep 2026 | 101,270.98 | 118,077.91 | **+16,806.93** | 5,666.97 → 22,473.90 |
| **Jun–Sep** | **255,757.83** | **304,344.08** | **+48,586.25** | |
| Oct 2026 (open) | 38,855.99 | 45,168.90 | +6,312.91 | 1,708.67 → 8,021.58 |

Every trailing rung is unchanged to the cent in every month — the whole movement is the first-month
rung. August's first month becomes **$23,271.90**, which is the figure the Gross Profit tile has
shown all along (§4a) and the owner's rule of thumb (§17.2). On the LuxeLink takeover-evaluation
uploads (§COMMCALC-03, the prospect's own feeds, not the live book): Jun +3,351.48, Jul +7,619.57,
Aug +9,560.67, Sep +6,661.25 → **Jun–Sep +27,192.97** (Mar–Sep +33,225.12), first month
1,237.99 → 7,899.24 in September, exactly §17.2's measured earned figure.

**A PERIOD WITH NO SHEET UPLOAD IS UNREPORTED, NOT ZERO.** Measured on the same org:
`raw_ma_commission` has rows from **June 2026** onward and **none** for Feb–May 2026, while
`raw_ma_daily_tx` covers every month. So under this decision the first-month rung has no source in
those four months. There is deliberately **no fallback** to the other feed (that would double-count
the rung across periods), and the absence is REPORTED — `rung_source_gaps` names the rung, the feed
and "UNREPORTED here, not zero" (§COMMCALC-16's rule). **Recompute Jun 2026 onward only;** recomputing
Feb–May 2026 would publish a $0.00 first month for months whose sheet was never uploaded.

**Statements are per-period snapshots** (`commcalc.account_statements`, 72 scopes × Feb–Oct for this
org). Applying mig 1087 rewrites no stored row: Jun–Oct 2026 move when those periods are RECOMPUTED.

### COMMCALC-17.6 Locks

`backend/harness_month_leg_resolution.py` §G — 68 checks, DB-free, no new harness (§17.1). G1–G6 prove
the vocabulary and the field reading are sound on the REAL labels; G7–G9 pin the owner's rule of
thumb as arithmetic on the sheet; **G10–G13 reproduce the wrong answer through the real booking
functions** and assert the right one is unreachable under either setting; G14–G15 pin the data shape
that causes it; G16–G17 pin the zero-join measurement the fix's shape depends on.

`backend/harness_month_leg_resolution.py` §H — 34 further checks on the FIX, in the same home (no
sibling harness): H1–H5 reach the answer §G13 proved unreachable and prove not one cash row of a
sheet-sourced rung books; **H6–H9 pin BYTE-IDENTITY for an org that declares nothing**, on both
settings and through both booking functions, and re-assert §G's two single-feed answers unchanged;
H10–H16 pin RULE TWO and the fail-to-the-scalar posture (a mistyped feed, an unknown rung key, a
non-dict map, bucket resolution with no month count, an unlabelled row never guessed into M1);
H17–H21 pin the GP ladder following the books rung by rung and the basis being NAMED; H22–H24 pin
"everything has a reason" under suppression; H25–H28 pin the UNREPORTED-not-zero period gap;
H29–H31 pin the live movement as figures.

`backend/harness_ma_income_one_home_guard.py` **CHECK 2d — the build gate that cannot un-wire:** no
file under `backend/app` outside the home may compare the month-spiff switch to a feed name (any
spelling: a literal, `BASIS_EARNED`/`BASIS_RECEIVED`, `in`/`not in`), and the four functions inside
the home must keep calling the resolver. Verified to BITE (a planted
`cfg["month_spiff_source"] == "daily_tx"` in another module fails the run). Wired into CI in the
*MA one-home guard* step, with the proof harness beside it.

Same class: §COMMCALC-16 (an absence written down as a measurement), §COMMCALC-15.2 (the rung is a
fact about the booking), §19.26 (missing beats wrong on a money gate), §19.18 (a registry written
and its callers left unwired — which is what CHECK 2d exists to prevent here).
