## §POS-01. THE REGISTER ENTERS A PRODUCT IT DOES NOT HAVE, AND NEVER LOSES A CART (owner ask 2026-10-16)

Owner, verbatim, in two messages the same evening:

> "in the pos menu , let the user edit the product descriptinon fields and add a product to the
> ineventory if a new product is being entered manually, promtp the user to create the new product
> if the product is not found."

> "also if a person leaves the cash register it gets blank if you come back it shoudl automatically
> store for the next session in suspensed state"

Three gaps at the till, one screen (`pos/sales/page.tsx`):

1. **A line's description could not be touched.** The cart showed the product's name and type as
   plain text. A customer buying "the blue one, 64GB" went onto the receipt as whatever the catalog
   happened to call it, and the only way to correct a product's own name was to leave the sale,
   open Products & Services, and start the sale again.
2. **A product the catalog had never heard of was a dead end.** A scan or a search that matched
   nothing opened the picker with the term filled in and showed "No products match." — and that was
   the whole of it. Nothing offered to create the item, and nothing could put it in inventory, so
   the sale was rung against the nearest wrong product or not at all.
3. **The cart lived only in the browser's memory.** A reload, a navigation, a crashed tab or the end
   of a shift erased a part-rung sale with no trace. The customer was then re-rung from memory —
   where the things remembered wrong are the discounts and the serial numbers.

### POS-01.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index for every existing mechanism before building anything:

| the question | what already answered it | what was done |
|---|---|---|
| which products match, and are they in stock here | §33 `pos/product_filters.py` + `pos/product-filters.tsx` | REUSED untouched — the create prompt hangs off the picker §33 already owns, and the form takes §33's own `ProductFilterOptions` option lists |
| what are the fields of a POS product | the catalog page's INLINE form (`pos/products/page.tsx`) | EXTRACTED to `pos/product-form.tsx` and dereferenced by both screens. The register did NOT get a second field list |
| how does a product get created | `POST /pos/products` (§33's row, unchanged) | REUSED as-is, so the till and the catalog create identical rows |
| how does a serialised unit get into stock | §11b `inventory_integrity_router.receive_unit`, behind THE duplicate-IMEI landing guard | REUSED — the register posts to `POST /pos/inventory/serial` and gets the same 409 evidence. The register writes no inventory table of its own |
| how does STANDARD (qty) stock get on hand | **nothing, for a single row.** Only the CSV count importer (`router.import_entity`, entity `inventory`) and mig 726's in-database `pos.receive_transfer` | NEW one home `pos/stock_landing.py` + `POST /pos/inventory/standard`. Both siblings checked below |
| is there a suspended / held / parked sale | **nothing.** `pos.sales.status` is `completed`\|`voided` only; no held-cart table, no browser persistence | NEW one home `pos/held_sale.py` + `pos.held_sales` (mig `1088`) |

### POS-01.2 One fact, one home, dereferenced

- **"What a POS product IS"** → `frontend …/pos/product-form.tsx`. The field list, the defaults
  (`EMPTY_PRODUCT_FORM`), the row→form mapper (`productFormFrom`), the POST/PATCH body
  (`productFormPayload`), the save-enabled rule (`productFormReady`) and the "is this a barcode or a
  name" split (`productFormFromEntry`) are spelled once. The catalog page's inline form is DELETED
  and it now renders the shared component — this is a replacement, not a parallel copy
  (the §19.18 failure mode: a registry written and left unwired).
- **"A single-row entry puts standard stock on hand at this store"** → `pos/stock_landing.py`.
  The identity is `(org, product, store)` — the table's own unique key — and the arithmetic is
  **declared, not guessed**: `MODE_ADD` is a receipt and adds to on hand, `MODE_SET` is a count and
  replaces it. A writer that inferred the mode from whether a row happened to exist would turn a
  recount into a doubling. A 0-unit receipt onto an existing row writes NOTHING, so an idempotent
  retry cannot double anything, and the endpoint answers `before` AND `after` so a double entry is
  visible at the till rather than discovered at the next count.
- **"What is still in this register's cart"** → `pos/held_sale.py` + `pos.held_sales`, with
  `frontend/src/lib/pos-held-sale.ts` as the one client home. The cart is a property of the
  **terminal**, keyed on `(org, store_code, register_number)` — the SAME triple
  `pos.register_sessions` is keyed on, which is what makes the owner's "the next session" literal.

### POS-01.3 Why the held cart is on the server and not in the browser

`localStorage` answers "what did THIS browser profile have", which is not the question. A tablet
swapped between staff, a second browser, a private window or cleared site data all lose the cart,
and no other screen could ever see that a sale is part-rung. The hold belongs to the register, so it
lives where the register's other state lives. The lock asserts no POS page keeps a cart in browser
storage.

### POS-01.4 Restored VERBATIM — and what that does and does not mean

The agreed **unit price**, the **list price it overrode**, the **discount**, the **serial** and the
**description** come back exactly as they were left. Nothing is re-read from the catalog: quietly
moving a figure is how a $99 line becomes $199 between the two halves of one sale.

Stated plainly because it is the one exception: each line's **tax** IS re-derived from the store's
live rate on restore, by the same effect that already re-taxes the cart when the store is switched
mid-sale. A tax rate is a legal fact about the store, not a figure the cashier negotiated.

The age travels with the cart (`held_at`, kept across autosaves so it is the age of the SALE and not
of the last keystroke), and the banner says it: *"Resumed a suspended sale from this register — 3
lines, $1,081.49 · suspended 24 minutes ago by E42. These are the prices that were on the lines when
it was suspended."* Resuming is then a decision, with Keep it / Discard it beside it.

### POS-01.5 A suspended cart is not a sale

Nothing in `pos.held_sales` is a transaction: no transaction number is burned, no row reaches
`pos.sales`, no stock moves and no money is recorded. That is precisely why the register may save it
**automatically**, without asking, and why a cart nobody ever resumes has cost nothing. An empty
cart with no customer attached CLEARS the hold rather than storing a row, so an idle register leaves
nothing behind; a selected customer with no lines yet IS held, because that is a sale in progress.

The autosave is **gated on the restore having run** (`heldRestored`). Saving before it would
overwrite the cart the last session left with this session's empty one — the exact loss the feature
exists to stop — so the gate is asserted by the lock, with its negative control.

### POS-01.6 Siblings checked, fixed or EXCUSED in writing

| sibling | same question? | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `router.import_entity(entity="inventory")` — the CSV count importer | yes, the same upsert | **EXCUSED.** It answers a different fact: a counted sheet, where a product already counted at a store is SKIPPED as a duplicate ROW OF THE SHEET. Folding the two would make a re-uploaded count file double every figure. Pinned by `harness_pos_stock_landing.py` §D3 |
| mig 726 `pos.receive_transfer` / `ship_transfer` — stock between stores | yes, the same arithmetic | **EXCUSED, and LOCKED.** PL/pgSQL inside one transaction with the transfer's status machine; it cannot dereference a Python helper. §D2 pins that its `ON CONFLICT` still means ADD, so a divergence fails the build rather than going unnoticed |
| §11b `receive_unit` — a serialised unit | no: a different table and a landing guard | **REUSED.** The register posts to `POST /pos/inventory/serial`; `POST /pos/inventory/standard` REFUSES a serial-tracked product, so qty stock with no unit behind it cannot be created |
| `pos/special-orders/manage/page.tsx` — also creates a catalogue row | no: a narrower entity | **EXCUSED BY NAME.** A hidden-vendor special-order item (mig 864/865) through `POST /pos/special-orders/catalog`: 6 customer-facing fields plus the vendor linkage, with no department, category, inventory type, body style or cost, because a special-order item has none. Lock rule `b6` pins that it stays narrow — the day it grows the full field list, the lock goes red and the two are made one |

### POS-01.7 What the cashier now does

- **Fix a line.** Product type and description are inputs on the cart line. They are the LINE's own
  wording — what prints on the receipt and lands in `pos.sale_items` — so a correction changes this
  sale only. A ✎ beside the description opens the shared form to change the **catalogue product**
  instead; a rename then follows onto the open cart lines, while the agreed price does not.
- **Create what is not there.** The picker's empty state names what was searched for — *"'Anker
  65W charger' is not in the catalog"* — and offers to create it; a quick scan that matches nothing
  lands in that same picker with the scanned text in it, so there is ONE prompt and not two. A pure
  barcode fills the UPC and leaves the name to type; anything else is read as the name.
- **Put it in inventory.** The create modal carries an opening-stock block: a quantity for a standard
  product, the first unit's serial / IMEI for a serial-tracked one. Blank is legitimate — "created,
  none on hand yet" — and is never guessed into a 1. Then the product is rung up, which is why the
  cashier opened the form. The three facts are reported separately: if the stock does not land, the
  product still exists, the sale still rings, and the reason is said out loud rather than read as a
  silent zero.
- **Walk away.** The cart suspends itself 1.2s after the last change, and the next session on that
  register is handed it back with its age. Checking out, or Clear Cart, drops the hold — otherwise
  coming back would restore a sale the customer has already paid for.

### POS-01.8 Files, locks, and what is waiting on the owner

| | |
|---|---|
| backend one homes | `backend/app/modules/pos/held_sale.py` (PURE — no DB, no clock, no org id), `backend/app/modules/pos/stock_landing.py` (PURE) |
| endpoints | `POST /pos/inventory/standard`; `GET` / `PUT` / `DELETE /pos/held-sale` (`pos/router.py`) |
| frontend one homes | `…/pos/product-form.tsx`, `frontend/src/lib/pos-held-sale.ts` |
| frontend changed | `…/pos/sales/page.tsx` (editable line fields, the create prompt, the create/edit modal, restore + autosave), `…/pos/products/page.tsx` (its inline form REPLACED by the shared one) |
| migration | `database/migrations/1088_pos_held_sale.sql` — **WRITTEN, NOT APPLIED**, surfaced for owner approval. Additive, idempotent, carries its REVERT, touches no existing row of any table |
| proofs | `harness_pos_held_sale.py` (68 checks), `harness_pos_stock_landing.py` (46) |
| lock | `harness_pos_product_form_lock.py` (40) — one form on both screens, one payload rule, one not-found prompt, stock through the endpoints, one suspended-cart client |
| ADAPTIVE | every held-sale endpoint answers `available: false` before mig 1088 is applied, and the register then behaves exactly as it did before the feature existed (a cart lost on reload) instead of erroring. So applying the migration turns the feature ON; it is not a precondition for the register working |
| RULE TWO | no carrier, tenant, store, product or register number appears in either module; the register number defaults to 1 only to agree with `pos.register_sessions.register_number`'s own default |

Same class: §33 (one filter helper, one filter component), §19.18 (a registry written and left
unwired is not a fix), §11b (a landing guard belongs to the landing, not to its callers).

## §COMMCALC-18. AN ACCESSORY LINE AND A RENT LINE BOTH MOVE IN DOLLARS (owner ask 2026-10-17)

Owner, verbatim: *"add accessories sales in the sales comparoison to cpomapre month over month and
also addexpenses"*.

### §COMMCALC-18.1 WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and the class

The Sales Comparison already tallied accessory **dollars** (`sales_comparison.tally` → the shared
`_is_accessory`), and `_combine` already returned `rev_delta` / `rev_pct` for every category. The
**table rendered neither**: its only change columns were `Change` and `Change %`, both read off the
UNIT pair. So the one category whose headline metric is money — Accessories — was the one category
whose month-over-month change the grid could not show, and the payload had been carrying the answer
all along.

**THE CLASS:** *a period-over-period report must carry a change column for every metric it reports
on, not only for the metric most of its rows happen to use.* A row whose headline is dollars and a
row whose headline is units cannot share one change column. Fixed for every category at once — the
`$ Change` / `$ Change %` pair sits beside the unit pair for all of them, from the same two payload
fields the tiles headline, so a tile and its rows cannot disagree.

Store expenses were genuinely absent, and are the second half of the ask.

### §COMMCALC-18.2 DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate) — WHAT WAS REUSED, NOT REBUILT

Searched the index for every fact this needed before writing anything. **Nothing new derives a
dollar:**

| what the expense line needs | the ONE home it reads | new? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| which rows a month books, incl. a month nobody re-entered | `commcalc/expenses_effective.effective_series` (§19.50 — the carry-forward rule the P&L `coa.build_inputs` and the GP report `_compute_gp` both book) | no |
| those rows folded per store | `commcalc/expenses_effective.totals_by_store` | **NEW — §COMMCALC-18.3** |
| which store a spelling IS | `account/store_identity.store_key` over `coa.store_resolver` (§64) | no |
| the store→market stamp | `core.scope.store_market_resolver` via `router._store_market_resolver` | no |
| accessory dollars | the shared `_is_accessory` classifier via `sales_comparison.tally` | no |
| the % change | `sales_comparison._pct` | no |

No migration, no new endpoint, no new table, no route-pin change. The commission engine is not
touched (that thread owns it); the Peer Sales Comparison is not touched (its accessory column is
`peer_comparison._ratio`, a per-box ratio inside one month — a different question).

### §COMMCALC-18.3 ONE FACT, ONE HOME: `expenses_effective.totals_by_store`

`effective_series` said WHICH rows a month books; summing them **per store** was then re-spelled at
every call site. That is the copy-not-dereference shape the house rules forbid, and the fold is
exactly where this platform has been bitten twice — `coa._norm_store` only STRIPS, so `'b-1115'`
and `'B-1115'` became two stores holding one store's money (2026-10-09), and the leading-street-number
joins dropped money whose token no store row led with (§64).

So the fold is **one pure function with the store-identity fold INJECTED**:

```
expenses_effective.totals_by_store(rows, store_key_of=None) -> {store key: total $}
```

`store_key_of` is `store_identity.store_key(resolve, …)` partially applied. `None` keeps the raw
stripped spelling, which is byte-identical to what a code-keyed reader already did — so
`GET /commcalc/expenses-trend` was wired to it with **no change in output**, and the Sales Comparison
passes the real fold because **it has to**: the sale feed spells a store by its **ADDRESS**
(`5619 N. Broad St.`) and `store_expenses` spells it by its **CODE** (`B-103`). Without the fold the
two vocabularies cannot meet at all. Measured live (house org, September 2026): **28 of 28** expense
stores join a store with sales, **$381,345.94 of $381,345.94**, nothing stranded.

### §COMMCALC-18.4 AN EXPENSE IS NOT AN ITEM SOLD

The expense line is reported BESIDE the sales, never inside them. Pinned, not asserted
(`harness_sales_comparison.py` §E5 runs the same fixture with and without expenses and requires
every per-item total, the revenue, the GP and the transaction count to come back **byte-identical**):

- It is its own category, flagged `expense: True`, last in the order, and **absent** from the payload
  entirely when no expenses are handed in — so every existing caller is unchanged.
- It never enters `overall.current_rev`, any per-item tile, or the transaction count. Its totals live
  on their own keys (`overall.current_exp` / `previous_exp` / `exp_pct`, and `expenses_meta`).
- Its unit fields are **0**, because an expense has no unit; `pct` mirrors `rev_pct` so sorting the
  table on *Change %* sorts this row on the only change it has.
- On screen it is a tile beside Revenue, with the change colour **inverted** — spending more is not
  the green that selling more is.
- **Reported ONCE per store.** When several sale spellings fold to one store the expense lands on
  that store's canonical row and the spellings it covers are named in `expenses_meta.store_merges`;
  a row per spelling would multiply one month of rent (§E7 is the regression).
- **A store that spent money and sold nothing is still reported** (§E8), with `rev_pct: None` rather
  than a fabricated 0%.
- **A carried month says so.** `expenses_meta.base_carried_from` / `compare_carried_from` name the
  month the figures came from, and the screen prints it — a carried month is the P&L's own rule, not
  an estimate, but the reader is told rather than left to assume the sheet was re-entered. Live: the
  house org has **Mar–Sep** entered, so a base month of **2026-10** carries September's
  $381,345.94 and the notice names it.
- **An expense read that FAILS leaves the line off, never $0.00.** A zero expense makes every store
  look profitable — the dangerous half of §COMMCALC-03.28, which had no symptom.
- The same RBAC keyset and store / market picks that filter the sale rows filter these, tried on the
  store CODE, its canonical spelling, and the kept sale stores' canonical set (the picker's options
  are sale-feed spellings).

### §COMMCALC-18.5 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

`harness_expense_one_path.py` §G (now **137 passed / 0 failed**, was 129):

- **G4/G5/G6** — the expenses trend dereferences `totals_by_store`; the Sales Comparison dereferences
  `effective_series`, `totals_by_store` **and** `store_key`. A caller that stops fails the build.
- **G1/G2/G3** — the fold is pure, takes its store rule as an argument, and states no identity rule
  of its own (no `.upper()`, no squash, no token split).
- **G7** — **no second copy**: a scan for the retired shape (a `store_code` read feeding an `amount`
  sum) anywhere in the router or the chart of accounts.
- **G8** — the negative control: G7's scanner is proved to FIND that shape in a control string, so
  G7 cannot pass blind.

`harness_sales_comparison.py` §E1–§E8 proves the fold, the carry rule (incl. a `source_key` system
row NOT carrying), the leak test, the accessory dollar change, the merge regression and the
sold-nothing store — DB-free.

### §COMMCALC-18.6 MEASURED LIVE (house org, read-only, 2026-10-17)

September vs August 2026, the real modules over the real feed: **accessory sales $93,692.94 vs
$107,432.72 = −$13,739.78 (−12.8%)** while **store expenses rose $370,394.59 → $381,345.94
(+3.0%)** across 28 stores — the comparison the owner asked for, and it reads the wrong way on both
sides. Revenue and transaction counts came back identical with and without the expense line.

Files: `commcalc/expenses_effective.py` (`totals_by_store`), `commcalc/sales_comparison.py`
(`category_defs(with_expenses=)`, `_expense_cell`, `build(expenses=, store_key_of=)`),
`commcalc/router.py` (`sales_comparison` expense read; `expenses_trend` rewired),
`frontend/…/commcalc/sales-comparison/page.tsx`, `frontend/src/lib/reports.ts`,
`backend/harness_sales_comparison.py` §E, `backend/harness_expense_one_path.py` §G.

## §COMMCALC-19. THE FIGURES AT THE TOP OF A REPORT ARE SOMETHING YOU CAN SEND (owner ask 2026-10-19)

Owner, verbatim: *"on the sales comparison dashboard it shoudl give an option to send teh snapshot of
the top part to to the desired people"* — pasted with the live screen, which also carried the defect
§COMMCALC-19.4 is about.

### §COMMCALC-19.1 WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING, and the class

Sending already had ONE home: `frontend/src/lib/send-report.tsx` (`SendReportButton`). It already does
everything the ask names — the recipient picker over employees and saved contacts, free-typed email
addresses and WhatsApp numbers, the channel ladder, an optional message, and delivery through
`POST /notify/send-file` so the send lands in the Notify history. **Nothing about sending needed
building.**

What was missing is CONTENT. That button can only send an `ExportPayload`, and `<ReportShell>` only
ever handed it the **table**. So every report in the house could mail its ROWS and no report could mail
the FIGURES a manager actually reads — the tile row at the top.

**THE CLASS, not the instance:** *a number on screen that nobody can send is a number that gets retyped
into an email.* The instance was one dashboard. The fix is therefore a **shared converter** —
`frontend/src/lib/tile-snapshot.ts` — not a snapshot block inside the Sales Comparison page. The next
report that wants this calls `tileSnapshotSheet` and gets the same columns, the same ordering and the
same honesty rule for free. A per-page snapshot builder would have been exactly the sibling derivation
the duplicate gate forbids.

### §COMMCALC-19.2 DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate) — WHAT WAS REUSED, NOT REBUILT

| The question | Who already answers it | Built here? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| who may this go to, over which channel, with what message | `frontend/src/lib/send-report.tsx` `SendReportButton` | **no — reused whole** |
| how does a file reach a recipient and the Notify history | `POST /notify/send-file` → `notify/digest_delivery` channel ladder | **no** |
| how is an `ExportPayload` turned into .xlsx / .pdf | `frontend/src/lib/export.tsx` (`renderExcelBase64` / `renderPdfBase64`) | **no** |
| what shape is a SENT tile row | *nothing — surveyed ~20 tile pages; no path answered it* | **NEW — §COMMCALC-19.3** |
| can this month-over-month expense change be measured at all | *nothing* | **NEW — §COMMCALC-19.4** |

### §COMMCALC-19.3 ONE FACT, ONE HOME: `tile-snapshot.tileSnapshotSheet`

`frontend/src/lib/tile-snapshot.ts` is THE home for "the tile row as something you can send". It fixes
the sheet's shape once — **Measure | This period | Compared period | Change | Note** — so a manager
comparing two reports' snapshots is not re-learning the layout, and it owns two rules a page may not
restate:

* **money is honoured per ROW**, not per column, because a tile row legitimately mixes units and
  dollars (487 phones beside $31,298.61 of accessories);
* **an absent figure is BLANK, never 0.** The same rule `export.money` already applies to a withheld
  money cell — and it matters MORE here, because a snapshot outlives the screen and carries no small
  print, so a fabricated `$0.00` in a mailed sheet is read as a measurement (§19.49's class).

The change label is a **tri-state**, and that is the whole reason the module exists rather than a
one-line formatter: a measured percent; `null` → `new` (no base to divide by); `measured: false` →
`not measured`, with the reason printed in the Note.

The Sales Comparison page says only WHICH tiles it has and what each one means, and it builds them from
the SAME `totals_by_category` / `overall` objects the tiles render from — not a second read and not a
re-derivation — so what lands in someone's inbox cannot say anything the screen does not.

### §COMMCALC-19.4 THE ±0% THAT WAS A LIE: `sales_comparison.expense_change_measured`

The owner's own paste of the screen read **"Store expenses $276,162.69 ± 0% was $276,162.69"**.

Measured: that figure is **August 2026, 288 rows** of one tenant's `store_expenses`, and that tenant's
sheet **ends at August**. So a base month of October and a compare month of September both inherited
the SAME carried sheet, and the report divided it by itself. The carry-forward rule (§19.50) was
behaving exactly as the P&L books it; the **percent** was the lie. "± 0%" reads as *spending held
steady*, when the truth is that nobody had entered either month.

`expense_change_measured(base_carried_from, compare_carried_from)` is the one home for the question
*can this change be measured at all*. Both windows inheriting the same month → **False**, and it
compares the two through `expenses_effective.period_sort_key`, so `2026-08` and `August 2026` are one
sheet rather than two. The flag then rides the whole way:

| Link | Where |
| --- | --- |
| the predicate | `commcalc/sales_comparison.expense_change_measured` |
| the payload | `expenses_meta.change_measured`, and `pct` / `overall.exp_pct` **withheld as `None`** |
| each grid row and the total | `rev_pct` / `pct` `None`, `change_measured: False` |
| the tile | grey **not measured** instead of a percent, plus an amber panel naming the carried month |
| the SENT row | the same words, and the reason in the Note column |

The FIGURES are untouched — they are what each month books. `rev_delta` stays `0.00` because that IS
the subtraction. It is the **percent** that is a claim, so the percent is the thing withheld. *An
absence is reported with its reason, never as a result.*

### §COMMCALC-19.5 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

| Lock | What fails the build |
| --- | --- |
| `frontend/prove_tile_snapshot.mjs` (**41 checks**) | drives the REAL `tile-snapshot.ts` under Node 22 type-stripping — the fixed column order, all three states of the change label with the owner's own $276,162.69 as the regression, blank-never-zero, money per row, the caller's order preserved, purity, and a negative control for each |
| `backend/harness_tile_snapshot.py` (**45 checks**) | the WIRING: the page dereferences the converter and declares no snapshot columns of its own; **no other frontend file spells the snapshot's headers**; the page spells no notify endpoint beside `SendReportButton`; the five links of the honesty chain above, each one named; the proof is run by a workflow whose path filter covers every file it reads; registration here |
| `backend/harness_sales_comparison.py` §F | `expense_change_measured` on its own and through the real `build`: the regression, the withheld percent, the untouched figures, one-side-carried still measured, two DIFFERENT carried months still measured, and the §E5 leak test repeated for this path |

### §COMMCALC-19.6 WHAT IS NOT DONE HERE

The converter is shared, but only this report is wired to it. Rolling the Send button onto the other
tile pages (Peer Sales Comparison, Spiff Impact, the Manager Report Cards, the Management Overview
tiles) is a page-by-page wiring job with no new mechanism, and it is offered rather than taken.

Files: `frontend/src/lib/tile-snapshot.ts` (**new**), `frontend/prove_tile_snapshot.mjs` (**new**),
`backend/harness_tile_snapshot.py` (**new**), `backend/app/modules/commcalc/sales_comparison.py`
(`expense_change_measured`), `frontend/…/commcalc/sales-comparison/page.tsx`,
`backend/harness_sales_comparison.py` §F, `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml`.

## §COMMCALC-23. A FACT THE PLATFORM MEASURES PER MONTH MAY NOT BE INHERITED FROM ANOTHER MONTH (owner directive 2026-10-20)

Owner, verbatim: *"sepatember and october expeses wll be carried forward but salary and commisson
shoudl be derived from the actuals"*.

### §COMMCALC-23.1 THE CLASS, stated once so nobody re-derives it

**A fact the platform MEASURES per month was being inherited from another month by a rule written for
facts that genuinely repeat.** Rent repeats. A lease, a utility, an insurance premium: entering them
once and carrying them forward is right, and that is what the carry-forward rule (§19.50) is for.
Payroll does not repeat — it is measured, every month, from hours and from calculated commission.

The dangerous half is that the result is a PLAUSIBLE NUMBER rather than a blank. A missing figure gets
noticed; a wrong figure of the right size does not. This is the same class as §19.49 (*an absence is
reported with its reason, never as a result*), seen from the other side: here an absence was reported
as **another month's measurement**.

### §COMMCALC-23.2 MEASURED LIVE, 2026-10-20, before the fix

Every one of the **3,724** `store_expenses` rows in the house is `source_key` NULL — i.e. hand-entered
— so every one of them carries. What that meant per tenant:

| Tenant | What a carried month showed | Of which was another month's payroll |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Luxelink Wireless LLC | September **and** October both read **$276,162.69** (its sheet ends at August 2026) | **$159,512.55** — Employee Salaries $133,460.00, DM Salaries $25,500.01, Employee Commission $552.54 |
| Cellfonz R Us | October read **$381,345.94** (carried from September) | **$143,735.94** — Employee Salaries $127,289.93, Employee Commission $16,446.01 |
| Vzone | September and October read **$12,605.00** (carried from July 2026) | **$7,000.00** |
| NY LOGISTICS | $6,493.00 | **$0.00** — it enters no labour on the sheet, so nothing changes for it |

Luxelink's $276,162.69 is the very figure on the screen the owner pasted the day before — **58% of it
was last August's payroll**, which is also why its `± 0%` (§COMMCALC-19.4) was two copies of one sheet.

### §COMMCALC-23.3 DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate) — WHAT WAS REUSED, NOT REBUILT

| The question | Who already answers it | Built here? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| which expense rows are labour the platform derives and books elsewhere | `commcalc/labour_vocabulary.resolve` (§4e) | **no — extended with a narrow exact-name test, `derived_row_names` / `is_derived_row`** |
| what does this store spend in a month it never saved | `commcalc/expenses_effective.effective_series` (§19.50) | **no — given a `derived_names` parameter; the rule itself is unchanged** |
| what did this month's hours cost, per store | `account/coa.wages_by_store` → `derive_wage_cells` (§14y) | **no — dereferenced** |
| what rep commission does this month owe | `commcalc.rep_commissions.total_payout`, the figure the P&L books on `rep_comm` | **no — dereferenced** |
| which store is this address | `account/store_identity.store_key` / `store_identity_index` (§64) | **no — injected** |
| how do those two figures become expense-sheet rows for ONE month, per store | *nothing* | **NEW — §COMMCALC-23.4** |

### §COMMCALC-23.4 ONE FACT, ONE HOME: `commcalc/labour_actuals`

`backend/app/modules/commcalc/labour_actuals.py` is THE home for *"what did this month's
platform-derived labour actually cost, per store"*. **It derives no dollars of its own** — no rate
times hours, no feed read. It assembles the figures the platform already derives, and its only new
decision is the SHAPE: `as_expense_rows` emits rows that look like `store_expenses` rows, so a reader
that already sums an expense sheet picks up the month's own labour with no arithmetic change.

Three rules it owns, and the reason each one is a rule rather than a convenience:

* **The halves stay apart.** `fold` returns salary and commission separately. The first draft returned
  a blended per-store total and split it by ratio where only one half was wanted — an invented
  per-store number, which is the kind of plausible arithmetic this house treats as a defect.
* **The CALLER chooses the halves, because the right answer differs per surface and the difference is
  money.** A surface whose only labour figure is the expense sheet takes BOTH. The GP report takes
  **salary only** — `net_profit` already subtracts `rep_pay` from `rep_commissions`, so a commission
  row here would subtract the same dollars twice. The P&L takes **neither**: it derives `wages` and
  `rep_comm` from these very sources itself, so it needs the carried rows gone and nothing put back.
* **An unmeasured half is reported, never shipped as a zero.** `measured` is per half, and a half that
  could not be read contributes no rows at all. A zero labour cost makes every store look profitable,
  which is the dangerous direction.

Rows are stamped `source_key='labour_actual'`, so the carry rule can never take a measurement of ONE
month into another: they are system rows, and system rows have never carried.

### §COMMCALC-23.5 THE FIVE READERS, AND WHY THE P&L IS NOT ONE OF THEM

| Reader | Gets back |
| --- | --- |
| the live P&L (`account/coa`) | **nothing** — the carried labour rows are gone and it derives both halves itself |
| the GP report (`/commcalc/gp-report`) | **salary only** (commission is already on `rep_pay`) |
| the expenses trend (`/commcalc/expenses-trend`) | both halves, per month, plus `labour_unmeasured` |
| the Sales Comparison expense line (`/commcalc/sales-comparison`) | both halves, per month, plus `labour_measured` and what the carried sheet was not allowed to hand over |
| the takeover evaluation's cost benchmark (`_prospect_expense_window`) | both halves, per month in the averaging window |

The plumbing those readers share — resolve the vocabulary, resolve the store identity, read the month's
actuals, relabel canonical → store code — has ONE home too, `router._labour_actuals_code_keyed`. Four
steps written out four times is how one of them later gets a filter the others never got.

### §COMMCALC-23.6 WHAT THE NUMBERS BECOME

| Tenant / month | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Luxelink, September 2026 | $276,162.69 (all August) | **$242,305.37** = August rent $116,650.14 + September's own salary $112,951.52 + commission $12,703.71 |
| Luxelink, October 2026 | $276,162.69 (all August) | **$198,299.57** = $116,650.14 + salary $79,504.18 + commission $2,145.25 |
| Cellfonz R Us, October 2026 | $381,345.94 (all September) | **$239,728.48 and INCOMPLETE** — $237,610.00 carried + commission $2,118.48, with the **salary stated as not measured** |
| Cellfonz R Us, September 2026 | $381,345.94 | **unchanged** — it has its own sheet, and the rule only ever concerns a CARRIED month |

The Cellfonz October row is the point of the honesty rule. `coa.wages_by_store` REFUSES that month:
only **49.38%** of its 403 scheduled employee-days carry a punch or a correction, and 204 of them have
neither, so paying it would pay those days nothing (§14y's interlock). Before this change that refusal
was invisible, because September's payroll was sitting in the figure. Now the report says the salary is
unknown — **which is a missing-clock-data defect to fix, not an expense figure to read.**

### §COMMCALC-23.7 THE ± 0% GETS ITS PERCENT BACK, FOR A REASON

`sales_comparison.expense_change_measured` (§COMMCALC-19.4) withheld the percent when both windows
carried the SAME sheet. Once each month supplies its own labour that is no longer one sheet compared
with itself — the labour half of each figure is that month's own measurement — so the predicate now
takes `base_month_labour` / `compare_month_labour` and reports the change as measured, with the screen
saying that the rest still comes from one inherited sheet. **§19.49 cuts both ways: a measurement must
not be suppressed any more than an absence may be asserted.**

### §COMMCALC-23.8 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

A registry written and its callers left reading past it has happened three times here (§19.18), so the
wiring is what the build checks:

| Lock | What fails the build |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/harness_expense_one_path.py` §H (**11 checks**) | **every live caller of the carry rule passes the labour vocabulary** — the scanner reads each call's balanced argument text, and has a negative control proving it can see an un-wired call; the five readers are counted; no caller spells the row names; the keying plumbing is one helper, not a copy per reader |
| `backend/harness_labour_actuals.py` (**90 checks**) | the halves match the vocabulary exactly; `fold` is pure, total and keeps the halves apart; the row shape, naming and `source_key`; an unmeasured half contributes nothing; **the regression** — the $276,162.69 month reproduced and closed over the real carry rule; the I/O shell's `measured` verdict, including a failed read; RULE TWO and purity |
| `backend/harness_sales_comparison.py` §G | a carried month's own labour makes the change measurable again, and a month that measured nothing is back to one sheet |
| `backend/harness_labour_vocabulary.py` §G4 | still no second copy of the vocabulary — it caught this PR spelling the house row names in `labour_actuals` |
| `app/modules/core/module_graph.py` | `derived_labour_actuals` — the fact, its home, its callers and its locks, added BY HAND (§50) |

### §COMMCALC-23.9 WHAT IS NOT DONE HERE

* **No migration and no money moved on its own.** Nothing is written; every figure above is a READ.
  The live P&L is unchanged because it never read the carried labour rows. The GP report and the
  Sales Comparison are live reads, so they restate on deploy; the **stored** consolidated P&L
  snapshots only restate when the owner presses Recompute.
* **A hand-typed labour row nobody derives still carries.** The membership test is the vocabulary's
  EXACT names, not its broad cross-month protection tokens, so `Owner / Mgmt Salaries` and
  `Dm Salary` (a Cellfonz spelling nothing fills in) keep carrying forward. That is the safe default:
  the platform has no actual for them, so withholding them would understate the month. A tenant that
  wants one of them treated as derived names it in its own vocabulary — a config row, not code.
* **`GET /commcalc/commission-by-store` still bridges store vocabularies by leading street number**,
  the join §64 replaced. It is an auto-fill for a sheet a human then edits, and it belongs to another
  owner's feature, so it is named here rather than quietly rewritten.

Files: `backend/app/modules/commcalc/labour_actuals.py` (**new**),
`backend/harness_labour_actuals.py` (**new**),
`backend/app/modules/commcalc/labour_vocabulary.py` (`derived_row_names`, `is_derived_row`),
`backend/app/modules/commcalc/expenses_effective.py` (`carryable_rows`, `excluded_summary`,
`derived_names`), `backend/app/modules/account/coa.py`,
`backend/app/modules/commcalc/router.py` (`_labour_actuals_code_keyed` + the four readers),
`backend/app/modules/commcalc/sales_comparison.py`, `backend/app/modules/core/module_graph.py`,
`backend/harness_expense_one_path.py` §H, `backend/harness_sales_comparison.py` §G,
`frontend/…/commcalc/sales-comparison/page.tsx`, `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml`.

## §POS-02. THE RECEIPT AN ADMIN EDITS, PRINTS AND EMAILS (owner ask 2026-10-17)

Owner, verbatim: *"admin should be able to edit the receipt, teh template for the receipt for vzone
ahoul be same as uplaoded from rq, the email option should show which email to send to and it should
be editable, the from email address should show the company name Vzone Wireless or whatever name is
set up during onboarding"*.

Four asks, one mechanism: an admin edits the receipt and SEES what the edit does; a tenant whose
receipts come from its own POS can have its till slips print in that same layout; emailing a receipt
shows the address and lets it be changed BEFORE anything is sent; and the customer sees that mail
from the business's own name.

### POS-02.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched this index and the code for anything already answering *"what does this org's receipt look
like"* before building. There were **three** answers:

| Who | What it did |
| --- | --- |
| `frontend …/pos/sales/page.tsx` → `buildReceiptHtml` | assembled the till receipt's HTML **in the browser**, applying the template's toggles, the brand block and the disclaimers |
| `pos/receipt_formats/render.render_html` (§POS-IMPORT) | printed a receipt **imported** from a POS as a structured `Document`, in that POS's own layout |
| `frontend …/pos/ReceiptTemplateSection.tsx` | **hand-drew an imitation** of a receipt as the editor's preview, with a carrier and a product name written into the JSX |

So an admin editing "the receipt template" changed the first, the second kept its own look, and the
third showed neither. **EXTENDED, not duplicated:** the till slip's rules moved out of the browser
into `pos/sale_receipt.py`, which also assembles the SAME `Document` an imported receipt is parsed
into and hands it to the EXISTING `render.render_html` — no second renderer, and that module is
unchanged. The preview and the emailed copy are the same call.

Nothing new was built for the email itself either: it goes through `notify/channels/email_resend`,
the one email channel, and the config keys it reads (`email_receipt_subject` / `email_receipt_body`)
were already declared in the POS registry — marked *"not yet enforced"* since the module landed,
because nothing could render a receipt where there is no browser. That absence was not a missing
feature; it was the second answer's cost.

### POS-02.2 One fact, one home, dereferenced

| Fact | Home | Dereferenced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What this org's receipt looks like | `pos/sale_receipt.py` | the till copy, the reprint, the admin preview, the emailed copy — through `frontend/src/lib/pos-receipt.ts`, which is the only thing that spells a receipt URL |
| A POS setting's effective value at this store | `pos/pos_config_effective.py` (store override → org default → declared default) | every server read of the receipt's toggles, brand block and disclaimers |
| What this tenant is called | `core/tenant_identity.py` | the From name on every business-facing email, `_tenant_display_name`, the data-QA sentence, the operator company picker, the helpdesk facet, the payroll statements |
| How a `From:` header is assembled | `notify/channels/email_resend.from_header` | all ~25 send sites — one place strips quotes and brackets so a tenant's name cannot forge a second header |
| Which layout prints | `pos.receipt_templates.layout` (mig `1089`) × `pos/sale_receipt.LAYOUTS` | the renderer, the PATCH validator, the migration's CHECK — all three read the same two names |

### POS-02.3 The second copy that could not be removed, and the lock that holds it

The store-override → org-default → declared-default rule for `pos.pos_settings` existed **only** in
`frontend/src/lib/pos-config.ts`. The server now has to resolve the same settings to render a
receipt, and a TypeScript registry cannot be dereferenced from Python — so there are two copies by
necessity. They are pinned rather than trusted: `harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §B reads the `default:`
literals straight out of `pos-config.ts` with a regex and compares them key by key against
`pos_config_effective.SERVER_DEFAULTS`, failing the build and **naming the key** when one side drifts.
A default changed in the browser alone is a red build, not a receipt that quietly prints differently.

### POS-02.4 The fallback is said out loud

`layout = 'pos_format'` means *"print it the way the POS this org declared does"*. A tenant can ask
for that and have declared no POS — today **two of the four tenants have no `commcalc.pos_profile`
row at all**. The renderer prints the till slip in that case (never nothing), and `layout_note`
carries the sentence saying so, which the editor and the receipt response both show. The same shape
as the `basis` rule in §COMMCALC-66: a last-resort placement must not read as evidence that it was
chosen.

### POS-02.5 A receipt restates a sale — it does not re-price it

Every printed figure comes from the `pos.sales.receipt` JSONB snapshot the checkout stored. The
renderer does exactly ONE piece of arithmetic — when discounts are shown on their own line, the
Subtotal row shows the GROSS figure, so `Subtotal − Discounts + Tax` adds back to the total the
customer actually paid (§A of the harness proves the identity). A sale with no stored snapshot is
**refused**, with a sentence saying only register sales carry one; it is never rendered from the sale
row's own totals, because a receipt reconstructed from a different source is a second answer to what
the customer paid.

### POS-02.6 Siblings checked, fixed or EXCUSED in writing

| Sibling | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `pos/receipt_formats/render.py` (imported receipts) | **reused unchanged** — the till sale becomes the same `Document` |
| `pos/sales_from_reports.resolve_format` | **reused** as the one reader of "which POS did this org declare" |
| The editor's hand-drawn preview | **deleted**; it now renders the real thing in an iframe |
| 8 ad-hoc `select("name")` reads of `storeops.tenants` | **rewired** to `core/tenant_identity` (`commcalc/router` ×2, `core/data_qa_api`, `core/operator_api`, `helpdesk/router`, `storeops/payroll_approval` ×2, `storeops/router._tenant_display_name` — which used to fall back to the PLATFORM's name for a tenant's own mail) |
| `core/router._mint_tenant_alias` | **EXCUSED** — reads `slug,name` as a slug fallback for a login alias, not as the business's display name |
| Multi-column reads of the tenant row (`hr/letters`, `commcalc/agency`, `core/router` tenant lists) | **EXCUSED in the lock** — the name rides along with that row's other columns; it is the row being read, not this fact re-derived |
| `core/auth_notify._email_otp` (sign-in / reset OTP) | **EXCUSED deliberately** — a platform credential email IS from the platform; only the invite, which already holds the tenant's name, sends under it |

### POS-02.7 What the admin and the cashier now do

- **Admin** (Receipt Template): edits the fields as before, now picks the layout, sees the line
  *"Emailed receipts come from …"* with the actual name the customer will see, and watches a live
  preview that is the real renderer's output, debounced 400 ms.
- **Cashier** (checkout / reprint): prints the server's copy; the receipt modal shows
  **"Email the receipt to:"** pre-filled with the customer's own address, editable before sending,
  and says who it comes from. Typing an address where the capture prompt was pending saves it to the
  customer too, so the next sale already knows it.

### POS-02.8 Files, locks, and what is waiting on the owner

| | |
| --- | --- |
| New | `backend/app/modules/pos/sale_receipt.py` (pure) · `backend/app/modules/pos/pos_config_effective.py` (pure) · `backend/app/modules/core/tenant_identity.py` · `frontend/src/lib/pos-receipt.ts` · `backend/harness_pos_receipt_render.py` (127 checks) · `database/migrations/1089_pos_receipt_layout.sql` |
| Endpoints | `GET /pos/sales/{sale_id}/receipt` · `POST /pos/sales/{sale_id}/email-receipt` · `POST /pos/receipt-template/preview` (+ `layout`, `layout_options`, `layout_note`, `pos_format`, `from_name`, `layout_column_ready` on `GET /pos/receipt-template`) |
| Locks | `harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §B (the two config copies), §E6 (a second tenant-name reader fails the build), §H (the register builds no HTML, the editor draws no imitation), §I (endpoints + registration) |
| WAITING ON THE OWNER | **migration `1089`** — one additive column with a default equal to today's behaviour. Printing and emailing work before it is applied; applying it turns the layout CHOICE on |
| MONEY IMPACT | **NONE** — a receipt restates a sale already rung; no P&L, GP, commission, payout or tax path reads any of this |
| RULE TWO | no tenant, carrier, POS or product name appears in any new module, nor in the preview's sample sale; `pos_format` resolves through the org's own declaration |

Same class: §COMMCALC-66 (a fallback must not read as evidence), §19.18 (a registry written and its
callers left unwired is not a fix), §POS-01 (one home for the cart, one client that spells the URLs).

## §POS-03. THE FORMAT A RECEIPT PRINTS IN, CHOSEN AT THE COUNTER (owner ask 2026-10-19)

Owner, verbatim: *"all stores should have the option to print the print in the required format from
the print receipt screen as there are receipts from the thermal printer also amd teh system should be
able to add the driver of the thermanl printer epson or citizen"*.

### POS-03.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index for an existing mechanism before building. **`pos/sale_receipt.py` (§POS-02) is
already the one renderer** and already holds the layout vocabulary (`LAYOUTS`) and the paper
vocabulary (`PAPER_PX`, `paper_width_mm` / `font_size_px` on `pos.receipt_templates`). **Nothing
anywhere supported a printer**, per-store or otherwise — no table, no setting, no driver path. So
this EXTENDS the renderer with ONE resolver and the existing `pos.pos_settings` kv table with three
store keys; it adds no second print path, no second format list and NO migration.

### POS-03.2 The class that was wrong

Not "this store cannot print 58 mm". The general fact that was wrong: **the layout was a single
stored per-ORG value, as if an organisation printed one way.** One counter prints the same sale on a
thermal roll and, minutes later, on the office laser; an admin serving one of them changed it for
every store. The class is *"which format THIS print uses is a question with three answers in
precedence order, not one stored value"* — so the fix is a resolver, for every caller of the
renderer, not a flag for the store that complained.

### POS-03.3 One fact, one home, dereferenced

| Fact | Its one home |
| --- | --- |
| Which layout and which paper THIS print uses, and WHICH of the three said so | `pos/sale_receipt.print_choice` — request → store declaration → org template, each validated against the renderer's OWN `LAYOUTS` / `PAPER_PX` |
| What this store prints receipts on | `pos_config_effective.printer` (`receipt_printer_label`, `receipt_paper_width_mm`, `receipt_layout` on `pos.pos_settings`) |
| What the screen may OFFER | `sale_receipt.layout_options` / `sale_receipt.paper_options`, both DERIVED (`paper_options` from `PAPER_PX`) and handed to the browser on the receipt response — the picker declares no formats of its own |
| The choice as wire fields | `frontend/src/lib/pos-receipt.ts::choiceParams`, used by BOTH the print path and the email path, so the emailed copy cannot be a different format from the paper one |
| The picker itself | `frontend/src/components/pos/PrintFormatPicker.tsx`, used by the till's completion modal AND the Sale Log reprint |

### POS-03.4 A blank setting is not a width

`printer()` returns **blank** for a store that never declared, not a guessed 80 mm. That is the
difference between honouring a declaration and inventing one, and it is what lets `print_choice`
report `paper_source: "org"` instead of pretending the store asked.

### POS-03.5 Nothing is stored at print time

The request applies to ONE print. `with_choice` lays it over a COPY of the template row, so one
cashier's pick cannot leak into the next receipt, and a fresh sale starts from the store's own
declared setting again. An unusable request (a layout the tenant cannot print, a width this renderer
does not have) resolves exactly as a stored one would and `layout_note` says what will actually come
out — never a silent substitution.

### POS-03.6 The thermal printer, and what the system can honestly do about it

The owner's second half — *"the system should be able to add the driver of the thermal printer
epson or citizen"*. Browsers cannot install a printer driver, and a web page cannot address a USB
till printer without one; what the operating system already does well is own the driver. So what
ships is the half that is ours: **each store DECLARES its printer** (`receipt_printer_label`, free
text) and the print screen says what the slip is sized for and offers the matching width, while the
driver stays with Windows/macOS and the browser's own print dialog picks the device. Raw ESC/POS
(printing to the device directly, no dialog) needs a helper installed at the till and is a separate
decision, put to the owner rather than assumed. RULE TWO holds either way: a printer make is text a
store types into a config row and is **never branched on in code** — locked by §K10.

### POS-03.7 Siblings checked

| Path that answers "what does this print look like" | Done |
| --- | --- |
| The till's completion modal | Picker, defaulting to what the server resolved |
| The Sale Log reprint | Same picker, same resolver — a reprint is often at a different counter with different paper |
| The emailed copy | Carries the SAME choice (§K13), so the customer's copy is the one handed over |
| `receipt_auto_print` | Prints with no request, i.e. the store's own declaration — correct by construction |
| The admin preview (`POST /pos/receipt-template/preview`) | EXCUSED: it previews the ORG TEMPLATE being edited, which is the thing a store's declaration overrides; a per-print choice there would preview something nobody saved |

### POS-03.8 Files, locks, money

| | |
| --- | --- |
| New | `frontend/src/components/pos/PrintFormatPicker.tsx` · `sale_receipt.print_choice` / `paper_options` / `clean_paper` / `with_choice` · `pos_config_effective.printer` + 3 keys · `harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §K |
| Endpoints | NO new route — `GET /pos/sales/{sale_id}/receipt` gains `layout` / `paper_width_mm` query params, `POST /pos/sales/{sale_id}/email-receipt` the same two body fields |
| Migration | **NONE** — the three store settings are rows in the existing `pos.pos_settings` kv table |
| Locks | §K (the precedence, the derived option lists, the copy, the blank-is-not-a-width rule, RULE TWO on printer makes), §B (the three new defaults pinned key-by-key to the browser registry — change one side only and the build goes red) |
| MONEY IMPACT | **NONE** — a receipt restates a sale already rung |

Same class: §POS-02 (one renderer), §COMMCALC-66 (a fallback must not read as evidence).

## §POS-04. STRAIGHT TO THE RECEIPT PRINTER, WHEN A STORE ASKS FOR IT (owner ask 2026-10-20)

Owner, verbatim: *"the receipts will print to the thermal printer only if desired by the user, there
cannot be any harcoded rule so we need have a helper"*.

### POS-04.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

`pos/sale_receipt.py` (§POS-02) is already the one renderer and `print_choice` (§POS-03) is already
the one resolver for what a print uses, so the destination was ADDED to that resolver rather than
answered a second time, and the printer's byte stream renders the SAME content model as the paper
copy. `pos_config_effective` already resolves a per-store setting, so the opt-in and the helper
address are two more rows in `pos.pos_settings`. **No new endpoint, no new table, no migration.**

### POS-04.2 What a browser cannot do, stated plainly

A browser hands a page to the operating system's print dialog. It cannot speak to a USB till
printer and it cannot install a driver — so "add the Epson or Citizen driver" is, in software, two
different things. The driver belongs to Windows / macOS / CUPS and stays there. What the platform
can own is the *content* and the *route*: it renders the slip as the printer's own commands and a
small helper on the counter PC (`tools/pos-print-helper/receipt-helper.js`, Node, no dependencies)
hands them over. The helper binds `127.0.0.1` only, accepts exactly one request — *print these
bytes* — runs no command its caller names, and holds no credential.

### POS-04.3 The class that was fixed, and the trap avoided

A byte stream for the printer is a second **medium**, not a second receipt. Had it read the sale and
the template for itself, "what does this slip say" would have had two answers and they would have
drifted — the duplicate defect the index rules forbid. So `sale_receipt.slip_model` was extracted as
the ONE content home (which lines, in what order, with which figures, and the discount arithmetic
done once), and `thermal_html` was moved onto it: its output was proved **byte-identical on eight
slip variants** (80 and 58 mm, discounts folded and separate, completed and voided), so no tenant's
paper receipt changed. `receipt_escpos` renders the same model for the printer.

### POS-04.4 Nothing is hardcoded

| Decision | Where it lives |
| --- | --- |
| Does this store print straight to the printer? | `receipt_direct_print` per store, **false everywhere** until someone turns it on |
| Where does its helper listen? | `receipt_helper_url` per store (default the loopback address, so a different port needs no release) |
| Where does THIS receipt go? | the cashier's own choice on the print screen — both routes are offered on every print, and the store's setting only decides which is selected first |
| What if the helper is not running? | the receipt prints through the dialog and the cashier is **told** which route it took; a closed helper window never costs a customer their receipt |
| An unknown destination? | reads as the dialog — never a silent no-print |

### POS-04.5 Siblings checked

| Path | Done |
| --- | --- |
| The till's completion modal, the Sale Log reprint | The same picker, now with a *Send to* choice; both go through `print_choice` |
| `receipt_auto_print` | Prints with no request, i.e. on the store's declared destination — direct where the store asked for it |
| The emailed copy | Unchanged: an email has no destination, and the bytes are built only for a print that is going to the printer |
| The admin preview | EXCUSED: it previews the org template, which has no counter and no helper |
| Admin toggles (serials, tax breakdown, discounts, disclaimers, signature line) | Proved to reach the PRINTED slip, not only the paper one (§L8) |

### POS-04.6 Files, locks, money

| | |
| --- | --- |
| New | `backend/app/modules/pos/receipt_escpos.py` (pure, stdlib) · `sale_receipt.slip_model` / `PAPER_COLS` / `DESTINATIONS` / `clean_destination` / `destination_options` · `pos_config_effective.printer` + 2 keys · `tools/pos-print-helper/` (helper + step-by-step install guide) · `harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §L |
| Endpoints | NO new route — `GET /pos/sales/{sale_id}/receipt` gains a `destination` query param and five answer fields |
| Migration | **NONE** |
| Locks | §L (one content home, both media, the wrapping, the cut, the opt-in default, the dialog fallback, the helper's own limits, RULE TWO), §B (the two new defaults pinned key-by-key to the browser registry) |
| MONEY IMPACT | **NONE** — a receipt restates a sale already rung |

Same class: §POS-02 (one renderer), §POS-03 (one resolver for what a print uses), §19.18 (a registry
written and its callers left unwired is not a fix).

## §POS-05. A RECEIPT THAT WOULD NOT PRINT, AND THE ONE FACT THAT HAD THREE DERIVATIONS (owner report 2026-10-20)

Owner, verbatim: *"can tprint the reeipt from the vzone login , it says 357a4772 error"*.

### POS-05.1 What the reference was, and how it was read

`357a4772` is not a code or a setting: it is an **unhandled-500 reference**, minted by
`app/main.py::_log_system_error` (`secrets.token_hex(4)`) and handed to the caller instead of a stack
trace. The trace itself is written to stderr AND to `core.failure_log` keyed by that reference — so
the report was diagnosable without reproducing it:

```
GET /api/v1/pos/sales/{id}/receipt
  File "app/modules/pos/router.py", in _receipt_bundle
    "layout_options": _sr.layout_options(fmt.get("label") if fmt else ""),
AttributeError: module 'app.modules.pos.receipt_formats.rq' has no attribute 'get'
```

Four such crashes, 20:33–20:34 UTC, all on the same sale. **Read a `token_hex(4)` reference out of
`core.failure_log` before guessing** — that is what it is there for.

### POS-05.2 The class, not the instance

The instance is "the Vzone login cannot print". The class is: **"which receipt format has this tenant
declared" was derived three times, in two different shapes.**

`sales_from_reports.resolve_format` answers `{"ok", "pos", "format", "reason"}` where `format` is the
**registry row** `{source, label, parse, module}`. Three callers in `pos/router.py` each unpacked that
themselves — the admin editor kept the ROW (and read `.get("label")` off it), the print path narrowed
it to the **module** (which the renderer needs), and the rebuilt-sales list unpacked it a third way.
§POS-03 then needed the format's label on the print path and copied the admin screen's
`fmt.get("label")` onto the module. A module has no `.get`.

Why only one tenant: a company with **no POS declared** gets `None`, and `fmt.get("label") if fmt
else ""` never touches it. Only the company that *has* a declared, registered POS reached the broken
expression — so the defect was invisible on two of three tenants and total on the third.

### POS-05.3 The fix is one home, dereferenced

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ONE home | `sales_from_reports.declared_format(client, org_id)` → `{available, pos, label, module, reason}`, the key set named once as `DECLARED_FORMAT_KEYS` |
| ONE reader | `pos.router._declared_format` — the only thing in that router that calls `resolve_format`; nothing there unpacks the registry row any more |
| Four dereferences | `get_receipt_template` (admin editor) · `_receipt_bundle` (print, reprint, email) · `preview_receipt_template` (preview) · `sales_from_reports_list` (rebuilt sales) |
| Never raises | the declaration is a database read, and a receipt must still print on the till slip when that read fails — a failure answers `available: false` with the reason, not a 500 |

The renderer is handed `fmt["module"]`; a person is shown `fmt["label"]`; the fallback decision reads
`fmt["available"]`. No caller holds a shape of its own.

### POS-05.4 The lock

`harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §M (11 checks + 2 negative controls) fails the build if:

- `pos/router.py` calls `resolve_format` again, or grows a second reader (`_declared_format` must be
  defined once and called exactly four times);
- any caller reads `fmt.get("label")`, `fmt.get("module")` or `fmt.LABEL` by hand;
- the renderer is handed the record instead of `fmt["module"]`;
- the record's key set drifts from `DECLARED_FORMAT_KEYS`.

**M5 is the regression**: a sale of a tenant whose declared POS IS registered is run through
`_receipt_bundle` against a DB-free fake client, and the bundle must build. It raises the production
`AttributeError` on the commit before this one.

### POS-05.5 Siblings checked

| Path | Done |
| --- | --- |
| The admin editor (`GET /pos/receipt-template`) | Rewired to the one home; its own try/except and row-unpacking deleted |
| The admin preview | Rewired; hands the module to the renderer |
| The rebuilt-sales list (`GET /pos/sales-from-reports`) | Rewired; `format_label` is now `""` rather than `null` when no format is registered, which every reader of it already treats the same |
| `sales_from_reports._rebuild` (line 489) | EXCUSED — it needs `ok` and the module for the rebuild itself, which `resolve_format` answers directly; it is in the module that OWNS the resolver, not a caller re-deriving it |
| `receipt_formats.registry` | Unchanged — still the one lookup for "which formats exist" |

### POS-05.6 Files, locks, money

| | |
| --- | --- |
| New | `sales_from_reports.declared_format` + `DECLARED_FORMAT_KEYS` · `pos.router._declared_format` (replaces `_declared_receipt_format`) · `harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §M |
| Endpoints | NO new route; `GET /pos/sales/{sale_id}/receipt` stops returning a 500 for a tenant with a declared POS |
| Migration | **NONE** |
| MONEY IMPACT | **NONE** — a receipt restates a sale already rung; no figure moves |

Same class: §19.18 (a registry written and its callers left unwired is not a fix), §POS-02 (one
renderer), §POS-03 (one resolver for what a print uses).

## §POS-06. PAY BY BANK TRANSFER — THE ACCOUNT A RECEIPT TELLS A CUSTOMER TO PAY INTO (owner ask 2026-10-21)

Owner, verbatim: *"need to add the option of adding the payment information to the customer when
creating the receipt for the customer as a check mark, two boxes to fill out routing number and
account number to be sent to the customer, tehy will be saved in the register set up"*.

### POS-06.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index and the tree for an existing home for bank numbers before building. **Two exist,
and neither answers this question:** HR's direct-deposit intake holds an EMPLOYEE's own account
(`storeops.employee_onboarding_profile.intake_data`, masked and encrypted, §CORE-04) and
`storeops/store_lease.ACH_FIELDS` holds a LANDLORD's, for paying rent. This is the business's own
account, read by a customer, so it is a third subject — but the HOUSE RULES those two established
are reused rather than re-derived: encrypted at rest through `core.crypto`, a family registered in
`core.encryption_backfill.SWEEPS`, and masked to the last four wherever a screen can see it.

Nothing new was created for the receipt itself. `print_choice` (§POS-03) already resolves what THIS
print uses, so the tick is a field on it; `slip_model` (§POS-04) already is the one content home with
two renderers, so the paragraph is an ordinary footer block and **`receipt_escpos.py` did not change
at all**; `pos_config_effective` already resolves store-override → org-default, so the numbers are
two more rows in `pos.pos_settings`. **No new table, no migration.** One new endpoint, because the
generic settings save could not be used — see §POS-06.4.

### POS-06.2 What it does, in the owner's own terms

| His words | Where it is |
| --- | --- |
| "as a check mark" | A tick on the print receipt screen, in the one picker both the till's completion modal and the Sale Log reprint use. **Off on every receipt**: there is no stored default, because which customer is paying by transfer is known at the counter and nowhere else. |
| "two boxes to fill out routing number and account number" | `ReceiptRemitFields` — one editor, in POS → Settings → Pay by bank transfer. |
| "to be sent to the customer" | The paragraph prints on the till slip, on the emailed copy, in the printer's own byte stream and in the tenant's own POS layout. |
| "they will be saved in the register set up" | `pos.pos_settings`, per store with a company default — the same register setup every other receipt setting lives in. |

### POS-06.3 Who may set it, and who may only tick it

The boxes are gated on `pos_settings`, like every other setting write; the tick is open to anybody
who can print a receipt. That split is deliberate and it is the main security decision in this
section: **a cashier who could type a routing number onto a customer's receipt could redirect that
customer's payment**, and a receipt is a document people trust without checking. So the counter
chooses WHETHER the account prints, never WHICH account it is. The print screen shows the account
masked (`Routing ••••0021 · Account ••••7890`) so staff can confirm the right one before printing,
and says where to set it when nothing is declared rather than offering a tick that prints nothing.

### POS-06.4 Why these two settings needed an endpoint of their own

`GET /pos/settings` is the register's own config read — every signed-in POS user reaches it and every
POS screen receives what it answers. A bank account in that payload would be casually readable by
every POS login, which is the 2026-10-12 class (§CORE-04: two employees' routing numbers found in
plain text). So these two keys, and only these two, are answered MASKED.

That makes the generic settings editor unusable for them, and the trap is sharper than it looks: a
text box would show `••••7890`, and `digits("••••7890")` is `"7890"` — **a perfectly valid
four-digit account number.** The real account would have been replaced by its own last four the
first time anybody pressed Save on that screen, every receipt printed afterwards would have carried
a number that cannot be paid into, and nothing would have looked wrong at any point. The negative
control written for this section is what found it. Two things stop it now: `PosSettingDef.sensitive`
makes the generic editor skip the key entirely, and `receipt_remit._refuse_mask` refuses any value
carrying the mask character before length or checksum are even considered.

### POS-06.5 A wrong number is the expensive failure, so it is refused at the save

A receipt is the one place a wrong bank number costs real money: the customer pays, it goes nowhere,
and nobody finds out until they chase it. So the number is validated BEFORE it is stored, never at
print time:

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Routing: nine digits AND the ABA check digit (`3·(d1+d4+d7) + 7·(d2+d5+d8) + (d3+d6+d9) ≡ 0 mod 10`) | Arithmetic over a published format, naming no bank. Every real routing number satisfies it; a transposed pair of digits — the typo that would otherwise reach a customer — almost never does. 40 of any 400 consecutive nine-digit numbers pass, which is the negative control. |
| Account: 4–17 digits | There is no checksum to lean on, so length is the only honest check. |
| Either one blank | CLEARS it. A store that stops taking transfers empties the box. |
| Only one of the two on file | A receipt carries NEITHER. Half a bank account is not a payment instruction, and one line alone would read as the system having forgotten the rest. |
| Anything carrying the mask character | Refused outright (§POS-06.4). |

### POS-06.6 One paragraph, four media, no renderer that decides anything

`receipt_remit.block` builds the paragraph once; `_receipt_bundle` hands that one string to every
medium. The paper copy and the emailed copy get it because `thermal_html` renders `slip_model`'s
`blocks`; the printer gets it because `receipt_escpos.lines` renders the same `blocks`; the tenant's
own POS layout gets it in the Document's `comments` slot, which both of that format's renderers
already print. **Not one renderer was taught what a bank block looks like** — which is the §POS-04
one-content-home paying for itself a second time.

### POS-06.7 Siblings checked

| Path | Done |
| --- | --- |
| The till's completion modal · the Sale Log reprint | The same picker, so the tick is in both |
| The emailed copy (`POST /pos/sales/{id}/email-receipt`) | Carries `remit` in its body, so the copy that was emailed is the copy that was handed over |
| The printer's byte stream | Carries it, with no change to `receipt_escpos.py` |
| The tenant's own POS layout | Carries it, in `comments` |
| The admin template preview | EXCUSED — it previews the org template against a sample sale; the tick belongs to a real print at a counter, as the destination does (§POS-04.5) |
| Legal disclaimer blocks on the POS layout | PRE-EXISTING GAP, untouched: `document()` has never carried the disclaimers either. Named here so it is not mistaken for something this change introduced |
| `GET /pos/settings` · the generic settings editor | Both closed against the two keys (§POS-06.4) |

### POS-06.8 Files, locks, money

| | |
| --- | --- |
| New | `backend/app/modules/pos/receipt_remit.py` · `frontend/src/components/pos/ReceiptRemitFields.tsx` · `encryption_backfill.backfill_receipt_remit` + its `SWEEPS` family · `PosSettingDef.sensitive` · `harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §N |
| Changed | `sale_receipt` (`print_choice` gains the tick; `slip_model` / `thermal_html` / `document` / `html` forward one string) · `pos_config_effective.SERVER_DEFAULTS` + 2 keys · `pos-config.ts` + the same 2 · `PrintFormatPicker` · `pos/router` (`_receipt_bundle`, the masked settings read, the new editor) |
| Endpoints | `PUT /pos/receipt-remit` (new) · `GET /pos/sales/{id}/receipt` gains `remit` and five answer fields |
| Migration | **NONE** — `pos.pos_settings` is a kv table and these are two more keys |
| Locks | §N (24 checks + 3 negative controls): validation, the mask, the seal, the store→org resolution, the tick's gate, one paragraph in four media, the two closed save paths, RULE TWO |
| MONEY IMPACT | **NONE in the platform** — no figure in any report moves. It does put a payment instruction in a customer's hands, which is why the number is validated, the write is gated and the value is sealed |

Same class: §POS-04 (one content home, many media), §CORE-04 (encrypted on write and sealed at rest
are one fact), §POS-05 (one fact, one home, dereferenced).

## §POS-07. THE CUSTOMER'S OWN ADDRESS ON THE RECEIPT (owner ask 2026-10-21)

Owner, verbatim: *"teh receipt shoudl show the complete address for the customer as in the system"*.

### POS-07.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index and the tree for an existing home for "a customer's address, written out" before
building. **One existed, private to one caller:** `pos/sales_from_reports._customer_lines_fn` joined
`address_1 + address_2` and `city + state + zip` itself for the receipt rebuilt from an imported sales
report (§30.14's bill-to). Nothing else wrote an address out for a human — `customer_master` and
`pos/router` select those columns only to compare or to edit, and `customer_identity.norm_address`
normalises them for a **different question** ("are these two records the same person").

So nothing new was derived: the private copy was EXTENDED into the one home and its own caller
rewired to it. No new table, no new endpoint, no migration.

### POS-07.2 THE CLASS, not the instance

The instance is "the till receipt does not print the address". The class is that **"what does this
customer's record say, written out" had no home**, so the only caller that wanted it spelled the five
columns itself — and every other medium that shows a customer a receipt (the till copy, the reprint,
the emailed copy, the printer's byte stream, the tenant's own POS layout, the admin preview) carried
the name alone. Two paths answering one question with one of them fixed is the duplicate defect the
house rules forbid.

### POS-07.3 The one home

`backend/app/modules/pos/customer_bill_to.py`, PURE (no client, no I/O):

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `FIELDS` / `COLUMNS` | the five columns, named once — a reader SELECTS `COLUMNS` rather than spelling four of five and silently dropping a line of someone's address |
| `lines(row)` | the street (with its apartment or suite), then the city, state and postal code. A field the record does not hold takes no line and leaves no blank one; `None` and `{}` give `[]`, the walk-in case, never an error |
| `block(name, row)` | the whole bill-to block, `lines` LEADING with the name — the shape the structured Document's `bill_to` and the till slip's head both want |
| `has_address(row)` | whether the RECORD holds one at all, so "why is the address not on the receipt" is answered about the record |

### POS-07.4 Every medium, from one block

`_receipt_bundle` reads the customer once (its select now appends `COLUMNS`), calls `lines(customer)`
once and hands the SAME list to both media — `sale_receipt.html` (the paper copy, the emailed copy
and the tenant's POS layout) and `sale_receipt.slip_model` for `receipt_escpos.payload_base64` (the
cut slip). `receipt_escpos.py` did not change at all: it renders `slip_model`, so the address reached
the printer the moment the model carried it (the §POS-04 content home paying off a second time).

The admin preview renders it too, from a sample RECORD read through the same `lines()`
(`PREVIEW_CUSTOMER`), so an admin can see the block their `show_customer` toggle produces.

### POS-07.5 One toggle, one block

The address prints with the customer, under `show_customer` — not behind a second toggle. A receipt
that names the customer and hides where they live answers half a question, and the owner's ask is the
complete address. With `show_customer` off, name and address are both off (proof O10).

### POS-07.6 Siblings checked

| Path | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| `pos/sales_from_reports._customer_lines_fn` (imported receipt's bill-to) | **Rewired** to `lines(row)`; its own join deleted. Wording unchanged, so no imported receipt re-renders differently |
| `receipt_escpos.payload` (the printer) | **No change needed** — it renders `slip_model` |
| `receipt_formats.render.render_html` (the tenant's POS layout) | **No change needed** — it renders the Document's `bill_to` |
| `customer_identity.norm_address` | **Excused, deliberately** — it answers "same person", one normalised string with punctuation stripped; a shared home would make one of the two answers wrong |
| `customer_master` / `pos.router` customer selects | **Excused** — they read the columns to compare or to edit a record, and write no address out for a human |
| The customer screens (`pos/customers/page.tsx`) | **Excused** — a form holding one field per column, not a written-out address |

### POS-07.7 Files, locks, money

| | |
| --- | --- |
| New | `backend/app/modules/pos/customer_bill_to.py` · `harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §O · `pos.router.PREVIEW_CUSTOMER` |
| Changed | `sale_receipt` (`slip_model` / `thermal_html` / `document` / `html` forward one list) · `pos/router` (`_receipt_bundle` selects `COLUMNS`, both media and the preview) · `sales_from_reports._customer_lines_fn` (dereferences, no longer joins) |
