## §POS-08. THE EMAILED RECEIPT AS A FILE (owner ask 2026-10-21)

Owner, verbatim: *"the receipt is going the body of the meial it should as a pdf attachment aswell"*.

### POS-08.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index and the tree before building:

| Existing mechanism | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| §POS-04 `sale_receipt.slip_model` + `receipt_escpos.lines` — the exact rows of characters a till slip prints | **Reused as the content.** The PDF draws those rows; it does not re-read the sale. |
| §POS-02 `sale_receipt.document` + `receipt_formats.render.render_words` — the POS layout's positioned words | **Reused as the content** for a tenant whose receipts print in its own POS's layout. |
| `sale_receipt.clean_layout` — which layout this print uses | **Reused.** The file asks the same resolver the mail body asks, so the two cannot differ. |
| `notify/channels/email_resend.send_email(attachments=…)` | **Reused.** The attachment hook already existed and was being passed `[]`. |
| `pos/receipt_pdf.py` | **Not it, and deliberately not extended.** That module READS an uploaded PDF (pdfplumber) for the format parsers. Reading and writing a PDF are different questions; the new module says so in its docstring. |
| `notify/render.build_pdf`, `commcalc/commission_statement.render_pdf`, `payout_structure.render_pdf` | **Excused.** Each renders ITS OWN document family (a report's sheets, a statement, a structure doc) from its own model. A receipt is a third family, and folding them together would mean one of the three answers "what does this document look like" wrongly. All four now share the house's one PDF toolkit (reportlab) and nothing else. |

No new table, no migration, no new endpoint.

### POS-08.2 A third MEDIUM, never a third receipt

This is the §POS-04 shape again. The receipt has two content homes; the PDF is a renderer of THEM:

| The receipt's layout | What the file draws | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the till slip | `receipt_escpos.lines(slip_model(...))` — the same rows the printer cuts | ONE page, as wide as the roll the store declared (`PT_PER_MM`), as long as the slip. A roll has no page break, so neither has the file |
| the tenant's own POS | `render_words(document(...), fmt.PRINT_LAYOUT)` — the same words that format's own parser reads back | letter, paginated by the words' own `top`; a receipt longer than a page continues, and no line is dropped to make it fit |

The module reads no toggle, no figure and no line of its own (proof P11): the only thing it takes
from the snapshot is the sale's number, for the file's name and title. `sale_receipt.for_render` is
now the one home for the printed customer name, so the file cannot say "John S." where the mail says
"John Smith" (P12).

### POS-08.3 Both ways, every time

The mail carries the receipt in its body — where a customer reads it without opening anything — and
as `receipt-<transaction>.pdf`, which they can keep, forward to an insurer or print. Nothing is
configurable here: the owner's ask is "as well", and a receipt a customer cannot keep was the
complaint.

### POS-08.4 A file that cannot be built never costs a customer their receipt

`_receipt_bundle(want_pdf=True)` catches anything the render raises, the mail goes with the body
alone, and the answer says so (`attached: false`, `attachment_error`, and a message that reads "The
PDF copy could not be built, so it went in the body only"). The alternative — a 500 on the send —
would lose the receipt entirely to save the attachment.

Built ONLY where something attaches one (P14): a print screen has no use for a file and a page render
is not free.

### POS-08.5 The defect this change's own proof found

`§P8`. Touching the canvas after a page is closed opens the next one, and reportlab then writes that
empty page into the file — every POS-layout receipt would have carried a blank second sheet. Fixed by
setting the font at the START of each page; the check stays so it cannot come back.

### POS-08.6 Files, locks, money

| | |
| --- | --- |
| New | `backend/app/modules/pos/receipt_pdf_render.py` · `sale_receipt.for_render` · `harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §P |
| Changed | `pos/router` (`_receipt_bundle(want_pdf=…)` and the three answer fields; the email send attaches) · `sale_receipt.html` (dereferences `for_render`) |
| Endpoints | **NONE new** — `POST /pos/sales/{id}/email-receipt` answers three more fields |
| Migration | **NONE** |
| Locks | §P (17 checks + 3 negative controls), read back with pdfplumber so the assertions are on what a customer's reader shows. §M9 / §N17 / §O13 re-pinned 2 → 3 call sites: the third medium is counted, so a medium added without being handed the one paragraph, the one block of lines or the format MODULE fails the build |
| MONEY IMPACT | **NONE** — the file restates a receipt that restates a sale already rung |

Same class: §POS-04 (one content home, two media — this is the third), §POS-07 (one home,
dereferenced), §POS-02 (one renderer).

## §POS-09. SENDING A RECEIPT — ONE HOME, TWO CHANNELS, EVERY SCREEN (owner ask 2026-10-21)

Owner, verbatim: *"i need the emial option in sales log viewer and the send notification option via
whats app also"*.

### POS-09.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index for an existing mechanism that sends a receipt to a customer, and for one that
sends a FILE on WhatsApp. Both exist and both are REUSED rather than re-derived:

| Searched | Found | Reused how |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "email this receipt" | §POS-02 `sale_receipt.email_view` + `POST /pos/sales/{id}/email-receipt` | unchanged; the panel calls it |
| "the receipt as a file" | §POS-08 `receipt_pdf_render.receipt_pdf` via `_receipt_bundle(want_pdf=True)` | unchanged; WhatsApp attaches the same file |
| "send a document on WhatsApp" | §47 `notify/channels/whatsapp_meta.send_document_detailed` (the approved template, else free-form inside Meta's 24-hour window) | unchanged; the endpoint hands it the file and asks nothing about the window |
| "what counts as a phone number" | TWO copies — `whatsapp_window.digits` and `whatsapp_meta._to_number` | COLLAPSED: `_to_number` now dereferences `digits` |
| "the print choice rides with the copy" | §POS-03 `pos-receipt.choiceParams` | third caller, same spelling |

**Nothing new was derived.** The only new logic is `sale_receipt.whatsapp_view` — the same
five-field question `email_view` already answers, asked of the other channel.

### POS-09.2 THE CLASS, not the instance

The ask names a screen ("sales log viewer"), but the missing thing was not a button. **Sending a
receipt had no home.** It lived inline in the till's completion modal, keyed to the sale that had
just been rung — which is why the Sale Log, where a counter opens yesterday's receipt or one rung at
another till, could only print, and why a second channel would have had to be written twice and then
kept in step.

So the fix is a home, not a button: **one sender in the browser**
(`frontend/src/components/pos/SendReceiptPanel.tsx`) mounted by both screens, over **one view home**
per channel in `sale_receipt`. A channel added there reaches every screen that mounts the panel, and
a screen added later gets both channels for free.

### POS-09.3 The browser decides nothing

`email_view` and `whatsapp_view` answer the same five fields — `to`, `to_source`, `valid`,
`from_name`, `caption`/`subject`. A typed value beats the customer's record, a blank falls back to
the record, and **neither is invented**: no address and no number means `to: ""`, `to_source:
"none"`, `valid: false`, and the button is simply unavailable. The number is normalised by the
channel's own rule, handed in — `whatsapp_view` takes `digits` as a parameter and holds no copy of
it, so there is nothing in `sale_receipt` to drift.

### POS-09.4 The duplicate that was already there

`whatsapp_meta._to_number` and `whatsapp_window.digits` were two statements of one rule (strip the
punctuation, prepend the US country code to a bare ten digits). They had not diverged yet; a
different decision about, say, a leading `00` in either would have made the window we look up and
the number we send to two different numbers. `_to_number` now reads `digits`, and §Q4 fails the build
if a second `isdigit()` ladder appears on either side.

### POS-09.5 What the customer gets

The **same receipt**, on either channel: the §POS-08 PDF, built once by the one renderer from the
same two content homes as the paper copy, with the line the email subject carries as its caption. A
customer handed both does not get two different receipts. WhatsApp **refuses outright** when the file
could not be built (503) rather than sending a bare line claiming an attachment — the mail is the
other way round (§POS-08: the body alone still goes, and says so), because a mail's body IS the
receipt and a WhatsApp caption is not.

### POS-09.6 Files, locks, money

| | |
| --- | --- |
| New | `frontend/src/components/pos/SendReceiptPanel.tsx` · `sale_receipt.whatsapp_view` / `whatsapp_phone` / `WHATSAPP_MIN_DIGITS` · `pos-receipt.whatsappSaleReceipt` · `harness_pos_receipt_render.py` §Q |
| Changed | `pos/router` (the new endpoint; `_receipt_bundle(typed_phone=…)` answers `whatsapp`) · `notify/channels/whatsapp_meta._to_number` (dereferences `whatsapp_window.digits`) · the register page (its inline email block replaced by the panel; it keeps only `saveReceiptEmailToProfile`) · the Sale Log reprint modal (mounts the panel) |
| Endpoints | `POST /pos/sales/{sale_id}/whatsapp-receipt` — **one** new route; `harness_db_resilience.EXPECT_ROUTES` re-pinned 1799 → 1800 |
| Migration | **NONE** — no new fact is stored; both recipients are columns the customer record already has |
| Locks | §Q (17 checks + 2 negative controls). §Q4 fails the build on a second phone-number rule, §Q7 on a second sender in the browser, §Q13 on a re-implementation of Meta's window, §Q17 on an effect copying a customer's address into state (a fresh panel per sale instead), §K14 re-pinned 2 → 3 callers of the one print-choice spelling |
| MONEY IMPACT | **NONE** — a receipt restates a sale already rung |

Same class: §POS-04 (one content home, every medium), §POS-07 (one home, dereferenced), §POS-08
(the file it sends), §47 (the WhatsApp ladder it does not re-implement).

## §COMMCALC-20. A HANDSET THAT BOOKS A REBATE BOOKS A COST (owner report 2026-10-19)

Owner, on LuxeLink September 2026: *"how come the device cost is less than the device rebate"* —
Device cost **$164,730.35** against Device purchase rebates (contra-COGS) **−$180,191.91** on the
Chicago company. A contra-COGS larger than the COGS it nets against makes device gross profit
positive out of nothing.

### §COMMCALC-20.1 THE CLASS, not the instance

A handset's **rebate** books off `commcalc.raw_ma_commission`, one row at a time, unconditionally.
Its **cost** books only when the same handset's `sku` can be priced off `commcalc.raw_ma_fulfillment`
— and an order-type **allowlist** (`device_cogs._MA_DEVICE_ORDER_TYPES`, `{'branded handset'}`)
silently decided which fulfillment rows were allowed to carry a price at all.

The allowlist was correct when it was written (404 fulfillment rows, one device family) and wrong
the day the distributor opened a second one. A family nobody had added priced **nothing**, so every
handset bought under it booked a full rebate against a cost of zero — and nothing on the statement
said so, because the drop was counted in `meta` and `engine._assemble` never shows `meta` to a
reader (the §K3(b) lesson, again).

**Measured live, LuxeLink (org `854f6d7b`), 2026-10-19:**

| period | device cost before | after | delta | rebate | net device COGS after | unpriced handsets |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| June 2026 | 59,529.80 | 59,529.80 | 0.00 | −57,000.46 | 2,529.34 | 8 → 8 |
| July 2026 | 137,185.10 | 137,185.10 | 0.00 | −126,636.77 | 10,548.33 | 9 → 9 |
| August 2026 | 260,206.80 | 262,456.74 | +2,249.94 | −251,946.31 | 10,510.43 | 26 → 20 |
| **September 2026** | **222,525.36** | **248,824.65** | **+26,299.29** | −239,367.80 | **9,456.85** (was −16,842.44) | 77 → 6 |
| October 2026 | 64,284.95 | 77,534.58 | +13,249.63 | −72,436.31 | 5,098.27 (was −8,151.36) | 39 → 2 |
| **total** | **743,732.01** | **785,530.87** | **+41,798.86** | −747,387.65 | 38,143.22 | |

71 of September's 77 unpriced handsets were certified-pre-owned iPhones bought under a second
order-type family; $26,299.29 of real cost was dropped against $27,449.27 of rebate that booked
regardless. The independent confirmation is the shape of the last column: net device COGS was
$2.5k–$10.5k in every month the allowlist happened to cover and went **negative** in the two months
it did not. After the fix every month is positive and in the same band.

### §COMMCALC-20.2 DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate) — WHAT WAS REUSED, NOT REBUILT

| question | existing mechanism | what this change did |
|---|---|---|
| what did this handset model cost | `device_cogs.ma_unit_price_from_rows` (§COMMCALC-03) | **EXTENDED** — one new optional argument, no second pricer |
| what did the devices activated this month cost | `device_cogs.ma_sold_cost_from_rows` | **EXTENDED** — names the unpriced models it already counted |
| is this fulfillment row a device | two literal `order_type` membership tests | **FACTORED** into `_ma_row_prices_a_device`, the ONE test, read by the price map and the coverage |
| a vendor order-type family nobody classified | `ma_store_pnl.ma_tx_coverage` + `NO_RULE_REASON` + `load_unbooked_reasons` (daily-tx feed, mig 312) | **REUSED WHOLE** — `ma_fulfillment_coverage` is its fulfillment-side twin and dereferences the same literal and the same config loader |
| the prospect/takeover evaluation's handset cost | `prospect_eval.evaluate` through the same two homes | **THE SIBLING, FIXED IN THIS PR** — it passes the same evidence |
| saying on the statement what `meta` knows | `L["device_cost"]["note"]` (§K3(b) honest zero, §70 restatement) | **EXTENDED** — appended, so all three facts can be true at once |

### §COMMCALC-20.3 THE FIX: evidence, not vocabulary

A fulfillment row prices a handset when **the two feeds agree it is one** — its `product_name` is a
`sku` that a handset actually **activated** under on `raw_ma_commission`
(`device_cogs.ma_device_product_names`). That is evidence, not a name list: it carries no
distributor, carrier or tenant name (RULE TWO), it can never remove a price the cost side would
have used (a sku that is not activated is never looked up), and the next family the distributor
opens prices itself with no code change.

Verified over LuxeLink's whole fulfillment sheet: the derived test reproduces the allowlist exactly
where the allowlist was right (917 `Branded Handset` rows, 24 of 24 product names matched) and
supplies the family it had missed (108 rows, 8 of 8 matched), while the SIM kits (400 units at
$3.00) and the charge cables match nothing and stay out, as they always did. The allowlist remains
as the fallback for a caller with no commission feed to take evidence from, so omitting the
evidence is byte-identical to the pre-2026-10-19 behaviour.

**One home, one reader.** `_ma_row_prices_a_device` is the only place `order_type` is tested;
`ma_unit_price_from_rows` and `ma_fulfillment_coverage` both read it, and `harness_…` §I15 fails the
build if a third reader appears or either stops dereferencing it.

**What is still not measured is REPORTED, never coded around.** 6 handsets in September and 2 in
October are on no fulfillment sheet at all; `device_cogs.unpriced_handsets_note` — the ONE home for
that sentence — says so on the statement line, names the models, and states plainly that their
rebate booked while their cost did not. `ma_fulfillment_coverage` reports every order-type family
with what it did, and a family that prices nothing and carries no stated reason gets
`NO_RULE_REASON`. LuxeLink's two such families are $1,225.62 of SIM kits and cables; one
`commission_org_config.pl_ma_unbooked_reasons` row retires each — CONFIG, never code.

| what | where |
|---|---|
| **Which fulfillment rows price a handset?** The ones whose `product_name` is a `sku` a handset activated under; the order-type allowlist is the evidence-free fallback | `account/device_cogs._ma_row_prices_a_device` (the ONE test) over `ma_device_product_names`; read by `ma_unit_price_from_rows(rows, device_names)` and `ma_fulfillment_coverage`. Callers: `device_cogs._ma_sold_cost` (live P&L), `commcalc/prospect_eval.evaluate` + `commcalc/router` pl-trend (the takeover evaluation). Lock `harness_device_inventory_cogs.py` §I (**106** checks total; §I1 is the regression, red on the pre-change code) |
| **What did each fulfillment order-type family do?** Every family named, with its reason; an unruled one reported, never papered over | `account/device_cogs.ma_fulfillment_coverage` → `device_cogs.resolve` `meta.fulfillment_coverage`. Reasons from `commcalc.commission_org_config.pl_ma_unbooked_reasons` through `ma_store_pnl.load_unbooked_reasons` — the SAME config and the SAME `NO_RULE_REASON` literal as the daily-tx coverage (§COMMCALC-11) |
| **A handset whose cost could not be priced** | `account/device_cogs.unpriced_handsets_note` — the ONE home for the sentence — appended to `L["device_cost"]["note"]` by `coa.build_inputs`. Names the count and the models, and says the rebate booked while the cost did not |

| MONEY IMPACT | **YES, and it is a RESTATEMENT** — LuxeLink device cost rises $41,798.86 across Jun–Oct 2026, almost all of it Sep ($26,299.29) and Oct ($13,249.63). Gross profit falls by the same amount in those months. No other tenant has MA fulfillment rows, so nothing else moves. **A P&L Recompute is required** before the stored statements show it |
| RULE TWO | no distributor, carrier, tenant or product name decides whether a row prices a handset; the test is the two feeds' own agreement, and the reasons map is per-org config |

Same class: §COMMCALC-66 / §66 (a fallback must not read as evidence), §19.18 (a registry written
and its callers left unwired is not a fix), §COMMCALC-11 (a vendor order-type family nobody
classified is reported, never silent), §42.7/§K3(b) (a declared or dropped figure must SAY so on
the statement, because `meta` never reaches a reader).

## §CORE-13. A MIGRATION GRANTS WHAT IT CREATES — Data API reachability stops being inherited (Supabase notice 2026-10-20)

Supabase, forwarded by the owner on 2026-10-20: *"On October 30 … Supabase will stop automatically
granting Data API access to new tables in the 'public' schema for existing projects. Your existing
tables are not affected … Any table created in 'public' from that date onwards needs an explicit
GRANT before supabase-js, PostgREST, or GraphQL can reach it. This includes migrations that recreate
your schema: new projects, preview branches, and local `supabase db reset`."*

### CORE-13.1 WHAT IT MEANS HERE, MEASURED

Measured against the live project and the 499 migrations on `main`, 2026-10-20:

| Question | Answer | How it was checked |
|---|---|---|
| Does the browser read tables through the Data API? | **No.** `@supabase/supabase-js` is used for auth (`signInWithPassword`, `getSession`, `onAuthStateChange`) and realtime channels only. There is no `.from()` or `.rpc()` call site in `frontend/src` or `mobile/src`. | grep of both trees for `supabase.` |
| Does the **backend** read tables through the Data API? | **Yes — all of it.** `app/core/database.py` builds one PostgREST client per schema and every module chains `.table(...)` on it. There is no direct SQL path. | `app/core/database.py`; 2,369 `.schema("…")` sites across `commcalc` / `storeops` / `pos` / `core` / `notify` |
| Does any migration create a table in `public`? | **None of 501 created relations.** Every one is schema-qualified (`commcalc` 238, `storeops` 113, `core` 106, `pos` 35, `notify` 6, `assets` 3). | parse of `database/migrations/*.sql` |
| Is there anything to repair in production? | **No.** Existing tables keep their grants; nothing in the unapplied backlog creates in `public`. No SQL was handed over. | the notice's own wording + the parse above |

So the dated change breaks nothing on 30 October. **The exposure it names is the one worth fixing:**
366 of those 501 relations carry no grant of their own and are reachable only because
`ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` happens to be set for their schema in the live Supabase project — a fact
that lives in a dashboard, not in `database/migrations/`, and that the vendor is now in the business
of changing. That is the §19.18 shape: a fact every caller depends on, stored somewhere nobody in
this repository can read.

### CORE-13.2 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

The instance is `public`. The class is **a migration that leaves a relation's reachability to a
default set outside this repository.** And because this backend speaks only PostgREST, an ungranted
relation is not "invisible to the browser" — it is invisible to the application, arriving as
`42501 permission denied for table <x>` from a route that was green on the author's branch and dies
the first time the migration runs against a project created under the new default: a preview branch,
a `supabase db reset`, or a new tenant project.

**`service_role` only.** Supabase's example snippet grants `anon` and `authenticated` as well.
Copying it here would widen exposure for no gain, because nothing signed-in-but-not-the-backend ever
reads a table. The gate asks for the backend's role and nothing else.

### CORE-13.3 THE GATE

`backend/harness_data_api_grant_guard.py`, run as the `security.yml` job **A new table is granted by
the migration that creates it (Data API)**. Stdlib only, no DB, no network. It fails the build on:

| | |
|---|---|
| **A** | a migration newer than `CUTOFF` creates a relation with no schema qualifier — on Supabase that lands in `public` |
| **B** | a migration newer than `CUTOFF` creates `<schema>.<rel>` in a Data API schema and does not grant it to `service_role` **below** the create. `GRANT … ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA` covers only the tables that exist when it runs, so a create underneath it is not covered — the check is position-aware, not a substring test |
| **C** | `DATA_API_SCHEMAS` is not exactly the set of schemas the migrations create in, **both ways**. Declared, never derived (§CORE-10): a new schema has to be written down by a human, who then has to say whether the Data API serves it |
| **D** | `CUTOFF` was raised. It is a shrink-only ratchet pinned at `1089`, the highest migration on `main` the day the gate shipped |
| **Z** | ten negative controls, each check planted with its own defect — including a create inside a `--` comment, a grant that omits `service_role`, and a grant positioned above its own create |

**Grandfathered deliberately.** Everything at or below `CUTOFF` keeps the reachability it has:
those tables exist in the live project, the notice does not touch them, and backfilling 366 grants
would be a production schema change for no live defect. The gate starts green and the debt can only
shrink, by lowering `CUTOFF`.

The convention itself is in `CLAUDE.md` under house conventions, so it is read before a migration is
written rather than discovered when CI goes red.

### CORE-13.4 DUPLICATE CHECK (the CLAUDE.md build gate, applied and recorded)

Searched the index and `backend/harness_*` for an existing mechanism answering "is this relation
reachable": `harness_pos_grants_lock.py` (§30.16) locks four POS PII **functions** *switched off* and
fails a later migration that re-opens them — the opposite question, and function-scoped; it is left
alone. `harness_grant_model.py` and `harness_core_grant_universe.py` are about **permission grants to
people** (market/store scope), not SQL privileges, despite the name. `harness_unique_numbers_lock.py`
owns migration numbering. No existing gate reads `create table` against `GRANT`, so this is a new
home rather than a sibling derivation, and no second copy of any of their facts was made.

Same class: §19.18 (a registry written and its callers left unwired is not a fix), §CORE-10 (a
lesson in a note is enforced by whoever remembers it; a lesson in CI is enforced), §30.16 (a copied
schema-wide GRANT silently undoing a narrower REVOKE).

## §COMMCALC-24. A LIVE SESSION IS READ WHERE IT LIVES (owner report 2026-10-20)

**Owner, verbatim:** *"ups portla live login does not work i hvae tried again today"*. He was right,
and the row proved he had been right for five days.

**What the row and the server-side screenshot show.** His 17:47Z attempt reached the real UPS
Franchise Reporting System sign-in page, filled his username and password, and parked on **Sign In**
with the portal's own reCAPTCHA badge beside it (`login_shot_at` 2026-10-20T17:55:17Z; the stored
`login_shot` decodes to exactly that page). It then closed with *"Live session closed after
inactivity."* — the `_preauth_loop`'s `_HUMAN_ACTION_IDLE_SECONDS` budget, eight minutes, elapsed
having received **not one click**. The login was never broken. **He simply could not see it.**

**THE CAUSE.** `live_login._SESSIONS` is a plain dict in ONE process's memory. On this deploy
(§41 — `SERVICE_ROLE=api` on the API host plus `BROWSER_SERVICE_URL` at the sweeps worker)
`/live-login/start` carried `require_browser_service()`, so it proxied and the session was created on
the **worker**. `/live-login/state` and `/live-login/frame` carried no such gate, so they answered
from the **API host**, where that registry is empty: `{"phase": "idle", "message": "No live session
running…", "shot": None}`. His hands were pointed at the worker and his eyes at the API host.

**THE CLASS, which is why this is not a one-line patch.** The gate's old spelling asked *"does this
endpoint launch a browser?"*. `/frame` launches nothing — it reads a dict — so a reviewer adding it
left the gate off, **correctly by that question**. The question that matters is *"does this endpoint
touch `_SESSIONS`?"*, and if it does it must run in the process that has them. So the requirement is
**renamed at its home**: `require_session_host()`, because the old spelling is what misled the eye.
Three endpoints that obviously drove a browser were gated; **six that read or steered the session
were not — and the read half is the entire operator-facing surface.**

### COMMCALC-24.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

- **`app.core.service_role.require_browser_service` / `browser_allowed`** (§41) — "may this process do
  browser work". **DEREFERENCED, never copied**: both halves of the new home call into it and read no
  environment of their own; the lock fails if the gate body ever grows a `SERVICE_ROLE` or `environ`
  read. This is an EXTENSION of §41's mechanism under a name that fits the real question, not a
  second role reader.
- **`main._proxy_browser_work`** (§41) — the forwarder that already carries method, path, query,
  headers and body to the worker verbatim, where the JWT is re-authenticated and the org checks
  re-run. **REUSED unchanged**; the only change on that path is that it now pools its HTTP client,
  because `/frame` polls it ~3/s and a TLS handshake per frame is not a video feed.
- **§COMMCALC-13's `present_auth_status`** — what a *finished* session leaves on the ROW. A different
  axis of the same home (that one is about the row, this one about the process), so it EXTENDS that
  module-graph fact rather than forking a sibling: one home, one question.
- **`supply/router`'s session endpoints** (§51) — the vendor-ordering door onto the SAME sessions.
  Checked here, not left to drift (see §COMMCALC-24.3).
- No new table, no new column, **no migration**, no new endpoint, no new report.

### COMMCALC-24.2 One fact, one home, dereferenced

| question | home | reader |
|---|---|---|
| can THIS process hold live sessions? | `app.core.service_role.browser_allowed` | `live_login.sessions_live_here()` |
| must this request run where they are? | the same | `live_login.require_session_host()` |

`sessions_live_here()` is **pure and never raises**: an unintrospectable or exploding role reads as
`True`, which keeps the single-service answer (sessions are local) rather than declaring a working
deploy blind. Reading a live session as absent is the one regression this must not cause.

`require_session_host()` is called as the **first statement** of every live-login handler, before
`require_org` and before a DB client is opened — exactly as `/start` always did — so a request that
belongs on the worker is forwarded before it does work it would only throw away.

### COMMCALC-24.3 The siblings, fixed here rather than excused

- `commcalc/router` — all **nine** live-login endpoints (`start`, `state`, `frame`, `click`, `input`,
  `submit`, `submit-totp`, `resend`, `cancel`) now call the gate; six of them did not.
- `commcalc/router` `/data-sources/{sid}/run` and `supply/router` `/orders/{po_id}/open-session` were
  already gated by the role module, but **by the old spelling** — the exact divergence the lock
  exists to stop. Re-pointed at the named home. *The lock found both; they were not in the hand-made
  list.*
- `supply/router` `/orders/{po_id}` is **deliberately NOT gated**: it is the whole PO page, and
  proxying it would make an order unreadable whenever the sweeps worker is down. Instead it
  dereferences `sessions_live_here()` and reports **`observable`**, with `for_this_order` as `None`
  rather than `False` when this process cannot see — so a blind process never presents its blindness
  as the owner's answer. It is the one named exemption in the lock, and it must earn it.
- The VidaPay pull's inner session reuse is a legitimate best-effort read of a per-process registry —
  it falls back to the cold `storage_state` restore — so it degrades, it does not lie.
- **`harness_browser_sweep_kinds.py` was a sibling LOCK, and CI found it, not me.** It already asks
  the same question from the other direction — it walks the call graph for the browser *reach* and
  asserts the endpoint is gated — but it matched the gate by the literal string
  `require_browser_service()`, so the rename failed a correctly gated `open_order_session`. Two locks
  on one requirement with two spellings is the divergence the index rules forbid, so it now accepts
  either name through one `_GATE_CALLS` vocabulary — and **proves the alias rather than assuming it**
  (3 new checks: the renamed gate exists at its home, it dereferences `require_browser_service`, and
  it reads no environment of its own). Make `require_session_host` decide the role itself and that
  file stops accepting the spelling. The two locks are complementary and both are kept: this one
  scans `@router` endpoints touching the registry, that one follows helper calls to a browser launch.
- **`harness_one_domain_lock.py` was the THIRD lock on the same spelling, and it did not go red — it
  went BLIND.** Its AST scan matched `require_browser_service` as a bare call name, so after the
  rename it stopped recognising the gate at all: the set of endpoints whose `DIRECT_ROUTES` coverage
  it asserts fell from **19 to 8**, and *eleven endpoints silently left that assertion*. Nothing
  failed on the merits — only the non-vacuity bound (`len(endpoints) >= 10`) turned the job red. That
  bound is the whole reason this was caught, and it is the §19.x lesson again in a new costume: **a
  scan that cannot see its subject does not fail; its assertion ceases to exist.** The scan now reads
  the vocabulary and accepts both the bare and the attribute call form
  (`live_login.require_session_host()`). Coverage itself was never actually broken — `DIRECT_ROUTES`
  already carries `live-login/[^/]+`, so every newly gated endpoint is direct — but nothing was
  *checking* that for eleven of them.

**THE REAL LESSON OF THIS CHANGE, and the fourth design fix in it.** Renaming one function broke
three locks in three different ways because each had **its own literal copy of the gate's name**. So
the gate's VOCABULARY now has one home beside the gate — `app.core.service_role.GATE_FUNCTION_NAMES`
— and every lock dereferences it. A fourth spelling is one line in one place. `harness_live_session_host`
§G fails the build if a lock that scans for the gate spells a name itself again, proved red by
hard-coding it back.

### COMMCALC-24.4 Locked so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_live_session_host.py` — **50 checks**, DB-free, no network, no browser. §A the one
home, and the gate dereferences the role module · §B the fact is pure and a raising role still reads
`True` · §C **THE LOCK**: a regex scan of every `@router` endpoint in both routers — any handler
touching `get_session`/`start_session` must call the gate, with the single named exemption above ·
§D the gate precedes `require_org` and `sb()` · §E the supply sibling reports `observable` · §F
controls, including the exact pre-change `/state` body text, armed so a revert reads RED · **§G the
gate's name-list has one home and every lock that scans for it dereferences that list**, keeping no
literal copy beside it.

Wired into `carrier-vocab-guard.yml` as *"live-session-host lock"*.

**Proved red two ways on main's shape:** removing the gate from `/frame` fails **2** checks; before
the fix the scan reported **6** ungated endpoints. The sibling lock is proved red too: making
`require_session_host` read the environment instead of dereferencing fails **2** of its checks.

### COMMCALC-24.5 Cross-references

Same class: §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers left unwired is not a fix), §COMMCALC-13 (a
status that outlived the process that owned it). Neighbours: §41 (the split deploy and the
forwarder), §COMMCALC-10 (the progress watchdog on the same session), §COMMCALC-11 (the human check
this session was parked on), §CORE-03 (where the credential it signs in with is sealed), §51 (the
vendor-ordering door onto the same sessions), §COMMCALC-07 (the UPS pull this login exists to feed).

## §COMMCALC-25. THE FILTERS ON DEVICE FORECASTING & VENDOR PAYABLES — a date window with one home, and a store selection that binds through identity (owner reports 2026-10-22)

Three reports, one evening, on the same screen (`/commcalc/payables`, §15 module 095):

1. *"Device Forecasting & Vendor Payables should have all the regular filters with data range store etc"*
2. *"the filter for market brings up te forcastoing but hte filter for store does not bring up anything"*
3. *"the forcasting should summaroze in grid format to tbe exported to understand how many phones are
   needed of a particular model per store"*

### COMMCALC-25.1 DUPLICATE CHECK (the build gate) — what was REUSED, not rebuilt

| Needed | Already existed | What this change did |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a shared report filter bar | `frontend/src/components/StandardFilterBar.tsx` (RULE FIVE §3d) | adopted its date RANGE (`periodMode="range"`); the screen already carried market + store. No new control was written |
| "is this row inside the date range" | `commcalc/vip_invoice_filter.in_date_window` (§15v) — **and two more answers beside it** | PROMOTED to `commcalc/date_window.py` and the §15v copy now dereferences it. No sibling predicate was added |
| "which store is this string" | `account/store_identity.build_store_resolver` via `coa.store_resolver` (§64) | dereferenced. This module states no spelling rule of its own |
| store options, one per physical store | `core.scope.fold_store_spellings` / `org_store_options` (§13e) | kept — the fix is in what an option BINDS, not in the list |
| store→market stamping | `core.scope.store_market_resolver` (§13a) | unchanged; it is the half that already worked, and the model for the fix |
| the grid's figures | `/payables/forecast` rows | PIVOTED (`frontend/src/lib/forecast-matrix.ts`). No second derivation, no second fetch |

### COMMCALC-25.2 THE CLASS — a window is one fact, and three surfaces each owned a copy

`/payables/forecast` stated its window as a look-back NUMBER, `/owed-by-date` and its vendor-feed
fallback as their own inline `gte`/`lte` pairs, and §15v as `in_date_window`. Four answers to "which
days am I measuring" on two screens. `commcalc/date_window.py` is now the ONE home — `day` (validates
a leading calendar day rather than truncating ten characters), `in_window` / `row_in_window`
(**inclusive both ends, compared on DAYS, FAIL-CLOSED on a dateless row** — the convention
`standard-filters.ts periodOk` already used on the client, so screen and server drop the same rows),
`resolve_window` (a look-back and a date range are the SAME window with two front ends; `basis` and
`days_measured` name which answered), `apply_window` (the server twin), `undated` (the count a
windowed surface must REPORT).

**An off-by-one fell out of stating it once.** The forecast scanned `today - lookback` — `lookback + 1`
days — and divided the units by `lookback`, so every velocity read ~14% high at a 7-day window. The
span the query scans and the divisor are now the same number (`harness_payables_filter_scope.py` §B4).

### COMMCALC-25.3 THE STORE HALF — and why only it was broken

The asymmetry IS the diagnosis. Every row is STAMPED `market = resolver(row.store)`, and that
resolver accepts any spelling, so a market pick matches whatever the feed calls the store. The store
half was compared as a **string**: the picker's label against `row.store`. MEASURED live 2026-10-22
against the real resolver, house org:

| source | spellings matching NO option | rows unreachable by any store pick | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `commcalc.asset_ledger` | 13 of 33 | 10,801 | **0** |
| `commcalc.device_payable_ledger` | 15 of 37 | 4,044 | **0** |
| `commcalc.raw_sales` | 6 of 28 | 10,024 | **0** |

§13e made that the NORMAL case rather than the exception: for a store spelled two ways the surviving
option is, by construction, not the spelling the other half of the rows carry.

**The fix is the class.** Rows AND options both carry `store_key` — `store_identity.store_key` over
`coa.store_resolver` — and the comparison is made on that key, while `store` stays the display value.
A new `store_aliases` row therefore teaches this filter, the P&L and the GP report in the same instant.

### COMMCALC-25.4 The siblings, fixed here rather than excused

`GET /payables/due` narrowed by store with the same string equality (so its DUE report was empty for
the same stores) and `_owed_from_vendor_feed` carried its own window pair. Both are fixed in this
change — the harness fails the build if either comparison returns.

### COMMCALC-25.5 THE GRID (owner ask 3)

`frontend/src/lib/forecast-matrix.ts` — PURE, framework-free. `buildForecastMatrix(rows, metric)`
pivots the **already-filtered** rows into stores × models: one column per model ordered by total
units, one row per store, the unassigned bucket LAST and never dropped. Four metrics (units to order
/ projected demand / sold in window / on hand). `matrixExportRows` + `matrixExportColumns` feed
`ReportExportBar`, so the spreadsheet is the screen (RULE FOUR). **A store is keyed on its identity,
not its spelling** — two spellings of one physical store are ONE row whose orders ADD, instead of two
rows that each look too small to act on.

### COMMCALC-25.6 Locked so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_payables_filter_scope.py` (**52 checks**) — §A the window semantics incl. the
timestamp-on-the-end-day and fail-closed regressions · §B `resolve_window` incl. the off-by-one ·
§C the store-identity regression (a raw-string comparison binds **1 of 4** live feed spellings; the
key binds all four) · §D the router dereferences both homes and **no string-equality store
comparison or private window pair survives** · §E §15v still reads the shared home and answers
identically. `frontend/scratchpad/prove_forecast_matrix.mjs` (**36 checks**) — the pivot, the
identity fold, what-you-see-is-what-exports, and §G the SCREEN's wiring. Both run in
`carrier-vocab-guard.yml` job **`vip-invoice-filter`**, beside the §15v proof they now share a home
with. No migration: nothing here is a schema change.

### COMMCALC-25.7 Cross-references

Same class: §64 / §70 (store identity — one home for "which store is this address"), §13e (one option
per physical store, whose fold made this defect the normal case), §15v (the other reader of the window
home), §19.18 (a registry written and its callers left unwired is not a fix). Neighbours: §15 (module

## §COMMCALC-26. A CARRIER'S TERMS ARE DECLARED, NOT WRITTEN IN CODE — the selling window, the net terms, the device cost source, and "out of pocket" (owner reports 2026-10-22)

Three reports in one message, all on the same page as §COMMCALC-25:

1. *"under Luxelink it is using Boost - it should not , also it should not say sell before 60 days as
   that is boost requirement , total is sell before 12 days"*
2. *"there is no data appearing for the phones which were purchased as per handset ordering and not
   sold before 12 days to be apparing in the aging ... if the imei is not sold then the device has to
   be paid out of pocket whch needs to be highlighted universally"*
3. *"simlarly Upcoming Invoice Payment Due does not sow any data - some thing is not working ??"*

### COMMCALC-26.1 ONE CLASS, FOUR SYMPTOMS

A carrier's arrangement was hard-wired in four different ways:

| the fact | where it lived | consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the selling window | the literals `< 45 / 45-60 / > 60` in `asset/router.get_aging`, **again** in `asset/router.on_inventory_by_store`, and **again** in `commcalc/device_history.AGING_BUCKETS` (whose comment asked the next reader to "keep the edges in lock-step" — the admission) | one carrier's 60 days shown to every tenant |
| which feed says "still unsold" | `asset_ledger` only | a tenant with 0 of those rows saw "this program doesn't apply to your account" |
| which feed says what is due | `vip_invoices` only | same, on Upcoming Invoice Payment Due |
| net payment terms | reachable ONLY via `payable_source_map.distributor_id` → `distributors.terms_days` | a map with no distributor link computed **no due date at all** |
| a device's cost | had to be a column on the device's own row | the Total activation feed has none, so every device was unpriced |

All five are now DECLARED columns on the existing config spine (`commcalc.payable_source_map`,
mig **1091**). RULE TWO, and **no new registry** — the duplicate check is 26.2.

### COMMCALC-26.2 MEASURED LIVE 2026-10-22 (why these are facts, not opinions)

| | Cellfonz R Us (Boost) | Luxelink (Total) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `asset_ledger` | 36,461 | **0** |
| `vip_invoices` | 4,062 | **0** |
| `raw_ma_fulfillment` (handset ordering) | 0 | 1,401 |
| `device_payable_ledger` | 11,000 | **4,288** — every `owed` NULL, every `due_date` NULL |
| `raw_ma_daily_tx` | 0 | 91,409 → **2,115 dated invoices, $2,049,592.50** |

**House org, the aging ladder:** 1,755 unsold on-inventory devices, of which **890 carry $0 owed and
were aged nowhere at all** — `buckets` only ever counted `owed > 0`, which is a billing-exposure read,
not an age one.

### COMMCALC-26.3 THE TWO JOINS THAT LOOK RIGHT AND ARE NOT

This is the part worth not re-deriving. Pricing a Total device needs a join, and there were three
candidates:

| candidate | measured | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the existing `owed_link` (mig 620): `activation_order` → fulfillment `order_number` | **0 of 4,322** | no key, no join |
| `activation_order` → `raw_ma_daily_tx.order_number`, which HAS a price and a real due date | **3,535 of 4,322 (81.8%)** — but its `retail_cost` equals the handset's fulfillment price in only **45 of 2,753** comparable rows (fulfillment **$529.00** vs feed **$195.00** on the same iPhone 13) | it is an ACTIVATION charge, not the device cost. Config alone would have understated the payable by ~⅔ while looking plausible |
| `sku` → fulfillment `product_name` | **3,370 of 4,322 (78%)**; of the 952 misses, **903** are the distributor's own `Product Not Available` sku | the join that binds. Per-model, so it needs `owed_mode='unit_price_map'` rather than `owed_link` |

**And the due date is NOT the 12 days.** The processor's own due dates run `tx_date + 1` (60,368 rows),
`+2` (11,576), `+3` (12,924) — the activation charge's terms, not a handset invoice's. The 12 days is a
SELLING deadline, so it is declared as one (`sell_within_days`) and `net_terms_days` is left UNSET for
Total: the out-of-pocket verdict then falls back to the window and says so (`basis = 'window'`).
Setting `net_terms_days = 12` would have invented a payment deadline no feed states.

### COMMCALC-26.4 THE ONE HOMES

| question | home |
| --- | --- |
| how long may a handset sit unsold, and when is it OUT OF POCKET | **`commcalc/device_aging_policy.py`** — PURE. `resolve_policy` (window + warn edge DERIVED from one declared fraction), `bucket`, `bucket_ladder`, `days_held`, `due_on`, `out_of_pocket` (three states: True / False / **None = not measured**, with its `basis` named — `due_date` beats `window`, and a SOLD device is never out of pocket) |
| which devices are unsold, from whichever feed this carrier declares | **`payables/unsold_inventory.py`** — `load_policies`, `ledger_sourced_maps`, `fetch_unsold_from_ledger` (shapes the per-IMEI ledger into the aging report's own vocabulary), `stamp_aging` (THE universal flag, one computation feeding both the headline and every row) |
| what the distributor's own feed says is due, at INVOICE grain | **`payables/vendor_invoice.py`** — `is_debt_line` (the debt test **shared** with the Daily Owed tab's date-grain read, so two grains cannot disagree about the same money), `group_invoices`, `summarize` |
| what a handset cost | **`account/device_cogs.ma_unit_price_from_rows`** — already the P&L's price home. READ, never re-derived |
| which days are in scope | **`commcalc/date_window.py`** (§COMMCALC-25) |

**The warn edge is derived, which is what makes Boost safe:** `0.75 × 60 = 45`, so the house default
ladder is byte-identical to the literals it replaces, while Total's 12 yields 9/12. Pinned by
`harness_device_aging_policy.py` §A1.

### COMMCALC-26.5 The siblings, fixed here rather than excused

`/on-inventory-by-store` held a **third** copy of the ladder — found by the lock on its first run, not
by reading — and now dereferences the same home. `age_buckets` ages EVERY unsold device (the 890
house devices above), while `buckets` is left untouched so the `flagged_owed` figure other surfaces
reconcile against does not move in this change; `buckets` is a strict subset of `age_buckets`, and the
response says so. The aging report's empty-state card was Boost-shaped too (it keyed on
`/asset/filter-options`, an asset-ledger derivative) and now requires the REPORT to be empty as well.
Ledger-sourced rows carry no `market` column, so the market filter resolves them through §13a's
store→market resolver rather than letting them all through.

### COMMCALC-26.6 Locked so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_device_aging_policy.py` (**73 checks**) — §A the derived ladder incl. the Boost
equivalence · §B bucketing for both carriers · §C `due_on` (a due date is never invented from a
window) · §D the verdict's three states and its basis precedence · §E `stamp_aging` · §F the invoice
home incl. the (number, due date) key — grouping by number alone would render Luxelink's 2,536
numberless lines as ONE $606,525.41 invoice due on 44 days at once · §G **the four surfaces keep no
literal and no private copy** · §H negative controls proving the lock can go red. Runs in
`carrier-vocab-guard.yml` job `vip-invoice-filter`.

### COMMCALC-26.7 What is owner-gated

Migration **1091** is additive and every column is NULL after it runs, which is byte-identical to
today. The VALUES are a separate, approval-gated data step:
`database/runbooks/payables_carrier_terms_2026-10-22.sql` (config rows only — no money moves, no
rebuild), followed by one press of "Rebuild ledger".

### COMMCALC-26.8 Cross-references

Same class: §COMMCALC-25 (the filters on the same screens, and the window home this reads), RULE TWO
(§3), §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers left unwired is not a fix). Neighbours: §15 (module
095 and `payable_source_map`), §23z (Device Payable as at a date — the other windowed payable surface,
and the leading-edge lesson that a feed's own incompleteness is not a defect), §COMMCALC-03 (the
handset price home this dereferences), §13a (the store→market resolver the ledger rows use).

## §COMMCALC-27. THE OPERATOR'S INPUT IS SERVICED BEFORE THE NEXT FRAME TICK (owner report 2026-10-22)

Owner, on the UPS Team Portal live login, the day after §COMMCALC-24 made the window visible to him
at all: *"it just freezes , it is not swift access, must easier it seems i hvae to press hard"*.

**The class, not the instance.** `_preauth_loop` and `_post_auth_loop` are SINGLE-THREADED: one
thread streams frames (`_pump`), detects state (`_preauth_detect`) and executes the human's input
(`_do_input`). Both serviced exactly ONE queued command per iteration, and every iteration began
with a full `_pump` — 80ms in CDP mode, 300ms without. `_do_click` then ended with a mandatory
~750ms burst of `wait_for_timeout(250)` plus `vp._wait_settle` plus a re-classification for auth.
So the Nth click was charged for the (N-1)th click's VERIFICATION before it was even dequeued: a
burst drained at a few events a second. Pressing again — the rational response — lengthened the
queue and made it worse. The general fact that was wrong is not "the UPS portal is slow"; it is that
**work which only makes sense once the operator has STOPPED was sitting on the latency path of their
next action, and their input was waiting behind a frame tick.**

### COMMCALC-27.1 Duplicate check (the build gate)

Searched the index and the tree for an existing home for "how promptly does operator input reach the
page": §COMMCALC-10 (`preloop_limit` / `inactivity_limit` — how long a phase may go WITHOUT
progress, a different question), §COMMCALC-13/24 (what a session leaves on the row, and which
process may answer about one), §41 (the forwarder, which adds one network hop per event but does not
schedule them), `_FRAME_PUMP_MS` / `_FALLBACK_PUMP_MS` / `_FRAME_GUARANTEE_S` (frame CADENCE, not
input servicing). No second mechanism answers this; `_preauth_loop` was the only servicer and is
EXTENDED here rather than joined by a sibling. `backend/scratchpad/live_login_lowlat_proof.py` is a
scratch probe of the FRAME path, not a lock, and is untouched.

### COMMCALC-27.2 One fact, one home, dereferenced

- **`live_login.operator_input_pending()`** — THE one reader of "is the operator still acting".
  PURE and never raises: an unreadable queue reads as NOT pending, so the failure mode is the old
  always-settle behaviour rather than silently skipping verification forever.
- **`live_login._next_input()`** — pops HUMAN INPUT only, so draining a burst can never reorder or
  swallow a `SUBMIT_CODE` / `RESEND` / `CANCEL` / `PULL`.
- **`live_login._INPUT_DRAIN_MAX`** — the one declared bound on a drain, so a flood still cannot
  starve the inactivity check or the frame pump.
- `_do_click` DEREFERENCES `operator_input_pending` and keeps no copy of the rule; the harness fails
  the build if any other method reads the queue depth for this decision.

**The frontend half of the same question.** The backend can only service what reaches it, and
`commcalc/email-imports/page.tsx` used to `await` ONE POST PER CHARACTER — a 12-character password
was 12 sequential round trips, each crossing the §41 forwarder, before the first letter appeared
("i cannot put the password , it is very slow", 2026-10-22). Keystrokes are now buffered in
`pendingTextRef` and flushed as ONE `type` event on `LIVE_TYPE_FLUSH_MS` (70ms, one home in the
page). Ordering is the invariant that makes batching safe: `flushText()` runs before ANY other event
(named key, click, double-click, scroll), and every event goes out on ONE promise chain
(`sendChainRef`), so a flushed password can never land behind the Enter that submits it. The
`LiveInputEvent` union types both senders, which also pays off one entry of the lint register rather
than adding to it.

### COMMCALC-27.3 The siblings, fixed here rather than excused

- **`_post_auth_loop` has the identical defect** and is fixed in the same change: "take control" on
  an authenticated session is the same operator typing into the same single-threaded loop.
- The **last click of a burst still settles in full** — nothing pending behind it — so a human
  finishing sign-in is still concluded from their own click, and `_preauth_detect` re-classifies
  every `_CLASSIFY_POLL_S` regardless. The fix removes latency, not verification.
- **RULE TWO:** no portal, tenant or processor name appears anywhere on the latency path; the
  harness asserts their absence.

### COMMCALC-27.4 Locked

`backend/harness_live_input_latency.py` — **68 checks, DB-free, no browser**: one home + purity
(§A), input-only draining (§B), THE LOCK that BOTH loops drain (§C), the bound and that the pump and
idle check still run every iteration (§D), the behaviour on a fake page — burst skipped while input
is queued, taken in full for the last click (§E), order-preserving and lossless draining (§F), and
armed negative controls including the pre-change one-command-per-tick shape and a cap of 1 (§G), and
the FRONTEND half — no awaited request per character, and every event on one ordered chain (§H).
Wired into CI in the `carrier-vocab-guard` lock job, whose path filter names the live-view page as
well as the harness.

### COMMCALC-27.5 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-13 (what a finished session leaves on the row), §COMMCALC-24 (which
process may answer about a session). Same class: §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers left
unwired). Neighbours: §COMMCALC-10 (the progress watchdog on the same session), §COMMCALC-11 (the
human check these clicks are solving), §41 (the forwarder each event now crosses), §COMMCALC-07 (the
UPS pull this login exists to feed).

## §COMMCALC-28. A POLL'S CADENCE IS A GAP BETWEEN RESPONSES, NEVER A TIMER RATE (owner report 2026-10-23)

Owner, after §COMMCALC-27 shipped and deployed (PR #528, squash `b59b82a8`, production built
2026-10-22 22:38 UTC): *"it is very laggy"*. The input half was genuinely fixed — this is a second,
independent cause on the same screen, on the other side of the wire.

### COMMCALC-28.1 THE CLASS, stated once so nobody re-derives it

`setInterval(poll, 300)` fires every 300ms **whether or not the previous response has come back**. The
live-view frame poll crosses three hops (browser → the page's own API route → the API host → the
session host, §41), so its round trip routinely exceeds 300ms. Past that point the polls overlap and
never recover: there is no back-pressure, the number in flight grows to `RTT / interval` and stays
there. Two costs follow, and the second is the one the owner felt:

1. **Every overlapping poll is answered with a full frame of the SAME paint.** `/live-login/frame`
   returns a JPEG only when `_seq` has advanced past the caller's `since`. Overlapping requests all
   carry the `since` that was current when they were issued, so N in-flight polls each ship the same
   viewport-sized JPEG (quality 55, base64 in JSON — a third larger than the bytes).
2. **They hold the browser's per-origin connection budget.** A browser allows ~6 concurrent
   connections per origin over HTTP/1.1. Frame polls occupying them means the operator's own
   keystroke POST waits in the queue behind pictures of the page they are typing into.

> **A poll's cadence is the gap between its RESPONSES, not the rate of a timer. Work that only makes
> sense once the operator has stopped must never hold the connection their next action needs.**

This is the same rule as §COMMCALC-27, one layer out: there, the operator's click waited behind the
previous click's verification; here, it waits behind the previous frames' downloads.

### COMMCALC-28.2 DUPLICATE CHECK (the build gate) — what was REUSED, not rebuilt

| question | existing home | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| how promptly does the operator's input reach the page | `live_login.operator_input_pending` + the drained loops (§COMMCALC-27) | **reused, untouched** |
| which process may answer about a session | `live_login.require_session_host` (§COMMCALC-24) | **reused, untouched** |
| how often does the worker produce a frame | `_FRAME_PUMP_MS` / `_FALLBACK_PUMP_MS` / `_FRAME_GUARANTEE_S` (§COMMCALC-13) | **reused, untouched** — the worker's cadence is not the client's |
| does this frame differ from the one the client has | `LiveLoginSession.frame_since(since)` | **reused, untouched** — the server was already correct; the client asked wrongly |
| how often does the CLIENT ask for a frame | `setInterval(refreshFrame, 300)` + `nudgeFrames`'s three timers | **EXTENDED into one scheduler — §COMMCALC-28.3** |

No second mechanism polls frames. `refreshFrame` was the only fetcher and remains the only fetcher;
what changed is that exactly one caller may invoke it, and only when none is in flight. No endpoint,
table, migration or backend behaviour changes here, and no money is touched.

### COMMCALC-28.3 ONE FACT, ONE HOME, DEREFERENCED

In `frontend/src/app/(platform)/commcalc/email-imports/page.tsx`:

- **`pollFrames`** is THE one issuer of a frame request. It returns early when one is in flight, and
  arms the next one in a `finally` — so a failed or slow response slows the cadence instead of being
  skipped, and cannot stop the loop.
- **`frameBusyRef`** is THE one reader of "a frame request is already in flight". Nothing else may
  issue one; `refreshFrame` is awaited in exactly one place.
- **`frameSoonRef`** records a nudge that arrived mid-flight, so it is honoured once that response
  settles rather than becoming a second parallel request.
- **`frameOpenRef`** stops the loop when the modal closes, so a closed view is never polled.
- **`LIVE_FRAME_GAP_MS` (300)** and **`LIVE_FRAME_NUDGE_MS` (120)** are the two cadences, one home
  each. The nudge may never be slower than the idle gap, and the idle gap may never exceed one
  second — both asserted.

`nudgeFrames` no longer takes a list of delays and no longer calls the poll itself: it sets the flag
the one scheduler reads. A burst of clicks therefore adds no requests at all; it only brings the next
one forward.

### COMMCALC-28.4 THE SIBLINGS

The frame poll is the only fixed-rate poll on this screen's latency path; `pollLogin` (the row poll
while a login runs in the background) awaits its own request before sleeping 3s and so already paces
itself by its responses. The upload-list refresh after a submit fires on a fixed ladder of timers,
but it is not on any operator input path and ships no frames — explicitly excused rather than
changed. The harness asserts the page declares **no** `setInterval` in code at all, so a future
fixed-rate poll on this page fails the build wherever it is added.

### COMMCALC-28.5 LOCKED

`backend/harness_live_input_latency.py` §I — 91 checks in the file now, DB-free and browser-free. It
fails the build if a `setInterval` drives the frame path (or appears in this page's code at all), if
anything calls `refreshFrame` outside the scheduler, if the in-flight guard or the mid-flight
remember is removed, if the next poll stops being armed in a `finally`, if the nudge fans out timers
again, or if either cadence loses its one home. Three armed controls assert the pre-change shapes —
the `setInterval(refreshFrame, 300)`, the fan-out `nudgeFrames`, and a bare `refreshFrame()` call —
all read as broken. The harness already runs in the `carrier-vocab-guard` lock job.

### COMMCALC-28.6 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-27 (the input half of the same latency question), §COMMCALC-13
(what a finished session leaves on the row), §COMMCALC-24 (which process may answer about a session).
Same class: §COMMCALC-27 (work that only matters once the operator stopped, on the path of their next
action). Neighbours: §41 (the three hops each poll crosses), §COMMCALC-10 (the progress watchdog on
the same session), §COMMCALC-07 (the UPS pull this login exists to feed).


## §COMMCALC-29. A DECLARED SOURCE THAT CANNOT BE READ IS REPORTED — never read as "nothing was declared" (defect found in live data 2026-10-23)

**Found in my own work, one day after shipping it.** The owner applied §COMMCALC-26's migration and
carrier-terms runbook and pressed Rebuild ledger. The rebuild reported success. Read back against
the live ledger: 4,322 Luxelink devices, 2,923 unsold, **0 priced**, every row
`owed = NULL, owed_source = 'unconfigured'`, and the out-of-pocket exposure headlined **$0.00**. The
true exposure was **$595,125.59** across 2,283 devices.

**The immediate cause was one config value, and it was mine.** The runbook declared
`payable_source_map.owed_price_table = 'raw_ma_fulfillment'`. That column does not name the price
list — the price list is always the distributor's handset-ordering sheet and is deliberately NOT
configurable (`account/device_cogs.ma_unit_price_map`, the one home §COMMCALC-26.4). It names the
EVIDENCE feed: the table whose rows prove which product names are handsets at all, which is the
commission feed `raw_ma_commission`, the one carrying a `sku` per activated line.
`raw_ma_fulfillment` has no `sku`, so the read raised PostgREST `42703`.

### COMMCALC-29.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

Correcting the value fixes the instance. The general fact that was wrong is this: **a reader that
swallows a declared read's failure into an empty result makes a broken DECLARATION indistinguishable
from an absent one.** "No invoice has priced this device" is a sentence about the DATA; the truth was
a sentence about the SETUP, and nothing anywhere said so. Three readers in `payables/engine.py` had
exactly that shape, and each one's silence is a different wrong answer:

| declared read | what the silence says | what it costs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the device-cost EVIDENCE feed (`owed_price_table`/`_model_field`) | "nobody invoiced this device" | every device unpriced — the 2026-10-23 defect |
| `owed_link` (mig 620) | the same | every device the related report would have priced |
| the sold-match feed (`sold_match_table`/`_imei_field`) | "this device is unsold and has no store" | the out-of-pocket list OVERSTATED, the store filter empty |

A second, quieter copy of the same class sat in the summary: a device can be out of pocket and carry
no cost, and the sum then understates the exposure **while looking like a total**. $0.00 was
presented exactly as a real figure would have been.

### COMMCALC-29.2 THE ONE HOME

`backend/app/modules/payables/declared_source.py` — PURE, standard library only.

- `Complaints(label)` — the declared reads that failed during one build. Append-only, never raises.
- `read_declared(complaints, kind, table, field, read, empty, label)` — the fail-soft every caller
  already had, with the failure KEPT. `read` is the only thing that touches a client, which is what
  keeps the module provable with a lambda that raises.
- `COST[kind]` — what the silence costs, stated once per kind so a new declared read cannot ship
  wordless; the harness asserts every kind has one.
- `owed_source_label(declared, have_prices)` → `price_source_unreadable` when a cost source was
  declared and produced nothing, else `unconfigured`. **`unconfigured` keeps its old meaning**: this
  carrier declares no cost source at all.
- `merge(result, complaints)` — folds the notes into the build result under the key `warnings`.

### COMMCALC-29.3 DEGRADE, DON'T DIE

The old `_unit_price_map` held the evidence read and the price read inside ONE `try`, so an evidence
failure returned `{}` and threw away the price home's documented no-evidence behaviour — its
order-type allowlist, which still prices most handsets. Measured on the live feeds: with evidence
**2,283 of 2,923 (78.1%)** unsold devices price; with the allowlist alone **2,143 (73.3%)**; with the
old code **0**. The price read now sits OUTSIDE the evidence branch, and the harness proves that
structurally (§D10) because it is the difference between 73% and nothing.

### COMMCALC-29.4 WHO SEES WHAT — reusing the §19.36 boundary, not a second copy

A complaint names the table and the column, because the person who must fix it is the platform admin
reading the rebuild response. It travels under the MESSAGE KEY `warnings`, which
`core/setup_notice.py` already owns: the super admin sees the technical text, everyone else gets the
one `SETUP_NOTICE` sentence and the detail goes to the server log. No decision about customer-facing
copy is re-made here.

### COMMCALC-29.5 The siblings, fixed here rather than excused

All three readers above take a `complaints` and record; `_sold_imei_set` passes it through. Dropping
the optional `store` column remains a known benign fallback and is deliberately NOT a complaint —
failing the key-only read too is. `unsold_inventory.stamp_aging` gained
`out_of_pocket_unpriced` + `amount_incomplete`, the one boolean a screen reads before presenting the
sum as a total — the verdict itself is unchanged and still comes from
`commcalc/device_aging_policy.py` (§COMMCALC-26), because the defect was never in the verdict but in
presenting an incomplete sum of it as a total. The payables screen renders the rebuild's warnings, and `lib/owed-source.ts` is the
one home for the words — rendering the raw `owed_source` is what made the broken declaration read as
an absent one.

### COMMCALC-29.6 Locked so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_payables_declared_source.py` — **42 passed, 0 failed**. §A the pure home, §B the two
labels keep their distinct meanings, §C the exposure total cannot look complete when it is not
(including the exact 2026-10-23 shape), §D the RATCHET: each of the four readers must accept a
collector, the build must make one per carrier and pass it to each, the notes must reach the build
RESULT and not just a log line, no literal `owed_source = "unconfigured"` may survive, and the price
read must stay outside the evidence branch.

### COMMCALC-29.7 What is owner-gated

- `database/migrations/1092_payable_price_source_comments.sql` — COMMENTs only, no column, grant or
  row touched, nothing to recompute. It names on the columns themselves which table
  `owed_price_table` points at, because mig 1091 shipped them with no comment and the very first row
  written against them got it wrong.
- `/mnt/project-files/payables-carrier-terms/STEP_3_fix_price_source_2026-10-23.sql` — the one-Run
  correction (`owed_price_table = 'raw_ma_commission'` on the two Total rows), then one more Rebuild
  ledger press. Verified against the live feeds before it was handed over: 54 evidence skus, 36
  priced models, 2,283 of 2,923 devices priced, $595,125.59. The 640 that stay NULL are 618 rows of
  the distributor's own "Product Not Available" sku plus 22 models never bought on the sheet — NULL
  on purpose, never a $0 that would read as settled.

### COMMCALC-29.8 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-26 (the declared terms this is the honesty half of), §COMMCALC-25
(the filters on the same screen). Same class: §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers left
unwired), §66 (a last-resort placement read as evidence — the same mistake one layer up), §19.36 (the
boundary reused here). Neighbours: §64 (store identity, which the same rebuild stamps), §19.48 (the
complete paged read these three readers all cross).

## §COMMCALC-30. A HUMAN WHO IS WATCHING IS NOT IDLE (owner evidence 2026-10-23)

Not a report — a finding. The owner's 00:48 live-login session did not fail; the row read
`auth_status: None`, *"Live session closed after inactivity."*, with `login_shot_at 00:48:45`. It was
killed by its own idle budget at roughly 00:56, while he was working in it.

### COMMCALC-30.1 THE CLASS, stated once so nobody re-derives it

`_touch()` resets the activity clock, and it is called by operator COMMANDS only — `submit`,
`resend`, `input_event`, `cancel`, `pull`. The `/live-login/state` and `/live-login/frame` polls never
called it, by deliberate design: a poll is automatic, so letting it count as activity would let an
abandoned browser tab hold a headless browser open forever.

The error is not that polls were excluded. It is that **one fact was being used to answer two
different questions**:

- *Is anybody there?* — answered correctly by "has a surface asked about this session recently".
- *Is the person there acting?* — answered correctly by `_touch()`.

`_HUMAN_ACTION_IDLE_SECONDS` (8 minutes, against the ordinary 20) is **shortened on the assumption
that nobody is acting**. Applied to a human who is demonstrably present — reading the page, or
solving the captcha the phase is named for — that assumption is simply false, and the shortening
closes the session out from under exactly the person it is waiting for.

> **A budget shortened because we assume nobody is there must not apply while someone demonstrably
> is. Watching is not acting — but it is being there.**

### COMMCALC-30.2 ONE FACT, ONE HOME, DEREFERENCED

- **`_note_viewer()`** records a sighting. It is called by the two methods that ANSWER a question
  about a session — `state()` and `frame_since()` — so presence is recorded *wherever the question is
  answered*, rather than at each endpoint that might forget to. It deliberately does **not** touch
  `_last_activity`.
- **`viewer_present()`** is THE one reader of "is a human watching this session right now". Pure,
  never raises, and a session nobody has polled reads as NOT watched — so the failure mode is the
  pre-fix budget, never a browser held open.
- **`_VIEWER_PRESENT_SECONDS` (30)** is the one presence window. A client polls frames every ~300ms
  (§COMMCALC-28), so 30 seconds of silence means the tab is gone.
- **`inactivity_limit(phase, watched)`** remains the one budget reader. `watched` changes exactly one
  thing: the shortened `human_action` budget does not apply, and the ordinary `_IDLE_CLOSE_SECONDS`
  does instead.

**Nothing gets a budget LONGER than one that already existed.** That is the load-bearing constraint,
not a detail: a longer watched budget was written first and reverted, because `in_flight_stale_after_s`
(§COMMCALC-13) derives the staleness window from the longest an operator may legitimately hold a
session — and widening it past an hour would have made a killed worker's leftover `authenticating`
row read as *live*, which is the one regression §COMMCALC-13 exists to prevent. `max_inactivity_limit()`
is now the home that derivation dereferences, so a budget added later widens it instead of silently
invalidating it.

### COMMCALC-30.3 THE SIBLING, EXCUSED WITH ITS REASON

`_post_auth_loop`'s `_POST_AUTH_IDLE_SECONDS` (15 minutes) is **not** a site of this defect, and is
left unchanged rather than silently: it is the hold-open window for an already signed-in browser, not
a budget shortened on the assumption nobody is acting, so no watching human is being cut short by it.
The excuse is recorded at the call site too.

### COMMCALC-30.4 DUPLICATE CHECK (the build gate) — what was REUSED, not rebuilt

| question | existing home | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| how long may a phase go without an operator input | `inactivity_limit` (§COMMCALC-10) | **EXTENDED with the `watched` argument — not joined by a sibling** |
| how long may a phase make no progress | `preloop_limit` | **reused, untouched** |
| how long may an in-flight row stand before it is a leftover | `in_flight_stale_after_s` (§COMMCALC-13) | **re-pointed at `max_inactivity_limit()` so it cannot be invalidated** |
| has the operator acted | `_touch` / `_last_activity` | **reused, untouched — deliberately not conflated with presence** |
| how promptly does input reach the page | §COMMCALC-27 | reused, untouched |
| how often does the client ask for a frame | §COMMCALC-28 | reused, untouched — and it is what makes presence detectable at all |

### COMMCALC-30.5 LOCKED

`harness_live_login_progress.py` §J — 95 checks in the file now, DB-free and browser-free, in the
same job that already ran it. It fails the build if the unwatched budgets move, if a watched phase
ever asks for more than `max_inactivity_limit()`, if `_last_seen_at` gains a fourth site, if a
sighting touches the activity clock, if `state` or `frame_since` stops recording one, or if the loop
reads the raw flag instead of `viewer_present()`. `harness_terminal_status.py` §F now locks the whole
derivation CHAIN — budget → `max_inactivity_limit` → the constants — rather than one constant's name,
which is strictly stronger. Three armed controls assert the pre-change shapes read as broken.

### COMMCALC-30.6 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-27 (input on the latency path), §COMMCALC-28 (the frame poll, whose
cadence is what makes presence observable), §COMMCALC-13 (what a finished session leaves on the row,
and the staleness window this must not widen), §COMMCALC-24 (which process may answer at all).
Neighbours: §COMMCALC-10 (the progress budgets this sits beside), §COMMCALC-11 (the human check the
8-minute budget was named for), §COMMCALC-07 (the UPS pull this login exists to feed).
