## §COMMCALC-31. DETECTION IS OFF THE OPERATOR'S INPUT PATH TOO, AND THE SESSION SAYS WHAT IT IS DOING (owner report 2026-10-26)

Two sentences from the owner on the UPS Team Portal login, four days after §COMMCALC-27 shipped and
deployed: *"it does not go past it , it is very slow to react"* and *"also it shoudl show what is
going on it seems nothing is moving"*. His 18:06 UTC attempt is on the row — the start path is
healthy; the window he was given was not.

### COMMCALC-31.1 THE CLASS — the same sentence, a second place

§COMMCALC-27 established the rule and fixed ONE site of it:

> **Work that only makes sense once the operator has STOPPED must never sit on the latency path of
> their next action, and their input must never wait behind a frame tick.**

It took the click's ~750ms VERIFICATION off that path. It left the loop's own DETECTION on it.
`_preauth_detect` is not cheap: `_classify` reads the text of **every frame** of the page and
`_captcha_present` queries selectors across all of them. On a heavy portal that costs far more than a
frame tick — and the order of the tick was `_pump` → (every `_CLASSIFY_POLL_S`) detect → **then**
drain the operator's input. So the first click of a burst was charged for a pump PLUS a whole page
re-read before it was even dequeued. The fix named the class correctly and then stopped at the
instance, which is precisely what the 2026-09-20 directive forbids.

### COMMCALC-31.2 ONE FACT, ONE HOME, DEREFERENCED

- **The input drain LEADS the tick**, in `_preauth_loop` and `_post_auth_loop` alike — ahead of the
  pump and ahead of the detect, not after them. That is what makes the rule true of the first click
  of a burst and not only the rest of it.
- **`detect_due(now, last_detect, input_pending)`** is THE one answer to *may detection run on this
  tick*. Pure, and it never raises: unreadable inputs read as **DUE**, so the failure mode is the old
  always-detect behaviour, never a session that silently stops noticing a captcha.
- **It reads the home §COMMCALC-27 already established** — `operator_input_pending` — rather than
  peeking at the queue a second time. One reader of "still acting", as it was before.
- **`_DETECT_DEFER_MAX_S` (4s)** is the ceiling, and it is load-bearing: *defer while they are
  acting* with no ceiling is exactly how a captcha appearing mid-burst would stop being seen. Past
  the ceiling detection runs regardless of input.

### COMMCALC-31.3 THE REPORTING HALF — a standing instruction does not move

`phase` and `message` are an INSTRUCTION ("complete the login on the screen"), not a report of
progress. They are identical for a session grinding through a page re-read and a session that has
stopped, which is why *"nothing is moving"* was a reasonable reading and not a display preference.
The step in flight is a **different fact** from the phase, so it gets its own home:

- **`_note_act(doing)`** is the one setter. Lock-only — it never touches the page or the row, because
  it runs on the hot path.
- **`activity()`** is the one reader: the step, how long it has been in flight, and the age of the
  newest frame. Ages are **None** before the first frame, never a fabricated `0` that would read as
  "a frame just arrived".
- **`state()` and `frame_since()` dereference it.** Neither composes its own answer, and the
  *unchanged* frame payload carries it too — so the line moves even when the picture does not, which
  is the whole point.
- The modal renders it only when the backend sent one. There is no client-side "working…".

What it buys beyond comfort: *"it does not go past it"* is still undiagnosed, and this is the
instrument that will say which step the next attempt sits on instead of leaving it to memory.

### COMMCALC-31.4 THE SIBLINGS, CHECKED

| other path that answers the same question | verdict |
| --- | --- |
| `_post_auth_loop` (the same operator typing into the same single-threaded loop) | **FIXED in this PR** — its drain leads its tick too |
| `vidapay_sweep`'s `_classify` call sites (the unattended sweeps) | **excused with the reason**: no operator is waiting on them, so nothing of theirs is on a latency path |
| `_drive`'s single pre-loop classify | **excused**: it runs before any input queue exists |
| `_do_click`'s post-click re-classify | **already fixed** by §COMMCALC-27 and untouched here |

### COMMCALC-31.5 DUPLICATE CHECK (the build gate) — what was REUSED, not rebuilt

| question | existing home | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| is the operator still acting | `operator_input_pending` (§COMMCALC-27) | **reused, untouched** — the deferral reads it |
| how promptly does input reach the page | §COMMCALC-27 | **EXTENDED to the detect path — not joined by a sibling** |
| how often may state be re-detected | `_CLASSIFY_POLL_S` | **folded into `detect_due`; the loop no longer compares against it inline** |
| how long may a phase go without input | `inactivity_limit` (§COMMCALC-10, §COMMCALC-30) | reused, untouched |
| is a human watching | `viewer_present` (§COMMCALC-30) | reused, untouched |
| how often does the client ask for a frame | §COMMCALC-28 | reused, untouched — the activity line rides that same poll |
| what phase is this session in | `phase` / `message` | reused, untouched — deliberately NOT conflated with the step in flight |

### COMMCALC-31.6 LOCKED

`harness_live_input_latency.py` §J and §K — 151 checks in the file now, DB-free, browser-free, in the
job that already ran it. It fails the build if the drain stops leading either tick, if the loop
re-decides the poll interval itself instead of dereferencing `detect_due`, if the deferral loses its
ceiling (an unbounded deferral is an armed negative control), if `detect_due` stops reading
`operator_input_pending`, if detection is removed rather than deferred, if a surface reads the raw
activity field instead of `activity()`, if `_note_act` grows a page or row write, or if the frontend
invents a step the backend never sent.

### COMMCALC-31.7 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-27 (the rule this applies in its second place), §COMMCALC-28 (the
poll that carries the activity line), §COMMCALC-30 (who is there), §COMMCALC-13 (what a finished
session leaves on the row), §COMMCALC-24 (which process may answer at all). Neighbours:
§COMMCALC-10 (the no-progress budgets), §COMMCALC-11 (the human check), §COMMCALC-07 (the UPS pull
this login exists to feed).
## §COMMCALC-35. A DEVICE'S ARRIVAL ON THE SHELF HAS ONE DATE (owner ask 2026-10-26)

Owner, verbatim: *"invenotry aging in luxeliunk shodul say sell within 10 days of receiving the
phones in stock and it should be on every sales reps daSHBOARDS WHEN TEHY LOG IN"*.

**Module:** `backend/app/modules/commcalc/inventory_stock_age.py` (the one home) ·
`backend/app/modules/commcalc/device_history.py` (`build_aging_inventory`, the caller that disagreed)
**Lock:** `backend/harness_inventory_stock_age.py` — 36 checks · and
`backend/harness_inventory_stock_age_guard.py` — the build gate, run by `carrier-vocab-guard.yml`
**Migration:** none. The window itself is a config ROW (§COMMCALC-35.6).

### COMMCALC-35.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

The ask looks like a number change. It is not: it names a fact the platform had no single answer for
— **the date a handset was received into stock.** `commcalc.inventory_aging_device.received_date`
exists and is **NULL on all 10,525 rows house-wide** (measured against production 2026-10-26, both
tenants). The POS export carries the unit's AGE instead — `raw_row`'s `"Age in Store"` — landed as
`days_in_stock` against the file's `as_of_date`.

So the receipt date must be DERIVED, and three callers each derived it:

| caller | what it did | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `router._derived_received` (`GET /inventory-recon`) | `as_of_date − days_in_stock` | right |
| `router._mi_ever_over_days` (the MI aging bonus gate) | `as_of_date − days_in_stock` | right |
| `device_history.build_aging_inventory` | read `days_in_stock` **verbatim** | the age ON THE DAY THE FILE WAS PULLED |

The third is the defect, and it was invisible because its answer is a plausible number: a unit last
seen in a 2026-07-25 snapshot reported **9 days** on the Device History screen in October, where the
other two reported **102**. The MI gate's own comment already recorded the shared fact — *"the
luxelink aging export carries age, not a received date"* — beside its own private copy of it, which
is the §19.18 shape this index has now logged four times.

### COMMCALC-35.2 THE ONE HOME

`backend/app/modules/commcalc/inventory_stock_age.py` — PURE, standard library plus
`device_aging_policy`. No DB, no I/O.

- `received_on(row)` — THE derivation. The feed's own `received_date` when it has one, else
  `as_of_date − days_in_stock`, else `None`. A negative age is refused rather than dating a receipt
  in the future.
- `received_basis(row)` — `received_date` | `age_at_snapshot` | `not_measured`. A surface that shows
  a deadline can say whether a receipt document supplied the date or the POS's age did.
- `current_snapshot(rows)` / `on_shelf(row, snapshot)` — **the ghost rule, reused not re-derived.**
  `inventory_aging_device` is upserted one row per `(org, imei)` (mig `216`), so a row's `as_of_date`
  is the last file that unit appeared in, and a flip that never ran leaves `on_hand=true` on a unit
  that is long gone. `account/balance_sheet.py` already measured ~$129k of such ghosts. ON THE SHELF
  therefore means `on_hand` **AND** carrying the org's current snapshot date. Measured 2026-10-26:
  Luxelink holds **1,444** `on_hand=true` rows and **888** at the current snapshot.
- `days_on_shelf(row, today)` — counted to TODAY, never read off the file. This is the line
  `device_history` crossed.
- `days_left(row, policy, today)` — the window minus the age. Negative is RETURNED, not clamped:
  "4 days over" and "due today" are different conversations.
- `resolve_window(carrier_id, policies, maps)` → `(policy | None, reason | None)` — §COMMCALC-35.4.
- `shelf_row` / `summarise` — the render shape and its headline.

### COMMCALC-35.3 THE AGE IS NEVER THE FILE'S AGE

Stated separately because it is the half most likely to be undone by a well-meaning edit. A reader
that wants "days in stock" will find the column sitting right there, already an integer, already
named for the question. It answers only for the day the file was pulled. Every surface asking a rep
or a manager to act TODAY must count to today, and the guard (§COMMCALC-35.5) fails the build on the
one assignment that re-introduces it.

### COMMCALC-35.4 AN UNESTABLISHED DEADLINE IS NOT THE HOUSE DEFAULT

`resolve_window` deliberately does **not** fall back to the house 60 days the way
`unsold_inventory.policy_for` does:

| situation | answer |
| --- | --- |
| carrier known and mapped | that carrier's declared policy |
| carrier unknown, every active map declares the SAME window | that window — not a guess: whichever carrier it is, the number is the same |
| carrier unknown, the org's windows DIFFER | no policy, reason `carrier_windows_differ` |
| the org declares no map at all | no policy, reason `carrier_not_identified` |

The 60-day fallback is right for a payables TOTAL, which must not lose a device. It is wrong on a
rep's card, where printing "45 days left" over a 10-day carrier's phone is the exact defect
§COMMCALC-26 was opened for. Two callers, two needs, one window resolver that is explicit about
which it is serving.

### COMMCALC-35.5 Locked so it cannot un-wire

`backend/harness_inventory_stock_age_guard.py` — the build gate. Three axes:

1. **No second derivation.** No function outside the one home may subtract `days_in_stock` from an
   `as_of_date`. It resolves **each file's own `timedelta` import aliases** from its AST rather than
   assuming the spelling: the first draft of this scanner missed
   `from datetime import timedelta as td`, and a guard with a blind spot is the patchwork it exists
   to prevent.
2. **Every collapsed caller still dereferences it**, by name — `_derived_received`,
   `_mi_ever_over_days`, `build_aging_inventory` — plus the specific assignment
   (`days = int(dis)`) whose return would restore the stale age. Counting copies alone would pass a
   caller quietly reverted to believing the file.
3. **The shelf test is not re-invented**, and `balance_sheet`'s per-store variant is excused BY NAME
   with its reason (latest `as_of` per STORE, a different grain, pinned by its own harness) rather
   than by silence.

Six negative controls N1–N6 pin that reading either column to DISPLAY it is not flagged, that a
`timedelta` subtraction without `days_in_stock` is not flagged, and that the real defect is caught
under all three `timedelta` spellings.

`backend/harness_inventory_stock_age.py` — 36 checks, DB-free, including the owner's regression
stated as arithmetic (a unit received 16 days ago reads **6 days over** a declared 10-day window and
**4 over** the previous 12, so the CONFIG ROW moves the number and no literal in code does) and the
stale-snapshot defect stated as a measurement (102, not 9).

### COMMCALC-35.6 What is owner-gated

`/mnt/project-files/inventory-aging-window/RUN_luxelink_sell_within_10_2026-10-26.sql` — one Run, one
column, one row: `payable_source_map.sell_within_days` 12 → 10 on the Luxelink Total/MA map. No code
change ships the number. Coordinated with the branch declaring `net_terms_days = 21` on the same two
rows, which writes a disjoint column set, so neither reverts the other.

## §COMMCALC-36. A REP'S SHELF, ON THE SCREEN A REP LANDS ON (owner ask 2026-10-26)

Owner, verbatim, same sentence as §COMMCALC-35: the selling deadline *"should be on every sales reps
daSHBOARDS WHEN TEHY LOG IN"*.

**Module:** `backend/app/modules/commcalc/router.py` (`GET /commcalc/my-shelf`) ·
`frontend/src/app/(platform)/commcalc/targets/my/_components/ShelfAging.tsx`
**Lock:** the pure logic is §COMMCALC-35's two harnesses; the endpoint composes them and owns no
arithmetic of its own.
**Migration:** none.

### COMMCALC-36.1 WHY THAT SCREEN

`/commcalc/targets/my` is the configured `home` for the `sales_rep` role (mig `015`), so it is the
first screen after sign-in rather than a page a rep would have to find. Management Overview reports
are dashboard TILES and a new sidebar row is where reports go to be unfound (the 2026-10-08 ruling),
so the deadline goes on the landing screen itself.

### COMMCALC-36.2 FOUR FACTS, FOUR EXISTING HOMES

Nothing is derived in the endpoint. It composes:

| fact | home |
| --- | --- |
| which stores does this login reach | `storeops.router.scope_keyset` (§14x — evidence: scheduled or clocked in) |
| when did this unit arrive, is it still here | `commcalc/inventory_stock_age.py` (§COMMCALC-35) |
| how long may it sit | `commcalc/device_aging_policy.py` over declared `payable_source_map` (§COMMCALC-26) |
| is this a device at all | `asset/inventory_buckets.inv_bucket` (§11a — the ONE classifier) |
| which store is this address | `account/store_identity` via `_store_code_resolver` (§13a) |

The span being EVIDENCE-based is load-bearing, not incidental: **9 of Luxelink's 32 active rep logins
carry no `store_code`** (measured 2026-10-26), and the card sits above the targets and OUTSIDE that
page's "no store assigned" early return so those reps still see their shelf.

### COMMCALC-36.3 THE POS SNAPSHOT, NOT THE PAYABLE LEDGER

`commcalc.device_payable_ledger` is the carrier's PAYMENT story. Measured 2026-10-26: its Luxelink
unsold set (**3,095** units) and the POS on-hand set (**888**) overlap by **twelve**, and for several
IMEIs its `invoice_date` equals the snapshot date on which the POS flipped the unit off-hand — i.e.
it is the activation/transaction date (`raw_ma_commission.tx_date`), independently confirmed by the
payables thread the same day. Counting a SELLING window from it would be wrong twice over: wrong
anchor, wrong population. A rep asked what is on their shelf is told what is on their shelf. The
card never reads the ledger, which is also why it cannot disagree with the dealer-owned-device
(BYOP) exclusion now in §COMMCALC-32 (PR #561, merged 2026-10-26): a line whose own carrier feed
declares no handset was bought leaves the payable totals under its own status. That section and this
one answer different questions about the same devices — which units the carrier will pay for, versus
which units are physically on a rep's shelf — and neither reads the other's source.

### COMMCALC-36.4 WHAT IT REFUSES TO INVENT

- A unit whose carrier cannot be identified shows its AGE and names why the deadline is missing
  (§COMMCALC-35.4). It never inherits the house 60.
- A unit with no age is counted as `undated`, apart from both "overdue" and "fine"; `no_window` is
  counted apart from `undated`, because an unknown age and an unknown deadline are different gaps
  with different fixes (a feed versus a config row).
- A FAILED READ says so on the card. "You have nothing aging" and "we could not ask" are different
  sentences and only one of them is reassuring.
- The device filter REPORTS what it held back, with model names. Measured on the live snapshot the
  442 excluded units are exactly two names — "Total by Verizon SIM Kit" (435) and "Total Wireless
  BYOT SIM Kit" (7) — so no handset is lost to the filter, and they were drowning the real signal:
  **442 of the 689 overdue rows, carrying $1,326 of the $71,268**.
- "Received" is labelled on the card as derived from the POS age in stock, because no vendor receipt
  date exists in this platform (§COMMCALC-35.1). Calling it a receipt date would be the quiet
  overstatement the house rules treat as a defect.
- An empty card prints the server's REASON — no snapshot, no span, no devices, or no declared window
  — never a zero (the §29.12 "never blank" rule).

### COMMCALC-36.5 Verified against production, not only in a harness

Driving the real pure modules over the real rows at the 2026-10-26 snapshot: **446** phones,
tablets, watches and hotspots on hand at Luxelink, **247** already past a 10-day window
(**$69,941.61**), **0** undated, **0** without a window. One Chicago store's rep sees 36 units, the
oldest received 2026-07-02. All **20** store spellings in the feed resolve to a roster `store_code`
through the real `store_identity` resolver.

Under the window in force before the change (12 days) that same 446-unit shelf reads **170** overdue
worth $55,482.32; at 10 days it reads **247** worth $69,941.61, so **77** units cross and the 50 that
read "due today" at 12 are already past at 10. The config row, not code, carries the number. Counting
the SIM kits in, the figures are 612 and 689 — which is the measurement that decided they stay out of
the card.

## §COMMCALC-32. A LINE THAT BOUGHT NO DEVICE IS NOT A DEVICE PAYABLE (owner report 2026-10-26)

**What he saw.** Every row on the payables tab read `Product Not Available`, with `—` under Owed,
Rebate, Net owed and Due, and two of them carried the status **discrepancy** — which the legend on
that same screen defines as *"the device was sold but no equipment rebate came back — the dealer is
still carrying its cost"*. His words: *"product not available , it shoudl show the product"*.

**What was true.** There was no product to show, because no handset was bought on those lines. The
carrier feed says so itself: `commcalc.raw_ma_commission.activation_type2` declares `branded` on
3,567 rows (every one of them naming a model) and `byop` on 869 (every one of them naming none); 59
rows declare nothing at all. Zero of those 928 unnamed lines carry `device_margin`,
`consumer_financing` or `is_financed = Yes`. Two other feeds were checked for a recoverable model
and ruled out, which is worth recording so nobody re-derives it: `inventory_aging_device` covers 1 of
888, and `raw_sales.serial_1` covers 260 — with PLAN descriptions ("Total MAX 5G BYO Plan $30"),
confirming rather than contradicting the declaration.

So the screen was not failing to look up a product. It was asserting a cost the owner never incurred,
on the one status whose whole meaning is "you are out of pocket for this handset".

### COMMCALC-32.1 THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

The instance is 869 BYOP rows on one Luxelink feed. The general fact that was wrong:
**a ledger that writes one row per ACTIVATION has assumed that every activation bought a device, and
an activation is not a purchase.** A payable must be able to say "nothing is owed here because
nothing was bought" as a positive answer, distinct from "something is owed and I could not price it".
Before this change those two collapsed into the same blank, so a missing price and a missing purchase
looked identical — and whichever way the row then fell, one of them was a lie.

The second half of the class is the one §66 already names: **the absence of a value is not evidence.**
A line that merely fails to name a product proves nothing — the feed may simply have omitted it. Only
the feed's OWN declaration counts. That is why the 59 rows that declare nothing stay unclassified and
keep their payable status, and why the harness's §A9 is the test that matters.

### COMMCALC-32.2 DUPLICATE CHECK (the build gate) — what was REUSED, not rebuilt

| the question | who already answered it | what this change did |
| --- | --- | --- |
| did this line sell a device? | `commcalc/product_mix.py` — the device-class vocabulary, §COMMCALC-03.21 | **EXTENDED** it with `no_device_declared()` + `DECLARED_NO_DEVICE_BASIS`; `product_class_of` now dereferences the same predicate instead of re-reading the tokens |
| which dates is a surface showing, both ends inclusive? | `commcalc/date_window.py` — the window one home, §COMMCALC-25 | **EXTENDED** with `ahead_window()`; no second date arithmetic was written |
| which store is this address? | `account/store_identity` (§64), via `_store_key` | **REUSED** verbatim as the key of the per-store split |
| which market is this store in? | `_market_by_store` / `_market_of` (RULE FIVE) | **REUSED** — the owed tab's new market filter resolves through the same home the list tab does, so "North" means one thing on both |
| is a placement evidence or a fallback? | `carrier_dollar_class.component_is_evidence` (§66) | **REUSED as doctrine**: only the declared basis excludes a row |

Nothing new was created to answer a question already answered. What IS new is a vocabulary that did
not exist anywhere: which ledger statuses are payable at all.

### COMMCALC-32.3 ONE FACT, ONE HOME, DEREFERENCED

`backend/app/modules/payables/ledger_status.py` — the ONE home for *"is this ledger row money that is
owed?"*. Pure, and deliberately **zero imports**, because `engine` reaches `asset.router` which
reaches `unsold_inventory`, and a status vocabulary that cannot be imported from either end is a
vocabulary nobody can dereference.

- `PAYABLE_STATUSES` = open · due · discrepancy · offset; `NON_PAYABLE_STATUSES` = no_device.
- `is_payable(status)` is **fail-open**: a status this module has never heard of counts as payable, so
  a future status cannot quietly delete money from a total.
- `exclude_non_payable(q, column)` is the one place a QUERY expresses the exclusion, so every reader
  excludes by the same `not.in` rather than by its own list of strings.
- `EXCLUDED_NOTE` is the sentence the screens show. One wording, one home.
- `OWED_SOURCE_NO_DEVICE = "no_device_declared"` keeps the reason ON the row: the blank Owed now says
  *why* it is blank, next to §COMMCALC-29's `unconfigured` / `price_source_unreadable`.

Callers wired, all three in the same PR: `payables/engine.py` (writes the status),
`payables/router.py` (list · `/due` · `/owed-by-date` · the drill-down's `is_payable`),
`payables/unsold_inventory.py` (the out-of-pocket read, which is the one that would otherwise have
headlined a BYOP phone as unrecovered cost).

**The row is kept, not dropped.** A dropped row cannot be audited and cannot be argued with, so the
lines stay listed under their own status and the count of them is reported — `no_device_excluded` plus
`no_device_note` on the response, shown in the legend. A count that cannot be read comes back `None`
and the screen says nothing rather than claiming zero.

### COMMCALC-32.4 THE DATES PICK THEMSELVES

Owner, same day: *"should auaomatically pick teh dates from today and 3 days ahead as the payment
terms are 21 days from the date of invoice, the month and date shoudl not be entered manually"*.

`commcalc/date_window.py::ahead_window(today, days=3)` → today through today+3, four days inclusive,
basis `default_ahead`. It is the window home's own arithmetic, so "both ends inclusive" is still
stated once. The router's `_due_window(start, end, all_dates)` is the only place that decides:
an explicit window wins, `all_dates=True` means no window, otherwise the automatic one. The screen
prints the window it was actually given (`window` on the response) instead of implying it, and keeps
an **All dates** toggle — an automatic default that cannot be escaped is a different defect.

The 21 days themselves are NOT in code. They are `payable_source_map.net_terms_days`, declared per
carrier (§COMMCALC-26), and the harness's §D2 fails the build if a carrier's feed column name ever
appears in engine code (RULE TWO).

### COMMCALC-32.5 WHO OWES WHAT, ON THE SAME FOLD

Owner: *"filtered by market and store and who owes what for eveyr date mentioned on that list , to
make sure thee correct account is debited."* A date total cannot answer that — the money is paid per
store. So the per-store split rides **with** the date row (`by_store`, `stores`) rather than being a
second request that could be filtered differently and silently disagree; the date row expands into it.
The split keys on the canonical store identity (§64), not on a spelling, so two spellings of one store
are one line to debit. Money whose store did not resolve is reported as `unassigned_owed` and labelled
*"store not resolved — cannot be debited to an account"*; it is never folded into another store's
figure, because a wrong account debited is worse than an unattributed one.

### COMMCALC-32.6 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

`backend/harness_payables_device_rows.py` — **51 passed, 0 failed**. §A the one no-device predicate
(A9: an unnamed product with no declaration must NEVER read as no-device). §B the status vocabulary
(B4: an unknown status is payable). §C the automatic window. §D the RATCHET: `activation_type2` may
not appear in engine code (RULE TWO), no literal status string may survive in the engine,
`_due_window(start, end, all_dates)` must be the only window decision, the per-store split must stay
on the date fold, and unattributed money must stay named.

### COMMCALC-32.7 WHAT IS OWNER-GATED

- `database/migrations/1093_payable_device_class_field.sql` — additive, nullable
  (`device_class_field`, `no_device_tokens`), with COMMENTs and a `-- REVERT:` block. Applied with
  both left NULL, behaviour is exactly as before: the question is simply not asked.
- The one-Run config SQL: `net_terms_days = 21` and `device_class_field = 'activation_type2'` on the
  two Total rows, then one **Rebuild ledger** press. The rebuild is what re-statuses lines; applying
  the migration moves no money.
- **The clock start is still a question to the owner, and there are now TWO candidates.** 21 days
  runs from the invoice date. The ledger's own `invoice_date` is the ACTIVATION date
  (`raw_ma_commission.tx_date`) — measured here and confirmed independently by the rep-dashboard
  thread on 2026-10-26. `inventory_aging_device.received_date` is NULL on all 4,742 Luxelink rows
  (10,525 house-wide), so there is no stored receipt date; but the same row carries `days_in_stock`
  (the POS export's own "Age in Store") and `as_of_date`, so a receipt-anchored date IS derivable as
  `as_of_date − days_in_stock`. **Corrected 2026-10-26** — an earlier reading of this section said no
  per-device receipt date existed anywhere, which was wrong: the platform already derives one in
  three places (`commcalc/router.py::_derived_received`, `::_mi_ever_over_days`,
  `device_history.build_aging_inventory`, the last of which reads `days_in_stock` as-is and so ages a
  stale snapshot wrongly). Measured coverage against this ledger: **3,064 of 4,364 unsold IMEIs
  (70.2%)** have a derivable receipt date, 3,175 appear in the inventory feed at all, and only 388
  are on hand at the current snapshot — so a receipt-anchored window is buildable but leaves ~30% of
  devices with no clock start, which is a different answer from "fall back to activation". Nothing
  here is wired to either until the owner rules; whichever is chosen, it is read through the one home
  that thread is collapsing those three derivations into, never a fourth derivation.

### COMMCALC-32.8 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-29 (why a blank Owed must name its reason), §COMMCALC-26 (the
declared terms this reads), §COMMCALC-25 (the window and store filter on the same screen),
§COMMCALC-03.21 (the device-class vocabulary extended here). Same class: §66 (an absence read as
evidence), §19.18 (a mechanism written and its callers left unwired). Neighbours: §64 (the store
identity the per-store split keys on), §13e (store-spelling folding), §19.36 (the notice boundary the
excluded-count note crosses). Still open and NOT fixed here: **Weekly Owed to Distributor** reads
`commcalc.asset_ledger` and `billing_friday`, which are Boost-only, so it is blank for every Total
tenant — it must roll up each carrier's own declared cadence off the SAME daily owed home as
`/payables/owed-by-date`, not derive the money a second way.

## §COMMCALC-33. WHAT THE CARRIER ALREADY RECOVERED IS READ, AND A PLACEHOLDER IS NOT A MEASUREMENT (owner report 2026-10-26)

**What he said.** Against a banner reading *"2656 unsold devices must be paid OUT OF POCKET —
$544,447.78 … These are past their payment due date and still unsold, so the invoice is funded from
your own cash rather than from the sale"*:

> *"the payments for all phones automatically are done from commission and rebates received and auto
> adjusted"*

**He was right, and the netting was never missing.** It sits on the row the build already reads:
`commcalc.raw_ma_commission.rebate` is **negative on 3,442 of 4,495** Luxelink lines, totalling
**−$834,234.25** — the device cost deducted from his commission, line by line. Measured 2026-10-26
against the live ledger, on the very 2,656 devices the banner named:

| | devices | amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fully deducted already | 1,070 | $228,779.70 |
| partly deducted | 957 | owed $305,380.43 vs $277,294.00 deducted |
| no deduction found | 37 | $10,287.65 |

So roughly **$38,374** is genuinely unrecovered where the screen said **$544,447.78** — an
overstatement of about fourteen times, in the direction that tells an owner he is short half a
million dollars of cash. (The $28,086 shortfall inside the partly-deducted group compares two
sources — the ordering sheet's price against the statement's deduction — so part of it will be price
differences or a deduction landing on a later statement. That caveat is published with the figure
rather than filed off it.)

### COMMCALC-33.1 THE CLASS, and it is not "we forgot to read a column"

`payables/engine.py` held this, for every carrier whose recovery is matched by IMEI:

```python
elif rebate_source == "imei_match":
    mt = cfg.get("reimbursement_match_table")
    if mt:   # pending until a Total reimbursement report exists -> stays 0 when unset
        rebate_amount = 0.0
```

**A placeholder that returns a NUMBER is a claim.** `0.0` does not say "not wired yet"; it says
*nothing was recovered against this device*, and it said it in all 4,495 rows of the ledger. Every
reader downstream believed it: 1,400 lines went to `discrepancy` — the status whose own legend says
the dealer is still carrying the cost — and the out-of-pocket banner presented the gross as cash. The
honest value for an unwired source is **unknown**, and unknown must be labelled, never billed.

The single float could not hold the three states the question actually has, which is why the fix is a
type and not a line:

| state | what it means | what a surface may say |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **recovered** | measured, amount known | already settled by the carrier |
| **uncovered** | measured, recovery falls short | THIS is out of pocket |
| **unmeasured** | nothing wired, or the declared source could not be read | the figure is NOT NETTED — never "$0.00 recovered" |

### COMMCALC-33.2 DUPLICATE CHECK (the build gate) — what was REUSED, not rebuilt

| the question | who already answered it | what this change did |
| --- | --- | --- |
| is a basis evidence, or a last resort? | `commcalc/carrier_dollar_class.py::component_is_evidence` (§66) | **REUSED as doctrine** — `is_measured` is the same allowlist shape, so an unruled basis is not evidence |
| a declared source that cannot be READ | `payables/declared_source.py` (§COMMCALC-29) | **REUSED** — `source_unreadable` stays distinguishable from "nothing declared", which is that section's whole lesson |
| which ledger rows are payable at all | `payables/ledger_status.py` (§COMMCALC-32) | **REUSED** unchanged; a no-device line never reaches this arithmetic |
| the selling window and the out-of-pocket verdict | `commcalc/device_aging_policy.py` (§COMMCALC-26) | **REUSED** — the verdict is independent of the recovery and was not touched |
| the ePay and Boost/VIP recovery reads | `_epay_reimb_amount`, `_classify_rma` | **REUSED**, now folded through the same home so all three sources answer in one vocabulary |

Nothing new was created to answer a question already answered. What is new is the vocabulary for
*"do we know what was recovered?"*, which existed nowhere.

### COMMCALC-33.3 ONE FACT, ONE HOME, DEREFERENCED

`backend/app/modules/payables/recovered_amount.py` — PURE, standard library only.

- `MEASURED_BASES` + `is_measured(basis)` — the ALLOWLIST. **Fail-CLOSED**, deliberately the opposite
  of `ledger_status.is_payable`: there an unknown status must stay payable so money cannot vanish
  from a total; here an unknown basis must not count as proof, because a wrong "measured" **deletes a
  real liability**. The two live side by side and their defaults point opposite ways on purpose.
- `sign_of(cfg)` / `from_value` / `from_row` — **the sign is declared, never guessed.** On the MA
  statement a recovery is a deduction and arrives negative; on Boost/VIP and ePay a reimbursement
  arrives positive. `abs()` would turn a charge into a credit; `> 0` reads a deduction as nothing,
  which is exactly how $834,234.25 went unseen. So it is config
  (`payable_source_map.reimbursement_sign`), and an undeclared sign keeps the historic meaning
  rather than inventing one.
- `resolve(amount, basis)` — an absent amount forces the basis back to unmeasured, so no stale basis
  survives on a row behind it, and an amount cannot smuggle in a basis nobody ruled.
- `out_of_pocket(owed, recovered, basis)` / `split(rows)` — ONE convention for the arithmetic.
- `UNMEASURED_NOTE`, `RECOVERED_NOTE` — one wording, so "deducted from commission" and "not netted"
  read the same on every screen.

Callers wired in the same PR: `payables/engine.py` (all three recovery sources; writes
`rebate_basis`, and `rebate_amount` as **NULL** where nothing measured it) and
`payables/unsold_inventory.py::stamp_aging` (the exposure figure every surface headlines).

### COMMCALC-33.4 THE HALF I GOT WRONG FIRST, recorded because the next person will reach for it too

The first draft **dropped** unmeasured devices from the exposure total — "unknown is not a bill".
That is the same defect reversed: a second claim nobody measured. Worse, it was a cross-tenant
regression. The Boost/VIP aging rows carry **no recovery basis at all**, so they would all have read
as unmeasured and **Boost's real exposure would have gone to $0.00** — the identical shape to the
2026-10-23 defect in §COMMCALC-29, introduced by the fix for it.

Two existing proofs caught it (`harness_device_aging_policy.py` §E1/§E1b and
`harness_payables_declared_source.py` §C6, which compare the WHOLE summary dict precisely so that
unannounced drift fails the build). The corrected rule:

> **An unnetted liability is reported IN FULL and flagged. It is never silently settled, and never
> silently dropped.**

A second lesson from the same pass: `amount_incomplete` already meant "flagged devices with no
price". Overloading it with "not netted" quietly changed what every existing reader believed, so the
new doubt got its **own** flag, `amount_not_netted`. Two doubts, two booleans.

### COMMCALC-33.5 WHAT A SURFACE MAY NOW SAY

`stamp_aging` returns `recovered_amount`, `netted_devices`, `recovery_unmeasured`,
`recovery_unmeasured_amount`, `recovery_note`, `amount_not_netted`. `out_of_pocket_amount` is the
whole liability — the GAP where the recovery was measured, the GROSS where it was not — and
`recovery_unmeasured_amount` says how much of that figure has never been netted. A screen can
therefore state exactly what it knows instead of choosing a side.

`discrepancy` now requires a MEASUREMENT: sold, and something measured that no rebate came back. An
unchecked rebate is no longer an accusation.

### COMMCALC-33.6 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

`backend/harness_payables_recovered_amount.py` — **66 passed, 0 failed**, DB-free. §A the sign
convention (A8: no number at all is unmeasured, never a recovery of 0.00). §B the allowlist (B4 an
unruled basis is not measured; B8 unreadable stays distinguishable from absent). §C the arithmetic
(C3 the corrected unmeasured rule; C4 a MEASURED zero IS out of pocket in full — the distinction the
whole section exists for). §D the split. §E the live 2026-10-26 shapes. §F the RATCHET: **no
`rebate_amount = 0.0` may survive in the engine**, every source must fold through `resolve`, the
basis must be WRITTEN to the row, an unmeasured recovery must be stored NULL, `discrepancy` must
require `rebate_measured`, nothing may `abs()` a recovery value, and the recovery path may name no
carrier column.

### COMMCALC-33.7 WHAT IS OWNER-GATED, AND ONE DEFECT REPORTED NOT FIXED

- `database/migrations/1094_payable_recovery_sign_and_basis.sql` — additive, nullable
  (`payable_source_map.reimbursement_sign`, `device_payable_ledger.rebate_basis`), COMMENTs,
  `-- REVERT:` block, both grants restated. Applying it moves no money; the ledger re-statuses only
  on the owner's next **Rebuild ledger** press.
- The one-Run config SQL: `reimbursement_field = 'rebate'` and
  `reimbursement_sign = 'negative_is_recovery'` on the two Total / MA rows. Until it is run, the
  banner keeps its $544,447.78 — but now says that figure is **not netted**, which is the honest
  version of the same screen.
- **REPORTED, not repaired here (pre-existing RULE TWO violation).** `payables/engine.py` reads the
  table name `raw_ma_commission` **literally** in the store-account fallback (the mig-314 index
  path), which is a carrier feed name in code. It predates this change and sits in a different code
  path; widening a money fix to reach it is how a PR stops being reviewable. The new ratchet
  therefore binds the recovery path, and this line is named here so it is not lost.

### COMMCALC-33.8 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-32 (the no-device status, whose rows never reach this arithmetic),
§COMMCALC-29 (a declared source that cannot be read — the sibling whose vocabulary is reused),
§COMMCALC-26 (the declared window and cost source), §COMMCALC-25 (the filters on the same screen).
Same class: §66 (a last-resort placement read as evidence), §19.18 (a mechanism written and its

## §COMMCALC-34. A BILLING PERIOD IS DECLARED, AND THE MONEY IS READ ONCE (owner report 2026-10-26)

**What he said**, verbatim:

> *"Weekly Owed to Distributor does not show anything in luxelink"*

### COMMCALC-34.1 WHY IT WAS BLANK — two causes, and only one of them is code

Measured 2026-10-26 against production (read-only):

| cause | measurement | whose fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **the report reads one carrier's column** | `asset/router.get_owed_weekly` read `commcalc.asset_ledger` filtered on `billing_friday`, and nothing else. That is ONE carrier's weekly consignment rhythm, stamped by ONE carrier's portal sweep, on ONE carrier's table. The Total tenant has **0** `asset_ledger` rows, so every figure on the report was Σ over an empty set. | **this PR** |
| **no due dates exist to group** | `commcalc.device_payable_ledger` holds **4,495** rows for that tenant and **0 with a `due_date`** (`due_source` NULL on every one), because `commcalc.payable_source_map` has `net_terms_days` NULL **and** `due_date_field` NULL for its carrier. Nothing says when a device falls due. | **REPORTED, not coded around.** The owner's `net_terms_days = 21` config run (queued with mig 1093) is the missing declaration. Defaulting 21 days in code would be RULE TWO and would put a deadline on real money no feed states. |

The house org, by contrast, carries a due date on all **11,000** of its rows (`due_source = 'report'`).
So the structural fix below lands first and the figures arrive when the config run does — the report
says which, rather than printing $0.00 either way.

**THE CLASS, named rather than the instance.** Not *"Luxelink's weekly report is empty"* but: *"which
billing period does this dated money fall in" is a DECLARED cadence over the carrier's own payable
rows* — never one carrier's column on one carrier's table. This is §COMMCALC-26.1's class arriving on
a fifth surface, and §COMMCALC-33.8 named it as still open.

### COMMCALC-34.2 THE DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate — what was searched for, what was reused)

| searched | found | what was done |
| --- | --- | --- |
| is there a home for "what is owed, on which date"? | `payables/router.owed_by_date` held a ledger query AND a vendor-feed fallback, both private to it | **FACTORED OUT** into `payables/owed_read.py` and REUSED by both surfaces. Giving the weekly report its own read was the obvious repair and would have been two paths answering *"what do I owe"* — free to disagree the moment either learned something the other did not. The money is now read ONCE and grouped twice: by due date for the daily surface, by billing period for the weekly one. |
| is there a home for "when is this device due"? | §COMMCALC-26 (`net_terms_days` / `due_date_field` on `payable_source_map`) | **REUSED whole.** No due date is derived here; the cadence groups dates the build already stamped. |
| is there a home for "did this line buy a device"? | §COMMCALC-32 `ledger_status` | **REUSED** — `exclude_non_payable` gates the shared read, so a line that bought no device never reaches this arithmetic. |
| is there a home for "is this vendor line a debt"? | §COMMCALC-25 `vendor_invoice.is_debt_line`, whose own docstring says a change to it must reach both grains | **DEREFERENCED** — the read it absorbed carried an inline copy of the comparison, which is exactly the drift that docstring warned about. One test now, both grains. |
| is there a window home, a market home, a store-identity home? | §COMMCALC-24 `commcalc/date_window.py` (`apply_window`, so both ends stay inclusive the same way), RULE FIVE `core/scope.py::store_market_resolver`, §64 `account/store_identity.py` | **REUSED, injected by the caller.** The shared read holds no copy of any of them — the vendor fallback it absorbed carried its own `gte`/`lte` pair, which is how one screen ends up with two meanings of "inclusive". |
| a cadence column anywhere? | none | **CREATED** — mig 1095, on the config spine that already carries the selling window and the cost source. |

### COMMCALC-34.3 THE TWO ONE-HOMES

**`backend/app/modules/payables/billing_period.py`** — the ONE home for *"which billing period does
this dated money fall in, and what says so"*. Pure, stdlib only, no clock of its own.

Three ways a period can be known, kept apart and each NAMED in the answer's `basis`:

| basis | what said so |
| --- | --- |
| `period_field` | the feed already stamps the period on the row. **This WINS and is never recomputed** — a derived billing day that disagreed with the sweep's own would move a figure every other surface reconciles against, and the two would drift exactly as §19.18 describes. |
| `weekly_declared` | the carrier declares a weekly cadence and a weekday, so a due date rolls forward to the first such day **on or after** it. Not *after*: money due ON the billing day bills that day, and rolling it would postpone a real liability by seven days. |
| `due_date` / `house_default` | each invoice falls due on its own date; the period IS that date. **The house default asserts no rhythm**, which is byte-identical to today's behaviour. |
| `weekday_undeclared` | cadence `weekly` with no weekday declared. The money is still shown and still counted under its own due date, and the screen says the grouping is **not the carrier's own**. Dropping it would hide a real liability behind a missing config row (§COMMCALC-29); guessing Friday would be the same defect in a config column instead of in code (§COMMCALC-26.3). |
| `no_date` | no date was recorded. **NOT MEASURED** — reported beside the periods, never folded into one. |

`is_measured(basis)` is an ALLOWLIST (the §66 shape), so an unruled basis reads as NOT measured.
`week_window` returns the seven days **ENDING** on the billing day, as ISO strings, so a screen states
the range it rolled up instead of leaving a reader to guess whether the six days before it are in. It
takes **no weekday** — a span is seven days ending on its billing day whatever weekday that is, so the
parameter would have been a validity gate and nothing more, which is exactly what made the first draft
of the caller pass a literal `4`. A guessed Friday in a caller is the same defect as a guessed Friday
in the home, one import away.

**`backend/app/modules/payables/owed_read.py`** — the ONE read, `dated_owed`, returning
`{rows, source, grain, note, entities, truncated}`. Two sources, named per tenant:

- `device_ledger` — `commcalc.device_payable_ledger`, grain a **DEVICE**, gated by `ledger_status`.
- `vendor_feed` — the processor's own dated amounts, used only when the ledger produced **nothing**,
  which for a Total / MA tenant is not *"you owe nothing"* but *"no device carries an amount"*. Grain
  an **ORDER LINE** — there is no IMEI on this path at all, and the response says so rather than
  serving a drill-down that cannot exist.

Both empty is `source: None`, never a $0.00 total dressed as a measurement (§COMMCALC-29.1).

### COMMCALC-34.4 WHAT THE SURFACES NOW DO

- **`/payables/owed-by-date`** (daily) keeps its behaviour exactly and holds **no ledger query of its
  own**; the grouping by date is all that remains of it. Its private vendor fallback
  (`_owed_from_vendor_feed`, `_VENDOR_FEED_TABLE`) is **DELETED, not left beside the new one** — a
  dead second reader is a future divergence that compiles (§19.18).
- **`/asset/owed-weekly`** answers from the consignment column FIRST and unchanged, so a consignment
  tenant sees exactly the figures it saw before, with `period_source: "stored_column"`. Only where
  that found nothing does it resolve the declared cadence and roll the SHARED read up, reporting
  `period_source: "shared_owed_read"` and the basis that answered. The fallback is fail-soft and
  REPORTS (`declared_period.error`) rather than reading a failure as *"nothing is owed"*.
- **THE SCREEN SAYS IT.** A server that serves a figure to a screen that renders none has moved the
  blank report one layer down, not fixed it. `commcalc/asset/owed-weekly` gains an *Owed in this
  period* block: the total, the period count with the basis in WORDS, the money that could not be
  dated, the cadence sentence and the grain sentence (both from the server, one home each), and a
  table of the periods with the span each covers. A period the server did not measure prints **not
  measured**, never $0.00 — a measured zero is exactly what this report's whole defect looked like.
  The three consignment cards, *By Store*, *Upcoming Fridays* and the device table are suppressed
  **only** where the declared roll-up really answered, because three $0.00 cards and *"Nothing bills
  on this Friday"* printed under a real total would contradict the figure above them. The export
  carries the same figures, with the same words instead of a zero a spreadsheet would total.

### COMMCALC-34.5 LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

`backend/harness_billing_period.py` — **84 passed, 0 failed**, DB-free, stdlib only, with mutation
controls. §A the cadence
vocabulary and the fail-CLOSED allowlist, including a **config row handed straight in where a
resolved cadence was expected** (a config row is also a dict — the trap that raised `KeyError` while
this was built). §B the weekly roll forward and the on-the-day case. §C the stamped period wins. §D
the undeclared weekday is shown and counted. §E nothing is dated that carries no date, and the
unplaceable money is reported beside the periods. §F **ONE READ**, locked by AST: exactly one
definition of the shared read may exist in the whole triangle, the daily endpoint may hold no ledger
query, and the dead fallback must stay gone. §G the debt test is dereferenced. §H RULE TWO, scanned
over the **executable text only** — a carrier name that explains behaviour is not one that decides it,
so the owner's own report stays quoted in the prose while `if carrier == "…"` would still fail. §I the
consignment path is untouched. §J registration. §K the SCREEN — it reads the roll-up, prints the
span and the basis, shows an unmeasured period without a figure, suppresses the consignment sections
only where something really answered, and reports a failed roll-up in words.

### COMMCALC-34.6 WHAT IS OWNER-GATED

`database/migrations/1095_payable_billing_cadence.sql` — additive, idempotent, nullable:
`payable_source_map.billing_cadence` / `billing_weekday` / `billing_period_field`, two CHECK
constraints pinning the vocabulary the home rules on, a COMMENT on every column, a `-- REVERT:` block
and the grant restated. **Every column is NULL after it runs, which is byte-identical to today** — the
resolver's house default asserts no rhythm. The VALUES are a separate, approval-gated data step, and
the `net_terms_days = 21` run in §COMMCALC-34.1 is the one that makes the figures appear.

### COMMCALC-34.7 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-26 (the declared window, net terms and cost source — the config

## §COMMCALC-37. A REPORT IS ITS PAGE AND ITS FILTERS, AND AN UNFILTERED EXPORT IS REFUSED (owner ask 2026-10-27)

> **Numbered COMMCALC-37, not COMMCALC-35.** Two other threads merged into `main` while this was
> being built and took 35 and 36. `harness_index_section_register.py --next` reads the index in your
> WORKING TREE — it is not a reservation — so re-check right before pushing. The sixth and seventh
> time two threads have raced for one index number (§50 notes the first four, §CORE-17 the fifth).

Owner, verbatim: *"need the followig reports pulled … do each report by the day with all regular filters
we have been using and also the send options / item sales should be in detail and pulled for every
item"* — fourteen named reports on the back-office portal he had just signed into.

### COMMCALC-37.1 WHAT WAS WRONG — not a missing feature, a silent wrong answer

`portal_report_pull.pull_reports_on_page` (§COMMCALC-07) reached a report and pressed its export
control. It took `date_from`/`date_to` and used them **only to word the summary string**. Nothing set
a date on the page, nothing set a dropdown, nothing ticked a detail box, and nothing pressed the
report's Run control. So the file that landed was whatever that page happened to default to — often
the last run, often today, often a summary where detail was asked for.

**THE CLASS, stated once so nobody re-derives it.** *A report is not identified by its page. It is
identified by its page AND the parameters it was run with.* Exporting the page's default silently
answers a different question from the one asked, and the row that lands carries no sign of it — the
figures look ordinary, they are simply about a different day or a different grain. A reconciliation
built on top would inherit that and never see it. So the parameters are DECLARED per report, and a
report whose declared parameters could not all be set is **NOT EXPORTED**. Refusing is the honest
outcome; an unfiltered export is not.

### COMMCALC-37.2 ONE FACT, ONE HOME, DEREFERENCED

| fact | its one home | how callers get it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what must be set on this report before exporting | `portal_calibration[<report_key>]["params"]`, read by `prp.report_params` | the loop reads it once per report; nothing else parses that key |
| how a declared value becomes a form value | `prp.resolve_param_value` | the ONLY place a date token becomes text |
| which date tokens exist | `prp.DATE_TOKENS` | spelled once |
| which verbs a declaration may use | `prp.PARAM_KINDS` — a closed list | `apply_report_params` dispatches on it |
| does this report run once per day | `prp.is_per_day` — **DERIVED** from the declaration (`{date}` appears in a value) | never a second switch beside the declaration that could disagree with it |
| which days one per-day report covers | `prp.pull_days` — inclusive, oldest first, bounded by `MAX_WINDOW_DAYS` | the loop; a backwards or unreadable range is no days, never a crash |
| one report over its days | `prp.pull_one_report` | returns ONE result dict whatever the number of days, so a per-day report and a window report read identically to every surface |

RULE TWO holds throughout: no report name, menu word, selector or filter value appears in this
repository. The fourteen reports, their navigation, their filters and their Run control are rows on
the tenant's `data_source` (`portal_reports`, `portal_calibration`). Adding the fifteenth report — or
onboarding a second tenant of the same kind — is a config row, never a code change.

### COMMCALC-37.3 THE ORDER, AND WHY IT IS THAT ORDER

Per report, per day: **reach the page → set every declared parameter → press Run → export → ingest**.
Run sits between the parameters and the export deliberately: a portal that renders its grid on Run
exports the *previous* run's grid otherwise, which is the stalest possible way to be wrong and the
hardest to notice. A report that declares no Run control simply has none pressed, and a report that
declares no parameters behaves byte-identically to before this section.

### COMMCALC-37.4 THE REFUSAL, AND WHAT IT SAYS

`apply_report_params` returns the LABELS it could not set — the operator's own words for the filter,
not a selector — and the loop skips that day's export and names them. A day covered is counted
(`days_run`), so a report that managed nine of ten days reports the gap as a gap rather than as a
smaller number. A Run that does not respond is its own message, because it is a different fix from a
filter whose box has moved.

### COMMCALC-37.5 DUPLICATE CHECK (the build gate — what was searched for, what was reused)

| the thing that might already exist | what the index says | what was done |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a pull loop that reaches a report and exports it | §COMMCALC-07, `portal_report_pull` | EXTENDED in place — no sibling loop |
| a per-report selector store | `portal_calibration` + `prp.calibrated` (§COMMCALC-07) | reused; `params` and `run_selector` are keys in it, not a new column or table |
| a day window | `prp.date_range` / `window_days` / `MAX_WINDOW_DAYS` | reused; `pull_days` walks the SAME window and is bounded by the SAME ceiling |
| an operator's Cancel | `should_stop` (§COMMCALC-07) | reused — honoured per day, so a long per-day pull stops on the day, not at the end |
| a line → declared-category map | `pos_report_feed` (§COMMCALC-07) | untouched; this section changes only WHICH file reaches it |

Nothing new was created, so nothing new needed registering beyond this section and the
`portal_report_pull` module-graph fact's second axis.

### COMMCALC-37.6 LOCKED

`harness_portal_report_pull.py` §J — 147 checks in the file now, DB-free and browser-free, driven
against a fake page that records every `fill` / `select_option` / `check` / `click`. It fails the
build if the parameters stop being applied before the export, if Run stops sitting between them, if a
day is exported when a declared filter could not be set (the check counts the EXPORTS, not the error
string — an armed negative control proves why), if `is_per_day` becomes a second switch instead of a
derivation, if `pull_days` loses its ceiling or its ordering, if a malformed declaration is guessed at
rather than dropped, or if a date token with nothing to put in it is quietly resolved to something
plausible.

### COMMCALC-37.7 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-07 (the one pull loop and the adapter contract). Neighbours:
§CORE-03 (the stored portal credential this login rides), §COMMCALC-24 (which process may answer),
§COMMCALC-31 (the live login that captures a calibration), §CORE-17 (the drill-down every landed
figure owes).

## §COMMCALC-38. WHAT A SUPPLIER BILLED US HAS A SUPPLIER-NEUTRAL HOME, AND THE INVOICE FEED SHIPS WITH ITS DOOR (owner ask 2026-10-27)

> **Numbered COMMCALC-38.** Three other threads merged into `main` while this and its sibling
> §COMMCALC-37 were being built, taking 35, 36 and 37's neighbours in turn.
> `harness_index_section_register.py --next` reads the index in your WORKING TREE and is not a
> reservation — re-check right before pushing. Likewise the migration numbers: this change was built
> as 1096/1097 and shipped as **1098/1099** because both were claimed mid-flight.

Owner, verbatim: *"i want to pull in invoices from ups and then compare to the sales reports to make
sure every single shipment is being paid for and cash collected by the sales reps, the time should be
recorded so incase the payment is not taken then it shoudl be addressed with the employees … make it
as a recon under supplier / distribuot , also all these we are doing for ups should be stored in index
so when a ups store signs up it can use all of these as a dfault option"*.

This section is the PULL and the HOME. The reconciliation it exists to feed, and the signup preset,
are their own sections and are named in §COMMCALC-38.8 as NOT BUILT YET — stated, so nobody reads
this as the whole ask delivered.

### COMMCALC-38.1 WHY RUN NOW SAID NOTHING USEFUL

He had already created the login row. It carried `processor = 'other'`, and `router._SOURCE_SCRAPERS`
has no handler for `other`, so `run_data_source` stamped *"scraper for 'other' not wired yet — reports
ingest via the email sweep or the Data Imports upload"* and stopped. That message is honest and it was
useless to him: nothing on the screen offered a processor that would have worked, because none existed.

### COMMCALC-38.2 THE CLASS — three facts that had been one

| the question | where it lives now |
| --- | --- |
| which column of an exported report is which fact | `commcalc/report_columns.py` — the MECHANISM (`norm`, longest-synonym-first `map_headers`, `header_score`, `cell`, `money_or_none`) |
| what does THIS feed call those facts | each feed's own `COLUMN_SYNONYMS`, overlaid by the tenant's `portal_calibration.column_synonyms` |
| what does one supplier-invoice line say | `commcalc/supplier_invoice_feed.py` — PURE |

`pos_report_feed` carried the mechanism and the vocabulary welded together. A second feed needed the
mechanism against its own vocabulary, and the only thing standing between this repository and a copied
normalizer was that nobody had looked. That copy would have failed in a specific, expensive way:
`norm` is what makes `'B-1115'` and `'b 1115'` one store key, and this platform has already lost a
phantom store holding $289 to a store code compared under one rule here and another rule there. So the
mechanism moved to one home, `pos_report_feed.norm` / `map_headers` / `header_score` / `_cell` became
DEREFERENCES at their old spellings and signatures (every existing caller reads the same code it
always did, and its 111 checks are unchanged), and the new feed reads the same home.

One money parser, too. `merchant_portals.money` parses a portal money cell and remains the only one;
`report_columns.money_or_none` dereferences it and adds exactly one rule — **a blank cell is None, not
0.0**. A supplier invoice needs that distinction and a recon needs it more: 0.0 asserts the supplier
billed nothing for this shipment, a blank asserts nothing at all, and a recon handed a zero would
close the line as *collected in full*. Same lesson as §COMMCALC-33, in the place it would have cost
the most. A line whose charge cannot be read is SKIPPED with its reason and reported, never coerced.

### COMMCALC-38.3 SUPPLIER-NEUTRAL, AND THE SIBLING IS NAMED

`commcalc.vip_invoices` / `vip_invoice_lines` (mig 008) already hold DISTRIBUTOR invoices. They are
not reused, and the reason is written into mig 1098's header rather than left for a reader to notice:

- they are keyed on one portal's internal invoice id (`vip_id bigint`) and carry **no supplier and no
  `source_id` column**, so a second supplier's invoices landed in them would be indistinguishable from
  the first's;
- they are read by the P&L (`coa.build_inputs` → `vip_fees` / `vip_ap`), the balance sheet, device
  COGS and the Distributor Invoices report (§15v), so widening them is a money change on paths another
  piece of work owns.

So "a supplier invoice" gets `commcalc.supplier_invoice_line` (mig **1098**, SURFACED not applied),
which names no supplier. **`vip_invoices` is the EXCUSED SIBLING** that should fold into it later, with
that reason recorded. Two homes for one question is a defect; an unstated one is a worse defect.

### COMMCALC-38.4 THE GRAIN, AND THE TWO RECON KEYS

One row per invoice LINE, upserted on `(org_id, source_id, invoice_number, shipment_key, service_key,
charge_date)` — `supplier_invoice_sweep.ON_CONFLICT`, read from both files by the harness so it cannot
drift from the migration's unique index. An invoice's own line numbering is not in every export, so
the key is what identifies the CHARGE.

- **`charge_date` is the day the charge happened** (shipped / pickup / service date), falling back to
  the invoice date only when the export carries no charge date. A recon keyed on the invoice date would
  look for the sale in the wrong week.
- **`shipment_key` / `counter_key`** are the two references a recon may match on — `MATCH_KEYS`, an
  ALLOWLIST, so a reference kind added later reads as NOT matchable until somebody rules on it rather
  than silently becoming a join key (the §66 shape). Both are kept verbatim AND normalized by
  `match_key`, which is `report_columns.norm` and only that: the supplier prints
  `1Z 999 AA1 01 2345 6784` and the POS prints `1Z999AA1012345 6784`, and two normalizers would make
  one shipment read as unbilled on one side and uncollected on the other.
- An export carrying **no** shipment reference on any line says so once, in its warnings, naming the
  column to declare — because it decides how the recon can match at all, and a recon that fell back to
  day-and-amount without saying so would read as exact when it is not.

### COMMCALC-38.5 THE FEED SHIPPED WITH ITS DOOR, AND THAT IS THE RATCHET WORKING

Mig 1084 (§12a.2a) fixed the class that "the platform can dispatch this feed" and "a tenant can find
this feed" were unrelated facts, and armed `harness_connector_scope_lock.py` §I to fail the build on a
dispatchable key with no `connector_registry` row. **This is the first feed to ship after that ratchet,
and the lock fired on the first run** — naming `supplier_invoice` as added and doorless. The registry
row (mig **1099**) and `router._SOURCE_SCRAPERS[supplier_invoice]` are therefore one change, not two,
and `DISPATCHED_KEYS` names the new key by hand so a feed that later LEAVES still announces itself.
No host and ANY scope on the row, deliberately: a connector KIND, not a supplier, and any tenant may be
invoiced by one.

## §COMMCALC-39. A DECLARATION IS READ OFF THE PAGE, AND A DECLARED REPORT RESOLVES TO ITSELF (owner ask 2026-10-27)

Owner, verbatim: *"do each report by the day with all regular filters we have been using and also the
send options / item sales should be in detail and pulled for every item"* — fourteen named reports.

### COMMCALC-39.1 THE DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY — every declared report filtered itself out

`pull_reports_on_page` resolves a source's reports with
`mod.report_specs(proc, src_row["portal_reports"], src_row=src_row)`. For the CARD feed that second
argument is genuinely an enabled list and its keys are already canonical. For a DECLARATION-driven
feed the declaration and the "enabled list" are the SAME list, and the adapter built its filter from
it under a different rule from the one it keyed the specs by:

| declared as | the spec's key | the filter the old rule built | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `["Item Sales"]` | `item_sales` | `{"item sales"}` | dropped |
| `[{"key": "item_sales"}]` | `item_sales` | `set()` — a dict is not a `str` | dropped |

So a source that declared fourteen reports resolved to **none**, and said *"No reports are enabled for
this portal source"* — the same sentence an unconfigured source gets, which is exactly what would
have made it look like a setup mistake rather than a defect. It was latent only because no tenant had
declared a report yet.

**THE CLASS:** *one argument meaning two different things to two callers.* `enabled_keys` meant "the
filter" to the adapter and "the declaration" to the loop, and nothing made them agree. The fix is a
single `spec_key(item)` — the one rule for "which report is this" — dereferenced by BOTH the
construction and the filter, so the two cannot be derived differently again. A genuinely narrower
enabled list still narrows; that was never the problem.

`specs_for(src_row, proc)` and `setup_hint_for(src_row, proc)` are the one home for resolving a
source's reports, because the capture below must read exactly the set the pull will run — a capture
reading a different set would calibrate a report nobody pulls and miss one somebody does.

### COMMCALC-39.2 WHERE A DECLARATION COMES FROM — the page, not a guess

§COMMCALC-37 made a report's filters DECLARED and refuses to export a report whose declared filters
could not be set. That is right, and it makes the declaration load-bearing: a wrong selector is now a
report that never exports. A portal can carry ids its own framework generated (`ctl00_…_txtFromDate`
rather than `#DateFrom`), so a guessed selector produces exactly that failure with no way to tell
which guess was wrong.

So the declaration is READ from the page, through the session that is already signed in:

| fact | its one home |
| --- | --- |
| what controls does this page offer | `prp.read_page_controls` — one page evaluation, returning plain dicts so the suggester needs no browser |
| which selector should a declaration use | `prp.control_selector` — `#id` escaped for CSS, else `[name="…"]` |
| what is this control FOR | `prp.control_purpose` — the page's own words, longest phrase first, tenant words declared in `portal_calibration.control_words` (RULE TWO) |
| what declaration do those controls imply | `prp.suggest_params` — PURE |
| reach a report and suggest its declaration | `prp.capture_report_calibration` — navigates by the SAME ladder the pull uses |

`POST /commcalc/data-sources/{sid}/live-login/calibrate` runs it on the live authenticated page, as
the sibling of `PULL` on the same single-threaded loop (`LiveLoginSession.calibrate` /
`can_calibrate` / `run_calibrate_blocking` / `_handle_calibrate`, with `calibrate_fn` built by
`router._live_calibrate`). It is never called by the auto-pull: a session that signed in to fetch
reports must not start reading pages nobody asked about.

**IT WRITES NOTHING.** Not to the portal, not to `portal_calibration`. A capture is evidence about a
page, not a decision about a tenant's config, and a capture that silently rewrote a working
declaration would be the worst kind of helpful. Three suggestion rules, each because its opposite is
worse:

- the date boxes are declared with the **tokens**, never with the day the capture happened to run — a
  captured literal date would pull one day forever and look like it was working;
- a detail / itemized tick box is declared **ticked**, because the owner asked for every item and an
  untouched box is the page default §COMMCALC-37 exists to stop trusting;
- **Run and Export come back under their own keys**, not as params, because the loop presses them at a
  fixed point in its order and a param pressing Run early would export the previous run's grid.

Anything whose purpose the page's own words do not state is returned in `unrecognised` — named for a
human, with its own dropdown options so the value can be declared without opening the portal — and
never guessed into a param.

### COMMCALC-39.3 DUPLICATE CHECK (the build gate — what was searched for, what was reused)

| the thing that might already exist | what the index says | what was done |
| --- | --- | --- |
| per-report selectors and filters | `portal_calibration` + §COMMCALC-37 | REUSED — this writes the same shape it reads, and nothing new is stored |
| reaching one report | `prp.navigate_to_report` | REUSED whole: a capture that reaches a page proves the pull will reach it, and one that cannot says which report needs its navigation declared first |
| a live authenticated browser, and work queued onto it | `LiveLoginSession` + the `PULL` command (§COMMCALC-24) | EXTENDED with a sibling command — no second session, no second worker, no second loop |
| what the last pull saw | `GET /data-sources/{sid}/pull-diagnostic` | different question (what the pull DID), untouched; this answers what the page OFFERS before a pull is run |
| the normalizer that compares words | `report_columns.norm` (§COMMCALC-38) | DEREFERENCED, so a label compared here and a header compared there cannot drift |
| resolving a source's declared reports | was inline in the pull loop | EXTRACTED to `specs_for` and fixed (§COMMCALC-39.1) — one resolver, two callers |

### COMMCALC-39.4 LOCKED

`harness_portal_report_pull.py` §K — 183 checks in the file now, DB-free and browser-free. It
reproduces the defect in both declared shapes and keeps the shipped rule as an **armed negative
control**, so restoring it fails the build. It also fails the build if a date box is suggested with a
literal date instead of a token, if Run or Export becomes a param, if a detail box stops being
declared ticked, if an unrecognised control is guessed into a param rather than named, if a
framework-separated id stops being escaped, if the suggester learns to write `portal_calibration`, or
if a portal is named in the capture's executable text.

### COMMCALC-39.5 NOT BUILT YET, SAID PLAINLY

A screen for the capture. Today it is an endpoint and its answer is JSON: an operator (or whoever is
driving the live login) runs it and confirms the declaration onto the source row. The owner's
*"when a ups store signs up it can use all of these as a default option"* — the signup preset that
would make a confirmed declaration the house default for the next tenant of this kind — is still
unbuilt, and §COMMCALC-38.8 carries that same note.

### COMMCALC-39.6 Cross-references

Same home, other axes: §COMMCALC-07 (the one pull loop), §COMMCALC-37 (the declared filters this
capture writes for), §COMMCALC-38 (the one normalizer and the invoice feed). Neighbours:
§COMMCALC-24 (which process may answer), §COMMCALC-27 / §COMMCALC-31 (the operator's input leads the
tick, which is why a capture is a queued command and not a second thread), §COMMCALC-13 (what a

## §CORE-17. A REPORTED FIGURE NAMES THE ROWS BEHIND IT — the one drill-down (owner ask 2026-10-24)

> **Numbered CORE-17, not CORE-16.** The allocator handed out `CORE-16` while this was being
> built, and PR #532 (*a self-call carries the tenant it is acting as*) merged it first, so
> this section moved — the fifth time two threads have raced for one index number (§50 notes
> the first four). `harness_index_section_register.py --next` reads the index in your WORKING
> TREE, which is what had merged when you branched; it is not a reservation. Re-check right
> before pushing: `git fetch origin main && git show origin/main:docs/SYSTEM_DATA_FLOW_INDEX.md
> | grep -c "<NUMBER>"`.

Owner, verbatim: *"cash variance at employee should have the drill down from wheter the data is cming
from , update in index thta drilldown is needed for every report geenerated from any data which
comming from within the platforma as a defalut , assign an agent o check all reports to check where
the drill donw ins not there and sytart building it"*.

### §CORE-17.1 THE HOUSE RULE (owner directive 2026-10-24)

**EVERY REPORT BUILT FROM DATA THE PLATFORM HOLDS HAS A DRILL-DOWN, BY DEFAULT.** A report that
summarises — a tile, a rollup row, a per-person, per-store, per-month or per-line total — opens that
figure to the ROWS IT WAS BUILT FROM, and every row NAMES WHERE IT CAME FROM: the report, feed or
upload, and the keys that address the row inside it.

Three things follow, and they are build gates, not advice:

1. **The drill-down is the shared one** — `core/report_drilldown.py` on the server,
   `components/DrillDownPanel.tsx` on the screen. A report does not invent a shape.
2. **A source is named through `sourceLabel()`**, never printed as a table. The operator reads
   *"management envelope count"*; `envelope_count` never reaches a screen (§19.38).
3. **A report with no drill-down is WRITTEN DOWN as owing one** —
   `backend/harness_drilldown_pending.txt`, gated by `harness_drilldown_coverage.py`. A new report
   route is **un-mergeable** until its author declares which it is: `shared`, `own`, `flat`,
   `not_report`, or `owes`. "By default" is enforced, not remembered.

A report that genuinely has nothing to drill to (it already shows the source rows) declares `flat`
and says so. A config screen, wizard or work queue declares `not_report`. Both carry a written
reason — an excuse nobody wrote down is indistinguishable from an oversight.

### §CORE-17.2 DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate)

Searched: §4e (the P&L drill-down — `account/coa.py` `accrue_detail`/`add`, `scopeFinancials.ts`
`drillFilter`/`nextRung`/`lineTieOut`, `plStatement.plQuery`, PR #408), §6i/§6j
(`commcalc/commission_drilldown.py` `explain_rep` / `attach_line_identity`,
`GET /commission-explain` / `/commission-drill`), §19.38 (`frontend/src/lib/sourceLabels.ts` — a
feed's plain name), §66 (`carrier_dollar_class.component_is_evidence`), §COMMCALC-09
(`payout_slice_evidence` — is a stored value evidence at all), §2 / `data_lineage_registry.py` (which
table is which feed), `closing/metric_catalog.figure_unit`, and `GET /ma-overview-recon/drill`.

REUSED, NOT REBUILT:

- **the feed's plain name** — `sourceLabel()` is the ONE home and the panel dereferences it. No
  second vocabulary; `harness_report_drilldown.py` §F2 fails the build if a table a drill can name
  has no entry there.
- **"we could not measure this"** — `UNMEASURED_REASONS` is `closing/cash_variance`'s own wording,
  asserted identical by §G5. A fourth spelling of the same sentence is the divergence.
- **the unit vocabulary** — `money` / `count` / `hours`, the words
  `closing/metric_catalog.figure_unit` already uses.
- **the cash legs** — the cash-variance drill re-reads nothing and re-derives nothing: the rows are
  `day_row`'s own output, the verdicts the ones already on them, the figure the group's own
  `net_variance` off `totals()`. A drill-down that recomputed its evidence could disagree with the
  table above it, which is the §COMMCALC-09 defect in presentation form.

NAMED SIBLINGS, EXCUSED HERE, TO CONVERGE (not silently left):

- **`GET /ma-overview-recon/drill`** is already a generic "rows behind a tile, with its
  `source_table` named" endpoint over twelve tables. It is the closest existing mechanism and it is
  **not** extended here, because it is bound to `ma_overview.SOURCES` / `match_all` / the tile
  registry — one scannable table per tile with a row predicate — and cannot express a figure derived
  by comparing five tables (which is what cash variance is). It should adopt this panel's RESPONSE
  SHAPE so there is one shape and one renderer; that is MA-commission territory and routes to the
  commission agent. Ledger state: `own`.
- **the P&L drill (§4e)** computes its tie-out in TypeScript (`lineTieOut`) over a payload shape that
  predates this. Converging it would re-open PR #408's 56+58-check proof and is a PR of its own.
  Ledger state: `own`, with the note that its drill rows still name no source feed.

### §CORE-17.3 THE MECHANISM

| What | Where | Says |
|---|---|---|
| **ONE source row reference** | `core/report_drilldown.origin(table, schema, keys, column, note)` | which table, which schema, the keys that ADDRESS the row, the column the figure was read out of. A blank key is dropped, so a key that is present means something. A table nobody named is `traceable: False` — never guessed |
| **ONE row behind a figure** | `report_drilldown.drill_row(label, origins, amount, in_figure, measured, reason, fields)` | `amount=None` ⇒ `present: False` / `measured: False` with a reason sentence — **absence is never zero**. `in_figure=False` keeps a row the figure deliberately excludes IN the drill-down, flagged, because those rows are the context that makes the figure readable |
| **The report against its own evidence** | `report_drilldown.tie_out(amount, rows)` | Σ(counted rows) vs the figure. `ties: True` only when every counted row is measured AND the total matches to the cent; **`None`** — never False — when a counted row has no number, because a sum missing a row was never a comparison; `False`, in words, when the rows are all measured and total something else: *"the report and its own evidence disagree"* |
| **The panel a screen renders** | `report_drilldown.panel(...)` → `{schema, figure, subject, rows, rows_total_count, capped, tie_out, sources, untraceable_origins, note}` | **`sources` is the owner's question answered in one read**: the distinct tables the rows came out of, each with how many rows touched it. The tie-out is over ALL the rows, BEFORE the `ROW_CAP` of 400, and `rows_total_count` always states the true count, so a capped panel cannot present a shorter month as the whole of one. An origin naming no table is REPORTED under `untraceable_origins` |
| **The one renderer** | `frontend/src/components/DrillDownPanel.tsx` (+ `DrillToggle`, `useDrillOpen`, `DrillSources`, `DrillTieOut`) | prints every source through `sourceLabel()`; shows the tie-out sentence AS SERVED including when it fails; a row with no figure reads *"not measured"*, never $0.00; `extraColumns` lets a report add its own columns off each row's `fields` without forking the component |
| **The cash-variance producer** | `closing/cash_variance.py` — `LEG_ROW_KEYS`, `LEG_SOURCE_COLUMN`, `LEG_EXTRA_TABLES`, `PAIR_LEGS`, `day_drill_row`, `group_drilldown`, `drilldowns` | which keys address each leg's row and which column held it, named ONCE so the screen, an export and a support query reach for the SAME row. The received leg built from BOTH counted envelopes names both tables, or it would credit the whole drawer to one envelope |
