| **The endpoint** | `GET /closing/cash-variance` → `drilldown: {employee_name: {<name>: panel}, store_code: {<code>: panel}}` + `drilldown_pair` | one panel per rollup row, keyed on the subject the rollup is keyed on, re-bucketed with the SAME key functions `by_employee` / `by_store` used — so a panel can never hold a different set of days than the row it opened from (the §4e grain defect) |
| **The screen** | `/closing/cash-variance` — the Employee and Store views, each row a `DrillToggle` | the figure is the group's `net_variance` and its LABEL says *"net of short and over"*, because $0.00 here means *they cancelled out*, never *clean*; the note carries the two gross counts beside it |

**THE FIGURE TIES BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT IS A REAL CHECK, NOT A TAUTOLOGY.** `net_variance` is
`over_total − short_total`, summed over exactly the out-of-band days the panel marks `in_figure`. The
harness plants a dropped day and a mis-scored day and **both break the tie-out**. In-band days and
unmeasurable days are shown and not counted, and the panel says in words how many.

### §CORE-17.3a THE TILE SHAPE — Σ(one field) over the report's own rows (added 2026-10-24, batch 1)

Most of the 93 owe the SAME drill-down: a tile shows a total, the report already holds the per-row
figures it was folded from, and there is no way from one to the other. Ninety-two per-report folds
would be ninety-two answers to "which rows is this?" — the sibling defect, arriving one report at a
time. So the fold is in the one home and a report declares only what is particular to it.

| What | Where | Says |
|---|---|---|
| **The shared fold** | `core/report_drilldown.tile_panel(figure_label, amount, rows, value, tables, row_label, keys, in_figure, …)` | `value` reads a row's contribution (**None ⇒ the row has no number**, shown with its reason, never counted as nothing); `tables` names where it was read from, as a tuple or a per-row callable; `in_figure` is the predicate for WHICH ROWS THE TILE COUNTS, defaulting to "the row has a number", so a short/over tile counts its own subset and keeps the rest as context |
| **Every tile from one declaration** | `report_drilldown.tiles(catalogue, rows, totals)` | a tile is added by adding a ROW to the catalogue, never by writing another fold. A tile whose `total` key the report did not produce is **ABSENT** rather than a panel asserting a figure behind nothing — so a feed that never resolved for the range offers no link instead of an empty panel that reads like a bug |
| **`figure_label` vs `row_label`** | both, deliberately two words | they were one word (`label`) for an afternoon, and in a catalogue dict one silently ate the other: **every tile on the first report served the row accessor as its own title**. `harness_cash_recon_drilldown.py` §C11 caught it before it shipped. The two names are what stop it recurring |
| **The first report on it** | `closing/cash_recon_drilldown.py` — `catalogue(tolerance, processor_table, sales_table)`, `drilldowns(rows, totals, …)` | the §CORE-17 audit's **#1** of the 93: eleven cash tiles, sixteen figures, the most disputable money on the platform and no way to the store-day that produced it. The declaration computes NOTHING — per tile it names the `totals` key, the row field, the tables and the predicate |
| **The endpoint** | `GET /closing/cash-recon-management` → `drilldown: {<tile key>: panel}` | folded from the SAME `out` and `_totals` the response serves, so a tile and its drill-down cannot disagree — and if the declaration is wrong the tie-out says so on the manager's screen rather than silently |
| **The screen** | `/closing/cash-recon-management` — a link per figure on each tile, ONE panel open at a time below the strip | `DrillTileLinks` + `useDrillTile` (shared, in `DrillDownPanel.tsx`, so the remaining reports inherit the shape). A tile offers a figure's link only when the server actually sent that panel |
| **Which table a processor feed lands in** | `commcalc/data_lineage_registry.BILLPAY_PROCESSOR_FEEDS` + `billpay_processor_feed(source_label)` | the processor leg's provenance depends on which processor `metric_source_of_truth` resolved. Keyed by that stored value, so a new processor is a ROW plus its ingest edge, never a branch in a report. An unknown processor returns **None** and the drill reports an untraceable origin — a wrong provenance claim is worse than an admitted gap |

**WHY THE TIE-OUT EARNS ITS KEEP HERE.** A tile drill-down is the claim *these are the rows that
figure was summed from*, and the wrong field or the wrong predicate makes a drill-down that LOOKS
like proof. `harness_cash_recon_drilldown.py` (52 checks) plants a one-cent total, a dropped
store-day, a blanked row, a wrong bucket total and a flipped variance sign — **each one breaks a
tie-out**. It also fails the build when a MONEY total the endpoint serves has no declaration, which
is how the screen reached eleven undrillable tiles.

### §CORE-17.3b A TILE RECOMPUTED ON SCREEN HAS NO SERVER-FOLDED EVIDENCE — reported, not papered over (2026-10-24, batch 2)

**THE FINDING, from `/closing/tender-recon` (the audit's #2).** Some report pages recompute their own
tiles in TypeScript over the rows left after the client-side standard filters, so that the tile, the
table and the export can never disagree (RULE FIVE). The drill-down panels, though, are folded
server-side over the whole range. Under a store or market filter the two therefore describe
**different populations**, and a panel explaining a figure the screen is not showing would look like
proof of the wrong number — which is worse than no drill at all.

**WHAT SHIPPED, AND WHAT DID NOT.** `commcalc/tender_recon_drilldown.py` declares all seven figures
and they tie exactly on the unfiltered range, which is the default view. The page offers a figure's
drill **only while the tile and the panel agree to the cent** and states the reason on screen when
they do not. That is a **reported gap, not a fix**: `/closing/tender-recon` therefore **deliberately
still reads `owes`** in `harness_drilldown_pending.txt` and the owed count did **not** move for it.
`harness_tender_recon_drilldown.py` §G asserts all three, so the partial cannot be mistaken for the
finished thing — and the count cannot be quietly lowered while it stands.

**THE REAL REMEDY, stated once so nobody re-derives it: one fold serving both sides.** The
client-side total recompute is itself a second implementation of the endpoint's own fold — the
duplicate the index rules forbid, in TypeScript. Closing it properly means this report's standard
filters moving SERVER-SIDE (the posture `harness_closing_filter_contract.py` already enforces across
the closing module), after which the tile and the panel are the same fold over the same rows and the
agreement guard becomes dead code to delete. It is not done here because the store key on this recon
is a matched address string and the market is joined from the roster on the client, so moving the
filters is a change to the endpoint's identity handling rather than a line in a drill-down PR.

> **SUPERSEDED 2026-10-24 by §CORE-17.3d.** The partial below was reported twice and then found a
> third time, so the cause was fixed rather than restated: a tile now reads its number off its own
> narrowed panel, and the remedy proposed here (moving this report's filters server-side) was NOT the
> one taken — see §CORE-17.3d for why. `/closing/tender-recon` reads `shared` now. Kept because the
> reasoning for refusing a dishonest drill still stands, and because it is the record of a gap being
> reported rather than papered over.

**THE SIBLING TO CHECK WHEN IT IS DONE:** `/closing/pickup` computes its four cash footers over "the
envelopes CURRENTLY ON SCREEN" — the same class, and the same remedy. `/closing/tender-recon-3way`
already drills the same question through `/closing/tender-drilldown`, which is why this report ranked
#2: one question, two paths, only one carrying evidence.

### §CORE-17.3c A FIGURE'S FEED IS A FACT THE READ KNOWS — one home, dereferenced (2026-10-24, batch 3)

**Built:** `/closing/epay-recon`, `/closing/accessory-recon`, `/closing/external-credit-recon`
(PR batch 3). Declarations: `backend/app/modules/closing/day_recon_drilldown.py` (the two day recons
— same grain, one row label, one set of row fields, two catalogues) and
`backend/app/modules/closing/external_credit_drilldown.py` (the card-settlement tally).
Proof: `backend/harness_day_recon_drilldown.py` (67 checks, incl. §Z negative controls).
Owed count **92 → 89**.

**THE PROBLEM THIS BATCH NAMED.** Both day recons read their "actual" leg from the SALES PAIR, and
`closing/router._b2b_sales_rows` picks between the live daily feed and the monthly archive, falls back
to the other, and unions per store. Which side answered is a fact that read knew and **every caller
threw away** — leaving a drill-down three bad options: name both tables (a provenance claim nothing
checked), name a constant (wrong half the year), or name nothing (a silent blank).

**THE FIX IS AT THE SELECTION, not in the declarations.** `_b2b_sales_rows_sourced(client, org_id,
date, cols) -> (rows, tables)` is now the real read and `_b2b_sales_rows` a thin rows-only wrapper
over it. `_epay_sales_by_store` and `_b2b_money_by_store` return `(aggregate, tables)` and the
endpoints hand those tables to the catalogue. The primary/fallback/union logic exists **once**
(locked: §E5/E6 pin `open_month = str(date)[:7]` and `primary, other = (` to exactly one occurrence
each). A declaration that re-derived the pick would be the second copy the house rules forbid.

**AN UNRESOLVED TABLE NOW READS AS UNTRACEABLE, NOT AS NOTHING — fixed in the SHARED fold.** The
declaration shape for a config-resolved feed is `tuple(t for t in (x,) if t)`, so an unregistered
processor or an empty sales read collapses to `()`. `tile_panel` was then building an EMPTY origin
list, which reported **zero** untraceable origins: a provenance gap wearing the clothes of a clean
answer. `core/report_drilldown.tile_panel` now emits one untraceable origin for such a row, so every
report naming a config-resolved feed inherits the honesty — cash recon's processor and sales legs
included (§Z7 asserts it at the shared fold, not at these two reports).

**A GAP STATUS CANNOT BECOME A MEASURED ZERO.** The card-settlement tally has three statuses that mean
*we do not know* (`no_processor_data`, `no_declared_data`, `dm_merged`). `external_credit_drilldown`
imports `GAP_STATUSES` from `external_credit_recon` — the report's own tuple, the same one its `totals`
reads — so a status added there cannot start reading as $0.00 here (§D1 pins object identity). Those
store-days appear in every panel, carrying their reason, **un-counted**. The "Without evidence" tile
deliberately has **no** drill: it is three counts added together on the screen, and a figure the screen
composes itself has no single fold behind it.

**TWO SIBLING DUPLICATES CLOSED IN THE SAME PR.** (1) The "offer a tile's link only when the server
served a panel" loop had been written locally in each page that gained tile drills, and one of them had
bolted its own extra condition on. It is now `useDrillTile(panels, gate?)` → `.dl(...)` in
`frontend/src/components/DrillDownPanel.tsx`, with the per-page difference as the `gate` parameter;
`cash-recon-management` and `tender-recon` were migrated onto it and their locks re-pointed there
(§E10/§E11, and the batch-1/2 harnesses' E9/G1). (2) The ePay and accessory screens carried a
byte-identical `Stat` component each — the sibling defect in its smallest form — now
`closing/_lib/DrillStat.tsx` with `STORE_DRILL_COLUMNS` as the client side of
`day_recon_drilldown._row_fields` (§E12).

**A SCREEN NO LONGER RECOMPUTES A SERVER FOLD.** The accessory recon's "Net variance" tile was
`declared - actual` in TypeScript. A figure the screen folds itself is undrillable *by construction*,
which is the §CORE-17.3b class arriving one tile at a time. It is a served `totals["variance"]` now,
and §B4 fails the build if the client arithmetic returns.

**A ROW ADDRESSES A STORE-DAY, not a store.** Both day recons take the date as a parameter rather than
carrying it on their rows, so an origin keyed on `store_code` alone addressed every day there has ever
been. Both endpoints now stamp `close_date` on each row (additive to the payload) and §A8 pins the key
set.

### §CORE-17.3d ONE FOLD FOR A FIGURE AND ITS EVIDENCE, even under a screen filter (2026-10-24, batch 4)

**This SUPERSEDES the reported gap of §CORE-17.3b.** That section recorded a partial: a report whose
tiles are folded in TypeScript over the rows the reader filtered down to, while its drill-down panels
are folded server-side over the whole range. Under any filter the two describe different populations,
so the drill was offered only where they happened to agree, and the route stayed `owes`. The remedy
written down there was "move this report's standard filters server-side".

**Three reports hit it, so the cause got fixed instead of a third excuse written.**
`/closing/tender-recon` (§CORE-17.3b), `/closing/pickup` (named there as the sibling) and
`/closing/tender-recon-3way` (its "Selection totals" strip, found while surveying batch 4). Three
instances is the class, and the house rule is explicit: *name the class, not the instance.*

**THE FIX IS ONE FOLD, NOT SERVER-SIDE FILTERS.** Moving the filters would change each endpoint's
identity and keyset handling on money screens, lose the instant client-side filtering, and still leave
two folds. Instead:

1. `core/report_drilldown.drill_row` now carries `row_key` — the natural key of the REPORT ROW a drill
   row explains, the same dict its origins are keyed by. `tile_panel` fills it from the catalogue's own
   `keys`, so every report already on the tile shape gets it with no change.
2. `frontend/src/lib/drill-narrow.ts` is the ONE home for restricting a panel to a screen's selection:
   `narrowPanel(panel, keep, label?)`, `narrowPanels`, `rowKeyOf`, `screenKey`, `agreesToTheCent`.
3. **The tile reads its number OFF the narrowed panel** (`panels[k].figure.amount`) rather than
   reducing the rows again. That is what makes them one fold: there is no second arithmetic to drift.
   A report's own client reduce survives only as the fallback for a figure no panel was served for,
   and such a tile offers no drill.

**WHY A CLIENT-SIDE FOLD IS ALLOWED TO BE AUTHORITATIVE HERE, given the server is the authority.**
Because with nothing dropped it is not a fold at all: `narrowPanel` returns the server's own panel
object untouched when the selection is the whole range. `frontend/prove_drill_narrow.mjs` §A8 pins that
identity by object identity, and §A2–A7 keep it field-by-field as a regression guard, so a future change
that starts recomputing the unfiltered case has to come back and agree rather than quietly ship a second
arithmetic. The fixtures are real panels from the real server declarations, regenerated and checked by
`backend/harness_drill_narrow_fixtures.py` (`--write` after a deliberate shape change).

**A NARROWED VERDICT NEVER CLAIMS A CHECK IT COULD NOT MAKE.** The server's tie-out is a real
comparison — the figure comes from the report, the rows from the evidence, and they can disagree. A
narrowed figure is Σ(the selection's rows), so comparing it against those rows could only come back
True: a check that cannot fail, printed as though it had passed. So a narrowed tie-out states what IS
true (the figure is the selection's own total), carries `by_construction`, keeps the server's whole-range
verdict beside it as `whole_range`, and the renderer marks it **∑** rather than ✅. `ties` is still
**null**, never true, when a kept row has no number.

**IT REFUSES RATHER THAN GUESS ON A CAPPED PANEL.** The server caps a panel at `ROW_CAP` rows and
computes its tie-out over all of them before the cap. Narrowing a capped list would produce a figure
missing rows nobody can see, so `narrowPanel` returns `null`, `narrowPanels` leaves it out, the screen
offers no link, and the page says which figures could not be opened and why. A row the server sent with
no `row_key` is KEPT, never dropped — dropping it would silently shrink the figure, which is the exact
failure this mechanism exists to prevent.

**Shipped on `/closing/tender-recon`** (owed count 89 → 88), which is where the excuse was written, so
the mechanism and the first conversion are proved together. The other two conversions landed as batch
5 — see §CORE-17.3e.

### §CORE-17.3e THE TWO REPORTS THAT GAP WAS BLOCKING, and one claim that turned out false (2026-10-24, batch 5)

Both conversions §CORE-17.3d left open, with one correction worth more than either of them.

**`/closing/tender-recon-3way` — `backend/app/modules/closing/three_way_drilldown.py`.** Ten figures.
The same tenders captured three independent ways per store-day (the rep's closing sheet, the POS
X-report, the sales transactions), and a "Selection totals" strip over whatever the reader filtered down
to. It is the §CORE-17.3d shape exactly: the server folds once, the screen narrows the served panels to
its own selection with `lib/drill-narrow`, each tile is READ OFF its narrowed panel, and the page's own
reduce survives only as the fallback for a figure no panel was served for (which says so on screen).

- **`flat_rows(days)` and `totals(rows)` are the ONE home for the flattening and the strip.** The
  endpoint returns one block per calendar date; the screen flattens the same payload for its cards, so
  two flattenings would be two populations. One home, dereferenced by both.
- **Net and gross are both drillable, in their own right.** `gross_cx`/`gross_xs` sum |difference| per
  store-day so offsetting errors cannot hide in them (the owner's explicit caution, 2026-08-03); the net
  figures are folded PER ROW rather than subtracted from two other tiles, which is what makes them
  openable at all. A figure composed from two other tiles has no rows of its own by construction.
- Its selection key is the store-DAY (`ROW_KEYS = ("store_code", "close_date")`); the page's flat rows
  carry `date`, so `screenKey` maps it — locked by §F3 of the harness.

**`/closing/pickup` — `backend/app/modules/closing/pickup_drilldown.py`. IT WAS NOT IN THE CLASS.**
§CORE-17.3b listed this screen as the sibling instance, on the strength of its own comment ("footer
totals over the envelopes CURRENTLY ON SCREEN"). That reading was half wrong, and checking it rather
than inheriting it is why this is the short half of the batch: **every filter on that page — date or
range, store, market, employee, DM — is a QUERY PARAMETER**, so the server already returns exactly the
envelopes on screen and its fold covers exactly them. The screen needs the plain tile shape; no
narrowing is applied, and `harness_batch5_drilldown.py` §F5 FAILS THE BUILD if `drill-narrow` is wired
into it, so a later reader cannot "fix" it back into the class it was never in.

- Twelve figures, keyed per envelope: the store-day AND the person who filed it, because two envelopes
  for one store-day are two people's declarations.
- **The counted figures still refuse to cover an envelope nobody counted.** Folding a declared amount
  into an "actual" total would manufacture agreement; reading an uncounted envelope as $0.00 would
  manufacture a 100% shortfall. The declaration reads that refusal off the same fields the endpoint
  does, and each excluded envelope appears in the panel with its reason (`not_collected` /
  `not_recorded`) rather than vanishing from it.
- **One figure the screen WAS folding itself is now served**: the gross cash column's footer total
  (`total_cash_gross`), which was the only footer with no rows behind it by construction.

**`/closing/billpay-pickup` — the sibling, fixed in the same breath.** The bill-pay pickup is the same
process wearing a second screen (owner directive 2026-09-02, "the same process same wiring") over the
same envelope fields, so its seven figures are declared as a SECOND CATALOGUE in
`pickup_drilldown.py` — `billpay_catalogue()` — reusing the one label, the one row-fields function and
the one set of state readers. No sibling file, locked by §H1. The two screens also share ONE stat tile
and one set of drill columns now (`closing/_lib/DrillStat.DrillPickupStat` /
`ENVELOPE_DRILL_COLUMNS`); each had carried a byte-identical `Stat`, which is the sibling defect in
its smallest form and is how it came back after §CORE-17.3c fixed it for the day recons.

- A bill payment taken **on a card** has no physical cash to collect, so it never counts as waiting;
  it is still SHOWN in that panel, not counted, with its reason, and it is counted at a real $0.00 in
  the waiting-CASH panel. Shown-not-counted and counted-at-zero are different facts and the reader of
  either figure needs the difference (§H4, §H6, §H6b).
- The card side is its own figure (`total_credit`) and is never added into a cash one (§H5).

**REPORTED, NOT PAPERED OVER (defect, owner's to decide).** Bill-pay envelopes carry
`actual_picked_amount` exactly as cash ones do, and `GET /closing/billpay-pickups` **never totals it**
— so that screen has no counted side at all. That is not a figure missing its rows; it is a figure
that does not exist, and the cash page's whole honesty argument (declared is the number a short pickup
does not change) therefore has no counterpart on the bill-pay side. Adding it changes what the report
SHOWS, so it is written down here rather than slipped in with a drill-down.

**Four reasons added to `report_drilldown.UNMEASURED_REASONS`** — `no_processor_data`,
`no_declared_data`, `dm_merged`, `not_collected` — so an un-numbered row says in words why, in the one
place those words live. Changing that tuple deliberately fails `harness_drill_narrow_fixtures.py`; the
fixtures are regenerated with `--write`, never the check relaxed.

Proof: `backend/harness_batch5_drilldown.py` (74 checks, §Z1–Z7 negative controls). Owed count 88 → 85.

### §CORE-17.3f AN ACCUSATION NAMES ITS EVIDENCE (2026-10-25, batch 6)

Two reports whose every figure is a claim ABOUT A NAMED PERSON, which is a different bar from a
measurement: a recon row says *this rep declared $400 and the feed says $380, so the close is
blocked*, and a chargeback row says *$150 is coming out of this district manager's commission*. A
figure that costs someone money has to show which days it is counting and where each side of the
comparison came from.

**`/closing/recon` — `backend/app/modules/closing/recon_drilldown.py`.** Four figures (blocks, flags,
pending, all rows), and because they are COUNTS their panels are the accusations themselves. The rows
a count does not count stay in the panel as context — that is the difference between a drill-down and
a filtered list.

- **An accusation is addressed by day, store, person AND figure**, because one rep-day can be blocked
  on cash and flagged on credit at the same time: two accusations about two figures, not one row.
- **The declared side names the closing row; the counterpart names the sales-pair side the read
  ACTUALLY answered from.** `_b2b_day` now reports its `sales_tables` (§CORE-17.3c), so this is
  dereferenced rather than guessed — and every other caller of that read can now do the same.
- **A PENDING ROW IS AN ACCUSATION THE REPORT REFUSES TO MAKE.** The feed was not loaded, or the rep
  could not be matched, so nothing was compared. It names no feed (a counted, stated provenance gap),
  carries no variance, and says which of the two blanks it is — `no_sales_feed_match` or
  `not_computed`. A $0.00 variance there would read as *we checked and it agreed*.
- **The rule that made a row a block is NOT copied into the declaration.** `router._money_issues` is
  the one home for it (cash short blocks, cash over flags; credit over blocks, credit under flags,
  outside the tenant's tolerance) and writes its verdict onto the row; the declaration shows that
  verdict. A second copy of the thresholds could drift from the one actually applied, so §E2 fails
  the build on any number in either declaration.
- **Its four counts were reading the whole month while the table read the filter** — pre-existing and
  never written down. They are narrowed now (§CORE-17.3d). The SEVERITY filter is deliberately NOT
  part of the selection, because the four tiles ARE that filter: including it would make every tile
  read its own subset the moment one was clicked (§F3).

**The DM-verify chargeback strip (`/closing/verify`) —
`backend/app/modules/closing/ops_chargeback_drilldown.py`.** Four money figures above
"Missed verifications & chargebacks", each one money taken, or about to be taken, out of a named
DM's pay. Plain tile shape: every filter there is a query parameter.

- `to_be_foregone` is pending + posted **folded from the rows**, not composed from two other tiles —
  a tile composed from two tiles has no rows of its own. A waived chargeback is forgiven: counted in
  neither, still shown. The statuses it covers are declared once (`FOREGONE_STATUSES`).
- It names **one** table, `ops_chargeback`, because that is where the amount and the decision live —
  not the closing or verification tables a reader would look in and not find it. There IS no
  verification row; that absence is why the chargeback exists.

**Not converted, and why** (both are work QUEUES whose figures are not folds): `/closing/management`
is a list of closing attempts and `/closing/closing-pickup-status` a compliance queue. What they owe
is per-ROW provenance (which attempt, by whom, at what time, and the accepted closing row it led to),
which is a different affordance from a figure's panel and is not served by forcing the tile shape
onto them. They stay `owes` with that reason in the ledger rather than being marked done.

Proof: `backend/harness_batch6_drilldown.py` (57 checks, §Z1–Z6 negative controls). Owed count
85 → 83.

### §CORE-17.3g THREE PEOPLE COUNT ONE ENVELOPE (2026-10-25, batch 7)

Batch 7 of the §CORE-17 audit: **`/closing/envelope-report`** (the Management Envelope Receipt) and
**`/closing`** (the Daily Closing dashboard). Owed count **83 → 81**. Proof:
`backend/harness_batch7_drilldown.py`, **99 checks**, §Z1–Z8 negative controls, wired into the
carrier-vocab-guard lock job.

**The receipt — `closing/envelope_drilldown.py`, 9 figures on 5 tiles.** Three different people
record three different numbers for one envelope, in three different tables, and the screen showed
them side by side as if they were one measurement. So each figure names ONLY the tables it was read
out of: `daily_closing` for a count of envelopes filed, `+ envelope_count` for a variance (one is
scored against the other), `+ ops_chargeback` for the chargeback figures, because that is where the
amount and the decision live and nowhere else. A short envelope nobody assigned to anyone does NOT
name the chargeback table — §B4 caught the first cut of this declaration claiming it on every row.

- **An uncounted envelope is not a clean one.** It is a real envelope and `envelopes` counts it, but
  it is deliberately not counted in short / over / match or in either dollar figure, with
  `not_counted` as its stated reason. Folding it in at $0.00 would read as "management counted this
  and it came out exactly right", which is the opposite of the truth and the exact reading the
  receipt exists to prevent.
- **The By-employee rollup gets ONE PANEL PER LINE**, keyed on the employee name that line is keyed
  on. That is the owner's original ask — *"cash variance at employee should have the drill down from
  where the data is coming from"* — applied to the second surface of that shape, and it is not a new
  mechanism: `cash_variance.drilldowns` / `group_drilldown` already serve one panel per rollup row.
  The figure is the line's own `net_variance`, and the LABEL SAYS "net of short and over" because a
  rep $50 short one day and $50 over the next nets to zero while twice having handed over the wrong
  cash. The note carries both gross counts and the envelopes nobody counted.
- The basis a stored count was SCORED on rides on each row in the tenant's own wording, resolved
  once at the endpoint from `envelope_report.basis_label` — the declaration spells no basis key
  (§B8), and the processor term is now read ONCE and dereferenced by both the selector's labels and
  the drill-down's (§G8; it was read twice).

**The dashboard — `closing/rollup_drilldown.py`, 11 figures on 10 tiles, and the grain is a FACT.**
These tiles are not Σ(rep submissions). `verified_overlay` makes a DM's correction authoritative FOR
THE STORE-DAY — its own docstring says it "is applied to store-day AGGREGATES only" and that per-rep
detail keeps the reps' raw figures — so a panel of rep-days would NOT add up to the tile on any day a
DM corrected, and the gap would read as a defect in the report rather than as the design. §D3 proves
exactly that: the store-day fold ties AND the rep-day fold does not. The endpoint now KEEPS the
corrected store-day figure its overlay loop already computed and threw away (§G9).

- A corrected store-day names `daily_closing_verification`; an uncorrected one names
  `daily_closing` alone, and the row says in words whose figures they are. A provenance claimed
  where no authority was exercised is a lie that reads like rigour.
- **A DM corrects money, not counts.** The count panels therefore name the closing sheet alone even
  on a corrected day — §E4 caught the money reader being reused for them.
- `days` has NO panel on purpose: it is a DISTINCT count of dates, not a sum over rows, so no set of
  rows adds up to it and a panel would be a claim nobody could check. The DM-verified tile is TWO
  figures (verified / filed), and the unverified store-days are shown in the verified panel,
  uncounted — they are the work the figure measures.

**The dashboard's two cash tiles are the close recon's own accusation, folded as money.** Both come
from `_money_issues`, so they are declared as a SIBLING in `closing/recon_drilldown.py`
(`submission_catalogue`), not in a file of their own — one fact, one home, two folds, the shape
`pickup_drilldown.billpay_catalogue` already set. Their grain is the rep-day, so `metric` is no part
of their address. They ARE the client-folded class (§CORE-17.3d): narrowed through
`lib/drill-narrow` and READ OFF their narrowed panels, with the client reduce kept as the fallback.
The panels are served only to a caller who may review money, because the endpoint already withholds
those figures from everyone else and the evidence behind a hidden figure is the hidden figure (§G12).

**REPORTED, NOT PAPERED OVER — a live presentation defect on the dashboard.** A rep-day the recon
could not judge (the sales feed was not loaded for that day, or the rep could not be matched to it)
contributes 0.00 to both cash tiles. The SUM is right; the presentation is not, because
"Cash short $0.00" then reads as "no cash is missing" when nothing was compared at all. The figures
are UNCHANGED — a figure is never moved to make a screen read better — and those rows now appear in
both panels, uncounted, each naming which of the two blanks it is (§F3, §F4). It is the same class as
§CORE-17.3f's pending recon rows, on the dashboard.

### §CORE-17.3h A RATE OR AN AVERAGE GETS NO PANEL (2026-10-25, batch 8)

Batch 8 of the §CORE-17 audit: **`/crm/reports`** (conversion, sources, rep activity) and
**`/helpdesk/dashboard`**. Owed count **81 → 79**. Proof: `backend/harness_batch8_drilldown.py`,
**79 checks**, §Z1–Z7 negative controls, wired into the carrier-vocab-guard lock job. Declarations:
`backend/app/modules/crm/reports_drilldown.py` and
`backend/app/modules/helpdesk/dashboard_drilldown.py`.

**THE RULE THIS BATCH SETTLES, for every report after it: a figure that is a QUOTIENT gets no
drill-down of its own. It offers the counts it divides, each with a real panel.** `win_rate` is won
÷ closed, `close_rate` is closed ÷ total, `avg_resolution_hours` is a mean over the resolved
tickets. There is no set of records that ADDS UP to a percentage or to a mean, so a panel behind one
could only be a tie-out that cannot fail — the worst kind of reassurance, and precisely what
`report_drilldown.tie_out` exists to refuse. The three declarations therefore serve **no key at
all** for those figures (locked: harness §A5/§A6, §E4), the screens' rate tiles link to their
numerator and denominator instead (§H2, §H3), and the counts' own panels say in words which half of
the rate the reader is looking at. The house had already settled this shape once — the Daily Closing
dashboard's DM-verified tile serves `verified` and `filed` rather than one ratio (§CORE-17.3g) — and
this section is that ruling written down so the next report does not re-derive it.

**The average's DENOMINATOR was never on the screen.** `/helpdesk/dashboard`'s "Avg resolution
(hrs)" is computed only from tickets carrying BOTH `created_at` and `resolved_at`. On a period with
200 tickets of which 12 are resolved it is a measurement of 12 and reads as a measurement of 200. So
`helpdesk/dashboard_drilldown.totals` folds `measured`, the endpoint now serves it, the tile shows
"over 12 of 200 resolved", and that is the figure the tile's drill-down opens. The unresolved
tickets appear in that panel, uncounted, with `not_resolved` as their stated reason — never folded
in at zero hours, which would drag the mean toward a number nobody measured. §E5 caught the first
cut of this inheriting the generic unmapped-status reason instead, which would have explained the
wrong thing on the one panel a reader opens to understand the mean.

**The vocabulary is PROVENANCE, not decoration**, in both reports, because in both an entry missing
from it CHANGES the figure:

- `crm_stage` decides whether a lead reaches the funnel at all, so a lead whose stage resolves names
  it and a lead whose stage does not names only `crm_lead` (§B1, §B2). `crm_disposition` is named
  per row, only where a reason was actually recorded (§B3, §B4).
- `ticket_statuses` turns a `status_id` into a lifecycle stage, and an unmapped id silently falls
  back to `"open"`. That ticket names only `tickets`, carries `not_recorded`, and is still counted
  as open — the panel reports the fallback, it does not change the figure (§F2, §F3).

**REPORTED, NOT PAPERED OVER — two live defects these reports have today.**

1. **`pipeline_core.funnel` silently drops a lead whose `stage_id` is not in the stage vocabulary**
   (`if b is None: continue`), while `conversion_rates` counts every lead. So Σ(by_stage.count) can
   be LESS than the TOTAL tile on the same screen, and nothing said so. §C reproduces it from the
   real `funnel` and `conversion_rates` (total 4, Σ 3). The figures are UNCHANGED: the dropped lead
   is in the TOTAL panel with `stage_unknown`, it is in none of the per-stage panels (which are
   keyed on `stage_id` exactly as `funnel` keys its buckets, so they cannot disagree with it), and
   the screen now states the shortfall in words above the funnel.
2. **`/crm/reports/activity` returns `{"rows": []}` on ANY exception from its read**, so a failed
   read reads as "nobody logged anything". That is the endpoint's own shape and was not changed
   here; it is written down in `crm/reports_drilldown.py` and locked into §G7 so a reader of an
   empty rep-activity table knows the other reading.

**Per-row panels, keyed as each endpoint keys its own buckets.** One panel per funnel stage
(`stage_id`), per source line (the source NAME, including the `"Unknown"` bucket an unrecognised
source lands in), and per rep line (`actor_employee_id`, including the `"—"` bucket an unattributed
touch lands in). A touch names BOTH `crm_activity` and `crm_lead`, because the endpoint drops a
touch whose lead the caller cannot see — the lead is part of why the figure is what it is, not
context. Neither screen narrows its panels and neither should: every filter on both is a query
parameter, so the server folded exactly the records on screen (locked, §H4).

**The aging card is keyed on NOW, not on the period** — an open ticket is bucketed by how old it is
at the moment the page loaded, while every figure above it is keyed on `created_at` inside the
chosen range. Both are right and they are different questions, so the heading says so and the card
gets no panel: "how old right now" has no stable set of rows a server folded it over.

### §CORE-17.3i THE ROWS A WORK QUEUE EXISTS FOR HAVE NO EVIDENCE (2026-10-25, batch 9)

Batch 9 of the §CORE-17 audit: **`/closing/closing-pickup-status`** (Closing & Cash Pickup Status,
shared with the Daily Closing dashboard's own tab) and **`/closing/management`** (Management Review's
3-try attempt log). Owed count **79 → 77**. Proof: `backend/harness_batch9_drilldown.py`, **75
checks**, §Z1–Z6 negative controls, wired into the carrier-vocab-guard lock job. Declarations:
`backend/app/modules/closing/chain_drilldown.py` and
`backend/app/modules/closing/attempts_drilldown.py`.

**THE FINDING THIS BATCH RECORDS, for every work queue after it: a row can have NO provenance, and
that is the answer, not a gap in the tool.** Every earlier batch drilled from a figure to the rows it
was read out of. Here the rows the report exists for were read out of nothing: a store-day nobody
filed anything for has no closing sheet, no turned-away submit, no pickup envelope and no count — it
is on the report because the ROSTER expected that store to file. `chain_drilldown` therefore names no
table for it, which the shared fold already turns into a **stated, countable untraceable origin**,
and the row carries `not_filed` plus an `evidence` field saying in words that the roster is the only
thing that put it there. Naming a table would be a provenance claim nothing checked; leaving the row
out would hide the report's own subject. A row on these reports can name anywhere from zero to five
tables, one per stage that actually ran (locked: harness §B1–§B4).

**An unfiled store-day is never worth $0.00.** It contributes 0.00 to declared / collected /
still-in-store today, so "Cash still in stores $0" reads as "no money is waiting" when the drawer was
never counted. Those rows are shown in all three cash panels and NOT counted — and the tie-out still
holds exactly, because what they contributed was zero (§C1, §C2).

**REPORTED, NOT PAPERED OVER — the "No cash to collect" tile counts store-days nobody filed.**
`deposit_accountability.cash_pickup_state` reaches `nothing_to_collect` when there are no declared
envelopes AND nothing was collected, and a store-day with no closing has no declared envelopes. So an
unfiled store-day lands under a tile reading "No cash to collect" when the truth is that nobody told
us what was in the drawer. Reproduced from the real function (§C5); the figure is UNCHANGED and the
tile's panel says which of its rows are the unfiled ones (§C6).

**Management Review: a turned-away submit is not a recount.** One panel per attempt group, keyed on
`close_date|store_code|employee_name` — the screen's own row key, field for field, locked by §D2 —
with the badge's attempt count as its figure. `submit_refusal.is_real_try` stays the one rule for what
counts as a try, so a refused submit (which stored no closing at all) is shown and never counted:
counting it would read as a rep who recounted three times when their photo failed three times. The
words on such a row are the refusal's own submitter-facing sentence, dereferenced from
`submit_refusal.message_for` — the declaration spells no refusal's meaning of its own (§E2).
**Only the try the gate ACCEPTED names the closing row that stands**; a recount and a refusal name the
attempt log alone, and a group whose closing row could not be matched names no closing row at all
(§E3, §E4).

**Neither state vocabulary is re-spelled.** The closing states come from `unfinished_day.STATES` /
`LABELS` and the pickup states from `deposit_accountability.PICKUP_STATES` / `PICKUP_LABELS`, and the
screen asks for each tile's panel by that state's own key — so a state renamed in its own home moves
the tile and its drill together rather than leaving a dead link (§A3, §G5, §H2). A stage cell is read
BY KEY and never by position, so a chain that gains a stage cannot silently point these figures at
another one (§G6). Neither screen narrows its panels and neither should: every filter on both is a
query parameter (§H5).

### §CORE-17.3j A FIGURE READ OUT OF A SNAPSHOT NAMES THE SNAPSHOT — and the trail stops there (2026-10-25, batch 10)

Batch 10 of the §CORE-17 audit, the first FINANCE batch (CLAUDE.md routes the module to the
finance agent): **`/accounts/balance-sheet`**, **`/accounts/cash-flow`** and
**`/accounts/liabilities-due`** — the audit's #3 worst ("four tiles composed from four other
reports, composition invisible"). Owed count **77 → 74**. Proof:
`backend/harness_batch10_drilldown.py`, **88 checks** (85 as shipped; §I6 narrowed to its own subject
by batch 11 — see §CORE-17.3k), §Z1–Z9 negative controls, wired into the
carrier-vocab-guard lock job. Declarations:
`backend/app/modules/account/statement_drilldown.py` (the two statements — ONE declaration, see
below) and `backend/app/modules/account/liabilities_drilldown.py`.

> Numbered `.3j` while `.3i` (batch 9, the two closing work queues) was still in flight on its own
> branch; batch 9 landed first (PR #543) and this section was merged in after it. Same race
> §CORE-17's own header note describes — the letters are allocation order, not dependency.

**THE RULE THIS BATCH SETTLES, for every report built on a stored snapshot: NAME THE SNAPSHOT, AND
SAY WHERE THE TRAIL STOPS.** Both statement screens read exactly one table —
`commcalc.account_statements`, the row `statement_engine.compute_and_store` wrote. The compute knew
which feed each line came from (it had just read the asset ledger, the invoices, the borrowings) and
**it keeps the dollars and throws the provenance away**. So:

- every drill row names `account_statements`, keyed by the period, the scope and the line, because
  that is where the figure was actually read out of;
- a FEED is named only where the booking code reads that line from it unconditionally
  (`statement_drilldown.LINE_FEEDS` — the ledger and the PayGo batches for what is owed to the
  distributor, the invoices for unpaid AP, the borrowings for both inter-store lines, the two
  marketplace feeds for the settlement clearing, the two sales feeds for sales tax);
- a line whose feed is chosen from **per-org config at compute time** names **NO feed** and says
  which basis decided it (`CONFIG_RESOLVED_LINES` — inventory, the distributor payable, store cash
  on hand). The snapshot does not record which basis answered, and naming one would be a provenance
  claim nothing checked;
- **a line at $0.00 names no feed either.** Its feed WAS read and produced nothing, so claiming it
  answered is the same lie in smaller print (§Z5 shows the constant a careless declaration would
  serve, and that it differs from what is served).

Closing the gap properly means the COMPUTE storing the feed per line. That moves money-path code and
is a PR of its own; it is not done here and is written down instead.

**AND ONE FEED CANNOT BE NAMED AT ALL YET.** The chargeback reserve is booked from
`commcalc.chargeback_items`, which `coa` reads and migrations 030/036 INDEX — but no migration in
this repository CREATES it, so it is not a registered table and a `sourceLabels.ts` entry for it
fails the infra lock (`harness_carrier_vocab_guard` IW3). Naming it would therefore either break the
build or put a raw identifier on a manager's screen, so that line names no feed and says why in the
reader's own words (`statement_drilldown.UNREGISTERED_FEED_LINES`, `why_no_feed()`; §B5b, §B5c). The
remedy is a migration that creates or formally registers the table — a schema change, surfaced here
rather than smuggled into a drill-down PR.

**ONE DECLARATION FOR TWO REPORTS, because they share a GRAIN** — not merely a module. Both render
`sections[].lines[]` with a subtotal each out of one stored payload, and the Cash Flow's own lines
ARE Balance-Sheet line keys (`statement_engine.cash_flow` labels each "Change in <that line>"). One
row shape, one provenance rule, two catalogues — the `day_recon_drilldown` precedent (§CORE-17.3c),
rather than two siblings that drift.

**A DIFFERENCE AND A LEAF GET NO PANEL, which extends §CORE-17.3h from the quotient.** The Cash
Flow's tie-out delta is implied MINUS reported, and the reported half is the Balance Sheet's own cash
lines — which this payload does not carry. So the delta, the reported change and the two cash
balances serve **no key at all**; the implied change opens to the three subtotals and the screen says
where the other half lives. A cash-flow LINE gets none either: it is already the leaf, one
balance-sheet line's change between two stored statements, with nothing under it on this report
(§D3).

| What | Where | Says |
|---|---|---|
| **The two statements' declaration** | `account/statement_drilldown.py` — `LINE_FEEDS`, `CONFIG_RESOLVED_LINES`, `line_tables`, `balance_sheet_drilldowns`, `cash_flow_drilldowns` | a panel per section subtotal, per line, for Liabilities + Equity and for the imbalance (whose second row is counted NEGATIVE, so the two sides really do add up to the gap). Every figure is the statement's own, dereferenced |
| **The liabilities declaration** | `account/liabilities_drilldown.py` — `PAYABLE_BASIS_FEEDS`, `catalogue`, `drilldowns` | six tiles over six different row lists, each declaring which list, which field, which tables and which rows the figure counts. The feed is keyed on the stored basis value, so a new basis is a ROW plus its derivation — never a branch (RULE TWO) |
| **The endpoints** | `GET /account/balance-sheet/{period}`, `GET /account/cash-flow/{period}` → `drilldown`; `GET /account/liabilities-due` → `drilldown` | the statements attach theirs in ONE place (`router._with_statement_drilldown`), so a drill-down cannot exist on the unfiltered read and go missing on the filtered one. **No narrowing** on either statement: their store/market filter is SERVER-side |
| **The liabilities screen narrows, and its tiles read off the narrowed panels** | `/accounts/liabilities-due` — `narrowPanels` + `useDrillTile` | every filter there is client-side, so the §CORE-17.3d shape applies: one fold serves the tile and the panel. A company-wide row names no store and is KEPT rather than silently shrinking the figure |
| **One fold for the payroll tiles** | `liabilities_due.aggregate_payroll` now returns `rows` | the per-person cells come out of the SAME loop that produces `gross_total` and the tax split, so the drill-down behind those two tiles is the arithmetic they are, not a restatement (§G7). The cells are dropped from the served sections, because they travel inside the panels |
| **Provenance read per PERSON on a payroll row** | `liabilities_drilldown._hours_tables` | the one who clocked in names the time clock, the one whose hours were typed names the hand-entered hours, and the one with no punch at all names **the schedule** — `payroll_raw`'s own scheduled-hours fallback. Three people on one tile, three different answers (§E7) |
| **Rounding, dereferenced** | `report_drilldown.money` (new, public) | a declaration that writes `0.0` to say "zero" has acquired a dollar literal of its own, which the build locks on these declarations refuse. So the ONE rounding is public and both declarations read it |

**REPORTED, NOT PAPERED OVER — three live defects these reports have today.**

1. **NO `coa.BS_SPEC` LINE RECORDS A BREAKDOWN, SO THE BALANCE SHEET'S OWN EXPANDER NEVER OPENS.**
   `coa.add()` records a drill label only when its caller passes `detail_label`, and **not one**
   balance-sheet booking does — inventory, owed-to-distributor, invoices unpaid, the chargeback
   reserve and both inter-store lines all call it with three arguments (§C1 proves it at the source).
   The screen renders the expander whenever `line.detail` is non-empty, so on this statement it is
   always empty while the identical expander on the P&L is full. The figures are UNCHANGED: such a
   line's panel carries ONE row with no number, `detail_not_recorded`, and a tie-out of **None** —
   never a breakdown invented at $0.00, and never a tie claimed over a row nobody recorded (§C2, §C3).
2. **A SCOPE LOSES THE DETAIL THE TWO EXTRA LINES DO CARRY.** `statement_engine._book` records only
   `line["detail"]` (the org-wide roll-up) and never `detail_by_store`, while `engine._scoped` builds
   a non-consolidated scope's detail exclusively FROM `detail_by_store`. So the handset-payable and
   sales-tax lines — the only two that record a breakdown — show it on Consolidated and show nothing
   on any company, store or filtered read. That is the §4e defect (owner report 2026-10-07) returning
   on the lines added after it was fixed for `coa.add` (§C6).
3. **A MANUAL JOURNAL ENTRY FOLDED ONTO A COMPUTED LINE ADDS DOLLARS AND NO EVIDENCE.**
   `engine._assemble` matches an entry to a spec line BY LABEL and adds its amount without touching
   that line's detail. Where it happens the panel comes back `ties: False` **in words** — the report
   disagreeing with its own evidence, which is the outcome this mechanism exists to show rather than
   round away (§C7, §C8).

**AND ONE DEFECT THIS BATCH CLOSED, because the §CORE-17.3d remedy is what the drill-down needed
anyway.** On `/accounts/liabilities-due` every filter is client-side: under a store or market filter
the two distributor tiles kept showing the **unfiltered** total while the table beneath them showed
the filtered rows, and the rent and insurance tiles narrowed. The tiles now read their numbers off
their own narrowed panels, so the tile, its table and its evidence are one fold (§H4). No figure
moved: the unfiltered view is byte-identical.

**ONE EXISTING LOCK WAS NARROWED TO ITS OWN SUBJECT, not relaxed.** §4e's lock
`harness_pl_drill_detail.py` §G5 forbids a SECOND per-store drill-detail derivation anywhere in
`backend/app`, and detected one by the substring `detail_by_store` appearing in a file that does not
call `coa.accrue_detail`. Finding 2 above is *about* that grain, so the declaration's own defect
report tripped the lock from a DOCSTRING — prose, no derivation. The scan now reads **code only**
(comments and docstrings dropped by `tokenize`; a file that will not tokenise is scanned whole, so
the narrowing fails closed), and three new negative controls pin that it still catches a module which
builds the grain itself (§G5b), does not catch one that merely describes it (§G5c), and keeps the old
strictness on an unparseable file (§G5d). The rule is unchanged; 55 checks → **59**.

**No migration, no new table, no money moved** — three read-only `drilldown` payloads, one additive
`rows` key on a pure producer, and one public rounding helper on the one home.

### §CORE-17.3k A DIFFERENCE IS DRILLABLE WHEN IT IS FOLDED PER ROW (2026-10-25, batch 11)

Batch 11 of the §CORE-17 audit, the COMMISSION batch (CLAUDE.md routes the module to the
commission agent): **`/commcalc/discrepancy`** (Pay Discrepancy), **`/commcalc/carrier-vs-pay`**
(Carrier Earned vs Employee Paid — the audit's #5 worst, *"a report whose whole subject is a
disagreement about money, with no way to the two lines that disagree"*) and
**`/commcalc/commission-legs`** (Commission received over M1–M12). Owed count **74 → 71**.
Declaration: `backend/app/modules/commcalc/carrier_pay_drilldown.py`. Proof:
`backend/harness_batch11_drilldown.py`, **100 checks**, §Z1–Z9 negative controls, wired into the
carrier-vocab-guard lock job.

**THE RULING THIS BATCH SETTLES, and it narrows two earlier ones rather than contradicting them.**
§CORE-17.3h refuses a panel to a QUOTIENT and batch 10 extended that refusal to a figure computed as
`A_total − B_total`: no set of records adds up to either, so a tie-out against one is a check that
cannot fail. **Both differences on this batch's reports escape that, and the test is where the
subtraction happens.** A discrepancy row carries its own `gap` (`expected − received`, per commission
line, as `carrier_claim_value.claim_gap` computed it) and a carrier-vs-pay row carries its own
`difference` (`earned − paid`, per rep). The report's total is **Σ(those rows)**, so the rows and the
figure come from different places and CAN disagree — which is what makes the tie-out a real check.
It is the same distinction the 3-way recon's net figures turned on (§CORE-17.3e): *a figure composed
from two other tiles has no rows of its own; a figure folded per row does.* So: **subtract at the
row and it drills; subtract at the total and it does not.**

**ONE DECLARATION, THREE CATALOGUES — AND WHY THAT IS NOT THE SIBLING DEFECT.** The batch-10
precedent put two reports in one file because they share a ROW GRAIN. These three do not: a
discrepancy row is a commission LINE, a carrier-vs-pay row is a REP, a breakout row is a money
STREAM in a MONTH. Three row shapes is three catalogues, and one declaration pretending otherwise
would lie about two of its reports. They are in ONE module because what they share is the thing a
drill-down exists for — *where did this carrier-money figure come from*, *which side of it was never
reported*, and *what a snapshot can name* — and three files would be three answers to one question,
which is the duplicate defect arriving one report at a time.

| What | Where | Says |
|---|---|---|
| **The one declaration** | `commcalc/carrier_pay_drilldown.py` — `discrepancy_catalogue` / `discrepancy_drilldowns` / `discrepancy_store_drilldowns`, `carrier_vs_pay_catalogue` / `carrier_vs_pay_drilldowns`, `cells` / `breakout_drilldowns` | three catalogues, one provenance rule, one not-reported rule. Computes nothing: every figure is the producer's own, dereferenced |
| **Which feeds the WRITER of a stored discrepancy row read** | `data_lineage_registry.DISCREPANCY_WRITER_FEEDS` + `discrepancy_writer_feeds(source)` | keyed on the `source` value the engine STAMPS, so a third writer is a ROW plus its derivation, never a branch (RULE TWO). Only the writer that records enough to be named is listed; an unrecognised one resolves to NOTHING and the row names the snapshot alone |
| **Which feed a money STREAM was read out of** | `carrier_pay_drilldown.FEEDS_BY_STREAM` | keyed on `commission_received.STREAMS`' own stream keys, with the COLUMN where a stream is one column of a shared feed (`raw_mi`'s two residual columns). Locked both ways, and locked against the stream's own `source` sentence — the prose the page prints and the machine fact cannot diverge (§Y2, §Y2b, §Y2c) |
| **Which feed a REP's earned figure answered from** | `carrier_pay_drilldown.earned_tables` | read per ROW off the row's own verdict, because four reps on one tile have four different answers: a pre-attributed tenant names the CALCULATED rep commissions (§CORE-17.3j — the snapshot, not the feed the calculation read), a rep whose activations were looked up names both statement tables, and a rep the carrier side was never looked up for names **nothing** and is reported as an origin that cannot be traced |
| **The four feed constants that were only ever literals** | `data_lineage_registry.PAYMENT_DETAIL`, `MI_RESIDUAL`, `COMP_REPORT`, `MA_COMMISSION`, `CARRIER_STATEMENT`, `DISCREPANCY_SNAPSHOT` | named in the registry and dereferenced by `COMMISSION_CALC_FEEDS` itself, so a declaration naming a feed reads the one home instead of restating a table name at the call site |
| **The endpoints** | `GET /commcalc/discrepancy/{period}` → `drilldown` + `drilldown_store`; `GET /commcalc/carrier-vs-pay/{period}` → `drilldown`; `GET /commcalc/commission-received-breakout` → `drilldown` | each ATTACHES the declaration's output and folds nothing (§Y9) |
| **ONE FOLD, AND ONE COPY OF IT** | the discrepancy screen's headline reads `drilldown["gap_<tab>"].figure.amount` | the tile's number IS the panel's figure, so the two cannot drift (§CORE-17.3d) — and the per-tab total is therefore **not** also served under a key of its own, which would be the same number twice in one payload. The page's own reduce survives only as the fallback for a payload carrying no panel, and such a tile offers no drill (§Y9b, §Y12) |
| **No narrowing on any of the three** | `harness_batch11_drilldown.py` §Y11 | every filter that moves a figure on these screens is a QUERY PARAMETER, so the server's own fold already covers what is on screen. The lock FAILS THE BUILD if `lib/drill-narrow` is wired into any of them — the §CORE-17.3e `pickup_drilldown` posture, so a later reader cannot "fix" them into a class they were never in |
| **The By-Store gap opens too** | `discrepancy_store_drilldowns` | a district manager acts on that number, so it has rows. The store panels PARTITION the tab's panel — a line is in exactly one of them — and a line with no store at all is kept under a stated bucket rather than dropped, which would silently shrink the figure (§A16, §A17) |

**ABSENCE IS NEVER ZERO, THREE TIMES OVER, AND NOT ONE CENT MOVED.** A commission claim nobody could
price (`claim_gap` returns **None** rather than inventing a subtraction), a rep whose carrier
statement was never loaded, and a month a feed never delivered are all SHOWN, carry no figure, are
NOT counted, and say why. Each contributes zero to a sum either way, which is precisely what makes
this a change to the presentation and not to the number: §Z8 asserts that the screen's old reduce (a
null coerced to `0`, as JavaScript does) and the served fold (which skips it) agree on **every tab,
to the cent**, and §Z8b proves that comparison can fail.

**A MEASURED ZERO AND AN ABSENCE ARE DIFFERENT ROWS ON ONE PANEL.** The informational tab's $0.00
line and a rep the statement pays nothing against are real measurements and are counted (or, for the
rep, shown at $0.00 and excluded from a total that only covers reported reps); the unpriced claim and
the un-looked-up rep carry no figure at all. §Z3 plants the careless declaration that coerces the
unpriced gap to $0.00: it ties, exactly as the honest one does, and the difference is visible only on
the ROW — which is the whole argument for putting it there.

**WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED, so nobody reads a missing link as an oversight.** The
discrepancy screen's *Line items* and *Stores affected* counts (the table and the By-Store list
immediately below them ARE what they count), its **Phantom** tab (a different endpoint over a
different row shape — a panel for it would open the wrong rows), the carrier-vs-pay rep COUNTS
(cardinalities of states every panel row already carries), the breakout's per-leg table CELLS (a
stream's own leg total, already reachable through the group tile and the stream total), and
commission-legs **tab 2**, which is a config surface and not a report.

**THREE LIVE DEFECTS THESE REPORTS HAVE TODAY — REPORTED, NOT FIXED, AND NO FIGURE MOVED.**

1. **`GET /commcalc/discrepancy/{period}` RAISES on a claim that was never priced.** The endpoint's
   store rollup evaluates `r["gap"] > 0.50`, and `gap` is persisted **NULL** when the expected side
   could not be measured — which is right (`carrier_claim_value.claim_gap`: *a gap is a subtraction,
   so it cannot exist where one side does not*). `None > 0.50` is a `TypeError` in Python 3, so the
   whole Pay Discrepancy report 500s for any period holding one, and `SOLD_NOT_IN_MI` with no
   parseable MRC is exactly such a row written with `status='open'` — the branch that compares. NOT
   fixed here: the repair has to decide whether an unsized open claim counts toward `total_flagged`,
   which is a decision about money and belongs in front of the owner. §Z6 reproduces it against the
   real producer; §Z6b proves the drill-down itself survives that payload.
2. **The same screen counted an unsized claim as $0.00.** `tabTotal` was
   `rows.reduce((s, r) => s + r.gap, 0)` and `null` coerces to `0` in JavaScript. Closed as a
   presentation fix, with the figure pinned identical (§Z8).
3. **`GET /commcalc/carrier-vs-pay/{period}` narrows its ROWS under a market or store filter and
   leaves its TOTALS over every rep.** `rollup_by_rep` folds the totals first and the endpoint then
   filters `out["rows"]`, reporting what it dropped in `meta.filtered` — which the page never showed.
   So the four tiles describe the month while the table beneath them describes the selection. The
   panels are folded over the **unfiltered** rows, because that is the population the figure they
   explain was folded over and a panel about a different population is proof of the wrong number
   (§CORE-17.3b); the page now SAYS so, in a banner, instead of leaving the reader to assume the
   strip follows the dropdown. NOT fixed here: folding the totals over the kept rows moves a figure
   the owner reads. §Z7 pins the defect so a later fix cannot land without re-pointing the panels in
   the same breath.

**AND ONE GAP THAT IS THE LEGACY ENGINE'S, NOT THIS BATCH'S.** `ma_recon` records
`evidence.b2b.source_table` on every row it writes, so an MA-recon discrepancy row names the exact
sales feed its activation was found in — a stored fact, read per row, never guessed. The legacy
discrepancy engine records **no evidence at all**, and which of its two money feeds answered a given
row depends on that row's comp type, so its rows name the snapshot alone. Closing that properly means
the WRITER storing its provenance, which moves money-path code and is a PR of its own. A stored
`source_table` the registry's own display union does not recognise is IGNORED rather than printed
(§A8): a stored string is not a licence to put an arbitrary identifier on a manager's screen.

**ONE EXISTING LOCK WAS NARROWED TO ITS OWN SUBJECT, not relaxed — and it is the same shape batch 10
narrowed, one layer out.** `harness_batch10_drilldown.py` §I6 asserted `OWES_MAX == 74`, and an
EQUALITY against a MONOTONE GLOBAL counter can only hold for one commit: the moment the next batch
lowers the ratchet — which `harness_drilldown_coverage` *exists to require* — that file goes red for
doing exactly the right thing. Batch 11 (74 → 71) was the first to hit it. The subject of the check is
*batch 10 lowered it by three*, and the honest invariant for that is `<= 74`. The rule is unchanged
and it still FAILS CLOSED: a pin above 74 is red (§I6b), a deleted pin and an unparseable one are red
(§I6d), and the only behaviour added is that a LOWER pin passes (§I6c). 85 checks → **88**. The
general lesson, written down once: **a lock about a ratchet asserts the DIRECTION, never the value** —
a value assertion makes the lock expire on the next correct change, and the next reader's reflex when
it goes red is to edit the number, which is how a ratchet quietly becomes decoration. The whole class
was swept in the same breath: every `harness_*.py` was grepped for `OWES_MAX`, and only batches 10 and
11 pin it (batches 1–9 never did), so THIS batch's own §I6 — which had been written as the same
substring equality against `OWES_MAX = 71` — was rewritten shrink-only too, with the identical
`_owes_max()` reader and the same three negative controls. A successor lowering the ratchet to 68 now
has to touch neither file.

**ONE EXISTING LOCK CAUGHT THIS BATCH ONE STEP SHORT OF ITS OWN RULE, and was not touched.**
`harness_feed_watchdog.py` §F8 requires that once a table HAS a registry constant, every watchdog map
keys it BY that constant and never re-spells it. Giving `raw_payment_detail`, `raw_mi`,
`raw_comp_report` and `raw_ma_commission` constants therefore turned the PRE-EXISTING literals in
`DATA_DATE_COLUMN_BY_TABLE`, `FEED_CADENCE_BY_TABLE`, `FEED_LABEL_BY_TABLE` and the MA store-column map
into second copies the instant the constants appeared — the §19.18 shape, created by the very change
that was closing it. Ten keys now dereference; no value changed, no table was renamed, `watched_feeds()`
returns the identical set, 51/1 → **52/0**. **Naming a fact is half the fix: the other half is deleting
every copy in the same commit, and a lock that fires on the half-done state is doing its job.** The ~140
`client.table("raw_…")` call-sites across `app/modules/**` are query arguments rather than the
registry's declaration, are outside F8's subject, and are deliberately left for their own PR — one of
them is inside the commission engine, which belongs to another thread.

**No migration, no new table, no money moved** — three read-only `drilldown` payloads, one additive
`drilldown_store` mapping beside them, six feed-name constants and one writer map on the lineage
registry, and three reason sentences on the one home's `UNMEASURED_REASONS` whose KEYS are
`carrier_vs_pay`'s own reason constants (locked identical, §Y1, so the two vocabularies cannot drift).

### §CORE-17.3l A REPORT FAMILY'S GRAIN COUNT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (2026-10-25, batch 12)

Batch 12 of the §CORE-17 audit, the DEVICE-ASSET subsystem (commission agent): **`/commcalc/asset`**
(Asset Ledger), **`/commcalc/asset/dashboard`** (Asset Charges Dashboard),
**`/commcalc/asset/on-inventory`** (On-Inventory by Store), **`/commcalc/asset/owed-weekly`** (Weekly
Owed to Distributor — the audit's #8 worst), **`/commcalc/asset/inventory-recon`** (On-Inventory ↔ the
POS snapshot), **`/commcalc/asset/borrowed`** (Inter-store Borrowed Money) and
**`/commcalc/asset/lending`** (Asset Lending / Distributor PayGo). Owed count **71 → 64**.
Declaration: `backend/app/modules/asset/device_asset_drilldown.py`. Proof:
`backend/harness_batch12_drilldown.py`, **125 checks**, §Z1–Z12 negative controls, wired into the
carrier-vocab-guard lock job.

**THE RULING THIS BATCH SETTLES.** The batch was handed over as *"probably one or two grains — a
device, and a store-week of devices owed"*, with the instruction to MEASURE that rather than assume
it. Reading the seven producers gives **six**, because *a grain is the row a figure is Σ over, not the
subject the report is about*:

| grain | the report folded over it | why it is not one of the others |
|---|---|---|
| a STATUS / CATEGORY bucket of the ledger | `/commcalc/asset`'s five cards | the endpoint serves no device rows at all; the By-Status and By-Category tables ARE its rows, and two of its cards are folded over different ones of the two |
| a STORE × CATEGORY aggregate of the ledger | `/commcalc/asset/dashboard` | `asset_charges_summary` is a Postgres aggregate and the endpoint is totals-only by design — these are the only rows that exist |
| a STORE's unsold exposure | `/commcalc/asset/on-inventory` | money owed, in aging bands measured as of today |
| a STORE on ONE billing Friday | `/commcalc/asset/owed-weekly` | the population is the devices billing that Friday, nothing else |
| a STORE compared between TWO inventories | `/commcalc/asset/inventory-recon` | a disagreement in UNITS, with two sides and therefore two possible provenances |
| an inter-store LOAN / a weekly PayGo BATCH | `/commcalc/asset/borrowed`, `/commcalc/asset/lending` | the financing side: neither is keyed by a store at all |

**Four of those six are keyed by a store and are still four different grains**, in three different
units. One catalogue stretched over them would have to lie about three of its reports — and the
tie-out would have said so out loud, which is how we would have found out. `harness_batch12_drilldown`
§Y6b asserts the measurement: eight catalogue row shapes, and each panel's keys really address its
own grain. **The general lesson, written down once: a shared SUBJECT is not a shared GRAIN. Count the
row a figure is summed over, not the noun in the report's title.**

**ONE MODULE, SEVEN CATALOGUES, AND WHY THAT IS NOT THE SIBLING DEFECT.** The §CORE-17.3k argument,
one subsystem further out. What these seven share is not a row shape but the thing a drill-down exists
for — *which stored relation was this device-asset figure read out of* — and there are exactly THREE
answers in the family: the distributor's unit LEDGER, the POS unit SNAPSHOT, and the financing records
the platform writes itself. Seven files would be seven answers to one question.

| What | Where | Says |
|---|---|---|
| **The one declaration** | `asset/device_asset_drilldown.py` — `ledger_catalogue`/`ledger_drilldowns`, `charges_drilldowns`, `on_inventory_catalogue`/`_drilldowns`, `owed_weekly_catalogue`/`_rows`/`_totals`/`_drilldowns`, `inventory_recon_catalogue`/`_drilldowns`, `borrowings_catalogue`/`_drilldowns`, `lending_catalogue`/`_drilldowns` | seven catalogues, three provenance answers, one "an empty report drills to nothing" rule. Every figure is the producer's own, dereferenced |
| **A report with TWO row families** | `ledger_drilldowns` | the Asset Ledger's cards are folded over its By-Status table, EXCEPT the On-Inventory card, which is folded over its By-Category table. The catalogue therefore names which family each card belongs to — the one thing a plain `tiles()` catalogue cannot express, because a panel over the wrong population is proof of a different number (§A4) |
| **WHICH SIDE of the POS comparison answered, per ROW** | `device_asset_drilldown.recon_tables` | read off the producer's own `in_asset` / `in_b2b` verdict: a store the POS file never mentioned names ONLY the ledger, a store the ledger holds no unsold device for names ONLY the snapshot, and one neither reported names **nothing**. Naming both on every row would claim the POS mentioned a store it never did (§E4–§E6, §Z9) |
| **The per-row RMA net-loss rule** | `device_asset_drilldown.rma_net_loss` + `is_rma_row`, `RMA_CATEGORY`, `RMA_SHORTFALL_TOLERANCE` | `GET /asset/charges-summary` folded this inline, so the drill-down would have had to restate its three branches — the copied-fact defect in its smallest form. It is the ONE home now and the endpoint dereferences it; it returns the RAW net, so the endpoint stays one `round` over the raw sum and the figure is byte-identical (§Z6). Same posture as `three_way_drilldown` owning the flattening its strip is folded over |
| **`GET /asset/summary`'s own On-Inventory predicate** | `device_asset_drilldown.counts_as_on_inventory`, `OPEN_STATUS` | named once so the card and its panel count the same categories by construction. Deliberately still case-SENSITIVE — see defect 3 |
| **The five device-asset table constants** | `data_lineage_registry.ASSET_LEDGER`, `POS_INVENTORY_SNAPSHOT`, `STORE_BORROWINGS`, `STORE_BORROWING_PAYMENTS`, `PAYGO_BATCHES` | only `ASSET_LEDGER` is a registered ingest feed; the rest are the `DISCREPANCY_SNAPSHOT` shape — name constants for relations the platform writes itself. **Naming a fact is half the fix:** the pre-existing `asset_ledger` and `vip_paygo_payments` literals in six registry maps were re-keyed to the constants in the SAME commit, which is what `harness_feed_watchdog` §F8 requires (52/0, no value changed) |
| **The endpoints** | `GET /asset/summary`, `/asset/charges-summary`, `/asset/on-inventory-by-store`, `/asset/owed-weekly`, `/asset/inventory-recon`, `/asset/borrowings` → `drilldown`; `GET /commcalc/vip/paygo/summary` → `drilldown` + an additive `totals.devices_lifetime` | each ATTACHES the declaration's output and folds no panel of its own (§Y9, §Y9b) |
| **One fold for a figure the CLIENT used to sum** | `device_asset_drilldown.devices_lifetime` | "Devices billed (lifetime)" was a `reduce` on the lending page, so it had no server-folded evidence at all (§CORE-17.3b). Served now, from the same `history` the response carries, by the declaration that opens it; the page's own sum is gone and the figure is identical (§Z8, §Y12) |
| **No narrowing on any of the seven** | `harness_batch12_drilldown.py` §Y11 | every filter that moves a figure on these screens is a QUERY PARAMETER. The lock FAILS THE BUILD if `lib/drill-narrow` is wired into any of them, and §Y11b proves the scan is not vacuous by finding it on a page that really is in that class |

**WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED, so nobody reads a missing link as an oversight.** Four refusals,
each one an existing ruling applied:

- **A FIGURE COMPOSED FROM TWO OTHER TILES.** The Charges Dashboard's **Total Loss** (`appeals + rma`)
  and PayGo's **Grand total** (`lifetime + open week`) serve **no key at all** — not an empty panel.
  Both halves of both open instead (§CORE-17.3h as batch 10 extended it; §B2, §Y5).
- **A LEAF.** PayGo's "Outstanding now" and "Devices on the open week" are two columns of ONE stored
  batch row with nothing under them on this report — the batch's invoice list is a different
  endpoint. Batch 10's leaf ruling (§G1).
- **A COUNT WHOSE LIST IS ON SCREEN.** The ledger's device count, the on-inventory store count, the
  recon's mismatched-store count and the borrowing count (batch 11 precedent). Likewise the
  owed-weekly device counts, which every panel row already carries as a field — the carrier-vs-pay
  rep-count precedent exactly (§C1, §D1, §E1, §F1).
- **A ROLLUP THAT ALREADY HAS A DRILL OF ITS OWN.** PayGo's By-year rows filter the weekly ledger to
  exactly their batches on click; the Asset Ledger's By-Category rows already open to their device
  rows through `GET /asset/category-detail`; the Borrowed screen's "who owes whom" and "net position
  by store" tables re-partition loans printed in full below them. A second answer beside an existing
  one is the defect, not the fix.

**AND A DIFFERENCE THAT *IS* DRILLABLE, BY THE §CORE-17.3k TEST, TWICE.** The recon's
`total_abs_diff` is Σ|ledger − POS| folded per store AND per device type and then added up, so the
rows and the figure come from different places (§E2). A loan's `outstanding` is `amount − repaid` per
loan while `GET /asset/borrowings` serves `Σamount − Σrepaid`, subtracted at the TOTAL — so that
panel's tie-out really compares the two ways of reaching the number instead of restating one of them,
and it is the one figure on this batch most likely to catch a rounding divergence rather than assert
it away (§F3).

**FIVE LIVE DEFECTS THESE REPORTS HAVE TODAY — REPORTED, NOT FIXED, AND NO FIGURE MOVED.**

1. **The Charges Dashboard's RMA tile can only ever read "0 items".** `RMA` is not one of
   `CHARGE_GROUPS`' keys, so `data.groups['rma']` is undefined and the page builds the tile as
   `{count: 0, owed: total_loss.rma}`. The dollars beside it are real. NOT fixed: putting the true
   count on the tile changes a figure the owner reads. The panel's `rows_total_count` states how many
   store-RMA rows are behind the money, which is the honest half that costs nothing (§Z10).
2. **The On-Inventory ↔ POS recon drops every ledger device whose model does not classify.**
   `_asset_oninv_by_bucket` skips a row when `inv_bucket(device_model)` returns nothing, so the ASSET
   side runs short and the gap reads as missing POS stock. Still dropped — and the count now travels
   per store (`asset_unclassified`, kept OUTSIDE `by_store` so which stores appear is unchanged) and
   is SHOWN on the drill row, counted into nothing. The figure is untouched and the reader can finally
   see the hole (§E8, §Z11, §Z11b).
3. **"On Inventory" is matched case-SENSITIVELY by `GET /asset/summary` and case-INSENSITIVELY by the
   two `ilike` reads beside it.** `counts_as_on_inventory` is the summary's own predicate, named once.
   Deliberately NOT unified: making the summary case-insensitive would move the On-Inventory card for
   any tenant whose file spells the category differently, which is a decision about a figure (§Z7b).
4. **A PayGo batch the portal reported without an amount is folded into Lifetime Billed as $0.00** —
   `float(r['amount'] or 0)`. The panel shows it WITHOUT a figure and does not count it; a null adds
   zero to a sum either way, so the figure is identical to the cent and only the row changes (§G2,
   §Z3).
5. **The POS UNIT snapshot is not a registered lineage feed while the $ side of the SAME uploaded file
   is.** `inventory_value` is watched; `b2b_inventory` is not, so the watchdog cannot tell a stale unit
   snapshot from a missing one — and the recon page already warns that the automatic Inventory Aging
   import feeds the value side and not this one. NOT fixed: registering a feed needs a lineage seed
   migration, which this read-only batch does not carry (§Z12).

**ABSENCE IS NEVER ZERO, AND A MEASURED ZERO IS A DIFFERENT ROW.** A PayGo week with no reported
amount carries no figure; a store with nothing in an aging band, a loan nobody has paid against and a
fully-reimbursed return are real measurements at $0.00 and ARE counted (§C4, §F6, §B6). §Z3 plants the
careless declaration that coerces the unpriced week to $0.00: it ties, exactly as the honest one does,
and the difference is visible only on the ROW — which is the whole argument for putting it there.

**No migration, no new table, no money moved** — seven read-only `drilldown` payloads, two additive
keys on existing producers (`totals.devices_lifetime`, `rows[].asset_unclassified`, each folded in the
same loop as the totals it accompanies), five table-name constants on the lineage registry with six
pre-existing literals re-keyed to them, and no new entry in `UNMEASURED_REASONS` at all — the one
reason this batch emits (`amount_not_recorded`) is batch 10's own.

### §CORE-17.3m A TARGET IS A DECLARED NUMBER, NOT A MEASUREMENT (2026-10-26, batch 13)

Batch 13 of the §CORE-17 audit, the TARGETS family (commission agent): **`/commcalc/targets`** (Daily
Targets), **`/commcalc/targets/accessories`** (Accessory Sales Targets),
**`/commcalc/targets/action-plan`** (Daily Action Plan), **`/commcalc/targets/my`** (My Targets, with
the DM's area roll-up) and **`/commcalc/targets/report-cards`** (Manager Report Cards, PR #420). Owed
count **64 → 59**. Declaration: `backend/app/modules/commcalc/targets_drilldown.py`. Proof:
`backend/harness_batch13_drilldown.py`, **122 checks**, §Z1–Z14 negative controls, wired into the
carrier-vocab-guard lock job.

**THE RULING THIS BATCH SETTLES.** §CORE-17.3l said a grain fixes the ROW, the UNIT and the
PROVENANCE, and that sharing a catalogue needs all three to agree. This family is where the third one
does the work on its own. The batch was handed over as *"expect fewer grains than routes — but prove
it either way"*; reading the four producers (`targets_engine.compute_scope`, `aggregate_stores`,
`GET /targets/{period}/action-plan`, `manager_report_card.build`) gives **six**:

| grain | the report folded over it | why it is not one of the others |
|---|---|---|
| a SCOPE-DAY's ACHIEVEMENT | the Daily Targets tiles, My Targets | one calendar day of one store or one rep; counts or dollars; the sales feeds — or, for a DECLARED category, the store's own daily closing |
| a SCOPE-DAY's SCHEDULED HOURS | the same two | the same row in HOURS, out of the schedule — and a day the schedule does not reach yet has NO source at all, because its hours were ESTIMATED from the scope's weekly pattern (§CORE-17.3i) |
| a STORE-MONTH's ACHIEVEMENT | the summary, the accessory tiles, the action plan's team total, a report card's roll-up | one store row of the period summary; the feeds |
| a STORE-MONTH's DECLARED TARGET | the same tiles | the same row in the same unit, and a completely different provenance: **the config row somebody typed it into** |
| a STORE-MONTH's GAP | "Remaining" on the same tiles | the same row again, naming BOTH of the above, so it can disagree with either (§CORE-17.3k) |
| a REP's COMMISSION AT RISK | the action plan | one stored commission row per rep; money; the calculated-commissions snapshot (§CORE-17.3j) |
