   tables a period's sales came from was discarded every request. Collected read-only now, as a LIST
   of metas merged by the declaration, and no figure moved.
5. **The GP `NP Target` is a CODE LITERAL for any store nobody set one for.** `get_gp_report` falls
   back to `10000.0` on the `TypeError`, so such a store displays $10,000.00 and its attainment is
   measured against a number no manager chose (§CORE-17.3m). Why that column gets no panel.
6. **The GP `−Expenses` column folds payroll-derived SALARY rows whose own record it does not name.**
   `labour_actuals.as_expense_rows` synthesises a salary row per store from that month's payroll and
   those rows enter `exp_total` beside the entered sheet's. Every row of the expenses panel whose
   store had measurable hours therefore reports a stated, countable UNTRACEABLE ORIGIN beside the
   sheet (§CORE-17.3i).
7. **The carrier keyword ladder behind the GP carrier columns has no `carrier_id` filter.** A known,
   already-reported defect, restated in context because it is what places an undeclared payment type
   into a GP money column: for a dual-affiliation org one carrier's keyword rules can classify the
   other's dollars. Not fixed here. The carrier panels say so in words when part of the period's
   money was PLACED BY A PLATFORM GUESS, asked of the §66 allowlist that is the one home for it.
8. **`sales_comparison.tally` computes `other_units` and nothing ever reads it.** Home-internet, SIM
   and unclassified device sales are counted per store "for honesty" and `build` never puts them on
   the payload, so the honesty never reaches a screen.
9. **The comparison's expense line prints 0 units** where the right answer is that an expense has no
   unit. This declaration serves no panel for those columns rather than a zero that ties against
   itself.
10. **The Retention Analysis's sale index is capped at 300,000 rows and says nothing when it
    truncates.** Every churn past the cut then reads as "no sale matched" — a data-volume limit
    wearing the clothes of a missing sale.
11. **The Retention Analysis scopes the SUBSCRIBERS to a manager's stores and the SALE INDEX to the
    whole org**, so a scoped manager can be shown another store's name and dollars on their own
    rep's churn.
12. **The Zero Sales `scopes` total mixes two grains** — `len(rows)` over store rows AND rep rows. It
    reaches the API contract and no tile, and it gets no panel.

A thirteenth, found while wiring and stated plainly: **the GP endpoint's `totals` are company-wide
and are NOT re-folded after RBAC scoping.** The panels are therefore attached AFTER the scope
filters, so a store the caller may not see is in no panel row either — and for a scoped caller the
panel and the company-wide total then disagree, which makes the shared `agreesToTheCent` gate
withhold the drill rather than show a figure about rows the caller cannot see. A drill-down must not
become a disclosure.

A fourteenth, found by this batch's own CI and reported rather than repaired: **the
`harness_inner_component_inputs.py` lock has an apostrophe blind spot in its extent parser.** It ends
a component declaration by bracket balance over `strip_noise(line)`, which treats `'` as a string
delimiter line by line — so a two-line JSX comment whose closing `*/}` shares its line with a
possessive apostrophe loses that `*/}`, the opening `{` is never matched, and the declaration's
computed extent runs to the END OF THE FILE. This batch tripped it: a drill-link note inside the
comparison page's nested `Tile` made the lock compute `Tile` as 229 lines rather than 44 and report
three `<input>`s that are nowhere inside it. Both halves were put right in this PR — the note is
reworded without possessives, and **`Tile` is hoisted to module scope**, which removes the remount
hazard the lock exists for rather than stepping around it (it closed over exactly one page value, the
drill handle, now an explicit prop; `OverTile` beside it was hoisted for the same reason). The PARSER
is REPORTED: an over-long extent can **mask** a real offender by merging two declarations exactly as
easily as it invented one here. Measured over `frontend/src` with the harness's own `strip_noise`:
**96 lines in 68 files** lose a closing `*/}` this way — 191 lines in 124 files if every
block-comment closer is counted — and **zero** nested declarations currently have a runaway extent,
so the blind spot is latent rather than active today. Not fixed here because teaching `strip_noise`
about JSX comments changes a non-ratchetable safety lock across all of those sites and would surface
genuine nested-component offenders that are other work; the same disposition batch 14 took with
`harness_carrier_vocab_guard._TABLE_FIELD`.

**NO FIGURE MOVED, PROVED FALSIFIABLY.** §G reproduces the GP page's own pre-batch fold
(`COLS_BASE.forEach(c => totals[c.key] = rows.reduce(…))`) against the panel each tile now reads,
unfiltered AND under a real market filter that drops a row, with a non-vacuity witness asserting the
row really was dropped and **every one of the seven figures really changed** (§G3). §G6 pins the
safety net through the SHARED `agreesToTheCent` gate — a panel that disagrees offers no drill and the
screen keeps its own number — and §G7/§G7b the capped-panel refusal against a REAL cap. §G8/§G9b do
the same for the three server-folded screens, including a server-side witness where one store's rows
are removed from the READ and the total, the panel's figure and its row count all move together.

**THE NEW CALLER IS REGISTERED IN THE ONE FROZEN SNAPSHOT THAT HOLDS THEM.** Asking §66's allowlist
whether a carrier dollar's placement is evidence makes this declaration the FOURTH caller of the
`carrier_dollar_component` fact, and `harness_carrier_dollar_class.py` **§K3** is an exact-equality
snapshot of that fact's callers — so the hand-written `module_graph.py` edge the graph guard demanded
is only half the registration, and the snapshot is the other half. Both are in the same commit. The
`==` is untouched, and that it still bites was MUTATION-TESTED rather than asserted: an unregistered
fifth caller is red, and **removing the fourth caller's edge to make §K3 quiet is red too**, which is
the un-wiring shortcut §19.18 exists to stop. **§K8b** is ADDED beside §K8, never substituted for it,
so `connected()` is asserted for the new caller as well. Measured at the same time, so the class
cannot cost a second CI round: **§K3 is the only exact-equality caller snapshot in the suite** — every
other harness that reads `MG.FACTS` tests membership with `in`, and the three facts this module
dereferences are `report_drilldown`, `feed_lineage` and `carrier_dollar_component`.

**No migration, no new table, no money moved** — four read-only `drilldown` keys on four endpoints,
four pages wired to the shared panel, no change to any producer's arithmetic, two registry constants
added (`SCHEDULE`, `STORE_EXPENSES`) with every existing literal copy re-keyed by object identity,
and one `sourceLabels.ts` entry. `OWES_MAX` **45 → 41**, lowered by exactly the four routes served.

### §CORE-17.3s THE CARRIER-OWES-VERSUS-CARRIER-PAID FAMILY (2026-10-26, batch 19)

**`/commcalc/expected-commission` · `/commcalc/ma-commission` · `/commcalc/recovery` ·
`/commcalc/dlar-vs-platform`** — *what did we expect the carrier to pay, what did it pay, and what
is being clawed back or is missing.* One family because all four answer that one question from four
angles, and the family has a **stated seam**: three of them are MONEY on the dealer's position
against the carrier, while the fourth is the **cell COUNT the other three's money is computed on**.
That fourth one is in the family because a reader who disbelieves a dollar figure here goes to it
next — and it keeps its **own catalogue and its own grains** rather than being forced into theirs,
because counting cells is not folding money. Declaration:
`backend/app/modules/commcalc/carrier_owed_drilldown.py`. Proof:
`backend/harness_batch19_drilldown.py`, **163 checks**, **28 mutations / negative controls**, wired
into the guard job with a paths filter naming every file it is about.

**WHAT WAS CHECKED FOR A DUPLICATE, AND WHAT WAS REUSED INSTEAD OF REBUILT.** The index was searched
for an existing mechanism serving these figures before anything was written. Found and **reused by
object identity**: `processor_money_drilldown.sales_union_tables` (the one home for "which tables did
this period's sales actually come from" — §CORE-17.3n), `data_lineage_registry` for every relation
name a panel can print, `dlar_vs_platform`'s own `GRAIN_REP` / `GRAIN_STORE` / `STATE_NOT_REPORTED`
constants, and `expected_commission.TABLE` for the approved expected-to-earned moves. Found and
**deliberately not extended**: `commission_discrepancy` and `ma-overview-recon` both reconcile
carrier money, but at the LINE and the UPLOAD grain respectively, so neither has a row list these
tiles were folded from. Found and **refused a third path**: the MA summary legs, below.

**THE GRAIN COUNT, MEASURED OFF THE PRODUCERS (§CORE-17.3l).** Reading
`sale_installment_engine.compute_sale_installments`, the MA roll-up in `commcalc/router.py`,
`recovery.engine.build_recovery_ledger` + `bucket_totals` and `dlar_vs_platform.summarize` gives
**NINE** grains in **FOUR** row shapes, because a grain fixes the ROW, the UNIT **and** the
PROVENANCE:

| the grain | the row | why it is its own grain |
|---|---|---|
| an INSTALLMENT MONTH's EARNED | one month of one sale's ladder | money, out of whichever relation the PRODUCER'S OWN GATE says proved it — the residual report, the commission statement, the statement ∪ the daily transactions, or nothing nameable at all |
| an INSTALLMENT MONTH's EXPECTED | the SAME row | the same unit, separated **ONLY by provenance** (§CORE-17.3n): what the LADDER DECLARES, read out of the installment schedule, with no carrier evidence involved at all |
| an INSTALLMENT MONTH's PROMOTED | the same row again | the same unit and the APPROVED MOVE — a person's decision, with the approver's name on it, out of the promote ledger |
| a PROCESSOR ACCOUNT's STATEMENT MONEY | one merchant account on the roll-up | money, out of the commission statement's own named component columns. THREE figures on it — total payable, rebates and spiffs — one fold differing only in which columns hold the figure |
| a PROCESSOR ACCOUNT's ACTIVATIONS | the SAME row | a different UNIT over the same provenance (§CORE-17.3l) |
| a PROCESSOR ACCOUNT's AIRTIME MARGIN | the same row a third time | the same unit as the money and a provenance that is the DAILY TRANSACTION FEED ALONE — never the statement (§CORE-17.3n) |
| a RECOVERY ROW's OWED DOLLARS | one denied appeal, one device | money, out of the appeal ledger ∪ whichever evidence relation that row itself cites. FOUR figures, one per bucket, each counting only its own |
| a RECOVERY ROW's DEVICE COUNT | the SAME row | the same provenance, a different UNIT (§CORE-17.3l) |
| an ENTITY COMPARISON's CELLS | one rep or one door | count, out of the carrier activity report at its own grain ∪ whichever platform sales relations the period's union actually read. FOUR figures — compared, differing, undecidable, unattributed |

The harness MEASURES those triples off the panels and compares them **as a set**, never as a count
(§H1) — and §H1b states the two accidents that make nine-for-nine a coincidence rather than leaning
on it: expected-in-window and not-yet-earned share a triple outright because they are separated at
the ROW, while `earned`'s provenance in that fixture is a UNION because a person promoted one month
of it. §H1c shows the gate alone gives the single-relation triple where nobody promoted anything.

**THE SUBTRACTION RULING, APPLIED BOTH WAYS IN ONE BATCH (§CORE-17.3k).**
`compute_sale_installments` decides `expected_in_window and not paid_gate_met` **per ledger row**
and the header is Σ of those rows — so **Expected, not yet earned DRILLS**, and its panel is a real
fold rather than one total minus another. **The same ruling goes the other way on the comparison:**
its `Agree` is `cells_compared − cells_differing` and its `Attributed` is
`cells_differing − cells_unattributed − cells_undecidable`, both taken at the TOTAL, so **neither
gets a panel** — and every figure they are composed of does, **including `cells_differing`, which
has no tile anywhere on that page** and is offered as a link beside them. A figure with no tile is
still a figure a reader needs.

**THE §CORE-17.3o CALL, DECIDED PER PAGE BY READING THE PAGE, AND LOCKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.**

| route | call | why |
|---|---|---|
| `/commcalc/expected-commission` | **SERVER-FOLDED** | all four tiles read `data.totals` straight off the server; the page's `filterRows` narrows only the two TABLES (defect 9) |
| `/commcalc/ma-commission` | **SERVER-FOLDED** | its account and rep pickers are QUERY PARAMETERS, so the server folds again and every panel follows its tile by construction |
| `/commcalc/recovery` | **SERVER-FOLDED** | its bucket figures are the server's own over EVERY row, and the table below is a `status` query parameter |
| `/commcalc/dlar-vs-platform` | **SERVER-FOLDED** | its five tiles read `data.summary` while `filterRows` narrows only the table (defect 10) |

**No page in this family folds a tile in the browser, and none contains a `reduce(` at all** — §F2
asserts that directly, with §F2b as its non-vacuity witness, so "the text is absent" can never be
confused with "the scan is blind". §F1 fails the build if `narrowPanel` appears in the CODE of any
of the four (comments stripped, so each page carries the rule in its own header where somebody would
break it — §F1b), and §F1c / §F1d witness the stripper in both directions. **Narrowing the two
browser-filtered pages was considered and REFUSED:** their tiles would then disagree with panels the
screen never prints, which would HIDE defects 9 and 10 behind a figure nobody measured. The defects
are reported instead.

**AN UN-WIRING HOLE IN THE PROGRAMME'S OWN LOCKS, FOUND BY MUTATION-TESTING THEM AND CLOSED FOR
EVERY BATCH.** Every lock in this programme asserted a page renders the shared panel with
`"DrillDownPanel" in src` — **which the IMPORT alone satisfies.** Measured 2026-10-26 by deleting the
render from one of these four pages and leaving its import: `harness_batch19_drilldown.py` §F5 **and
`harness_drilldown_coverage.py` §D1 both stayed GREEN.** That is precisely the un-wiring the house
rule exists to forbid — a lock that cannot tell a wired caller from an unused import is not a lock.
Both now match the **JSX element** `<DrillDownPanel`, with §F5c as a non-vacuity witness in both
directions, and the fix went into the SHARED gate rather than only into this batch's harness, so it
holds for all **57** `shared` routes at once instead of for the batch that happened to find it. All
57 pass the stricter match, so no earlier batch was relying on an import.

**A DESIGN FIX, WITH ITS OTHER HALF.** The two CARRIER ACTIVITY REPORTS were spelled as LITERALS in
**five** places inside `data_lineage_registry.py` itself and named by no constant. They are now
`DLAR_REP` and `DLAR_STORE`, and **all five copies were re-keyed in the same commit**, asserted by
**object identity** and not equal text. §A3 fails the build if either name is ever spelled more than
once or anywhere but on its own constant's definition line — one home means ONE copy, not zero — and
§A3b is its non-vacuity witness in both directions. The **approved expected-to-earned moves** were
deliberately **NOT** made a registry constant: `expected_commission.TABLE` is already that fact's one
home, so a constant here would be the second copy the registry exists to prevent. That reasoning is
written INTO the registry beside where the constant would have gone, so the next reader does not
re-derive it. Writing the registry without wiring the callers to it is not a fix at all (§19.18).

**A FOLD MOVED TO ITS ONE HOME.** The recovery bucket totals were folded INLINE in
`recovery/router.ledger()`, where a drill-down declaration could not reach them without re-deriving
the same arithmetic — a sibling derivation, and the duplicate defect the index rules forbid. The
fold moved **byte-for-byte** into `recovery.engine.bucket_totals`, the router now calls it, and the
declaration is driven through that same function in §D. The figure and its explanation read the
same code.

**WHAT GETS NO PANEL, AND WHICH RULING SAYS SO.** Every rate, coverage and attainment percentage —
the expected-commission coverage rates, the MA per-unit averages, the recovery rate, every variance
percentage and match rate on the comparison — because a rate gets no panel and the two figures each
one divides are offered instead (§CORE-17.3h). The comparison's `Agree` and `Attributed` (the
subtract-at-the-TOTAL ruling above). **The MA SUMMARY LEGS**, because they are computed org-wide from
the component totals and there is no per-account figure to fold — the leg split and the account
roll-up are already two paths answering one question, and this batch declined to add a third. The
**stale and redundant promote counts** (they count rows of a CONFIG table against the ledger, not
money this report folded). The **activation MIX breakdowns** (a re-partition of the activation count
whose own tile already drills — the batch-16 `by_vendor` refusal). The **per-cell dollar deltas** on
the comparison (that report counts cells; it folds no money) and its **rebuttal text counts** (words,
not money).

**ABSENCE IS NEVER ZERO.** An account the AIRTIME FEED named but the commission statement carries no
line for is SHOWN WITHOUT A FIGURE, in the producer's own new vocabulary
(`no_commission_rows_for_account`), rather than as a fabricated $0.00 — and **no figure moved by a
cent**, because that row contributed 0.00 to the producer's total and contributes 0.00 here; only the
ROW changes, from a measured zero into a stated blank, which is the entire argument for putting it
there. A month proved by the sale itself names **NO RELATION AT ALL** and says so countably
(§CORE-17.3i): the engine's sale read does not record which of the two sales relations answered
(defect 1), and a stated untraceable origin is the honest answer rather than a guessed feed. **A ZERO
OVER ROWS THAT ALL CARRY NO FIGURE IS THE ABSENCE OF A FIGURE:** the promoted tile on a period nobody
promoted anything in, and any recovery bucket nothing landed in, are served **NO PANEL**, because a
$0.00 over zero counted rows ties trivially (0 == 0, True) and would read as a measurement (§B20,
§B20b, §D14). An empty report drills to nothing.

**A PANEL CANNOT DISCLOSE WHAT THE REPORT DOES NOT, BY CONSTRUCTION.** Every entry point takes
**only the endpoint's own response** — no client, no org id, no second read — so a panel can only
fold rows the caller was already served. The `drilldown` key is attached AFTER any scope filter, and
on the comparison that means after `in_keyset`. This matters here because three of the four endpoints
turn out to carry **no per-store RBAC scope at all** (defect 11), which is REPORTED rather than
papered over: the panels disclose exactly what the reports already do, and the remedy is the scope,
not the panel.

**FOURTEEN LIVE DEFECTS, ALL REPORTED, NONE FIXED, NO FIGURE MOVED.** Each carries a regression check
in the harness. The ones the drill-downs turn on: **(1)** `commission_engine._read_sales` returns
`_page("raw_sales") or _page("daily_sales_feed")` and **discards which of the two answered**, so an
activation-gated month cannot name its origin; **(2)** the expected-commission endpoint was dropping
the producer's own `gate_source`, which is the only way to tell a statement-gated chain from a
statement-∪-transactions one — collected read-only now; **(9)** and **(10)** the two pages that filter
in the browser while their tiles keep reading server totals; **(11)** the missing per-store scope on
three of the four; **(14)** the recovery endpoint caps its row list at 2000 with no flag saying it
truncated, so a large period's TABLE is short while its tiles are whole — the panels are fed the
UNCAPPED row set the buckets came from, which is what makes the tie-out real and leaves the cap
visible instead of hiding it behind a short panel. The full list, each with the harness check that
reproduces it, is in the declaration's module docstring.

**A NOTE ON §K3, WHICH COST BATCH 18 A CI ROUND.** `harness_carrier_dollar_class.py` §K3 is an
exact-equality snapshot of the `carrier_dollar_component` fact's callers, so a module that asks
`component_is_evidence` must be added to it in the SAME commit. This declaration **deliberately does
not ask it**: that allowlist is about the ePay keyword ladder's basis, while the MA sheet's components
are the feed's own named columns, so dereferencing it would have been a borrowed fact rather than a
shared one. §K3 therefore needed no edit — verified by re-grepping for exact-equality caller
snapshots over the two facts this module does dereference (`report_drilldown`, `feed_lineage`), of
which there are none.

**THE APPEAL-RECOVERY ENDPOINTS, REGISTERED HERE** — the `recovery` module has no section of its
own (it is listed under MODULES-WITHOUT-SECTION, and that remains a real gap this batch does not
close), so the route this batch serves is registered in full here.

| route | producer | what it serves |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /recovery/ledger?status=` | `recovery/router.ledger` → `recovery.engine.build_recovery_ledger` + `recovery.engine.bucket_totals` | the denied appeals whose line later paid or activated, bucketed into recoverable / expired / not recoverable / needs payment data, with each bucket's device count and owed dollars. **DRILL-DOWN §CORE-17.3s:** all six bucket figures open to the APPEAL LEDGER ROWS behind them — a bucket's dollars and its devices are ONE row shape and ONE provenance separated only by UNIT (§CORE-17.3l) — and each row names the appeal ledger plus whichever evidence relation the row itself cites, with a source the registry does not know naming NOTHING rather than putting an identifier on an owner's screen. A bucket nothing landed in is served NO panel (§CORE-17.3i). The bucket fold MOVED out of this router into `engine.bucket_totals` in the same PR so the figure and its explanation read the same code. Server-folded (`status` is a query parameter). Declaration `commcalc/carrier_owed_drilldown.py` (`recovery_drilldowns`), proof `harness_batch19_drilldown.py` §D. Defect found and REPORTED: the endpoint caps `rows` at 2000 with no flag saying it truncated, so a large period's TABLE is short while its tiles are whole — the panels are fed the UNCAPPED row set the buckets came from |

**No migration, no new table, no money moved** — four read-only `drilldown` keys on four endpoints,
four pages wired to the shared panel, one inline fold moved to its one home with its arithmetic
unchanged, two registry constants added (`DLAR_REP`, `DLAR_STORE`) with all five existing literal
copies re-keyed by object identity, one new `UNMEASURED_REASONS` entry and three `sourceLabels.ts`
entries. Each endpoint's payload was **deep-compared before and after the declaration runs over it
and is byte-identical** (§G1–§G4). `OWES_MAX` **41 → 37**, lowered by exactly the four routes served.

### §CORE-17.3t THE PERFORMANCE-AND-COACHING FAMILY (2026-10-26, batch 20)

**`/commcalc/productivity` · `/commcalc/coaching` · `/commcalc/atu-opportunity` ·
`/commcalc/kpi-failing`** — *how are reps and stores performing, and who needs coaching.* One family
because all four answer that one question from four angles, and they are read in sequence: a manager
opens **Failing KPIs** to see which door or person is below target, **Coaching** to see what the
miss costs that person in their own pay, **Productivity** for the output-per-hour context that says
whether the miss is effort or traffic, and **Autopay Opportunity** for the one concrete counter
behaviour to change. The family has a **stated seam**: Autopay is the one worth challenging, because
its subject is a CUSTOMER rather than a person being coached — it is in the family because it is the
answer to "so what do I tell them to do", and it keeps **its own catalogue and its own grain** (a
store row out of a transaction-grain read) rather than being forced into the others'. Declaration:
`backend/app/modules/commcalc/performance_coaching_drilldown.py`. Proof:
`backend/harness_batch20_drilldown.py`, **165 checks**, **23 mutations /
negative controls**, wired into the guard job with a paths filter naming every file it is about.

**THIS IS THE SHARPEST VERSION OF THE OWNER'S ASK IN THE PROGRAMME SO FAR**, and it is why the
ABSENCES carry more weight here than anywhere else. Every other family explains money to the person
who banked it; this one explains a figure that is **about a named employee, to their manager, before
a conversation**. A rep nobody clocked, a KPI the carrier never published and a pay breakdown the
run never itemised must each read as a **blank with a reason** — because as a zero they are an
accusation with nothing behind it.

**WHAT WAS CHECKED FOR A DUPLICATE, AND WHAT WAS REUSED INSTEAD OF REBUILT.** The index was searched
for an existing mechanism serving these figures before anything was written. Found and **reused by
object identity**: `processor_money_drilldown.sales_union_tables` (the one home for "which tables did
this period's sales actually come from" — §CORE-17.3n/§CORE-17.3r), `data_lineage_registry` for every
relation name a panel can print, `carrier_pay_drilldown.REP_COMMISSIONS` for the calculated pay
snapshot (batch 11 named it; a registry constant for it would be a second copy), `kpi_failing`'s own
`GRAIN_STORE` / `GRAIN_REP`, and `payout_slice_evidence.is_evidence` / `BASIS_FIELD` for "is this
stored pay breakdown a figure at all" (§COMMCALC-09). Found and **deliberately not extended**:
`exec_month_drilldown` (§CORE-17.3q) folds a rep row too, but at the ATTRIBUTION-POINT grain its own
filter bar works at, and `carrier_owed_drilldown` (§CORE-17.3s) folds an employee pay row at the
MONEY grain of the carrier's position — neither has the row list these tiles were folded from.
Found and **refused a second path**: the port-in rate, below.

**TWO SETTLED FACTS IN THIS NEIGHBOURHOOD WERE DEREFERENCED, NOT RE-DERIVED.** `kpi_failing` is the
ONE home for the carrier's port-in rate — `raw_dlar_store.port_pct` is port-**INS** and is ALREADY a
percent, and a past defect read it as a port-out rate and multiplied it by 100 (§62). This batch
reads **no KPI column at all**: every per-metric verdict is the classifier's own `failing` / `met` /
`no_data` list, read off the row, so that reading is not re-spelled anywhere. And the org tree
resolves a district manager for only a minority of stores, so `UNMEASURED_REASONS` carries
`no_dm_in_org_tree` for DM-keyed figures — **no figure in these four reports is DM-keyed** (the
store-upkeep index is an average and is refused under §CORE-17.3h), so the reason is correctly
unused here rather than forced onto a row it does not describe.

**THE GRAIN COUNT, MEASURED OFF THE PRODUCERS (§CORE-17.3l).** Driving
`productivity.compute_productivity`, the coaching fold in `commcalc/router.py` (reproduced AND pinned
to the router's own source text, because FastAPI cannot be imported in a DB-free harness),
`atu_opportunity.fold_transactions` / `summarize` / `by_store` and `kpi_failing.store_rows` /
`rep_rows` / `summarize` gives **TWELVE** grains in **FOUR** row shapes, because a grain fixes the
ROW, the UNIT **and** the PROVENANCE:

| the grain | the row | why it is its own grain |
|---|---|---|
| an EMPLOYEE-AT-A-STORE's BOXES | one employee under one store | count, out of whichever sales relations the period's union actually read |
| an EMPLOYEE-AT-A-STORE's ACCESSORY DOLLARS | the SAME row | the same provenance, a different UNIT (§CORE-17.3l) |
| an EMPLOYEE-AT-A-STORE's HOURS | the same row again | **`UNIT_HOURS` — the programme's first caller** — and a provenance that is the TIME CLOCK ALONE, in another SCHEMA, never the schedule, which records an intention rather than an hour |
| the SAME row with a MISSING PUNCH | the same row | the same unit over a provenance that is **nothing nameable**: a missing punch is an absence, not a row in a relation (§CORE-17.3i) |
| an EMPLOYEE PAY ROW's SHORTFALL | one employee on the coaching card | money, out of the calculated pay snapshot |
| an EMPLOYEE PAY ROW's POSTED PENALTY | the SAME row | the same unit, separated **ONLY by provenance** (§CORE-17.3n): the recorded penalty ledger |
| an EMPLOYEE PAY ROW's CHARGEBACK FILE | the same row again | the same unit again, and a provenance that is **NOTHING NAMEABLE AT ALL** — no migration in this repository creates that relation (defect 4), stated and counted |
| an EMPLOYEE PAY ROW's MONEY ON THE TABLE | the same row | the same unit over a provenance that is the UNION of all three above, because that figure is their sum |
| an EMPLOYEE PAY ROW's TIER STATE | the same row | a COUNT over the same snapshot — the people below full tier, with the people at full tier SHOWN beside them and deliberately not counted |
| a STORE ROW's CARD ACTIVATIONS | one store on the autopay table | count, out of the transaction-grain sales read |
| a STORE ROW's UNCONVERTED RECHARGE | the SAME row | the same provenance, a different UNIT (§CORE-17.3l) |
| a STORE-KPI ROW's FAILING COUNT | one door on the failing-KPI report | count, out of the carrier's own per-door report — never pooled with the employee grain below it, which is a count in the same unit out of the calculated snapshot (§CORE-17.3n) |

The harness MEASURES those triples off the panels and compares them **as a set**, never as a count
(§H1), and prints every triple it measured. §H1b states the collapse that makes twelve-for-twelve
honest rather than lucky: a failing-EMPLOYEE count and a below-tier count are **one grain** — both a
COUNT over an employee pay row out of the same snapshot — so the set holds one triple for the two
figures. §H1c and §H1d are the two real splits: three units on one employee-at-a-store row, and
three provenances on one employee pay row in ONE unit.

**THE §CORE-17.3o CALL, DECIDED PER PAGE BY READING THE PAGE, AND SETTLED BOTH WAYS INSIDE ONE
FAMILY.** This is the first batch where the same family answers it both ways, which is the clearest
statement yet that the call is about the PAGE and not about the report:

| route | call | why |
|---|---|---|
| `/commcalc/coaching` | **NARROWED** | its filter bar narrows `reps` in the browser and every tile is a `reduce(` over the survivors, so a server-folded panel would explain a figure the screen is not showing |
| `/commcalc/kpi-failing` | **NARROWED** | the same: its two headline counts and its whole by-metric block are folded in the browser from the filtered rows |
| `/commcalc/productivity` | **SERVER-FOLDED** | every filter is a QUERY PARAMETER, so the server folds again and each panel follows its tile by construction |
| `/commcalc/atu-opportunity` | **SERVER-FOLDED** | the same — the store, market and period selections are all sent to the endpoint |

§F1 fails the build if `narrowPanel` is absent from either narrowed page's CODE, §F1b fails it if it
appears in either server-folded page's code (comments stripped, so each page can carry the rule in
its own header where somebody would break it), and §F1c / §F1d witness the stripper in both
directions. §F2 / §F2b assert the same split by the pages' **actual folds** — a `reduce(` in each
narrowed page and none in either server-folded one — so the decision is checked against what the
code does and not only against what it imports. §F3 asserts each narrowed tile is read OFF its
narrowed panel through the shared `agreesToTheCent` gate, rather than the page keeping two numbers
and hoping.

**WHAT GETS NO PANEL, AND WHICH RULING SAYS SO. THIS FAMILY REFUSES MORE THAN ANY BEFORE IT**,
because performance reporting is mostly rates — and every refusal names the figures it offers
instead:

- **Every rate, index and score** (§CORE-17.3h): boxes per hour, accessory dollars per hour and the
  vs-store indices on Productivity (rates over rates), the stack-ranking and performance-review
  SCORES on its other two tabs (weighted averages of attainments), the tier percentage and the
  KPIs-met fraction on Coaching, and every attach percentage on Autopay. The two figures each one
  divides ARE served, which is the whole content of the refusal.
- **The failing-CELL count** (§CORE-17.3k): it adds store failing counts to employee failing counts,
  so there is no one row list it was folded from — the batch-18 `scopes` and batch-19 `entities`
  precedent. **Both halves of it are served** as the two panels above.
- **Autopay's three customer counts**: they are per MOBILE NUMBER and the per-store table carries
  none, so they have no row list on that payload at all (defect 6). Only ~38% of rows carry an MDN,
  which the producer states itself.
- **Autopay's two carry figures, its annualised figure and its customer saving** (§CORE-17.3m): each
  is this fold multiplied by a rate somebody typed into an assumptions box, and one of them has **no
  rows at all** because its base is hand-entered — those recharges never reach the POS export, which
  the producer says in its own `totals_measurable` note. A figure composed of a hand-typed number
  cannot state its provenance honestly.
- **The two row-count denominators** on Failing KPIs (the panels state the row count in their own
  headers) and **"worst KPI"**, which is a LABEL and not a measurement.
- **Any figure whose every row would be shown without a number**, and **a $0.00 or a 0 over zero
  counted rows**: a store nobody was clocked at gets NO hours panel while its two sales panels are
  still served, a period the chargeback file names nobody in gets no panel, and a metric nothing is
  failing gets none — because each would tie 0 against 0 (True) and read as a measurement.
  **A NON-ZERO figure over no counted rows is the opposite case and KEEPS its panel**, so the
  tie-out publishes the disagreement instead of the report hiding it (§E7).

**ABSENCE IS NEVER ZERO, FOUR TIMES.** An employee with sales and **no closed punch** is shown
WITHOUT an hours figure, names NO relation and is not counted, in a new vocabulary entry
(`no_time_clock_punches`) whose own words say the blank is a missing punch and never a person who
worked no hours. A door or employee the carrier **published no value for** is shown without a figure
(`kpi_not_reported`) — while one that **MET** the metric is a measured zero marked not counted,
because the two must never read alike. An employee whose pay breakdown the run **never itemised** is
withheld in `payout_slice_evidence`'s own basis word, asked of that home rather than inferred from
the stored column (§CORE-17.3j). An employee the chargeback file carries **no line for** is shown
without a figure, while one it carries a wholly non-deducting line for is a measured zero — the file
named them, and that is a different fact. **In every case no figure moved by a cent**: each of those
rows contributed 0.00 to the producer's own total and contributes 0.00 here. Only the ROW changes,
from a measured zero into a stated blank, which is the entire argument for putting it there.

**A DESIGN FIX, WITH ITS OTHER HALF, AND ITS SCOPE WRITTEN DOWN.** A figure that is output PER HOUR
WORKED has to name the relation an hour came out of, and `timelog` was spelled as a LITERAL in
`account/liabilities_drilldown.TIMELOG` with no constant anywhere. It is now
`data_lineage_registry.TIME_CLOCK`, and **that copy was re-keyed in the same commit**, asserted by
**object identity** and not equal text. §A3c fails the build if the literal reappears in **any**
drill-down declaration or lineage registry in the backend, with §A3d as its non-vacuity witness. The
constant's **SCOPE is stated in its own comment**, exactly as `STORE_EXPENSES` has carried since
batch 18: it is the one home for the PROVENANCE NAME, and deliberately NOT a rename of the forty-odd
PostgREST `.table("timelog")` reads, of `storeops/payroll_evidence.PUNCH_TABLE` (a constant whose
only use is such a read), of `core/scope.WORKED_AT_SOURCES` (its own table/column/soft-delete
registry, with its own lock) or of the `source_table="timelog"` audit arguments — a read or a write
is an I/O call, not a second statement about where a figure came from, re-pointing them is a payroll
change rather than a drill-down one, and **payroll work is the payroll-workforce agent's**. `shifts`
has coexisted with `WORKED_AT_SOURCES` on exactly these terms for two batches. The **rep-pay
snapshot** was deliberately NOT made a registry constant: `carrier_pay_drilldown.REP_COMMISSIONS` is
already its one home, so a constant here would be the second copy the registry exists to prevent —
and that reasoning is written INTO the registry beside where it would have gone.

**ONE HOME EXTENDED RATHER THAN FORKED.** `processor_money_drilldown.sales_union_tables` answers
"which tables did this period's sales actually come from" off the read's own meta, but it recognised
only the per-DAY union's way of saying the second relation contributed. The TRANSACTION-grain union
says it with `other_only_rows`, so a naive reading would have under-reported Autopay's provenance —
and the tempting fix was a second resolver for the transaction grain, which is the duplicate defect
the index rules forbid. **The one home was extended** to recognise both, a day meta carries no such
key so **every existing caller is byte-identical** (§A2b, with §A2c as the control that the new key
is not a free pass), and batches 14 / 16 / 17 / 18 / 19 were re-run green over the change.

**A PANEL CANNOT DISCLOSE WHAT THE REPORT DOES NOT, BY CONSTRUCTION.** Every entry point takes
**only the endpoint's own response** — no client, no org id, no second read — so a panel can only
fold rows the caller was already served. The `drilldown` key is attached AFTER everything each
endpoint filters: after `in_keyset` on Failing KPIs, and after the self-scope narrowing on the
coaching card. `/commcalc/productivity` turns out to carry **no per-store RBAC scope at all**
(defect 1), which is REPORTED rather than papered over: the panel discloses exactly what the report
already does, and the remedy is the scope, not the panel.

**ELEVEN LIVE DEFECTS, ALL REPORTED, NONE FIXED, NO FIGURE MOVED.** Each carries a regression check in
the harness. The ones the drill-downs turn on: **(1)** `/productivity` has no per-store scope
filter; **(2)** a productivity rep row carries no transaction count, so "sold nothing" and "the
sales union never named them" cannot be told apart and the row is counted exactly as the producer
counted it, with the note saying so; **(3)** `no_hours` cannot tell a missing punch from a genuine
zero either; **(4)** `chargeback_items` is created by **no migration in this repository**, so every
row of that panel reports a stated, countable UNTRACEABLE ORIGIN rather than a guessed feed, and it
has no `sourceLabels.ts` entry to give it a plain name (§CORE-17.3i, the batch-17
`exec_month_drilldown` precedent); **(5)** an ops-chargeback row's own lines need not sum to the
capped deduction the total is made of, so the panel follows the figure the total is Σ of and says so
in its note; **(6)** autopay's customer figures are on a basis the per-store table does not carry;
**(7)** `/atu-opportunity` was **discarding the provenance its own sales read returns** — carried
read-only now, with §D11b showing what that cost (an untraceable origin instead of a named feed);
**(8)** `failing_cells` mixes two row shapes; **(9)** the kpi-failing page re-derives the server's
own by-metric fold; **(10)** the coaching page re-derives "below full tier" with its own `1.0`
threshold, so the declaration reads the verdict the handler now states on each row and holds no
threshold of its own (§A9c). The full list, each with the harness check that reproduces it, is in
the declaration's module docstring. And **(11)**, which is **not this family's defect** and is
recorded here only because this batch's extension of `sales_union_tables` is what makes it matter
(found in review of this PR): `router._sales_rows_union_txn_range` builds its meta by **summing only
the numeric keys and drops `primary` and `other`**, which are the first two things that resolver
reads — so a RANGE read names **no source at all**, however many rows it returned. It is **latent
today**: its one caller, `/commcalc/tax-collected`, binds the meta and discards it, the same shape as
defect 7 above and as batch 18's zero-sales finding, so nothing is wrong on a screen. But
`/commcalc/tax-collected` is one of the **33 routes still owing** a drill-down, so the batch that
wires it would declare a silently empty provenance and might reach for a resolver of its own. **The
fix, for that batch:** carry `primary` and `other` through the range meta — ONE line, in the ONE home
— never a sibling resolver, which is the duplicate the index rules forbid. REPORTED and deliberately
**not** fixed here: widening this PR to `/commcalc/tax-collected` would change a report nobody asked
this batch to touch.

**A NOTE ON THE EXACT-EQUALITY CALLER SNAPSHOTS.** `harness_carrier_dollar_class.py` §K3 is an
exact-equality snapshot of the `carrier_dollar_component` fact's callers, and a module that asks
`component_is_evidence` must be added to it in the SAME commit — the hole that cost batch 18 a CI
round. This declaration **does not ask it**: the evidence question here is about a stored pay
BREAKDOWN, whose one home is `payout_slice_evidence`, not about the ePay keyword ladder's basis. The
four facts this module does dereference (`report_drilldown`, `feed_lineage`, `payout_slice_evidence`,
`kpi_column_meaning`) were re-grepped for exact-equality caller snapshots of their own and have
none — their callers are checked by `harness_module_graph_guard.py` A/B/C, which was run green after
the four hand-written edges went in.

**TWO HOLES IN THIS BATCH'S OWN LOCKS, FOUND BY MUTATION-TESTING THEM BEFORE CLAIMING THEM.** Every
lock this section claims was tested by BREAKING the thing it guards and watching which check went
red. Two of them did not, in their first draft, and both were the **identifier-instead-of-the-call**
hole batch 19 found in `"DrillDownPanel" in src` — reappearing in the very checks written to carry
that rule forward:

- **§F1** asserted `"narrowPanel" in` a narrowed page's code, which **the IMPORT alone satisfies**:
  renaming the call site and leaving the import kept it green. It matches the CALL `narrowPanel(`
  now, with §F1e as a non-vacuity witness that the call scan really is stricter than the identifier
  scan.
- **§J7** asserted `"harness_batch20_drilldown.py" in` the workflow — which **the PATHS FILTER also
  satisfies**, so pointing the `run:` line at another batch kept it green. It matches the `run:`
  line itself now, exactly once.

**AND THE LINT RATCHET CAUGHT A REAL ONE ON THE PAGE, MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED.** The
failing-KPI page filled its tile figures into a plain object AFTER the `byMetric` memo had resolved,
which `react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization` refuses — and it is right: a tile whose number is
written during render after its memo settled can come to disagree with the panel it opens. Both the
headline counts and every per-metric slice are built in ONE memo beside that fold now. Measured with
`npm ci` + `npm run lint:gate` **in this container** (5583 findings against a pin of 5583 — equal, not

### §CORE-17.3u THE SALES-OUTCOME FAMILY (2026-10-26, batch 21)

**`/commcalc/peer-comparison` · `/commcalc/product-mix` · `/commcalc/spiff-impact` ·
`/commcalc/tax-collected`** — *this store sold less than its peers; show me the rows.* One family
because all four fold **ONE month of the SAME retail sales lines** through the **same union read**,
and they are read in sequence: **Peer Sales Comparison** says WHO is behind, at store grain, inside
its own traffic band; **Product Mix & Ports** says WHICH REP inside that store and on which of the
two signals; **Spiff Impact** says WHAT THAT COSTS the store in carrier dollars and in profit. The
family has a **stated seam**: **Tax Collected** is the one worth challenging, because its subject is
a TAX AUTHORITY rather than a store being coached. It is in the family because it is the same retail
lines folded a fourth way — per day and per tender — and because it is the one of the four whose
figures reach the **financial statements**; it keeps **its own catalogue and its own two row
shapes** (a store row, and that store's DAY rows) rather than being forced into the others'. It is
also the report batch 20 handed forward: its defect 11 was that a RANGE read could name no relation
at all, and this batch is the one that had to fix it to serve this report honestly. Declaration:
`backend/app/modules/commcalc/sales_outcome_drilldown.py`. Proof:
`backend/harness_batch21_drilldown.py`, **156 checks**, **24 mutations / negative
controls**, wired into the guard job with a paths filter naming every file it is about.

**WHY THE ABSENCES CARRY THE WEIGHT HERE.** Every figure in this family is an **accusation about a
store or a person**: behind your peers, low on both signals, not earning this spiff. So the four
shapes of "we cannot answer that" must each read as a **blank with a reason** rather than a zero
somebody gets coached on. A store **alone in its traffic band** has nobody to be behind — being
alone in a band is not a result, and a gap invented from one store would be an accusation with no
peer behind it. A rep **below the mix report's own box floor** reaches no verdict at all and is shown
without one rather than counted as having passed. A store with **no stored P&L** has no profit to
lift. A sales line with **no date** is in its store's tax total and in none of its days.

**WHAT WAS CHECKED FOR A DUPLICATE, AND WHAT WAS REUSED INSTEAD OF REBUILT.** The index was searched
for an existing mechanism serving these figures before anything was written. Found and **reused by
object identity**: `processor_money_drilldown.sales_union_tables` (the one home for "which tables did
this period's sales actually come from" — §CORE-17.3n/§CORE-17.3r/§CORE-17.3t), `data_lineage_registry`
for every relation name a panel can print, `peer_comparison`'s own `BAND_MIN_PEERS` and
`DEFAULT_GAP_METRIC`, `product_mix`'s own `MIN_BOXES_TO_RANK` and `VERDICTS`, and
`spiff_impact.SPIFF_METRIC` — so a panel's NOTE says what the producer refused, in the producer's own
numbers, and this declaration compares nothing against any of them. Found and **deliberately not
extended**: `sales_margin_drilldown` (§CORE-17.3r) folds a store row out of the same sales union, but
at the MARGIN grain its own report works at; `performance_coaching_drilldown` (§CORE-17.3t) folds an
employee-at-a-store row, which is not a rep-at-a-store row judged on two signals — neither has the
row list these tiles were folded from. Found and **refused a second path**: the range provenance
resolver, below.

**THE GRAIN COUNT, MEASURED OFF THE PRODUCERS (§CORE-17.3l).** Driving `peer_comparison.build` /
`lagging` / `with_extra_metric`, `product_mix.build`, `spiff_impact.pay_type_options` /
`default_selection` / `store_money` / `units_per_100_boxes` / `build`, and `tax_collected.aggregate`
gives **ELEVEN** grains in **FIVE** row shapes, because a grain fixes the ROW, the UNIT **and** the
PROVENANCE:

| the grain | the row | why it is its own grain |
|---|---|---|
| a PEER STORE ROW, COUNTED | one store inside one traffic band | count, out of whichever sales relations the period's union actually read — and it is the report's ONLY grain, because every other column on it is a rate, an order statistic or a distinct-transaction set |
| a REP-AT-A-STORE ROW's BOXES | one salesperson under one store | count, out of the same sales union — the drill of the grain above, which is what makes the second report a continuation of the first rather than a rival |
| a REP-AT-A-STORE ROW's ACCESSORY DOLLARS | the SAME row | the same provenance, a different UNIT (§CORE-17.3l) |
| a SPIFF STORE ROW's PAID DOLLARS | one store on the spiff table | money, out of the **carrier's own compensation statement** |
| a SPIFF STORE ROW's PAID UNITS | the SAME row | the same provenance, a different UNIT |
| a SPIFF STORE ROW's NET PROFIT | the same row again | the same unit as the dollars, separated **ONLY by provenance** (§CORE-17.3n): the **stored financial statements**, named as the SNAPSHOT they are and the trail stops there (§CORE-17.3j) |
| a SPIFF STORE ROW's LOSS STATE | the same row | a COUNT over those same statements — the stores with no profit base to lift, with a store that has no stored P&L shown beside them and deliberately not counted |
| a SPIFF STORE ROW's BOXES | the same row | a count again, over a THIRD provenance: the sales relations the month's union read |
| a TAX STORE ROW's MONEY | one store on the tax report | money, out of the sales union — the same lines the three reports above fold, read a fourth way |
| a TAX STORE ROW's TRANSACTION COUNT | the SAME row | the same provenance, a different UNIT |
| a TAX STORE DAY ROW's MONEY | one DAY under one store | the same unit and provenance over a **different ROW SHAPE**, which is why a store's own figure and the company's are two grains and not one |

The harness MEASURES those triples off the panels and compares them **as a set, for EQUALITY**, never
as a bound (§I1), and prints every triple it measured so a lost grain names itself. §I1b is the real
split that earns the spiff report its place — **three provenances on one store row** — and §I1c is
the other, two row shapes inside one report. §I2 states the overlap that makes the family a family:
the peer report's counted store row and the mix report's counted rep row come out of the **same
sales union**.

**THE §CORE-17.3o CALL, DECIDED PER PAGE BY READING THE PAGE — AND THIS BATCH SETTLES ITS HARDEST
CASE.** Batch 20 settled "narrowed or not" both ways inside one family. This one answers the question
that was still open underneath it: **what does a browser filter that narrows the TABLE but no FIGURE
mean?**

| route | call | why |
|---|---|---|
| `/commcalc/tax-collected` | **NARROWED** | it re-adds its own tender and per-store tiles with a `reduce(` over the rows it holds and filters by market in the browser, so a server-folded panel would explain a number the screen is not printing |
| `/commcalc/peer-comparison` | **SERVER-FOLDED** | every filter is a QUERY PARAMETER — month, ranked metric, band cut-offs, market — so the server folds again and each panel follows its figure by construction |
| `/commcalc/spiff-impact` | **SERVER-FOLDED** | the same: month, pay type, band cut-offs and market are all sent to the endpoint |
| `/commcalc/product-mix` | **SERVER-FOLDED**, *and it HAS a browser filter* | its "only reps low on both" checkbox narrows `shown`, the rep TABLE. It touches **no figure above the table** — the flagged count is the length of the server's own flagged list and the three medians are the server's own basis, computed over every rep either way. **A panel explains the FIGURE, not the table**, so narrowing here would make every panel disagree with the tile it was opened from |

That last row is the ruling's sharpest statement so far: the call is not "does this page filter
anything", it is "does this page fold the figure the panel explains". §G1 fails the build if
`narrowPanel(` is absent from the narrowed page's CODE, §G1b fails it if it appears in any
server-folded page's code (comments stripped, so each page can carry the rule in its own header
where somebody would break it), §G1c/§G1d witness the stripper both ways, and §G1e witnesses that
the CALL scan is stricter than the identifier scan. §G2/§G2b assert the same split by the pages'
**actual folds** — a `reduce(` in the narrowed page and none in any server-folded one — and **§G2d
asserts the product-mix filter is real** and that the page says in its own header why it is not
narrowed anyway.

**WHAT GETS NO PANEL, AND WHICH RULING SAYS SO** — every refusal names the figures it offers instead:

- **Every rate** (§CORE-17.3h): boxes per bill payment, accessory $ per box, family plan %, port
  share, cheap share, free share, the carrier's own port %, the share of the P&L line, the share of
  all carrier dollars, the profit lift, the % of revenue, the paid units per 100 boxes, and the
  effective tax rate. On the spiff page **every tile is a rate**, which is why each one links the
  MEASURED FIGURES IT DIVIDES — the line total, the profit, the revenue, the boxes.
- **Order statistics**: the band's best, median and leader, and the mix report's three median tiles.
  A median over the rows is not a fold of them, and no row list adds up to one.
- **Subtractions composed at the TOTAL** (§CORE-17.3k): the gap to band median and to band best; the
  profit lift (both sides of which drill); and **the non-taxable revenue**, whose company total is
  `revenue - taxable_revenue` out of two separately rounded sums while every store row folds its
  own — the two really can disagree, demonstrated in §F6c rather than claimed.
- **Distinct-transaction sets**: the peer report's bill payments and its new/port/BYOD/upgrade/swap/
  tablet parts. The payload itself says the parts are not a partition; a row list under them would
  be re-counting transactions the report never summed.
- **The two correlation coefficients** on the mix report, which are neither a sum nor a rate of
  these rows, and **the estate model table**, whose per-model rows the endpoint does not return.
- **Any figure whose every row would be shown without a number**, and **a $0.00 or a 0 over zero
  counted rows**: a store whose flagged count is zero because nobody there was ranked gets no panel,
  and a tender bucket nothing went through gets none — each would tie 0 against 0 and read as a
  measurement. **A NON-ZERO figure over no counted rows keeps its panel** so the tie-out publishes
  the disagreement.

**ABSENCE IS NEVER ZERO, FOUR TIMES.** A store **alone in its traffic band** is shown WITHOUT a
verdict and not counted, in a new vocabulary entry (`no_peer_in_band`) whose own words say being
alone in a band is not a result. A rep **below the ranking floor** is shown without one too
(`below_ranking_floor`) — the report reaches no verdict about them at all, and counting them as
having passed would be the same lie in the other direction. A store the statement run **never
computed** is shown without a profit figure (`not_computed`), never as one that broke even. A store
the **sales union never named** is shown without boxes (`not_recorded`). **In every case no figure
moved by a cent**: each of those rows contributed 0.00 to the producer's own total and contributes
0.00 here. Only the ROW changes, from a measured zero into a stated blank.

**TWO DESIGN FIXES, EACH WITH ITS OTHER HALF.**

1. **The stored financial statements are a registry constant.** A figure read out of a statement run
   has to name the relation it came from, and `account_statements` was spelled as a LITERAL in
   `account/statement_drilldown.SNAPSHOT` with no constant anywhere. It is now
   `data_lineage_registry.FINANCIAL_STATEMENTS`, and **that copy was re-keyed in the same commit**,
   asserted by **object identity** and not equal text (§A4b). §A5b fails the build if the literal
   reappears in **any** drill-down declaration or lineage registry in the backend, with §A5c as its
   non-vacuity witness. The constant's **SCOPE is stated in its own comment**, exactly as
   `STORE_EXPENSES` and `TIME_CLOCK` carry theirs: it is the one home for the PROVENANCE NAME, and
   deliberately NOT a rename of the PostgREST `.table("account_statements")` reads or of the
   `control_box_api` registry row — a read is an I/O call, not a second statement about where a
   figure came from, and **finance work is the finance agent's**.
2. **"Which figures can be explained at all" moved INTO the one home.** Batch 20's declaration held a
   private copy of the rule that skips a tile whose total is absent, is `None`, or is a zero no row
   counts toward. This batch needed the same rule, and a second copy is the duplicate defect the
   index rules forbid — so the rule is now `report_drilldown.served_tiles`, **batch 20's declaration
   dereferences it by identity**, and neither file holds a copy (§A3). Behaviour is byte-identical
   and batch 20's harness was re-run green (165/165) over the change.

**ONE HOME EXTENDED RATHER THAN FORKED — AND BETTER THAN THE ONE-LINE FIX PROPOSED FOR IT.**
`processor_money_drilldown.sales_union_tables` could not answer for a multi-month RANGE read at all;
batch 20 reported that as its defect 11 and proposed carrying `primary` and `other` through the range
meta. **A single carried pair would have been wrong**: two months in one range can be led by
different relations, so the carried pair would name one and silently drop the other. The range read
now carries its **per-month metas** (one line in `router._sales_rows_union_txn_range`) and the ONE
resolver **unions its own answers over them** (§A2/§A2b) — one home for all three unions rather than
a range resolver beside it. A single-month meta carries no `per_period` key at all, so **every
existing caller is byte-identical** (§A2c, with §A2d as the control that the new key is not a free
pass).

**A PANEL CANNOT DISCLOSE WHAT THE REPORT DOES NOT, BY CONSTRUCTION.** Every entry point takes
**only the endpoint's own response** — no client, no org id, no second read — so a panel can only
fold rows the caller was already served. The `drilldown` key is attached AFTER everything each
endpoint filters: after the RBAC keyset and the market filter on the peer, mix and spiff reports.
`/commcalc/tax-collected` turns out to carry **no per-store RBAC scope at all** (defect 1), which is
REPORTED rather than papered over: the panel discloses exactly what the report already does, and the
remedy is the scope, not the panel.

**SEVEN LIVE DEFECTS, ALL REPORTED, NONE FIXED, NO FIGURE MOVED.** Each carries a regression check in
the harness. **(1)** `/commcalc/tax-collected` applies **no RBAC store scope at all** (§H7).
**(2)** A sales line with **no transaction date** is counted in its store's TAX TOTAL and appears in
**none of that store's days**, so that store's DAY panel comes back **explicitly NOT TIED** and names
the difference — reproduced in §F5 rather than reconciled by a panel that drops the undated line to
make the sum work. **(3)** `/commcalc/spiff-impact` was **discarding the provenance its own sales
read returns** — the same shape as batch 20's defect 7 and batch 19's twice before that — carried
read-only now. **(4)** A RANGE sales read could name **no relation at all**; fixed in the ONE
resolver, above. **(5)** The spiff estate's profit-without-it base subtracts the **estate-wide** spiff
from only the **measured** profits, so the estate lift is understated whenever a store has spiff
dollars and no stored P&L — which is why the estate base gets no panel. **(6)** The mix report's
estate MODEL table has no row list on its payload. **(7)** The peer report's set-based columns
(bill payments, the box parts) **cannot be summed**, which the report says itself and which is why
they are refused. The full list, each with the harness check that reproduces it, is in the
declaration's module docstring. Plus the composed-total divergence under "what gets no panel" above.

**A NOTE ON THE EXACT-EQUALITY CALLER SNAPSHOTS.** `harness_carrier_dollar_class.py` §K3 is an
exact-equality snapshot of the `carrier_dollar_component` fact's callers, and a module that asks
`component_is_evidence` must be added to it in the SAME commit. This declaration **does not ask it**:
it asks no evidence question of the ePay keyword ladder at all. The five facts this module does
dereference (`report_drilldown`, `feed_lineage`, `peer_traffic_band`, `device_price_band`,
`spiff_store_impact`) were re-grepped for exact-equality caller snapshots of their own and have none
— their callers are checked by `harness_module_graph_guard.py` A/B/C, run green after the five
hand-written edges went in.

**EVERY LOCK IN THIS SECTION WAS MUTATION-TESTED BEFORE BEING CLAIMED**, one at a time, by breaking
the thing it guards and watching which check went red. The ids observed firing: **§A5b** (a second
copy of the stored statements' name reintroduced into a declaration), **§A3** (batch 20's declaration
pointed back at a private copy of `served_tiles`), **§G5** (the render deleted, the import left),
**§G1** and **§G1b** (each page's narrowing decision, broken in its own direction), **§I1** (a grain
removed from the measured set — it named itself in `missing`), **§J1b** (the pin raised), **§K4** (a
hand-written caller edge removed) and **§K7** (the guard job's `run:` line pointed at another batch
while the paths filter still named this one). The two shapes batch 20 found — an **identifier where
the CALL or the ELEMENT was meant**, and a **paths-filter mention standing in for a `run:` line** —
were written into this file's locks from the first draft as a result, with §G1e and §K7b as their

**A WEAKNESS IN THIS HARNESS WAS CAUGHT BY A LOCK THAT BELONGS TO SOMEBODY ELSE, WHICH IS THE
SYSTEM WORKING — THE SECOND BATCH RUNNING TO BE CAUGHT BY THIS ONE.**
`harness_subject_set_lock.py` **§B1** refuses a harness that asserts a bare LOWER BOUND on a set it
derived from the code, and four checks in this file's first draft did exactly that:
`len(PEER_PAYLOAD["rows"]) == 3 and len(PEER_PAYLOAD["bands"]) >= 2`, `len(_floor) >= 1`,
`len(SPIFF_PAYLOAD["rows"]) >= 3` and `len(_nosnap) >= 1`. The point of the refusal is precise: a
`>=` stays **green while a subject silently LEAVES the set and another takes its place** — the guard
goes blind and nothing says so. All four now declare the expected SUBJECTS at module level and
compare for **equality**, printing `extra` and `missing` both ways. For `_floor` and `_nosnap` that
matters doubly: the whole content of those two checks is **WHICH** rep or store was withheld, and a
count cannot say which. The replacement was mutation-tested the way batch 20's was — **one member of
the derived set swapped for a ghost at UNCHANGED SIZE**, where the old bound stays green: **§C1**
went red naming `extra=['S9'] missing=['S3']`, and **§E4** went red naming `extra=['S3']
missing=['S1']`. §C1b and §E4d are the two in-file witnesses that the equality really is stricter
than the bound it replaced. Neither `harness_subject_set_lock.py` nor
`harness_subject_set_pending.txt` was touched — that list is a ratchet pinned at 50 against a ceiling
of 50, so adding a row would be a relaxation and would fail anyway.

**AND THE LINT RATCHET WAS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED.** `node tools/eslint-ratchet.mjs` **in this
container**: 5583 findings against a pin of 5583 — equal, not below, because the gate exits 1 on an

### §CORE-17.3v THE LAST FOUR COMMCALC REPORTS (2026-10-26, batch 22)

**`/commcalc` · `/commcalc/reports` · `/commcalc/mdf-entitlement-coverage` ·
`/commcalc/activations`** — the four remaining COMMCALC report routes that print a figure a reader
can be asked to trust. **THREE declarations, not one**, and the reason is the grain rule (§CORE-17.3l
/ §CORE-17.3n) rather than taste: a **rep-per-store row of payout**, a **store-month of
entitlement** and a **store row of counted devices** are three different subjects, and one module
pretending otherwise would be three catalogues sharing nothing but a filename. The dashboard and the
Rep Breakdown tab **do** share a grain — the same stored rep-commission snapshot, folded the same
way — so they share **ONE catalogue** in one declaration; a second catalogue over that grain is the
sibling derivation the index rules forbid.

- `backend/app/modules/commcalc/rep_incentive_drilldown.py` (**new**) — `/commcalc` + `/commcalc/reports`
- `backend/app/modules/commcalc/entitlement_coverage_drilldown.py` (**new**) — `/commcalc/mdf-entitlement-coverage`
- `backend/app/modules/commcalc/activation_count_drilldown.py` (**new**) — `/commcalc/activations`

Proof: `backend/harness_batch22_drilldown.py`, **131 checks**, **21 mutations / negative controls**,
every producer driven **for real** and every grain **measured off the panels as a SET compared for
equality** (never a `>=` bound), each equality mutation-tested with a **ghost swapped in at unchanged
size** — the control that distinguishes an equality check from the bound it replaced.

**THE SIX GRAINS, MEASURED.** Three row shapes, and two of the six separated by **provenance alone**
(§CORE-17.3n):

| # | row shape | unit | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | rep × store | money | the calculated rep-commission snapshot |
| 2 | rep × store | count | the same snapshot, one UNIT apart (§CORE-17.3l) |
| 3 | store × month | count | the carrier's two payment records, unioned |
| 4 | store × month | money | the same two records — money that ARRIVED |
| 5 | store × month | money | **the same row, same unit** — what an ABSENT month was worth, priced from the rate **declared** in company commission settings |
| 6 | store × month | money | **the same row, same unit** — priced from the rate **observed** in that store's own payments, where none was declared |

Rows 5 and 6 are the sharpest §CORE-17.3n case in COMMCALC so far: identical subject, identical
unit, and the only difference is **which relation answered**, decided per row. A reader asking "what
is this gap worth" is owed that distinction, because one number is the company's own declaration and
the other is an inference from the carrier's behaviour.

**A PANEL EXPLAINS THE FIGURE, NOT THE TABLE — settled BOTH ways inside ONE catalogue**
(§CORE-17.3o). The call was made by **reading each page**, not by convention:

- `/commcalc` prints the server's own fold. Its KPI strip has no browser filter, so the panels are
  **not narrowed** and `drill-narrow` is absent from the page.
- `/commcalc/reports` folds the reader's own **rep + store filter in the browser**, so its panels
  **are narrowed** (`lib/drill-narrow`), and each figure is read **off its narrowed panel only when
  that panel agrees to the cent** — a disagreement costs the link, never the figure.

Both directions are **locked off the pages' own text**: the lock fails the build if the dashboard
grows a `narrowPanel(` call or the breakdown loses one.

**ONE FACT, ONE HOME — and the other half of it, in the same commit.** *Which payload column holds
each activation bucket's count* was a literal map inside `commcalc/router._ACT_BUCKET_FIELD`. A fold
writes a bucket under a column key and a panel has to name that figure **by the same key**, so a
second copy is a panel that silently explains the wrong number. The map moved to
`activation_bucketing.BUCKET_FIELD`, beside the bucket rank and the excluded families, **and the
router's copy was deleted in the same commit** — naming the fact is half a design fix and deleting
every copy is the half that has been skipped three times here (§19.18). New graph fact
`activation_bucket_column`, with the re-keyed router registered beside the new caller. The
calculated rep-commission snapshot is **dereferenced, not re-named**: `carrier_pay_drilldown.REP_COMMISSIONS`
stays its one home (§CORE-17.3t settled that), and batch 22 gave that fact its own graph block
(`rep_pay_snapshot`) with the five pre-existing callers named for the first time. The two carrier
payment relations and the month-end upload are dereferenced from `data_lineage_registry`; **no new
registry entry was added**, because every name needed was already in there.

**TWO LOCKS THAT READ THE FORM OF THE TREE, NOT THE FACT THEY ASSERT — found by moving the map,
fixed here.** Both are the same class as the holes batches 19–21 found, and both now fail the build
on the thing they were always about:

- `harness_activation_bucketing.py` §E7 lifted `_ACT_BUCKET_FIELD` out of `router.py` with
  `ast.literal_eval`. It therefore **silently depended on the duplicate** this batch removed, and
  crashed on an `ast.Attribute` before any check ran — killing every later step in its job. It now
  dereferences the one home, and a new **§E7b fails the build if the router ever re-declares a map
  of its own**. Mutation-tested both ways: re-inlining the literal fires §E7b, changing a value in
  the one home fires §E7. §E8–§E11 read the payload with `.get` so a mutated map lands as named
  failures instead of a `KeyError` that hides the rest of the file.
- `harness_batch21_drilldown.py` §J6 asserted `/commcalc` is still `owes`. The right intent against
  the wrong thing: the claim is that a row that batch did not serve was not quietly **deleted**, and
  a later batch **serving** it is the programme working. It now asserts the row still exists with a
  declared state, with a non-vacuity control; deleting the row fires §J6.

**THE ROUTE-COUNT TRIPWIRE.** `harness_db_resilience.py` §I0 pins the app's leaf route count
exactly, so an endpoint appearing or vanishing is noticed by a human. This batch adds **one** route
and removes none (`grep -cE '^\+.*@router\.'` = 1, `'^-.*@router\.'` = 0), so the pin advances
**1800 → 1801** with a dated note naming `GET /commcalc/commissions/{period}/drilldown`. The exact
match is untouched — not a `>=`, not a range, and `EXPECT_ROUTES` is not set in the workflow to
dodge it; §I0b, the drift-proof form, needs no re-pin.

**THE ONE RELATION THAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE FEED REGISTRY.** The subsidy panels name
`commission_org_config` — the company commission settings a human typed the entitlement rate into.
That is a **config row, not an external feed**: it has no arrival cadence, no staleness and nothing
for the feed watchdog to measure, so putting it in `data_lineage_registry` would add a row to a
population whose every check is about ingest. The posture `targets_drilldown.TARGETS` already takes,
taken again rather than re-litigated. It has a `sourceLabels.ts` entry (*company commission
settings*) so a reader sees plain words.

**ABSENCE IS NEVER ZERO.** Three shapes of "we cannot answer that", each a blank with a reason:

- A rep whose payout slices the run **never itemised** is shown **without a figure**, in
  `payout_slice_evidence`'s **own basis word**, and is **not counted** (§CORE-17.3j). A `$0.00`
  there tells a rep they earned nothing beside a total that is correct.
- A store whose **first entitled month is not declared** is never counted as missing. Its observed
  absence is its own figure on the report — evidence, not an accusation.
- A gap **nothing can price** is counted as a gap and shown without a figure, and the priced total
  comes back **explicitly NOT TIED** (`ties is None`) rather than letting a short sum look complete.

**WHAT IS REFUSED, AND WHY.**

- The dashboard's **Activations** card composes two measured halves **at the total** — each half
  drills on its own (§CORE-17.3k).
- **Reps Calculated** is a distinct count, not a fold of its rows.
- The Rep Breakdown's **Subtotal** and **Installment** footers (defects 1 and 2 below).
- The **Month range** tab: its grain is already `exec_month_drilldown`'s and a second catalogue over
  it would be the duplicate defect. Left **owed**, honestly.
- Every **per-market** panel on `/commcalc/activations` (defect 3 below).
- The duplicate **Devices counted** chip, which is the same measurement as **incl. upgrade** under a
  second label; one figure gets one panel.

**EIGHT LIVE DEFECTS — REPORTED, REPRODUCED, NOT REPAIRED** (three on the rep-incentive screens,
two on the subsidy report, three on the activations report; each is written down in its
declaration's docstring and carries a regression check in the harness driven off the real code, and
none is hidden behind a number the screen does not print). The three that change what a reader is
shown:

1. **The Rep Breakdown's Subtotal footer adds a never-recorded slice in as zero.** The page prints
   each rep's Subtotal **cell** as a dash where the run never itemised it, then totals the column
   with a plain reduce over the same rows — the arithmetic `payout_slice_evidence.sum_slice` exists
   to refuse, and which the Month-range tab already avoids. The footer keeps its own number; it is
   refused a panel and the shared gate withholds the link on any month where the two differ.
2. **The two tabs mean different things by `installment`.** The breakdown footer sums a column the
   one home does not sum at all, which is why that footer is refused as well as being composed at
   the total.
3. **The activations By-Market fold destroys every market label.** `router._blank(mk, key="market")`
   builds `{key: label, "market": "", …}` — a **dict-literal key collision**, so every market row's
   label is blanked before it is printed. No per-market panel is served, and the grouping is **not
   re-derived beside the report**: a panel cannot name a subject the report has thrown away, and
   inventing it back would be a second fold of a figure the report itself lost.

And the five the panels state rather than hide:

4. **The dashboard reads the snapshot twice** — tiles from `/commissions/{period}`, panels from
   `…/drilldown`, so a Run Calculation landing between the two requests leaves the page holding a
   figure from one read and evidence from another. The shared `agreesToTheCent` gate makes that
   VISIBLE instead of silent (the link is withheld); the real remedy is one read, which means giving
   that endpoint an object shape and breaking every existing caller.
5. **The union of the two carrier payment feeds records no tag for which side answered.**
   `_mdf_entitlement_run` keeps the MAX per store-month — correct, because the two are two reads of
   ONE payment — but a received store-month can therefore name only the relations the read drew rows
   from AT ALL. The panel says so in words rather than picking one.
6. **`GET /commcalc/mdf-entitlement-coverage` applies no per-store RBAC scope.** It takes `org_id`
   and an optional `store` and passes no keyset. The panels disclose exactly what the report already
   does, so this is REPORTED and the remedy is the scope — the same shape as §CORE-17.3u's defect 1
   on `/commcalc/tax-collected`.
7. **`incl. upgrade` and `Devices counted` are equal by construction**, on every period for every
   tenant, and the screen prints them side by side as two findings. One figure, one panel.
8. **A device whose dealer code resolves to no store is counted under a placeholder row** with a
   blank market, landing in the company total, the placeholder store row and `(no market)`. Those
   are REAL rows of this report and the panel counts them exactly as the report does, naming the
   placeholder in its own words — dropping them would make the panel disagree with the report.


**WHAT IS STILL OWED, HONESTLY** (three routes read and deliberately **not** reclassified):

- `/commcalc/custom-report` — the only figures above its rows are the shared `ReportShell` footer,
  which §CORE-17.3u already refuses as a disposition, plus a pivot whose evidence rows sit directly
  beneath it. Still `owes`, because it **is** a report and reclassifying it would hide it.
- `/commcalc/store-takeover` — a real report needing its own family (the takeover evaluation's own
  grain, §COMMCALC-03.23).
- `/commcalc/whatif` — most of a what-if is refusable by §CORE-17.3m (declared targets) and
  §CORE-17.3h (rates), but the **measured base** it starts from should drill and deserves its own
  pass rather than a corner of this one.
