### §CORE-17.3w THE FINANCE SET — WHAT WE WERE BILLED, WHAT IS ON THE SHELF, AND WHAT ARRIVED (2026-10-26, batch 23)

**`/accounts/device-purchases` · `/accounts/device-payable` · `/accounts/inventory` ·
`/accounts/recon`** — four of the eleven `/accounts/*` routes that still owed a drill-down, read
page by page and endpoint by endpoint. **THREE declarations, not one, and not four**, and the reason
is the grain rule (§CORE-17.3l / §CORE-17.3n) rather than the menu:

- `backend/app/modules/account/device_billing_drilldown.py` (**new**) — `/accounts/device-purchases`
  **and** `/accounts/device-payable`. **ONE family over two screens**: a reader works them through in
  sequence to answer ONE question — *what did we buy from the distributor, and what of it do we still
  owe?* — both fold the units the distributor billed at the same STORE ROW, and the payable report
  already **imports the voided-invoice rule from the purchases one** so the two can never disagree
  about which invoices count. A second module over that grain would be the sibling derivation the
  index rules forbid.
- `backend/app/modules/account/inventory_value_drilldown.py` (**new**) — `/accounts/inventory`, both
  of its endpoints. Deliberately **not** folded through `account/statement_drilldown.py`: that one
  owns the figure the Balance Sheet reads **out of** the stored snapshot (§CORE-17.3j), while these
  are the live per-store sources that line is computed **from**. Folding them there would claim the
  snapshot produced a figure the aging report produced.
- `backend/app/modules/account/memo_recon_drilldown.py` (**new**) — `/accounts/recon`. Deliberately
  **not** folded through `commcalc/carrier_pay_drilldown.py`: that family compares what a CARRIER
  earned against what a REP was PAID out of the commission snapshot (§CORE-17.3k); this one compares
  what the DISTRIBUTOR CREDITED against what the RESIDUAL REPORT earned, and the relations have
  nothing in common.

Proof: `backend/harness_batch23_drilldown.py`, **114 checks**, **21 mutations / negative controls**,
every importable producer driven **for real** — `device_purchases.aggregate`,
`device_payable.aggregate` through the real `store_placer` / `voided_invoice_set` /
`coverage_scan` / `coverage_state`, and `balance_sheet.device_inventory_cells` /
`inventory_recon_rows` — and the grains **measured off the panels as a SET compared for equality**
(never a `>=` bound), with a **ghost swapped in at unchanged size** as the decisive control.

**AN ACCUSATION NAMES ITS EVIDENCE** (§CORE-17.3f). `/accounts/recon` prints the word *underpaid*
beside a dollar figure per store **and writes those findings into the platform's flag stream**. It was
the one route in this set whose output is an accusation, and a figure that carries that word and
cannot name its rows is the shape §CORE-17 exists to end.

**THE FOURTEEN GRAINS, MEASURED.** Three row shapes over sixteen panels, and NINE of the fourteen
separated from a sibling by **provenance alone** (§CORE-17.3n):

| # | row shape | unit | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | store | money | the distributor's invoice **LINES** — what was billed |
| 2 | store | count | the **SERIALISED unit rows** — one row per unit that arrived with a serial, which is a different count from the quantity a line declares |
| 3 | store | money | **the same row, same unit as 1** — the serialised units judged against the **unit LEDGER**'s own per-unit amount and payment date. What was BILLED is the invoice's money; what is still OWED is the ledger's, and a reader is owed that distinction because only one of them is the invoice we were sent |
| 4 | store | count | the same two relations — the unpaid UNITS rather than their money |
| 5 | billed item | money | the invoice lines — the non-device items, under a basis the payload names itself |
| 6 | billed location | money | the invoice lines — the spend whose location no store vocabulary matched, a real row of this report |
| 7 | store | money | the **emailed value snapshot**, or **NOTHING NAMEABLE** per row — the EFFECTIVE inventory value, whose source is decided PER ROW by a precedence rule and read off the producer's own basis word |
| 8 | store | money | **the same row, same unit** — the emailed report's own per-store total |
| 9 | store | money | **the same row, same unit** — the **per-device aging rows**, the other claim about the same shelf |
| 10 | store | count | the per-device aging rows — the phones themselves |
| 11 | store | money | **BOTH**, because the per-store DELTA is a disagreement between them |
| 12 | store | money | the **scraped credit memos** — what arrived |
| 13 | store | money | **the same row, same unit** — the **residual report**, what was earned |
| 14 | store | money | **BOTH** — the per-store difference |

Grains 7–11 are the sharpest §CORE-17.3n case the finance module has reached: one store row, one
unit, and **which relation answered decided per ROW** rather than per figure — a manual override a
human typed, else the emailed snapshot, else the device rows — read off `effective_source` and never
guessed. A store with neither source is shown **without a figure** and is not counted
(§CORE-17.3i), and its origin is reported as one that **cannot be traced** rather than attributed to
a guess.

**A DIFFERENCE DRILLS WHEN IT IS FOLDED PER ROW** (§CORE-17.3k), and both of this batch's
differences are: the inventory delta and the credit-memo difference each carry their own figure on
every row, so the panel explains the figure instead of re-deriving it, and each row names BOTH
relations because the disagreement is between them.

**THE ROW THE CREDIT-MEMO REPORT'S OWN FIGURE NEEDS.** Its company-wide earned figure counts **every**
residual row, while its per-store rows count only the rows whose rep name reached a store — the
report says so itself and calls that side best-effort. A panel folded over the store rows alone would
therefore come back NOT TIED by exactly the money nobody could attribute. That money is a REAL row of
this report, already folded and already printed, so the panel carries it as **ONE MORE ROW** taken
from the payload's own `mi_unattributed` — dereferenced, never re-derived — naming the residual
report with **no store key**, because there is no store to key it on. On the difference panel the
same row is counted **NEGATIVE**, exactly as `statement_drilldown` counts the second side of the
balance sheet's imbalance. It is handed to the one home **with the other rows**, not patched onto a
built panel: editing a folded panel would put a declaration in charge of a capped list it cannot
honestly re-total. `harness_batch23_drilldown.py` §F7a proves the row is load-bearing by removing it
and measuring the shortfall against the report's own figure.

**A PANEL EXPLAINS THE FIGURE, NOT THE TABLE — settled BOTH ways, by READING each page**
(§CORE-17.3o):

- `/accounts/device-purchases` and `/accounts/device-payable` fold their own tiles in the browser
  over the rows the standard filter bar left on screen, so their store-keyed panels **are narrowed**
  (`lib/drill-narrow`) and each figure is read **off its narrowed panel only when that panel agrees
  to the cent** — a disagreement costs the link, never the figure. The figures those pages themselves
  refuse to narrow (they print `—` under a filter) keep the server's own panel, offered only while
  nothing is selected: the page's own rule honoured rather than a second one invented.
- `/accounts/inventory` and `/accounts/recon` are **server-folded and NOT narrowed**. Inventory
  Values has no store, market or period filter at all — override inputs, a connector form and a save
  — and the recon's controls are a tolerance, a recompute, an analyze and two writes. `drill-narrow`
  must not appear in either page.

Both directions are **locked off the pages' own text**: the lock fails the build if a server-folded
page grows a `narrowPanel(` call or a narrowed one loses it, and it matches the **`<DrillDownPanel`
ELEMENT** rather than the identifier, because an unused import satisfies an identifier check.

**ONE FACT, ONE HOME — and the other half of it, in the same commit.** Five relation names these
panels must say out loud were literals: the distributor's invoice **LINES** and **SERIALISED UNITS**,
its **CREDIT MEMOS**, the **emailed inventory-value snapshot** and the **same report at device
grain**. All five are now NAME constants in `commcalc/data_lineage_registry.py` (the
`DISTRIBUTOR_INVOICES` shape — none is a new ingest edge, so none joins
`INGEST_TABLES_BY_MODULE`), and **every literal copy that file itself held was deleted in the same
commit**: `inventory_value` appeared in SEVEN of its own maps and `vip_credit_memos` in one, and all
eight dereference now with string-identical values and no map changed. Naming a fact is half a design
fix; deleting every copy is the half that has been skipped three times here (§19.18).
`harness_batch23_drilldown.py` §A2 fails the build if either name is re-declared in that file.

What is **not** renamed is the PostgREST `.table("…")` / `_fetch_all(…)` reads across the finance
module: a read is not a second statement about where a FIGURE came from, and re-pointing them is a
finance-module change rather than a drill-down one — the posture `ASSET_LEDGER` keeps for its own 74
reads and `FINANCIAL_STATEMENTS` states for the statement engine's.

**AND THE BASIS VOCABULARY IS DEREFERENCED TOO, which is what stopped a false provenance.** Which
relation an inventory figure came out of is decided by the org's configured basis, and the words for
those bases live in `balance_sheet.INVENTORY_BASES`. `inventory_value_drilldown.SOURCE_RELATION` is
keyed on that vocabulary **plus the two words that are not bases** — a human's manual override, and
the grid endpoint's own older spelling of the report basis — and §E9b compares its key set against
the shared tuple for **EQUALITY**, so a new basis fails the build here instead of silently resolving
to no relation at all. One of those config words happens to read like a table name and is
deliberately NOT dereferenced from the feed registry: it is a basis, not a relation, and the relation
it maps to is the per-device aging rows.

**ONE ADDITIVE EXTENSION TO THE ONE HOME, for a fact that is genuinely per row.**
`report_drilldown.tile_panel` already took a CALLABLE for `tables`, because one store-day's
provenance differs from the next one's. It now takes one for `column` as well, for the same reason:
one store's effective value came out of the override column a person typed and the next store's out
of the **swept column of the same relation**, and a panel that named one column for both would be
wrong on half its rows. A plain string behaves exactly as before, so no existing declaration changes
and `harness_report_drilldown.py` stays at 61/61.

**WHAT IS REFUSED, AND WHY.**

- **"Devices matched to the unit ledger"** and **"per-store attribution %"** — RATES (§CORE-17.3h).
  The counts and the figures each divides are offered instead.
- **"Invoices in window"** — a DISTINCT COUNT of invoice numbers, not Σ(a field) over the report's
  rows. The store rows carry no invoice count to add up, so a panel would have to count something the
  report did not.
- **The unit-reconciliation block** on the purchases report, and **"payable including voided"**, the
  five `excluded_voided_*` figures and `distinct_device_payable_*` on the payable one — every one is
  taken at the TOTAL (§CORE-17.3k). The counted halves drill; the excluded halves are the payload's
  own per-invoice list printed directly underneath.
- **The excluded-ghost chip**, the **sweep status line**, the **status badge** (a verdict against a
  tolerance the reader chooses) and the **unmatched-rep list** — not folded figures, or already the
  rows.
- **The reconciliation tab's `effective` total** — that tab prints no such total, and a panel for a
  figure a screen does not print would be evidence for nothing.
- **A 0 over zero counted rows**, through the one home's own `served_tiles` rule: such a panel ties 0
  against 0 and reads as *"nothing was there, and here is the proof"*. A NON-zero figure over no
  counted rows KEEPS its panel so the tie-out publishes the disagreement.

**EIGHT LIVE DEFECTS — REPORTED, REPRODUCED, NOT REPAIRED.** Each is written down in its
declaration's docstring and carries a regression check driven off the real code or pinned to the
producer's own source text, and none is hidden behind a number the screen does not print.

1. **THE INVENTORY GRID'S "EFFECTIVE (ON BS)" COLUMN AND ITS TOTAL IGNORE THE ORG'S CONFIGURED
   INVENTORY BASIS, so on two of the three bases the page prints a number the Balance Sheet does not
   use.** `GET /account/inventory-values` computes `effective` inline as *manual override, else the
   swept report value*, while the Balance Sheet goes through `balance_sheet.apply_inventory_basis`,
   whose precedence is *manual, else the CONFIGURED basis, else the other source* — and under the
   `asset_ledger` basis the emailed report is not a source at all. **The same page's reconciliation
   tab prints the TRUE effective value under a column with the SAME HEADER**: two columns, one
   header, two rules, one screen. §E10 reproduces the disagreement from both sources. The panel's
   note says so in the reader's own words; the repair changes a displayed finance figure and is
   surfaced for the owner rather than slipped into a read-only drill-down PR.
2. **THAT ENDPOINT'S PER-ROW PROVENANCE IS A THIRD VOCABULARY FOR THE SAME FACT** — it writes the
   product name of the portal it swept from where the shared basis resolver writes `report`,
   `devices`, `asset_ledger` and `manual`. The declaration reads each payload's own word through one
   keyed table, so a new basis is a ROW and never a branch (RULE TWO), and a word neither endpoint
   has served resolves to NO relation and says it cannot be traced.
3. **AN UNPLACED OR SUPERSEDED AGING ROW IS EXCLUDED FROM THE CELLS AND REPORTED ONLY AS A CHIP**, so
   the device side is legitimately short of the ledger's own sum. The panels count exactly what the
   report counts and the note names the exclusion in the report's own words — a panel that quietly
   added those rows back would disagree with the figure above it.
4. **THE PURCHASES REPORT'S COMPANY ROLL-UP PRINTS ONE POPULATION TWICE.**
   `device_purchases.aggregate` emits the company-not-mapped rows under `unresolved` as the **SAME
   dict objects** it already serves in `by_store` (§C9 proves the identity), and the page renders both
   tables, so that money reads as two findings. The panels count the store population ONCE, exactly
   as the tiles do, and the unresolved table's own figures get no panel.
5. **"ALREADY PAID BY THIS DATE" IS DASHED RATHER THAN NARROWED** while the payable beside it
   narrows, although both are Σ over the same store rows — the asymmetry is the page's, not the
   producer's. The panel is offered for it only on the unfiltered view, which makes the asymmetry
   visible instead of papering over it with a narrowed figure the tile does not print.
6. **THE CREDIT-MEMO REPORT NAMES ONLY THE FIFTEEN LARGEST UNATTRIBUTED REP NAMES, with no count and
   no remainder beside them — a silent row cap on the evidence behind an accusation.** The
   unattributed TOTAL is served whole, so the panel's figure is complete and its single row carries
   that total; the note says the report names only the largest few behind it. Re-deriving the full
   list beside the report would be a second fold of a figure the report itself truncated.
7. **A CREDIT MEMO WHOSE STORE RESOLVES NOWHERE IS BUCKETED UNDER A PLACEHOLDER ROW**, so it lands in
   the company total and in that row. Those are REAL rows of this report and the panels count them
   exactly as the report does, naming the placeholder in the report's own words. Dropping them would
   make the panel disagree with the figure above it.
8. **THE FLAGS THAT REPORT ARE WRITTEN FROM A TOLERANCE A TEXT BOX ON THE SCREEN SUPPLIES.**
   `recon.sync_flags` re-runs the reconciliation with whatever tolerance the request carried, so the
   same month can be flagged differently per request. The panels explain the FIGURE and never the
   verdict, so nothing here depends on it; it is written down because a drill-down that showed the
   figure while the verdict moved underneath it would be evidence for the wrong thing.

**WHAT IS STILL OWED, HONESTLY — seven finance routes read and deliberately NOT reclassified.** Each
**is** a report, so calling it `flat` or `not_report` would hide it from the programme, which is worse
than leaving it owed. The reasons live here and **not** in the ledger, because a note on an `owes`
row reads as an excuse (the coverage gate's §C4):

- **`/accounts/analysis`** and **`/accounts/trends`** — real reports whose figures are read out of the
  stored statement snapshots and three COMMCALC-owned trend endpoints. The statement-snapshot grain is
  `account/statement_drilldown.py`'s and the month grain is `commcalc/exec_month_drilldown.py`'s, so a
  catalogue here would be a second derivation over one or both; the three trend endpoints are another
  module's surface besides. Their headline margins are rates (§CORE-17.3h) and their projection and
  valuation blocks are declared or assumed numbers (§CORE-17.3m). A pass of their own.
- **`/accounts/cost-centers`** and **`/accounts/profit-centers`** — both regroup the P&L the statement
  engine already assembled, and `/accounts/pl`'s own TypeScript drill (§4e) is the excused `own` path
  over that very grain. Serving them before that one converges would be the sibling derivation this
  programme is about; converging §4e is a PR of its own, as §CORE-17.2 already says.
- **`/accounts/royalty`** and **`/accounts/royalty/recon`** — a real family of their own (the
  franchisor's own printed report, stored as printed, against the daily sales landings). They share no
  grain with anything in this batch and deserve the whole pass rather than a corner of one.
- **`/accounts/residual-per-sub`** — a real report whose figures are a store × month MATRIX rather
  than a tile over rows, with an aggregate row that is the server's own company line when unfiltered
  and Σ(the visible stores) when filtered. That provenance switch is the interesting part and needs
  its own measurement, not a hurried catalogue.

**No migration, no new table, no money moved** — five read-only `drilldown` keys attached to existing
payloads, **no new endpoint and therefore no route-count re-pin** (`harness_db_resilience.py` §I0
stays at **1801**; `grep -cE '^\+.*@router\.'` = 0 and `'^-.*@router\.'` = 0), four pages wired to
the shared panel, **no change to any producer's arithmetic**, and one additive callable on the one
home. Each producer's payload is **deep-compared before and after the declaration runs over it and
is byte-identical** (§H1). `OWES_MAX` **25 → 21**, lowered by exactly the four routes served.

### §CORE-17.3x THE PAYROLL AND WORKFORCE SET (2026-10-26, batch 24)

**`/storeops/payroll` · `/storeops/reports` · `/storeops/hours-budget`** — three of the ten
`/storeops/*` and `/hr/*` report routes, served; the other **seven were read and deliberately left
owed**, with the reason for each written down below. **TWO declarations, not one**, and the reason is
the grain rule (§CORE-17.3l) rather than taste: a **person over a PAY PERIOD**, whose hours may come
out of the time clock, out of the schedule or out of nothing at all, is not a **store over a
WORK-WEEK**, whose hours come out of the schedule alone. The two payroll screens **do** share a grain
— the same endpoint, the same merged per-employee rows, the same four figures — so they share **ONE
catalogue**; a second over that grain would be the sibling derivation the index rules forbid.

- `backend/app/modules/storeops/payroll_hours_drilldown.py` (**new**) — `/storeops/payroll` + `/storeops/reports`
- `backend/app/modules/storeops/scheduled_hours_drilldown.py` (**new**) — `/storeops/hours-budget`

Proof: `backend/harness_batch24_drilldown.py`, **106 checks**, **16 mutations / negative
controls**,
both declarations driven **for real** and the grains **measured off the panels as a SET compared for
equality** (never a `>=` bound), the equality mutation-tested with a **ghost swapped in at unchanged
size** — the control that distinguishes an equality check from the bound it replaced.

**WHAT WAS WORKED NAMES THE TIME CLOCK; WHAT WAS PLANNED NAMES THE SCHEDULE — PER ROW, OFF THE
PRODUCER'S OWN WORD.** Batch 20 settled that an hour worked names the closed punch and never the
schedule (`UNIT_HOURS`, §CORE-17.3t). This is the report where that bites, because `Actual Hours`
here is **not** "hours worked" on every row: `payroll_hours_basis.py` (the one home, §14y) decides
per (person, day) which evidence answered, and its own measurement is why — `shifts.actual_hours`
carries a figure on **7 of 7,740** rows, so payroll's pre-2026-10-10 `actual_hours or
scheduled_hours` fell through to the plan on effectively every row and nobody was told. So each drill
row names the relation that basis word says answered: the time clock for a punched day, the schedule
for a day paid from the plan **and** for a manager's correction (which is typed onto
`shifts.actual_hours` on this read), and **nothing at all** where nothing was measured. The map is
`BASIS_RELATIONS`, keyed on the engine's **own basis constants**; the harness fails the build if the
one home grows a basis the map has no entry for, so a blank can only ever mean "measured nothing" and
never "nobody taught the panel about this basis".

**THE FIVE GRAINS, MEASURED.** Two row shapes, and the first pair is the sharpest §CORE-17.3n case
in the workforce module so far — same row, same unit, and the only difference is which relation
answered:

| # | row shape | unit | provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | person × pay period | hours | the schedule alone — what was PLANNED |
| 2 | person × pay period | hours | **the same row, same unit** — the time clock where a punch closed, the schedule where the period was paid from the plan, and NOTHING NAMEABLE where nothing was measured |
| 3 | person × pay period | money | the schedule + the employee record the rate was read from |
| 4 | person × pay period | money | the hours' own relation per row + the employee record |
| 5 | store × work-week | hours | the schedule alone |

Grains 1 and 5 are the same unit out of the same relation and are told apart by the **ROW ALONE** —
which is exactly why these are two declarations and not one.

**ABSENCE IS NEVER ZERO (§CORE-17.3i), IN THREE SHAPES.**

- A person for whom **nothing was measured** and who is not ticked to be paid from the schedule is
  shown **without a figure**, names **no relation**, and is **not counted**. A `0.0 h` there reads as
  *this person worked and produced nothing*, which in a payroll context is an accusation with nothing
  behind it. Such a row carries 0 in the payload, so the report's own total is unchanged and the
  tie-out still holds to the cent — the honest blank and the correct figure are compatible rather
  than a choice.
- A person whose **only punch is open or auto-closed** carries the engine's own `punch_unusable`
  instead. The two blanks are **different facts** and the panel keeps them apart: one says a punch
  exists and the company's own rule refuses to count it, which is a thing to go and fix. The router
  drops a zero-hour basis before naming a row's dominant one — correctly, since it is naming where
  the HOURS came from — so the reason reads the engine's tally **unfiltered**, which is the only
  place that word survives. The precedence is declared, not accidental.
- A **store nobody has scheduled this week** is served **no panel at all**: its `0.0 h` over no rows
  would tie zero against nothing and read as *we checked, there was nothing*, which is
  indistinguishable from a week nobody has written yet (the one home's own `served_tiles` rule,
  dereferenced, never copied).

**THIN PUNCH COVERAGE IS SURFACED, NEVER SMOOTHED.** House punch coverage is partial and measured
read-only on production — roughly **54%** (Jul), **52%** (Aug), **66%** (Sep), **62%** (Oct), and
**June 2026 has none at all**; a Cellfonz October salary figure was ruled NOT MEASURABLE at 49%. A
figure folded over such a month is still the figure people are paid by, so it is not changed — but
three things let the reader see how little of it rests on a measurement, and none of them is
arithmetic of the declaration's own: every row carries the basis word **and the producer's own
sentence for it**, every row carries the producer's `hours_by_basis` tally **verbatim** (so a
fortnight of punched and planned days is not collapsed to one word), and the panel's **`sources`**
list counts the rows per relation — *"the schedule · 3"* beside *"our own time clock · 2"* is
readable without opening anything. Every hours panel's note says the shortfall in words.

**PAY VISIBILITY IS THE REPORT'S OWN GATE, ASKED AGAIN (agent rule 4, mig `434`).** Pay-per-hour,
gross pay and salary are hidden below market manager, per-org configurable, and `GET
/storeops/payroll` STRIPS those keys server-side. The new sibling endpoint asks the **same**
`pay_visibility.can_see_pay` and applies the **same** `strip_pay`, and a gated caller is served the
two HOURS panels and **neither money panel** — not a panel of `$0.00`s, which is what folding
stripped rows would produce. Measured, not assumed: there is a second line of defence, because over
stripped rows the money figures have no counted row at all and the one home's own refusal catches
them even if the gate were bypassed. The hours panels are served either way, because a gated caller
still runs hours corrections.

**THE FIX IS AT THE READ, NOT IN THE DECLARATION (§CORE-17.3c, taken again).**
`router._store_week_hours` summed a store's week of shifts and returned a float: **which rows, and
which column of each**, was a fact that read knew and every caller threw away — which is why the
Hours Budget screen printed a figure with no way to the rows behind it. It now has a sourced form,
`_store_week_hours_sourced(...) -> (total, rows)`, with the plain one a thin wrapper over it so the
over-budget projection check is byte-identical, and the per-row fact travels on the row under the
field names the declaration declares (`drill_hours`, `drill_basis` — dereferenced by the router,
never spelled there). A shift with no stored `scheduled_hours` had its hours worked out from
`start_time`/`end_time`, so it names **no column** rather than an empty one.

**ONE FACT, ONE HOME — AND THE OTHER HALF OF IT, IN THE SAME COMMIT.** The **employee record** and
**hand-entered hours** became `data_lineage_registry.EMPLOYEE_ROSTER` / `.MANUAL_HOURS`, and the one
pre-existing literal copy of each (`account/liabilities_drilldown.EMPLOYEES` / `.MANUAL_HOURS`) was
**deleted** and dereferences the constant now, string-identical, no read changed — naming a fact is
half a design fix and deleting every copy is the half that has been skipped three times here
(§19.18). The time clock and the schedule are dereferenced, not re-named. **No new feed registry
entry**: both names are NAME constants beside `STORE_ROSTER`, because an employee record is a config
row with no arrival cadence for the feed watchdog to measure (the `targets_drilldown.TARGETS`
posture). The **paid-hours basis** finally has a `module_graph` block of its own
(`payroll_hours_basis`), with its **eleven pre-existing callers named by hand** for the first time —
batch 22's `rep_pay_snapshot` posture, taken again.

**THE ONE HOME GAINED ONE ADDITIVE THING.** `tile_panel`'s `column` now takes a **callable of the
row**, exactly as `tables` already did, because the column a figure was read out of genuinely differs
per row here (a punch's own hours column for one person, the schedule's for the next) and naming one
for both would name the wrong column on half the rows. A plain string behaves exactly as before, and
the harness pins both forms.

**A PANEL EXPLAINS THE FIGURE, NOT THE TABLE (§CORE-17.3o), DECIDED BY READING EACH PAGE.**

- `/storeops/payroll` and `/storeops/reports` fold their own tiles **in the browser** over the rows
  their filter bar leaves on screen, so their panels **are narrowed** (`lib/drill-narrow`), matched on
  the person-and-store key the server serves with every drill row, and each figure is read **off its
  narrowed panel only when that panel agrees to the cent** — a disagreement costs the link, never the
  figure.
- `/storeops/hours-budget` is the negative, and it has a browser filter too: every figure on it is
  **one store's own server-folded number**, so filtering hides whole rows and changes no figure.
  `drill-narrow` is deliberately absent from it. The call is not "does this page filter", it is "does
  this page fold a figure over a population the server did not" (batch 22's reading, from the other
  side). Both directions are locked off each page's own text.

**WHAT IS REFUSED, AND WHICH RULING SAYS SO.**

- **`Employees`** on the StoreOps Reports strip — a cardinality, not Σ(a field), whose count the
  panel's own header already states (the "Reps Calculated" ruling).
- **`Net (Actual − Sched)`** and its `▲/▼` cue — a difference whose two halves each drill
  (§CORE-17.3k, as batch 10 extended §CORE-17.3h).
- **`Pay Rate`** — a leaf: one column of one employee record, and a rate besides (§CORE-17.3h). It is
  named as the PROVENANCE of the money figures instead, which is where it belongs.
- **The weekly hours budget and the DM override** — a figure somebody typed and a recorded decision,
  neither folded from rows (§CORE-17.3h's leaf extension, §CORE-17.3m). They get plain-words labels,
  not panels.
- **The By-Store view's rows** — the page regroups the very rows these panels hold, under a store key
  those rows already carry, so the narrowed tile panel answers that question exactly.
- **The PTO accrual and chargeback panels** on `/storeops/payroll` — a month-keyed ledger at another
  grain, with its own producers, and the page already says in words that it is keyed to the calendar
  month. Left to its own family rather than stretched into this one.

**TWO LIVE DEFECTS — REPORTED, REPRODUCED, NOT REPAIRED, NO FIGURE MOVED.**

1. **`storeops.manual_hours` NEVER REACHES THIS REPORT'S FIGURE.** 569 hand-entered correction rows
   exist (37 house, 532 Luxelink) and `GET /storeops/payroll` deliberately does not read that table
   (§14y records it, and the router says so in its own comment). A correction a manager typed on the
   Time Clock screen is therefore invisible to the Payroll Report — so this family **never names that
   relation**, because naming it would be a provenance claim about a read that did not happen. The gap
   is written down in the declaration, in the registry constant's own docstring, and here; the harness
   fails the build if a panel starts naming it.
2. **A MANAGER'S CORRECTION IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE SCHEDULE IT WAS TYPED OVER.** On this read
   a `clocked_corrected` day is a `shifts.actual_hours` edit — the same relation a `schedule_opt_in`
   day comes out of — so the two bases name ONE table and are told apart only by the basis word
   travelling on the row. Stated rather than hidden: the row's fields carry the basis and its
   sentence, and the relation named is the one the figure was really read from.

**WHAT IS STILL OWED, HONESTLY** (seven routes read, classified and deliberately **not**
reclassified — a wrongly reclassified report is hidden from the programme, which is worse than the
debt):

- `/storeops/timeclock` — a real report, and the one closest to this batch: its badges (`n punches`,
  `n hrs`, the auto-lunch total, `n clocked in`) fold the punch rows themselves. Its row is a PUNCH,
  not a person-period, so it is a **third family** needing its own declaration and a sibling endpoint
  (the list read is a bare array). Next, not padded into this PR.
- `/storeops/schedule` — the week grid's per-row, per-day and grand totals, plus the 8-week
  hours-trend total. Same SUBJECT as the Hours Budget (planned hours out of the schedule) at a
  **different row** (employee × week, and a per-day column), and its grid folds a bare `/shifts`
  array with nowhere to hang a key. Deserves the hours-budget declaration **extended**, which is a
  page-and-endpoint change of its own rather than a corner of this one.
- `/storeops/payroll-tax` — its only printed figures (`Gross`, `Net`) are computed **in the browser**
  by `lib/payroll-tax.computePay` from raw hours, a rate and a W-4. There is no server fold to open,
  and moving a withholding engine server-side is a **money-touching change surfaced for the owner**,
  not a drill-down PR. The §CORE-17.3b class, written down rather than half-served.
- `/hr` — the HR total-comp strip is server-folded (`GET /hr/compensation` serves its own `totals`),
  so it is the easiest of the seven; but base salary + commission − chargebacks is a **different
  provenance** on the person row (the commission snapshot joins it), which is its own family and
  touches the commission module's amounts. Named, not grabbed.
- `/hr/payroll-expenses` — the audit's own worst-first entry in this module: a store × month of
  employer tax and burden items. Its own grain, its own producer, and `labour_vocabulary` plus the
  carried-expense-month rule (§COMMCALC-23) must be dereferenced rather than re-derived. A family of
  its own, and the next one worth doing properly.
- `/storeops/visits/plan` — the DM quota monitor's `completed of required` and its per-DM counts: a
  visit-compliance grain, where `required` is a **declared** config figure (§CORE-17.3m) and
  `completed` is folded from visit rows. A store-visit family, not a payroll one.
- `/storeops/team` — `<TeamSnapshot>`'s headline tiles are the **targets engine's** own snapshot at
  the store/rep-target grain, which `commcalc/targets_drilldown` (§CORE-17.3m) already owns. A second
  catalogue over it would be two paths answering one question; converging the shared component onto
  that declaration is the right PR and is not this one.

### §CORE-17.3y INVENTORY AGING, AT DEVICE GRAIN (2026-10-26, batch 25)

**Route:** `/commcalc/asset/aging` (Inventory Aging). **Endpoint:** `GET /asset/aging`
(`app/modules/asset/router.py::get_aging`). **Declaration:** `app/modules/asset/device_asset_drilldown.py`
§8 — `aging_catalogue` / `aging_drilldowns` / `aging_totals` / `aging_rows` / `band_rows` /
`device_tables` / `device_keys`. **Lock:** `backend/harness_batch25_drilldown.py` (79 checks).

**OWNER ASK 2026-10-26, verbatim**, quoting this page's own banner: *"124 devices in the 9-12 day
window - sell before day 12 / $29,598.76 at risk of being billed unsold. These have days left; act
now., need a drill donw for these , whic store market date range etc"*.

#### .1 THE DUPLICATE CHECK — what was searched for, and what was REUSED rather than rebuilt

The build gate in `CLAUDE.md` is a search before a build, so: the index was searched for an existing
mechanism answering *"which devices are behind this aging figure, by store and date"*, and three
candidates were read before anything was written.

| searched | found | what happened |
|---|---|---|
| §CORE-17 — is there a home for "the rows behind a figure"? | `core/report_drilldown.py` (`tile_panel`, `tiles`, `tie_out`, `panel`) | **REUSED whole.** No fold, no tie-out and no panel shape is written here. |
| §CORE-17.3l — does the device-asset family already declare this report? | `asset/device_asset_drilldown.py`, SEVEN catalogues, none of them this report | **EXTENDED**, as an eighth declaration in the same module. A second module would be a second answer to "which relation was this device-asset figure read out of", which is the sibling defect §CORE-17.3l was itself written to refuse. |
| §COMMCALC-26 — who decides the band, and which feed answers "still unsold"? | `commcalc/device_aging_policy.py` (the ladder) and `payables/unsold_inventory.py` (the shape, the source and the stamp) | **DEREFERENCED, never re-derived.** The declaration reads the producer's own `_bucket` stamp; it re-applies no ladder and re-decides no source. |
| §COMMCALC-33 — is the out-of-pocket headline Σ of this report's amount column? | No: it is that cost NET of the per-device carrier recovery | **REFUSED a panel** (see .5). |

Nothing new was created but the declaration, its lock, one registry NAME constant and one label.

#### .2 THE SEVENTH GRAIN, AND WHY THE SIX WERE NOT ENOUGH

§CORE-17.3l measured six grains across its seven producers and every one of them is keyed by a
**store**, a **loan** or a weekly **batch**. This report's bands are Σ over **one row per unsold
IMEI**, and the grain is the row a figure is summed over rather than the subject the report is
about. Stretching the store-keyed On-Inventory catalogue over it would have declared a store's
exposure as the evidence for a device's, and `tie_out` would have said so out loud. The header's own
grain table now carries eight rows.

#### .3 ONE PANEL PER BAND, OVER THAT BAND'S OWN DEVICES

This is the one place in the family that does **not** hand `tiles()` a single row list. Everywhere
else each tile folds over the same rows, so the rows a tile does not count stay beside it as the
context that makes the figure readable (§CORE-17.3l's own rule). A device belongs to exactly **one**
band, so doing that here would serve the warning band a panel of 1,755 devices with 124 counted —
and `ROW_CAP` (400) would then very likely omit the 124 the owner clicked on, which is worse than
losing the context. So the declaration carries a `rows_of` accessor naming the band each tile is
folded over, and `aging_drilldowns` folds each tile over its own devices. Band isolation is locked in
**both** directions (harness §C).

#### .4 TWO RELATIONS, DECIDED PER ROW — AND THE IMEI IS SPELLED TWICE

Since §COMMCALC-26 this report serves two tenants off two different relations: a consignment device
is read out of `commcalc.asset_ledger` and a device the platform owes for out of
`commcalc.device_payable_ledger`. A panel naming one of them for every row would be wrong on every
row of the other tenant, so `device_tables` reads the producer's own stamp per row. The keys are per
row too, because the two relations do not spell the IMEI the same way — `esn_imei` on the
consignment ledger and `imei` on the payable ledger — and naming one for both would hand a support
query a column half the rows' table does not have.

**ONE FACT, ONE HOME, BOTH HALVES.** `device_payable_ledger` became a NAME constant in
`commcalc/data_lineage_registry.py` (`DEVICE_PAYABLE_LEDGER`) with a `sourceLabels.ts` entry, so no
database name reaches a screen. The provenance stamp itself was a literal in the module that writes
it: `payables/unsold_inventory.py` now declares `SOURCE_FIELD` and **writes through it** in the same
commit, and the declaration dereferences both it and `SOURCE_LEDGER`. Writing a registry and leaving
the caller on its literal is not a fix at all (§19.18, taken for the fourth time here).

#### .5 THE FOUR REFUSALS, each with a ruling behind it

- **The device COUNT beside every band**, and **Total Phones Outstanding**. Each is the cardinality
  of the money panel beside it — the band's own panel lists exactly those devices and serves
  `rows_total_count` — so a second tile proving how many there are is a tautology dressed as
  evidence (the batch-11 `store_count` ruling). The page carries the reason in a comment where the
  missing button would be.
- **`flagged_owed` / `flagged_count`.** Σ of the three band tiles, so a tie-out against either could
  not fail (§CORE-17.3h as batch 10 extended it). All three halves get panels instead.
- **The out-of-pocket headline.** Since §COMMCALC-33 it is the cost NET of what the carrier already
  recovered per device, and the netting is the payables module's verdict rather than a column on
  these rows. A fold over this report's own amount column would explain a DIFFERENT number and the
  tie-out would say so — correctly, and uselessly. It is declared in the PR that carries the
  per-device recovery onto these rows, not guessed at here.
- **`age_buckets`.** The same bands over the same devices, counted rather than priced — a second
  shape of a figure already drillable, which would be two answers to one question.

#### .6 A COST NOBODY RECORDED IS NOT $0.00

The report's own footer reads the device cost as `float(x or 0)`, so a device whose cost was never
recorded and a device that genuinely owes nothing enter the total identically. The declaration tells
them apart: the unrecorded one is **shown without a figure**, carries `amount_not_recorded`, and is
**not counted**, while the real $0.00 is counted as the measurement it is. The figure still ties,
because a blank adds zero either way — the point is that the gap is now **visible** rather than
averaged away, which is the §CORE-17.3i posture applied to a cost instead of to an absence.

#### .7 THE ROUTE WAS RE-CLASSIFIED FROM `flat`, AND THAT IS REPORTED

The 2026-10-24 audit pinned `/commcalc/asset/aging` as `flat` — *"already shows the source rows;
nothing is summarised above them"*. The first half is true and the second never was: three band
tiles, two footer totals and two alert banners sit above those tables, every one of them a fold the
reader had no way into. That is exactly the state the audit existed to find, so it is REPORTED here
rather than quietly re-pinned — a mis-classified route is how a ratchet stops ratcheting, and this
one hid the owner's own question for two days. **`OWES_MAX` does not move** (18): a `flat` route was
never counted as owing a drill-down, and lowering the pin here would claim a debt was paid that was
never on the books.

#### .8 ONE MORE DEFECT FIXED IN PASSING, because it is the same class

The three band tiles were still printing `Under 45 Days` / `45–60 Days` / `sell before day 60` —
one carrier's contract shown to every tenant — while the banner immediately above them had resolved
the carrier's **declared** window since §COMMCALC-26 (owner 2026-10-22: *"it should not say sell
before 60 days as that is boost requirement , total is sell before 12 days"*). The tiles now read
`windowLabel`, the same resolution, so one page no longer states two windows. The drill key on each
tile is the SERVER'S total key rather than the bucket name, so a renamed bucket cannot silently open
another band's panel.

Neighbours: §CORE-17.3l (the family this extends, and its grain rule), §COMMCALC-26 (the declared
window, which feed answers "still unsold", and the stamp), §COMMCALC-33 (the netting
that the out-of-pocket refusal points at), §CORE-17.3h (a composed figure gets no panel),
§CORE-17.3i (an absence is not a zero), §CORE-17.3c (the offer rule — a link only where the server
served a panel).

Three parallel sweeps over all **136** report routes in `REPORT_DIRECTORY` (plus `/closing/cash-variance`):

| state | routes | meaning |
|---|---|---|

| `flat` | 22 | already shows the source rows |
| `not_report` | 11 | config, wizard or work queue |
| `own` | 9 | a drill-down of its own that names its sources, predating this |

`/commcalc/sales-report`, `/commcalc/sales-recon`, `/commcalc/commission-ledger`,
`/commcalc/daily-commission`, `/commcalc/ma-overview-recon`, `/failures`. **Not one other page in
the platform names the table, feed or upload behind a figure** — which is why every `partial` verdict
in the audit was partial for the same reason, and why the provenance half is the shared mechanism's

Worst-first, by how disputable the money is: `/closing/cash-recon-management` (eleven cash tiles, no

`/commcalc/asset/owed-weekly`. Per-route findings: project folder `drilldown-audit/`.

**TWO GAPS FOUND BY THE AUDIT AND NOT CLOSED HERE, so nobody re-derives them:**

- **`REPORT_DIRECTORY` is not a complete registry of what a report is.** `/closing/cash-variance` is
  a report and is absent from it, because the owner's 2026-10-08 "cleaner look" ruling puts some
  reports on dashboard tiles rather than sidebar rows. `tileOnly` cannot stand in for the missing
  half — **327** nav entries carry it, nearly all setup screens — so the coverage gate names its
  exceptions in `EXTRA_REPORTS` rather than inferring them. Making the directory complete is a nav
  change of its own.
- **`"source"` means four different things across ~30 backend payloads** (a table name, a screen
  name, an upload route, a free sentence). `origin()` is the one shape going forward; the existing
  keys are not renamed here.

`backend/harness_report_drilldown.py` — **61 checks**, pure stdlib, driving the real functions:

zero; an excluded row is flagged, not dropped) · C `tie_out` (ties / **None** / False-in-words, and

with the true count, the tie-out before the cap, `untraceable_origins`) · E the cash-variance drill
end to end **with five negative controls** — a dropped out-of-band day breaks the tie (Z1), a
mis-scored day breaks the tie (Z2), a day tampered to unmeasurable leaves the evidence short and the

literal and no `compare`** so it can never become a second opinion about money, the reason vocabulary

`backend/harness_drilldown_coverage.py` — **17 checks**, the ratchet: every report route declared
exactly once, no ledger route has stopped existing, every excused state carries a written reason,
every `shared` route really renders the shared panel (writing the registry without wiring the caller

Re-pin it downward in
the same PR that builds a drill-down; a change that raises it is a report shipped without evidence.

### §CORE-17.6 WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE

- **No new table and no migration.** The drill-down presents figures other modules computed.
- **No business figure.** The one home carries amounts handed to it and computes none; §G4 fails the
  build on a non-zero dollar literal in it.
- **No write, no chargeback, no flag.** Opening a drill-down creates nothing. Turning a counted
  shortage into money off a rep's pay is still `envelope_report.chargeback_parent_row`, from a screen
  where a human ticks a box.
- **The 93 are not built in this PR.** They are written down, ratcheted, and ordered worst-first.

## §CORE-16. A SELF-CALL CARRIES THE TENANT IT IS ACTING AS (owner report 2026-10-24)

Owner, on the envelope payout screen:

> ℹ️ commission: commission accrual fetch failed (HTTPError: **409 Client Error: Conflict** for url:
> `…/commcalc/payout/accrued?org_id=854f6d7b…&as_of=2026-10-17&store_code=Nostrand`)
> ℹ️ salary: salary-owed fetch failed (HTTPError: **409 Client Error: Conflict** for url:
> `…/storeops/salary-owed?org_id=854f6d7b…&start=2026-08-18&end=2026-10-17&store_code=Nostrand`)

### `store_code=Nostrand` IS A RED HERRING — it never reached a handler

`GET /closing/payout-due` does not import mod-commission and mod-people; it **calls the platform's own
HTTP surface** at `INTERNAL_API_BASE_URL` (default `127.0.0.1:8000`) and forwards the caller's bearer
token. That call therefore re-enters `app/core/tenant_middleware.py` **from the outside** and must
prove the same two facts the browser's request proved — and it only ever proved one:

| fact the gate needs | the browser's request | the self-call (before this) |
|---|---|---|
| WHO is calling (`Authorization`) | ✅ | ✅ *(added 2026-08-04; without it the envelope read **$0.00 owed**)* |
| WHICH TENANT they act as (`x-active-org`) | ✅ | ❌ **dropped** |

`_tenant_is_ambiguous` then refuses to guess (§28), which is the correct behaviour, and
`_reject_tenant_choice` answers **409 `tenant_choice_required`** before the route body runs. So the
store code, the dates and the org_id in the URL were never looked at.

### THE EVIDENCE — the platform's own record, not an inference

`core.access_log`, 2026-10-24 17:55 UTC, read-only:

| time | status | path | actor | org |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 17:55:46.300 | **409** | `/commcalc/payout/accrued` | **NULL** | **NULL** |
| 17:55:46.308 | **409** | `/storeops/salary-owed` | **NULL** | **NULL** |
| 17:55:46.512 | 200 | `/closing/payout-due` | `ab08bb15…` | `854f6d7b…` (Luxelink) |

The pair of 409s sits *inside* the outer 200, and carries **no actor and no org** — the gate rejected
before `_set_actor` ran. Login `ab08bb15…` is the §28 login: **admin in three companies**
(house / Luxelink / Vzone), not a super-admin, and like all four multi-company logins it has
`is_default_org IS NULL`, so `default_org` is None and there is nothing to fall back to. A
single-membership login (92 of 96 when the gate shipped) could never see this.

### THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE

The general fact that was wrong is not "the envelope screen loses the tenant". It is:

> **a self-call re-enters the gate with LESS identity than the request that caused it.**

Both known instances are that class, two years apart in the same four helper functions — a dropped
token read as `$0.00`, a dropped tenant read as `409`. Both read as *a number*, not as *a refusal*.

### ONE FACT, ONE HOME, DEREFERENCED

`backend/app/core/internal_call.py` (**new**) is the ONE home for what a self-call carries:
`internal_api_base()`, `acting_tenant(org_id)`, `self_call_headers(authorization, org_id)` and
`self_call_note(status, what, sibling)`. The tenant comes from `tenant_middleware.acting_org()` — the
middleware's **already-validated** resolution, which wins over the handler's `org_id` default — and
falls back to that `org_id` outside a request the middleware saw (a sweep, a cron job).

**NOT A WIDENING.** `x-active-org` is untrusted by design: the middleware honours it only when it
names one of the caller's own memberships, and a super-admin's cross-tenant administration already
reads the same header. Declaring the tenant the outer request was validated for removes a guess; it
grants nothing. Proved by `harness_internal_self_call.py` C6.

**ALL TEN SELF-CALL SITES WIRED**, not the two that were reported:

| module | sites |
|---|---|
| `closing/router.py` | `_get_commission_accrued`, `_get_salary_owed`, `_post_commission_payout`, `_post_salary_advance`, the closing-expense P&L system-line push |
| `storeops/router.py` | `_pto_push_expense_line`, `_payex_push_expense_line`, `_payex_push_gross_line`, `_additional_payroll_push_line`, `_dm_targets_summary_bulk` |

The five `storeops` pushes sent **no headers at all** and so were 401ing silently — the same class,
found by looking for the siblings rather than by a second report. `authorization` is now threaded
from each manager-gated route. **REPORTED, NOT HIDDEN:** the pg_cron sweep
`POST /storeops/salary-advance/additional-payroll/run-due` is secret-gated and holds no user token, so
its push still cannot authenticate; it now says so through `self_call_note` (401 → "this figure is NOT
$0, it is UNKNOWN") instead of appearing to succeed. Giving a cron a service identity is a separate,
money-touching decision and is left for the owner.

### LOCKED SO IT CANNOT UN-WIRE

`backend/harness_internal_self_call.py` (42 checks, DB-free, no socket). Section **E is the build
gate**: it walks the AST of every `backend/app/**/*.py`, resolves each `requests.*` call whose URL
derives from an `*INTERNAL_API_BASE*` variable (one hop through a local `url =` assignment), and fails
the build when any of them does not pass `headers=self_call_headers(...)`, when a second copy of the
base URL appears, or when a module hand-rolls an `{"Authorization": authorization}` dict. E1 fails if
the scan ever finds fewer than 9 sites, so it cannot pass by matching nothing, and E5–E7 are negative
controls. Verified to bite: un-wiring one site turns E2 and E4 red.

Section C is the regression, run through `tenant_middleware`'s **own** predicate: the old header dict
is ambiguous for the reported login, the new one is not.

### DUPLICATE CHECK (build gate)

Checked §28 (which company am I in), §22 (operator entry sessions), §CORE-07/§CORE-12 (login
identity), §50 (the module graph) and §16–18 before writing a line. **REUSED, not rebuilt:**
`x-active-org` stays the one tenant selector and `_pick_active_org` / `_tenant_is_ambiguous` stay the
one server-side rule — this change makes a caller *declare* through them, it does not add a second
gate. `harness_ambiguous_tenant.py` keeps the gate's own cases (single membership, `is_default_org`, a
foreign header); this harness does not re-prove them and that harness, previously **run by nothing**,
is now executed in the same CI job — so `harness_unrun_pending.txt` shrinks 315 → 314 and
`harness_ci_pipefail_lock.PINNED_MAX` with it. `_sib_note` was not deleted: it now dereferences
`self_call_note`. **No second self-call mechanism was created.**

### §16–18 CROSS-REFERENCES

Registered in `app/modules/core/module_graph.py` as fact `internal_self_call`
(home `app/core/internal_call.py`, lock `harness_internal_self_call.py`, callers
`closing/router.py` + `storeops/router.py`). Depends on: §28 (the gate that refuses to guess),
§CORE-07 (who a login is). Feeds: §47.8 (the envelope basis), the four payroll P&L system lines
(§COMMCALC-23 labour), §4 (expenses). Neighbours: §22 (the other cross-tenant declaration),
§19.18 (writing a registry without wiring the callers is not a fix), §50 (the interlink itself).

CI: `carrier-vocab-guard` job `internal-self-call-tenant`. **No migration.**

Files: `backend/app/core/internal_call.py` (**new**), `backend/app/modules/closing/router.py`,
`backend/app/modules/storeops/router.py`, `backend/app/modules/core/module_graph.py`,
`backend/harness_internal_self_call.py` (**new**), `backend/harness_unrun_pending.txt`,
`backend/harness_ci_pipefail_lock.py`, `.github/workflows/carrier-vocab-guard.yml`.

## §NOTIFY-01. A FAILED SEND IS REPORTED WITH ITS RECIPIENT, ITS REASON AND ITS FIX — never as a count (owner report 2026-10-24)

Owner: *"send report shows Sent: 6 ok, 10 failed., which failed and why should be listed with how to
fix it"*.

**THE INSTANCE, measured in production before anything was changed.** The 18:03 send of *Closing &
Cash Pickup Status* wrote 16 `notify.send_log` rows: **6 emails sent**, and **10 WhatsApp failures
that are FIVE people × TWO files** (the .xlsx and the .pdf), every one of them Meta
`(#133010) Account not registered`. So the sentence overstated the damage by a factor of two, named
nobody, and gave no remedy — while the row carrying the provider's own words sat in the database. It
also could not say the thing that mattered most: **all five also received the email**, so nobody
missed the report.

**THE CLASS.** Not "the Send box is terse". **Nothing owned the question "what did this send actually
do"**, so all four paths answered it their own way and discarded the reasons: `/notify/send`,
`/notify/send-file` and `/notify/send-to-designated` each returned the same two integers, and
`notify/digest_delivery` parked the raw provider string on a leg for every reader to interpret. Adding
a list to the one button would have been the patchwork the house rules forbid.

**ONE HOME: `backend/app/modules/notify/send_outcome.py`** (PURE — no IO, no app import).
- `classify(channel, error)` → `{code, reason, fix, recognised, error}`. An **ALLOWLIST**: a code this
  house has ruled on gets a plain-language reason and the console step a human takes; anything else is
  `recognised: False` with **no fix** and the provider's own words as the reason. A confident wrong
  remedy costs more than an admitted gap — the same rule as
  `carrier_dollar_class.component_is_evidence` (§66).
- A ruling is **channel-scoped**. A WhatsApp-only code quoted by an email failure is not recognised; a
  ruling declared for any channel (an expired access token) reaches both.
- `summarize(rows, note=)` → the outcome a surface renders, built from the `send_log` rows the send
  just inserted, so no caller keeps a second list in step with them. **One entry per (channel,
  target)** — a PERSON on a CHANNEL, not an attachment — with the attempt counts kept beside it so the
  old number stays accountable. A target that carried one file and failed another is `partial` and
  counted **failed**: something it was owed did not arrive.
- `headline(outcome)` is the ONE sentence, tri-state: all delivered / partly delivered / **nothing
  arrived** — and a send with nobody to send to says why instead of claiming a success.
- `stamp(rows)` is the READ side: `GET /notify/send-log` explains a failed history row in the same
  words, including rows written before this module existed.

**THE SIBLINGS, fixed in the same PR, not excused.** `_dispatch` and `send_file` both return
`outcome`; the two "nobody to send to" early returns of `/send-to-designated` go through
`_nothing_sent`, which carries the reason in the same shape; and a `digest_delivery` leg now
dereferences `classify` instead of leaving its raw string to be read.

**THE SURFACES render it, never re-word it.** `frontend/src/lib/send-outcome.tsx`
(`SendOutcomeView`) is the one home for what a send result looks like on screen, used by the Send
modal (`lib/send-report.tsx`, the one sender — §COMMCALC-19) and by Report Recipients. The Notify
history shows the stamped reason with the provider's raw text on hover. **No remedy sentence is copied
into the browser** — a second spelling of a fact is a future divergence, and a lock fails the build if
one appears.

**WHAT THIS DID NOT DO.** It did not make WhatsApp work. The live finding stands on its own and is a
data/configuration defect, REPORTED rather than hidden: the sender number is not registered with
Meta's Cloud API **for the account our access token belongs to** (every attempt on 2026-10-24 is
`#133010`, where every day up to 2026-10-23 had worked — the token/phone-number PAIRING broken by the
2026-10-22 rotation, *not* a missing registration, and the allowlist's remedy says so because the
plausible wrong fix is the thing this mechanism exists to avoid; the existing diagnostic
`GET /notify/whatsapp-account` is pointed at rather than rebuilt), and behind that the Meta app is
still in development mode — 163 historic
`(#131030) Recipient phone number not in allowed list` failures, and exactly one number has ever
received anything. Both fixes are Meta-console steps for the owner; the app now says so on the screen
where the failure appears.

**LOCK: `backend/harness_notify_send_outcome.py`** — 53 checks, DB-free, driving the REAL module over
the REAL production error strings, with the owner's exact 16 rows as the regression (§D: 6 ok, 5
failed, every one named, one deduped fix, and the 10 attempts still stated). The un-wiring locks, each
with an armed control: an **AST scan of every `return {…}` in `notify/router.py` whose keys include
both `sent` and `failed` fails the build unless it also carries `outcome`** (so a new send path cannot
go back to two integers); the digest leg must dereference the same home; no module but the one home
may rule on a provider error code; every surface must render the one view; and no remedy sentence may
appear in the browser. In CI as **"A failed send names who, why and the fix"**.

## §STOREOPS-01. A TYPED PAYROLL FIGURE SAVES ON ITS OWN, AND A SAVE SAYS WHAT IT WILL COST BEFORE IT LANDS (owner report 2026-10-26)

**What he said**, of Hours Approval, pay period 2026-10-05 → 10-18, payable 10-23:

> *"tehere is a lag in saving andf updating the hours when a change is done m teh ssystem shoudl
> confirm that the new hours will be this after teh change and to save it every time , if multiple
> hours are adjusted it shoudl show mnultiple hours before saving what the neew payroll will be"*
> … *"if you see i havd to enter hours for simarjyot 3 times to get the correct horus and still i
> cannot see the correnct hours"* … *"i selected mohammed sami but nothing showed up in filters"*
> … *"tehre shoudl eba button of refresh also so only the data we are working on shoudl refreshed"*

**He typed three times and the system recorded once.** Measured read-only against production on
2026-10-26: `storeops.payroll_approval` for **E043** / 2026-10-05..18 holds ONE adjustment (−10.97)
and `storeops.payroll_change_log` holds exactly ONE matching row. Two of his three attempts never
reached the server, and nothing on screen said so.

### STOREOPS-01.1 THE CLASS — five mechanisms, one symptom

Not "the save is slow". Five independent faults, each of which on its own loses a typed number:

| # | the mechanism | what the reviewer saw |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **there was no save.** `storeops/payroll_approval.py` wrote `hours_approved` only alongside a DM *approval*; the board had no Save button. A figure typed and not approved in the same click was never sent. | "it did not save" |
| 2 | **a reload wiped the typed boxes** — `load()` ran `setEdits({})` **including after a REFUSED save**, so a missing reason cost the whole batch with no error beside the cleared cells. | "I had to type it 3 times" |
| 3 | **the board's boldest column ignored the save.** `Payable` rendered `hours_payable` (worked − lunch ± adjustment), which does not contain `hours_approved`; the saved correction appeared only as the input's grey **placeholder**. The server was right and the screen was stale. | "still i cannot see the correct hours" |
| 4 | **the person filter could not match anybody, ever.** `GET /core/filter-options` keys its `reps` options by NAME (a `{name: email}` fold), and this board alone sent that value as `employee_id` — compared against `E043`. Not a wrong answer: a guaranteed empty one. | "nothing showed up in filters" |
| 5 | **the lag was a 200k-row scan nobody asked for.** `storeops/payroll_approval.py::_worked_days_from_sales` reads up to 200,000 `commcalc.raw_sales` rows on every GET, and its only consumer is the evidence list on a row the clock holds nothing for. One save paid for two full scans (the POST's own derivation, then the UI's reload). | "there is a lag in saving" |

**And a sixth fault that is upstream of all of them, REPORTED and not repaired here:** `GET
/storeops/payroll` does not read `storeops.manual_hours` (`storeops/router.py` says so at `~:2051`; §14y and
`payroll_hours_drilldown` both record it as a live defect). So the DM's own corrections never reach
this board's `Worked`, and the reviewer rebuilds them by hand. E043 carries **six** correction rows
totalling **−16.00 h**, every one reasoned *"wrong clock out"*, filed 2026-10-19 — against the
102.84 h the board showed as the only truth. The hand-rebuilt figure landed **5.03 h** away from the
one the system already held.

### STOREOPS-01.2 WHAT THIS COSTS, measured on the live period

Three rows of 2026-10-05..18 were hand-corrected against force-closed punches. **E029 (Mohammed
Sami) has never once clocked out**: all 8 punches were closed by `force_clockout_cron` at 02:00,
~12 h each.

| employee | clock says | hand adjustment | payable today | intended | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E029 | 125.18 | **+18.49** | **143.67** | 88.20 | **+55.47 h / $943.00** — sign inverted, and already DM+HR approved |
| E043 | 102.84 | −10.97 | 91.87 | 86.84 (−16.00 already filed) | +5.03 h / $85.51 |
| E282 | 339.56 | −273.56 | 66.00 | — | a fortnight cannot hold 339.56 h |

A confirmation stating *"125.18 → 143.67, pay $2,442.39"* in words stops the first row dead. That is
the feature, and this is why it is not cosmetic.

### STOREOPS-01.3 THE FIX, one home each

- **`frontend/src/lib/hours-approval-preview.ts` — THE one home for "what will this save do to the
  payroll?"** Pure (no React, no fetch, no clock, no tenant/store/person name, no rate of its own).
  The dialog renders this object AND `previewToRows` builds the request from the SAME object, so the
  confirmation cannot describe a write that differs from the one that lands. `payableNow` /
  `payableAfter` are the single restatement of the server's own precedence (`storeops/payroll_approval.py::list_approvals`:
  `approved if approved is not None else payable`) — not a second rule.
- **`save`, an ACTION on the existing `storeops/payroll_approval.py::decide` path**, deliberately not a sibling endpoint: the reason
  gate, the negative-payable guard, the org scoping and the `payroll_change_log` write are the same
  rules, and a second write path for one field is the duplicate defect §19.18 names. It records the
  figure and moves **neither** approval stage — a correction typed into an approved row must not
  quietly re-sign it in the corrector's name.
- **A correction can be taken back.** An explicit empty `hours_approved` CLEARS it back to the
  computed figure, reason-gated and logged exactly like the correction it removes. A payroll number
  may not move anonymously in either direction.
- **The person filter in `storeops/payroll_approval.py::list_approvals` dereferences
  `core/person_identity.py::folded_token_key`** (§owner report
  2026-10-14, the one home for "is this the same human") so an id OR a name matches, order-free and
  accent-folded. An existing caller passing `E043` stays byte-identical. Registered on the
  `person_identity` fact in `core/module_graph.py`, so a caller that goes back to a local name rule
  fails the build.
- **The uncounted corrections are SHOWN on the row** — signed total, day count, and each day's reason
  on hover — carrying `manual_hours_counted: false` by name, and folded into **nothing**. Proved: the
  payable figure is byte-identical to before they were visible. Folding them moves a pay figure,
  which is the owner's call, not a side effect of a display fix.
- **`⟳ Refresh` on both boards** (Hours Approval and Salary Advances) re-reads the range on screen and
  changes no filter, drops no selection and keeps every unsaved figure — the browser's own refresh is
  what loses the filters, which is the only reason it was being used.
- **Salary Advances awaits both reloads before saying "recorded"**, and when the advance's `paid_date`
  falls outside the range on screen it SAYS so: `cash_paid_total` is windowed on `paid_date`
  (`get_salary_owed`), so such an advance is recorded correctly and still changes nothing here (`storeops/router.py`).
  Silently showing no change is what reads as a failed save.

**Locks.** `backend/harness_payroll_approval_save.py` (41 checks, DB-free, recording fake) and
`frontend/prove_hours_approval_preview.mjs` (34 checks, the real TS through the project's own `tsc`).
Between them they pin: `save` stamps no status and no signature; the reason gates and the
negative-payable guard are unchanged; a clear is logged with the figure it reverts to; an HR approval
survives a DM save while `send_back` still invalidates it; `approve` is byte-identical to before; the
person filter matches a name in any order or case and an unknown person yields an EMPTY board;
`manual_hours` moves no figure; and the sales scan is skipped when every employee has a clock record.

**Duplicate check, per the index rules.** Searched before building: §14y (`payroll_hours_basis`, the
one home for paid hours and its basis — not touched, this board reads `GET /storeops/payroll` as it
always did), §14z (clock variances), §CORE-17.3x (`storeops/payroll_hours_drilldown.py`, which already REPORTS
the `manual_hours` gap — extended in spirit, not duplicated), §19.45 (`storeops/payroll_log_identity.py`, the one
writer of the change log — reused), §64 (store identity — untouched), and `person_identity`
(dereferenced rather than re-derived). No new endpoint, no new table, **no migration**, and no second
derivation of any figure.

**Still open, and the owner's decision, not ours.** (a) Whether `storeops.manual_hours` should be
FOLDED into paid hours rather than reported beside them — it moves money, and the router's own
comment forbids doing it as a side effect. (b) `force_clockout_cron` is manufacturing ~12 h punches
for anybody who never clocks out (E029: 8 of 8 days), which is the upstream cause of all three
hand-corrections above; the auto-closed punch is already `punch_unusable` in §14y's vocabulary, but
`schedule_fallback` mode still pays it. (c) **E029's live row is overstated by $943 and is
DM+HR-approved** — a data repair, reported here, never "fixed" in code.

## §CORE-18. A LENGTH CAP DOES NOT DECIDE WHICH PART OF A STATUS SURVIVES (found 2026-10-27)

**Owner report 2026-10-27, verbatim:** *"Is all the data being ingested properly for kpi, Ismail
reported that data was off"*.

**The §COMMCALC-16 diagnostic worked.** The DLAR sweep's 2026-10-26 run detected that the carrier had
renamed the store report's unit-count fields, and the line it composed named them **and** named the
fields the portal is sending that nothing reads — the new spelling, which is the entire point of that
mechanism. What reached the operator, measured live on `commcalc.dlar_sweep_config.last_detail`, was
**600 characters** ending:

```
… ⚠ PORTAL FIELD CHANGED: store (DLAR): 'gross_activation_quantity' NOT SENT, store (DLAR):
'prepaid_activations' NOT SENT, store (DLAR): 'postpaid_activations' NOT SENT, store (DLAR):
'upgrades' NOT SENT,
```

mid-list, with the conclusion gone. `router._sweep_set_status` wrote `detail[:600]`. **The detection
worked and the finding was destroyed on the way to the column.**

### CORE-18.1 The class, not the instance

> **A length cap on a human-read status must not decide WHICH part of it survives. Keep both ends and
> elide the middle, and say how much was dropped.**

A head cut silently privileges whatever is written first, which is usually the restatement of what
already went fine. It is worst exactly where it matters most: a diagnostic's conclusion is written
last, and the part of a status that GROWS is the middle — one entry per changed column, one per store.
So the longer the list of things wrong, the more certain it is that the answer is the text thrown away.
The elision also carries a COUNT, because a bare `…` cannot be told from a sentence that trails off —
which is how the 2026-10-26 line read.

### CORE-18.2 The one home

`app/core/status_detail.py` — `fit(detail, limit=600, keep_tail=None)`. PURE, stdlib only. A line that
already fits is returned **unchanged**, so every healthy status is byte-identical to before. Over the
cap, head and tail are both kept with `MARK` (`" …[N chars elided]… "`) between them. A cap too small
for both ends degrades to the plain head cut, and nothing in it can raise: a status writer is the last
place in the system that may throw.

### CORE-18.3 The callers, wired

| caller | what was being cut |
|---|---|
| `commcalc/router._sweep_set_status` | every portal sweep's `last_detail` — the DLAR instance above |
| the same function's `core.job_run` insert | the durable history of the same line |
| `commcalc/router._pull_diag` | a connector pull's probe `status` |
| `commcalc/router._source_stamp` caller | a `data_source` row's `last_status` |
| `commcalc/vidapay_sweep` | the ORIGINAL status, which a prepended prefix pushed into the tail |
| `commcalc/auto_calc` | the later entries of a joined error list |

**Excused, with reason:** `supply/catalog_scrape` and `supply/ordering_logic` cap a product
*description*, not a status — the head IS the useful part; `core/control_box` caps a redacted log
context, where the head is the subject.

### CORE-18.4 Locks

`backend/harness_status_detail.py` — 32 checks, DB-free, in CI. §B is the regression from the **real**
2026-10-26 line, with a pre-fix control proving the head cut dropped the answer. §C proves a middle
four times longer still cannot push the conclusion out. §D fuzzes every input length and every cap for
an over-cap result. §E proves the writer never raises on junk input or a junk cap.

**A control that passed for the wrong reason, caught in the writing:** the fixture's invented new
spelling was first `activation_quantity`, which is a substring of the OLD `gross_activation_quantity`,
so the pre-fix control found the old name in the truncated head and called it the answer. The fixture
now uses spellings that are substrings of no old field name. A negative control must be able to fail.

Same class: §COMMCALC-16 (the diagnostic this one was silencing), §19.26 (missing beats wrong), §19.21
(a status that reports what was pulled rather than what was written).
